I need some underbelly scales from black dragon whelps to pay for the shoes Argus sent me from Goldshire. If you can get 6 of them for me, then I can pay Argus with some... and have enough left to fashion something for you.

Black dragon whelps are often flying around south of Lakeshire, but they like to wander. You might have to just keep an eye out and hunt them when you see them.

passages.title: Underbelly Scales
passages.text: I know that greedy Argus will send someone to collect his scales if I don't give them to him soon.  Have you found those scales yet?

passages.title: Underbelly Scales
passages.text: Thanks!  These will get me out of debt to Argus...

passages.title: The Collector
passages.text:
This note is a schedule with a list of days and times when a person -- described only as "The Collector" -- will receive a shipment of gold from the mines in Elwynn Forest.

From the schedule, it looks as if the Collector resides near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in eastern Elwynn.

This sounds important. You should report it to Marshal Patterson at Eastvale Logging Camp.

passages.title: The Collector
passages.text:
What?!?  We haven't had our people working the Elwynn mines for months!

Let me see that note you have...

passages.title: The Collector
passages.text: Hm... I have heard of this "Collector" but I don't know whom he's working for.  Thank you for the schedule.  It will help us solve this mystery.

passages.title: A Baying of Gnolls
passages.text:
As if the attacking orcs weren't enough! Now I have gnoll brutes and mystics prowling along the ridge north of my stable, taking my horses when they stray...

If you can get rid of those gnolls, my horses and I would be very grateful.

passages.title: A Baying of Gnolls
passages.text: Thank you for all your help, <name>.

passages.title: The Lost Tools
passages.text:
I could really use a hand here, <name>. With the town under siege, it's been hard to get supplies. My tools were being delivered from Goldshire by wagon but the bridge was blown out. We put the tools in a boat but the orcs hit it with a catapult. Just my luck, my toolbox sank right to the bottom of the lake.

Retrieve my toolbox, <name>, and I'll make it worth your while.

passages.title: The Lost Tools
passages.text: Were you able to find my tools?

passages.title: The Lost Tools
passages.text: Excellent recovery, <name>!  I never thought I'd see these tools again.

passages.title: Howling in the Hills
passages.text:
<name>, the gnolls are still out there. I can hear their baying as they hunt in the hills above Lakeshire. And one cry is louder than the rest - Yowler, their leader.

Kill Yowler and send his pack scattering! Bring me his paw as proof.

And be careful, this gnoll is their leader for a reason. He is no Mongrel...

passages.title: Howling in the Hills
passages.text: Yowler is a dangerous creature, <name>.  If you're not ready for him, I understand.

passages.title: Howling in the Hills
passages.text: Again, thank you for your help.  The Stormwind army is so busy dealing with the orcs, they don't have the troops to protect Redridge from local threats like the gnolls.

passages.title: Selling Fish
passages.text:
Lake Everstill is famous for its spotted sunfish. There's always demand for them...and I'm running low!

Bring me a batch of 10 and I'll barter well for them. If you can't fish yourself, then...maybe you can get them off the murlocs!

passages.title: Selling Fish
passages.text: You have some sunfish for me, eh?

passages.title: Selling Fish
passages.text: Pleasure doin' business with you, matey!

passages.title: Blackrock Bounty
passages.text:
The Blackrock Clan must be destroyed. The Enemy has invaded our lands. These mountains fall under the sovereign right of the King of Stormwind. Our sources tell us that the leaders of each unit within the Clan are known as Champions. You'll find them in their encampment to the north, just west of the road to the Burning Steppes.

Magistrate Solomon wants these foul brutes dead. Slay 15 Blackrock Champions and return to me.

passages.title: Blackrock Bounty
passages.text: I see you have fought valiantly against the Blackrock Clan, <class>.  Your service to our township is great indeed.

passages.title: A Free Lunch
passages.text:
Can you do me a favor? I've prepared a lunch for Guard Parker, but he's out on patrol...he's a big, strong Stormwind guard who can defend himself, but it's much too dangerous out there for a townsperson like me.

So if you deliver his lunch for me, then come back here and I'll give you a free lunch! Parker patrols the stretch of road leading to Duskwood.

passages.title: A Free Lunch
passages.text: Darcy sent me a lunch, did she?  Such a kind heart she has.  Well...let's have it!

passages.title: A Free Lunch
passages.text: Thanks, I could really use the meal.  Guarding Lakeshire from the orcs and gnolls is tough work!

passages.title: Visit the Herbalist
passages.text:
Before you go back to Darcy, can you bring her some flowers for me? You can get them at the herbalist shop back in Lakeshire, at the west end of town.

But when you get the flowers...don't tell the herbalist, Martie, whom they're from, or whom they're for...

passages.title: Visit the Herbalist
passages.text:
You need a bouquet of flowers?  You haven't been in town very long...have you already found for yourself a sweetheart here?

I know I shouldn't pry, but it's nice to see that love is in the air... especially in dangerous times like these.

passages.title: Delivering Daffodils
passages.text: Here is your bouquet. I chose Daffodils for you. They're my favorite!

passages.title: Delivering Daffodils
passages.text: Hello again, <name>.  Did Parker like the lunch I sent him?

passages.title: Delivering Daffodils
passages.text:
Oh, those are lovely!  I can't wait to put them in some water!

But...these are Martie's favorite flowers.  Parker didn't have you go to that jealous vixen for this bouquet, did he?  You didn't tell her who they were for, did you?  If you did, then it wouldn't surprise me if she poisoned them.

Oh, but it's not your fault.  Thank you, and here's your meal.

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text:
What I am about to tell you could cost me my life. The Defias gang is up to something big. Last I heard they were working in conjunction with various gnolls, kobolds and even goblins.

Take this note to Stoutmantle. It explains as much as I know on the subject.

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: Good to see you back, <name>.  What did Wiley have to say for himself?

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: Bah!  I should have let that scoundrel rot when I had the chance.  But this information is crucial.  Good work.

passages.title: Ghoulish Effigy
passages.text:
I live so far from the protection of town, it's a wonder the ghouls and the walking dead haven't eaten me! In fact, just yesterday a pack of Bone Chewers was pounding on the walls of my house!

I want to make an effigy - a kind of "scarecrow" for Ghouls. To do that I need some Ghoul Ribs. You can get them from Flesh Eaters, Bone Chewers, Brain Eaters, Rotted Ones and Plague Spreaders.

Get the ribs for me, and I will repay you with some coin.

passages.title: Ghoulish Effigy
passages.text: I think I hear a pack of Ghouls scurrying around the back of the house - I better put that effigy up quick!  Did you get those Ghoul Ribs for me?

passages.title: Ghoulish Effigy
passages.text: Ah, thanks.  These will do just the trick!

passages.title: Ogre Thieves
passages.text:
A few weeks ago I was picking herbs far from my house, and a band of ogres attacked me! I ran, and I was forced to leave behind a crate of precious tools and herbs.

After they chased me off, the ogres swaggered back to the ogre mound in southern Duskwood. I'm sure my crate is somewhere near the mound.

Please, <name>, retrieve this crate for me for I miss it sorely.

passages.title: Ogre Thieves
passages.text: Do you have my crate?  If so, then please...give it to me quickly!

passages.title: Ogre Thieves
passages.text:
Thank the Nec-...well, thank YOU, <name>!  You have more than earned your reward.

Aha!  Happy!  Happy nights ahead!!

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: I wonder what Wiley meant when he mentioned the Stonemasons. Perhaps that was a slip of tongue. Could the Defias gang be related to the Stonemasons? Only one man would know for sure: Mathias Shaw, head of SI:7. Show him Wiley's Note and see if he has anything to add to this growing mystery. If you have trouble finding Shaw, check the Barracks in Old Town.

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: What business do you have with me?  I am a very busy man. . .

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: This matter might be more complex than Stoutmantle realizes.

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text:
If ye be readin' this, it means that Ol' Captain Sanders is in a watery grave. So my treasure is yours now, ye jest need to follow the clues. 

First ye need to find me footlocker. It's probably half-buried in sand by now, along the Western Coast of Westfall near the shipwreck. There be lots of shipwrecks but only one rusty anchor on the coast. Find that anchor and you'll find me locker! Look in there for the next clue.

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: The footlocker slowly creaks open.  Sand and water seem to be its only contents. But wait!  A small crab scurries out with a clue to the treasure in his claws!

passages.title: <NYI> <TXT> Stormwind Commendation
Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: The clue to the treasure reads: Good work, matey! Now ye need to head due east. East up the bluffs, east to the road. Look for the ol' chimney ruins near the side of the road. There you'll find an old barrel with your next clue.

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: Good work, treasure hunter!

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: Searching through the barrel you discover another piece of parchment. This one reads: Now from this here barrel, face ye North. Straight as the crow flies, keep ye walkin' till you see the empty jug next to the lone windmill on the sea bluffs. If ye poke around that jug, ye just might find what you're lookin' for.

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: You're on your way to the jackpot, treasure seeker!

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: Sure enough, deep within the Old Jug there is another clue to Sanders' treasure. The ink has run in some places and the paper smells like whiskey but you can make out some of the text: Now that ye found me ol' whiskey jug, you're almost to the treasure! Just face West from the bottle and walk down to the shore. Once ye get to the water, keep going! Swim straight west till you find the island with me treasure chest!

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text:
The hinges on the old chest are rusty but they still work.  You force the chest open and take the booty.

Congratulations!

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text:
The Stonemasons' Guild was run by a man named Edwin VanCleef. VanCleef was responsible for rebuilding Stormwind after the orcs razed it in the First War. Apparently, VanCleef and his men were unhappy with their treatment by the King after the reconstruction was complete. That just might explain a thing or two.

I have written a more detailed account for your Master in Westfall. Take this to him at once!

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: Did Master Shaw shed any light on things?

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: Edwin VanCleef. . .I know the name well.  To think that a man so industrious and talented could turn into such a scoundrel unnerves me.  I'll need further proof before I believe this.

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: We need to discover the location of the Defias hideout. <name>, my scout reports that a Defias Messenger has been seen on the roads between Moonbrook, the Gold Coast Quarry and the Jangolode Mine. I want you to capture him. If he resists, kill him and bring me whatever he is carrying.

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: <name>, were you able to gather any information?  Did you locate the messenger?

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text:
This is indeed firm proof that VanCleef is in charge.  Now all we need to know is where the Defias gang is hiding out.

We've had a stroke of luck while you were gone.  We captured a thief trying to steal Saldean's wagon.  He has promised to lead us to the hideout in exchange for his life.  I want you to defend the traitor so he can reveal the hideout.  Return to me once you have uncovered the location.

passages.title: Messenger to Westfall
passages.text:
Something odd is afoot with the Stormwind Army. They should have been here in force by now. Time is a luxury we don't have, however. I will not stand by and watch the people of Lakeshire give their lives without trying to enlist more help. I've heard word of a people's militia forming in Westfall.

Take this plea to their leader, Gryan Stoutmantle. Perhaps Stoutmantle's men can lend some support here until the King sends reserves.

passages.title: Messenger to Westfall
passages.text: Hail, <class>.  What business do you have with The People's Militia?

passages.title: Messenger to Westfall
passages.text: Good Messenger, you have served your master well.

passages.title: Messenger to Westfall
passages.text:
Magistrate Solomon's note pains me to read. But it is obvious he knows not the war which is waged in Westfall or else he would know better than to expect aid from the Militia. If Stormwind had not deserted us as well, we would not have the need for the Militia.

Take this response to your master in Redridge, <class>. And let him know that my heart is heavy with the loss of good men.

passages.title: Messenger to Westfall
passages.text: Shall we expect the People's Militia soon?  Does Lord Stoutmantle's news bode well?

passages.title: Messenger to Westfall
passages.text:
I do say, this is not good at all.  I did not realize that Stoutmantle's situation was not unlike ours here in Lakeshire.  What action is so important that it calls the Stormwind Army away from its people?  Bah, I should not ponder aloud.

Here, messenger.  Accept these coins in exchange for your service to the Township.  I might call upon you again.

passages.title: Messenger to Darkshire
passages.text: I require your assistance once again. I have written to Lord Ebonlocke, requesting that he sends his trained guards, the Night Watch, to help with Lakeshire's defense. It is imperative this message makes it to him swiftly. You must exercise extreme caution. Ebonlocke is the mayor of Darkshire, in the heart of Duskwood. Do not stray from the roads.

passages.title: Messenger to Darkshire
passages.text: You appear to have traveled from afar, <class>.  What business do you have here in Darkshire?

passages.title: Messenger to Darkshire
passages.text: Thank you for making the long journey here.  This is indeed important information.

passages.title: Messenger to Darkshire
passages.text:
If I did not know Magistrate Solomon personally, I would say the man has gone mad. Send the Night Watch to Lakeshire because Stormwind refuses aid? The Night Watch was formed because Stormwind left us when this foul magic seeped into the land. If I sent my Night Watch, this town would be overrun by evil before the guards even reached the forest's edge.

Take this letter of response to your Master in Lakeshire.

passages.title: Messenger to Darkshire
passages.text: Ah, good to see you back, messenger.  Shall I inform the Marshal that the Night Watch is on its way from Darkshire?

passages.title: Messenger to Darkshire
passages.text:
By the Light!  The Stormwind Army retreated from Westfall.  And the Guard no longer protects Darkshire?  There is some treachery abound.  How could this be so? 

Oh I forgot to reward your service, <class>.  Here are some coins.  Now excuse me.  Something is amiss in Stormwind and I must get to the bottom of it.

passages.title: Manhunt
passages.text:
If the "Collector" is taking gold from our mines then he's stealing from the kingdom! Bring the Collector to justice, and bring me the ring mentioned in the pickup schedule you gave me. It may tell us whom the Collector is working for...

That Pickup Schedule says the Collector is hiding out at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. You should search for him there.

passages.title: Manhunt
passages.text: Did you find the Collector?  Did you discover whom he's working for?

passages.title: Manhunt
passages.text:
You found him?  Well done, <name>.  He won't be "collecting" from the Elwynn Mines again!

And this ring you found is interesting... it's a membership ring for the old Stonemason's Guild in Stormwind. I haven't seen one of these in years, since back in the days when the Defias Brotherhood used to infest this land.

passages.title: Supplies from Darkshire
passages.text:
Oh, what is a poor old man to do? I need some supplies from Darkshire, but the village is so far away and I am so old and feeble...I would never make the trip.

Can you go to Darkshire and bring me back some Ghost Hair Thread? You can get it from Madame Eva at her home on the Darkshire square.

passages.title: Supplies from Darkshire
passages.text: Ah, Ghost Hair Thread is what you need, is it?  I'm afraid I have none in stock, but I can make some for you...if you can supply the ghost hair.

passages.title: Ghost Hair Thread
passages.text:
There is a poor, sad spirit, Blind Mary, who haunts an old farm house in the hills south of Darkshire.

Here, take this Spectral Comb and ask Blind Mary to comb her hair. Then bring back the comb and I will glean from it the Ghost Hair I'll need for the thread.

And take care, for dark things now lurk near that house...

passages.title: Ghost Hair Thread
passages.text:
<Sob> Oh please, don't look at me!  I tore out these eyes with my own hands, but I can still feel your gaze!

I'm hideous!  Hideous!  Please, look away!!

passages.title: Ghost Hair Thread
passages.text:
What is this?  A comb?  It's lovely!  And it glides through my hair as if it weren't the stiff, stringy horror that it is.

Oh, if only I had a mirror...

passages.title: Murloc Poachers
passages.text:
Murlocs are becoming a problem. Larger groups of the fishmen are dropping anchor along the shores of Lake Everstill and fishing up a storm! We need them gone before they eat all the fish in the lake!

Hunt murlocs! Bring me eight of their fins and I might have something for you...

passages.title: Murloc Poachers
passages.text: Do you have those fins?  Hurry, we need those murlocs driven from the lake!

passages.title: Murloc Poachers
passages.text:
Well done, <name>.  I hope you didn't have too much trouble with those murlocs.

It's strange seeing them so far from the sea.  I wonder if they're here because they're running from something...

passages.title: Poor Old Blanchy
passages.text:
Poor Old Blanchy! Such a tired beast after all the work we put her through. I fed her before we left the farm, but we weren't expecting the wagon to break on us. If you could bring her a few handfuls of oats from the fields, I'd be grateful.

I bet you could find some around all of the farms in Westfall, if you can steer clear of those horrific machines that have taken over. There are several farms southwest of here.

passages.title: Poor Old Blanchy
passages.text: Old Blanchy is on her last leg.  Did you happen to find any oats for her?

passages.title: Poor Old Blanchy
passages.text: Thank you so much, <name>!  Poor Old Blanchy will be so happy!

passages.title: The Coast Isn't Clear
passages.text:
You probably noticed all of the shipwrecks along the coast. The Great Sea is treacherous indeed. The coast of Westfall needs to be kept clear, so that if sailors find their way to our beaches, they are safe. The Murlocs are trouble though.

Kill 7 Tidehunters, 7 Warriors, 7 Oracles and 7 Coastrunners and I will see to it that you are rewarded.

passages.title: The Coast Isn't Clear
passages.text: Well done, <name>.  You have quite a knack for combat.  Thanks to you the Coast of Westfall is a safer place.

passages.title: Red Leather Bandanas
passages.text:
The Defias Front is constantly shifting. I've been following their movements for quite some time now. On a side note, I've ascertained that many members of the gang can be tracked by the Red Leather Bandanas they wear.

Bring me 15 of these Bandanas and I'll see to it you are rewarded.

passages.title: Red Leather Bandanas
passages.text: Bring me 15 red leather bandanas and I'll pay you well.

passages.title: Red Leather Bandanas
passages.text: Nice work, <race>.  Please accept one of these items as payment for all your hard work.

passages.title: Return the Comb
passages.text:
NO!!!!!

Take it, take this comb away from me!

I'm a monster, and no one will ever think me lovely again!

passages.title: Return the Comb
passages.text: I sense that you have seen Blind Mary.  You have my Comb...?

passages.title: Return the Comb
passages.text: I can make a spool of Ghost Hair Thread with this, and have a few strands to spare.  Here are some coins for those extra strands.

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text:
So Stoutmantle sends a scrawny <race> like you to protect me? Guess you'll have to do. Better bring some friends too. 

You know the deal, right? You watch my back and I'll take you to the Defias hideout. But you better be close by my side. The Defias gang wants my head now. If they see me with you, they'll try to kill me.

Let me know when you and any friends you can round up are ready to go.

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: Most excellent, <name>!  VanCleef is as good as ours now that we know where he is hiding.

passages.title: Gather Rot Blossoms
passages.text:
If you bring me some rot blossoms then I can brew you up a batch of zombie juice.

rot blossoms grow in strange places. In particular, I hear you can find them inside the skulls of Skeletal Horrors and Skeletal Fiends... not that I've gotten close enough to look!

The Raven Hill Cemetery is lousy with those skeletons. You may as well get rid of them while you're looking for rot blossoms. The town of Darkshire would be grateful.

passages.title: Gather Rot Blossoms
passages.text: Hi, <name>.  Do you have those rot blossoms for me yet?

passages.title: Gather Rot Blossoms
passages.text:
Good,  you got the rot blossoms.  And I'll tell Althea Ebonlocke of the Night Watch that you were killing skeletons.

Keeping the people of Darkshire safe is a grim burden for the Night Watch, and news that others are helping stem the tide of fiends in Duskwood is welcome news indeed.

passages.title: Deliver the Thread
passages.text: Here is your thread, <name>. It has a thousand uses, from binding evil spirits to sewing life into inanimate objects.

passages.title: Deliver the Thread
passages.text: I need to string the Ghost Hair Thread along my door and my windows to keep out unwanted spirits.  Did you get it for me?

passages.title: Deliver the Thread
passages.text:
Delightful!  This will do splendidly...

Here, good <name>, take this as payment for your honorable deed.

passages.title: Zombie Juice
passages.text:
I need a bottle of a certain liquor - Zombie Juice. Tavernkeep Smitts at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire should have some.

And please hurry, <name>. These nights get cold, and I need that drink to put fire in my veins again!

passages.title: Zombie Juice
passages.text: You need some Zombie Juice, do you?  Hmm...that's some strong stuff - I don't usually get requests for it.

passages.title: Juice Delivery
passages.text:
Here's your Zombie Juice...

...and be careful with this stuff. It's strong enough to raise the dead!

passages.title: Juice Delivery
passages.text: I need that Zombie Juice to keep me warm on these cold, dark nights.  Did you get it for me?

passages.title: Juice Delivery
passages.text:
A thousand thanks, <name>.  You warm an old man's heart with your foolish-...I mean...with your kindness!

Here you are, friend.  Take this as a token of my gratitude.

passages.title: Note to the Mayor
passages.text:
Take this note to Ello Ebonlocke, the Mayor of Darkshire.

He and I are old friends...and when he reads it and discovers what you did for me...I'm sure he'll be just as happy as I am! Hahahaha!

passages.title: Note to the Mayor
passages.text:
Abercrombie...?  I don't know a person of that name.  You say you have a letter for me from this Abercrombie fellow?

Well let's have it then...

passages.title: Note to the Mayor
passages.text:
<Ello looks at the letter...>

What language is this?  It looks ancient...I can't read it.

passages.title: A Dark Threat Looms
passages.text:
If my suspicions are correct, this is some type of explosive powder. This must be analyzed by an explosives expert so we know just what we're dealing with here.

There's only one man for the job. Ashlan Stonesmirk was assigned to monitoring the ogres at the Mo'grosh Stronghold to the east. Head that direction and locate him so that he can shed some light on what this substance is.

passages.title: A Dark Threat Looms
passages.text: You say somethin', sonny?  Can't hear a bloody thing besides the ringin' in me ears.  Say, what's that you got there?

passages.title: A Dark Threat Looms
passages.text: Ah, well Ol' Hinderweir is wise to be worried.

passages.title: Rise of the Silithid
passages.text:
I urge you to take this report to someone who has working knowledge in this kind of thing.

I know this night elf scholar named Gracina Spiritmight. She's spent a lot of time studying life forms that are unique to the ecology of Azeroth; she's a historian to boot! If you want someone to help figure out what exactly this threat is, and more importantly how to stop it, give her the report. We'll need the help.

Last I heard, she was residing in the Temple of the Moon, located in Darnassus.

passages.title: Rise of the Silithid
passages.text: Peace and tranquility be upon you, stranger.  Why have you sought me out this day?

passages.title: Rise of the Silithid
passages.text:
This report... we night elves know of the terror mentioned here.  Fizzledowser was wise to send this, and you, to me.

These creatures will consume the Tanaris desert rapidly; they are nothing short of one of the greatest menaces we all will ever face.  Familiarize yourself with this name, <name>: silithid.  The insects mentioned here are the silithid, and they are the tools of one of the greatest threats that both the Horde and Alliance face.

If only we were smart enough to see that before.

passages.title: Raven Hill
passages.text:
Something's amiss at Raven Hill, <name>. Calor swears that someone--or something--is haunting the buildings there. Two nights running he's noticed the shadows moving, and the third before that he says he saw light in one of the windows.

If, as you say, you care about the safety of Duskwood, find out what monster haunts in Raven Hill.

passages.title: Raven Hill
passages.text: No! Please don't kill me! It's just me... Jitters!! They're everywhere... I can't escape them! Monsters in Raven Hill? N-n-n-o... couldn't be. Only harmless Jitters.

passages.title: Deliveries to Sven
passages.text:
Do you know Sven? Now, there is a man who does the work of the Light! He and his followers keep a camp at the northwestern edge of Duskwood.

Unfortunately, because they are so few, they cannot even spare a man to fetch supplies from town. Will you deliver these supplies to him?

passages.title: Deliveries to Sven
passages.text: You look a sturdy type, <class>. Have you come to join our fight?

passages.title: Deliveries to Sven
passages.text: These supplies will be most useful. The aid of the Carevin family is always appreciated. Here is a little something for your trouble.

passages.title: The Hermit
passages.text: There was an old man who used to come into town to buy supplies rather frequently, but I haven't seen him for quite some time now. He lives out in a shack overlooking Raven Hill cemetery, if I remember correctly. Perhaps you should go see if something is amiss.

passages.title: The Hermit
passages.text:
Elaine Carevin? Hehe, oh yes... of course, the Carevins.

No, nothing's wrong but it is hard for me to go into town now. The roads are dangerous and I'm not getting any younger. Maybe you can do an old man some favors?

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: There is but one task left for you to complete. Edwin VanCleef must be assassinated. While it saddens me to condemn any man to a death sentence, it is for the greater good of the people of Westfall that VanCleef is laid to rest once and for all. Bring me the villain's head once the deed is done.

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text: How goes the hunt for Edwin VanCleef?

passages.title: The Defias Brotherhood
passages.text:
<name>, your bravery is remarkable.  The People's Militia thanks you for your service to the people of Westfall.  With VanCleef dead, this marks the beginning of the end for the Defias Brotherhood.  Hopefully some day soon peace will once again grace the plains of this fair land.

I salute you, Sir!

passages.title: Oh Brother. . .
passages.text:
We were deep in a vast mine in Westfall, hidden beneath a barn in Moonbrook. No clue where these stinkin' thieving types came from. Anyway, the mine tunnel collapsed on us. I got out but the others... well... the others haven't been heard from.

You look like you might have better luck in there. If you could look for my brother, I'd be thankful. He always carried his Explorers' League Badge. If you can't find him, that badge would at least give me some peace of mind.

passages.title: Oh Brother. . .
passages.text: Did you find any sign of my brother?  Is there any hope after all this time?

passages.title: Oh Brother. . .
passages.text: My suspicions were correct.  My poor brother.... Well, thank you for bringing some conclusion to this mystery, even if the conclusion was grim.

passages.title: Collecting Memories
passages.text: Many of my friends perished that horrible day when the mine tunnel caved in. If your adventures happen to bring you into that wing of the mine in Moonbrook, please keep an eye out for any sign which might identify them. If you come across any of their Miners' Union Cards, bring them back to me and I'll make sure their families get some resolution from this horrible accident.

passages.title: Collecting Memories
passages.text: Were you able to retrieve any of my old co-worker's Miners' Union Cards?

passages.title: Collecting Memories
passages.text: Thank you for collecting these, <name>.  Your efforts will help bring peace to the dead in the wake of this tragedy.  I will see to it that the families are notified.

passages.title: Wanted: Gath'Ilzogg
passages.text:
Wanted! Gath'Ilzogg, Leader of the Blackrock attacks on Stonewatch Keep and raids against the township of Lakeshire. 

Gath'Ilzogg is extremely dangerous. He is reportedly holed up in the recently conquered keep plotting the Blackrock clan's further crimes against humanity. The orc infestation must be quelled at all costs. A gracious reward will be given to whatever brave soul can deliver the head of Gath'Ilzogg to Magistrate Solomon.

passages.title: Wanted: Gath'Ilzogg
passages.text: What do you have there, <race>?

passages.title: Wanted: Gath'Ilzogg
passages.text: Fantastic work, <name>!  Gath'Ilzogg led those brutes into battle, killing many innocent humans.  Vindication is ours.  This is the first step in reclaiming the keep for the kingdom of Stormwind!

passages.title: A New Threat
passages.text:
I hope you're here to lend us a hand, <class>. After the last trogg attack, we could use all the help we can get.

I hear the buggers have been popping up all across the lands, and it seems Coldridge Valley is no exception. They've been spotted all over the hills to the southeast and near the frozen lake.

And that's not all, just a few nights ago, they attacked and overran our camp to the west! 

We're a bit shorthanded here, <lad/lass>, and we need strong arms to help drive the troggs back.

passages.title: A New Threat
passages.text: If the problems we've had here are indicative of what is happening elsewhere in our lands, by Magni's beard, we have some troubles ahead of us! I can only hope that the king and Senate are taking steps to deal with the threat the troggs pose.

passages.title: A Warden of the Alliance
passages.text:
You have been so very kind to me, <name>. I never dreamed that I'd have so much fun during Children's Week. Thank you.

I wish all the orphans were lucky enough to get to do the stuff we did. Do you think we could find Craggle Wobbletop again and get a foam sword rack from him? I think he's still pushing that cart in the Canals outside the Trade District. That way, everyone else at the orphanage could do something fun too!

After that, it'll be time for me to go home.

passages.title: A Warden of the Alliance
passages.text: It is a pleasure to see you again, <name>.  Have you attended to the duties you've volunteered for during Children's Week?

passages.title: A Warden of the Alliance
passages.text:
What's this? A gift for all the orphans!

May the heavens bless you, <name>.  You've done more for Randis than most would ever think of doing for him.  Thank you - you're a shining star in the skies of the Alliance.

Randis had so much fun with you, <name>.  He wanted to give you one of his favorite pets to remember him by.

passages.title: Children's Week
passages.text:
You're willing to help us here at the orphanage? Bless you, friend; your aid during Children's Week will be invaluable.

Take this whistle. You will only be able to use it for a short amount of time - typically not longer than Children's Week itself. When you use it, you will be able to talk with the child you've agreed to look after. Using it again will dismiss the child.

By all means <name> - use the whistle and meet your ward! I'm sure the child will be most eager to meet you.

passages.title: Children's Week
passages.text:
Zug zug!  My name is Grunth, and I guess you're looking after me?  You're an adventurer, like my mom and dad were.  My matron says that they died with honor in battle.  I'm happy to meet you.

I hope we'll do plenty of things together.  I have some things I'd like to do, and the matron says you'll be like a big brother to me during this week.  I'd like that a whole bunch.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text:
Darkness seems drawn inexorably to Duskwood. Master Carevin's quest is the expulsion of evil and heresy. Through our efforts are the people of Darkshire kept safe.

You believe yourself worthy to join us?

I once thought as you. Disillusioned by the complacency of the Watch, I joined Master Carevin. If you wish to prove yourself, it will not be through words.

Test your skills against the Nightbane Shadow Weaver worgen in Brightwood Grove--bright, hah!--and the Rotting Orchard.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text:
Impressive, <name>. It would seem that you are capable enough to handle yourself. Perhaps a more suitable challenge could be found for one of your abilities.

It is curious though... The worgen seemed to just appear out of thin air. But then, with all the other strange creatures that have moved across our borders, I suppose it's only one of many concerns.

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Look To The Stars
passages.text:
My Gnomish friend, Cog, has promised to help me build a device which will let me peer towards the stars. A truth exists, beyond magic, that can explain the strange transformation in the forest.

Bring to me a bronze tube made by a skilled engineer. That is the first step, according to Cog's blueprint.

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Look To The Stars
passages.text: Have you found a skilled engineer to create a bronze tube yet?

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Look To The Stars
passages.text: This is perfect, <name>.  The first step is complete!

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Look To The Stars
passages.text: According to Cog's blueprint, what I need now is a way to reflect light. I remember a woman by the name of Mary who became well known around these parts for always carrying a looking glass. Perhaps you can track Mary down and see if she might lend us a reflective surface for this project? I believe she once resided in southern Duskwood. . .

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Look To The Stars
passages.text: Why yes, I used to own a looking glass.

passages.title: WANTED: "Hogger"
passages.text:
Wanted: Hogger

A huge gnoll, Hogger, is prowling the woods in southwestern Elwynn. He has overpowered all attempts at his capture.

The Stormwind Army has placed a generous bounty on the Gnoll. To earn the reward, bounty hunters should venture into the woods and deal with the beast.

passages.title: WANTED: "Hogger"
passages.text:
He did WHAT?

 Great, now we have a bloodthirsty beast right beneath the streets of Stormwind, with a whole army of gnolls at his command.  Definitely an improvement, I feel safer already. 

 Here's your reward, <name>.  But promise me you'll check in with the Stockades guards in Stormwind at some point, just to ensure that things are going smoothly.

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Look To The Stars
passages.text: The looking glass was one of my finest treasures until. . .the incident. After that happened, I discarded it behind the barn. There was an Insane Ghoul who used to roam back there. Perhaps he picked it up. Rumor has it the devilish beast resides in the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery.

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Look To The Stars
passages.text: I showed Cog the beginnings of our star-viewing machine.  He was impressed.  Did you happen to find a reflective device?

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Look To The Stars
passages.text: Most superb!  This will work perfectly.  Many thanks!

passages.title: Theocritus' Retrieval
passages.text:
<You hear a disembodied voice...>

Do not be alarmed. I am Theocritus, High Mage of Tower Azora in Elwynn Forest. The pendant you are holding is a method of communication between the Shadowhide Gnolls and their master, Morganth.

Through months of research, I believe I too can communicate through these pendants. If you can hear this message, then my spell was a success.

Bring me this pendant and I will reward you for the service.

passages.title: Theocritus' Retrieval
passages.text: I spoke to you through a pendant, you say?  Hmm...give it to me, so that I might study it.

passages.title: Theocritus' Retrieval
passages.text:
You have my gratitude, <name>.  I sent that message to the Shadowhide Pendants weeks ago and had believed it a failure.  But it seems the spell did reach at least some pendants, after a significant delay.

In time I hope to learn how to send an attack through the pendants, to immobilize any Shadowhide Gnolls who wear them.

But before that is possible, I'm afraid that much more research is required.

passages.title: Dwarven Outfitters
passages.text:
What do we have here? You look as though you might need something to keep your hands warm, hm?

I'll tell you what would help: a pair of nice, warm gloves. And, being the kind soul that I am, I'd be more than happy to provide you with a suitable pair. I've one condition, however.

I need you to go get me some wolf meat. Nice arrangement, hm? You bring me some wolf meat, and I'll make sure you don't lose any digits to frostbite. Well, what do you say?

passages.title: Dwarven Outfitters
passages.text: Wolves giving you a bit of trouble? You'd do well to avoid the fangs and claws and other sharp bits, yes?

passages.title: Dwarven Outfitters
passages.text: Ah! Wonderful. The wolf meat should do nicely. Oh, don't worry, <name>, I wouldn't forget my part of the bargain. Here, one of these should fit you.

passages.title: Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore
passages.text:
Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore

Known leader of the Shadowhide Gnoll Clan, working under the enemy of the Township and Kingdom, Morganth. By mandate of Magistrate Solomon, this vile betrayer of Stormwind is wanted dead. Show his paw to the Magistrate as proof of his death.

passages.title: Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore
passages.text: What news do you bring before the Court?

passages.title: Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore
passages.text: So the evil Lieutenant Fangore is dead?  Good riddance to that foul creature.  You are very brave, <class>.  The Township of Lakeshire thanks you for your aid.

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Look To The Stars
passages.text:
Now there is just one more item needed to complete this device. Cog's blueprint calls for a lens of some sort. The only lens I know of that would be large enough will be very difficult to acquire.

There is an ogre by the name of Zzarc'Vul who resides in the mound in southern Duskwood. If you can, bring to me his monocle and I will use that as our lens!

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Look To The Stars
passages.text: Were you able to convince Zzarc'Vul to lend us his monocle for our experiment?

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Look To The Stars
passages.text: At last!  The stargazing device is complete!  Thank you, <name>.  Now I can continue my research. . .

passages.title: The Troll Menace
passages.text:
The trolls're acting up. More than usual, I'd say. We've seen them put together war parties before, but this time it's... different.

What matters most, however, is the continued protection of Anvilmar. I've no intention to let these trolls flank Anvilmar while its attention is turned towards troggs. Go thin their ranks a bit. They need to know that we're still not without defenses.

passages.title: The Troll Menace
passages.text: Hopefully that did the trick.  Anvilmar will be safe from trolls for the time being.  Now, to find out what it is that has the trolls so agitated.

passages.title: The Boar Hunter
passages.text:
Nothing like a day of boar hunting, eh?

Though, here in Coldridge Valley, there are so many boars it almost takes the fun out of it. No need to get them charging. They're all angry and ready without any help. In fact, recently, there've been so many boars in the area, it's become dangerous for me to do my daily hunting.

Long story short, if you could help me kill some of the boars, I would appreciate it.

passages.title: The Boar Hunter
passages.text: Excellent! I can go back to my... leisurely... hunting now. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Furlbrow's Deed
passages.text:
This is an old deed to an expanse of farmlands within Westfall. It is signed by a Theodore Furlbrow and cosigned by his wife, Verna. And on the back of the deed are hastily scrawled words:

"We leaned on Furlbrow and got his deed. Thought it might be handy if you wanted to forge one of these for your own place.

The Furlbrows won't give us trouble. Last I saw them they were on their way out of Westfall, stuck with a broken wagon."

You think the Furlbrows might want their deed back...

passages.title: Furlbrow's Deed
passages.text: We don't need any civilian vigilante types getting involved, kid. Leave this one to the professionals.

passages.title: Furlbrow's Deed
passages.text:
This is useless. Look at the date on this letter. The Furlbrows have been squatting on the Jansen Stead for five years.

They never could quite get their wagon... fixed.

passages.title: Tiger Hunting
passages.text:
When I was but a young girl, my father trained me in the art of tiger hunting.

You'll find the young felines much easier to track and slay. One can often find young tigers near the expedition camp.

Test your tracking skills and see if you can hunt some of the beasts down. Start your hunt near our camp, to the south.

passages.title: Tiger Hunting
passages.text: You have finished with the young tigers... but the thrill of the hunt still holds you captive.

passages.title: Tiger Stalking
passages.text:
Young tigers are one thing. Fully-grown cats are another. Hunting the grown Stranglethorn tigers will prove an even greater challenge.

The adult cats normally spend their days south of Kurzen's Compound, east of the river.

passages.title: Tiger Stalking
passages.text: Tiger blood coats your hands, your weapons, and your <class> garb.  Yet still you crave more.

passages.title: Tiger Prowess
passages.text:
Elder Stranglethorn tigers are the strongest of the bunch. More than one <race> <class> has seen <his/her> own demise at the tip of those razor-sharp teeth and heavy claws.

Ajeck will be thrilled to know that you have bested them. The largest pack of these elders can be found to the south, near the Sundering, on the border of the Cape of Stranglethorn.

passages.title: Tiger Prowess
passages.text:
You have defeated the strongest tigers in Stranglethorn.  You have become a great tiger hunter, and have every right to stop your hunt right here and now.

Something tells you, however, that a stronger cat still waits for you within that jungle...

passages.title: Tiger Mastery
passages.text:
Legends speak of an elusive tigress... a feline so powerful that she dwarfs even the elder males. The hunters at Nesingwary's Expedition have hunted for her without success. Many of them have fallen prey to her raking claws, their bodies now decaying at the foot of her hill, north of Grom'gol.

They call the beast Sin'Dall.

You resolve to do what no <race> has done before: hunt, kill, and claim the paw of Sin'Dall.

passages.title: Tiger Mastery
passages.text: How goes the hunt?

passages.title: Tiger Mastery
passages.text: Most impressive, I do say!  I send you out to defeat the kittens, and you return with a paw the size of a gnome!  You are a true Master Tiger Hunter, <name>!

passages.title: Bloodscalp Ears
passages.text:
Damn trolls! They've been killing off our agents in the jungle! I've already lost a good number of my best guards to skirmishes with them. The costs are piling up! How will I explain this to Baron Revilgaz?

Decisive action... Think, Kebok... you weren't assigned to the post you have today for sitting around... I've got it! You... <name>, is it? You'll help me, won't you? There's money to be had!

Here's the deal... you bring me the ears of fifteen Bloodscalp Trolls, and I'll compensate you well.

passages.title: Bloodscalp Ears
passages.text:
You've had success I hope? All over the place, those trolls. Filthy devils.

Oh yes, that reminds me! Be sure to tell your friends, yes? We could use much assistance!

passages.title: Bloodscalp Ears
passages.text:
Oh excellent, excellent. That'll help a little, for the present...

<He trails off, grumbling about profit margins and costs...>

What? You're still here? Reward? Oh, right... of course, here, take this... it should be more than enough.

passages.title: Panther Hunting
passages.text:
If you want to be a part of the hunt with this crack group under Hemet Jr.'s leadership, you're going to need to prove yourself an able panther hunter. You should start out easy: just focus on the young panthers for now. As you improve and gain experience as a hunter, you will undoubtedly find increasingly dangerous quarry.

Start by heading east. Return to me when you are a master panther hunter.

passages.title: Panther Hunting
passages.text: You feel more experienced already.  Perhaps it's time to move on to bigger prey.

passages.title: Panther Stalking
passages.text:
The youngest panthers fell easily before you. panthers that have come of age will naturally be stronger, and quicker, and more difficult to defeat.

Larger panther tracks lead to the west.

passages.title: Panther Stalking
passages.text: You take a moment to silently congratulate yourself on your panther hunting so far.

passages.title: Panther Prowess
passages.text:
Now the hard part. As panthers grow older, they become more wily, blending in with their environment and becoming difficult to spot. These cunning panthers are known by the name "shadowmaw", for their tendency to suddenly appear out of the darkness... with a waiting mouth full of teeth.

If you want to prove yourself as a true panther hunter, shadowmaws are the only way to do so. They prowl to the southeast, across the river.

passages.title: Panther Prowess
passages.text: The shadowmaw panthers proved no match for your skills as a hunter.  Only one task remains.

passages.title: Panther Mastery
passages.text:
You've almost proven yourself to be a master hunter of panthers. Yet there is one panther which has eluded your grasp.

Songs are sung about a mighty panther by the name of Bhag'thera. You will see if you can use your skills to kill the great beast.

Bringing the Fang of Bhag'thera to Erlgadin should be proof enough that you are a master panther hunter.

passages.title: Panther Mastery
passages.text: You're still alive!  Excellent!  How fares the hunt?

passages.title: Panther Mastery
passages.text: So the great Bhag'thera is dead!  Cheers to you, <name>.  You are a mighty <class> indeed!

passages.title: Raptor Hunting
passages.text:
So you think your hunting skills are in tip-top shape? I can put them to the test in a jiffy. Head out into that jungle and kill ten Stranglethorn raptors. We'll see just how much of a big game hunter you are.

And no, I won't tell you where you can find them! Locating the beasts is half the challenge.

Okay, go west.

passages.title: Raptor Hunting
passages.text: Stranglethorn raptors were not a problem for a wily <class> like you.

passages.title: Raptor Stalking
passages.text:
It is time to step up the challenge. Venturing into the jungle and bagging 10 lashtail raptors should be sufficient. They will certainly be stronger than the raptors you have already disposed of.

The lashtail raptors mainly stay southeast of here, near the Kal'ai Ruins.

passages.title: Raptor Stalking
passages.text: Hemet Nesingwary Jr. doubted you, but his doubts were unfounded.  You are absolutely destroying these raptors.

passages.title: Raptor Prowess
passages.text:
A particularly cagey brand of raptor, known by locals as the "Jungle Stalker", prowls the forests to the south, across the river. They are far more difficult to track down and kill than the other breeds you've been trying your luck at.

Killing these Jungle Stalkers will undoubtedly make for a good tale around the fire.

passages.title: Raptor Prowess
passages.text:
You are no longer just a raptor hunter.  You are an honest-to-goodness raptor SLAYER.

Though one fabled raptor still eludes you...

passages.title: Raptor Mastery
passages.text:
Before returning to Nesingwary's Expedition, you will have to complete the impossible: hunt the raptor that no other hunter has been able to capture. That beast goes by the name of Tethis, and he's been known to terrorize the southeastern corner of Northern Stranglethorn.

Bringing Tethis' talon back to that dwarf hunter should be proof that you are no ordinary <race>.

passages.title: Raptor Mastery
passages.text: Ah, so you're hunting Tethis?  Tracked her all the way back to camp, did you?

passages.title: Raptor Mastery
passages.text:
Master <name>, the raptor slayer!

Has a nice ring to it, eh?

passages.title: Supplies to Private Thorsen
passages.text:
Hmm. Yes, I do have something you could do, actually. Lieutenant Doren and his followers up in the north need their regular supplies from us.

They haven't been delivered, and with the trolls attacking, I'll need someone to do it. Doren's camp lies northwest of the road at the entrance to Stranglethorn from Duskwood. Give the supplies to Private Thorsen, if he's not in the camp, then he'll be patrolling south of it. He'll take care of them.

Mind you, if you fail, you'll owe me restitution.

passages.title: Supplies to Private Thorsen
passages.text: Yes? What do you want? Oh, supplies from the goblins. Strange seeing a <race> delivering them, usually they send their own. No matter... you didn't touch them did you? Good good... we wouldn't want anything to happen to our mines, oh no.

passages.title: Supplies to Private Thorsen
passages.text: These land mines will help us defend ourselves from that animal Kurzen and his men. Thank you for bringing them. If you need further work, I can probably find something for you to do. And you won't have to deal with those goblins, hm?

passages.title: A Dark Threat Looms
passages.text: You take a sample of the strange smelling powder.

passages.title: A Dark Threat Looms
passages.text: Did you happen to discover any clues, <name>?

passages.title: A Dark Threat Looms
passages.text: This is an alarming discovery, to say the least!

passages.title: Bookie Herod
passages.text:
If Kurzen knows Thorsen's secret, then we have a spy in our midst. We must determine how the secret was leaked!

Thorsen's contact within Kurzen's camp was Bookie Herod. Herod is Kurzen's logistics officer and knows everything about the running of Kurzen's Compound. If you can get Herod's notes or records, maybe we can find out how Thorsen was discovered.

When we were still with Kurzen, Bookie's office was on the top floor of the camp's only two-story house. His records are probably still there.

passages.title: Bookie Herod
passages.text:
These are Bookie Herod's notes and records.

Among them are: a list of supplies within the camp, material requests from Colonel Kurzen, and various letters and correspondences.

passages.title: Investigate the Camp
passages.text:
I've gotten reports of a group of hunters that have set up camp upriver of the Venture Company mining camp on Lake Nazferiti. Now, normally I wouldn't care, but improbably, I heard that Hemet Nesingwary Jr. was one of the hunters there. He's certainly well-connected, if you catch my meaning, and you never can be too safe.

Why don't you go check out the camp, <name>, see what they're about?

passages.title: Investigate the Camp
passages.text: Hmmm, so my information was correct, as usual.  Interesting.  Well, I don't suppose they pose any sort of threat of interference with our operation, but perhaps they have a need for some of our excellent manufactured products.  Hmmm...

passages.title: Colonel Kurzen
passages.text:
You have proven yourself time and again, and your resourcefulness seems to rival even that of Kurzen himself. You may be the salvation of our band of rebels...if you can pit yourself against Kurzen and prevail!

He commands his men from deep within the Stockpile. You must enter that cave, brave through his defenders, and face Kurzen and his leaders.

Farewell, <name>. My hope, and the fate of my men, go with you.

passages.title: Colonel Kurzen
passages.text: Dare I hope that Kurzen and his defenders are dead, <name>?

passages.title: Colonel Kurzen
passages.text:
I dared not believe the reports, but you bring us proof that...Kurzen and his leaders are defeated.  You have saved us!

These jungles are filled with menaces of all types, but none had the cruel intellect of Kurzen.  We may all breathe easier now that he is gone.

passages.title: The Second Rebellion
passages.text:
We're fighting a losing battle with Colonel Kurzen. Not only is he a brilliant tactician, he outnumbers us at least 10 to 1! To survive, we need to use his own, covert tactics against him.

Enter his camp to the east and kill his men. Lots of them. And get out before reinforcements can close on you.

passages.title: The Second Rebellion
passages.text:
Well done.  The loss of those Jungle Fighters will relieve some of the pressure on our camp.

But now that you've had a taste of the forces we're up against, do you still want to throw your lot in with us??

passages.title: Bad Medicine
passages.text:
To have a chance against Kurzen, we need his healing support neutralized. He has gathered a large number of medicine men who heal his forces with jungle remedies and poison our fighters with venom fern extracts.

We need those remedies and extracts for our own. Search the Kurzen Compound - his medicine men and jungle fighters will have the remedies, and the extracts are probably stowed in some of the camp's supply boxes.

passages.title: Bad Medicine
passages.text: I'm waiting on those remedies and that extract, <name>.

passages.title: Bad Medicine
passages.text: Well done, <name>.  These remedies will keep more of us alive and in fighting shape.  And the extracts will help us create our own remedies.

passages.title: Troll Witchery
passages.text: While I study those legends you acquired, gather for me implements of evil troll magic. Enter the territory of the Skullsplitter trolls, a second tribe to the distant south, and acquire Skullsplitter Fetishes from their Witchdoctors and Mystics.

passages.title: Troll Witchery
passages.text: Do you have those fetishes, <name>?  They might hold the secret to Kurzen's degradation...I must know!

passages.title: Troll Witchery
passages.text: Thank you.  I will study these fetishes and see if they hold the secret of Kurzen's fall into evil.

passages.title: Mai'Zoth
passages.text:
Kurzen may be dead, but...that which drove him to evil still lives! Through my studies I have discovered this: An Ogre Mage - Mai'Zoth - dwells in an Ogre Mound within the eastern mountains of Stranglethorn. He is rumored to employ mind-controlling magic, and I am positive that he corrupted Kurzen.

If Mai'Zoth is allowed to live, then his evil may influence others, and may even cause another Kurzen to surface.

Kill him, and bring me his Mind's Eye, the artifact he uses to corrupt others.

passages.title: Mai'Zoth
passages.text: I give you my blessing.  Mai'Zoth's strength is matched only by his evil.

passages.title: Mai'Zoth
passages.text:
Aha!  You've done it!  You are a great force for good, <name>, and may your strength never fade!

I will study this Mind's Eye and determine if it may be used for good.  If not...then it must be destroyed.

passages.title: Kurzen's Mystery
passages.text:
Colonel Kurzen was once a great, noble man - I must find what caused his fall into depravity! He may be under the sway of troll magic. To confirm this, I must study some of their legends.

There are 4 tablets hidden within the troll ruins of Stranglethorn. I must see what is written on these tablets! Transcribe their markings and bring the transcriptions back to me.

The first tablet is in the Bal'lal Ruins, the second is in the Vile Reef, and the third and fourth are in the Ruins of Zul'Kunda.

passages.title: Kurzen's Mystery
passages.text: <name>!  Do you have the troll legends?  I must know their secrets!

passages.title: Kurzen's Mystery
passages.text: Thank you, <name>.  I will study these legends to see if there is some link between the trolls and the evil that has possessed Colonel Kurzen.

passages.title: Big Game Hunter
passages.text:
<name>, you are a hunter worthy of our company. From the battlefields of Lordaeron to the deepest jungle, I have rarely witnessed such prowess with weaponry as you have demonstrated.

You have killed the ferocious Sin'Dall, the elusive Bhag'thera, and the treacherous Tethis. But the true prize is the head of King Bangalash. That white tiger is the reason I am here... yet still, he taunts me from his roost to the south. Kill King Bangalash and your hunting prowess is proven to be second to none.

passages.title: Big Game Hunter
passages.text: I see you're back, old bloke.  King Bangalash has caused me to come crawling back to camp many times.  Hang in there.

passages.title: Big Game Hunter
passages.text:
Bloody well done!  Right-o!  Congratulations, <name>, for succeeding where others have failed.

I am honored to count you as a comrade of our great hunting party here.  No one will ever doubt your expertise in hunting and tracking!

Cheers to you, I say!  Cheers!

passages.title: Skullsplitter Tusks
passages.text:
It's expensive and hard to kill enough tigers to support the export of tiger fangs to the islands in the South Seas. Luckily, we've developed a technique that allows us to take mundane horn-like objects and turn them into undetectable forgeries.

The closest match we've found, amazingly, are the tusks of the Skullsplitter trolls.

Hey, before you say anything, what the buyer doesn't know doesn't hurt them, am I right? Bring me a large number of them so we can get to work on the monthly shipment!

passages.title: Skullsplitter Tusks
passages.text: Tough buggers, aren't they? Well, have you had any luck? Sorry to seem impatient, but this has been a huge thorn in my side! Well?

passages.title: Skullsplitter Tusks
passages.text: Ah, good work, good work! Ugh, though you could have done a better job cleaning off the-- Well, no matter, no matter! My thanks to you, <name>, our operation will no doubt see increased output and productivity thanks to your help! Good good, now, onto other matters...

passages.title: Krazek's Cookery
passages.text:
I do most of the cooking at the camp. And it used to be a lot of work, until I bought a mechanical cooking pot from a goblin merchant in Booty Bay. The pot is a wonder! It saved me countless hours...until it broke!

Can you take the pot back to the goblin for me so he can fix it? His name is Krazek.

passages.title: Krazek's Cookery
passages.text: Hello!  You brought me something?

passages.title: Krazek's Cookery
passages.text:
Oh I see, it's a Krazek's Crock Pot!  An ingenious piece of work, but it can break a spring or throw a gear now and then.  Let me see what's wrong with this one...

Aha!  Its steam charger is rusted out, it has a cracked knuckle-gasket and its fobulator is missing teeth.  I'm surprised the pot could even boil a turnip in this state!

Can I fix it?  Of course I can fix it!

But there's a price.  Oh yes, there is always a price...

passages.title: Alas, Andorhal
passages.text:
Alas, the time to attack Andorhal and drive out the lich that controls it is upon us!

Inside the ruins of the city is where the lich - Araj the Summoner - holds dominion. He is guarded by numerous Scourge surrounding the remains of city's center, and his personal retinue of guardians attached to him directly is formidable. You will need numerous allies to even stand a chance of facing him successfully.

Destroy Araj, <name>, and bring me a shard from his phylactery as proof!

passages.title: Alas, Andorhal
passages.text: Your task has been given to you, <name>.  Do you have a shard from the lich's phylactery as proof of the task being accomplished?

passages.title: Alas, Andorhal
passages.text:
You've done it!  Araj... the lich is finally defeated!

You've done a tremendous service to the Alliance on this day, <name>.  Your bravery and perseverance are a testament to what it means to be a true hero.  Please - accept this as a token for all to see and know that you have delivered the Alliance a victory for the ages!

passages.title: A Meal Served Cold
passages.text:
One of my most famous dishes is Chilled Basilisk in Lime Vinaigrette. But the problem is... the meat is impossible to keep fresh, and I must serve the dish tonight for a noble's birthday!

So if you can bring me a Chilled Basilisk Haunch from a freshly-killed Cold Eye Basilisk, quickly, then I will owe you a king's feast!

Cold Eye Basilisks are known to roam along the beach dunes of northwestern Stranglethorn, so you have much traveling to do. And be swift!

passages.title: A Meal Served Cold
passages.text: <name>!  Do you have that haunch?  I must begin preparing it soon, or the banquet will be ruined!

passages.title: A Meal Served Cold
passages.text:
Ah, this will do nicely!  Many, many thanks!

Now if you'll excuse me, I must get the haunch chopped, marinated and garnished for the banquet.

passages.title: Hostile Takeover
passages.text:
He's done it this time! Bad enough that Gelriz's muscling out the moguls who were appointed by the trade princes, now he tries to cut in on the most notorious pirate!

Revilgaz won't have it, and he's told me to take care of the problem in my own way.

My way? Theft. The Venture Co. geologists near Lake Nazferiti are deeply interested in those strange blue crystals they have been finding in the mines. Bring me samples of the stone from their geologists, I don't care what you have to do to get them.

passages.title: Hostile Takeover
passages.text:
I need those stones, <name>. By whatever means necessary! Just do it, don't give me the details!

It's about results, <name>, nothing more, nothing less.

passages.title: Hostile Takeover
passages.text: Fascinating. That the crystals have been tumbled using this process can only indicate that they are planning to use them as some sort of fuel or other catalyst. I don't know much more than that. Samples will have to be dispatched to Head Chemist Gigglefont.

passages.title: Red Silk Bandanas
passages.text:
It's no secret that the trademark of the Defias Gang is their Red Bandanas. But we've learned that the material from which these bandanas are made signifies the member's rank.

That being said, I want you to eliminate as many high ranking Defias members as you can. The highest ranking members will undoubtedly be found in VanCleef's secret hideout. When you're done bring me 10 Red Silk Bandanas as proof of their deaths and I will reward you. Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Red Silk Bandanas
passages.text: Have you been reclaiming our land from the Defias gang?  If so show me 10 Red Silk Bandanas as proof.

passages.title: Red Silk Bandanas
passages.text: Well done, <name>!  On behalf of The People's Militia I salute you for your efforts.  Soon we will return this land to the people with help from brave souls like you.

passages.title: Jungle Secrets
passages.text:
Thank you for saving me, <name>. I know how this looks, but...allow me to explain.

I was charged by Lieutenant Doren to re-enlist with Kurzen's men, so that I might spy on them and bring sorely needed intelligence to the rebels. You saw here what I had thought would be my chance to infiltrate Kurzen's Compound. I was wrong, and again, thanks for saving me.

This was a top secret mission, so you must tell no one. But if you speak with Doren he will explain.

passages.title: Jungle Secrets
passages.text:
Yes, what Thorsen told you is true.  You must be discrete with this.  At one time, we rebels were fiercely loyal to Colonel Kurzen.  But such was Kurzen's corruption, our passion twisted into rage.   If it was made known that Private Thorsen has had recent dealings with Kurzen's men, then one night he would find himself with a slit throat.

To my knowledge, only Sergeant Yohwa, Thorsen and I were privy to Thorsen's mission.  But there must be another.  A traitor.

passages.title: Between a Rock and a Thistlefur
passages.text:
The Thistlefur furbolgs are threatening our expansion! Thistlefur Village to our west blocks the way between us here and the Splintertree Post. It's a path that would circumvent the village of Astranaar; without it, we give the Alliance an extra expansion path.

<name>, we must not allow... an expansion path gap!

Proceed to Thistlefur Village and thin out the furbolgs. You will be given compensation for this task, but more importantly you will be doing your duty for the Horde!

passages.title: Between a Rock and a Thistlefur
passages.text:
Well done <class>, well done!  I will continue to send forces to thin out the furbolg, but I can at least count on a different path that will be free of Alliance entanglements.  The Horde conquest of Ashenvale is now in full swing!

You've earned your pay this day, hero.  I salute you!

passages.title: A Decisive Strike
passages.text:
My ploy worked. It appears that these beasts in Loch Modan are following the lead of a chieftain named Grawmug. Grawmug is heavily guarded, however. Two of his most elite guards, Gnasher and Brawler, never leave his side.

If you feel yourself worthy, <name>, I want you to lead the assassination mission on Grawmug and his two thugs inside this cave. Go! I'll free myself from these bindings and meet you shortly.

passages.title: A Decisive Strike
passages.text: Most excellent, <name>!  You have brought hope to Loch Modan.  With Grawmug dead, we stand a better chance of seeing the Troggs eliminated from the land.

passages.title: Ice and Fire
passages.text:
Soren did well to send you out on recon. That's some good information you have right there.

Trouble is, this just adds more work for us to do. The trolls, confused as they are right now, still would like to kick the dwarves right out of Coldridge. And I'm certainly not going to let some fiery demon turn our snowy valley into a mountain lake.

The troll leader, his servants, and the fire creature should all be in the cave to the southeast. Take 'em all out.

passages.title: Ice and Fire
passages.text: <name>! Any luck?

passages.title: Ice and Fire
passages.text:
I'm glad you've returned safely, <name>.  While it may not look like it now, you've proven to be a tremendous asset in the protection of Anvilmar.

Here, take this as a symbol of my gratitude.

passages.title: Missing In Action
passages.text:
At last, friends of the Alliance!

Help... please... 

The last thing I remember these foul Orcs overpowered our regiment. Most the men were killed. I took a strong blow to the head and everything went black. Now I am held captive in this cave. Help me, I am hurt badly.

I'll need help getting back to town... please... you're my last hope...

passages.title: Missing In Action
passages.text: You have served the Kingdom well, <class>.  Thank you for assisting Corporal Keeshan with his escape from those dreaded Blackrock Orcs.  You shall be rewarded for your brave acts this day.

passages.title: Call of Water
passages.text:
Islen will have one more task for you before rewarding you with your next totem. The vial of water I've given you is necessary for whatever that task is.

Go now and find her. We shall meet again some day.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text:
You might have noticed some larger worgen wandering around with the Shadow Weavers in the woods? From what we can tell, these Dark Runners make up the bulk of the worgen numbers.

On my rangings, I've also noticed that they have overrun the Rotting Orchard southwest of town. These worgen are a bit tougher than the last you faced.

Be on your guard.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text:
You performed well against the Dark Runners, <name>. But it seems as though their numbers are inexhaustible. Every time we make progress, more spring up to refill their ranks.

What is the evil power that draws them here? Why have they come to disturb our unhappy realm...

I will put my faith in Master Carevin. No doubt he will get to the bottom of the problem.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text:
Your previous accomplishments have convinced me that you are ready to take on the toughest worgen infesting the woods.

Of the worgen that have made their new home here, the Vile Fangs and the Tainted Ones have proven the most dangerous. They've settled down near some of the caves and in the mine to the south.

From far away you can even see the light from their bonfires...

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text: <name>, to be honest with you, I did not believe that you would get this far, but you are clearly a <class> to be reckoned with. In fact, if you wish to formally join Master Carevin's struggle, I will gladly write for you a letter of recommendation.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text:
Here you go, <name>. Bring this message to Master Carevin.

<He quickly removes a piece of faded parchment and offers it to you.>

A few more like you, and we will outnumber the Night Watch! Perhaps then we could complete the work that we few carry on today.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text: Yes, what is it? Make it quick, I've pressing matters to attend to.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text:
Excuse me for my cold reception, <name>, but as I'm sure you can tell, I am an extremely busy man. I see that you have impressed Calor--and I assure you, that is no small feat--and that he has given his recommendation.

There are unsavory types afoot, <name>, and we can use the help of all who have proven themselves. We battle against demons, the undead, and those who would provide them aid. Be vigilant, be wary, and trust none who would not give aid to our cause.

Glory under the Light.

passages.title: In Defense of the King's Lands
passages.text:
We need to protect the Loch, <name>! With so many of the King's soldiers fighting valiantly on remote battlefields, we've become overwhelmed on the home front. Troggs are tunneling up from every crevice! The Trogg infestation poses the largest threat to Ironforge.

We need you, brave adventurer, to venture forth and lay waste to the Trogg threat. Slay 6 Stonesplinter Troggs and 6 Stonesplinter Scouts and report back. You will find most of the vermin through the passes into the mountains to the south.

passages.title: In Defense of the King's Lands
passages.text:
Well done, <name>!  You demonstrated uncanny courage on the battlefield.  Our war against the Troggs will be won with efforts such as yours.  You have served King Magni well.

If you fancy yourself well-suited for this kind of adventuring, I suggest you speak with Mountaineer Gravelgaw.  The Captain has him assigned to a rough patrol that I am sure he can use some help with.  Check with Gravelgaw just inside the tower.

passages.title: The Weathered Grave
passages.text:
The weathered grave marker reads simply:

MORGAN LADIMORE

<Upon further examination, you notice that dirt over the grave has been recently disturbed, and that a good amount of the dirt seems to have been displaced...>

passages.title: The Weathered Grave
passages.text:
Morgan Ladimore?

Ahh, yes, of course. His was a long and sorrowful tale. I knew him, well, before he left for the war, but that was the last time I saw him. A noble and good man, he was, but he suffered a bad end.

Here, I should have something here that can tell the tale better than my own recollections...

passages.title: Wolves at Our Heels
passages.text:
Sven and I have dangerous days ahead of us, what with the Necromancer to the east and all. And out here alone as we are, we have to hunt for our own food. It seems every time I'm heading back to camp with some meat on me, starving or rabid dire wolves come out of the forest wanting a bite. It goes without saying, living out here is dangerous work!

But if you can rid us of some of those wolves, we'd have an easier time of it. They mostly prowl north and east of here, near the river.

passages.title: Wolves at Our Heels
passages.text:
Oh good.  You thinned out that pack quite a bit, and without those wolves nipping out our heels, we can bind our minds to dealing with Morbent Fel.

Here, take some of these Flash Bundles.  They make them in town, and a lot have been donated to Sven to help with his cause.

passages.title: Morgan Ladimore
passages.text:
<He searches through the shelves and comes up with a leatherbound book.>

If you would like to know more, you might ask Althea, she's been the one to handle the... trouble... with him of late.

passages.title: Morgan Ladimore
passages.text:
Morgan Ladimore? Never heard of...

Oh, you mean Mor'Ladim! I guess you haven't heard the story?

Well, I'll give you the short version. A wandering undead calling itself Mor'Ladim has been wandering Duskwood. From what we've gathered, it appears to be the undead body of Morgan Ladimore, of whom you apparently know. He's been causing us all sorts of problems, attacking Watchmen on patrol and killing people.

<She sizes you up.>

You seem to be capable enough, maybe you could lay him to rest.

passages.title: Mor'Ladim
passages.text:
From what my scouts tell me, Mor'Ladim wanders throughout Duskwood, following a strange and meandering path through the cemetery. We buried him out past the house on the hill, you know where that is?

There isn't anything I can do to help you, but I wish you good luck.

passages.title: Mor'Ladim
passages.text: I don't blame you if you're having trouble with him, <name>. Some of our strongest Watchers have been lost to Mor'Ladim.

passages.title: Mor'Ladim
passages.text:
You killed him? That's no small accomplishment, <name>! On behalf of the people of Darkshire and the Night Watch, I thank you.

Ah... there is one small matter, however...

passages.title: The Daughter Who Lived
passages.text:
I should have told you this earlier...

How do I put this...

Morgan may have believed that his family was all dead, but, in fact, his daughter Sarah Ladimore is now a Watcher. She's always been troubled by the... circumstances... surrounding her father's death. Perhaps you could go to bring the news to her.

passages.title: The Daughter Who Lived
passages.text:
Yes? My father...

<Her eyes become downcast.>

I wish... there was something I could have done for him... If only I had talked to him before he...

passages.title: Sven's Camp
passages.text:
Digging through the mound, you find a small, dirt-stained book.

The book has no title, but...it has information Sven would like to know.

passages.title: Sven's Camp
passages.text: You found what??  Please, let me see it...

passages.title: Sven's Camp
passages.text:
<Sven reads the book's pages, then slams it shut.>

That shadowy figure I saw was a witness to my family's death!  There are questions I'd like to ask that man...if only I knew who he was!

passages.title: A Daughter's Love
passages.text:
Here, take this and lay it on his grave. Maybe... somehow, he'll know that I'm okay, and that none of us hold him responsible for what happened.

<There are tears in her eyes now, as she slides a ring from her right hand, and presses it into your hands.>

And... thank you, <name>.

passages.title: A Daughter's Love
passages.text: Leave me be...

passages.title: A Daughter's Love
passages.text:
<A ghostly voice sounds on the wind...>

This is...? Sarah? Could it be she's still alive? The weight is removed from my shoulders...

<name>. Take my sword, Archeus. As my soul is put to rest, I have no more need for it. It was forged to do good, and though I have proved myself unworthy to hold it, perhaps you will carry on the Light through it.

Lys, my love...

passages.title: Errand for Apothecary Zinge
passages.text:
The Royal Apothecary Society needs your assistance. Listen closely, and both of us may profit from my plan.

Apothecary Keever in the next room may be... touched... but his research does potentially bear fruit if it were pursued by a clever researcher. Fortunately, I am such a researcher. I want you to take this purchase order to Alessandro Luca, the proprietor of Blue Moon Odds and Ends; he'll give you a testing kit. When you have it, bring it back to me and I'll outline your task in detail.

passages.title: Errand for Apothecary Zinge
passages.text: Yes, and what may I assist you with?  Are you here on business for the Royal Apothecary Society, or have you arrived here merely to brighten my day?

passages.title: Errand for Apothecary Zinge
passages.text:
Ah, Zinge needs a kit, does she?  It saddens me that Zinge does not choose to grace myself with her sweet presence.

Very well, let me procure a kit for you.

passages.title: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery
passages.text:
Hm, I don't suppose you'd be willing to do a favor for me, <lad/lass>? A stack of letters came through the pass today, but I don't have the time to send them along.
