Listen... why don't we have Admiral Cantlebree take care of this... situation?

passages.title: Farshire
passages.text:
My lads should be able to take it from here, <name>. Valiance Keep is built to take a beating far worse than this. I worry about our farmlands and mine in Farshire, however.

We sent a full detachment to protect our mining operations right before the invasion - they should be able to defend the civilians.

Gerald Green's in charge of the villagers there. There's a passage out of the northern wall out of Valiance Keep; it'll take you straight to him. See what you can do to help them.

passages.title: Farshire
passages.text: You're here to help?  You're just in time then!

passages.title: The Fall of Taunka'le Village
passages.text:
We are lost, <name>. This place has been our home for many generations, but it is no longer safe. There remains only death... Death and a memory of what used to be.

I have called for the evacuation of Taunka'le. All remaining taunka must leave at once and make their way to our capital city, Icemist, located in the Dragonblight.

<Wintergale points east.>

You must help get my people to safety, <name>. Mother Tauranook awaits you at the village gates. Hurry! The Scourge closes in from all sides!

passages.title: The Fall of Taunka'le Village
passages.text:
<Mother Tauranook wipes her tears away.>

There was once a time when I could walk across this tundra and the snow would fill my view for as far as I could see.

But the snow has left us - signaling that our time here has come to an end. We leave behind Taunka'le Village and the Borean Tundra with many happy memories...

<Mother Tauranook whimpers.>

Perhaps the future will welcome our return - along with the snow.

passages.title: Across Transborea
passages.text:
The path across Transborea, to the east, is the only way to reach the Dragonblight. Many perils await you as you make your journey across the tundra. Beware the Scourge and its influence upon the beasts of the land. Rumors have started to spread about our very own taunka brothers and sisters rising from the dead and attacking caravans on their way to the Dragonblight! Defend your caravan and get the evacuees to safety!

Wartook Iceborn waits for you across the bridge leading into the Dragonblight.

passages.title: Across Transborea
passages.text: It's gone. It's all gone.

passages.title: Across Transborea
passages.text:
<Wartook looks upon you grimly.>

Icemist is no more...

passages.title: Cracking the Code
passages.text:
I sense a distinct peculiarity in the drakes here but the meaning of the runes that cover their bodies still eludes me.

Without a codex, it will take more time than we can afford for me to interpret them.

Not far from here is a Kirin Tor traitor, Caleras, who is likely to have a copy of the tome I require. His underlings hold the runes I will need for my translation.

Hurry, mortal. Malygos gains strength with every passing moment.

passages.title: Cracking the Code
passages.text:
Hurry, mortal.

Malygos gains strength with every passing moment.

passages.title: Cracking the Code
passages.text:
You have done well, <race>.

Let us hope for a clue that we can use against Malygos.

passages.title: Stealing the Exodar's Flame
passages.text: This flame, stolen from the heart of the Exodar itself, floods you with warmth. This raw power is foreign to you, but the Talespinner might know more...

passages.title: Stealing the Exodar's Flame
passages.text: You're practically glowing, <race>. What do you have there?

passages.title: Stealing the Exodar's Flame
passages.text: This fire seems new... Yet, you say it came from the Exodar? Fascinating! To make your way into that ship...  Of course, I'll pay you for this. If you find anything else like this, be sure to speak with me again.

passages.title: Stealing Silvermoon's Flame
passages.text: This flame, stolen from Silvermoon, floods you with warmth. This raw power is foreign to you, but the Loremaster might know more...

passages.title: Stealing Silvermoon's Flame
passages.text: You're practically glowing, <race>. What do you have there?

passages.title: Stealing Silvermoon's Flame
passages.text: What a glorious fire! You received this from Silvermoon, you say? Unbelievable! With the flames of all four cities, who knows what we could accomplish?

passages.title: Hatching a Plan
passages.text:
Our goals here are simple. We are to remain hidden from Malygos, observe his brood, and thwart his efforts wherever possible. To that end, I have a task for you.

The blues are laying their eggs at the base of the Nexus. Exposure to so much arcane energy will surely make them hatch sooner, and there's no telling what effect it will have on their spawn.

I don't intend to find out. Slay the local wyrmkin and use their frozen axes to break the eggs.

passages.title: Hatching a Plan
passages.text: Have you destroyed the blues' eggs, <class>?

passages.title: Hatching a Plan
passages.text:
It pains me to order the destruction of dragon eggs, enemy or no.

May the ends of this war justify the means....

passages.title: Buying Some Time
passages.text:
Now that we have this phylactery, I shouldn't have any problems getting the information I need. It won't take long for the Scourge in the Temple City to notice something's up, however.

I won't be able to fend off a full scale attack here. Or maybe I would... but I'd rather not find out.

I want you to head down there and inflict some casualties. Hopefully they'll be distracted long enough for these two to spill their guts... figuratively, of course. Take Lurid with you, he might be of aid.

passages.title: Buying Some Time
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: Buying Some Time
passages.text: That should buy us some time.  Isidorus has been cooperative, but I really needed that alone time with the lich.

passages.title: Drake Hunt
passages.text:
I need more drake hatchlings to continue researching the runes covering their bodies.

They can be found around the northwest edge of the valley....

<Raelorasz pokes his hand with a spear and coats the tip with his blood.>

Take this and use it on one of them. Wait for it to become subdued, then bring it here to me before it expires.

passages.title: Drake Hunt
passages.text:
The fate of these young drakes need not burden your conscience, <race>. Malygos alone is accountable for this.

I am working ceaselessly to discover the secrets of these runes.

Rest assured, we shall take no more lives than we must.

passages.title: Puzzling...
passages.text:
Something about this scrap of metal prevents you from casting it aside.

Perhaps Raelorasz might be able to shed some light on its purpose.

passages.title: Puzzling...
passages.text: What have you found, <class>?

passages.title: Puzzling...
passages.text:
It was wise of you to bring this to me, <name>.

If you truly desire to contribute to our efforts, no matter the risk, I shall share with you its meaning.

passages.title: Words of Power
passages.text:
The lich has spoken, <name>. The high priests of En'kilah hold the secret to entering Naxxanar.

Go to the Spire of Blood, the Spire of Pain and the Spire of Decay and slay each of the priests.

Return once you've obtained the three scrolls.

passages.title: Words of Power
passages.text: Taking your time, are you?  I don't know how much longer I can keep this lich restrained.

passages.title: Words of Power
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>.  Now for one last bit of information.

passages.title: The Cell
passages.text:
You've discovered a fragment of a special prison, <name>.

Malygos' minions use similar prisons to hold their captured mages and other arcane entities, but this prison was constructed to hold something... stronger.

In hopes that the enemy of our enemy will prove to be a friend, you must search for the prison's remaining fragments.

They are likely to be in the possession of Malygos' most trusted underlings.

passages.title: The Cell
passages.text: Have you discovered any other pieces to the prison?

passages.title: The Cell
passages.text:
<The pieces you've collected begin to glow brightly in Raelorasz' hands.>

It is done.

I sense a strong presence within this prison. Let us hope it proves to be an ally.

passages.title: Surrounded!
passages.text:
Our situation is nearly hopeless. We were ordered to take the Wailing Ziggurat with a handful of men.

We'll be lucky if we can hold this position against the Scourge. We're outnumbered, injured and have no escape route.

If you can take some of the pressure off of us, we might be able to solidify our position. Kill some of the undead circling the structure - we'll hold off their advance.

passages.title: Surrounded!
passages.text: That should buy us some time, <name>.  We'll hope against hope for reinforcements from Valiance Keep.

passages.title: Keristrasza
passages.text:
I am... free?

I was destined to spend an eternity roaming an empty abyss, and now am saved? You cannot fathom my gratitude, mortal.

When I refused to bend to his will Malygos bound me to that prison, then shattered it and scattered the pieces. Should I live one hundred of your lifetimes, I shall not forget this kindness.

Perhaps, in time, I will find ways to repay you. For now, though, we must focus our attention on Malygos. I am weak, and there is much to be done.

I need your help, <name>.

passages.title: Keristrasza
passages.text:
We cannot wait for me to regain my strength.

I must rely on you to make our preparations....

passages.title: Striking Back
passages.text:
We must act to preserve the balance! Time is against us.

There is a camp located in the shadow of Ethel Rethor within northwestern Desolace. There, they use ice stones to communicate with the elementals, as they do in Silithus. Much as I am loath to do this, the spirits will understand - you must summon one of this Ahune's lieutenants and destroy it. Perhaps this forestalling action will be enough...

passages.title: Striking Back
passages.text: You have done well. It may seem a small act, but even this can aid the fight as a whole. Take this with my blessing, and return later, as I may have more for you to do.

passages.title: Striking Back
passages.text:
We must act to preserve the balance! Time is against us.

Neptulon has long had a base of operations on an island in western Stranglethorn. There, the Twilight Cult has set up ice stones to communicate with the Tidehunter's realm, much like they do in Silithus. Much as I am loath to do this, the spirits will understand - you must summon one of this Ahune's lieutenants and destroy it. Perhaps this forestalling action will be enough...

passages.title: Striking Back
passages.text: You have done well. It may seem a small act, but even this can aid the fight as a whole. Take this with my blessing, and return later, as I may have more for you to do.

passages.title: Bait and Switch
passages.text:
During my captivity I was able to learn much about Malygos. Fate now allows us to use this knowledge against him.

There is a great blue dragon, Saragosa, who circles high above the Nexus. She serves both as the aspect's guardian and as his consort. If any serious threats arise, she alerts her master of the danger.

I suffered greatly at the hand of Saragosa during my captivity, and now her time to die has come. First, however, we must fashion the perfect bait....

passages.title: Bait and Switch
passages.text: Have you gathered the mana shards I require?

passages.title: Bait and Switch
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

I am drained from the effects of my confinement and my strength is returning ever so slowly.

I shall use the power from these crystals wisely. They are a byproduct of Malygos' malevolent schemes. With luck, they will play a part in his undoing.

passages.title: Striking Back
passages.text:
We must act to preserve the balance! Time is against us.

Firewatch Ridge in Searing Gorge is an established bastion of Twilight Cult activity. Recently, they have been using ice stones in the cave to communicate with the Tidehunter's realm, much like they do in Silithus. Much as I am loath to do this, the spirits will understand - you must summon one of this Ahune's lieutenants and destroy it. Perhaps this forestalling action will be enough...

passages.title: Striking Back
passages.text: You have done well. It may seem a small act, but even this can aid the fight as a whole. Take this with my blessing, and return later, as I may have more for you to do.

passages.title: Striking Back
passages.text:
We must act to preserve the balance! Time is against us.

Silithus is the Azerothian base of the Twilight Cult. In the north, they have been using new ice stones to communicate with the Tidehunter's realm. Much as I am loath to do this, the spirits will understand - you must summon one of this Ahune's lieutenants and destroy it. Perhaps this forestalling action will be enough...

passages.title: Striking Back
passages.text: You have done well. It may seem a small act, but even this can aid the fight as a whole. Take this with my blessing, and return later, as I may have more for you to do.

passages.title: Striking Back
passages.text:
We must act to preserve the balance! Time is against us.

In order to ensure Ahune's success, the cult has established a base near the Dark Portal itself in Draenor. They use ice stones to coordinate the frost lord's arrival. Much as I am loath to do this, the spirits will understand - you must summon one of this Ahune's templar protectors and destroy it. Perhaps this forestalling action will be enough...

passages.title: Striking Back
passages.text: You have returned victorious?

passages.title: Striking Back
passages.text: You have done well. It may seem a small act, but even this can aid the fight as a whole. Take this with my blessing, and return later, as I may have more for you to do.

passages.title: Finding the Phylactery
passages.text:
No time for small talk, <name>. I was sent on what was to be a suicide mission to take this ziggurat. I've accomplished my duty as a soldier, now is the time to get some answers.

This lich has knowledge I seek, yet I cannot inflict pain to his physical body to obtain that knowledge.

The lich stored his soul in a phylactery, and while it remains hidden, I won't be able to pry the information from him.

Return to the camp and take my horse, Dusk, she will lead you to the phylactery. Bring it to me.

passages.title: Finding the Phylactery
passages.text: You're back, <name>.  Did you get the phylactery?

passages.title: Finding the Phylactery
passages.text: Just in time, <name>.  Pinning down a lich is not as easy as it looks.

passages.title: Saragosa's End
passages.text:
Using the mana crystals you provided, I have created this Power Focus.

Saragosa is a glutton. She will be unable to resist its lure. Inside it lie magics that will greatly diminish her power. Let us hope she does not see through my ruse....

Prepare yourself, <name>, and speak to me again when you are ready to face Saragosa.

passages.title: Saragosa's End
passages.text: Saragosa must not be allowed to live!

passages.title: Saragosa's End
passages.text:
This world is a better place now that Saragosa is no more, but our work is not yet finished.

The time has come to strike at Malygos himself!

passages.title: Let Nothing Go To Waste
passages.text:
The wolvar have always been our natural enemies. But the incursion of your peoples into the Great Dragonblight has forced them into a small space upon the glade to the north.

Combined with the land's upheaval this morning, they have become even more aggressive than ever before. They have made several raids upon our goods... things that we'll need if we are to survive the trek from our home here.

As a sign of good faith and friendship, retrieve our goods from the Snowfall Glade wolvar.

passages.title: Let Nothing Go To Waste
passages.text:
The natural balance has been tipped over and over of late.

I hope that you will be able to help us survive the upheaval of our way of life.

passages.title: Let Nothing Go To Waste
passages.text:
I will not say that I am pleased to ask you to do such things on our behalf. It is all we can do to prepare quickly for our departure, though we know not yet where we go.

My sorcerers tell me that you are here to save the land from He Who Walks in Shadow.

I trust that you will save the peoples of the land as well.

passages.title: Slay Loguhn
passages.text:
Already it goes from bad to worse. There is only one course to take... regrettably, Loguhn must die!

He's the alpha male of the Snowfall Glade tribe and one mean wolvar. But it's the only way to get a short break from their attacks and stealing forays.

You will find the "Render of Flesh" in front of his hovel upon the northern rise of the glade. It's larger than the others and hard to miss. Kill him and smear his blood upon yourself, both to show your dominance and respect.

passages.title: Slay Loguhn
passages.text: Is that Loguhn's blood or your own, <race>?

passages.title: Slay Loguhn
passages.text:
Loguhn's honorable sacrifice at your hands is exactly what my people need. Now we will make the most of the wolvar in-fighting for his place.

It will have to be enough.

passages.title: Planning for the Future
passages.text:
We must move decisively against the wolvar if we're to have a chance of survival. However, I worry that in our zeal, too many of them will be slain.

The Snowfall Glade wolvar have as much right to exist as do we. You and I will see to it that they get that chance.

If Elder Ko'nani hasn't asked you already, he will ask you to deal with them. While you're upon the glade to the north, I'd like you to bag up their pups and bring them back to me.

passages.title: Planning for the Future
passages.text: How many pups could you have possibly saved in so short a time?

passages.title: Planning for the Future
passages.text:
Well, I guess you saved plenty of them. Thank you, <race>.

Now the wolvar will have a chance of surviving along with us. If we survive at all, that is.

Do you think that you could return tomorrow so that we can save more of the pups?

passages.title: Spirits Watch Over Us
passages.text:
Powerful spirits watch over my tribe -- Kaskala will not be lost.

Issliruk will give us courage, Tayutka will make sure our survivors always have food and shelter and Karkut will watch over the fallen so they do not lose their way.

Issliruk's guidance is the one we need the most right now. I asked my nephew, Iruk, to bring me Issliruk's totem, but the Kvaldir's spears struck him down and his body fell into the waters to the north. Bring me the totem, <name>. Don't let my nephew's death be in vain.

passages.title: Spirits Watch Over Us
passages.text: The totem, <race>.  Do you have it?

passages.title: Spirits Watch Over Us
passages.text: Can you feel Issliruk's presence, <name>?  He does not want his children to perish at the hand of the mist-walkers.

passages.title: One Last Delivery
passages.text:
That's it then. With the last of the ore you salvaged we now have enough to send to Valiance Keep.

If Farshire is wiped off the face of Azeroth, then at least let us be remembered as the first ones to defend our land and the last ones to give up.

Take this ore to Hilda Stoneforge - she is a good friend of mine. Tell her to make some good weapons with this ore. We'll need plenty of them in the days to come.

passages.title: One Last Delivery
passages.text: What do you have there?

passages.title: One Last Delivery
passages.text: Ore from Farshire?  We weren't scheduled for a shipment just yet.  Is something wrong?

passages.title: Incense for the Summer Scorchlings
passages.text:
Did you know that our festival fires burn in every land with an Alliance settlement? Flame Wardens tend to them in camps outside of each town, ensuring the bonfires are bright and the celebrations continue.

With each Flame Warden is a summer scorchling -- an emissary to the elemental spirits of fire.

Would you like to honor a scorchling, <name>? Take this summer incense and bring it to any summer scorchling. Appease the little fire spirit, and it may reward you.

passages.title: Incense for the Summer Scorchlings
passages.text: A fiery salutations to you, honored <class>.  Welcome to this hallowed ground of the Midsummer Fire Festival.

passages.title: Incense for the Summer Scorchlings
passages.text:
Ah, and what is this?  Such a delightful aroma!  I am sure it will burn with a flame pure and bright!

Take this blossom, <name>.  Take it, and leave me be... I must attend to this precious fuel...

passages.title: Call to Arms!
passages.text:
Farshire has a fighting chance now, <name>. That's all we could've asked for and you've made it possible.

All we need now is a rallying point. I'll have my men deliver the weapons to our town hall. Go and ring the town hall bell so any survivors know to rally there.

It's time to show the Scourge what we're made of.

passages.title: Call to Arms!
passages.text: Have you rallied the survivors, <name>?

passages.title: Call to Arms!
passages.text: Thanks once again for aiding us, <name>.  The people of Farshire will always remember you.

passages.title: Incense for the Festival Scorchlings
passages.text:
Did you know that our festival fires burn in every land with a Horde settlement? Flame Keepers tend to them in camps outside of each town, ensuring the bonfires are bright and the celebrations continue.

With each Flame Keeper is a festival scorchling -- an emissary to the elemental spirits of fire.

Would you like to honor a scorchling, <name>? Take this summer incense and bring it to any festival scorchling. Appease the little fire spirit, and it may reward you.

passages.title: Incense for the Festival Scorchlings
passages.text: A fiery salutations to you, honored <class>.  Welcome to this hallowed ground of the Midsummer Fire Festival.

passages.title: Incense for the Festival Scorchlings
passages.text:
Ah, and what is this?  Such a delightful aroma!  I am sure it will burn with a flame pure and bright!

Take this blossom, <name>.  Take it, and leave me be... I must attend to this precious fuel...

passages.title: Mustering the Reds
passages.text:
Malygos is certainly aware that something is amiss.

I know him. His focus is fragmented. I am confident that I can lure him from the safety of his realm when he learns what has become of his precious Saragosa.

Take me to Raelorasz at once, <name>. He must rouse every dragon he commands to face Malygos.

passages.title: Mustering the Reds
passages.text: You have news for me, <name>?

passages.title: Mustering the Reds
passages.text:
Word of Keristrasza's rescue has reached my ears. You are to be commended.

I am eager to speak with her again.

passages.title: The Tides Turn
passages.text:
The spirits have heard our cry for help, <name>. It's a sign that Kaskala might yet be saved.

Take advantage of the confusion the weather has created and slay the Kvaldir leader. Your actions will sway the battle in our favor, I am sure of it.

passages.title: The Tides Turn
passages.text: Have you done what I asked of you, <name>?

passages.title: The Tides Turn
passages.text: You've done us a great favor, <race>.  The fight is not yet won, but my people now have a chance.

passages.title: Springing the Trap
passages.text:
We owe this opportunity in great part to your efforts, <name>.

It is only fitting that you initiate the attack on Malygos.

Take this spark and use it to light the signal fire northwest of the Nexus. Keristrasza will direct you from there.

passages.title: Springing the Trap
passages.text: Did you meet with Keristrasza?

passages.title: Springing the Trap
passages.text: We have dealt a blow to Malygos, but it has come at a high price.

passages.title: Shards of Ahune
passages.text: These shards pulse with foreboding. Do they hold the last essence of the Frost Lord?

passages.title: Shards of Ahune
passages.text: Greetings, <name>.  You look worried, but you shoud rejoice.  The Frost Lord is defeated!

passages.title: Shards of Ahune
passages.text:
Yes, these shards hold the final essence of the Frost Lord in this land.  We will dispose of them and banish Ahune to the nether regions of cold.

Thank you, <name>.  Your name will echo in the chants of the Earthen Ring for days without end.  Please honor us by accepting this vestige, a symbol of your kinship with warmth and light.

passages.title: [ph] Now, When I Grow Up...
passages.text:
When you were my age did you know that you wanted to be a <class> when you grew up?

I'm not sure what I want to be. I used to want to be a Blood Knight, but not anymore. Now I want to be a Rock Star! Like the blood elf in L70 ETC!

When they aren't touring, they hang out in Silvermoon City! Could you take me there? They hang out in the Walk of Elder's on a balcony... Probably to keep the fans away But that shouldn't stop us from trying, right?

Please take me there. Please!

passages.title: Now, When I Grow Up...
passages.text:
Maybe I already asked you this, but when you were my age did you know that you wanted to be a <class> when you grew up?

I'm not sure what I want to be. Maybe a mage or a warlock or a Blood Knight, like I said before? Or maybe... A rock star!! Like Sig Nicious, the blood elf, in the Tauren Chieftains!

I heard that when they aren't touring, they hang out in Silvermoon City! They just sit on a balcony in the Walk of Elders waiting for people to stop by.

Please take me there. Please!

passages.title: Now, When I Grow Up...
passages.text: Elite Tauren Chieftain are the coolest!

passages.title: Now, When I Grow Up...
passages.text:
Did you see that?  They were cheering for me!!

Now I know how they feel when they are up on stage singing!  I felt the power and the energy!

Just like they say in their song!

My mind is made up, I am going to be a rock star when I grow up!

passages.title: A Tauren Among Taunka
passages.text:
<Wartook points northeast.>

She is quite kind, you know. If it were not for your emissary, the surviving refugees may have given up hope. While she may not be taunka by birthright, the tribe has taken to her as a village elder for the time being.

If you are who I think you are, please go and pay Emissary Brighthoof a visit inside the refugee camp. She has been waiting for you.

passages.title: A Tauren Among Taunka
passages.text:
What you see here is all that remains of the taunka from the Borean Tundra and the Dragonblight. They are a broken people... battered and brought to the brink of extinction by the Scourge.

<Brighthoof shakes her head.>

Only the Horde can save them now. Only the Horde can mend their broken spirits. We will nurse them back to full health and they will in turn strengthen the Horde in Northrend.

passages.title: Into the Fold
passages.text:
Before we can officially bring these taunka into the Horde we must recover our armaments from the Anub'ar Nerubians that infest the nearby woods. The armaments were lost when a caravan from Agmar's Hammer was ambushed by the Scourge late last night.

Venture out into the woods to the east of Westwind Refugee Camp and recover those armaments, <race>.

passages.title: Into the Fold
passages.text: Without armor and weapons our newest members will be defenseless in their trek to Agmar's Hammer.

passages.title: Into the Fold
passages.text:
This is exactly what we need, <name>! Brandishing Horde arms will lift their spirits and give them the protection they need against the Scourge.

Are you prepared for the ceremony of initiation?

You will be the one to admit our new allies into the Horde.

passages.title: The Taunka and the Tauren
passages.text:
The Scourge have seized control of the capital city of the taunka, Icemist Village! All living taunka that escaped the massacre are being held in protective custody at the Westwind Refugee Camp on the western border of Dragonblight.

Lord Hellscream believes that the taunka must join the Horde if they are to survive and has sent a tauren emissary to Westwind to bolster our relationship with the winter tauren. Travel to Westwind Refugee Camp and seek out Emissary Brighthoof. You will assist her.

passages.title: The Taunka and the Tauren
passages.text:
What you see here is all that remains of the taunka from the Borean Tundra and the Dragonblight. They are a broken people... battered and brought to the brink of extinction.

<Brighthoof shakes her head.>

Only the Horde can save them now. Only the Horde can mend their broken spirits. We will nurse them back to full health and they will in turn strengthen the Horde in Northrend.

passages.title: Pride of the Horde
passages.text:
I was one of the guards chosen to escort the caravan carrying the armament shipment to this camp. The attack came fast and without warning. We fought and killed dozens of the beasts, but in the end there were simply too many. Tor'zin and I barely made it out alive...

If not for our injuries we would be out in the woods hunting down those fiends ourselves. Will you help us regain our lost pride? Search the woods east of here for Anub'ar Nerubians and kill them! For the Horde!

passages.title: Pride of the Horde
passages.text:
<Roh'kill salutes you.>

You have preserved our honor, <name>. Tor'zin and I both thank you for this selfless act!

passages.title: Raining Down Destruction
passages.text:
Beneath us is iron's ancient bastion, Thor Modan. Thousands of years ago, the stone giants tore the land asunder, collapsing part of the city and exposing much of the rest.

Even now, the iron dwarves attempt to reclaim their old capital, but we will not permit it. My giants fill the trench with boulders and debris, hoping to seal it off and kill the servants of iron as they work. Take up the boulders you see near the trench to the northeast, and help us put an end to their efforts.

passages.title: Raining Down Destruction
passages.text: What have you to report?

passages.title: Raining Down Destruction
passages.text: As quickly as we're able to fill the trench, the iron dwarves keep clearing it. Our assault from above will not take the city alone. You must aid the earthen fighting in the plaza below.

passages.title: Blood Oath of the Horde
passages.text:
They are ready, <name>. These taunka will all willingly join the Horde and give all that they have to see the Scourge driven from this world.

<Brighthoof hands you a scroll bearing the insignia of the Horde.>

Within this scroll you will find the blood oath of the Horde. Tradition dictates that our new taunka brothers and sisters utter the sacred words herein.

Take the scroll and swear the taunka into the Horde, commander. Return the scroll to me when you have completed your duty.

passages.title: Blood Oath of the Horde
passages.text: They will strengthen the Horde, commander.

passages.title: Blood Oath of the Horde
passages.text: Thank you for doing this, Commander <name>. They had nothing left. You have given them purpose and with purpose comes hope... Hope for a new tomorrow... for a new life.

passages.title: Filling the Cages
passages.text:
'Ol Budd's seen better days.

Ever since our stay in Ghostlands he's been useless to us. We've had to find ways to make it on our own, and today that means sellin' trolls to the highest bidder.

Fortunately, we've recently found a use for Budd. Something about his condition allows him to mingle with the local trolls, so we taught him a little game that's turned us a tidy profit.

See for yourself. Talk to Budd, take him southwest to Drak'Zin Ruins and use this cage as soon as he tags a troll.

passages.title: Filling the Cages
passages.text: Have you managed to cage an ice troll?

passages.title: Filling the Cages
passages.text:
Great work, <class>. Looks like we'll be keepin' Budd around a little longer.

We'll have your cage picked up right away. Here's your share of the bounty.

Oh, and welcome to the camp. Stick around and I'm sure we'll find a use for ya....

passages.title: Into the Breach
passages.text:
If we can't overcome the defenders inside Thor Modan, the iron dwarves can hold out forever. The Earthen are bravely taking on the constructs built by the sons of iron, but they cannot break into the city.

The tunnels narrow too quickly for my fellow giants to be of use, so our options are few. Would you be willing to venture into the city and kill the dwarf commanding the resistance?

passages.title: Into the Breach
passages.text: Were you able to kill the commander?

passages.title: Into the Breach
passages.text: Well done, <name>. The loss of the iron dwarf commander should be enough to break the remaining defenders. The Earthen should be able to deal with the survivors.

passages.title: The Damaged Journal
passages.text:
This battered, mud-stained journal has seen better days. Leafing through the pages, you discover dozens of notes, diagrams, and maps.

The author's handwriting seems vaguely familiar, but you're unable to place it until you discover an entry signed with the name of Brann Bronzebeard.

The back half of the book, containing the most recent entries, has been torn away. Pages litter the battlefield, and it will be impossible to know what Brann discovered here until the book is whole again.

passages.title: The Damaged Journal
passages.text: What's that you have there?

passages.title: The Damaged Journal
passages.text: You found Brann's journal? Incredible! The league hasn't gotten a report from him in some time, and we began to fear he may have been captured or killed. What did he discover inside Thor Modan?

passages.title: Truce?
passages.text:
Watch yerself, mon.

Drakuru shrunk more <race> heads than I can remember - and even if I could remember, I couldn't count that high. Lucky for you I be stuck in dis cage or I'd be addin' one more to da list.

But things bein' what they are, mebbe we be puttin' our differences aside fer a time, eh?

Drakuru know things, mon. Things that will aid you in your struggle here.

<Drakuru cuts the palm of his hand on one of his tusks and extends it through the cage.>

So, what you say, mon... truce?

passages.title: Truce?
passages.text: Good choice, mon. You won't be livin' to regret it....

passages.title: Truce?
passages.text:
There!

Now we be connected by blood, mon. A true bond we be havin'.

You lissen carefully to Drakuru, <race>. There be much to do.

passages.title: Vial of Visions
passages.text:
First things first, mon. There be some preparatory work that need doin'.

No tellin' how long dey gunna keep me here. Ya be needin' a powerful elixir so we can be keepin' in touch.

Lucky for you, I know just the thing! And the ingredients all be close by.

I need a vial from the pretty little troll over there, some waterweed from the lake just north of here, and a few haze leaves found around the camp here.

Hurry now, mon, before dey be haulin' me away.

passages.title: Vial of Visions
passages.text: You got da stuff, mon?

passages.title: Vial of Visions
passages.text:
<Drakuru takes the ingredients and deftly combines them in the vial.>

This should do it, mon. Now it be time to get to work.

passages.title: Subject to Interpretation
passages.text:
A legendary set of artifacts, lost for thousands of years, were created to make Drak'Tharon Keep impervious.

Most think they be myth, but Drakuru knows better, mon!

I nearly discovered where one be, but got captured while interpreting hieroglyphs. Ya gotta summon my soul back dere so I can finish readin' em!

Use my elixir at da brazier on Drak'Zin Ruins, southwest of here. You'll hafta mix in da frozen mojo my bruddas be holdin'. I hate ta see my bruddas fall, but it be for the greater good.

passages.title: Subject to Interpretation
passages.text:
Ahh, yes. Ya done good, mon.

I be readin' the walls just fine from here....

passages.title: Navigation Charts (Deprecated)
passages.text:
You've uncovered the first part of a navigation chart drawn on flayed dragonskin. If you could complete it you'd be able to find the kvaldir's future plans of attack.

Other mariners in Riplash might have the missing charts on them. Karuk would be interested in the information they contain.

passages.title: The Runic Prophecies
passages.text:
We've no time to lose! Now that we've reassembled the runic keystone -- well, most of it -- we can decipher the contents of those very same runic plates Brann was working on before he fled.

We have no way of knowing if he managed to read the contents of all three plates, but we'll have to assume he got enough information to determine his next destination.

Stand before each of the plates and use the keystone to determine the contents of each. Brann may be counting on us!

passages.title: The Runic Prophecies
passages.text:
<Torthen listens as you recount the contents of the runic plates.>

By Madoran's hammer, he's discovered a whole new titan city!

'The cradle of stone and iron.'

'Ulduar nestled in the storm.'

What d'you suppose that means? Could it be where we come from, after all these years?

We have to follow him! We have to find him!

passages.title: Softening the Blow
passages.text:
Our best bet for moving our forces quickly to Icecrown Glacier lies with the network of tunnels beneath the ancient iron dwarf city of Thor Modan.

Brugar Stoneshear and his Explorers' League boys aren't going to be happy, but orders are orders.

The news might go over better if you brought him a cask of that moonshine sold by that trapper, Hugh Glass, down at Redwood Trading Post, southeast of here along the tree line.

Man's not right in the head, but you won't find better moonshine out here.

passages.title: Softening the Blow
passages.text: What's that you have there?

passages.title: Softening the Blow
passages.text: Let me get this straight -- a <race> I don't know brings me a cask of the finest booze in this miserable forest. Ok, then, what are you after?

passages.title: Rifle the Bodies
passages.text:
The Moonrest Gardens to the southwest were the final resting place of a group of Highborne elves. It was also a ley line nexus.

The blue dragonflight used a magical device they call a surge needle to destroy that nexus, freeing the power to redirect at their will.

I want more information and you are going to get it for me!

After the land was destroyed at the ruins, the ghosts of the Highborne rose up and decimated half of the mage hunters there. Go rifle their corpses for clues.

passages.title: Rifle the Bodies
passages.text: You have returned.  What did you uncover?

passages.title: Rifle the Bodies
passages.text:
Curious, they seek an accord with the Ethereum. The ethereals could prove a powerful ally for Malygos and his madness.

This will not do!

passages.title: Rifle the Bodies
passages.text:
The Moonrest Gardens to the southwest were the final resting place of a noble group of Highborne elves. It was also a powerful ley line nexus.

The blue dragonflight used a magical device they call a surge needle to destroy that nexus, freeing the power to redirect at their will.

I need more information and I hope that you will get it for me.

After the upheaval at the ruins, the ghosts of the Highborne rose up and decimated half of the mage hunters present. Go rifle their corpses for clues.

passages.title: Rifle the Bodies
passages.text: You have returned.  What did you uncover?

passages.title: Rifle the Bodies
passages.text:
Curious, they seek an accord with the Ethereum. The ethereals could prove a powerful ally for Malygos and his madness.

This will not do!

passages.title: zzOLDHunting Tarot: Lesser Beasts
passages.text: Staring into the card, the image blurs until you see yourself standing covered in the furs from many wolves and bears. You can only assume this is your destiny should you invoke the tarot's power.

passages.title: Brothers in Battle
passages.text:
I hope Gryan knows I withdrew my men from Thor Modan when the battle began. There's no way we can excavate anything until that place settles down.

You seem like a brave sort, though, and you have Stoutmantle's trust.

Thor Modan is just to the northeast of us and the battle still rages between our Earthen brothers and the creations of those accursed iron dwarves. Help our brethren to even the odds and I'll start figuring out how we're going to accomplish this survey of Thor Modan.

passages.title: Brothers in Battle
passages.text:
<Brugar listens to your report.>

It sounds like things may be calming down there a bit. We'll start looking for entrances to the iron dwarves' tunnel system.

passages.title: Uncovering the Tunnels
passages.text:
The first place we'll search for entrances to the Thor Modan tunnel system will be the outlying buildings.

As I left the site with my men, it looked like the iron dwarf defenders were taking refuge inside the buildings. Be careful as you explore them.

Any tunnel entrances are likely to be toward the back of the buildings. I'm not sure what Stoutmantle thinks we're going to find down there, but I doubt the iron dwarves will make the search easy.

passages.title: Uncovering the Tunnels
passages.text:
<Brugar utters a stream of foul dwarven words.>

No entrances? None?

No, of course it couldn't be that easy. Well, I suppose there's no avoiding a foray into the city proper. My boys'll never get back to their real work.

passages.title: Prevent the Accord
passages.text:
We need to kill two birds with one stone here, <class>. You're the stone.

Our two birds are Wind Trader Mu'fah and Goramosh. They should be somewhere in the western half of the Moonrest Gardens. Most likely they're in the larger two-story building overlooking the pit.

I require proof of their demise, if you would be so kind.

passages.title: Prevent the Accord
passages.text: Have you prevented the accord between the blue dragonflight and the Ethereum?

passages.title: Prevent the Accord
passages.text:
Unfortunate that Goramosh indicated the accord had already been reached.

Nonetheless, that's two less worms we'll have to worry about. Let us get to more important business.

passages.title: Prevent the Accord
passages.text:
We need to kill two birds with one stone here, <class>. You're the stone.

Our two birds are Wind Trader Mu'fah and Goramosh. They should be somewhere in the western half of the Moonrest Gardens. Most likely they're in the larger two-story building overlooking the pit.

I require proof of their demise, if you would be so kind.

passages.title: Prevent the Accord
passages.text: Have you prevented the accord between the blue dragonflight and the Ethereum?

passages.title: Prevent the Accord
passages.text:
That's alright, <class>, just put them down on the ground there in front of Agmar's throne.

Unfortunate that Goramosh indicated the accord had already been reached.

Nonetheless, that's two less worms we'll have to worry about. Let us get on to more important business.

passages.title: Avenge this Atrocity!
passages.text:
These so-called mage hunters came here and destroyed our resting place.

Avenge us, or I will see to it that your base of operations is overrun with the spirits of the dead!

passages.title: Avenge this Atrocity!
passages.text: Somehow I sense that you haven't quite killed enough of these defilers!

passages.title: Avenge this Atrocity!
passages.text:
Very well, you have satisfied my request if nothing more.

Thank you, <race>.

passages.title: Sacrifices Must be Made
passages.text:
I've got it, mon!

To da north, on da Ziggurat at Zeb'Halak be a stone head with ruby eyes. One o' dem be da Eye of the Prophets! Bring it to the brazier there and drink my elixir.

Again, ya be needing some mojo for my elixir to work - dis time from da warlord, Zim'bo. He be hidin' in one of da huts in Zeb'Halak.

It be a shame to kill Zim'bo, mon, but he swore da blood oath to defend Drak'Tharon and he done failed. Now at least his mojo be helpin' us to reclaim Drak'Tharon.

passages.title: Sacrifices Must be Made
passages.text: You get da Eye of the Prophets, mon?

passages.title: Sacrifices Must be Made
passages.text:
Dis be it, mon!

It be even more precious than I hoped. Dis be sure to bring mah people hope in dese dark times.

No time to waste, now. Let's be seein' where da next artifact be hidin'.

passages.title: Agmar's Hammer
passages.text:
Directly east of this refugee camp stands Agmar's Hammer - testament to the Hordes' power in the Dragonblight.

While I have no doubt that our Horde brothers and sisters are already seeing the result of your efforts to bring the taunka into the Horde, I want you to deliver news of your success to Overlord Agmar in person.

Go now, <name>! Race the winds! East to Agmar's Hammer!

passages.title: Agmar's Hammer
passages.text:
While you have undoubtedly championed the cause of the Horde elsewhere, many more have been working towards expanding our grasp deeper into Northrend. Even now we have forces establishing bases in the frozen reaches of this desolate wasteland.

We surround the Scourge on all sides. Victory nears as our armies amass at the foot of the Wrathgate, Angrathar. Soon we will tear down the gate and breach Icecrown.

But there is much work left to be done...

First we stop the Nerubians!

passages.title: Tua'kea's Crab Traps
passages.text:
With all of the troubles, I've lost my assistants. I was wondering if maybe you could help me?

I have many crab traps under the waves of the harbor. Will you retrieve them for me? I'm too old for that sort of thing and the waters can be very dangerous.

Please, take this bladder. It will help you to breathe while you're down there.

passages.title: Tua'kea's Crab Traps
passages.text: How many crabs did you manage to retrieve?

passages.title: Tua'kea's Crab Traps
passages.text:
I'm a simple trapper. The world has turned upside-down all of a sudden. It doesn't make sense.

I hope that you'll be able to set it right again.

passages.title: End Arcanimus
passages.text:
There is one last thing that I would have you do, <name> the <race>. I would have you destroy Arcanimus!

The sorcerers to the west used that giant device in the sky to bore a massive pit into our resting place. When they did that, they unleashed a monstrosity!

I would not care if it were only a concern for mortals, but Arcanimus feeds upon the spirits of the dead.

You will put an end to it now!

passages.title: End Arcanimus
passages.text: Do you think me a fool? Arcanimus is still eating the souls of my brothers and sisters, <class>!

passages.title: End Arcanimus
passages.text:
You have my deepest gratitude, <name>.

If you haven't already, you should alert your betters to the danger that the blue dragonflight has unleashed. By blowing apart the ley line anchor underneath the gardens, they threaten to destroy us all!

passages.title: Steady as a Rock?
passages.text:
Orlond's notes indicate that he brought a piece of equipment called a portable seismograph with him, but the device is nowhere to be seen.

The survey log shows that Orlond completed all his readings in the Thor Modan tunnel, save one labeled the 'east end of the exposed tunnel.'

The last entry in the log indicates Orlond tried to take refuge in the water and was attacked by subterranean threshers. They might've taken his equipment.You'll need to recover it before you can take the last reading.

passages.title: Steady as a Rock?
passages.text: What did you find?

passages.title: Steady as a Rock?
passages.text:
<Brugar looks over the report.>

This isn't good at all. Even if we could excavate the tunnels behind the blockage, there's no guarantee they wouldn't collapse again. It looks like some of these areas haven't been used in generations. We'll have to give Captain Gryan the bad news.

passages.title: Test Quest for Craig
passages.text: klajsdklajlsd

passages.title: The Bait
passages.text:
I'm sure of it... our ancient aquatic nemesis, Tu'u'gwar, "He Who Plays With Food", has returned. We must lay a trap for him, you and I.

If Tu'u'gwar has one weakness it's his stomach. There's one meat for certain that he'd never be able to pass up.

"Two Huge Pincers", the mother of all crabs, Kili'ua, paces upon her island out in the waters to the southwest. You must pay her a visit and return with her meat.

passages.title: The Bait
passages.text: You return with the succulent flesh of Kili'ua?

passages.title: The Bait
passages.text:
You were able to slay Kili'ua... perhaps you'll be able to do the same to Tu'u'gwar.

Perhaps not.

passages.title: Sweet Revenge
passages.text:
You there... you look the fighting type. I want some sweet Revenge on the Scourge that killed my family. Go get me 2 Stone Hunks O' Gargoyle so that I can throw them on the ground and stomp on them violently until they are mashed into itty bitty pebbly bits. 

Yes. Go. Kill.

passages.title: Last Rites
passages.text:
I served Arthas in death, because I had no choice. He had control over my will and my body. The Cult of the Damned serves Arthas in life... willingly.

Now that we know the words of power to enter Naxxanar we can put an end to the cultist blight. Go to En'kilah and look for the teleportation orb beneath the floating citadel.

Work your way up and meet me at the top. Arm yourself with what courage you can, we might not make it out of this alive.

passages.title: Last Rites
passages.text: Hail, <name>.

passages.title: Last Rites
passages.text:
You did well, <name>.  I was hoping to leave my sister out of all this.  Thanks to you she is alive and well.

My obligations to my king and my army have been fulfilled.  It is clear I'm not welcome among my comrades anymore.  I will have to find my own way, fighting no wars but my own and following no orders but my heart's.

Perhaps we shall meet again, <class>.  Until then, take this as a token of my gratitude.

passages.title: Chug and Chuck!
passages.text:
Hey there! You look like you can handle your brew.

But can you handle your brew mug?

We like to keep things lively around camp, and nothing says fun like a good old-fashioned mug toss!

Think you've got the aim to hit S.T.O.U.T.? Just grab a sampler, take a sip, and see if you can land a hit. It's trickier than it looks, but that's half the fun. Step right up and give it a shot!

passages.title: Chug and Chuck!
passages.text: Toss one back, then toss one forward. S.T.O.U.T. can take the abuse, it's why I built him.

passages.title: Chug and Chuck!
passages.text:
Do you know what that was?  Gnomish engineering at its finest!  S.T.O.U.T. took the abuse like a champ!

I think you're ready now to take on the Dark Irons if they show up again.

passages.title: Sweeter Revenge
passages.text: Satisfyingly crunchy. Now... you... <race> thing... there's an Abomination wandering the hillside to the south. Go kill it. Kill it good.

passages.title: A Scarlet Among Us
passages.text:
It's good to see that you were not ravaged by the Scourge as well. Perhaps you'd be willing to lend a hand. 

The Scarlet Crusade has taken up a post to the north with the obvious intent of battling the Scourge. The thing that bothers me is that they were building before we were attacked - they must have known something. 

I need to know if one of our Villagers was involved. Search for evidence on those of us that were brought back as ghouls. If you find anything, bring it to me.

passages.title: The Damaged Journal
passages.text:
This battered, mud-stained journal has seen better days. Leafing through the pages, you discover dozens of notes, diagrams, and maps in the dwarven language.

The only text you're able to decipher is the name of Brann Bronzebeard scrawled at the end of one of the entries.

The back half of the book, containing the most recent entries, has been torn away. Someone thought the notes important enough to attempt to destroy them. Perhaps gathering the missing pages from the battlefield will yield some clues.

passages.title: The Damaged Journal
passages.text: What's that you have there?

passages.title: The Damaged Journal
passages.text: Who is this Brann Bronzebeard? The iron dwarves found no reason to treat with him, but I have no idea why we'd be interested in his writings.

passages.title: Mr. Floppy's Perilous Adventure
passages.text:
Excuse me, <Mister/Ma'am>, do you know the way back to the soldiers' camp?

Mr. Floppy and I decided to go for a walk in the woods, and my brother Walter was gonna come with us, but then he had squire things to do.

So Mr. Floppy and I went by ourselves, but we got lost, and there were a whole bunch of hungry wolves, but we found this tower.

The wolves went away, but we're still lost.

I asked Mr. Floppy, and he doesn't know the way back. Would you help us? Please?

passages.title: Mr. Floppy's Perilous Adventure
passages.text:
Thank goodness you found Emmy! When she left without me, I was worried she'd get lost.

I'm glad to see Mr. Floppy's back safe and sound, too.

passages.title: Spiritual Insight
passages.text:
<race>, we have not heard from our people at Indu'le Village since the ground shook and was torn apart!

Have you ever been upon a vision quest? You've bested Loguhn, so you must be capable.

I will give you a special incense to sprinkle into my brazier. Breathe deep from its vapors and your spirit will be sent aloft to view what has transpired at Indu'le.

As your spirit soars, I will be able to look through your eyes.

passages.title: Spiritual Insight
passages.text: What do you think?

passages.title: Spiritual Insight
passages.text:
Ghosts and gibbering madness? This cannot be!

We must seek further guidance.

passages.title: Seared Scourge
passages.text:
<Hic>... gotta burn these corpshes 'fore they shtart walkin' around again.

Poppa always said, only thing worshe than havin' to kill a troll is havin' ta kill a troll twice.

Say,<hic>... shpeakin' of Scourge, we can't get into tha' troll keep up north 'til we get them trolls thinned out a bit.

How 'bout ya take shome o my grog here and put them bashtards outta their misery?

passages.title: Seared Scourge
passages.text:
Well done!

<Mack laughs hysterically for a moment.>

Aww, come on now. That was funny...<hic>.

passages.title: Freedom for the Lingering
passages.text:
The sacred ground of the elves to the west has been torn asunder. Now their magic is moving through the land causing ruin where it flows.

The souls of the Kalu'ak are in danger as the blue dragons forces attempt to control the magic.

The power came up through the lake, instantly slaying most in the village. Those that survived were driven insane.

<name>, you must release these spirits so that they may move on. Leave the deranged living alone; they may yet regain their sanity in time.

passages.title: Freedom for the Lingering
passages.text: <Elder Mana'loa looks through you, sensing that you have not yet completed his task.>

passages.title: Freedom for the Lingering
passages.text:
Not the most pleasant task, but necessary and merciful.

And now there is something else that you are destined to do for the Kalu'ak.

passages.title: Conversing With the Depths
passages.text:
The watery goddess, Oacha'noa, must be consulted; only she will know what the destiny of the Kalu'ak is to be. And only The Pearl of the Depths can call her forth from the murky nether.

Off the coast to the southwest rises The Briny Pinnacle. Atop it sits the altar upon which the pearl rests.

Commune at the altar and Oacha'noa is certain to hear your call. Do as she says lest you incur her wrath and bring ruin upon all of the tuskarr.

Should you survive, return to the mystic.

passages.title: Conversing With the Depths
passages.text:
You spoke with Oacha'noa?!

If it is her will that we stand with your people then so be it. Elder Ko'nani will accept this as our destiny, for weal or woe.

My people believe that all souls are one with the magic of the world. We must oppose the blue dragon attempts to control the magic or we are all doomed!

I never thought that a <race> would be the champion of the Kalu'ak, but you have proven me wrong. On behalf of my people, I give you thanks, <name>.

May the gods smile upon you and keep you safe.

passages.title: Message from the West
passages.text:
<Torvus shakes your hand, giving you a letter in the process.>

<Torvus speaks under his breath.>

Just play along, <name>.

It is good to see you here, soldier! Lord Hellscream has undoubtedly sent his strongest warriors to Lord Agmar!

<Torvus speaks under his breath.>

Read it and then destroy it in the fire pot next to me.

passages.title: Message from the West
passages.text:
<Torvus nods at you.>

So we are understood? I will return to my lord and tell him that you have accepted.

passages.title: Repurposed Technology
passages.text:
Ok, I've got it! The rewiring is a little complicated, but nothing a clever <class> like you can't handle.

Take my tools and put some of the harvest collectors out of commission. Once they're down use the tools to plug all the red wires into the blue sockets. That'll make them go into self-defense mode. Hurry, <name>. Before long there won't be anything left to save.

passages.title: Repurposed Technology
passages.text: You done yet, <name>?

passages.title: Repurposed Technology
passages.text: Nice job!  I finally feel useful again... and that's sayin' something.

passages.title: From the Depths of Azjol-Nerub
passages.text:
The undead Nerubians that attacked Icemist Village came from a gigantic sinkhole known as the Pit of Narjun. If left alone, those fiends will no doubt flank our forces at the Wrathgate and end our march to victory.

I need eyes on the ground, <name>. You are to head west and investigate the Pit of Narjun. We need to locate their primary exit point and seal it off! Find me that location.

passages.title: From the Depths of Azjol-Nerub
passages.text:
That damned sinkhole must be directly connected to Azjol-Nerub. This is worse than I thought.

<Juktok pauses to think for a moment.>

Seek and destroy... That'll be the next course of action.

passages.title: Search and Rescue
passages.text:
Orcs... they just don't lissen <hic>. Know what I mean, <race>?

Kurzel's been with us fer years. You'd think she'd get a feel fer how we do things by now. Lure the fools in fer the dangerous work, then reap the rewards when it's safe. What's so hard to understand?

Not her though... she goes off and takes matters into her own hands. Probably dead by now, but I'd feel horrible if we didn't follow after her, and I'm in no shape to do it myself <hic>.

So whatdya say, pal?

passages.title: Search and Rescue
passages.text:
I knew it!

Even my going missing wasn't enough to get those spineless weasels to come in here after me.

Well, they sent you. I suppose that's something....

Here, take this. I'd rather it go to you than to those dimwits back at the camp.

passages.title: Seared Scourge
passages.text:
Whatcha waitin' fer, <class>? Them shcourged trolls ain't gunna kill themselves!

You know the drill. Git up ta Drak'Tharon up north... Take some o thish here grog and hurl it at 'em from a distance...<hic>. Then jusht sit back an' watch 'em burn.

passages.title: Seared Scourge
passages.text:
Well done!

<Mack laughs hysterically for a moment.>

Aww, come on now. That was funny...hic.

passages.title: Black Blood of Yogg-Saron
passages.text:
Angrathar, the Wrathgate... I watched as the metal holding the gate together pulsed and undulated as if it were alive! In 50 years I've never seen metal "breathe."

Only ones who knew anything about it were the tuskarr. They called it the "Black Blood of Yogg-Saron" and told me to keep my distance.

There's a sinkhole outside Icemist Village to the west called the Pit of Narjun. I've heard of these sinkholes being rich with this strange ore. If you head that way, could you try and get me some samples?

passages.title: Black Blood of Yogg-Saron
passages.text: What's life without risks?

passages.title: Black Blood of Yogg-Saron
passages.text:
It's so light... As if it weighs nothing at all! I'll need time to analyze the metal and see if I can do anything with it! Tests! I need to run tests!

I'll keep in contact, <name>. If anything comes of this, you'll be the first to know.

passages.title: An Enemy in Arthas
passages.text:
We are in the midst of a civil war. At the heart of this world the last living members of my species defend themselves against total annihilation. The Lich King seeks to rule the kingdom of Azjol-Nerub at any cost. Those that do not acquiesce are branded enemies of the Scourge and marked for death.

In Arthas we both have an enemy...

Join our cause and rid this place of the taint of Anub'ar! Let Anub'arak himself hear the anguish of their death cries!

passages.title: An Enemy in Arthas
passages.text: The Azjol Empire will rise again!

passages.title: An Enemy in Arthas
passages.text: There are thousands more and they spill out from every dark crevice in Northrend. Alone you stand no chance, but together... Maybe...

passages.title: The Lost Empire
passages.text:
You have proven that you are willing to assist the Azjol Empire in its time of need and as such the Azjol Empire will assist the Horde.

Take this scroll back to your leader. It documents the strengths and weaknesses of the Nerubians attacking Icemist Village. Consider it a gesture of good faith - a willingness to help your people. Use the knowledge on those pages to crush the Anub'ar and you will have done a service for us all.

Farewell, <race>.

passages.title: The Lost Empire
passages.text: What have you got there?

passages.title: The Lost Empire
passages.text:
<Overlord Agmar looks over the document.>

Is this what I think it is? With the information contained within these pages we will CRUSH the Anub'ar assault!

You have done well to bring this document to me, <name>. Perhaps you will be allowed to watch or even participate in the final battle at Angrathar! LOK'TAR!

passages.title: Heart of the Ancients
passages.text:
Secrets of da ages, be revealed to me now!

<Drakuru peers through the Eye of the Prophets.>

Ahh, great be mah destiny, <name>. You be lucky ta know me....

There! I be seein' it, mon. The Heart of the Ancients. Dis be too easy!

You gunna find da heart lyin' near da corpse of a goblin east of here. He be up in a chamber, near a river of broken trees.

Hurry, mon, before someone else be findin' it!

passages.title: Heart of the Ancients
passages.text:
This unfortunate goblin must have unearthed the Heart of the Ancients during his excavations in the region.

It's doubtless that he had no clue as to its nature.

You determine that it must have been overlooked in the chaos sweeping through the area.

passages.title: Nozzlerust Defense
passages.text: You, <class>! These undead south of us are being a constant nuisance to our work. Go clear them out, will ya?

passages.title: Nozzlerust Defense
passages.text: Oh!  Yeah, the undead.  Here's your coin, bugger off.

passages.title: Stocking Up
passages.text:
Hello hello! The Scourge to the south are digging up some ancient dragon thing. I could care less why they're doing it, but they're pulling cartloads of composite ore in the process.

Go lift me a bunch of that ore. That stuff should yield a pretty penny for all the weapons the Horde are crafting.

passages.title: Stocking Up
passages.text: Did you get the ore?  My carrier will be back shortly - we need to get this shipment out while the fight's still going!

passages.title: Stocking Up
passages.text: Hah!  That's quite a load!  Your back feeling alright?

passages.title: Shaved Ice
passages.text:
I've never seen you before... are you new to the Vice? Glad to have you. I could always use some more hands.

You get the materials, I'll finish my machine, then we can sell it to those commander types and all go home rich.

I actually have most of the primary components, so I just need some of the materials for the weapon itself. Narf said that jagged ice shards from those elementals to the north would make perfect shrapnel for my bombs - go nab some, will ya?

passages.title: Shaved Ice
passages.text: Do you have the shards?  I'm almost finished with the main refrigeration unit.

passages.title: Shaved Ice
passages.text:
Excellent!  They're even sharper than I expected them to be.  I'll pack them in the snow until the bomb is ready.

Let's see... what next...

passages.title: Soft Packaging
passages.text:
I need some new packaging for the shrapnel bombs. All the stuff I have is too hard and the shrapnel doesn't spread when it bursts. 

What we need is some really thin animal hide. Those jormungar tunnelers to the west might work... or perhaps the condors sifting through the dragon bones. Go get me whatever you can find.

passages.title: Soft Packaging
passages.text: How goes the hunt?  Do you have my hides?

passages.title: Soft Packaging
passages.text:
Good... good... these should do fine.  The shrapnel bombs are almost finished. 

Wait... what happened to my ice shards?  Narf told me shards from those elementals should be enchanted, but they're melting just like the ones hanging from Narf's grumpy chin!

passages.title: Something That Doesn't Melt
passages.text:
No no no! Those ice shards didn't work at all! They'll melt before they even do any damage. That's the last time I'll trust Narf's word on materials. This means we need something else entirely for the shrapnel.

I know! I'm brilliant. Bone splinters.

There are some bones all around here that the jormungar have been gnawing on pretty thoroughly. Go check them out and see if you can find me some splintered bone that I can use.

passages.title: Something That Doesn't Melt
passages.text: Were there any splinters to be found?

passages.title: Something That Doesn't Melt
passages.text: Excellent!  That should be the last thing I need to test out the new bombs.  Just a moment and I'll try this out!

passages.title: Scourge Armaments
passages.text:
I can't make a damned thing out of this ore. It simply will not hold together! Despite my best efforts the Scourge metal will not bend!

Perhaps if I had some samples of some forged Scourge armaments I might be able to reverse engineer the process by which the items are created.

Icemist Village is crawling with armored Scourge Nerubians. Go there and get me some Scourge armaments! With your help I might actually succeed in creating something from this ore.

You'll find Icemist to the west.

passages.title: Scourge Armaments
passages.text:
<Borus throws his tools down.>

These are useless!

passages.title: Scourge Armaments
passages.text: These are in excellent condition, <name>. I'll get to work right away. If anything comes of this, you will be the first to know!

passages.title: Hard to Swallow
passages.text:
Those troops are sure to be needin' a hefty supply of food in their bellies.

I'll let you in on a little secret that a squeamish <race> like you would never know... those jormungar worms taste just like chicken.

Go provoke one of those giant hulking jormungar to the east. You're not likely to be able to kill one straight out, so just toss this down its throat when it opens its mouth wide. Bring me back as many of the slabs of meat as you can tote.

passages.title: Hard to Swallow
passages.text: Did ya get it all?  You certainly stink of it.

passages.title: Hard to Swallow
passages.text: Ha ha!  One of those meat slabs landed clear over here!  Nice work there!

passages.title: Lumber Hack
passages.text:
Next up, we need to haul in some lumber for all the towers the Alliance are building. There are some thin trees to the south, but the trees the harpies are nesting in to the north look much more fit for structures.

Take this. When you get to the harpy nesting area, use the control and one of my Shredders should come to you. Gather as much lumber as it can carry. The harpies are sure to disagree with you chopping down their homes - just deal with them as necessary.

Hop to it!

passages.title: Lumber Hack
passages.text: Where's that carrier?  Hope the Jormungar didn't get him.  He was carrying a good sized load that time.

passages.title: Lumber Hack
passages.text: If a tree falls in the forest, and you can't hear it through the saw blade, does it really make a sound?

passages.title: Harp on This!
passages.text:
<class>, did you see that? That's the harpy that's been leading the attack on our shipments to the gate! I've seen her in the back of Coldwind Heights before.

 Those harpies have slowed our profits long enough! Kill them all.

passages.title: Harp on This!
passages.text: That should make those uglies think twice.  Here... take your reward and get away with ya.

passages.title: The Might of the Horde
passages.text:
The taunka are now our brothers in arms. We must show our solidarity and retake Icemist Village.

You will find Icemist Village west of Agmar's Hammer, sitting at the foot of the mountains. Travel there and challenge the Anub'ar Nerubians! Plant our beloved Horde banner at Icemist Village and destroy all that dare come to tear it down!

Let the Anub'ar feel the true might of the Horde! Let our battle standard be the last thing that they see before death!

passages.title: The Might of the Horde
passages.text: It is a challenge, <name>!

passages.title: The Might of the Horde
passages.text: We have crushed them by land! Soon we will crush them by air!

passages.title: A Strange Device
passages.text:
Picking up this strange device, you are certain that it is magical in nature. Unfortunately, it doesn't seem to connote any other kind of use.

Perhaps the archmage back at Stars' Rest to the east of the Moonrest Gardens would be able to tell what it's used for?

passages.title: A Strange Device
passages.text: What do you have there?

passages.title: A Strange Device
passages.text: <name>, if I'm not mistaken, you've uncovered the key to allow us to discern exactly what the mage hunter forces are up to!

passages.title: Marked for Death: High Cultist Zangus
passages.text:
I witnessed his treachery with my own eyes! The traitor led an Anub'ar assault on this stronghold, taking out some of my best soldiers.

<Gort shakes his head.>

He'd been working with the Scourge the whole time and we didn't have a clue! How many more like Zangus are there? We'll find 'em all and when we do...

<Gort makes a cutting motion across his neck.>

First on the list is Zangus. Our scouts report that he is hiding in The Pit of Narjun, west of here. Find him, kill him, bring me his head.

passages.title: Marked for Death: High Cultist Zangus
passages.text: Is that a severed orc head in your pack or are you just happy to see me?

passages.title: Marked for Death: High Cultist Zangus
passages.text:
<Gort holds the head up and stares into its dead eyes.>

I told you we'd get you...

Here's your reward, <class>. That's one less headache for us to worry about.

passages.title: The Flesh-Bound Tome
passages.text:
The tome is bound in flesh and appears to be bleeding. Upon examination you discover page after page filled with strange symbols that appear to be written in blood.

Whatever knowledge is held within the pages of this tome could be important. Return it to Captain Gort at Agmar's Hammer, east of Icemist Village.

passages.title: The Flesh-Bound Tome
passages.text: <Gort raises an eyebrow.>

passages.title: The Flesh-Bound Tome
passages.text:
<Gort takes the tome from you.>

Savages... Bound in orc flesh... This language... Its existence has never been proven. It is the language of death... The tongue of the Scourge.

passages.title: The Runic Prophecies
passages.text:
Brann's journal also contained a guide to iron dwarf symbols. I've inscribed these on a keystone which will help you to understand the words inscribed on the rune plates.

From the journal entries, it seems Brann may be chasing after clues to the origins of his people. Keep your eyes open for any clues as to his destination.

Return to Thor Modan, northeast of here, stand before each of the plates, and use the stone to determine the contents of each. We can't allow the Alliance to find him first.

passages.title: The Runic Prophecies
passages.text:
<Sage Paluna listens as you recall the translations of the plates.>

So Brann thinks he's discovered a new titan city?

'The cradle of stone and iron.'

'Ulduar nestled in the storm.'

I will ask the chieftain to dispatch longrunners to the Storm Peaks. My people know these lands well and have the best chance of tracking down this wayward dwarf.

passages.title: A Strange Device
passages.text:
Picking up this strange device, you are certain that it is magical in nature. Unfortunately, it doesn't seem to connote any other kind of use.

Perhaps the archmage back at Agmar's Hammer to the northeast of the Moonrest Gardens would be able to tell what it's used for?

passages.title: A Strange Device
passages.text: What do you have there?

passages.title: A Strange Device
passages.text: <name>, if I'm not mistaken, you've uncovered the key to allow us to discern exactly what the mage hunter forces are up to!

passages.title: Projections and Plans
passages.text:
This is a teleportation device. If I had to guess, I'd say that it leads to the surge needle platform floating above the Moonrest Gardens to the west.

I need you to use it to investigate what's up there. It appears that the device works both ways so you shouldn't have to jump off.

I expect that once you teleport to the top of the surge needle, there will be some sort of apparatus on it to observe.

You should be able to use the teleporter from anywhere within the gardens.

passages.title: Projections and Plans
passages.text: Back so soon?

passages.title: Projections and Plans
passages.text:
What you're describing... that's a projection of the Arcanomicon!

<The archmage's show of concern is quickly masked behind an impassive countenance.>

The Arcanomicon is a map of all of the magical ley line intersections in the world. The blue dragonflight has been using it to find and destroy ley line 'anchors' to send the magical power back to the Nexus.

The question is, why is the path of destruction leading east when it should be heading west instead?

passages.title: Projections and Plans
passages.text:
This is a teleportation device. If I had to guess, I'd say that it leads to the surge needle platform floating above the Moonrest Gardens to the southwest.

<name>, I need you to use it to investigate what's up there. It appears that the device works both ways so you shouldn't have to jump off.

I expect that once you teleport up to the top of the surge needle, there will be some sort of apparatus on it to observe.

You should be able to use the teleporter from anywhere within the gardens.

passages.title: Projections and Plans
passages.text:
What you're describing... that's a projection of the Arcanomicon!

<The archmage's show of concern is quickly masked behind an impassive countenance.>

The Arcanomicon is a map of all of the magical ley line intersections in the world. The blue dragonflight has been using it to find and destroy ley line 'anchors' to send the magical power back to the Nexus.

The question is, why is the path of destruction leading east when it should be heading west instead?

passages.title: Strength of Icemist
passages.text:
<Greatmother Icemist bows.>

It is an honor to meet you, hero. It is because of your actions that many of us are here now, alive and ready for battle against the Scourge.

You have done so much for us that it shames me to ask you for your assistance once more. Despite my pleas, my only son, Banthok, left here to go in search of his father, High Chief Icemist. He was last seen heading west, towards Icemist Village. Please find Banthok. I do not know what I would do if I lost my son.

passages.title: Strength of Icemist
passages.text: My father still lives! We must save him! I cannot do it alone, <race>. You must help me!

passages.title: Chains of the Anub'ar
passages.text:
They have my father bound by magical chains in the middle of Icemist Village. From what I have been able to gather, the prison is controlled by three powerful Anub'ar magi - each holding a piece of the key.

Scour Icemist and locate the magi. Kill them and take their key fragments. With all three pieces we might be able to free my father. Once he is free...

Retribution will come swiftly.

passages.title: Chains of the Anub'ar
passages.text: Bring me those key fragments!

passages.title: Chains of the Anub'ar
passages.text:
Yes, this will work.

<Banthok expertly manipulates the key fragments.>

Here it is, <class>. With this key, my father will be freed of the Anub'ar prison.

passages.title: The Focus on the Beach
passages.text:
The mage hunter forces are active on the Glittering Strand to the south of Moonrest Gardens. My guess is that you'll find a heavily guarded focus on the beach and a captain who is in charge of it.

No doubt the captain will have some sort of controlling device on their person. Get the controller and use it on the focus.

With any luck, we'll be able to get some more information about what they're really up to out there.

passages.title: The Focus on the Beach
passages.text:
How very odd that it imprinted this information upon you magically.

So, not only do we know that they've redirected the flow of the power coming out of the Moonrest Gardens, but we now know that the power is being purposefully changed in some way. Just what are they up to with all of that magic?

I don't like where this is leading, <name>, not one bit!

passages.title: The Focus on the Beach
passages.text:
The mage hunter forces are active on the Glittering Strand to the south of Moonrest Gardens. My guess is that you'll find a heavily guarded focus on the beach and a captain who is in charge of it.

No doubt the captain of the force down there will have some sort of controlling device on their person. Get the controller and use it on the focus.

With any skill on your part, we'll be able to get some more information about what they're really up to out there.

passages.title: The Focus on the Beach
passages.text:
How very odd that it imprinted this information upon you magically.

So, not only do we know that they've redirected the flow of the power coming out of the Moonrest Gardens, but we now know that the power is being purposefully changed in some way. Just what are they up to with all of that magic?

I don't like where this is leading, <name>.

passages.title: A Letter for Home
passages.text:
You find a letter secreted in the lining of her robes. It reads:

"Father,

I'm sorry for disappearing on you. If you're reading this letter, then I'm dead.

I've been forced to work for Malygos's armies under threat that our family would be killed if I didn't. I feel so ashamed.

If there's anything that you can do to fight them, don't worry about me. I have them fooled and I'm sabotaging them from the inside.

I love you, Daddy!

Em"

Commander Saia Azuresteel will want to see this!

passages.title: A Letter for Home
passages.text:
A letter for me?

<The commander studies your face a moment.>

I suppose not... must be bad news.

passages.title: A Letter for Home
passages.text:
Oh no... and we sent you down there to kill her, didn't we?

<The commander shakes her head and sighs.>

I'm sorry. I'll see to it that the letter is delivered to her father, Archmage Malin in Stormwind, right away. Don't worry, you won't be implicated... it wasn't your fault.

Try to put it out of your mind. There was no way that you could have known, <name>.

passages.title: Voices From the Dust
passages.text:
<Drakuru places the Eye of the Prophets on his brow and the Heart of the Ancients on his chest.>

We be close, mon, very close!
