passages.title: Learning The Reins
passages.text:
Most of the tournament's competitions require competitors to master the command of a mount in battle. In order to familiarize you with mounted combat, we've put up training dummies all over the northern part of the tournament grounds.

Visit the stables outside the pavilion, equip your lance, and mount up on the Sunreaver hawkstrider. Familiarize yourself with the mount and use its abilities to defeat the three different kinds of training dummies.

passages.title: Learning The Reins
passages.text: How goes the mounted combat practice?

passages.title: Learning The Reins
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Mounted combat is often hard to pick up for those accustomed to fighting on foot. I have no doubt that you'll continue to improve with practice, which is more than I can say for some warriors.

passages.title: Up To The Challenge
passages.text:
When you have mastered the skills of the aspirant, you may choose to take the aspirant's challenge. The challenge will test your mounted combat skills and assess whether or not you're prepared to become a valiant. Should you pass, you will be able to join your capital city's delegation as a valiant.

When you are ready to begin the challenge, return to me.

passages.title: Up To The Challenge
passages.text: Do you wish to take the aspirant's challenge?

passages.title: Up To The Challenge
passages.text: Very well, I will make the arrangements.

passages.title: The Aspirant's Challenge
passages.text:
You have trained hard as an aspirant, <name>, and now the time has come to test your mounted combat skills against a skilled opponent.

Equip your lance, then go to the stables outside the pavilion and mount up on the stabled Quel'dorei steed.

At the Aspirants' Ring on the northern side of the tournament grounds, you'll find Squire David. He'll make certain that you're ready for the fight and call out your opponent.

Good luck, <name>. May your horse be steady and your aim true.

passages.title: The Aspirant's Challenge
passages.text: Congratulations are in order, <name>. You have bested your challenger and earned the right to advance to the rank of valiant.

passages.title: The Aspirant's Challenge
passages.text:
You have trained hard as an aspirant, <name>, and now the time has come to test your mounted combat skills against an experienced opponent.

Equip your lance, then go to the stables outside the pavilion and mount the Sunreaver hawkstrider.

At the Aspirants' Ring on the northern side of the tournament grounds, you'll find a human child called Squire David. He'll ask if you're ready for the fight and call out your opponent.

Good luck, <name>. May your mount be steady and your aim true.

passages.title: The Aspirant's Challenge
passages.text: Congratulations are in order, <name>. You have bested your challenger and earned the right to advance to the rank of valiant.

passages.title: Threat From Above
passages.text:
Highlord Tirion Fordring has doubled the guard since your exposure of the Cult of the Damned's infiltrator. He doesn't believe that they will stop just because their Black Knight has been defeated.

Our skytalon scouts have reported sighting a frost wyrm named Chillmaw leading a cult raiding party. If we don't intercept them, the tournament will come under attack. The scouts reporting seeing Chillmaw to the southwest, flying over the area between the Ironwall Rampart and Aldur'thar.

passages.title: Threat From Above
passages.text: <name>, you and your allies have spared the tournament from a devastating attack. Though our skytalon riders are brave, they  have their hands full keeping the peace on the tournament grounds and would be hard-pressed to defend the skies against the cult's attack. You have the thanks of the Argent Crusade and all who have gathered here to compete.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Stormwind
passages.text:
You've proven yourself worthy of competing under the banner of Stormwind, <name>. Now, you should introduce yourself to Marshal Jacob Alerius, who leads the Stormwind delegation. As Stormwind's grand champion, he will enter you into the tournament on behalf of the city and oversee your training and testing as valiant.

It has been an honor working with you, <name>, and I wish you luck in the competition ahead.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Stormwind
passages.text: Welcome aboard then, Valiant <name>. The Stormwind delegation is proud to count you among its members.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Ironforge
passages.text:
You've proven yourself worthy of competing under the banner of Ironforge, <name>. Now, you should introduce yourself to Lana Stouthammer, who leads the Ironforge delegation. As Ironforge's grand champion, she will enter you into the tournament on behalf of the city and oversee your training and testing as valiant.

It has been an honor working with you, <name>, and I wish you luck in the competition ahead.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Ironforge
passages.text: It's good to meet you, valiant. Ironforge needs competitors like you to prevail in the tournament.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Gnomeregan
passages.text:
You've proven yourself worthy of competing under the banner of Gnomeregan, <name>. Now, you should introduce yourself to Ambrose Boltspark, who leads the Gnomeregan delegation. As the gnomish grand champion, he will enter you into the tournament on behalf of the city and oversee your training and testing as valiant.

It has been an honor working with you, <name>, and I wish you luck in the competition ahead.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Gnomeregan
passages.text: Welcome aboard then, Valiant <name>. The Gnomeregan delegation is proud to count you among its members.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Darnassus
passages.text:
You've proven yourself worthy of competing under the banner of Darnassus, <name>. Now, you should introduce yourself to Jaelyne Evensong, who leads the Darnassus delegation. As the night elf grand champion, she will enter you into the tournament on behalf of the city and oversee your training and testing as valiant.

It has been an honor working with you, <name>, and I wish you luck in the competition ahead.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Darnassus
passages.text: Welcome to the Darnassus tournament delegation, <name>. It will be a pleasure to train and compete alongside you.

passages.title: A Valiant Of The Exodar
passages.text:
You've proven yourself worthy of competing under the banner of the Exodar, <name>. Now, you should introduce yourself to Colosos, who leads the Exodar delegation. As the draenei grand champion, he will enter you into the tournament on behalf of the city and oversee your training and testing as valiant.

It has been an honor working with you, <name>, and I wish you luck in the competition ahead.

passages.title: A Valiant Of The Exodar
passages.text: Welcome aboard then, Valiant <name>. The Exodar's delegation is proud to count you among its members.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Orgrimmar
passages.text:
You've proven yourself worthy of competing under the banner of Orgrimmar, <name>. Now, you should speak with Mokra the Skullcrusher, who leads Orgrimmar's competitors. As Orgrimmar's grand champion, he will enter you into the tournament on behalf of the city and oversee your training and testing as valiant.

It has been an honor working with you, <name>, and I wish you luck in the competition ahead.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Orgrimmar
passages.text: So you want to compete for Orgrimmar? Just because you've beaten up a few dummies doesn't mean you'll win, but you'll be training with the best from now on.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Sen'jin
passages.text:
You've proven yourself worthy of competing under the banner of Sen'jin, <name>. Now, you should speak with Zul'tore who leads Sen'jin's warriors. As the troll grand champion, he will enter you into the tournament on behalf of the city and oversee your training and testing as valiant.

It has been an honor working with you, <name>, and I wish you luck in the competition ahead.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Sen'jin
passages.text: You think you have what it takes to compete for Sen'jin? I think we'll be finding out.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Thunder Bluff
passages.text:
You've proven yourself worthy of competing under the banner of Thunder Bluff, <name>. Now, you should speak with Runok Wildmane, who leads Thunder Bluff's competitors. As Thunder Bluff's grand champion, he will enter you into the tournament on behalf of the city and oversee your training and testing as valiant.

It has been an honor working with you, <name>, and I wish you luck in the competition ahead.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Thunder Bluff
passages.text: On behalf of Thunder Bluff and its warriors, I welcome you, <name>. Always fight honorably and bravely beneath our banner.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Undercity
passages.text:
You've proven yourself worthy of competing under the banner of the Undercity, <name>. Now, you should speak with Deathstalker Visceri, who leads the Undercity delegation. As grand champion, he will enter you into the tournament on behalf of the city and oversee your training and testing as valiant.

It has been an honor working with you, <name>, and I wish you luck in the competition ahead.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Undercity
passages.text: Welcome to the Undercity delegation. <name>. As a valiant, you'll train with us to prepare you for the highest level of competition.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Silvermoon
passages.text:
You've proven yourself worthy of competing under the banner of Silvermoon, <name>. Now, you should speak with Eressea Dawnsinger, who leads the Silvermoon delegation. As Silvermoon's grand champion, she will enter you into the tournament on behalf of the city and oversee your training and testing as valiant.

It has been an honor working with you, <name>, and I wish you luck in the competition ahead.

passages.title: A Valiant Of Silvermoon
passages.text: So you want to compete for Silvermoon? Very well. I'll add you to the rolls and you may begin working with the other valiants immediately.

passages.title: The Valiant's Charge
passages.text:
In your training as a valiant, you'll have the chance to test your skills against valiants representing other cities. Although a valiant's battles are not a formal part of the competition, you will learn valuable lessons about the fighting styles and weaknesses of your opponents.

The valiants are a spirited lot, competing amongst themselves for honor and notoriety.

Train as a valiant until you are confident of your ability to best all who face you, then bring me the seals you have earned.

passages.title: The Valiant's Charge
passages.text: Are you ready to demonstrate your mastery of the valiant's skills?

passages.title: The Valiant's Charge
passages.text: Impressive, valiant. I will make the arrangements for your test immediately.

passages.title: The Valiant's Challenge
passages.text:
You are nearly ready to compete on behalf of Stormwind in the grand melee. To prove yourself worthy to enter the lists on behalf of our city, you must defeat a champion of the Argent Crusade.

Go to the stables outside the pavilion, equip your lance, and mount up. Speak to Squire Danny at the Argent Valiants' Ring on the western edge of the grounds. The squire will call out your opponent when you're ready.

After the battle is concluded, we will speak of the outcome.

passages.title: The Valiant's Challenge
passages.text: Have you overcome the Argent champion?

passages.title: The Valiant's Challenge
passages.text: You have proven yourself worthy of the title of champion, <name>. You will compete at the tournament's highest level on behalf of Stormwind, riding in the grand melee with your weapon at the ready and our mighty pennant at your back.

passages.title: Valiant Of Gnomeregan
passages.text:
Welcome, champion. Word of your combat prowess has already reached my ears. Gnomeregan's delegation could really benefit from a <class> like you.

You will train and rise through the ranks as you have before, but when you are named a champion of Gnomeregan, your squire will have the option of carrying our banner into battle.

passages.title: Valiant Of Gnomeregan
passages.text: We're proud to count you among us, <name>, and we look forward to training with you.

passages.title: Valiant Of Orgrimmar
passages.text:
So, you have become a champion? Then, you have proven yourself a worthy combatant and I would proudly welcome you into Orgrimmar's delegation.

You will train and rise through the ranks as you have before, but when you are named a champion of Orgrimmar, your gruntling will have the option of carrying our banner into battle.

passages.title: Valiant Of Orgrimmar
passages.text: Welcome, then, <name>. I look forward to watching you train with my men.

passages.title: Valiant Of Thunder Bluff
passages.text:
Welcome, champion. As grand champion of the Thunder Bluff delegation, I would be honored to welcome you into our ranks, if you are willing.

You will train and rise through the ranks as you have before, but when you are named a champion of Thunder Bluff, your gruntling will have the option of carrying our banner into battle.

passages.title: Valiant Of Thunder Bluff
passages.text: I am honored that you have chosen to join our delegation. I know you will make us proud, <name>.

passages.title: Valiant Of Undercity
passages.text:
Welcome, champion. The Forsaken delegation could always use more <class>s like you. Would you join us?

You will train and rise through the ranks as you have before, but when you are named a champion of the Undecity, your gruntling will have the option of carrying our banner into battle.

passages.title: Valiant Of Undercity
passages.text: You have chosen wisely, <name>. Both of us will benefit from this arrangement.

passages.title: Valiant Of Silvermoon
passages.text:
So, you have become a champion? Then, you have proven yourself a worthy combatant and I would proudly welcome you into Silvermoon's delegation.

You will train and rise through the ranks as you have before, but when you are named a champion of Silvermoon, your gruntling will have the option of carrying our banner into battle.

passages.title: Valiant Of Silvermoon
passages.text: It will be an honor training and competing with you, <name>.

passages.title: To the Rescue!
passages.text:
You're coming with me, <name>.

There's no one else that I can spare, and we cannot afford for Splintertree to be lost.

Prepare yourself, and speak to me again when you are ready.

passages.title: To the Rescue!
passages.text: Work complete!

passages.title: To the Rescue!
passages.text:
Gorka's death was not in vain, <name>.

Splintertree would have certainly fallen if we hadn't come when we did.

Now we must get to work shoring up her defenses.

This isn't over....

passages.text:
You are nearly ready to compete on behalf of Ironforge in the grand melee. To prove yourself worthy to enter the lists on behalf of our city, you must defeat a champion of the Argent Crusade.

Go to the stables outside the pavilion, equip your lance, and mount up. Speak to Squire Danny at the Argent Valiants' Ring on the western edge of the grounds. The squire will call out your opponent when you're ready.

After the battle is concluded, we will speak of the outcome.

passages.text: Have you overcome the Argent champion?

passages.text:

Go to the stables outside the pavilion, equip your lance, and mount up. Speak to Squire Danny at the Argent Valiants' Ring on the western edge of the grounds. The squire will call out your opponent when you're ready.

After the battle is concluded, we will speak of the outcome.

passages.title: Playing With Felfire
passages.text:
<Draaka leans down to speak to you.>

Listen... Before you say anything, I KNOW we're not to meddle with demonic energies....

But look around you! These are desperate times, <class>.

We'll most likely die here, regardless. May as well go out in a blaze of glory, I say!

So... Are you in?

Take this canister and go southeast to Felfire Hill. Use it near the patches of felfire and bring it back to me when you've filled it.

Oh, and best not to mention this to anyone....

passages.title: Playing With Felfire
passages.text: Did you fill up that canister for me, <class>?

passages.title: Playing With Felfire
passages.text:
Oh, yes!

This will teach those elves, just you watch!

passages.title: A Blade Fit For A Champion
passages.text:
Good, honest, honed steel may not carry the day. The other combatants are using enchanted blades and I find myself at a disadvantage, but all is not lost.

There's an old legend from Grizzly Hills about a maiden cursed with a frog's form to protect the blade she has long guarded. She lives among the lake frogs on the shore of Ashwood Lake, just east of Ashwood Post. The only thing said to break the curse is a kiss, freely given. Apply this balm before kissing anything, <name>. Otherwise, you'll catch warts.

passages.title: A Blade Fit For A Champion
passages.text: Were you able to recover the blade?

passages.title: A Blade Fit For A Champion
passages.text: So the tales were true? This is a fine blade and I have no doubt that it will serve me well in the tournament. You have my thanks, <name>.

passages.title: A Worthy Weapon
passages.text:
Of all the times to have such rotten luck!

My tournament blade has gone missing. I've heard the bards telling tales of travelers offering winter hyacinths to a lonely maiden in return for gifts. Those hyacinths grow only on the ice flowing from the Ironwall Dam, on Crystalsong Forest's northwestern border with Icecrown. Gather the flowers and take them to the circle of lamps in Drak'Mar Lake in northeastern Dragonblight, near Zul'Drak and Grizzly Hills. Ask the lonely maiden for a worthy blade.

passages.title: A Worthy Weapon
passages.text: Were the wandering bard's tales true? Have you brought a blade?

passages.title: A Worthy Weapon
passages.text:
<The grand champion accepts the Blade of Drak'Mar from you.>

A fine weapon, and perfectly balanced. It will serve me well in the next match.

passages.title: The Edge Of Winter
passages.text:
Curse that death knight for breaking my sword!

In southern Crystalsong Forest, overlooking the Crystal Vice's exit, you will find Lord Everblaze. Kill him and take the everburning ember from his corpse.

Bring it to the center of Winter's Breath Lake in northern Howling Fjord, and use it to free the maiden encased in ice. She is the guardian of an ancient sword and will award it to whoever frees her.

Prove your worth and earn the weapon that she has guarded for so long, <name>.

passages.title: The Edge Of Winter
passages.text: Did you win the blade I seek?

passages.title: The Edge Of Winter
passages.text: The blade is as fine as the stories say. It would seem there's little reason to complete the repairs on my customary blade. Winter's Edge is far superior and I will continue to carry it. You have my thanks, <name>.

passages.title: A Valiant's Field Training
passages.text:
The tournament is a time for testing your skills against your peers, but we must not forget that the real enemy, the Scourge, will not wait. As you hone your skills against others, so should you maintain your edge in combat against the enemy.

Travel to the area southwest of the Valley of Fallen Heroes and north of Corp'rethar. There, the Scourge raises dead heroes and turns them against us. Defeat these minions of the Scourge, do honor to our allies, and keep yourself prepared for combat.

passages.title: A Valiant's Field Training
passages.text: Have you tested yourself in combat against the Scourge?

passages.title: A Valiant's Field Training
passages.text: Welcome back from your exercises, <name>. Even while we practice for the competition, it's good to remind ourselves that the Scourge is still out there.

I suggest you do the same. The valiants practice in the ring just outside our tent. Equip your lance, go to the stables outside the pavilion and mount the stabled Ironforge ram, then challenge other Alliance valiants.

Hrmphh...

passages.text: The blade is as fine as the stories say. It would seem there's little reason to complete the repairs on my customary blade. Winter's Edge is far superior and I will continue to carry it. You have my thanks, <name>.

passages.title: A Valiant's Field Training
passages.text:
The tournament is a time for testing your skills against your peers, but we must not forget that the real enemy, the Scourge, will not wait. As you hone your skills against others, so should you maintain your edge in combat against the enemy.

Travel to the area southwest of the Valley of Fallen Heroes and north of Corp'rethar. There, the Scourge raises dead heroes and turns them against us. Defeat these minions of the Scourge, do honor to our allies, and keep yourself prepared for combat.

passages.title: A Valiant's Field Training
passages.text: A good day of training will never hurt anyone. It's good to see you keeping up.

passages.title: The Grand Melee
passages.text:
The grand melee is the most important of the tournament's competitions. Victory will not be easy, but I am confident that we will win. You must practice with your mount until the two of you work as one.

It will help prepare you for the rigors of tournament combat.

Go to the stables outside the pavilion, equip your lance, mount the stabled Darkspear raptor, and challenge the valiants. They wait in the Horde Valiants' Ring just outside our tent.

passages.title: The Grand Melee
passages.text: Have you completed your training for the grand melee?

passages.title: The Grand Melee
passages.text: Training against other valiants will quickly teach you what you need to know to best them. Keep it up and you'll have no trouble defeating them in competition.

passages.title: A Blade Fit For A Champion
passages.text:
I've heard that the Alliance champions are seeking after ancient blades for their warriors. We can't afford to let them have that kind of advantage.

There's an old legend from Grizzly Hills about a maiden cursed with a frog's form to protect the blade she has long guarded. She lives among the lake frogs on the shore of Ashwood Lake, just east of Ashwood Post. The only thing said to break the curse is a kiss, freely given. Apply this balm before kissing anything, <name>. Otherwise, you'll catch warts.

passages.title: A Blade Fit For A Champion
passages.text: Were you able to recover the blade?

passages.title: A Blade Fit For A Champion
passages.text: So the tales were true? This blade should be enough to best anything those Alliance entrants can come up with.

passages.title: A Worthy Weapon
passages.text:
Of all the times to have such rotten luck!

My tournament blade has gone missing. I've heard the bards telling tales of travelers offering winter hyacinths to a lonely maiden in return for gifts. Those hyacinths grow only on the ice flowing from the Ironwall Dam, on Crystalsong Forest's northwestern border with Icecrown. Gather the flowers and take them to the circle of lamps in Drak'Mar Lake in northeastern Dragonblight, near Zul'Drak and Grizzly Hills. Ask the lonely maiden for a worthy blade.

passages.title: A Worthy Weapon
passages.text: Were the wandering bard's tales true? Have you brought a blade?

passages.title: A Worthy Weapon
passages.text: This is a fine weapon that will help me crush the competition. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Edge Of Winter
passages.text:
Curse that death knight for breaking my sword!

In southern Crystalsong Forest, overlooking the Crystal Vice's exit, you will find Lord Everblaze. Kill him and take the everburning ember from his corpse.

Bring it to the center of Winter's Breath Lake in northern Howling Fjord, and use it to free the maiden encased in ice. She is the guardian of an ancient sword and will award it to whoever frees her.

Prove your worth and earn the weapon that she has guarded for so long, <name>.

passages.text: Did you win the blade?

passages.text: Have you tested yourself in combat against the Scourge?

passages.title: A Valiant's Field Training

passages.title: The Grand Melee
passages.text:
The grand melee is the most important of the tournament's competitions. Victory will not be easy, but I am confident that we will win. You must practice with your mount until the two of you work as one.

It will help prepare you for the rigors of tournament combat.

Go to the stables outside the pavilion, equip your lance, mount the stabled Silvermoon hawkstrider, and challenge the valiants. They wait in the Horde Valiants' Ring just outside our tent.

passages.title: The Grand Melee
passages.text: Have you completed your training for the grand melee?

passages.title: The Grand Melee
passages.text: Training against the other valiants will sharpen your claws and hone your battle instincts. When the competition begins, you will be ready.

passages.title: Threat From Above
passages.text:
The Argent Crusade has doubled the guard since your exposure of the Cult of the Damned's infiltrator. They know the cultists won't stop until they've destroyed this area and thwarted the tournament.

The Argent Crusade's scouts have reported sighting a frost wyrm named Chillmaw leading a cult raiding party.

You must intercept and destroy them before they attack. The scouts reporting seeing Chillmaw to the southwest, flying over the area between the Ironwall Rampart and Aldur'thar.

passages.title: Threat From Above
passages.text:
<name>, you have spared the tournament from a devastating attack. The Argent Crusade and all who gather here are in our debt and we'll make certain they remember it. For all their bluster about providing protection, the peacekeepers and skytalons spend more time breaking up drunken brawls than keeping us safe from the Scourge.

It's no matter. We always protect our own.

passages.title: Taking Battle To The Enemy
passages.text:
The coliseum is perched in the most dangerous part of the world, <name>. The territory we've taken from the Scourge has been paid for in blood and misery, yet the enemy continues to strike back with a seemingly limitless army. To make matters worse, this undead army is supported and assisted by mortal sympathizers, the Cult of the Damned.

Go forth into Icecrown and slay any cultists you encounter.

passages.title: Taking Battle To The Enemy
passages.text: You are a true champion, <name>, both inside the ring and on the field. We must all be vigilant against the Scourge and you are a great example to our brethren and your own people.

passages.title: Among the Champions
passages.text:
As a champion, you have mastered the art of mounted combat, besting challengers of all levels. When the tournament begins, those you have defeated will have redoubled their efforts and will seek to avenge their losses to you.

It would be wise to continue practicing your skills against the combatants waiting in the Ring of Champions. Equip your lance, go to the stables on the southern side of the grounds. then mount up on any mount you're permitted to use, and face the champions.

passages.title: Among the Champions
passages.text: Have you finished training with the other champions?

passages.title: Among the Champions
passages.text: Well done. Training against the other champions is one of the best ways to prepare yourself for tournament competition. I know you'll make the Alliance proud, <name>.

passages.title: Taking Battle To The Enemy
passages.text:
While we all play at mock combat, it will do us good to remember that the real enemy surrounds us. The Argent Crusade wants to use competition to find the best fighters, but we can tell that by who returns from battle. Let's show the paladins that we are willing to take battle to the Cult of the Damned, even while making preparations for the tournament.

Go forth into Icecrown and slay any of the cultists you encounter. They have a strong presence around Aldur'thar and Deathspeaker's Watch.

passages.title: Taking Battle To The Enemy
passages.text: You have done well in demonstrating our commitment to fighting the Scourge, no matter where we are or what we are doing.

passages.title: The Shadewalker
passages.text:
Now that the demon gates have been destroyed, the power of the forest must be replenished. The Forest Heart must be retrieved!

Gaivan Shadewalker, a powerful druid of the claw, has gone southwest, past Felfire Hill, to the Dor'Danil Barrow Den. Therein rests the Forest Heart. It is protected by the druids of Ashenvale deep below the ground.

Seek out Gaivan and tell him of what has transpired, <name>.

passages.title: The Shadewalker
passages.text:
You are brave to come here, <class>, but you may be too late. All of the druids are either dead or have been driven insane.

Still, your tale is intriguing, and if what you say is true, then Gnarl must have the Forest Heart and soon, or Ashenvale will begin to wither!

passages.title: Among the Champions
passages.text:
As a champion, you have mastered the art of mounted combat, overcoming challengers of all levels. You must make certain that you can defeat anyone you face when the tournament begins.

You should continue honing your own skills and learning more about the weaknesses of your opponents. Champions representing all cities practice in the Ring of Champions near the stables. Go to the stables, equip your lance, and pick any mount you're permitted to ride, then face the champions.

passages.title: Among the Champions
passages.text: Have you finished training with the other champions?

passages.title: Among the Champions
passages.text: You handle your mount well, <name>. In time, your competitors will learn to fear you.

passages.title: Rain of Destruction
passages.text:
Just in time, <class>. The elves have launched another attack!

From the guard towers, use the accursed ore to mark targets for Draaka.

Her projectiles will strike your target and erupt in fel magic flame, destroying any nearby enemies.

There is strong prejudice against the use of demonic magics. Unjustified, but real nonetheless. For this reason, I will transform you into an imp for the duration of the mission to prevent you from being identified.

passages.title: Rain of Destruction
passages.text: Has the enemy fallen, <name>?

passages.title: Rain of Destruction
passages.text:
Did you feel it, <name>!?

The raw fel power seething through your being?

There is nothing else like it!

passages.title: The Goblin with Two Brains
passages.text:
Do you see them, along the shore? Such magnificent specimens! Look at their primitive society in action, working like a well-oiled machine from the lowliest grunt to their leader, who I've named "King Burgrurble."

I must study their brains.

Can you procure an intact Slobberfang Murloc brain stem for me? Kill them - for science!

passages.title: Blood of the Weak
passages.text:
We knew the elves wouldn't go down without a fight, but no one expected them to be able to lay siege to Splintertree...

Time for them to pay for their actions!

Nearby, in the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, lies something very dear to the enemy - the Forest Heart.

I need someone to make their way to the heart and corrupt it.

That someone is you, <name>.

First though, bring my axe to Durak here in the mines. He'll make use of the blood of our enemies.

passages.title: Blood of the Weak
passages.text:
Tainting the Forest's Heart?

How ruthless - an utterly vicious blow....

I adore the idea!

passages.title: To Catch a Fish-Thing
passages.text:
Look at these results! Such a unique electrochemical makeup -- ah, but I wouldn't suspect a lowly <class> would understand the magnormity of what I've discovered here. I'll need a live specimen.

I would acquire one myself, but apparently they bite.

Here, I've configured this trap to hone in on their unique brain patterns. Just set the trap, then hit this button to slurp up a Slobberfang. But first, I'll need you to sign this indemnification waiver. This technology is bleeding edge!

passages.title: Pierce Their Heart!
passages.text:
There...

The blood of the fallen Kaldorei is turned. It can now be used on the Forest Heart in Dor'Danil Barrow Den. Doing so will utterly corrupt it.

The sacred relic of the arrogant elves will be turned against them. How poetic!

<Durak laughs cruelly.>

The barrow den lies nestled against the hills to the southeast. One of my imps has laid a blood trail from the entrance to the heart.

Make haste! Kadrak is not likely to be in a patient mood.

Off you go, <class>.

passages.title: Pierce Their Heart!
passages.text:
It is done?

Good work, <name>. That will gradually weaken their forces, as well as their spirit.

passages.title: Demon Duty
passages.text:
Listen, <class>, I know this assault on Splintertree has everyone worked up, but if we forget about the satyr portals we'll come out of this crisis to face an even larger one.

<Locke stares at your expressionless face.>

You don't know about the portals?

To the northeast, in the regions of Satyrnaar and Xavian, the satyrs are attempting to summon in demons to bolster their numbers.

We must be vigilant in closing those portals, no matter what issues we face here!

passages.title: Demon Duty
passages.text:
Good work, <race>.

One less thing we have to worry about!

passages.title: Threat From Above
passages.text:
Highlord Tirion Fordring has doubled the guard since your exposure of the Cult of the Damned's infiltrator. He doesn't believe that they will stop just because their Black Knight has been defeated.

Our skytalon scouts have reported sighting a frost wyrm named Chillmaw leading a cult raiding party. If we don't intercept them, the tournament will come under attack. The scouts reporting seeing Chillmaw to the southwest, flying over the area between the Ironwall Rampart and Aldur'thar.

passages.title: Threat From Above
passages.text: Have you defeated the Cult of the Damned raiding party?

passages.title: Threat From Above
passages.text: <name>, you and your allies have spared the tournament from a devastating attack. Though our skytalon riders are brave, they  have their hands full keeping the peace on the tournament grounds and would be hard-pressed to defend the skies against the cult's attack. You have the thanks of the Argent Crusade and all who have gathered here to compete.

passages.title: Among the Champions
passages.text:
As a champion, you have mastered the art of mounted combat, overcoming challengers of all levels. You must make certain that you can defeat anyone you face when the tournament begins.

You should continue honing your own skills and learning more about the weaknesses of your opponents. Champions representing all cities practice in the Ring of Champions near the stables. Go to the stables, equip your lance, pick any mount you can ride, then face the champions in practice bouts.

passages.title: Among the Champions
passages.text: Have you finished training with the other champions?

passages.title: Among the Champions
passages.text: You handle your mount well, <name>. In time, your competitors will learn to fear you.

passages.title: Making Stumps
passages.text:
As you've been told by now, we are to escort a diplomat from within the besieged lumber camp to safety.

As it stands, that's simply impossible. The elves have a thousand arrows trained on the camp's exits.

First we must create a diversion - something that will take their eyes off of the camp for a time.

My idea is simple. Take this axe and cut down the trees they've been nurturing in the region.

When you're through, light the brazier here to speak with me again.

passages.title: Making Stumps
passages.text:
Nice work, <name>.

You've demoralized the enemy and harvested resources for the Horde.

Let's hope the rest of the mission goes as well.

passages.title: Heroic: The Celestial Planetarium
passages.text:
Listen, <lad/lass>! Azeroth's fate is at stake here.

Our only chance is to get to the Celestial Planetarium in time to find this Algalon and stop him from beaming back any messages to his Titan masters.

Locate the Celestial Planetarium and come back with any information you get. We might still have some time to prepare for Algalon's arrival.

passages.title: Heroic: The Celestial Planetarium
passages.text: Did you find it, <name>?

passages.title: Heroic: The Celestial Planetarium
passages.text:
It's locked?  Figures!

I'll let Brann know... maybe he can uncover something in the Archivum.

passages.title: Heroic: Algalon
passages.text:
You really did it, <name>. Take the sigils to the Archivum Console and see if you can gain access to the Celestial Planetarium.

You best hurry, <lad/lass>. Time is of the essence.

passages.title: Heroic: Algalon
passages.text: The console's bright lights scan the glass surface repeatedly, as if awaiting some form of input.

passages.title: Heroic: Algalon
passages.text:
Stand by for verification.

Access to the Celestial Planetarium granted.  Please retrieve your key.

passages.title: Heroic: All Is Well That Ends Well
passages.text:
We'd best hurry now, <name>. We're going to have to transmit the reply-code from Dalaran.

Take it to Rhonin, I will meet you there.

passages.title: Heroic: All Is Well That Ends Well
passages.text: You're ready, <name>?

passages.title: Heroic: All Is Well That Ends Well
passages.text: You're here.  Let us hope this works.  For all our sakes.

passages.title: Heroic: Freya's Sigil
passages.text:
Freya's Sigil is going to be one of the tougher ones, I reckon.

According to the Archivum, the essence of the Sigil is tied to her three elder servants, Brightleaf, Ironbranch and Stonebark. Should any of the elders be harmed, the Sigil's integrity will be compromised.

Sparing the elders, however, means that Freya will be more powerful when you face her.

What can I say, <name>. We're stuck between a rock and hard place.

passages.title: Heroic: Freya's Sigil
passages.text: Freya's sigil, <name>?  Do ye have it?

passages.title: Heroic: Freya's Sigil
passages.text: Excellent job, <name>.  We're one step closer to saving Azeroth!

passages.title: Heroic: Hodir's Sigil
passages.text:
Hodir's Sigil won't be easy to obtain. Not only are ye going to have to defeat Hodir himself, but yer going to have to do it before he destroys the chest that contains it!

Check the Archivum console if you need more information. That thing contains more knowledge than all of the world's libraries put together!

passages.title: Heroic: Hodir's Sigil
passages.text: Did ye obtain the sigil, <name>?

passages.title: Heroic: Hodir's Sigil
passages.text: Ye did it!  I don't know how, but ye did!

passages.title: Heroic: Thorim's Sigil
passages.text:
Thorim's not himself, <name>. He's come under a dark influence.

An evil presence under the guise of an illusion pretends to be his lost wife, Sif.

Ye can't let him be overcome by this impostor's spell. If he does, the location of his sigil might forever be lost!

Yer going to have to beat some sense into him and yer going to have to do it quick.

As always, the Archivum Console will give ye all the gory details... even the ones ye don't like.

passages.title: Heroic: Thorim's Sigil
passages.text: Well, <name>?  Do ye have it?

passages.title: Heroic: Thorim's Sigil
passages.text:
Ye never cease to impress, <name>.

Ye and me are having a pint together after all this is done, ye hear me?

passages.title: Heroic: Mimiron's Sigil
passages.text:
Mimiron's a clever one. His entire abode is rigged with some sort of self-destruction mechanism.

Unfortunately yer gonna have to race against it if ye want to get his sigil. Check the Archivum Console for more details if ye need them.

passages.title: Heroic: Mimiron's Sigil
passages.text: Were you able to obtain the sigil, <name>?

passages.title: Heroic: Mimiron's Sigil
passages.text: I've got to hand it to you, <name>.  Our odds might not be the best, but I feel a lot better with you lending a hand.

passages.title: Mastery Of Melee
passages.text:
The heart of tournament competition is mounted melee combat. Take this lance and mount the stabled Quel'dorei steed just outside the pavilion.

Once you're mounted, seek out Jeran Lockwood. He's on the northern edge of the tournament grounds at the training area east of the Aspirants' Ring. Jeran will instruct you on how to use your defenses to keep you safe while attacking a melee target at close range.

passages.title: Mastery Of Melee
passages.text: Keep the words of the master in mind as you practice with the training dummies.

passages.title: Mastery Of Melee
passages.text:
The heart of tournament competition is mounted melee combat. Take this lance and mount the stabled Sunreaver hawkstrider just outside the pavilion.

Once you're mounted, seek out Jeran Lockwood. He's on the northern edge of the tournament grounds at the training area east of the Aspirants' Ring. Jeran will instruct you on how to use your defenses to keep you safe while attacking a melee target at close range.

passages.title: Mastery Of Melee
passages.text: Keep the words of the master in mind as you practice with the training dummies.

passages.title: The Ghostfish
passages.text:
Any Northrend angler worth <his/her> salt knows about the pygmy suckerfish. It's not edible, but sometimes useful to alchemists.

There is, however, a stealthy fish that hides among the suckerfish in the River's Heart of Sholazar Basin. The phantom ghostfish. When out of water, they become increasingly translucent until they fade away completely. Some hypothesize they return to Sholazar, and others are more... superstitious.

I want you to catch this fish and discover its secret by any means!

passages.title: The Ghostfish
passages.text:
So eating it makes you invisible... what a strange defense this clever fish has developed.

I'd like to digest this for a bit.  Pun not intended, <name>.  Really.  Why don't you come see me tomorrow?

passages.title: Jewel Of The Sewers
passages.text:
Hard to believe that most people fish in the Dalaran Sewers for giant rats and mutated fish. Especially when those waters are filled with priceless jewelry - discarded by broken hearted fools, thieves, and careless drunks.

The trick is to let your hook drag the bottom and don't pull up too hard when you get something. Try it out, <name>. I'd be willing to trade whatever you find for a few trinkets of my own.

passages.title: Jewel Of The Sewers
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: Jewel Of The Sewers
passages.text: Well now, that looks like it could be valuable.  Difficult to know until it's cleaned up and appraised, but I'm still willing to make the trade if you are.

passages.title: Blood Is Thicker
passages.text:
The bloodtooth is a feisty little fish used in a recipe to cure infected wounds. We could use some of them, if you're up to it.

As the name suggests, they've a hunger for blood. The only way I know how to catch the little devils is by creating a blood pool and fishing in it.

Get yourself covered in blood - just slaughter a beast in the Borean Tundra - and then jump in the water. It'll wash right off and create the perfect fishing spot.

passages.title: Blood Is Thicker
passages.text: Any luck with the bloodtooth?  Don't forget what I told you about making blood pools.

passages.title: Blood Is Thicker
passages.text: You are a brave one, <name>.  I hope you didn't lose any extremities making your fishing spot.  If you've still got the fishing bug, come back tomorrow and we'll talk some more.

passages.title: Mastery Of The Shield-Breaker
passages.text:
You'll need to learn how to break through an opponent's defenses to succeed in mounted combat. Take this lance and mount the stabled Quel'dorei steed just outside the pavilion.

Once you're mounted, seek out Valis Windchaser. He'll be on the northern edge of the tournament grounds at the training area east of the Aspirants' Ring. Valis will teach you the basics of using a ranged shield breaker attack to make a ranged target vulnerable.

passages.title: Mastery Of The Shield-Breaker
passages.text: Commit Valis's lesson to memory, <name>. It will mean the difference between winning and losing your mounted combat matches.

passages.title: Disarmed!
passages.text:
I've received word of an unfortunate accident at the Dalaran prison; a guard had his arm severed and thrown into the water by a particularly vicious inmate.

Our first aid clinic promises they can reattach the arm if we bring it back.

You fish long enough in the water outside the prison, and I'd bet my favorite fishing pole that arm will surface. Find that arm, and bring it to Olisarra the Kind here in Dalaran. She'll know what to do.

passages.title: Disarmed!
passages.text: Hi there.  Do you have something for me?

passages.title: Disarmed!
passages.text:
Oh, hello there <name>.  Marcia said you'd be coming by with that poor man's missing arm.

She also gave me this bag to give you as a reward.  It smells horrible, and I'm anxious to make the trade if you don't mind.

passages.title: Mastery Of The Charge
passages.text:
Your strongest attack in mounted combat is undoubtedly the charge. Take this lance and mount the stabled Quel'dorei steed just outside the pavilion.

Once you're mounted, speak with Rugan Steelbelly. He's on the northern edge of the tournament grounds at the training area east of the Aspirants' Ring. Rugan will tell you how to use this powerful ability and teach you some basic strategies.

passages.title: Mastery Of The Charge
passages.text: Have you mastered the use of the charge?

passages.title: Mastery Of The Charge
passages.text: With a teacher like Rugan, you'll be an expert at mounted combat in no time.

passages.text: Commit Valis's lesson to memory, <name>. It will mean the difference between winning and losing your mounted combat matches.

passages.title: Mastery Of The Charge
passages.text: Have you mastered the use of the charge?

passages.title: Mastery Of The Charge
passages.text: With experience and practice, you will become deadly with the charge.

passages.title: All Apologies
passages.text:
This could be the end of me... Perhaps my actions were not thought out as well as they should have been...

The good news is that we pushed back an attack that would have otherwise meant the end of Splintertree. Let us pray that Saurfang sees it that way.

I am certain to be summoned to Orgrimmar to explain my actions.

Please, <name>, go ahead of me and present this letter to his advisor Eitrigg.

Do what you can to soften his heart towards me.

passages.title: All Apologies
passages.text:
Fools!!

This Draaka woman has allowed herself to be manipulated by a demon!

<Garrosh studies you for a moment.>

And I smell its taint on you as well, <class>....

passages.title: The Looting of Althalaxx
passages.text:
Before you rejoin the battle, <class>, something urgent has come to my attention. My scouts report that the Forsaken are scouring the ruined tower of Althalaxx to our south.

Prior to the assault, that bleak tower housed a fanatical arm of the Shadow Council commanded by the fallen highborne Athrikus Narassin. Narassin is long since dead, but if any of his work survives, we can't allow it out of our sight. Retrieve his research and kill the Forsaken commander who's plundering the ruins.

passages.title: The Looting of Althalaxx
passages.text: Narassin is no longer our concern, but if his life's work should fall to our enemies, centuries of dark wisdom could be called down onto our heads. How goes the hunt?

passages.title: The Looting of Althalaxx
passages.text:
Let's see what we've got here.... By Elune, his notes are scrawled in a half dozen languages. What is this, blood? This archive makes my flesh seethe, but at least it's secure. It will take us some time to decipher these notes.

Oh - your reward? Yes, here. Nice work with those undead scavengers. Now get back to the fight.

passages.title: Contributin' To The Cause
passages.text:
The bestest of the champions come to the chapel to hear the argent confessor speak every day.

You should see how much she inspires them, <name>. Not only do they fight for the Argent Crusade, but they put a lot of money into the collection basket when I take it around.

Maybe you'd like to contribute too?

passages.title: Contributin' To The Cause
passages.text: Do you want to contribute?

passages.title: Contributin' To The Cause
passages.text: Thank you. I just know the crusade will put it to good use!

passages.title: At The Enemy's Gates
passages.text:
Even as we ready for the tournament, Argent Crusade forces prepare the way for an assault on the enemy's stronghold of Icecrown Citadel.

In the Court of Bones in southwestern Icecrown, a few brave crusaders have set up a forward camp on the southern side of Corp'rethar. Equip your lance and mount the stabled campaign charger at the camp, then destroy the Lich King's minions.

Do not fear the masses of boneguard footmen, <name>, for they can easily be trampled under your horse's hooves.

passages.title: At The Enemy's Gates
passages.text: Your bravery on the field has shown the crusaders what they already knew -- that our warriors are more than just parade ground decorations.

passages.title: Toxic Tolerance
passages.text:
You want to ride a Venomhide? Then I've got bad news for you.

The Venomhide Ravasaurs, they're all poison: Poison blood, poison spit, poison skin. You climb on one, you fall off dead in a few hours.

You'd have to build up a resistance to their toxins before I sold you one, and that takes a long, LONG time... you'd need to be splashed with poisonous blood while fighting one numerous times. If you're really interested, the venomhides prefer the northern area of the Marshlands, northwest of here.

passages.title: Toxic Tolerance
passages.text:
You did it? You actually did it?!

Ho ho! Stubborn as my wife, you are.

Do not fear the masses of boneguard footmen, <name>, for they can easily be trampled under your horse's hooves.

passages.title: At The Enemy's Gates
passages.text: Your bravery on the field has shown the crusaders that we are worthy allies.

passages.text: Your bravery on the field has shown the that we are a match for the Argent Crusade's own.

passages.title: Return Fire
passages.text:
The fires are mostly contained, but we have to do something about those wind riders!

Quick, <name>, you have to jump into one of our glaive throwers and return fire!

passages.title: Return Fire
passages.text: There's still more of them bombing us. Please, <name>, shoot them down!

passages.title: Return Fire
passages.text:
We're saved! You've shot down enough of them that we should be able to handle the rest.

I cannot thank you enough, <name>.

passages.text: Have served alongside the crusaders in the Court of Bones?

passages.title: At The Enemy's Gates
passages.text: The Argent Crusade has seen our resolve and they know that our warriors will see this through to the end.

passages.title: Battle Before The Citadel
passages.text:
Even as some of us labor on the tournament, our brothers prepare the way for an assault on the enemy's stronghold of Icecrown Citadel.

In the Court of Bones in southwestern Icecrown, a few brave crusaders have set up a forward camp on the southern side of Corp'rethar. Equip your lance and mount the stabled campaign charger at the camp, then destroy the Lich King's commanders.

Do not fear the masses of boneguard footmen, <name>, for they can easily be trampled under your horse's hooves.

passages.title: Battle Before The Citadel
passages.text: The Argent Crusade is heartened to have paladins like you fighting alongside us in the battle against the Lich King.

In the Court of Bones in southwestern Icecrown, a few brave crusaders have set up a forward camp on the southern side of Corp'rethar. Equip your lance and mount the stabled argent charger at the camp, then destroy the Lich King's commanders.

Do not fear the masses of boneguard footmen, <name>, for they can easily be trampled under your horse's hooves.

passages.title: Battle Before The Citadel
passages.text: The Argent Crusade is heartened to have paladins like you fighting alongside us in the battle against the Lich King.

passages.title: Battle Before The Citadel
passages.text:
As some crusaders prepare for the tournament, they have sent others to make an assault on the enemy's stronghold of Icecrown Citadel.

In the Court of Bones in southwestern Icecrown, a few brave crusaders have set up a forward camp on the southern side of Corp'rethar. Equip your lance and mount the stabled campaign charger at the camp, then destroy the Lich King's commanders.

Do not fear the masses of boneguard footmen, <name>, for they can easily be trampled under your horse's hooves.

passages.title: Battle Before The Citadel
passages.text: Everywhere we have met the Scourge, we have made them fear us, and this campaign is no different.

passages.text:
As some crusaders prepare for the tournament, they have sent others to make an assault on the enemy's stronghold of Icecrown Citadel.

In the Court of Bones in southwestern Icecrown, a few brave crusaders have set up a forward camp on the southern side of Corp'rethar. Equip your lance and mount the stabled campaign charger at the camp, then destroy the Lich King's commanders.

Do not fear the masses of boneguard footmen, <name>, for they can easily be trampled under your horse's hooves.

passages.title: Battle Before The Citadel
passages.text: Have you fought against the enemy in the Court of Bones?

passages.title: Battle Before The Citadel
passages.text: Everywhere we have fought the Scourge, we have taught them to fear us and this campaign will be no different.

passages.title: Wet Work
passages.text:
Listen carefully, <class>.

There are three leaders in this region who are commanding the elves, keeping their focus directed on the lumber camp. Slaying them will certainly cause panic and disarray, hopefully enough for us to successfully complete our mission.

While you're at it, bringing down their scouts can only aid our cause.

passages.title: Wet Work
passages.text:
Well done, <class>.

They're in complete disarray. Just look at them!

passages.title: To The Ramparts!
passages.text:
These woods may be silent but our enemies lurk behind every trunk. I've discovered many an orc with arrows in his back, his weapon still sheathed.

It is treacherous here, behind the lines, but we could use strong arms and sharp minds down at the Mor'shan Ramparts. Kadrak is preparing an offensive from there - he prefers action to talk. You and he will get along.

Speak with me when you are ready and I will fly you there.

passages.title: To The Ramparts!
passages.text: You are just in time, <class>. Old Kulg has been slinking around those woods too long. He grows too cautious, jumping at shadows. We will fear this forest no longer - the time has come to subdue Ashenvale once and for all!

passages.title: As Good as it Gets
passages.text:
Well, <class>, this is as good as it gets.

The elves are scrambling to recover from your recent deeds. There's no better time to break into the lumber camp!

Make your way in and speak with Overseer Gorthak. He'll instruct you as to how best escort the diplomat to safety.

Good luck!

passages.title: As Good as it Gets
passages.text:
<Gorthak sighs disappointedly.>

If only you'd arrived an hour ago....

The diplomat suffered mortal wounds at the hands of an elf assassin.

How the enemy was able to infiltrate the camp undetected remains a mystery.

passages.title: Sheelah's Last Wish
passages.text:
I... I cannot believe she's gone. It all happened so fast....

I understand that I have you to thank for avenging my mistress. For that, you have my gratitude, and that of Silvermoon.

In her wisdom, my lady foresaw this end. She prepared a missive to be delivered in the event that something happened to her.

We were to join an Orgrimmar retinue at the crossroads just north of here. Please, <race>, meet them in our stead and see that the message is delivered.

passages.title: Sheelah's Last Wish
passages.text:
<Gurtar listens as you inform him of Sheelah's passing.>

I'll deliver this to Hellscream personally, <race>.

In the meantime, there's something I need you to do for me....

passages.title: Gurtar's Request
passages.text:
I have a bit of a personal request for you, <class>.

It has been many moons since I have seen my love, Draaka. It will be many more before we are able to be together again. I fear that as time passes, her love for me will wane.

This braid has special meaning to the two of us, as do Thorned Bloodcups, the flower of this region.

I ask that you pluck the flowers and weave them into this twine, then present the gift to Draaka on my behalf.

passages.title: Gurtar's Request
passages.text: Hello, <name>.

passages.title: Gurtar's Request
passages.text:
<Recognizing at once the nature of the gift, Draaka begins to weep.>

Oh, <name>. Thank you for this gift! It means more than you could know.

He hasn't forgotten...

passages.title: Through Fire and Flames
passages.text:
Help me, <class>! Piggy men come burn stables - fire! Fire!

<Dorak wails incoherently before you can settle him down.>

Wolves still chained inside. Someone's got to save the wee wolves!

passages.title: Through Fire and Flames
passages.text: Hot!

passages.title: Through Fire and Flames
passages.text:
You save the wolves! So brave! Someday, maybe you get a wolf just like that to ride.

<Dorak looks at the burning stables, then at the nearby river.>

What should I do now?

passages.title: The Seeds of Life
passages.text:
Something is trying to devour the life of Darkshore from within! I'll ask around to learn more about the - thing - you discovered in the lake. Meanwhile, we need to protect the local wildlife from further harm.

Can you gather some materials for me? I'll need life in all its incarnations. Talk to Onu here in the grove to acquire a Seed of the Earth. Capture a Darkshore Wisp floating amongst the trees and we'll have a Seed of the Sky. Find a Seed of the Sea within seashells along the coast, west of here.

passages.title: The Seeds of Life
passages.text: Life is powerful, <name>. Concentrated in its purest form, it can overcome anything. Someday, even Darkshore will heal from its wounds. Did you find everything I need?

passages.title: The Seeds of Life
passages.text:
Perfect, this is everything. Did you have fun collecting the wisp? I used to chase the wisps around Ashenvale when I was just a girl.

<Lost in memories for a moment, Kathrena suddenly grows somber.>

I'm afraid I've found out what we're dealing with.

passages.title: In Defense of Darkshore
passages.text:
Now that we know our preventative measures work, we should cover as much ground as possible.

I've arranged to commandeer one of our hippogryphs, but I can't do this alone. Talk to my friend Orseus, next to the flight master right outside the grove here. Let him know when you're ready and I'll meet you there. We'll canvas Darkshore from the air and protect as many animals as we can!

passages.title: In Defense of Darkshore
passages.text:
So the animals are safe, then. Thank you, thank you!

But now it's time to turn our attention to the source.

passages.title: Vortex
passages.text:
The time has come, <name>. When you have steeled yourself we will speak again and I will summon forth a whirling vortex to speed your way up to the skies over Thunder Peak.

Channel the power of the Earthen Ring through the elemental to slay Lord Magmathar so that we may bring him into balance once more.

passages.title: Vortex
passages.text:
It is done. The power of fire is subdued and the four elements are returned to harmony.

You have saved the rest of Ashenvale through your brave and selfless actions, <name>. You have our eternal thanks.

passages.title: Vortex
passages.text:
The time has come, <name>. When you have steeled yourself we will speak again and I will summon forth a whirling vortex to speed your way up to the skies over Thunder Peak.

Channel the power of the Earthen Ring through the elemental to slay Lord Magmathar so that we may bring him into balance once more.

passages.title: Vortex
passages.text: Lord Magmathar must still be slain, <name>.

passages.title: Vortex
passages.text:
You've done it! The spirits were right after all!

The power of fire is subdued and the four elements are returned to harmony.

The rest of Ashenvale is spared this fiery fate. You have the eternal thanks of the Earthen Ring.

passages.title: Hungry, Hungry Hatchling
passages.text:
The venomhide hatchling looks at you expectantly, then begins to scrawl a pictogram into the dirt.

The drawings are rough, but you can make out the shapes of diemetradons, stegodons, and pterrordaxes. As the raptor finishes the sketch, it looks up at you, bares its teeth, and makes a biting motion.

Your venomhide hatchling must be craving fresh meat from these animals. Find and kill any type of diematradon, stegodon, or pterrordax in Un'Goro Crater and feed its meat to your hungry hatchling.

passages.title: Hungry, Hungry Hatchling
passages.text: The venomhide hatchling licks its lips and tilts its head to the side.

passages.title: Hungry, Hungry Hatchling
passages.text: The venomhide hatchling seems satisfied with the giant meal you've provided, but there's no way of telling when it will be hungry again.

passages.title: Keep the Fires Burning
passages.text:
This is no small task, <race>!

We have more ships arriving, and without the lighthouse they'll be lost - or worse! You are hereby charged with keeping its fire lit.

Collect the blubber from the hydras in these waters, then bring it to the forge here to melt it into oil.

Throwing that oil on the lighthouse fire will buy us the time we need.

passages.title: Keep the Fires Burning
passages.text:
Well, <class>...

Have you done as I asked?

passages.title: Keep the Fires Burning
passages.text:
Nice work, <race>!

No more ships will run aground, thanks to you.

passages.title: The Devourer of Darkshore
passages.text:
Now that the creatures of Darkshore are safe, let's turn our attention to the artifact you found in the lake. I believe it's the work of a minion of the Old Gods. We'll fight these fiends using the very lifegiving energies of Darkshore itself! Take the Lifebringer Sapling to the shore of the shallow lake to the south of here. Wave it over the waters of the lake and it should disable that ancient artifact.

Be careful, <name>. The artifact is likely to be guarded by who-knows-what.

passages.title: The Devourer of Darkshore
passages.text: I'm afraid to ask, <name>. Is the artifact destroyed? What about its guardian?

passages.title: The Devourer of Darkshore
passages.text:
Love of Elune, look at you. That must've been some fight! You're covered in what looks like... chowder.

If a mere minion could cause so much agony here in Darkshore, I can't even imagine the suffering that a true Old One could bring about.

Well, at least the animals are safe for now. I will plant the sapling you created to help rebuild this shattered land. Thank you, <name>! I'd give you a hug but, you know. Chowder.

passages.title: Leave No Tracks
passages.text:
To the southwest lies the corpse of a being somehow related to the Old Gods that the Twilight's Hammer cultists worship.

He was defeated before our time -- if not by the Titans themselves, certainly by one of their creations.

We've noted an increase in cult activity in that area which can only mean something terrible is amiss.

We're going to need to find out what they're planning to do there and why. Take this figurine, it'll help you avoid being detected while you gather intelligence.

passages.title: Leave No Tracks
passages.text:
This is dire news, <name>.  If you are correct, then we'd best act swiftly and decisively.

We cannot allow this "Soggoth" to be brought back to life.

passages.title: Soggoth and Kronn
passages.text:
The Master's Glaive was the site of an ancient battle, <name>. The titans sent twenty of their stone giants against Soggoth.

Of those twenty giants, one survived.

The tablets say that Kronn, the largest of the stone giants allowed himself to be entangled by Soggoth's tendrils -- just long enough to be lifted close enough to the creature's skull... within reach of his mighty sword.

It's a good thing he's dead... we don't really have twenty stone giants lying around to stop him again.

passages.title: Soggoth and Kronn
passages.text: The dwarf's story is unsettling... yet informative.  It seems we have few options left.

passages.title: The Offering to Azshara
passages.text:
The warlord said the horn of the ancients was being offered to Azshara above Nazj'vel.

Perhaps it's not too late to save the ancient relic from being destroyed.

passages.title: The Offering to Azshara
passages.text: You've done well, <name>.  Unfortunately the battle is far from over.

passages.title: Gorishi Grub
passages.text:
The venomhide hatchling looks at you expectantly, then begins to scrawl a pictogram into the dirt.

The hatchling's drawings seem to resemble various types of large insects, perhaps the gorishi silithids. The hatchling finishes his picture, then gestures at it with one short arm, snaps its jaws, and licks its lips.

It must want you to go to the Slithering Scar, in the center of the southern part of Un'Goro Crater, and gather silithid meat. When you have the meat, feed it to your hungry hatchling.

passages.title: Gorishi Grub
passages.text: The hatchling cocks its head and looks at you.

passages.title: Gorishi Grub
passages.text: Your venomhide hatchling flashes you a toothy smile and then settles in for a nap.

passages.title: Poached, Scrambled, Or Raw?
passages.text:
The venomhide hatchling's stomach growls as it gestures to get your attention. It begins scratching pictures of silithids into the dirt, adding small ovals underneath them. It looks at you hopefully and gestures at the circles.

They can only mean silithid eggs. The Noxious Lair, in western Tanaris and near the border with Un'Goro Crater, would probably be a great place to find the eggs your little hatchling wants.

passages.title: Poached, Scrambled, Or Raw?
passages.text: The hatchling looks at you.

passages.title: Poached, Scrambled, Or Raw?
passages.text: Your hatchling licks its lips after devouring the meal of silithid eggs. For a moment, you think it seems disappointed that feeding time has come to an end.

passages.title: Searing Roc Feathers
passages.text:
The hatchling looks at you for a moment, almost as if wondering whether you'll understand. It scrawls a picture of a pair of feathers in the dirt, then points with one claw to the bindings at its elbows and knees.

It doesn't seem hungry, but what could the feathers be for?

It must want them for adornments like the ones you've seen on other raptors. The largest feathers come from the searing rocs that congregate around the bones of large creatures in western Tanaris, northeast of Thistleshrub Valley.

passages.title: Searing Roc Feathers
passages.text: Your venomhide hatchling looks at you with anticipation.

passages.title: Searing Roc Feathers
passages.text: The venomhide hatchling accepts the feathers and begins looking them over, holding several up to its armbands.

passages.title: They Grow Up So Fast
passages.text:
With your expert feeding and care, your venomhide hatchling will grow quickly. As they grow, their hatchling teeth will be replaced by adult teeth. If you keep the teeth shed by your hatchling as it grows, you'll have an easy way to tell when it's mature enough to be trained as a mount.

Your venomhide will let you know what it needs, so pay close attention. When it has shed all of its baby teeth, return to me with your venomhide and the materials for your saddle and I'll do the rest.

passages.title: They Grow Up So Fast
passages.text: Have you been taking good care of that raptor?

passages.title: They Grow Up So Fast
passages.text:
It looks like both of you have managed to do some growing without killing one another.

There, everything's finished. I've trained your venomhide ravasaur to respond when you blow this whistle.

Few have the dedication to hand-feed and raise a venomhide, but they're well worth the effort.

passages.title: Sweeping Clean the Ruins
passages.text:
The big beards at Ironforge sent me here to check on Remtravel's dig the moment they got word of the disaster. Look at it! Precious artifacts washed to sea, months of tedious digging undone in a moment.

When the tidal waves hit, they demolished the murloc encampments along the shore. Good news? Naw, not with my luck. The survivors are squatting in the shelter of the ruins, and they're doing more damage than the elements ever could. Would you mind getting your waders on and taking care of things?

passages.title: Sweeping Clean the Ruins
passages.text:
Bravo, <name>! Now let's take a look-see at our new situation.

What? MORE murlocs? I swear on my stones, the more murlocs you kill, the more murlocs appear. Is it just me? We're going to need a new approach.

passages.title: Gearing Up To Ride
passages.text:
Your venomhide is strong and healthy and you've developed quite a bond. You'll be ready to ride him once I've completed your saddle and bridle. Just like you, they have to be specially conditioned to stand up to the toxins the raptor produces.

All you'll need to do is bring me some rugged leather, runecloth, and money to buy the rest of the supplies and I'll have that saddle for you in no time.

passages.title: Got Some Flotsam?
passages.text:
We can figure this out, <name>. We just need some Dwarven ingenuity. Think, Groffy, think!

These murlocs are just looking for a home, right? Let's do something constructive. I mean that literally.

All sorts of debris was washed ashore during the catastrophe, and some of the decimated murloc hovels may still be salvageable. Run along the shore here and gather up any building materials fit for a murloc. That's an admittedly low standard.

passages.title: Got Some Flotsam?
passages.text: Wet enough for ya?

passages.title: Got Some Flotsam?
passages.text:
<Archaeologist Groff picks through the wreckage.>

Well, not much here that don't look stepped on, sat on, or soaked in a toilet. But toss some thatch on top and it'll do.

Tell me, <name>, do you consider yourself an architect?

passages.title: A New Home
passages.text: Can we build it? Yes we can! Just west of the dig site I planted a banner on the shore. The sand is firm and it's as good a site as any. Take my tools and the parts you collected and build these ornery pests a different place to live.

passages.title: A New Home
passages.text: How goes our new seaside condo?

passages.title: A New Home
passages.text:
Har har, that sounds like quite a heap you built there. Did they take to it? Good, good! Let's see if my plan comes to fruition.

<Archaeologist Groff watches as scores of murlocs stream down the beach, pouring into the hovel from all corners of the compass. Gradually his brows knit together.>

What have I done?

passages.title: The Absent-Minded Prospector
passages.text:
Who are you again? <name>? Have we met? If you're here from the League, you can tell them I'm not leaving! Not without my find. I had it, right in my hands! Then the screaming. Then the wetness.

Listen here whos-yer-name, I documented the whole thing in my journal the day the tidal wave hit. And I know just where I left it! The journal. Not the find. Help me get the one so we can get the other! Or vice-versa! Do you follow? Follow me!

passages.title: The Absent-Minded Prospector
passages.text: Prospector Remtravel is an unsung hero! Like any great explorer, he is prone to wandering aimlessly.

passages.title: The Absent-Minded Prospector
passages.text:
Ah, you've helped the Prospector find his missing journal! To think it was here all along.

Someday you'll have to show me this other set of ruins he's always going on about.

passages.title: They Took Our Gnomes
passages.text:
The gnome explosives squad we requested from Tinker Town arrived last week. Just in time to face an assault by the Horde. We lost a lot of soldiers that day. Most of the gnome team was taken as well. Now we're neck deep in Horde, Silverwind Refuge has been lost and we're down a dozen gnomes.

I'm begging for your help here, <name>. Travel east to Silverwind Refuge and look for any gnome survivors. They were all carted off by a big, merciless orc named Thundrak. Find him and you'll find our gnomes.

passages.title: They Took Our Gnomes
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. Grim news you bring of the rest of the gnome team, but at least you managed to save a few. For that I am grateful.

passages.title: Searing Roc Feathers
passages.text:
The hatchling looks at you for a moment, almost as if wondering whether you'll understand. It scrawls a picture of a pair of feathers in the dirt, then points with one claw to the bindings at its elbows and knees.

It doesn't seem hungry, but what could the feathers be for?

It must want them for adornments like the ones you've seen on other raptors. The largest feathers come from the searing rocs that congregate around the bones of large creatures in western Tanaris, northeast of Thistleshrub Valley.

passages.title: Searing Roc Feathers
passages.text: Your venomhide hatchling looks at you with anticipation.

passages.title: Searing Roc Feathers
passages.text: The venomhide hatchling accepts the feathers and begins looking them over, holding several up to its armbands.

passages.title: Hungry, Hungry Hatchling
passages.text:
The venomhide hatchling looks at you expectantly, then begins to scrawl a pictogram into the dirt.

The drawings are rough, but you can make out the shapes of diemetradons, stegodons, and pterrordaxes. As the raptor finishes the sketch, it looks up at you, bares its teeth, and makes a biting motion.

Your venomhide hatchling must be craving fresh meat from these animals. Find and kill any type of diematradon, stegodon, or pterrordax in Un'Goro Crater and feed its meat to your hungry hatchling.

passages.title: Hungry, Hungry Hatchling
passages.text: The venomhide hatchling seems satisfied with the giant meal you've provided, but there's no way of telling when it will be hungry again.

passages.title: Poached, Scrambled, Or Raw?
passages.text:
The venomhide hatchling's stomach growls as it gestures to get your attention. It begins scratching pictures of silithids into the dirt, adding small ovals underneath them. It looks at you hopefully and gestures at the circles.

They can only mean silithid eggs. The Noxious Lair, in western Tanaris and near the border with Un'Goro Crater, would probably be a great place to find the eggs your little hatchling wants.

passages.title: Poached, Scrambled, Or Raw?
passages.text: Your hatchling licks its lips after devouring the meal of silithid eggs. For a moment, you think it seems disappointed that feeding time has come to an end.

passages.title: The Titans' Terminal
passages.text:
Now that we have the disc, a lot of our earlier finds are starting to make sense. Shortly after my arrival, Prospector Remtravel unearthed what he presumed to be a prehistoric toaster.

It's my belief that this slotted box is some sort of data reader. Unfortunately, it broke apart and washed away with the rest of our base camp when the tidal wave struck!

It can't have gone far, <name>. Pieces must be buried in the nearby sand. Here, use my trusty buried artifact detector to comb the beach for them.

passages.title: The Titans' Terminal
passages.text: Did you assemble all the pieces of the slotted device? We may need to remove Prospector Remtravel's sandwich from the ancient data interface.

passages.title: The Titans' Terminal
passages.text:
Why yes, yes, this is it! See here, the slot is the exact dimensions of the ancient disc, just as I'd surmised. Here's your reward, <name> - you've earned it.

Are you ready to meet history face to face? Let's see what the ancients have to say!

passages.title: A Trip to the Moonwell
passages.text:
It didn't work.

<A sorrowful and resigned expression upon his face, Pelturas removes the tear from the soup and gently washes it.>

The eruption of Thunder Peak must have affected it in some way. You must take the tear to the Moonwell of Purity, which still lies intact, protected by the goddess' power, at the southeast base of the volcano.

There, you will wash it in the sacred waters of Elune. What happens beyond that, I cannot say. I fear for my daughter's life. It is in your hands now, <name>.

passages.title: All's Well
passages.text:
Thank you for saving me from a fate worse than death, <name>! For saving both the child and myself!

Well, the child is almost saved. All you have to do is take the moonstones back west down the road to Astranaar. Hand them to Pelturas and he will know what to do.

Go in peace, my friend. Elune be praised!

passages.title: All's Well
passages.text: <name>, is that you? Have you returned with the cure for Relara?

passages.title: All's Well
passages.text:
Oh, <name>, you have saved my daughter! I know the power of the moonstones will give back my daughter her strength!

I can never repay you fully for the aid you have given me, but... please, take this. Other than Relara, it is my most dear possession.

passages.title: An Ounce of Prevention
passages.text:
Are you familiar with the Old Ones, <name>? Onu and I agree that the artifact you found in the lake can only be their work, and it's devouring Darkshore. Something is stirring up terrors we thought dead long ago. This is bigger than you or me, but my first concern is protecting the wildlife.

Here, this sapling contains the life essence you gathered for me. I believe it can protect the local fauna. Test it out on a nearby un-consumed bear, stag, or moonstalker, and let me know what happens!

passages.title: An Ounce of Prevention
passages.text: The sapling you carry grows in power even as we speak. Life is regenerative, <name>. Did it work?

passages.title: An Ounce of Prevention
passages.text:
Interesting ... It sounds like our cure will keep the wildlife safe, but you say you saw something else? Some kind of angry presence?

This is a good sign, <name>. Whatever is behind this isn't happy, and that means we're on to something.

passages.title: Little Orphan Roo Of The Oracles
passages.text:
The orphans have been looking forward to the opportunity to meet friends like you, <name>. It's wonderful that you've agreed to take one into your care.

Take this whistle. With it, you will be able to call for the orphan you have agreed to sponsor. It will only last for a limited time - not much longer than Children's Week itself, in fact.

Please, <name>, call upon your orphan. He will be excited to meet you and see the sights of Northrend with you.

passages.title: Little Orphan Roo Of The Oracles
passages.text: You taking care of us?

passages.title: Little Orphan Roo Of The Oracles
passages.text: You take us away from puppy-men hatchlings? Good. We like you already. Mean puppy-men hatchlings took all our favorite toys away.

passages.title: Little Orphan Kekek Of The Wolvar
passages.text:
The orphans have been looking forward to the opportunity to meet friends like you, <name>. It's wonderful that you've agreed to take one into your care.

Take this whistle. With it, you will be able to call for the orphan you have agreed to sponsor. It will only last for a limited time - not much longer than Children's Week itself, in fact.

Please, <name>, call upon your orphan. He will be excited to meet you and see the sights of Northrend with you.
