passages.title: Agility Training: Run Like Hell!
passages.text:
Before we go any further, we're going to have to get you into shape.

Devotion to the Old Gods is not going to save you when some emerald dragon comes chasing after you. You need to be fleet of foot, if you catch my drift.

Enough said. We'll summon your trainer... your job is to run away from him without leaving this camp.

Go!

passages.title: Agility Training: Run Like Hell!
passages.text:
Oh.  You're still alive.

Not bad.

passages.title: Poaching for Dummies
passages.text:
A new face around here, huh? You're in luck, making coin's easy thanks to my butcherbots. You go out and hunt some scorpids, some hyenas, maybe a few basilisks, set the butcherbot down, and let him do his thing! I've programmed him to extract all the valuable parts and place it safely in his hopper.

If you're interested, take him out to the northwest near Sandsorrow Watch first. Just bring him back once he's full and I'll pay you for the contents.

passages.title: Blackfin's Booty
passages.text:
<A torn page precedes the latest entry, which reads:>

Our self-proclaimed king will stop at nothing to acquire my family fortune. He has threatened and harassed me to no end.

I can't take it anymore!

I've buried the treasure and fed the map to Blackfin.

That should keep my cousin's grubby little mitts off of our precious heirlooms!

passages.title: Blackfin's Booty
passages.text: You've discovered Gilblingle's family treasure!

passages.title: Blackfin's Booty
passages.text: This item was highly prized by the local gilblin population - even coveted by King Gurboggle, himself!

passages.title: Do Me a Favor?
passages.text:
Hello there. Pleased to meet you! I'm Fizzle Brassbolts. Welcome to my Speedbarge.

I share your concerns about helping all of Thousand Needles. It's my firm belief that the Speedbarge is the best hope for the entire region.

Perhaps you could help us out a little bit here? I'll make sure that you're equipped with what you need to tackle everything else.

As to that, if you could just run this list of parts over to Jinky Twizzlefixxit in her shop, you'll be well on your way.

passages.title: Do Me a Favor?
passages.text: Is that the list of parts, finally? I've been waiting all day for that!

passages.title: Do Me a Favor?
passages.text:
<Jinky eyes the list of parts and spits!>

I don't have even half of that stuff!

passages.title: Do Me a Favor?
passages.text:
Hey there, <name>. I'm Pozzik, world-renowned rocket car pilot. Welcome to my Speedbarge.

I share your concerns about helping all of Thousand Needles. It's my firm belief that the Speedbarge is the best hope for the entire region.

Perhaps you could help us out a little bit here? I'll make sure that you're equipped with what you need to tackle everything else.

As to that, if you could just run this list of parts over to Razzeric in his shop, you'll be well on your way.

passages.title: Do Me a Favor?
passages.text: Is that my list of parts from Pozzik?

passages.title: Do Me a Favor?
passages.text:
Heya, pal, mind if I take a look at that list?

<Razzeric nearly spits!>

What's Pozzik thinking? He knows that I don't have even half of that stuff!

passages.title: Sea-Food Chain
passages.text:
Our time here draws to a close.

I must find my way across the chasm and discover the purpose behind the naga activities here.

If you are to follow me, you would be wise to conclude your search for a suitable mount first.

Search the area north of here and find a puffer hatchling. Once you've caught one, bring it to the trench to the west. I will prepare everything you need there.

passages.title: Hell's Shells
passages.text:
Fresh and stinking, these innards will prove to be irresistible for Nemesis, the befouled turtle god created by Twilight's Hammer.

Nemesis must eventually be destroyed, but first, we must collect a piece of his fiery armored shell. With it, we'll be able to work some magic to free the true ancient.

Go into the Flamewake and drop this bait near Nemesis. It will distract him. Pry off a piece of his shell... then run, if you hope to survive the encounter.

passages.title: Hell's Shells
passages.text:
Nemesis is a molten ball of fury protected by a stony shell of pure hatred.

His time will come.

passages.title: Hell's Shells
passages.text:
<The Arch Druid takes the shell from you with surprising reverence.>

Nemesis is an instrument of evil, but he was forged from a shell fragment of the true Ancient.

We will exploit this connection.

passages.title: Thunderdrome: Grudge Match!
passages.text:
It seems we have a special request! I have here a note from one Kelsey Steelspark, requesting to enter the cage and settle a dispute.

She's asked for you to be her partner, <name>. A fan of your previous victories? Or perhaps you're acquainted outside the ring?

I wouldn't back down now if I were you. This is the grand finale...

passages.title: Thunderdrome: Grudge Match!
passages.text: Stop wasting my time. Enter and fight!

passages.title: Thunderdrome: Grudge Match!
passages.text: Fantastic. I might challenge you to a duel myself someday.

passages.title: Children of Tortolla
passages.text:
My children.
They lie below.
In silt and sand.

The others corrupt them.
Darken them within their shells.

Slay the others.
Destroy the corruptors.
Save them...

passages.title: Children of Tortolla
passages.text:
My children.
Tell me they will be born free...

passages.title: Children of Tortolla
passages.text:
<race>.
You are not like the others.

Braver. Stronger.
A part of this world...
    and not the shadow that came before.

Thank you.

passages.title: An Ancient Awakens
passages.text:
I slumbered in the healing silt of Hyjal.
I slept until the world broke open.
When the others came, I was not ready.

I am ready now, <race>.

My children and I. Slow to anger.
But our wrath is final.

Tell those who sent you that we are prepared for war.

The others will be cast from the mountain.

passages.title: An Ancient Awakens
passages.text:
<name>!

You were able to earn the ancient's trust?

Wonderful! We are one step closer to taking back this mountain...

passages.title: Flight in the Firelands
passages.text:
<name>, our enemy is using this grotto in the Firelands to prepare an invasion. We're going to hit them hard right where they live.

But first, you'll need to get your wings. Flight in the Firelands does not work as it does in the outside world. Something about the dense, superheated air. You'll need some practice!

Get a Twilight Firelance from the rack behind me, equip it, then mount one of Aviana's Guardians. Practice flying - flap your wings! Visit a flag placed on the ledge below and return.

passages.title: Flight in the Firelands
passages.text: Do you feel comfortable flying yet?

passages.title: Flight in the Firelands
passages.text:
Well done! How does it feel?

It is challenging to master flight in this burning wasteland, but it is the only way.

I hope you're ready for battle, <name>...

passages.title: In the Outhouse
passages.text:
Hello? Hello! HELP!

I'm almost out of air! You have to get me out of here!

<The voice inside gags.>

One of those Southsea treasure hunters has got to have a crowbar!

passages.title: In the Outhouse
passages.text: Oh, for the love of the Light, do you have that crowbar yet? Drowning here!

passages.title: In the Outhouse
passages.text: Thank goodness! Now, just a little shove....

passages.title: Wave One
passages.text:
Here they come, <name>! The Twilight Knight Riders, astride black buzzards birthed in the scorching sulfurous breeding pools of the Firelands. The only way to defeat them is from the sky!

Take wing once more, <class>, and slay them.

Run into enemy riders with your lance to destroy them.

Go forth. Fly, fool. Fly!

passages.title: Wave One
passages.text: Flap! Flap I say... FLAP!

passages.title: Wave One
passages.text:
Spectacular flying, <name>! Their screeches of anguish echoed about this light-forsaken cavern.

But our work is not yet finished...

passages.title: In the Outhouse
passages.text:
Hello? Hello! HELP!

I'm almost out of air! You have to get me out of here!

<The voice inside gags.>

One of those filthy Southsea treasure hunters has got to have a crowbar!

passages.title: In the Outhouse
passages.text: Oh, for the love of profit, do you have that crowbar yet? Drowning here!

passages.title: In the Outhouse
passages.text: Thank goodness! Now, just a little shove....

passages.title: Pirate Accuracy Increasing
passages.text:
I don't know if you've noticed, but the cannonballs are hitting us. I'd say the Southsea pirates are getting more accurate... the ship is on fire!

You've got a river boat now. Go talk to Mazzer Stripscrew.

Put those fires out!

passages.title: Pirate Accuracy Increasing
passages.text:
Oh no, <name>, the cannonballs are hitting the Speedbarge. I'd say the Southsea pirates are getting more accurate... the ship is on fire!

You've got a river boat now. Please, go speak with Griznak.

Extinguish those fires!

passages.title: Art of Attraction
passages.text:
I have an idea. A brilliant idea! Those clown-looking fish have developed a symbiotic defensive relationship with the anemones. Having dismissed anemone disguise plausibilities, I've uncovered the chemical attractor that lures the fish.

I have a gyrocoptic thermascrub extractor that I've brought down to take samples. Use it to extract the chemical attractor from several of the anemones, then bring the samples back to me for rapid synthesis and deployment.

Go with haste! Brilliance is waiting!

passages.title: Art of Attraction
passages.text:
Superb! Chemicals abound!

My instantaneous chemical synthesizer is already pre-tested and prepared. Your deployment compound shall be ready in the blink of an eye!

passages.title: Odor Coater
passages.text:
Marvelous creation if I do say so myself. Ready for deployment.

Simply spray the clam divers with a bit of the chemical and they shall soon be accompanied by a protective aquatic companion. You can even spray yourself to similar effect if you so desire.

Speaking of desire, I would highly recommend that you moderate deployment of the chemical attractor to minimal applications. Large doses could result in undesirable effects...

Undesirable for you anyway. Likely very desirable for the fish.

Away!

passages.title: Odor Coater
passages.text: Fishy companions for all!

passages.title: Odor Coater
passages.text: Well done my odorific associate. You are both swift and assiduous, if I do say so myself. May your future travels be rampant with inspiration and opulence.

passages.title: Bellies Await
passages.text:
We have quite a stock of gathered clams to tote back to the cave, I was simply awaiting someone to do the toting. You've proven dangerous enough to be the sort.

I highly expect that such a fine meal shall not pass uncontested by predators on the way back, so I'd make your trip as swift as possible.

Thank you for your help, friend. It's been a pleasure.

passages.title: Bellies Await
passages.text: You look to have come back to us with purpose. Was your trip successful?

passages.title: Bellies Await
passages.text:
This is wonderful. I will begin cooking them immediately. It is good to know that of our many fears, starvation shall no longer need to be one of them.

I imagine the Admiral will have much work for you. Let me trouble you no further for a while.

passages.title: Filling Our Pockets
passages.text:
We've looted everything that isn't bolted down around here, but I'm not done yet. If we're bothering to do the Steamwheedle Cartel's dirty work for them, we're going to make as much cash as we can while we're here.

I haven't seen many earrings on these pirates, so the gold must be in the next best place...their teeth. The Southsea musketeers and strongarms to the south are the higher-ups here; they'll be the ones with the adornment. Bring me back a good fistful of gold fillings.

passages.title: Filling Our Pockets
passages.text: Don't get squeamish on me now.

passages.title: Filling Our Pockets
passages.text:
Nice!  Remember, gold is gold, no matter who's mouth, nose, or otherwise it's been in.

It's all perfectly sanitary after being melted down anyway. Or at least wiped off.

passages.title: Wave Two
passages.text:
You've stirred up the hornets, <name>. The ceiling is coming down on us! And their strongest fighters are taking wing on creatures warped and twisted by this world of flame.

Get back out there and take them down! Watch out for flaming boulders.

passages.title: Wave Two
passages.text: FLAP! For the love of all things merciful, flap. Flap harder!

passages.title: Wave Two
passages.text:
By the wings of Aviana - you were born to fly, <name>!

Quickly, let's get back out there and hit them again...

passages.title: To Arms!
passages.text:
As we struggled not to drown, my men and I were forced to abandon our weapons and much of our armor.

Erunak says to expect a major attack from the naga soon and I'm inclined to believe him.

If we're going to stand a chance, we'll need your help to recover our lost armaments. They should be lying on the sea floor near our shipwrecks.

Hurry, <race>, we're defenseless here.

passages.title: To Arms!
passages.text: Have you recovered our gear, <race>?

passages.title: To Arms!
passages.text:
Well done, <class>!

Thanks to you, my men will be ready to confront the enemy when they attack.

passages.title: Might of the Firelord
passages.text:
I've been charged with leading our military operations against the enemy. A humbling task when you consider there are demigods walking among us.

I'm going to have you carry out a series of hit-and-run attacks behind enemy lines. It will be important that you keep the enemy off guard and weaken their numbers ahead of our main force's attack.

Your first target will be the Ascendant's Rise, where the most highly trained Twilight's Hammer devotees have achieved a partial elemental state.

passages.title: Might of the Firelord
passages.text: You did well, <name>.  I've a new target for you.

passages.title: The Sanctum of the Prophets
passages.text:
The mad prophets of the Twilight's Hammer congregate in the area just north of the Ascendant's Rise.

It is said that their dark visions are granted to them directly by the Old Gods. Whether or not that is true, they provide tremendous spiritual guidance to the cult. Attacking the Sanctum of the Prophets will deal a devastating blow to the enemy's morale and if we're lucky you might run into one of the Firelord's own emissaries while you're there.

passages.title: The Sanctum of the Prophets
passages.text: You continue to prove your prowess, <name>.  At this rate Hyjal might survive this ordeal after all.

passages.title: Magma Monarch
passages.text:
The magma giants who serve Ragnaros are kept in line by their king's heavy-handed rule. Were we to take care of him, the rest will surely fall into disarray.

Without the giants, the fight on the ground will get a lot more even. Perhaps even tilt to our favor.

But felling the magma monarch will be no easy task. Use these drums to enlist the help of the great Tortolla who is capable of holding off King Moltron for an eternity. But holding him off won't be enough -- and that's where you come in.

passages.title: Magma Monarch
passages.text:
Excellent work, <name>.  We shall soon claim victory in Hyjal.

It has been an honor to fight along your side.

passages.title: The Firelord
passages.text:
With his gatekeeper gone, you've given the Guardians of Hyjal access to Sulfuron Spire.

Ragnaros will have no choice but to defend the main entryway to the Firelands himself.

Go through the Twilight's Hammer portal at the Sanctum of the Prophets and meet me inside. Malfurion and Hamuul will also aid us while the others continue to fight the enemy outside.

passages.title: The Firelord
passages.text: Yes, <name>?

passages.title: The Firelord
passages.text: Hyjal has been saved, <name>.  And it's all thanks to you.

passages.title: Brood of Evil
passages.text:
This egg you recovered is an alarming sign, <name>. The Twilight dragons are usually raised from stolen eggs from other dragonflights, which are then modified through dark magic.

This "natural" egg is evidence that one of their matriarchs has become a viable broodmother. We must destroy her before her brood spreads.

Go to the Ascendant's Rise where they claim these aberrations are kept and slay one of the juvenile drakes. We will use its skull to lure out its mother.

passages.title: Brood of Evil
passages.text: You've returned, <race>.

passages.title: Brood of Evil
passages.text: You've done well, <name>.  We will use this to draw out the Twilight matriarch.

passages.title: Death to the Broodmother
passages.text:
We've located the matriarch's feeding grounds south of the Ascendant's Rise.

She will be extremely angry to have lost one of her drakes. Place the skull there near the carcasses she devours. If she's anywhere in the vicinity, she will come out and attempt to exact revenge.

We will have a surprise waiting for her.

passages.title: Death to the Broodmother
passages.text: That went... better than expected.

passages.title: Secrets of the Flame
passages.text:
If we are to banish Ragnaros back into the Firelands, we will need to gain access to Sulfuron Spire.

Only the most trusted members of the Twilight's Hammer will have been entrusted with such valuable information.

Go search the Ascendant's Rise for any written tomes you might find. Foul as they are, we cannot waste the opportunity to learn about our enemy's weaknesses.

passages.title: Secrets of the Flame
passages.text: Did you succeed in your task, <name>?

passages.title: Secrets of the Flame
passages.text: These foul books should not be allowed to exist.  Yet the information inside them is of vital importance.

passages.title: The Gatekeeper
passages.text:
According to these tomes, one of Ragnaros' most powerful lieutenants serves as the sole gatekeeper to Sulfuron Spire.

You won't be able to defeat him alone.

Sound this horn when you engage in combat with Azralon and any of our forces in the vicinity will come to your aid.

You must hurry, <name>. It won't be long before the Firelord realizes what we're up to.

passages.title: The Gatekeeper
passages.text: You've returned, <name>?

passages.title: The Gatekeeper
passages.text: It is done.  Only the final step in your mission remains.

passages.title: Egg Wave
passages.text:
Without any defenders, the Firelands eggs are vulnerable.

Take wing once more and smash those eggs! Simply rush over them to crush them. Search all the nooks, crannies, and side-caves. Hurry!

passages.title: Egg Wave
passages.text: A decisive blow!

passages.title: A Natural Occurrence
passages.text:
This Elemental Shard is all that is left from the rift that stood here before. The connection between the shard and the rift is unknown, but perhaps someone more versed in the elements would know more.

Seek out an Earthen Ring Emissary in any capital city. This could be exactly what they are looking for.

passages.title: A Natural Occurrence
passages.text: You said you found this near an Elemental Rift?

passages.title: A Natural Occurrence
passages.text:
Yes, <name>, this shard does explain the occurrence of the rifts.  The elemental planes have been in chaos in Outland ever since Draenor was destroyed. These shards cause a weakness in the already damaged elemental planes and allow the elementals to cross over.

We're still collecting information on who or what is behind all of this.  However, the more shards you bring me, the better prepared we will be to fight the elemental invasion here in Azeroth.

passages.title: Your Underwater Mount (Temp)
passages.text:
I set up some ropes on the ledge below. Just tie off your lure to one of the ropes and release it into the abyssal stream. If all goes well, one of the rays should come up for it almost immediately.

I don't expect this to be even remotely easy, so hold on tight and keep an eye ahead at all times. If you should succeed in subduing one of the rays, bring it back here immediately so that we can feed it and cement the bond.

I have a good feeling this time. I think this is it, <name>.

passages.title: Flames from Above
passages.text:
We've identified the general direction where the infiltrators have been coming from, thanks to your work.

Now we just need to shut down their camp and put an end to their operations this side of Nordrassil.

Take this horn. It will signal one of our emerald drakes to swoop down and give these Twilight cultists a taste of the flames they so madly worship.

passages.title: Flames from Above
passages.text: Is it done yet, <name>?

passages.title: Flames from Above
passages.text: Excellent, <name>.  That should put a stop to the attacks once we finish these elementals off.

passages.title: Crushing the Cores
passages.text:
These searing guardians are murderous! We destroy them, and within minutes, they reignite from the ashes.

I think there's a way to destroy them permanently, but we'll need someone who can fight through the front ranks.

<name>, kill the searing guardians and take their smoldering cores to the nearby anvils. Smash them on the Twilight Anvils, and destroy them for good!

passages.title: Crushing the Cores
passages.text:
Are they dead?

It seems like nothing we do can cool this inferno...

passages.title: Crushing the Cores
passages.text:
Great work!

There was a time when adventurers would collect these cores in order to craft mediocre fire-resistant equipment. But for now, I'm glad just to destroy these fiends once and for all.

passages.title: Swift Approach
passages.text:
I've taken the liberty of performing some preliminary scouting. The naga may not be aware of our position, but they are not entirely unprepared for intruders.

Beyond their patrols, they have set up magical sentry devices that will warn them of unwelcome guests. Fortunately, they seem to have sacrificed quality for quantity, and there is definitely a window in which the devices can be destroyed before their alarms are answered.

I trust that you can see to this before our other soldiers arrive.

passages.title: Swift Approach
passages.text: It seems clear that they do not take us seriously, which actually worries me. We have no idea how many of these naga there really are. As time passes, I grow to fear that the shell we escaped was only a small piece of a very large puzzle.

passages.title: Swift Approach
passages.text:
Well done, <name>, and just in time too. The Admiral just started sending more men out. Strong sword arms to be sure, but I doubt they possess quite the same awareness and finesse that you do.

We were lucky to have you here when things went south. I suspect you will have a large role to play in things to come as well.

passages.title: An Occupation of Time
passages.text:
Look--<name> is it?--I need your help. I know most everyone in this cave thinks that we're not in a position to be worrying about anything but our own hides right now, but I cannot dismiss my ancestors so readily.

All I want from you, while you're out in the city proper, is to keep a watchful eye out for objects of significance. The statues interest me especially.

passages.title: An Occupation of Time
passages.text:
Thank you so much for taking this seriously.

This is some of the first definitive proof of other members of the Vashj family. Very interesting. And I'd never even heard of either of the other two figures you mentioned until now.

So much of our history was lost during the sundering - it's exciting to have a chance at reclaiming some of it.

passages.title: A Better Vantage
passages.text:
This cave is our only refuge. There's no help on the way. Whatever happens, this cave must remain safe or we are all sure to die down here.

We need a forward post to launch our attacks from. Something defensible.

In the eastern portion of the ruins on the lowest level, scout the north end of the gardens, the passage leading under the main structure just west of the gardens, and the cluster of buildings at the southeast corner of the ruins, under the bridges.

Bring me back any information you can.

passages.title: A Better Vantage
passages.text:
This is good intel. You have a sharp eye, <class>.

It sounds like the building tucked under the terrace at the far end of the ruins will make a suitable forward post. I will send some men immediately to start defensive preparations and we will reposition there as soon as possible.

passages.title: Gimme Shelter!
passages.text:
Please, <race>! You must help me!

I've barely managed to survive, what with naga, sharks, and that horrible monster that attacked our ship.

I can see a cave that might be safe, but I don't dare try to make it unless I know there's air inside.

Can you make sure it's ok?

passages.title: Gimme Shelter!
passages.text:
I cannot thank you enough, <race>.

I just hope this whole nightmare has a happy ending.

passages.title: Where's Wizzle?
passages.text:
Hey, <name>, you haven't seen my other brother, Wizzle, have you?

I just know that the pirates captured him! He said that he was going to try to sell them some engineering stuff, or something.

Would you please look for him up at the Southsea Holdfast to the east? I'll bet that no-good goblin he's always traveling with, Synge, got him into trouble!

passages.title: Where's Wizzle?
passages.text: Hey! Get me out of here!

passages.title: Crafty Crabs
passages.text:
It was that darn crab!

Here I thought that all the exercise from walking here was making me super buff! My pack just kept getting lighter and lighter. But no! That crab snipped a hole in my bag and all my parts were falling out the whole way here.

Please, help a good lookin' goblin out, will ya? Go back and help me pick up all of my stray parts. I'm sure those conniving vicious little crabs ran off with some of them too.

passages.title: Crafty Crabs
passages.text: Never underestimate the appeal of something shiny.

passages.title: Crafty Crabs
passages.text: Glad you know a quick buck when you see one. Pleasure doing business with you, buddy.

passages.title: Where's Synge?
passages.text:
Hey, <name>, you haven't seen our gunsmith, Synge, have you?

I just know that the pirates captured him! He said that he was going to try to sell them some rifles, or something.

Would you please look for him up at the Southsea Holdfast to the east? I'll bet that no-good gnome he's always traveling with, Wizzle Brassbolts, got him into trouble!

passages.title: Where's Synge?
passages.text: Hey! Get me out of here!

passages.title: Forgemaster Pyrendius
passages.text:
A terrible evil squats in the heart of this cavern, <name>. Forgemaster Pyrendius has personally crafted many of the cursed weapons that Twilight's Hammer is using in their conquest of the realms above.

Before we leave these lands of flame... Pyrendius must die.

He will not go down easy. But, if I'm reading the tome correctly, we can briefly open up small gateways to the Abyssal Maw, the realm of water. Lure Pyrendius onto a portal rune and activate it to weaken him!

passages.title: Forgemaster Pyrendius
passages.text: Is Pyrendius dead? This ashen heat of this cave is suffocating me!

passages.title: Forgemaster Pyrendius
passages.text: It is done! We'll seal this fiery hole up behind us and let the minions of the Twilight's Hammer discover the corpses we left behind. We couldn't have done it without you, <name>!

passages.title: Head of the Class
passages.text:
That settles it, "<name>damus!" You are head of your class!

You will get a chance to address a crowd of the most fanatical, bloodthirsty and certifiably insane people on this planet.

Go report to your instructor for the details, but remember: your goal is to exploit the animosity between the ogres at the Seat of the Chosen and the other, less privileged races.

If all goes well, we will smuggle Jarod out of here during the ensuing riot.

passages.title: Head of the Class
passages.text:
There you are, Yshkaldamus.  I've been meaning to talk to you about something.

I heard about the unfortunate incident that befell our poor friend, Okrog.

<Mylva looks to her left, then her right.  She finally nods and shoots a sly wink in your direction.>

You might be a better pupil than I had thought.

passages.title: Hammering It Out
passages.text:
The rift that was here left behind this strange device, but why?

Someone in a capital city may have more information.

passages.title: Hammering It Out
passages.text: What's this then?  Another device?

passages.title: Hammering It Out
passages.text:
Not another one! <name>, these devices have been springing up all around Azeroth. We know that they can instigate elemental disturbances in the area, including causing tears in the elemental planes.

The devices stink of Twilight's Hammer.  The engravings covering the surface and the captured elemental essence implicate Cho'gall and his minions are behind this.

If you find more of these, bring them to me or one of my associates. We need to learn more about what's behind this attack.

passages.title: Ze Gnomecorder
passages.text:
Zese goblinz dizgust me. Zer filzy goblin technology iz inferior to anyzing gnomish, yet...

<Professor Xakxak sighs.>

It iz ze last piece of ze puzzle! Wizout ze filzy goblin technology ze gnomecorder cannot be built!

Venture eazt into ze "Skunkworks" and take from zem zer filzy goblin junk! You vill most likely find zem on goblin technicians.

<Professor Xakxak laughs mockingly.>

Goblin technician? Vut iz zat anyvay?

<Professor Xakxak shrugs.>

Zome kind of oxymoron?

passages.title: Ze Gnomecorder
passages.text: Ze junk? Do you have zit?

passages.title: Ze Gnomecorder
passages.text: Ah, ze junk haz arrived! Zit is ze last piece of ze puzzle! Now to zet it up! Standby, <name>!

passages.title: Slash and Burn
passages.text:
Victory is possible, <name>.

This portal is not just a means of bringing back Cenarius through the dream. Think about it, <name>. Once a gateway through the Emerald Dream is open, our forces can use them to move freely from Moonglade, Nordrassil, and even Wyrmrest, to this strategic location.

All Ysera needs is time. It'll be up to you to keep the Twilight's Hammer forces in Darkwhisper Gorge from pulling together and attacking us from the east.

Take one of the emerald drakes and hit them hard, <name>.

passages.title: Slash and Burn
passages.text: You've returned, <name>.

passages.title: Slash and Burn
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>.  We might win this one yet.

passages.title: Return from the Firelands
passages.text:
I'll usher out the rest of the followers of Lo'Gosh and seal this portal behind us.

The rest of our forces at Mount Hyjal will want to hear of this victory. Return to Takrik Ragehowl and let him know what we've discovered and how we were triumphant!

Simply step through the portal to return to Mount Hyjal.

passages.title: Return from the Firelands
passages.text:
They're moving supplies to Hyjal straight from the elemental planes? Devious.

You've made Lo'Gosh proud by sealing that flamegate, <name>, but there may be more portals to seal. You should check with the other shrines!

passages.title: Do Yourself a Favor
passages.text:
So these night elves send out a desperate call for help to us, goes something like this:

<Gnombus changes the pitch of his voice to sound like a woman.>

"Please come help us! The big, mean Horde has goblins! Oh, we can't handle goblins! They pull our hair and make us cry!"

Right, anyway, so here we are.

The first thing I did was upgrade their aerial defenses with some of my new sniper guns. Problem is, they don't use guns. Do yourself a favor and lend 'em a hand, eh? Find 'em south of here.

passages.title: Do Yourself a Favor
passages.text:
<Kalen sighs.>

We use guns just fine, friend. CANNONS, on the other hand, I take issue with...

passages.title: The Only Way Down is in a Body Bag
passages.text:
The skies are swarming with heavily armored orcs on the backs of even more heavily armored wind riders. Our best efforts to bring them down have thus far proven fruitless. Our arrows usually just bounce off of those foul creatures. If we do happen to take one down the orcs deploy their goblin parachutes and safely land on the ground below.

I need you to use Gnombus's sniper cannons and blow up the Warsong wind riders and then blow up the parachuting orcs.

The only way down is in a body bag.

passages.title: The Only Way Down is in a Body Bag
passages.text: We can't get across the pass safely without the wind riders being taken out first.

passages.title: The Only Way Down is in a Body Bag
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>. The gnome technology, while somewhat obnoxious, is highly effective. We should now have a clear path to Windshear Hold.

passages.title: Return to Stardust
passages.text:
Huntress Jalin will be pleased to know that the way to Windshear Hold is now clear. Please return to Stardust Spire and inform her of your success. She will most assuredly have more work for you now that our path is clear.

Thank you and good luck, friend.

passages.title: Return to Stardust
passages.text:
With the airways clear our hippogryphs will be able to move into Stonetalon freely. Well done, <name>!

Now on to more pressing matters. 

What you witnessed at Trueshot Point was a small sampling of the decimation left in the wake of Hellscream's legacy. As Warchief of the Horde, Hellscream has declared Kalimdor as the Horde's sovereign territory. All that would oppose the Horde are destroyed.

We are Kalimdor's last line of defense. Should we fall, Kalimdor will also fall. The Horde must be stopped!

passages.title: Hellscream's Legacy
passages.text:
Enter Stonetalon Mountains through Talondeep Pass and head towards the smoldering trees. Seek out the Krom'gar incinerators that are destroying the forest and slay as many as you can! Be warned, the incinerators are powerful orcs. Attacking them through conventional means will likely result in your death. Destroy the oil canisters on their backs and they will be devoured by flame!

Report to Sentinel Heliana at Windshear Mine should you succeed. She will have your new orders.

passages.title: Hellscream's Legacy
passages.text: With the Krom'gar incinerators dealt with, the forest may be allowed to regrow. Only time can heal the wounds left by the Horde.

passages.title: Into the Maw!
passages.text:
Atop the Lightning Ledge, the Twilight's Hammer has erected an enormous flamegate. I do not know where it leads; I know it is not of this realm, and I cannot enter. None of my other followers have returned.

I need you to enter this realm and be my fangs within. Step through the flamegate. If he is still alive, meet with Jordan Olafson inside. He will give you a token that will allow you to use my powers in that realm.

Be bold, <name>. Find out where that flamegate leads, and destroy whatever lies within.

passages.title: Into the Maw!
passages.text:
Ah, you are the champion Lo'Gosh promised! Your eyes don't deceive you: you have entered the Firelands, an elemental plane of molten stone and fire. We've got our work cut out for us here.

Put aside your differences with the Alliance, there's plenty of danger to go around.

And take this: the Fang of Lo'Gosh will allow you to channel the ancient's power here within the Firelands. Use it well!

passages.title: Into the Maw!
passages.text:
Atop the Lightning Ledge, the Twilight's Hammer has erected an enormous flamegate. I do not know where it leads; I know it is not of this realm, and I cannot enter. None of my other followers have returned.

I need you to enter this realm and be my fangs within. Step through the flamegate. If he is still alive, meet with Jordan Olafson inside. He will give you a token that will allow you to use my powers in that realm.

Be bold, <name>. Find out where that flamegate leads, and destroy whatever lies within.

passages.title: Into the Maw!
passages.text:
Ah, you are the champion Goldrinn promised! Your eyes don't deceive you: you have entered the Firelands, an elemental plane of molten stone and fire. We've got our work cut out for us here.

Put aside your differences with the Horde, there's plenty of danger to go around.

And take this: the Fang of Goldrinn will allow you to channel the ancient's power here within the Firelands. Use it well!

passages.title: Reoccupation
passages.text:
There's no shortage of Kvaldir to slaughter. They're obviously still reeling from our assault. The city has been desolate so long, I doubt they expected any naga to contest them here.

There have been no reports yet of their leader. I'm sure that culling them further will force the coward to rear his head soon enough.

Shall we continue?

passages.title: Reoccupation
passages.text: I had heard tales of the fierceness of these Kvaldir, but so far, the boasts seem empty.

passages.title: Reoccupation
passages.text: Hah! It seems you were right. That broken trident is serving you just fine. I suppose I don't get to see you claw anything to death today after all.

passages.title: The Revered Lady
passages.text:
The Revered Lady has sent word for you. She awaits you at the far end of the temple gardens.

If you feel the need to mention the heroic exploits of your faithful battle brother, Azjentus, please don't hold back. I won't take your admiration of me as a weakness.

I'll hold you up no longer. The Lady awaits.

passages.title: The Revered Lady
passages.text:
Ah, my battlemaiden, you've come to me. The warrior caste whispers of nothing but your victories on the battlefield, and we've only just begun our assault to take the city.

You have served me proud thus far. May the Queen favor you that you might continue to do more of the same.

passages.title: Field Test: Gnomecorder
passages.text:
Ze Gnomecorder iz complete! Now ve must test zit!

Venture into Stonetalon Mountains to ze southeast and valk down ze Talondeep Pass until you reach a filzy goblin drill machine. I vill activate ze Gnomecorder ven you reach your destination!

passages.title: Field Test: Gnomecorder
passages.text:
<The Gnomecorder crackles and pops with static electricity.>

Come in, <name>. Can you hear me? Zis iz Professor Xakxak!

*POP*

*CRACKLE*

PERFECT! Viz ze Gnomecorder I vill be able to direct you about Stonetalon vile staying out of harmz vay!

Now, onto our next order of buziness!

passages.title: Burn, Baby, Burn!
passages.text:
Deze orc incinerators zat burn ze forest carry viz zem powerful veaponry! You must kill zem and take zhere flame thrower. Vonce you have ze flame thrower, search ze forest for varsong stockpilez and use ze flame thrower to burn zem down!

Burn zem all and I vill reward you! Yes, ze Gnomecorder can transport items!

Vait! Do you hear zat! I zink zhere iz an orc nearby! Vatchout!

passages.title: Burn, Baby, Burn!
passages.text:
<The Gnomecorder buzzes loudly.>

Vonderful! As promised, VOILA, your reward!

Now, I have a bit of news that you might find interesting.

passages.title: Into the Maw!
passages.text:
<name>, there you are! Goldrinn has a mission that only his champion can accomplish. Atop the Lightning Ledge, Twilight's Hammer has erected a flamegate. We don't know where it leads, but Goldrinn can't enter. The ancient needs you to be his fangs.

Step into the flamegate and talk to Jordan Olafson when you get inside. He'll give you a token to allow you to use Goldrinn's power in that realm. Find out where the flamegate leads!

passages.title: Into the Maw!
passages.text:
Ah, you are the champion Goldrinn promised! Your eyes don't deceive you: you have entered the Firelands, an elemental plane of molten stone and fire. We've got our work cut out for us here.

Put aside your differences with the Horde, there's plenty of danger to go around.

And take this: the Fang of Goldrinn will allow you to channel the ancient's power here within the Firelands. Use it well!

passages.title: Into the Maw!
passages.text:
<name>! Lo'Gosh needs you. Atop the Lightning Ledge, Twilight's Hammer has erected a flamegate. We don't know where it leads, but nobody who's gone through has returned. You are to venture inside and be the fangs of Lo'Gosh within.

Step into the flamegate and talk to Jordan Olafson when you get inside. He'll give you a token to allow you to use Lo'Gosh's power inside that realm. Find out where the flamegate leads!

passages.title: Into the Maw!
passages.text:
Ah, you are the champion Lo'Gosh promised! Your eyes don't deceive you: you have entered the Firelands, an elemental plane of molten stone and fire. We've got our work cut out for us here.

Put aside your differences with the Alliance, there's plenty of danger to go around.

And take this: the Fang of Lo'Gosh will allow you to channel the ancient's power here within the Firelands. Use it well!

passages.title: Visions of the Past: Rise from the Deep
passages.text:
What you told me of the naga before has been plaguing my mind. Who are these allies they're summoning? Do they really think they can defeat the Tidehunter?

Escaping this cave brings a degree of relief, but our purpose here remains. I'm hoping you will be willing to seek answers from the Battlemaiden one last time.

There's only one place that I can think of where they would have taken the artifact - the temple atop the ruins. It's sure to be well guarded. Proceed carefully.

passages.title: Visions of the Past: Rise from the Deep
passages.text:
Minions of the Old God? Two very potent foes have joined forces then. Their hope to defeat the Tidehunter may not be so foolish after all.

<name>, we can't let that happen. If Azshara defeats the Tidehunter and takes his power for herself, I'm not sure any number of us could ever hope to oppose her on the seas.

The first step is clear at least - we need to hunt down the fiend that destroyed our ships. The navy was confident enough to bring in a new fleet, perhaps they have a plan.

passages.title: Her Lady's Hand
passages.text:
Battlemaiden!

Find my Honor Guard upon the field of battle and relieve them of their foes. I need them to return to guard the priestesses immediately!

I will hold the entrance. Be swift!

passages.title: Her Lady's Hand
passages.text: I dispatched my Honor Guard when the fighting broke out. They are better equipped to deal with the chaos of this kind of battle, and I am hardly in need of their aid.

passages.title: Her Lady's Hand
passages.text:
Well done, Battlemaiden.

I will attend to the eastern bridge. I need you to attend to the temple itself. The ritual must not be interrupted.

passages.title: The Fires of Mount Hyjal
passages.text:
Do you see it, <name>? From the ridge southwest of here... plumes of black smoke curling into the sky.

Mount Hyjal is burning.

If the fires have raced this far up the mountain, surely they threaten the Grove of Aessina and all of our forces there. Can you investigate?

Speak with Laina Nightsky near the Grove of Aessina. Last I heard, she was fighting off the assault.

passages.title: The Fires of Mount Hyjal
passages.text:
Can this wait, <class>? The battle is not going well.

Oh, you're here to help. I hope you don't mind a little heat...

passages.title: To the Fathom-Lord's Call
passages.text:
Fathom-Lord Zin'jatar has sent word that the Kvaldir leader has shown himself. I would like you to make your way to him at the far end of the terrace above us, on the middle level of the ruins: Nar'shola Terrace.

Kill any Kvaldir that stand in your path on that terrace. We want the echoes of this defeat to ring in their minds so that they will dare not return to threaten our purpose here.

Your devotion does not go unnoticed, my battlemaiden. Go knowing that you have my blessing.

passages.title: To the Fathom-Lord's Call
passages.text: It is good of you to join me, Battlemaiden. The echoes of your combat graced your approach. It was a beautiful sound to behold.

passages.title: Bombs Away: Windshear Mine!
passages.text:
Ve have discovered ze vhereabouts of ze gigantic goblin bomb zat you discovered at Silvervind Refuge.

You remember Boog? Ze gnome you rescued from ze orcish vagon of agony? Vell, he and Minx have tracked ze bomb down to Windshear Mine. Go zhere immediately, <name>! Zey'll be expecting you.

passages.title: Bombs Away: Windshear Mine!
passages.text:
Good to see you again, <name>. Thanks for the rescue in Ashenvale. Damn shame about all the gnomes we lost.

You ready to get down to business?

passages.title: The Flow of Muisek
passages.text:
I've done all I can for you. Muisek stronger than the hippogryph just isn't within my power to work with yet, so I won't make you deal with the disaster that could bring.

But while you've been busy, I've fully readied the hippogryph muisek. Take it to my master, Witch Doctor Uzer'i in Camp Mojache. He can create powerful weapons with it, and hopefully he'll be impressed by what I've done.

passages.title: The Flow of Muisek
passages.text: I sense something familiar in your presence...

passages.title: The Flow of Muisek
passages.text: Well done indeed... I'd expect nothing less from my own daughter. She'll make a fine witch doctor someday.

passages.title: Don't Look Them in the Eyes
passages.text:
Keep your head down, <name>. No need to draw unwanted attention.

Looks like the orcs are piling that balloon up with some type of ore from the mine. Get in there and take the ore from the orcs. Bring me back whatever you manage to grab and I'll ship it off to the professor for examination.

Before you go, a word of advice: you can avoid the Krom'gar pretty easily in there as (1) they're dumb as dirt and (2) they can't see anything if they're carrying ore. Of course, you need to kill them to get their ore.

passages.title: Don't Look Them in the Eyes
passages.text: Get me those ore samples!

passages.title: Don't Look Them in the Eyes
passages.text: Not too much trouble, I hope. With these samples we should be able to figure out what they plan to do with the ore and the big bomb.

passages.title: The Twilight Egg
passages.text:
The egg is unlike any that you've seen before. Its translucent shell appears to bend the light around it.

Accompanying it, you find a note describing the arrival of a fertile broodmother at the Ascendant's Rise.

Perhaps you should show this to Aronus.

passages.title: The Twilight Egg
passages.text: You were right to come to me with this, <name>.  This represents a great threat to us if we do not act swiftly and boldly.

passages.title: Illegible Orc Letter
passages.text:
You've discovered a parchment with an impressive looking Horde seal imprinted upon its page. Unfortunately, the rest of the document is completely illegible as it is in orcish.

Take the letter to Boog. He might know what to do with it!

passages.title: Illegible Orc Letter
passages.text: What have you got there?

passages.title: Illegible Orc Letter
passages.text:
<Boog takes the letter from you and begins to examine it.>

Interesting.

<Boog smells the parchment.>

Hrm... Troubling...

<Boog folds the paper in half and looks at you.>

Can't understand a damn thing written here - if that is writing. Could just be toilet paper. Sure smells like it.

passages.title: Minx'll Fix It
passages.text:
The good news is that Minx is fluent in orcish and she's nearby. Head back into the mine and find her. She's probably deeper inside, standing around being useless.

Don't forget the parchment!

passages.title: Minx'll Fix It
passages.text: What have you got there?

passages.title: Minx'll Fix It
passages.text:
<Minx takes the letter from you and begins to read it.>

Uh oh...

<Minx smells the parchment.>

Disgusting!

<Minx folds the paper in half and looks at you.>

The good news is that this isn't toilet paper. The bad news is that the ink on this paper is a mixture of kodo poop and blood. That's not the worst of it, though...

passages.title: Orders from High Command
passages.text:
The letter is actually an order from Horde high command. Someone named Overlord Krom'gar has issued a "strip job" on this mine in order to obtain something called azure iron flake. Presumably this flake is obtained from breaking down the ore.

It gets worse. They plan to mix the azure flake with the explosives sitting inside the huge bomb outside and blow up Windshear Hold.

We don't have a moment to lose, <name>! Take this translated copy of the letter and return to Boog! He'll know what to do next.

passages.title: Orders from High Command
passages.text: Well? What's it say?

passages.title: Orders from High Command
passages.text:
<Beads of sweat roll down Boog's overly large forehead as he reads the translated letter.>

This is bad. Really, really bad. You have to warn Lord Fallowmere at Windshear Hold.

What in the... It's MOVING! The goblin balloon is taking off! We're too late!

passages.title: Oh, the Insanity!
passages.text:
So, I've been thinkin'...

If someone's out-of-their-mind-guano-crazy, do they know it?

Case in point, I coulda swore that I'd collected a barrel of gunpowder from the cannonballs around here, but it's nowhere ta be found.

I distinctly remember lifting the cannonballs from them Gilblins just west of here.

Maybe they're right... maybe I really have lost it.

passages.title: Oh, the Insanity!
passages.text:
You want nuthin' to do with me, <race>.

I'm a touch... screwy.

passages.title: Oh, the Insanity!
passages.text:
My gunpowder!

You found it! I'm not crazy after all!

passages.title: Commandeer That Balloon!
passages.text:
We don't have a moment to lose, <name>. You're going to have to commandeer that hot air balloon and stop it!

How? I have no idea! We don't have time to argue details! Grab onto that rope ladder and climb up! Just start banging on stuff once you're inside!

If you somehow manage to stop the balloon and survive, report to Lord Fallowmere at Windshear Hold in the west.

Good luck, we're all counting on you. Now if you'll excuse me I'm going to RUN FOR MY LIFE!

passages.title: Commandeer That Balloon!
passages.text: Amazing story, lad. I'd have never believed you had I not seen it with my own eyes. You did enough damage to that balloon to make those fiends pull back! Alas, the threat is far from over. We have only delayed the attack. There is much work to do if we are to stop the Horde from destroying Stonetalon!

passages.title: The Wormwing Problem
passages.text:
Skylord Omnuron has been too gentle with the Wormwing harpies. He allows them to share a perch on this mountain just because they're creatures of the air. Well <class>, not all creatures of the air are created equal.

When the attacks on Hyjal began, the Wormwing went into a frenzy. They're up there right now, assaulting a sacred shrine they once claimed to revere.

I'm not troubled. Now we have a reason to drive them from Hyjal, don't we?

passages.title: The Wormwing Problem
passages.text:
<Thisalee nods, contentedly, her eyes sparkling.>

Feels great to be off the leash, doesn't it?

passages.title: Dah, Nunt... Dah, Nunt...
passages.text:
So, seein' as ya been so kind to me, I'm inclined to let you in on a special secret.

I've found the biggest shiney of all, no more than 50 steps from where we're standin'!

Only one thing stands between you, me, and great fortune - and his name is Gnaws.

Don't fret now - I've got a plan.

Gnaws loves his grubs, so I've loaded one up with that gunpowder so as to make like a trap of sorts, ya see?

Just set it floatin' up in the reef. Once the shark is dead, we're rich!

passages.title: Dah, Nunt... Dah, Nunt...
passages.text: Well? Is Gnaws dead, <race>?

passages.title: Dah, Nunt... Dah, Nunt...
passages.text:
Amazing!

You watch the great white beast swim off into the depths and wonder to yourself if anything could ever take him down...

passages.title: Built to Last
passages.text:
My lady, I have a request from the High Priestess that I am to pass along to you. Many of the city's defenses remain from long before it sunk beneath the waves, and some of them are but a trivial task to reactivate, were it not for the countless Kvaldir that stand in our way.

We are told you are to be fighting on Nar'shola Terrace above us. You would do my lady a great service if you would but touch some of the devices as you pass. Your noble blood should prove more than sufficient to reactivate them.

passages.title: Built to Last
passages.text:
The Nar'shola Wards are performing perfectly. I will inform the Mistress of the Tides of your aid immediately.

Thank you for your assistance, my lady.

passages.title: Not Soon Forgotten
passages.text:
The Kvaldir leader has shown his rotting, ugly face but a short swim from here, down this hall to our west. We kill him now and the Kvaldir occupation of our once beloved city shall be ended.

Beware Battlemaiden, for he is no weakling. He has many Kvaldir at his command. Some Sira'kess Sea Witches have been dispatched to weaken him during your attack, but they will be interrupted if you let any of his Kvaldir attack them.

Show no mercy, Battlemaiden.

passages.title: Not Soon Forgotten
passages.text:
<The Kvaldir General crumples to the ground, defeated.>

<With this, the ruins of Vashj'ir have been claimed for Lady Naz'jar. Her ultimate goals remain uncertain, but it is clear that the naga came here with purpose.>

<If only you could continue, you are sure that the answers to defeating the naga lie within this vision, but the Wavespeaker's magics are waning, and you are losing your connection with the Battlemaiden.>

passages.title: With a Little Help...
passages.text:
Fine, I be helpin' ya. He not gettin' outa payin' me alimony that easy! 'Sides, there be the baby he had with me sistah ta take care of!

First thing we needin' is the innards of his closest friends. That'd be his cap'ns.

Go down there an' pay the three of them a visit.

passages.title: With a Little Help...
passages.text: A fresh heart, lungs, an liver be what we needin'. The ones from his cap'ns will have ta do though they all be likely picked.

passages.title: With a Little Help...
passages.text:
<Ajamon makes a face at the state of the organs.>

They's gonna have ta do. It not be like he had many friends. Ain't that right, Two-Tusk?

passages.title: A Prayer and a Wing
passages.text:
A winged visage? Could it be...?

<name>, there's no time to waste. You may have been speaking to Aviana herself, trying to return to us.

I'll need something from Aviana's past to reach out to her. High atop the ridge overlooking this shrine, you'll find a series of huge nests belonging to Blaithe, an ancient bird of prey that was once her consort. For ten thousand years he's been mad with grief.

Go to one of his roosts, and use this call to summon him. Kill Blaithe and bring me one of his feathers.

passages.title: A Prayer and a Wing
passages.text: Don't trouble yourself over Blaithe's condition. Grief robbed that creature of a soul epochs ago. He was but a shell of his former self, a beast of pure rage.

passages.title: A Prayer and a Wing
passages.text:
That was nasty work, <name>, but it had to be done.

And if Aviana is truly to be resurrected, then perhaps your actions have enabled Blaithe to someday come back as well?

Now let's see if we can contact our long lost guardian...

passages.title: A Plea From Beyond
passages.text:
<You can't make sense of the spirit's urgent plea, but maybe Choluna can decipher what's going on here.>

<Speak with Choluna back inside the shrine!>

passages.title: A Plea From Beyond
passages.text: Slow down, <class>! You look as though you've seen a ghost...

passages.title: Culling the Wendigos
passages.text:
The wendigos in the Grizzled Den to the southwest of town have long been a thorn in our side. They're never quite strong enough to threaten Kharanos directly, yet they prey on travelers, mountaineer patrols, and supply convoys.

I'm going to be withdrawing my observers from the Grizzled Den because I need them on the troll front. Would you help my men finish culling the wendigo population? Without strength of numbers, they won't be able to attack us.

passages.title: Culling the Wendigos
passages.text: Now that you've dealt with the wendigos, we should be able to focus our efforts on the Frostmane trolls to the east.

passages.title: Pilfered Supplies
passages.text: With the Frostmanes making trouble to our east, the wendigos have sensed our weakness and grown bolder in their raids. Only one of the four most recent supply wagons has made it here safely. The wendigos made off with the rest, stashing it in the Grizzled Den, a cave southwest of town. If you're willing to go down there and recover the stolen supplies, you would have the gratitude of all the townspeople and the mountaineers defending Kharanos.

passages.title: Pilfered Supplies
passages.text: Did you find any of the missing supplies?

passages.title: Pilfered Supplies
passages.text: Well done, <name>. The mountaineers will be glad to hear that half-rations are at an end. They'll need all their strength to continue fighting the Frostmanes.

passages.title: Rumble in the Lumber... Mill
passages.text:
Prepare yourself, <name>! The Warlord comes! Kill him and take his key. Use the key to release me.

Should we make it out of here, report the following to Lord Fallowmere at Windshear Hold:

The Horde has aborted their plans to destroy Windshear Hold due to the efforts of one of our heroes. They now plan to move the bomb to Battlescar Valley and drop it on our armies battling the Horde at that location.

They must be stopped!

passages.title: Rumble in the Lumber... Mill
passages.text:
A hero thwarted their plans to destroy Windshear Hold, eh? That hero was you, <name>. You are the pride of the Alliance!

It seems that you have bought us a little bit of time. I must plan for the battle that lies ahead of us. Seek out the other inhabitants of Windshear Hold and lend them your assistance. I will call for you when I am ready to initiate our defensive strategy.

passages.title: DUN-dun-DUN-dun-DUN-dun
passages.text:
If ol' Gnaws had heels he'd be on 'em right now.

Fortunately for you, I think like a shark.

Gnaws is mad as all get out and we're gunna use that to our advantage.

Here, I found this chain while out treasure-huntin'. Use it to tie off to that harpoon gun.

When Gnaws sees ya he'll be consumed with rage - that's when we strike!

You try to finish him off and I'll sneak in there and grab the shiney.

Hurry, <class>, before he grows them teeth back!

passages.title: DUN-dun-DUN-dun-DUN-dun
passages.text: This really ain't as bad as it looks...

passages.title: Thinning the Horde
passages.text:
The Horde's numbers swell as reinforcements from Ashenvale and Azshara arrive. There is no diplomacy to be had with the beasts. This is Hellscream's Horde and Hellscream's Horde wants our blood! We will not sit idly by and allow them to take our land and kill our people. We must act!

We must thin the Horde! Consider it your daily responsibility.

Venture forth into Stonetalon Mountains and slay as many of the Horde as you are able. Let them know that the Alliance will not surrender!

passages.title: Thinning the Horde
passages.text:
Good. Their blood is on Hellscream's hands. Send enough of them back to Orgrimmar in a body bag and the populace of the Horde might react.

<Lord Fallowmere laughs.>

Who am I kidding? They're monsters!

passages.title: Just Ask Alice
passages.text:
Mr. P is sick, <mister/miss>. Won't you help him? All you have to do is find his hat and batteries and he'll be all better. I'd go get them myself, but I can't leave Mr. P alone!

His hat was stolen by the meanies in the Venture Co. over at the water wheel and his batteries are hidden around Windshear Crag. You'll just have to look real hard for those!

Would you kindly bring Mr. P's stuff back so he can teach those baddies in the Horde a lesson?

passages.title: Just Ask Alice
passages.text: Mr. P is so sad. We need to make him happy!

passages.title: Just Ask Alice
passages.text:
<Alice claps excitedly.>

Mr. P you're gonna be ok! Hooray!

<Alice expertly places all of the parts you collected into Big Papa.>

Oh, Mr. P! I knew it!

passages.title: Heartstrike
passages.text:
We don't have any hope of taking the Nethergarde Mines from the Alliance... at least not yet. Nethergarde is well-defended, and their supply routes are established and strong. Our goal, then, is to damage their economy. We can't take the mine by force, but with surgical strikes we can drastically reduce the mine's efficiency.

I have men creating a distraction outside the mines. Head east, sneak into the mines, and speak with Rofilian Dane for your assignment.

passages.title: Heartstrike
passages.text: Finally... another operative shows up.  I hope you're loosened up... it's time to tango, partner.

passages.title: It's All Mine
passages.text:
All over this cavern you'll find unguarded piles of ore, just waiting to be tampered with. Our first choice would be to steal the ore, obviously, but that requires mine carts, protection, and labor... three things we just don't have. So instead, we're just going to ruin this little mining party with a little bit of highly corrosive solvent.

Take this bottle - CAREFULLY - and pour it onto those heaps of ore. 'Cause if we can't have this ore, then neither can they.

passages.title: It's All Mine
passages.text: I wouldn't store that solvent where I store my potions, if I were you.

passages.title: It's All Mine
passages.text: There's nothing quite like a big fat kick in the wallet, is there, you Alliance lunkheads?!

passages.title: Pick Your Fate
passages.text:
It costs the Alliance approximately fifty gold to train a miner, two hundred to train an engineer, and three hundred to train a foreman. Every Alliance goon that we kill isn't just a military victory... it's a financial one.

Now get down there and destroy their workers!

passages.title: Pick Your Fate
passages.text: Excellent work, friend.  I like the way you do business.

passages.title: Into the Mountain
passages.text:
The next phase of operations takes place deeper within the mine. Speak with Tak'arili for your next assignment. Just follow the mine cart rails to the southeast, and follow the curve around. You'll see him at the entrance to the mine's upper chamber.

It's been a pleasure doing business with you, <name>.

passages.title: Into the Mountain
passages.text:
Good, you here already.  Stick around for a bit, little <race>.  We gonna mess with the Alliance.

I love my job, mon.

passages.title: That's Not Us
passages.text:
First things first... it looks like we got ourselves a problem. These miners down the pathway to the right have been runnin' around like a chickens without they heads on. My best guess is that they dug too deep and found somethin' nasty... a demon, an elemental, or some kind o' tentacley beast.

Tak'arili don't like surprises. Find out what the problem is and take care of it, then we get ourselves back on track.

passages.title: That's Not Us
passages.text:
So it was a demon?  Those miners never seen a demon before?  We're in the Blasted Lands, mon!  Demons are everywhere!

<Tak'arili sighs.>

Ah well... let's get on to da good stuff, shall we?

passages.title: Some People Just Need Killing
passages.text:
The tunnel ahead, headin' west, will take you straight to Chief Prospector Hondo's office. He's the big cheese around here, and Tak'arili's heard tell that he's a darn fine miner. That's why he's gotta die.

There's just one problem: the pathway is completely FILLED with those pesky Nethergarde flunkies. That's why you gotta disguise yourself. Hop inside this box here, and sneak down the pathway. Hopefully you won't draw too much suspicion on your way to da killin'.

passages.title: Some People Just Need Killing
passages.text: Hondo ain't gonna know what hit him.

passages.title: Some People Just Need Killing
passages.text: Nice work, mon!  Without Hondo, these guys are helpless.  Dis mine'll be ours soon enough!

passages.title: Mission Complete
passages.text: We be done here, mon. Only thing left to do is send a report to Okrilla. You doin' anything right now?

passages.title: Mission Complete
passages.text: You've returned, <name>?

passages.title: Mission Complete
passages.text:
<Okrilla glances over the report.>

Impressive, <name>.  I wouldn't have hidden in that box, but otherwise, you have performed bravely and admirably.  The battle we won today may not win us any immediate spoils, but the damage you've done to the Alliance will last for a long time.

passages.title: The Dreadmaul Furnace
passages.text:
I meant what I said, <race>. You helped me, now I'll pass on what I know.

A demon hunter recently came through here, but only briefly. He was headed south, speaking of demons. Normally I'd have slain the night elf on sight, but he didn't seem to be Alliance scum, and anybody who kills demons is useful to me for the time being.

You should check in with Lynnore and Drazial, a pair of blood mages I sent down that way. They've camped in the back of an ogre cave.

passages.title: The Dreadmaul Furnace
passages.text:
Okrilla sent you?  Okrilla the killa'?

<Lynnore listens to your tale.>

Loramus was his name?  I'm sorry to say that we have not seen your demon hunter... but we have ways of finding him.

passages.title: Attune the Bloodstone
passages.text:
I admit, we haven't picked the most... convenient of spots to perform our studies, especially for passing adventurers who wish to enter and leave at will. Our agreement with the ogres is tenuous, and I'm afraid we can't convince them not to attack you when you draw near.

However, I can allow you to attune yourself to our bloodstone teleporters. Simply place your hands on the stone to my right, and you will be teleported outside of the cave. Then use the stone outside to teleport back!

passages.title: Attune the Bloodstone
passages.text: The attunement process is simple, but will certainly come in handy down the line.

passages.title: Attune the Bloodstone
passages.text: Excellent.  Now that that's out of the way...

passages.title: The First Step
passages.text:
To perform the ritual you've requested - and perhaps some more rituals in the near future - we're going to need blood. The Blasted Lands are filled with every type of reagent we might need for our blood magic... it's just a matter of the correct combination.

<Lynnore quickly confers with Drazial for a moment.>

Basilisks and hyenas, even amounts. And we're going to need plenty of it. Head east, to the center of the Blasted Lands. And don't forget... you can use that teleporter!

passages.title: The First Step
passages.text: Ogre blood only takes you so far.  Do you have it?

passages.title: The First Step
passages.text:
<Lynnore eyes the blood hungrily.>

More than enough, and still warm!  Now, let's get this ritual started, shall we?

passages.title: The Altar of Storms
passages.text:
Up on the bluffs above our comfy cave is a powerful altar. A powerful DEMONIC altar, guarded by cultists, but powerful nonetheless. If you can reach it, you can use it to bring Loramus back to us.

The altar will likely resist your efforts, so you'll have to protect Loramus' body while the ritual completes. Bring the demon hunter back to me afterwards.

passages.title: The Altar of Storms
passages.text: You... you fool!  What have you done?

passages.title: Time is Short
passages.text:
I was hunting a demon named Razelikh, when his ogre lieutenant Grol assaulted me. I was caught unaware, and I died... but so did Grol.

Razelikh plans to return to the Blasted Lands and overwhelm the lands with his demons. Even now, he is preparing to summon his legions to eliminate us.

<The demon hunter quickly draws a rune in the air, then hands it to you.>

Deliver this to Wazzik at the Dark Portal, to the southeast. He will guide you. Quickly! We haven't much time!

passages.title: Time is Short
passages.text: Do I know you, good <race>?

passages.title: Time is Short
passages.text:
What?  LORAMUS?!

Oh blast, keep it down, would ya?  If my boss gets word that I worked for Loramus, do you know how quickly I'd be on my rear end?!

<Wazzik takes the rune from you, presses it to his chest, closes his eyes, and nods.>

Well, you weren't lying.  Let's get to work.

passages.title: A Bloodmage's Gotta Eat Too
passages.text:
Contrary to popular belief, blood elf bloodmages do NOT drink blood. We eat normal food like everybody else - something which can be hard to come by in the recesses of an ogre stronghold.

The ashmane boars in the central valley of the Blasted Lands are, if nothing else, convenient for eating, as their meat does not require any cooking. Would you hunt these boars and help us replenish our foodstores?

passages.title: A Bloodmage's Gotta Eat Too
passages.text: I'm famished!  If you don't hurry, I might actually resort to drinking our reagents.

passages.title: A Bloodmage's Gotta Eat Too
passages.text: These are perfect, <name>.  Lynnore and I will eat well for the next several days.

passages.title: Enhancing the Stone
passages.text:
<Wazzik finishes packing the materials up in a neatly-wrapped package.>

That's all that Loramus asked of us. When you see him, make sure you let him know how much of a help I was. I fear he will not see my hand in this.

passages.title: Enhancing the Stone
passages.text: <class>... you return...

passages.title: Enhancing the Stone
passages.text:
This is sufficient.  If you see Wazzik again, you may tell him that he performed satisfactorily.  I will get the bloodmages to work on fashioning the stone knife of sealing.  There is no need for questions now.  All will be revealed in time.

While they work, I have another task for you to complete.  Actually, make that three tasks.

passages.title: Watching Our Back
passages.text:
<Warlord Dar'toon speaks in hushed tones.>

I have orders from... higher up... that you would be suitable for. I've seen the Alliance periodically referring to a stack of papers on that barrel over there. I'd like you to take a look at those papers and find out what it is that they're plotting. My duty and station prevent me from such a questionable task, but a newcomer like you might be able to slip in unnoticed...

passages.title: Watching Our Back
passages.text: Did you get a look at those plans, <name>?

passages.title: Watching Our Back
passages.text:
You're certain nobody saw you?  Good.

<Dar'toon listens to your recount of the information you saw.>

Hmph... fairly harmless stuff.  Either the Alliance are foolish enough to NOT be planning something against us... or they're hiding their information better than I expected.  Either way, well done, soldier.

passages.title: The Sunveil Excursion
passages.text:
Oh, right, I received a notification from someone a few days ago. The Reliquary, was it? They're looking for someone to... do something...

<The Warlord rifles through some papers.>

Ah, here it is! Yes, Rohan Sunveil of The Reliquary is seeking able-bodied adventurers to assist with an archaeological expedition to the south.

Here, take this with you. Why don't you go speak with that elf?

passages.title: The Sunveil Excursion
passages.text: Welcome, traveler.  Thank you for responding to my summons.

passages.title: The Amulet of Allistarj
passages.text:
When my master helped me to take my eyes out, he gave me the gift of sight... a sight much greater than yours, or even of these blood-craving elves. My sight allows me to see objects of demonic power, such as the Amulet of Allistarj.

Allistarj himself is dead, but he locked his amulet up in a trove inside the Serpent's Coil, to the east. Along with the other amulets, this relic will give us access to Razelikh's perch.

passages.title: The Amulet of Allistarj
passages.text: Allistarj left a piece of himself in that amulet.  Even now, I can sense his evil.

passages.title: The Amulet of Allistarj
passages.text:
<Lynnore examines the amulet.>

He was an archmage, I can feel it.  I will hold the amulet for you while you collect the rest.

passages.title: The Amulet of Sevine
passages.text:
Sevine's amulet is in the hands of a murloc, far to the east, on a shelf that overlooks the Shattershore. How it ended up in that murloc's possession, I cannot say, but I can state with certainty that you will find it there.

I feel a stronger connection with Sevine than with the rest of Razelikh's servants... possibly because she built the Altar of Storms, upon which you resurrected me. Bring her Amulet to Lynnore, along with the rest.

passages.title: The Amulet of Sevine
passages.text: Sevine's amulet... along with the others, we can reach the Rise of the Defiler.

passages.title: The Amulet of Sevine
passages.text:
<Lynnore hefts the amulet.>

A warlock... and a powerful one at that.  I will hold onto this until the time is right.

passages.title: The Amulet of Grol
passages.text:
Grol... the ogre who tore me apart.

<Loramus laughs.>

It would seem that Grol's body has changed hands several times since we died together, but it no longer rests with the ogres. His body, along with his amulet of power, is in a wrecked ship off the Shattershore, to the east. His amulet is the last... once combined, the three will give us access to Razelikh, and therein lies our chance to stop his madness.

passages.title: The Amulet of Grol
passages.text: The third amulet, from Razelikh's third lieutenant.

passages.title: The Amulet of Grol
passages.text:
<Lynnore clutches the third amulet.>

He was a powerful warrior, this one.  I will keep the amulet until Loramus is ready to proceed.

passages.title: You Are Rakh'likh, Demon
passages.text:
Hero, listen well.

First, we must travel to the Deathly Usher, who waits at the northern foot of the Rise of the Defiler, to our northeast. The usher will take us to the top of the rise. Once there, I need you to help me defeat Razelikh, for I fear that I am not strong enough to defeat him alone.

Most importantly, I need you to hold the stone knife, and do not use it until I tell you to. The knife will trap Razelikh's soul within its new, eternal prison.

If we succeed, speak with Wazzik.

passages.title: You Are Rakh'likh, Demon
passages.text:
I see.  So this was Loramus' plan all along.

I suspected correctly, but I suppose I refused to believe it.  And now, his final instruction for me makes much more sense:

He asked me to let you choose from one of these.

passages.title: The Mad Magus
passages.text:
There's only one ting left dat we can do. Ya gotta slay someone with the big mojo in Tony's presence.

No, not me!

Ol' Magus Tirth went crazy when he tried ta stop the waters rushin' in at the Cataclysm. Now he be hauntin' the area just south of the Holdfast.

Take dis soul stick an' use it on his corpse, mon. Then bring Tony back an' we be gettin' him back in his body.

Ya can use me spirit portal ta get down there an' back.

passages.title: The Mad Magus
passages.text: Ya gotta use the stick on Tirth's corpse if ya gonna help, <name>.

passages.title: The Mad Magus
passages.text: Now we gonna bring Tony Two-Tusk back ta life. You both ready, mon?

passages.title: Neptool's Revenge
passages.text:
No number of naga deaths will bring back the Rockpool tribe, but any amount of revenge will help the spirits of my people rest more easily.

Many of the more powerful Bloodwash have set up a fortress in the caverns to the northwest. Slay them, in the name of the Rockpool. The remaining Bloodwash have erected gladiatorial pools and Azsh'ir altars on our beach, where they pit my people against one another and worship their false god. Slay them, in the name of the Tidehunter.

passages.title: Neptool's Revenge
passages.text: The last Rockpool may be taken hostage today and killed tomorrow, landwalker... but they will pass into the underworld knowing that a brave <race> avenged their death.  Thank you.

passages.title: The Future of the Rockpool
passages.text:
The Rockpool tadpoles left upon this crate appear tired, scared, and nearly dried out. They need to be taken to the water, and quickly.

Perhaps if you can drag this crate across the beach and into the Forbidden Sea, far off the coast of the Red Reaches, then they will have a chance of escaping, and the Rockpool murlocs may live on...

passages.title: Our Fallen Friends
passages.text:
Based on what you're telling me, it sounds like there aren't many survivors... just restless spirits. The least we can do is give them their rest.

<Enohar takes a long draw off of a mug of black ale.>

Head back to the Shattershore and vanquish the worgen ghosts that still remain. Doing so should release their spirit from this world and allow them to pass into the next.

passages.title: Our Fallen Friends
passages.text:
<Enohar takes a sip off of a freshly-refilled mug.>

Aye, you've done well, lad.  You do the Alliance proud.

passages.title: Curtail the Darktail
passages.text:
The other thing that concerns me about those shipwrecks is all the vultures that they've attracted. Knowing how those birds operate, they've already picked the bones clean, but still... we can't allow them to further desecrate the bodies of our friends.

Before I brewed, I hunted. Here, take this bow, and more importantly, these arrows. They've been laced with a little concoction that should give those bonepickers a surprise.

passages.title: Curtail the Darktail
passages.text:
It's a tragedy, what happened on the Shattershore.  They weren't even soldiers... just people looking for a new home.

I think we've done all we can, <name>.

passages.title: Minor Distractions
passages.text:
Nethergarde has stood steadfast for years against the demon onslaught that plagues this land. Our watch is never-ending, our vigilance unfaltering, and our courage bottomless.

We have held these lands since the portal opened, but now these Horde insects have the insolence to stand in our way!? We have protected THEM as well as we have protected ourselves!

<Lungertz looks you over.>

Let's see if you've got a hand for combat. Slay one of the Horde's Okril'lon scouts that nibble at our perimeter.

passages.title: Minor Distractions
passages.text: Hmm... not bad.  You're quicker than many of my men.  Stick around, <name>... I may have use of you yet.

passages.title: Remove Their Arms
passages.text:
Say there... <name>, is it? I've got a proposition for you which involves explosions. Interested?

I couldn't help but overhear your conversation with the quartermaster. You see... I've been working on an explosive device. It's not very effective against other creatures, but devastating against artillery. If you're heading back into the field to visit those orcs, find some enemy supplies and give this thing a try. Who knows... maybe they like explosions too.

passages.title: Remove Their Arms
passages.text: Ahh, the sound of things going boom makes my heart pitter-pat.  You've made this gnome's day, <name>.

passages.title: A Closer Look
passages.text:
We've seen countless ships sail past the shore to the southeast, but most pass by inconspicuously. Several days ago, however, a powerful storm carried several of the ships to shore and left them wrecked.

I'd bet a pint of Nethergarde Bitter that they were Horde ships if I didn't love Nethergarde Bitter so much. I can pay you gold, though, if you'll go check out those ships and report back.

passages.title: A Closer Look
passages.text: What news from the Shattershore, <name>?

passages.title: A Closer Look
passages.text:
You saw worgen?  That's bad.

Worgen ghosts?  That's even worse.
