While I would not suffer any emotional harm should the beast devour you, I would prefer that you were the victor. Borelgore has been known to devour others who tried to hunt him.

passages.title: The Corpulent One
passages.text: Keep this up and I may have to keep you here at Eastwall, <race>.

passages.title: Righteous Indignation
passages.text:
The Mossflayers of Zul'Mashar spit in the face of the Light! They cannibalize, they criminalize, they prioritize the forces of evil over good! I advise that you remove their eyes, and give rise to the demise and the goodbyes of the unwise!

You will travel north, and you will rain down on them with righteous justice and indignation, <name>. The fury that they have wrought in the eyes of the Light shall be channeled through you.

passages.title: Righteous Indignation
passages.text: <Deacon Andaal is deep in prayer.>

passages.title: Righteous Indignation
passages.text: Oh, hallelujah, and praise, praise be to the Light, my brother!

passages.title: Into the Flames
passages.text:
This is the last time you will see me, <name>. I am leaving the caravan.

If you want to continue fighting by my side, hang on to Thresh'jin's body. I can wait for a while longer. When you are ready to say goodbye, throw the body into the bonfire atop Zul'Mashar's ziggurat.

Thank you for your companionship, <name>. You were strong.

passages.title: Only One May Enter
passages.text:
<Dalar flips through the codex.>

HAHAH!

Oh... That's bad.

<Dalar closes the codex and looks up at you.>

With this ring only ONE may enter the pocket dimension at Amber Mill. That person will then need to fight through an army of magi and kill the archmage that is generating the phase from the inside. Only then will the dimension fold, ejecting all of the magi.

The portal to entry is hidden at the back of a cave in Beren's Peril.

That's all I know. Take the ring back to Sylvanas.

passages.title: Only One May Enter
passages.text: What have you learned?

passages.title: Only One May Enter
passages.text:
Only one may enter? I know just the person for this mission.

<Sylvanas nods at you.>

I will prepare our forces and have them at the ready.

passages.title: Ix'lar the Underlord
passages.text:
I know we're supposed to head to Northdale, but that can wait, right? Besides, this lovely little goblin was just telling me about some Scourge that are even closer by.

So apparently there's this nerubian underlord named Ix'lar that has been trying to make a name for himself ever since the Lich King was slain. He's set up a camp of undead to our north.

Sure, Tyrosus wants us to kill banshees in Northdale. We'll get to that. But let's kill this nerubian first, while we're close!

passages.title: Ix'lar the Underlord
passages.text:
I couldn't stop him.  While you and Tarenar were out, Giddy ran north all alone!

Tarenar, you should have known better!  Gidwin gets so impatient sometimes, and you only egg him on.  If Giddy gets into any trouble, I'm blaming you for this.

passages.title: SI:7 Drop
passages.text:
Mathias Shaw and the SI:7 are here to assist us with operations up top in the Twilight Citadel. I need you to escort them there.

The Wildhammer are being kind enough to give us a lift in. The agents have some things that they need to do down in the Twilight Gate area first, though.

Speak with Angus Stillmountain and get yourself a squad to drop off. You'll fly them in. A big blue X marks the spot.

passages.title: SI:7 Drop
passages.text: I need you to escort those SI:7 agents safely to their destination, <name>.

passages.title: SI:7 Drop
passages.text:
That must have been deadly.

While I don't approve of their methods, no one can question the effectiveness of Master Mathias Shaw and his SI:7. Not to mention that you're here. Our victory is all but assured.

passages.title: Kor'kron Drop
passages.text:
Garona and a detachment of the Kor'kron are here to assist us with operations up top in the Twilight Citadel. I need you to escort them there.

I've called upon a local tribe of trolls to give us a lift in with their wind riders. The assassins have some things that they need to do down in the Twilight Gate area first, though.

Speak with the troll chief, Jon-Jon Jellyneck and get yourself a detachment of Kor'kron to drop off. You'll fly them in. A big red X marks the spot.

passages.title: Kor'kron Drop
passages.text: I need you to get those Kor'kon assassins safely to their destination, <name>.

passages.title: Kor'kron Drop
passages.text:
That must have been exciting.

Despite any losses that the Kor'kron may have incurred along the way, no one will be able to doubt their effectiveness, nor that of Garona. And with you in the mix, it's only a matter of time before victory is ours.

passages.title: Ogres & Ettins
passages.text: I want you to get in there past those boulders to the northwest at the Twilight Gate. Kill every Bloodeye Clan ogre and ettin in sight. Think you can handle that for me, <name>?

passages.title: Ogres & Ettins
passages.text: There are more to be killed, tauren. You do have the stomach for that, yes?

passages.title: Ogres & Ettins
passages.text:
And here I thought that today couldn't get any better.

I enjoy being wrong, occasionally.

passages.title: Move the Mountain
passages.text:
If the Twilight Gate is to fall, we need to get Skullcrusher the Mountain out of there!

Before they left, I saw to it that your SI:7 agents took some explosives hidden in a Twilight's Hammer crate. By now, they will have planted them on the steps leading up to the upper portion of the Citadel.

I want you to set the explosives off and then signal us when that monster's out of the way.

That's when we'll attack and finish off the ogre compound!

passages.title: Move the Mountain
passages.text:
If the Twilight Gate is to fall, we must get Skullcrusher the Mountain out of there!

Before they left, I saw to it that your Kor'kron assassins took some explosives hidden in a Twilight's Hammer crate. By now, they will have planted them on the steps leading up to the upper portion of the Citadel.

I want you to set the explosives off and then signal us when that monster's out of the way.

That's when we'll attack and finish off the ogre compound!

passages.title: Call in the Artillery
passages.text:
I prefer a stand up honorable fight. These monsters deserve nothing better than to be destroyed by the weapons in our hands. However, this particular situation calls for the use of more powerful measures.

Take this flare and mark each of the four buildings within the Twilight Gate to the southwest. Our cannons will handle the rest.

passages.title: Call in the Artillery
passages.text: Thanks to you, our cannoneers hit their marks. Tell me about the situation within the Twilight Gate.

passages.title: Call in the Artillery
passages.text:
A pity that we're no longer allowed to drop the Plague on our enemies. It would prove quite effective in this situation. Oh well, at least we have war machines to destroy their precious gates.

I want you to take this flare. Use it to mark each of the four buildings within the Twilight Gate to the northwest. The war machines will handle the rest.

passages.title: Call in the Artillery
passages.text: I must say that I rather enjoyed the sight of their buildings being hit.

passages.title: Signal the Attack
passages.text: Now that you've lured Skullcrusher the Mountain away from the Twilight Gate, it's time to signal your forces at Victor's Point to attack!

passages.title: Signal the Attack
passages.text: Now that you've lured Skullcrusher the Mountain away from the Twilight Gate, it's time to signal your forces at Crushblow to attack!

passages.title: Up to the Citadel
passages.text:
Now that the attack is underway, it's time to deal with the Twilight Citadel. If you don't mind, I'd like for you to escort the SI:7 forces to Master Mathias Shaw.

He's hiding somewhere up top. The SI:7 squad commander can tell you where.

Thank you, <name>. We look forward to joining you in the assault upon the Citadel!

passages.title: Up to the Citadel
passages.text:
Now that the attack is underway, it's time to deal with the Twilight Citadel. If you don't mind, I'd like for you to escort the Kor'kron forces up to Garona.

She's hiding somewhere up top. The Kor'kron squad commander can tell you where.

Thank you, <name>. We look forward to joining you in the assault upon the Citadel!

passages.title: Draconic Mending
passages.text:
Our dragons are returning from battle covered in Twilight corrupted flame and pursued by Twilight drakes.

My menders can tend to our dragons' wounds, but they must be defended. Keep the drakes off of my menders. Lend your healing to our dragons as well if you are able.

Thank you for your help with this. Our battles for Grim Batol are never-ending. We need to get our strongest dragons back into the battle as soon as possible.

passages.title: Draconic Mending
passages.text: Keep the menders safe as they heal our wounded dragons!

passages.title: Draconic Mending
passages.text: We will take Grim Batol back from the Twilight's Hammer and thier allies. It may take time, but this is one charge that we cannot forsake.

passages.title: Breach in the Defenses
passages.text:
Every inch of air and every hill surrounding the redoubt is constantly under the watchful eye of Lira's drakes. They must have found a way into the shrine from beneath.

Take this Flashgrowth mote. It should prove more than sufficient to close any hole, tunnel, or portal they might have used to get inside our defenses.

Find the breach in our defenses. Close it.

passages.title: Breach in the Defenses
passages.text:
Well done. Thank you, <race>.

I will not be so foolish as to let such an oversight happen again.

passages.title: Bird Down! Bird Down!
passages.text:
While you were fighting along the coast, I spotted a gryphon tumble out of the clouds almost due west of here.

It wasn't one of ours.

Likely it belonged to one of the Wildhammer. I know that Kurdran wanted to establish contact with the lost Wildhammer clans as one of his primary objectives after taking the beach. 

I can't spare any more of my men to scout it out, but I can spare you. Find that downed Wildhammer!

passages.title: Bird Down! Bird Down!
passages.text: Aw dang crap it all. You're just an Alliance <class>. I was hoping for a rescue.

passages.title: Wings Over Highbank
passages.text:
Aye, look! I think she's perkin' up already.

Okay <Mr./Miss> Alliance fancy-pants <class>. Is that your base I see on the shore? "Highbank" you say. Can me and my bird hunker down there until she's better?

Hop on! We'll fly together back to Highbank!

passages.title: Wings Over Highbank
passages.text:
Well done, <name>! Aiding that downed gryphon-rider has given us our first contact with the old Wildhammer clans. We'll be able to find out who's still left, and in what numbers.

Our campaign is looking up!

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter III
passages.text:
<Sylvanas speaks directly through you.>

You must find the being responsible for keeping this dimensional pocket active. Likely that fool, Ataeric... Search the compound for him. Should you find him, do what you must to stop him from channeling his magic. He is undoubtedly protected by a powerful arcane shield, and will send minions of arcane energy after you. Defeat the minions while they are near him to unleash their energies. No mage can handle that much power!

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter III
passages.text: Had I not witnessed what you did with my own eyes I would not have believed it, <name>. Now, with the Ambermill magi on our side, there is but one thing left to do before we retake Gilneas and send those Alliance dogs running for Stormwind.

passages.title: Minions of Al'Akir
passages.text:
Al'Akir has sent his minions to do Deathwing's bidding.

The message is clear. We join them or they destroy us.

I do not know much about you, <race>. But I do know this. If you prove yourself to be an enemy of Al'Akir's, your aid will not go unnoticed.

What do you say, <class>?

passages.title: Minions of Al'Akir
passages.text: You continue to prove to be a valuable ally, <name>.

passages.title: Beat it Out of Them
passages.text:
We paladins are normally taught to exercise judgment and control when dealing with foes, but this is an emergency, and I never paid too much attention to my trainers anyhow.

I'm going to head into the Plaguewood and find out what I can about Giddy. You deal with the Scourge just to our northeast, on the other side of this tower. The undead don't fear death, but if you beat them enough, their tongues might slip, and we may get some clues to Gidwin's location.

passages.title: Beat it Out of Them
passages.text: It sounds like you were successful.  Hopefully this is enough information to find Gidwin.

passages.title: Duskwing, Oh How I Hate Thee...
passages.text:
I have seen many things in my day, <race>. The peaks of Mt. Hyjal... the oddities of Outland... a wall of Scourge soldiers, proceeding into war. But I have never seen a bat as big, or as shockingly white, as Duskwing.

How he taunts me from his roost!

This albino demon bat circles to the southwest of here, due north of Blackwood Lake. Track him down and destroy him. If he flies too high for you to reach, use my flare to get his attention.

passages.title: Duskwing, Oh How I Hate Thee...
passages.text: I hope you've done away with that creature.

passages.title: Duskwing, Oh How I Hate Thee...
passages.text:
Excellent work.  I can now continue my work without the distractions of that great white beast.

I shall fashion this fur into something you can use.

passages.title: Gidwin's Fate Revealed
passages.text:
Quickly - find an entrance to the slaughterhouse to our south. I will meet you on the inside.

Be ready for a fight!

passages.title: Gidwin's Fate Revealed
passages.text:
You have no idea how happy I am to see you two!  You're a sight for sore eyes... sore eyes that have been starin' through a banshee for far too long now.

I'm sorry for causing so much trouble.  Will you take me back to the caravan?

passages.title: Journey's End
passages.text:
I've had just about enough of the funk of this place. Undead stink is bad enough, and then you add mushrooms to the mix? I hate mushrooms!

I'm going to head back to Light's Hope Chapel, <name>... and I'm taking Tarenar and Fiona with me. I think we've all earned a well-deserved break.

Let me give you this. It's my hearthstone - you can use it to travel instantly back to Light's Hope. I won't need it - I'm going to be riding in the caravan.

In the FRONT SEAT.

passages.title: Journey's End
passages.text:
You've been more help than anyone expected of you, <name>.  The doors of my caravan are always open to you.

The boys and I have even put together a little something special for you.  Here, take your pick!

passages.title: Scourged Mass
passages.text:
You can't just kill the Scourge. They will come back. You must destroy the vile matter that makes up their being... and even then, they may come back as spectres.

Few undead use up as much mass as the lumbering abominations. Kill them, then burn their bodies. You will find them all over the Plaguewood.

Never let your rage dissipate, <race>. Remember: these abominations are sewn together from the bodies of good people. Their crime is that they exist.

passages.title: Scourged Mass
passages.text:
A blessed fire cleanses even the most corrupt of flesh.

They stood no chance in the face of the Light.

passages.title: Defenders of Darrowshire
passages.text:
The battle of Darrowshire was one of the many tragedies that we humans suffered at the hands of the Scourge. Its effects are still felt even today.

Many of the town's valiant defenders now roam again as the ghastly servants of the Scourge. We will end their misery.

Hunt cannibal ghouls here within the Plaguewood. Many of these fiends were once the good folk of Darrowshire, and destroying their forms now will set their souls free.

passages.title: Defenders of Darrowshire
passages.text: It is good to hear you found the tortured souls of my brethren and freed them.  I find my strength renewed, knowing at least some of the defenders of Darrowshire no longer wallow in the vile subservience of the Scourge.

passages.title: The Corpsebeasts
passages.text:
To the south, gutless cultists are focused on a grim task: re-animating enormous hunks of flesh, to create giants known as corpsebeasts. Luckily for us, these giants are still lifeless and weak.

Take this charm - using it will place a font of holy energy on the ground. If you can manage to place three of them near one of the corpsebeasts that the cultists are reanimating, the holy energy should overload it, destroying its body forever.

passages.title: The Corpsebeasts
passages.text:
You are a true Champion of the Light, <name>.  I wish you luck in your future endeavors, wherever they might take you.

If you need anything in the future, you can always find me here - knee-deep in the corpses of the slain.

passages.title: Counter-Plague Research
passages.text:
I once worked for the so-called "Banshee-Queen", Sylvanas, as an apothecary. I used to admire her, but something's changed within her. She's not herself anymore.

I broke my vows with the Forsaken and joined the Crusade. Now, I use my knowledge of alchemy to seek a counter-plague agent. And the Plaguewood is the perfect place to do so.

I need to resupply a few reagents, any of which can be found within the Plaguewood. I'll pay you if you can find any of these items.

passages.title: Counter-Plague Research
passages.text: You got the stuff?

passages.title: Counter-Plague Research
passages.text:
I love the smell of fresh foot scrapings, don't you?

If we're going to find a cure to the plague, we need to get creative with our ingredients.  Now, if you don't mind, I'm going to get back to work.

passages.title: The Plaguewood Tower
passages.text:
With the recent, unfortunate developments involving Gidwin, it might not be wise for a man my age to take the dangerous trip through the Plaguewood. This is fine - I can visit the Plaguewood Tower on my next trip around the loop.

I do, however, have a delivery that I need to get to Judkins. You are younger than I, and stronger in combat. Will you take this delivery to him?

passages.title: The Plaguewood Tower
passages.text: Highbeacon's Parcel... is Argus safe?  Did something happen?

passages.title: The Plaguewood Tower
passages.text: Whew.  Every time Argus comes plodding through that Plaguewood, I fear it to be his last.  It's good to see that he's wise enough to send a youngblood like you in his stead.

passages.title: A Fate Worse Than Butchery
passages.text:
The people of Terrordale, they were sick, then they turned bad. Definitely not good times.

The pigs, though... they also got sick! What did pigs do to deserve to get sick? Hah hah hah! Nothing!

People I can forget about, but the bad pigs still make me sad. If you kill them, though... I might get happy.

passages.title: A Fate Worse Than Butchery
passages.text: I cry for the poor pigs.

passages.title: A Fate Worse Than Butchery
passages.text: I see them!  Can you?  The little pig spirits, on their way to the great sty in the sky...

passages.title: Mostly Harmless
passages.text:
Here's another favor you can do for me, pal.

We had a whole shipment of Landmines come in from Booty Bay just the other day. But someone stole the whole lot of 'em in the night!

Whoever it was must be sloppy, because they dropped them all over the swamp to the east. No goblin I know would be that careless.

I need you to go gather those landmines up for me. I'm sure they're perfectly safe and disarmed. Every single one. Yup.

passages.title: Mostly Harmless
passages.text: Hey, you get those things I asked you about?

passages.title: Mostly Harmless
passages.text:
What did I tell you, eh? Perfectly safe!

I'll see about getting some of these over to to your friends, <name>. At a discount.

passages.title: Add 'em to the Pile
passages.text:
I've been collecting the skulls of the skeletons I defeat. I've amassed a small pile of them.

If you come across any skulls, you are welcome to add them to my pile. The huge pile of skulls seems to keep the waves of undead at bay and... well... it also just makes me happy to look at it.

passages.title: Add 'em to the Pile
passages.text: You seem to have your hands full.  Are those skulls I see?

passages.title: Add 'em to the Pile
passages.text: May my pile never stop growing.

passages.title: The Way is Open
passages.text:
My fellow Shaman and I will stay here to keep the portal open.

You should go upstairs and notify Kurdran that the work here is done. It'll please him to hear some good news for once.

passages.title: The Way is Open
passages.text:
Ho! I knew you were a <class> I could count on, <name>. Use that portal anytime you need to get from Stormwind back to the Highlands.

Now then, time to get to business. We need to locate and unite the lost Wildhammer clans scattered around the Highlands. Talking with Thordun here is a good start!

passages.title: Pyrewood's Fall
passages.text:
The attacks against our front are a distraction. With our attention turned towards the worgen onslaught, the Alliance has managed to take Pyrewood Village from our occupying forces.

<Godfrey hands you a bundle of torches.>

It must be purged.

With these torches we will burn Pyrewood Village to the ground, leaving only ashes for the enemy to hide behind.

Let us not waste another minute. Pyrewood Village is located southwest of the Forsaken Front. Lead us there, <name>.

passages.title: Pyrewood's Fall
passages.text: I feel no remorse.

passages.title: Pyrewood's Fall
passages.text: The part of me that was Gilnean died at Tempest's Reach. Only vengeance remains, <name>. To that end, we have work to do. Spare me your pointless queries.

passages.title: I Never Forget a Face
passages.text: You have discovered a partially digested head. Lord Godfrey perks up when he sees it. Perhaps you should give it to him.

passages.title: I Never Forget a Face
passages.text: I never forget a face!

passages.title: I Never Forget a Face
passages.text:
I know that face, <name>. This head belongs to a former Gilnean known as Sean Dempsey. He was imprisoned with Crowley before the great outbreak.

I wonder if it would be possible to put him back together. The rest of him must be in the belly of these crocolisks.

passages.title: From the Belly of the Beast
passages.text:
I think we can rebuild him. Perhaps if we put him back together he can give us information about Crowley.

We must kill every crocolisk in this marsh until we find the rest of Sean Dempsey's body! From the belly of the beast this man will be reborn!

passages.title: From the Belly of the Beast
passages.text: At the very least we'll have some crocolisk hides to make fancy shoes out of.

passages.title: From the Belly of the Beast
passages.text:
Now let's see if I can do this.

<Godfrey starts mumbling under his breath.>

...leg bone connects to the thigh bone...

...arm bone to torso...

...sprinkle on a little Forsaken necromancy...

TA-DA!

passages.title: Morgan's Fruition
passages.text:
Emperor Dagran Thaurissan has total control over the city from his throne ahead. If we are to stop his armies, we're going to have to end their emperor's reign.

You'll need to get past his personal guard, including the giant Magmus, to reach him. Move as quickly as possible - if word gets out before you finish, the entire city will descend upon his throne.

Note that the doors across the Lyceum will only open once you've lit the braziers with torches from the flamekeepers. Good luck.

passages.title: Morgan's Fruition
passages.text: If you do not succeed, I have no doubt that Thaurissan will execute the lot of us.

passages.title: Morgan's Fruition
passages.text:
You've done it! You've actually done it! Morgan's years of planning and waiting have finally come to fruition.

She may have lost her land and family when Ragnaros tore this land asunder, but with the Dark Iron crippled we'll be able to safely build a new kingdom of our own in the Burning Steppes. Not even the Firelord himself will be able to breech the capital's walls!

Make sure you come back someday when we've finished, you'll be our guest of the highest honor. I thank you with all my heart, <name>.

passages.title: The Northern Flank
passages.text:
I have ordered a defensive perimeter set up on our northern coast, at the Slithering Cove. Our scouts reported that the naga were trying to make landfall there.

Gralok is in charge of the operation - report to him and secure that beach!

passages.title: The Northern Flank
passages.text:
Warlord Zaela sent you? Good.

If you Horde are as strong as your Warchief promised, I expect to see some bloodshed on these shores.

passages.title: Blood in the Surf
passages.text:
These naga scum think to move upriver to reinforce the Bastion of Twilight. We will RIP off their fish heads and PULL OUT their SPINES.

<Gralok drives his broadsword into the dirt.>

Destroy the Blackscale!

passages.title: Blood in the Surf
passages.text: After the battle we will mount their heads on pikes and build a wall all along the beach. THAT will show these belly-crawling SNAKES who owns the Highlands.

passages.title: Blood in the Surf
passages.text:
<Gralok sizes you up.>

You're a true fighter, <name>. I liked watching you work. Perhaps the Dragonmaw really DO belong in your Horde.

passages.title: Shells on the Sea Shore
passages.text:
I salvaged these mortars from the wreck of our airship when she detonated above Dragonmaw Port. But ammunition is in short supply!

While you're running along the beach, do me a favor and pick up any unexploded mortar shells you find.

Unexploded shells are the best kind - you never know WHEN they're going to go off. Perfect for surprising an enemy!

passages.title: Shells on the Sea Shore
passages.text:
Do you have the shells? Hand them here!

...Gently!

passages.title: Shells on the Sea Shore
passages.text:
Oh yeah. YEAH! These are DEFINITELY going to kill somebody.

Probably naga.

passages.title: Signal the Attack
passages.text: Now that you've lured Skullcrusher the Mountain away from the Twilight Gate, I need you to signal our forces to attack!

passages.title: Signal the Attack
passages.text: Now that you've lured Skullcrusher the Mountain away from the Twilight Gate, I need you to signal our forces to attack!

passages.title: Drinks on the Rocks
passages.text:
What's up, "bro"! We were just in the middle of our completely spontaneous beach party when something terrible happened, "dude"!

I had a whole case of Silversnap Ice, the Baron's own drink of choice, until the silt crawlers stole them! I've never seen crawlers drink, but they took them right into the water and down the beach! We need some sort of awesome hero who can help retrieve our specifically-branded favorite beverage!

<Brono stares at you a moment.>

That means you, "brah"!

passages.title: Drinks on the Rocks
passages.text: You got the goods, "bro"?

passages.title: Drinks on the Rocks
passages.text:
Our ice-cold, refreshing Silversnap Ice! I can't thank you enough, "dawg", for this entirely spontaneous act of heroism!

Here, have your very own bottle as a totally sincere gesture of thanks! Be sure to tell ALL YOUR FRIENDS how good it is.

passages.title: Rebirth of the K.E.F.
passages.text:
Emperor Dagran Thaurissan has total control over the city from his throne ahead. If we are to stop his armies, we're going to have to end their emperor's reign.

You'll need to get past his personal guard, including the giant Magmus, to reach him. Move as quickly as possible - if word gets out before you finish, the entire city will descend upon his throne.

Note that the doors across the Lyceum will only open once you've lit the braziers with torches from the flamekeepers. Good luck.

passages.title: Rebirth of the K.E.F.
passages.text: If you do not succeed, I have no doubt that Thaurissan will execute the lot of us.

passages.title: Rebirth of the K.E.F.
passages.text:
A true <class> if I've ever seen one! You've done the impossible! I knew we could count on you.

And with that, I'd like for you to be the first to know that the Kargath Expeditionary Force is now officially back in business!

I extend to you my personal gratitude for your efforts here. Remember always our motto: "First in, last out, always victorious. Remember always Kargath."

You are dismissed.

passages.title: On Her Majesty's Secret Service
passages.text:
Lorna Crowley, daughter of Lord Darius Crowley, is currently at the Gilneas Liberation Front camp, located near the Greymane Wall, to the southeast.

Our primary mission is to infiltrate the camp and capture her alive. The Dark Lady believes that she will be able to use Lorna as a bargaining chip against Crowley. I say we just kill her and bring her back as Forsaken, but we must do as the Dark Lady commands.

We must hurry before the rest of the Alliance forces arrive.

passages.title: On Her Majesty's Secret Service
passages.text: You have done it! Finally, everything is in place. Should Crowley not accept our terms, his daughter will be turned.

passages.title: Can't Take It With Them
passages.text:
Any shipping crew I had that you don't see hanging around this camp are DEAD! Those were some fine goblins, but what's worse is they're all still out there! It's a TRAGEDY!

I mean, it's a tragedy they still have all their stuff! It's horrifying to think of all the perfectly good materials and coins sitting out there in the water.

Hey! You can do me a favor! If you're killing gilblins out there, go get the ditty bags off my old crewmen!

C'mon, they're not gonna need it anymore! Be real!

passages.title: Can't Take It With Them
passages.text: You get those ditty bags? I hope you left the goblins there!

passages.title: Can't Take It With Them
passages.text:
WOW!

I don't know why I said that. I'm excitable! But man, there was a lot of stuff on these guys, check it out!

Here, you want this?

passages.title: In With a Bang
passages.text:
Our trade frigate's still all the way out there on the water, swarming with Gilblins! AHH!

Sorry about that. But really! We need a way to get you out there and get back our stuff. There's quality goods left on that ship! QUALITY! LIKE MY MIDDLE NAME!

Lucky for you, I have an idea! Head right outside the camp and check along the north wall... my son Jerry'll get you over there with our cannon! If he's been practicing, that is!

passages.title: In With a Bang
passages.text: You got it? Did you get it? Did you try the cannon? You didn't explode!

passages.title: In With a Bang
passages.text:
My high-grade fuse! My imported blasting powder!

And my--hello there! I'll just be taking that!

Those are all worth more gold than what you're wearing, you know! Thanks for your help!

passages.title: Cities in Dust
passages.text:
Our armies clash across the battlefield. Crowley and his forces are losing ground and they do not yet know the fate of Lorna Crowley. We will meet with Crowley and his compatriots at mid field and I will present them with terms of their surrender. They will either accept or we will kill them all and leave their cities in dust.

As my most trusted soldier, you are to stand by my side during the exchange. Tell me when you are prepared to leave.

passages.title: Cities in Dust
passages.text:
<Lady Sylvanas Windrunner grimaces in pain.>

This... is not over. Godfrey and his traitorous allies will pay for what they have done as will the remaining Alliance forces occupying Lordaeron.

Our work has only just begun.

passages.title: Blast Him!
passages.text:
Let's go fishing, <name>! Now that the mortars are ready, we can take out the leader of this invasion.

Fathom-Lord Heth'Jatar rules over the Blackscale warrior caste. Go to the Heth'Jatari Banners just northeast of here and honk this conch shell. It's like a dog-whistle. For fish.

When Heth'Jartar shows up, I'll order the mortars to concentrate fire. You'll see the targets of the incoming shells.

Lure Heth'Jatar into our mortar fire and pummel him into submission!

passages.title: Blast Him!
passages.text:
You want me to keep firing?

I can keep firing.

passages.title: Blast Him!
passages.text:
Boom baby, boom!

What? You killed the Fathom-Lord already?

I suppose we should stop shelling his corpse, then.

passages.title: The Southern Flank
passages.text:
Our new arrangement with the Horde will put my people in direct conflict with the Alliance.

Bring. Them. On.

As we speak, the Alliance moves up the peninsula to threaten Dragonmaw Port.

Find Rok'tar to the south - I believe he has set up a command post on one of the shipwrecks - and ensure that the Twilight Shores remain in our control.

passages.title: The Southern Flank
passages.text: Good timing, <class>. We were just about to unleash a counter-attack.

passages.title: Scouting the Shore
passages.text:
If the Alliance gains control of this peninsula, they will threaten Dragonmaw Port. Not going to happen.

South of here you'll see a small hill with a commanding view of the shoreline. Whoever controls that hill will have the upper hand all along the shore!

Rush over there and scout the beach head control point. It's marked by that enormous flag. Then return to me.

You don't have to capture it, unless you're spoiling for a fight with the Alliance.

passages.title: Scouting the Shore
passages.text:
Good work, <class>. Now you know the lay of the land.

If you're ever having difficulty fighting here on the Twilight Shores, remember that capturing and holding the Beach Head will give all Horde forces here a combat advantage!

passages.title: Blood on the Sand
passages.text:
Our objective in the Twilight Highlands is to storm the Bastion of Twilight, but the Alliance have decided to make war.

So we will give them war!

Slay their marines until the lesson is learned.

passages.title: Blood on the Sand
passages.text: Good, good. Let them reap what they sow!

passages.title: Victory From Within
passages.text:
A few of our men didn't make it through portals which were supposed to open inside this very abbey. You've already proven your elusiveness and battlehardiness... now I need you to do so again.

The abbey has two wings: a library, and a hall of arms. In each wing, you should find a portal.

Use this keystone on these portals. Doing so should force them open, allowing our remaining shock troopers to take this abbey.

passages.title: Victory From Within
passages.text: The abbey will fall shortly.  We can soon move on, deeper into Tyr's Hand.

passages.title: The Assassin
passages.text:
The fate of the Scarlet Crusade is tragic, if somewhat ironic. At one point, they led the charge of humanity against the undead. Now, they resemble those corpses that they once hunted. What caused their descent into undeath isn't certain, but it doesn't make them any less dangerous.

One of their deadliest was an assassin who went by the name of Rohan. We have intel that places him atop the bell tower in this very abbey. Find him and kill him, <name>. And try not to die on the way.

passages.title: The Assassin
passages.text: Fight well, <name>.

passages.title: The Assassin
passages.text:
The death of Rohan eases my spirits a bit.

I once fought beside him, you know.  He was an emissary of the Scarlet Crusade; one of the few that deigned to join us in our battle against Kel'thuzad, so many years ago.  How quickly things change.

passages.title: Scarlet Salvage
passages.text:
This battle was won before it started. Right now, we're just shooting for style points.

Within these barracks, the sniveling Scarlet Crusaders cling to their priceless artifacts, even though some of the objects are too holy for their now-undead hand to touch. So they keep them in chests, hidden from the world.

You will find these artifacts, and bring them back to me. They belong to the Argent Crusade. They belong in the hands of the righteous.

passages.title: Scarlet Salvage
passages.text: I hope you gave them a fight.

passages.title: Scarlet Salvage
passages.text: Well done, <name>.  I will deliver these to Tyrosus when we return.

passages.title: Befouled No More
passages.text:
Can you sense it? The taint is already lifting from this building.

A holy building wants to be holy, and villains like Rohan and the rest of his Scarlet scum only hold it back.

With the abbey secure, we are a step closer to taking Tyr's Hand. Report the results of our strike to Angela. She should be leading the charge on the cathedral from somewhere in the center of town.

passages.title: Befouled No More
passages.text: Good, the abbey is ours.  I never doubted Eligor's ability for a moment.

passages.title: Argent Upheaval
passages.text:
I'll say we've done enough damage to these barracks to call this a win. A commander, a huntsman, and a warlock, all slain... not to mention the relics that we've liberated. Or shall I say... YOU liberated.

The cathedral still remains, but not for long. Talk with Archmage Angela Dosantos, in the central courtyard. The fate of Tyr's Hand's cathedral falls in her able hands.

passages.title: Argent Upheaval
passages.text: It sounds like Korfax really cleaned house over at the barracks.  It's very much like him to show off like that.

passages.title: Firebeard's Patrol
passages.text:
I was on my way to join Firebeard's Patrol when my bird was shot down.

Twilight's Hammer launched surprise attacks all over the Highlands. Sometimes their buildings crawled right out of the earth in the middle of our villages. It was a nightmare!

In the chaos, Firebeard is one of the few who's kept his head on straight. He's trying to piece together a full gryphon wing from the survivors.

If you want to bring the Wildhammer into the Alliance, start by helping out Firebeard, to the west.

passages.title: Firebeard's Patrol
passages.text:
Come to join the patrol, lad? Glad to have ya.

I need some bodies helpin' to get our defenses under control here. Help me out and I'll see if I can't find some more prestigious work for ya.

passages.title: Mo' Better Shredder
passages.text:
<name>, I've got plans for a better shredder. But my engineers can't wade into a combat zone alone.

Go locate a salvageable shredder in the Twilight Shores, and use it to signal one of my salvage experts to join you. Defend the shredder while we make some "upgrades."

The Alliance won't know what hit them! At least, not until my marketing campaign kicks in!

passages.title: Mo' Better Shredder
passages.text:
That's right baby! That's right! Cold steel and hot death!

What should we name our new creation? The Gnugatron? No - better - the <name>-o-matic. That's got a ring to it.

passages.title: Colossal Guardians
passages.text:
The chest containing the scepter appears to be magically sealed and will not budge.

The plaque above it depicts two giant statues holding star and moon-shaped stones sockets at their center.

The two statues are pictured guarding pyramids that look like the ones outside.

Perhaps it's worth your while to investigate these.

passages.title: Colossal Guardians
passages.text: You wipe away the sand from the hieroglyphs only for them to become covered in a new layer.  You'd best hurry.

passages.title: Colossal Guardians
passages.text: You place the two gems inside the sockets in the wall.

passages.title: After the Fall
passages.text:
Aww, that was nothin', really.

Those statues were teetering as it was - just needed a little push is all.

How about you go and sort through that rubble?

I've got a feeling we're close to getting this all sorted out.

passages.title: After the Fall
passages.text: Find anything interesting, <name>?

passages.title: After the Fall
passages.text:
Fine work, <name>.

It looks as though our work here is nearly complete.

passages.title: The Highvale Documents
passages.text:
The Highvale have kept detailed records here for years. Deaths, births, seasons... but also vital scouting information and methods of contact with the rest of the Alliance.

The documents will be scattered in the chaos. If they fall into the hands of the Forsaken, more lives could be at risk! Please, you must retrieve the documents before they are taken by the Horde...

passages.title: The Highvale Documents
passages.text: Are they safe?

passages.title: The Highvale Documents
passages.text: Thank the Light. We will not let the Forsaken have anything that can be turned against us, no matter how small.

passages.title: The God Hakkar
passages.text:
Now it is time to capture the essence of the avatar of Hakkar.

Take the Egg of Hakkar to the Sanctum of the Fallen God in the Sunken Temple in Azeroth. Invoke the egg's power to stir the dead god.

He will send his minions against you. Defeat his bloodrinkers and take their Hakkari blood, then use the blood to dowse the eternal flames that hold Hakkar's spirit. When all the flames go out, the avatar of Hakkar will enter our world.

Defeat him, and place his essence within the Egg of Hakkar.

passages.title: Just You and Mathias
passages.text:
The SI:7 are all dead. Time to find Master Mathias Shaw.

Good thing the squad commander told you where he would be.

passages.title: Just You and Mathias
passages.text: Where are the rest of my people?

passages.title: Just You and Mathias
passages.text:
That's a blow to our efforts. Damn Cho'gall!

It's a good thing that the squad commander told you where to find Master Shaw.

passages.title: Just You and Garona
passages.text:
The Kor'kron are all dead. Time to find Garona Halforcen.

Good thing the squad commander told you where she would be.

passages.title: Just You and Garona
passages.text: Where are the Kor'kron?

passages.title: Just You and Garona
passages.text:
That's a heavy blow to our efforts. Damn that Cho'gall!

It's a good thing that the squad commander told you where to find Garona.

passages.title: Once More Into The Fire
passages.text:
Fine, fine. You want a piece of the action? You can join in.

Let me know when you're ready ta go.

passages.title: Once More Into The Fire
passages.text: They keep comin an' I'll keep swinging!

passages.title: Once More Into The Fire
passages.text:
A thing of beauty, isn't it? An' they keep comin' back for more. Love it!

I'll go find Keely and settle her nerves in a bit. Just one more go through the row.

passages.title: Doing It Like a Dunwald
passages.text:
They already left to hunt down the ettin that lead the attack on Dunwald. I asked them to at least give ya a chance to catch up, but I'm not sure waitin's in their blood.

They made off towards the town square, in the center of the ruins. You should go join'm before ya miss out on all the fun.

passages.title: Doing It Like a Dunwald
passages.text:
Thanks for your help. You've got a warrior's spirit in ya - you coulda fooled me for a Wildhammer if it weren't for your... well.. you know.

I know Firebeard sent you to unite us. My love for that dwarf runs shallow, but you know now we've got plenty of reasons to make enemies of Twilight. If you see him, tell him that when the battle starts, the Dunwald family will be there.

passages.title: Bring the Hammer Down
passages.text:
No foray into the field would be complete without a good old-fashioned take-the-bad-guys-out kind of mission.

Between the citadel veterans, the corrupted elementalists, and the twilight vindicators, I'm sure you'll have plenty of targets.

How you choose to kill them is up to you.

passages.title: Bring the Hammer Down
passages.text: None of us are too good to get our hands a little dirty. Or bloody, in this case.

passages.title: Bring the Hammer Down
passages.text:
There's nothing worse than a self-hating Twilight's Hammer cultist. Nothing! These idiots actually want to bring about the end of the world.

That marks them for extinction in my book.

Between the citadel veterans, the corrupted elementalists, and the twilight vindicators, you should have no shortage of targets.

I could care less how you choose to kill them.

passages.title: Bring the Hammer Down
passages.text: Feels good to get a little blood on your hands, doesn't it? Especially when that blood belongs to such self-deluded fools.

passages.title: Help from the Earthcaller
passages.text:
My investigation into Cho'gall's artifact has hit a dead end. The Twilight's Hammer enslaved a group of Wildhammer smiths and then drowned them in the lake when they were done with their services.

<Mathias spits.>

We need help. There's an Earthen Ring woman, Earthcaller Yevaa, southwest at the Elementium mine.

She and her goblin initiate need help with the shutting down the elemental portals hereabouts. I'm thinking that in exchange, she can help us with our problem.

passages.title: Help from the Earthcaller
passages.text:
<name>! I'm glad you're here.

Of course, I'm more than happy to lend you whatever assistance that I can.

passages.title: Help from the Earthcaller
passages.text:
My investigation into Cho'gall's artifact has hit a dead end. The Twilight's Hammer enslaved a group of Wildhammer smiths and then drowned them in the lake when they were done with their services.

<Garona spits.>

I hate to say it, but we need help. There's an Earthen Ring woman, a draenei named Earthcaller Yevaa. She and her pet goblin are southwest at the Elementium mine.

They need help with shutting down the elemental portals around here. In exchange, she can help us with our problem.

passages.title: Help from the Earthcaller
passages.text:
<name>! I'm glad you're here.

Of course, I'm more than willing to help you in any way that I can.

passages.title: Portal Overload
passages.text:
I used to be the caretaker of the Earthen Ring's portals here. But while we were away helping to save Deepholm, the Twilight's Hammer moved in and corrupted the area.

They're using powerful ascendants to guard our portals. That's where they've made a critical error.

I want you to go to the portals and use the controllers to overload them. This will unleash all of the portal's energy, debilitating the ascendant. Slay it.

passages.title: Portal Overload
passages.text: The last portal is deep within the mine here, but we'll deal with that in a bit.

passages.title: Spirit of the Loch
passages.text:
I have no knowledge of any artifact that Cho'gall is crafting, but I think I know one that can help.

Countess Verrall is the ancient spirit of Loch Verrall to the north. She has no love for the Twilight's Hammer, who have polluted her waters.

Seek her for the wisdom that you seek.

passages.title: Spirit of the Loch
passages.text:
I know why you are here, <name>. Your reasons sing within your fluids.

I know about the dead dwarf forgesmith polluting my lake. If you want to find out what his corpse remembers, you must earn it.

passages.title: Unbinding
passages.text:
Look, if there's one thing I know, it's elementals. I've been able to really gain an appreciation for how they feel. Let me tell you, they don't appreciate being enslaved one bit!

So, what I'm saying here is that if you were to free the enslaved elementals, I'm sure that not only would they show their gratitude, they'd also likely turn on their masters.

Sounds like a win-win to me, <name>.

passages.title: Unbinding
passages.text: What'd I tell you? Elementals aren't so bad after all, eh?

passages.title: Pay Attention!
passages.text:
Listen, <race>. It's not that I don't appreciate the rescue and all, but this is a dire situation.

You have to pay better attention out there!

I was watching, and you passed right over a busted alliance crate.

There's bound to be something in there that could help me and my boys.

How about you get out there and take a look-see, hrm?

passages.title: Pay Attention!
passages.text:
Sure enough...

This looks to be something that Nazgrim will take quite an interest in.

passages.title: Do the Honors
passages.text:
It looks like all that's left to do is to place the orbs on the pedestals at each corner of this mechanism.

We appear to have stumbled upon what may be the most important find in modern history.

<Harrison looks at you for a moment, then hands you the orbs.>

Well, go ahead, <name>.

We'd have never made this discovery without you.

passages.title: Do the Honors
passages.text:
Well, now. Would ya look at that!

As amazing as this is, I am confident that there's more to our discovery than meets the eye...

Much more.

passages.title: To the Surface
passages.text:
Nevin has just sent word that he and his men are making their way to the surface. He'll be waiting for you in the building that S.A.F.E. has established as its headquarters.

See Torben Zapblast over there? Talk to him when you're ready to head to the surface and he'll arrange to have you transported up there. It's been a pleasure meeting you, <name>, and I'm honored to have played a small role in helping you escape from Gnomeregan to start your life on the surface.

passages.title: To the Surface
passages.text: It's good to see you again, <name>.

passages.title: To the Surface
passages.text: It's good to see you again, <name>. Without your help, we wouldn't have been able to get so many survivors out of Gnomeregan this time. Everyone is going to be thrilled to meet you and hear your story.

passages.title: The Platinum Discs
passages.text:
The centerpieces of this treasure chamber are four huge platinum discs, each adorned with numerous sigils of an unknown origin. Touching them makes your hand tingle. Just after touching the discs, the visage of a large stone watcher springs forth.

"Salutations. I am a keeper of knowledge. The Creators' synthesis of the Earthen has been chronicled and stored here for this world in the Discs of Norgannon."

You have uncovered a wealth of previously undiscovered worldly lore!

passages.title: Narkrall, the Drake-Tamer
passages.text:
<name>, the stronghold at Bloodgulch is the heart of the Dragonmaw empire in the Highlands. It is just up the river. Narkrall Rakeclaw is using his considerable power to amass a wing of drake-riders there.

For the Dragonmaw to succeed, Bloodgulch must succeed. Go to Narkrall and make sure it is so.

passages.title: Narkrall, the Drake-Tamer
passages.text:
<Narkrall sizes you up.>

Another mewling Horde whelp? Zaela saps our strength by diluting our forces with the weak. Very well, <class>. Prove yourself to me, and show me what your Horde is made of.

passages.title: Princess Theradras
passages.text:
Do not be alarmed, young <race>. I am Zaetar, son of Cenarius, and I come to you for your assistance.

Long ago, I made the mistake of mating with Princess Theradras, a powerful earth elemental aligned with the Old Gods. Our children, the centuar Kahns, turned on me upon birth and slew me mercilessly. Now, Theradras' taint runs deep and threatens far more than just Maraudon.

Come slay her and free my spirit so that we may restore Desolace to a place of verdant life and promise, as Cenarius would want.

passages.title: Princess Theradras
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. As you can see, my mere presence here has resulted in a bloom of glorious life despite my mate's presence. Names aside, perhaps one day you will again venture into Desolace and find it a verdant oasis free of any traces of the Old Gods.

passages.title: Pool of Tears
passages.text:
The trolls that lurk within this temple have done grievous harm to my kind, <name>. We were sent here to guard this place, and were instead used to unleash the terrible powers within.

I must beg you for the help only a mortal can give. You can be my hand within the temple; should I enter by myself, I risk being turned against my brothers as well.

We shall make a pact. If you wish to help, first gather Atal'ai artifacts from the waters around the temple, and return them to me.

passages.title: Pool of Tears
passages.text: Your gathering of these artifacts will be a sign of faith. Once rendered, I will perform the ritual.

passages.title: Pool of Tears
passages.text:
The essence of the green dragonflight wafts from these artifacts; the vestiges of my corrupted kin. In purifying them, I form a bond between us.

Step forward, <name>, and receive the Oathstone of Ysera's Dragonflight.

passages.title: Dragon, Unchained
passages.text:
Lirastrasza is the last and greatest of the red dragons that the Twilight's Hammer captured. They're about to kill her.

I need you to take the Elementium Axe and free her from her bonds.

passages.title: Dragon, Unchained
passages.text: Use the axe to break Lirastrasza's chains.

passages.title: Dragon, Unchained
passages.text:
Isn't she a beauty?

Let's see what she does now that she's free.

passages.title: Dragon, Unchained
passages.text:
Lirastrasza is the last and greatest of the red dragons that the Twilight's Hammer captured. They're about to kill her, <class>.

You need to take the Elementium Axe and free her from her bonds before they do.

passages.title: Dragon, Unchained
passages.text:
Isn't she beautiful? So graceful.

I hope she gets her fill of revenge and then some.

passages.title: The Warden's Time
passages.text:
<Erunak's image penetrates your mind.>

You have done well, <name>, but more remains to be done.

Before moving on from this place, let us be sure that we leave it in disarray.

Find the one who leads these naga and repay him for his misdeeds.

passages.title: The Warden's Time
passages.text:
It is good that this operation has been undone.

Soon, I must move on...

passages.title: Back to the Elementium Depths
passages.text:
The Earthcaller's initiate, Goldmine, has need of you.

I think that they're ready for you to help them with whatever's down in that mine.

passages.title: Back to the Elementium Depths
passages.text: <name>, glad you're back! Have I got something fun for us to do!

passages.title: Back to the Elementium Depths
passages.text:
The Earthcaller has a goblin initiate? Goldmine is his name? He has need of you.

I think that they're ready for you to do their dirty work with whatever's down in that mine.

passages.title: Back to the Elementium Depths
passages.text: <name>, glad you're back! Have I got something fun for us to do!

passages.title: The Day that Deathwing Came: What Really Happened
passages.text:
These two have no idea how to tell a story. Theldurin's story was too short, and Lucien's tale was a little too tall, if you catch my drift.

Also, neither of their stories had action and fans admiring my awesomeness in them.

Sit back, <name>. I'll tell you what really happened that day.

passages.title: The Day that Deathwing Came: What Really Happened
passages.text: I seem to have lost my place... let's see... where was I...

passages.title: The Day that Deathwing Came: What Really Happened
passages.text:
I can't believe those guys would interrupt me like that.  My story was going so well, too...

Anyhow, thanks for sticking around so long.  It's nice to have someone new to share tall tales with.  I'm sure Lucien and Theldurin feel the same way.

You have any you'd like to share with us?

passages.title: Piece of the Past
passages.text:
<An ancient, slightly cracked slab of stone with an immense number of inscriptions etched on all sides of it. You're unable to decipher the language, but the sheer amount of text and the semi-ornate nature of the stone suggest that this might carry significant value.>

<Levia Dreamwaker, back with the Nespirah survivors, was looking for something exactly like this.>

passages.title: Piece of the Past
passages.text:
Hah! Did you see the admiral giving me dirty looks and decide to throw some sympathy my way? I've pretty much lost hope of making him understand that these ruins offer us some opportunity to salvage some usefulness out of this whole mess.

I'd actually hoped that you might turn up again - you seem like the only one I can rely on. Wait... what's that you have there?

passages.title: Piece of the Past
passages.text:
Brilliant! It will take me a while to translate, but this is precisely the kind of find I was hoping for.

There's no knowing if we will make it out of this place, but if it comes down to it, I will find a way to float this to the surface in hopes that it will one day be found.

Thank you again, <name>. Here... perhaps I have something that may be of use to you.

passages.title: Piece of the Past
passages.text:
<An ancient, slightly cracked slab of stone with an immense number of inscriptions etched on all sides of it. You're unable to decipher the language, but the sheer amount of text and the semi-ornate nature of the stone suggest that this might carry significant value.>

<Elendri Goldenbrow, back with the Nespirah survivors, was looking for something exactly like this.>

passages.title: Piece of the Past
passages.text:
Hah! Did you see the captain giving me dirty looks and decide to throw some sympathy my way? I've pretty much lost hope of making him understand that these ruins offer us some opportunity to salvage some usefulness out of this whole mess.

I'd actually hoped that you might turn up again - you seem like the only one I can rely on. Wait... what's that you have there?

passages.title: Piece of the Past
passages.text:
Brilliant! I can't have expected much more with the tools I gave you.

I should be able to fill in the blanks and get this all written out shortly. There's no knowing if we will make it out of this place, but if it comes down to it, I will find a way to float this to the surface in hopes that it will one day be found.

Thank you again, <name>. You're not bad.

passages.title: Water of Life
passages.text:
Take my Water of Life and pass it into the corpse of the drowned dwarf.

He was a worker of metals in life, and though his body now feeds my loch, the Water will allow him to tell you what you want to know.

Then, take your information and be gone from my demesne.

passages.title: Water of Life
passages.text:
The Hammer of Twilight? And you say you got this information out of a drowned Wildhammer dwarf?

You're kidding, right?

passages.title: Mr. Goldmine's Wild Ride
passages.text:
Okay, <name>, we need to get to the earth portal at the back of the cave.

I've "procured" a ride for us. Why walk when we can ride in style? I hope you don't mind mine carts.

Let me know when you're ready.

passages.title: Mr. Goldmine's Wild Ride
passages.text:
Oh no! My weapons and totems!

They're destroyed!!!

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Mount Hyjal!
passages.text:
All able-bodied members of the Horde are hereby ordered to report to Emissary Windsong at Nighthaven in Moonglade.

Our brothers in the Cenarion Circle report that Deathwing's minions have launched a destructive offensive against the world tree and threaten to burn it to the ground!

Speak with Cenarion Emissary Blackhoof to gain entry into Moonglade. Blackhoof is located at the tauren district in the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar.

Onward, <brother/sister>! Destiny calls!

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Mount Hyjal!
passages.text: We knew the Horde would send help and not a moment too soon!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Mount Hyjal!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Emissary Windsong at Nighthaven in Moonglade.

Our brothers in the Cenarion Circle report that Deathwing's minions have launched a destructive offensive against the world tree and threaten to burn it to the ground!

Speak with Cenarion Emissary Jademoon in Stormwind Keep to gain entry into Moonglade.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance! Fight on, <brother/sister>!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Mount Hyjal!
passages.text: Help us!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Mount Hyjal!
passages.text: We knew the Alliance would send help and not a moment too soon!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Deepholm!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Naraat the Earthspeaker at the Eastern Earthshrine in Stormwind City.

The Earthen Ring requires our aid! They report that the elemental plane of Deepholm threatens to overtake our world and destroy all life on Azeroth!

The Eastern Earthshrine can be found directly northwest of Stormwind Keep.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance! Fight on, <brother/sister>!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Deepholm!
passages.text: Our world is in danger, <name>! We need the help of great heroes, like you, to save it!

passages.title: The Gnoll King
passages.text:
<name>, I'm afraid I must ask of you the impossible.

I received my eyepatch because he willed it so. Countless thousands have perished to his wrath. It was only by sheer miracle that we were able to imprison him here.

Doing so was a grave mistake. We held out as long as we could, but then they came. From the shadows and darkness, gnolls in service of Hogger ripped my best men to pieces.

You must defeat the Gnoll King, lest he mounts another attack and slaughters us all in cold, bloodthirsty rage.

passages.title: The Gnoll King
passages.text: Have you defeated Hogger?

passages.title: The Gnoll King
passages.text:
You have performed a deed this day unlike any I have seen in my long career. Hogger's death will plague the Riverpaw for years to come, and hopefully put an end to their attacks on our people.

Greatest of heroes, please take this as a sign of my eternal gratitude.

passages.title: Show Me Your Papers
passages.text:
After your work in dealing with the Twilight's Hammer cult, Captain Anton recommended you for a delicate assignment.

My men recently discovered a group of cultists attempting to sneak into the city. The flow of traffic into the Stormwind has come to a halt. The king has decreed that all visitors must be searched before they can enter the gates. Take this copy of his proclamation and read it to the people assembled at the front gates, then assist the guards there in searching those who wish to enter.

passages.title: Show Me Your Papers
passages.text: So there were more cultists waiting to be admitted to the city? It's a good thing that you caught them, <name>. Reading over the note that you found, it seems they're planning something big.

passages.title: While We're Here
passages.text:
You know, while we're here, we might as well take care of the Twilight's Hammer intruders. This place used to be ours, after all!

I'd help, but with my totems and weapons broken, I'm pretty helpless.

passages.title: While We're Here
passages.text: They had it coming to them.

passages.title: Rune Ruination
passages.text:
Examining the Twilight Rune of Earth, you can almost feel its power extending further into the Elementium Depths.

It's probably connected to other runes. Initiate Goldmine thinks that you should destroy all of them.

passages.title: Rune Ruination
passages.text: We still have some runes to destroy, <name>.

passages.title: Rune Ruination
passages.text:
That'll teach 'em to move in on our territory!

What's that over across the way?

passages.title: A Fiery Reunion
passages.text:
That's Magmatooth, my estranged fire elemental. <name>, you gotta kill him or he's gonna kill me!

It was all just a big misunderstanding. How was I to know he'd be mad about me "borrowing" his heart down in Deepholm? He can't die... not permanently anyway!

He's got the controller to the portal on him for sure. You gotta get the controller and then use it in the Fire portal to take us back to the entrance.

passages.title: A Fiery Reunion
passages.text: <name>!

passages.title: A Fiery Reunion
passages.text:
We survived and all of the portals are now shutdown!

You don't think Magmatooth is going to hold a grudge, do you?

passages.title: Empire of Dirt
passages.text:
This war has taken its toll on us as a people. We have lost much to secure our place as the rightful rulers of Lordaeron. And though the moment is won, the battle continues to rage in other parts of the Eastern Kingdoms.

I must return to the Undercity to recuperate. I want you to go to Hillsbrad Foothills in my stead, <name>. As my most trusted soldier, you will lead our forces to absolute domination against our enemies in Hillsbrad.

Report to High Executor Darthalia at Southpoint Blockade, to the east.

passages.title: Empire of Dirt
passages.text: News of your conquest in Silverpine emboldens us, <name>. We are prepared to fight at your command and beat back the last remaining vestiges of humanity in Hillsbrad.

passages.title: Total War
passages.text:
Many of the Wildhammer have already fled their homes. It is time to wipe them from the map.

Up on the ridge to the north you will find abandoned houses in the Thundermar Ruins. Kegs of potent Thundermar ale have been left behind.

Thundermar ale is 220 proof; I don't know how that's possible.

Smash open the kegs and set their content aflame. Burn them out! Leave the dwarves nothing to return to!

passages.title: Total War
passages.text:
Yes, yes. Burn them out, as you would flush groundhogs from their holes...

Well done, <name>.

passages.title: Fortune and Glory
passages.text:
We have to keep moving, <name>. It's just a matter of time before those troops get their act together.

The coffer should be just beyond these ruins.

Stay on your toes. Something tells me this isn't over yet...

passages.title: Fortune and Glory
passages.text: Good to see you're still in one piece, <name>.

passages.title: Arrest the Infiltrators
passages.text:
You were right to bring this note to me, <name>. The king's proclamation came too late; they already have infiltrators at work in the city.

This note contains instructions and locations for cultists to meet, but it doesn't say what they're doing. Our enemies have grown smarter. It's going to be tough to track down all the infiltrators, but we have to get as many as we can. Use these cuffs to restrain any agents you find, bring them to the entrance of the Stockade, and report to me when you're finished.

passages.title: Arrest the Infiltrators
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>. The note you captured makes sense in light of this ritual the infiltrators mentioned. This city is infested with cultists and their sympathizers. We must act before their plans can come to fruition.

passages.title: War Forage
passages.text:
<Griff's stomach growls.>

Whenever we Dragonmaw go on the warpath, everyone stops hunting.

The best tasting food is stolen from the mouths of the enemy. Up on the ridge north of the river there's a bunch of wrecked Wildhammer houses. I bet they're loaded with food.

Bring some to my mouth.

passages.title: War Forage
passages.text: Hungry.

passages.title: War Forage
passages.text:
<Griff greedily snatches the heap of food, enough to feed dozens of men.>

Great! Did you get any for yourself?

passages.title: Crushing the Wildhammer
passages.text:
Since my people first claimed the Highlands, the Wildhammer dwarves have been our persistent foe. We fought them in Grim Batol, we fought them in the Wetlands, and even now open warfare rages to our north, across the river, amidst the Thundermar Ruins.

Prove your valor to me. Seek out and crush Wildhammer Warbrands. The best among them carry insignias - my warriors collect them by the dozen.

Can you?

passages.title: Crushing the Wildhammer
passages.text: Show me the insignias you've collected, <class>.

passages.title: Crushing the Wildhammer
passages.text:
<Narkrall clenches the insignias in his weathered hand.>

So, <class>. There's more to you than meets the eye.

Maybe your Horde can stand with the best of my warriors. Let's try you out...

passages.title: Fight Like a Wildhammer
passages.text:
S'not a boast to say that we Thundermars brew the finest ale in the Eastern Kingdoms. It's 220 proof. Yeah, you heard me!

As folks fled from the south to the town center, they were forced to leave behind their ale.

<Blundy pauses, allowing the gravity of the situation to soak in.>

GET IT BACK! That stuff'll turn even the stringiest of warriors into a whirlin' dervish of mouth-foaming destruction. Get them kegs! S'our only hope!

passages.title: Fight Like a Wildhammer
passages.text:
Get me that ale, <name>.

Hey, you haven't been skimmin' off the top, have you?

passages.title: Fight Like a Wildhammer
passages.text: Oh aye ... we get a few of these kegs out to the boys on the front and we're gonna see some fireworks. Thank you, <name>!

passages.title: Never Leave a Dinner Behind
passages.text:
Supplies are short, <name>. We've got refugees coming into Thundermar from up and down the ridge - that's a lot of mouths to feed.

Plenty of food stores were left behind as people pulled their families to safety. We need that food!

Scour the Thundermar ruins south, east, and southwest of here for food stores.

Careful, <class>! The fighting around the ruins is pretty intense.

passages.title: Never Leave a Dinner Behind
passages.text: Got some eats?

passages.title: Never Leave a Dinner Behind
passages.text:
It's good - hardly a worm or weevil to be found!

This is a lifesaver to the folk who fled here for survival.

passages.title: Dragonmaw Takedown
passages.text:
The Dragonmaw!

<Colin spits.>

Monsters, all of them. We've fought them up and down these highlands since the last war. And now they're joining forces with the Horde?

If you're going to convince us Wildhammers to unite under the Alliance banner, you'd best prove yourself against the Dragonmaw. Wade into the battle that's raging in the Thundermar ruins to the south and southwest. Kill Dragonmaw marauders and collect the insignias that their greatest warriors wear. Then we'll talk.

passages.title: Dragonmaw Takedown
passages.text: How goes the fight, <class>?

passages.title: Dragonmaw Takedown
passages.text:
Look at that! That's quite a collection of trophies you have there.

I'll spread the word. If a single Alliance <class> can do this, imagine what the rest of your lot can accomplish!

passages.title: The Darkest Depths
passages.text:
I've been seeing sea creatures acting oddly through the whole swamp. The murlocs, yes, but before that the gilblins, and the makrura... I even saw some naga wander ashore the other day.

Something's calling them here, and working them into a frenzy to boot. Many of the creatures have been drawn to Stagalbog Cavern to the west. Something's down there, and if it gets any stronger we'll all start wandering in there too...

You should put a stop to whatever it is before that happens.

passages.title: The Darkest Depths
passages.text: Oh my. It sounds like you ran across quite a sinister being. I wonder what one of those was doing all the way out here...

passages.title: A Disarming Distraction
passages.text:
The curse has taken over the expedition members' higher brain functions, but my calculations reveal their suppressed adolescent subconscious can still be stimulated by realistic imagery.

Utilize this holo-projector to distract them.

They are currently setting up explosives at the tomb to the east to attempt to gain access to secret passages in Uldum.

They seek dangerous re-origination technology beneath Uldum and must be stopped.

passages.title: A Disarming Distraction
passages.text: Greetings, user <name>.  I am happy to see you are still unaffected by the effects of the expedition curse.

passages.title: A Disarming Distraction
passages.text:
Well done, <name>.  The expedition has already doomed itself.

There is no need for it to endanger the rest of the world as well.

passages.title: To Fuselight Proper
passages.text:
This, <race>, is paradise. I've always wanted to live in a nice quiet town by the sea so I can focus on my explosions without any distractions.

Quiet's not for everybody, though... 'specially the adventuring hero-type, like yourself.

We've installed a teleporter in the backside of town that'll take you up to the top of the cliffs. From there, you can take the quick ride west into Fuselight proper, within the Badlands.

There should be more for you to do up there. Tell 'em that Flo sent you.

passages.title: To Fuselight Proper
passages.text: Welcome to Fuselight!

passages.title: A Strange Request
passages.text:
On to other matters. I have a package that I need delivered.

A young lady came by our town not long ago, looking for compressed blasting powder, a tempered mithril bomb casing, and some safety goggles. Naturally, we had plenty of blasting powder and bomb casings to sell her, but the safety goggles were a little harder to find.

Long story short, I've got the goggles, but she's already returned to her studies down in Lethlor Ravine. Will you bring these down to her?

passages.title: A Strange Request
passages.text: Ahh... you've found me.  Good.

passages.title: A Strange Request
passages.text: Thank you, <race>.  You may keep the goggles, as they have already served their purpose: they brought you to me.

passages.title: Back Under Cover
passages.text:
The cultists seem assured of their victory, even as we detain more and more of them. We must find out more about the ritual mentioned by the cultist you questioned.

These rituals seem to be the core of the cult's plan to attack Stormwind. I'm going to give you one of the robes taken from the arrested cultists. Put it on and go back to the cultist outpost at Mirror Lake Orchard in Elwynn Forest and see if you can get the cultists there to let you in on the plan.

passages.title: Back Under Cover
passages.text: It's good to see you again, <name>. We were worried that the tyrant Wrynn's guards had thrown you into the Stockade.

passages.title: Back Under Cover
passages.text: You need to familiarize yourself with the portal ritual quickly. We need to send as many teams into Stormwind as we can. They're discovering and arresting more of our brothers each day.

passages.title: Third Sample: Implanted Eggs
passages.text:
Nyxondra is being held against her will. She is hidden from her brood, right in the middle of their breeding grounds. She lays eggs, but they will be taken away before she can see them hatch.

Cruel? Perhaps... but not nearly as cruel as the treatment that their dragonflight showed my mistress.

Show me that I can trust you, <name>. Take Nyxondra's eggs, and bring them here. You will need to beat Nyxondra into submission before you can take them.

passages.title: Third Sample: Implanted Eggs
passages.text: Remember, <name>... this is for the good of the black dragonflight.  We are here to redeem them, not to hurt them.  This is but a step in their recovery.

passages.title: Third Sample: Implanted Eggs
passages.text:
You have done everything that I have asked you, without question.  Our job here in Lethlor Ravine is done.

It is now time that I revealed everything to you.

passages.title: When the Going Gets Tough, Cheat
passages.text:
I just can't get my invention to work! Gah!

That's it, I've decided. I'm going to cheat and use magic.

What my invention really needs is a solid piston that's thin enough to fit through a narrow copper tube, but strong enough to withstand repeated impact without breaking. The magical rods carried by those ogre magi to the north should work perfectly.

From what I can tell, only the instructors carry the strong staves.

passages.title: When the Going Gets Tough, Cheat
passages.text: I don't like to stoop to using magic on my inventions, but this is somewhat of an emergency.

passages.title: When the Going Gets Tough, Cheat
passages.text: A perfect fit!  My goat puncher is finally finished!

passages.title: Gnomebliteration
passages.text:
I have downloaded my program to the fusion core and have complete control over it.

I've created a small pocket of air inside to avoid vaporizing user <name>.

I will yield control of all movement functions so I can dedicate my cycles to keeping the core stable.

Go down the hill and neutralize as many of the expedition members as possible.

My analysis reveals you might feel... "guilt" as a result of such high fatality numbers.

User <name>, you must be assured that expedition members are without hope.

passages.title: Gnomebliteration
passages.text: It is done, user <name>.  I thank you for your assistance with this unfortunate task.

passages.title: I Said the Words...
passages.text:
Now that you're familiar with the ritual, it's time for you to perform it in the city. Dozens of our brethren have already infiltrated the city and made their way to the ritual sites.

I want you to visit the portal ritual sites in Stormwind's Dwarven District, Park district, and Cathedral Square. The teams there will have made most of the preparations and all you need to is read the last part of the incantation from the book.

Very soon, <name>, Stormwind will find itself awash in wind and water.

passages.title: I Said the Words...
passages.text: You've done an excellent job tracking down and combating the cultists, but I fear they are right about one thing. We will never know if we've gotten them all.

passages.title: Skullcrusher the Mountain
passages.text:
It was a trap! Cho'gall lured you in with the Hammer of Twilight so that his gronn could finish you off.

Survive and slay Skullcrusher the Mountain!

passages.title: Skullcrusher the Mountain
passages.text:
You did it, lad! You beat that damned gronn and sent Cho'gall packing into the Twilight Bastion.

Don't you worry. With your help and that of your friends, we'll get in there and we'll kill Cho'gall once and for all!

passages.title: Skullcrusher the Mountain
passages.text:
It was a trap! Cho'gall lured you in with the Hammer of Twilight so that his gronn could finish you off.

Survive and slay Skullcrusher the Mountain!

passages.title: Skullcrusher the Mountain
passages.text:
You did it, <name>! You beat that damned gronn and sent Cho'gall packing into the Twilight Bastion.

Don't you worry. With your help and that of your friends, we'll get in there and we'll kill Cho'gall once and for all!

passages.title: Troggish Troubles
passages.text:
I'll need some time to analyze these samples, as well as a break from this trogg-shooting duty. Go man one of my turrets and take out as many troggs as you can. I'll be here studying.

The turrets have two abilities: a regular shot, as well as an electrical overload, for when too many enemies get close! Heh, heh. Good luck.

Oh, and look out for the big, slow troggs. You probably don't want to let them anywhere near you.

passages.title: Troggish Troubles
passages.text: Not quite done yet.  Need some more time.

passages.title: Troggish Troubles
passages.text: The results are in.  I've identified traces of corruption in all three samples you brought me.  Rhea will be quite disappointed.

passages.title: All's Fair in Love, War, and Archaeology
passages.text:
First things first, though. I'm not just going to sit here and tell you everything we've discovered down in those ruins. We've got problems to take care of!

Most pressing is those upstart Reliquary hooligans, just on the other side of the tomb. They're makin' off with all of our loot! Don't they know that diggin's dwarf work?

Hunt down a few of their "excavators" - more like bandits, if you ask me - and bring some of these precious artifacts back to me.

THEN we'll talk titans.

passages.title: All's Fair in Love, War, and Archaeology
passages.text: Your bags look heavy.  Heavy with liberated artifacts, I presume?

passages.title: All's Fair in Love, War, and Archaeology
passages.text:
Chalice... worthless.

Vase... counterfeit.

Hieroglyph... interesting, but rather common.
