I've been making progress in my research, <name>. Based on what we've witnessed in the local flora, it's quite possible that your Lasher also accepts superheated liquids as a principal source of nutrition.

I'd like you to help me with a little experiment. The Emberspit Scorpions that inhabit the Magma Springs to the north spew out burning pools of fire during combat.

Take the Lasher and observe his reaction to the scorpions' Ember Pools.

passages.title: Some Like It Hot
passages.text: Did it work? So my theory was correct?

passages.title: Heart of Flame
passages.text:
You are the first mortal to witness a dragon council, <name>, and among the only beings in Azeroth to take part in the choosing of an Aspect.

My ascension has endowed me with incredible power. I have taken the liberty to strengthen Tarecgosa's bond with you, though she will require a more... permanent home.

I would have you venture one last time into the Plane of Fire and bring me the heart of Ragnaros.

When next we meet, I will be able to suitably thank you for all that you have done.

passages.title: Heart of Flame
passages.text: A fine day for a ceremony. Don't you think, <name>?

passages.title: Heart of Flame
passages.text:
You have done well, <name>.

Now prepare to receive a hero's reward.

passages.title: Heart of Flame
passages.text:
You are the first mortal to witness a dragon council, <name>, and among the only beings in Azeroth to take part in the choosing of an Aspect.

My ascension has endowed me with incredible power. I have taken the liberty to strengthen Tarecgosa's bond with you, though she will require a more... permanent home.

I would have you venture one last time into the Plane of Fire and bring me the heart of Ragnaros.

When next we meet, I will be able to suitably thank you for all that you have done.

passages.title: Heart of Flame
passages.text: A fine day for a ceremony. Don't you think, <name>?

passages.title: Heart of Flame
passages.text:
You have done well, <name>.

Now prepare to receive a hero's reward.

passages.title: The Tipping Point
passages.text:
On the day when Leyara attacked Hamuul, she was waiting near some ruins in Hyjal, northwest of the Regrowth. She acted strangely at the time: calm, silent, and staring off into the distance. Perhaps that location is of some importance to her.

The locket might react if brought to that location.

passages.title: Back to Basics
passages.text:
There are certain things that everyone needs, from the basic household cook to the master chef. One of the city's most important staples is rice flour. Most families keep at least one basket of rice in their houses and the residents of the Craftsmen's Terrace and Tradesmen's Terrace are no different.

I often ask my students to help with the task of pounding rice into flour since it's good practice and an endless task. Why don't you give it a try?

passages.title: Back to Basics
passages.text: It takes a lot of effort to ensure that there's enough flour for everyone's needs. Thank you for your help, <name>.

passages.title: Fish Head
passages.text:
There was an... incident... with an orc guard and one of Master Apothecary Faranell's abominations.

Apparently, the Kor'kron Overseer chopped its head clean off and kicked it into the slime.

Faranell's apprentices searched for hours but they can't find the thing. Care to try fishing it up? I'm sure the old fellow'd be grateful.

passages.title: Fish Head
passages.text: You haven't by any chance come across a severed abomination head, have you...?

passages.title: Fish Head
passages.text:
Ah! THERE it is! How ever did you find it?

Well, no matter. My apprentices weren't able to recover the head despite hours splashing about in the slime, though they DID recover this bag of shiny things... perhaps you've a use for what's inside?

My thanks.

passages.title: Ribs for the Sentinels
passages.text: One of my responsibilities is to feed the sentinels of Darnassus while they're on duty. It's a time-consuming task, but one I'm happy to undertake. It's also a great way to practice your skills. Would you mind helping me with today's meal? Simply take these ribs, cook them near a stove or fire, and distribute them to sentinels throughout the city.

passages.title: Ribs for the Sentinels
passages.text: Feeding all those sentinels is much easier with your help. Nobody had to wait in line for their meal this time.

passages.title: Tadpole Terror
passages.text:
Some of our apothecaries took to dumping their more volatile waste chemicals into Stillwater Pond and... well, let's just say that no one wants to know how big mutant flesh-eating toads can grow.

Would you consider fishing up some giant flesh-eating tadpoles before it gets to that? Just don't try to handle them with your bare hands.

passages.title: Tadpole Terror
passages.text: Catch any mutant tadpoles? Don't try to handle them with your bare hands.

passages.title: Tadpole Terror
passages.text:
Excellent work, <name>. I'll see that these are, ah, disposed of immediately.

After all, what would our fine apothecaries want with an army of monstrous, poison-spitting, flesh-eating super-toads?

passages.title: Like Pike?
passages.text:
You've fished in Brightwater Lake, yes?

The prize catch there is one of the lake's massive corpse-fed pikes. However, they only bite on a very specific type of bait... corpse worms.

Search the graves in the courtyard up top and you should find some.

passages.title: Like Pike?
passages.text: Catch that pike, yet?

passages.title: Like Pike?
passages.text: That's a fine, fat pike, <name>.  Well done.

passages.title: Time for Slime
passages.text:
It takes a special sort of fisherman to reap the bounty of Undercity's burbling slime troughs. Think you can handle gathering some of the squirming, sentient slime mold slithering about down there?

You can try to fish them up, but they're wily; you might be better off just diving into the ooze and grabbing them.

Remember, they're only useful alive and intact... who'd want to eat a dead slime mold?! Disgusting.

passages.title: Time for Slime
passages.text: Difficult to catch, aren't they?

passages.title: Time for Slime
passages.text: These slimes look perfect.  I will send these along to Eunice for preparation, thank you.

passages.title: The Sister's Pendant
passages.text:
Have you met Sister Aquinne? She and I trained together in Dolanaar, and she recently came to the city to study at the Temple of the Moon. We decided to go for a boat ride, but the clumsy oarsman managed to capsize the craft!

When we got back to the shore, Aquinne's moon pendant was missing. The lakes in Darnassus are full of giant catfish who will gobble up anything shiny!

I've been catching them nonstop, hoping to find the one with her pendant. I don't suppose you want to help?

passages.title: The Sister's Pendant
passages.text: Have you had any luck finding Aquinne's missing pendant? I must've caught fifty of those monsters and I have nothing to show for it!

passages.title: The Sister's Pendant
passages.text:
<Astaia takes the pendant from you.>

Underneath all the slime and tarnish, I think this is it! Aquinne will be so happy to have this back... after a thorough cleaning, of course. I can't thank you enough, <name>.

passages.title: The Nordrassil Summit
passages.text:
Hello, <class>! My brothers and sisters of the Earthen Ring have spoken well of your deeds in the wake of the Cataclysm. But much remains to be done if we are to heal this broken world.

Walk with me, friend. Preparations for a ceremony are underway, a ritual that I hope will be a turning point in our battle against the Twilight's Hammer.

When all is done, you will be able to spread the word about our triumph here.

passages.title: The Nordrassil Summit
passages.text: It can't be over. We mustn't give up hope!

passages.title: Elemental Bonds: Doubt
passages.text:
I do know the one you seek... but I do not know if it is wise for you to follow him. He has cast himself into the cyclone. The winds now tear at his body and mind, leaving nothing but shreds of flesh and doubt.

Chasing after him would only expose you to the same fate. The wind's edge leaves nothing uncut.

You have been warned. Now what will you do?

passages.title: Elemental Bonds: Doubt
passages.text: Stay vigilant, <name>! Do not give up on Go'el.

passages.title: Elemental Bonds: Doubt
passages.text: What is this... water?

passages.title: Elemental Bonds: Desire
passages.text: Once again, <class>, I cannot do this without your help. I will try to quiet this tempest, but you will need to fight back the unstable elementals that whirl around it. Only then can we free Go'el!

passages.title: Elemental Bonds: Desire
passages.text: My Go'el cannot tread these waters forever, <name>!

passages.title: Elemental Bonds: Desire
passages.text: Air, water... now earth?

passages.title: Elemental Bonds: Patience
passages.text:
With the Stonemother's blessing, I can take us to where Go'el is being held.

We must be careful. The Twilight's Hammer has agents all around. You help me hold them off while I attempt to get through to Go'el!

Speak with me when you are ready, and I will take you to him.

passages.title: Elemental Bonds: Patience
passages.text: We are nearly there, <name>. Stay by my side a bit longer. We will get through to him yet.

passages.title: Elemental Bonds: Patience
passages.text: <Aggra clenches her fists, and stares at the spot where Thrall stood moments ago.>

passages.title: Elemental Bonds: Fury
passages.text:
The totems, <name>! We need to activate them, or Go'el is lost!

Kill the elementals next to each of my totems, located around the edges of this plateau. Once all four totems are activated, we should be able to free the last piece of Go'el's soul!

passages.title: Lily, Oh Lily
passages.text:
The lilies that grow around Stillwater Pond can be rendered down into a delightful broth.

Well... by "delightful," I mean "won't immediately sicken any orc who drinks it."

Why don't you go gather some for me, hmmm? Just watch out for the giant flesh-eating tadpoles.

passages.title: Lily, Oh Lily
passages.text: Did you find enough Stillwater Lilies?

passages.title: Lily, Oh Lily
passages.text: Ah, what a luscious batch of lilies. Bravo! I'll boil them down right away...

passages.title: Roach Coach
passages.text:
For all the grousing those Kor'kron Overseers do about Undercity food, there's ONE thing they'll eat in spades: My sister Audrey's Thrice-Spiced Crunchy Stew.

Its popularity means she's always running low on ingredients. Could you gather some for her at the coach she sells them from?

You'll find traps all over the city; just take their contents to Audrey and she'll handle the rest!

passages.title: Roach Coach
passages.text:
I call my little traps "Cockroach Cabins."

Cockroaches check in, but they don't check out!

passages.title: Roach Coach
passages.text: Oh, and just as I was nearly out. Thank you!

passages.title: Into Coaxing Tides
passages.text:
Go'el must be in the plane of water... the Abyssal Maw itself! I shudder to imagine what fate awaits him there.

Find the elemental, Hydrius, near the Abyssal Breach. He knows of Go'el and is sympathetic to our fight against Ragnaros. If anyone can help you there, it's him.

I will meet you beneath the tides of Vashj'ir, <race>...

passages.title: Into Coaxing Tides
passages.text: I will do what I can to aid you, <class>.

passages.title: Into Constant Earth
passages.text: Time is short! My love lies in Deepholm. I will take us there when you are ready, and we will speak with Therazane the Stonemother.

passages.title: Into Constant Earth
passages.text: I already know what it is you seek, fleshlings. And I have chosen to aid you.

passages.title: Into Unrelenting Flame
passages.text:
We must travel now to the Firelands. Within that realm, Go'el's burning spirit could become as terrible as Ragnaros himself! Prepare yourself, for we will be alone in a hostile world.

Speak with me when you are ready... and may the ancestors protect us!

passages.title: Into Unrelenting Flame
passages.text: Be ready, <name>.

passages.title: One fer the Ages
passages.text:
I'm sure by now ye've heard the tale o' Old Ironjaw, the most famous and elusive fish in the waters o' Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern. Well, in his many years, he's been responsible for the rise o' many young ironjaws. Don't let the name fool ye, <name>, these young'uns are every bit as clever as their dad, but somewhat lackin' in experience.

With skill an' patience, ye could probably catch one, an' when ye do, bring it to the museum in Ironforge's Library an' put it on display fer all to see!

passages.title: One fer the Ages
passages.text: Did ye catch one o' Ironjaw's offspring?

passages.title: One fer the Ages
passages.text: Well done, <name>! Maybe seein' yer catch will inspire more dwarves to take up fishin'!

passages.title: Fish fer Squrky
passages.text:
Hae I introduced ye tae me pet, Squrky? I'm teachin' him tae fish all proper-like. Fer now, I've been feedin' him minnows fished from the pool in this cavern.

Maybe ye'd like tae give it a try? Just cast yer lure in the pool over there and feed Squrky any minnows ye happen tae fish up. He'll love ye ferever!

passages.title: Fish fer Squrky
passages.text: How's Squrky's lunch comin'?

passages.title: Fish fer Squrky
passages.text: Ye've done a good job. Squirky seems happy and I've had some time to make some new lures. Thank ye fer the help!

passages.title: Pond Predators
passages.text:
A well-meaning goblin visitor introduced Azshara snakeheads to our waters and now they're overrunning the pond.

Please, if you can catch some of these voracious predatory fish before they eat every smallfish and mud snapper in Thunder Bluff, I'd be terribly grateful.

passages.title: Pond Predators
passages.text: Have you caught any Azshara snakeheads, yet?

passages.title: Pond Predators
passages.text: Good work, <name>. It's up to all of Thunder Bluff's fishers to keep this vicious creature out of Mulgore's waters.

passages.title: The Ring's the Thing
passages.text:
One of the Forsaken from the Pools of Vision came to me and said he'd lost his ring to a blind cavefish in the waters there.

Or perhaps it was his finger. It was hard to tell; his jaw did not move and his Orcish was no better than mine.

In any case, I thought it would be a kind gesture towards our unusual visitors to catch and gut cavefish until the ring - or finger - was found.

Would you help?

passages.title: The Ring's the Thing
passages.text: You haven't seen a ring about, have you? I think one of the cavefish might have swallowed it...

passages.title: The Ring's the Thing
passages.text:
You found my ring, did you? I'm most grateful.

To be honest, I've no idea why I keep the thing. I'm not even certain how I acquired it... I suppose I am simply a creature of habit.

Still, as I said, I am grateful. Say... I found these things while searching for it myself. Perhaps they'd be of some use to you?

passages.title: Live Bait
passages.text:
If ye've ever fished fer crayfish, ye know they respond best to live bait, an' the more bait, the better. Would ye like to test my new bait? Simply smear this on yerself an' hop into Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh.

After ye've got the catch, take it to me friend, Cook Ghilm at Gol'Bolar Quarry, west of the lake. He's an expert at cookin' those oversized bugs!

passages.title: Live Bait
passages.text: Oh... this might hurt a wee bit.

passages.title: Live Bait
passages.text:
These are beautiful, <name>! Grimnur's goin' tae be so proud when he hears about this!

Oh, he did say tae pass this along tae ye, if the scheme worked.

passages.title: The Race to Restock
passages.text:
Thunder Bluff's fishing pond is being overrun with voracious Azshara snakeheads; there are hardly any smallfish or mud snappers left.

We already have fishers trying to kill as many snakeheads as they can, but can you assist us in our restocking efforts?

If you could gather some fish from Stonebull Lake and bring them here to Thunder Bluff, I would be very grateful.

passages.title: The Race to Restock
passages.text: Did you bring those fish from Stonebull Lake, yet?

passages.title: The Race to Restock
passages.text:
Your help is much appreciated, <name>.

Hopefully these fish will go a long way towards restocking our fishing pond.

passages.title: Craving Crayfish
passages.text:
One of the great delicacies of Mulgore is the crayfish that dwell in our lakes and streams. They are particularly popular during weddings or the celebration of a birth.

Would you help me catch some of these crafty crustaceans for the cooking pots of Thunder Bluff?

You can fish them up from Stonebull Lake, or simply dive in and grab them.

passages.title: Craving Crayfish
passages.text: Crayfish are so tasty. Have you caught many?

passages.title: Craving Crayfish
passages.text:
Ah, so many crayfish!

Did you fish these up? Or simply swim after them?

Well, no matter. Excellent work, <name>.

passages.title: The Gnomish Bait-o-Matic
passages.text:
One o' the gnomish engineerin' trainers gave me a blueprint fer a fancy lure he says'll help me catch fish faster and keep 'em from gettin' away. The whole thing sounds a mite silly if ye ask me, but I'll try anythin' once.

Here are the blueprints. Ye're going to need shiny baubles, which ye can buy from my assistant inside the buildin', a hair trigger ye can buy from an engineerin' supplier in Tinker Town, and a few rat traps from the Deeprun Tram.

passages.title: The Gnomish Bait-o-Matic
passages.text: How's that fancy new lure comin' along?

passages.title: The Gnomish Bait-o-Matic
passages.text: It doesn't look like anything I think a fish'd be interested in, but ye never know. Fish're strange creatures. Thanks fer givin' this a try, <name>.

passages.title: Keepin' the Haggis Flowin'
passages.text:
The haggis must flow. Aye, it's a figure o' speech, for haggis'll ne'er flow! Ye dinnae want to know what'll happen if the people o' Ironforge don't get their haggis.

I'm working on the next batch, but I'm still missing a couple of ingredients.

Sognar Cliffbeard is the meat vendor in the Military Ward, an' he'll sell you the big bag o' sheep innards I need. Ye can buy mild spices from any cooking supplier and ye can find sacks o' oatmeal in any inn or among the supplies in the city.

passages.title: Keepin' the Haggis Flowin'
passages.text: Do ye have those ingredients?

passages.title: Keepin' the Haggis Flowin'
passages.text: Ye got them all? Wonderful! I'll get started right away.

passages.title: Shiny Baubles
passages.text:
One of a fisher's most simple and effective tools is the shiny bauble; affixed to a line, even the most novice angler has a chance at a catch.

With all the fishing going on of late, though, Thunder Bluff is in woefully short supply!

Might I ask you to collect shiny stones from around the base of the central rise? Bring them to Nahari Cloudchaser so that she might craft more shiny baubles with them.

passages.title: Shiny Baubles
passages.text: Did you happen to bring me any shiny stones?

passages.title: Shiny Baubles
passages.text:
My, those are some very lovely stones! They'll make perfect shiny baubles, thank you.

Here... Kah told me you'd be by with the stones, and to give this to you upon your arrival.

passages.title: I Need to Cask a Favor
passages.text:
My stocks o' IPA, that's Ironforge Pale Ale for ye novices, are gettin' low. Luckily, the brewery isn't too far away an' they should have a new cask o' Drugan's IPA waitin' fer us. That Drugan's a genius of a brewer, I tell ye.

I won't be able to get down to Kharanos meself today, but perhaps ye can dash down there, pick up the new cask an' run it back 'ere? What d'ye say?

passages.title: I Need to Cask a Favor
passages.text: Well, did ye get the cask or not?

passages.title: I Need to Cask a Favor
passages.text: Ah, well done! I tell ye, that Drugan's a true polymath -- explorer, historian, brewer -- is there anythin' that man hasn't mastered?

passages.title: Pining for Nuts
passages.text:
The Shu'halo use pine nuts in so MANY dishes: meat, fish, vegetables, even baked into breads or sprinkled over sweet pastries.

The Earth Mother has blessed us in that the very BEST pine nuts come from the trees upon these very mesas. Simply gather pine cones and toast them over a cooking fire to release the nuts within.

Would you please be so kind as to gather some? There are hardly ever enough to go around...

passages.title: Pining for Nuts
passages.text: Have you found many of those tasty pine nuts?

passages.title: Pining for Nuts
passages.text:
You work so quickly!

I'll see that these are distributed to the various chefs and bakers of Thunder Bluff.

Thank you!

passages.title: Would You Like Some Flies With That?
passages.text:
It's not always about making food for the orcs, <class>. This time, it's about making food for what will hopefully be their replacements.

We need to start small, we need to catch flies. Flies love rotting meat, and we love rotting meat... as projectile weapons!

Check out the Meat Wagons for any extra bits of meat. Where you find the meat, you'll find the flies.

Bring me 25 bloated flies, and then I can start on the next stage of our cooking plan.

passages.title: Would You Like Some Flies With That?
passages.text: I bet some of that "meat" is still good.

passages.title: Would You Like Some Flies With That?
passages.text:
Ah!  Perfect!  Fat, slow and ready to be eaten!  Next up, we will feed them to our spiders.  Fatten them up, and then, we feed the spiders to the frogs...

Listen to me go on.  You don't need to know all the details.  This is just a small step in a grand cuisine in a grand scheme.

passages.title: Moat Monster!
passages.text:
Sometimes fishing means throwing something back, <class>.

We've been overfeeding these frogs for just that occasion. We've fed these frogs bloated spiders, that were fed bloated flies, and now, we are going to feed a real monster.

The moat above, in the Ruins of Lordaeron, is home to our very own moat monster.

Today is feeding day. But we must train it as well. In this bag, you will find a decoy kit and some bloated frogs. Use the decoy kit, then toss the frogs to the monster when it appears.

passages.title: Moat Monster!
passages.text: The dead feed the flies.  The flies feed the spiders.  The spiders feed the frogs.  The frogs feed our moat monster... It's a beautiful circle of life with the goal of ending life.

passages.title: "Magic" Mushrooms
passages.text:
You know of the Pools of Vision, yes?

There is a sort of mushroom that grows there... not the tough, rank fungi that dominates the place, but smaller, more delicate caps that grow beneath them.

They are rare and quite delicious, adding a flavor to meat dishes that one might even call magical.

...what? No, really. They just taste good. That's it.

passages.title: "Magic" Mushrooms
passages.text: Were you able to gather any mushrooms?

passages.title: "Magic" Mushrooms
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>! I'm sure these will impart a simply magical taste to whatever dish they're used in.

What? Stop looking at me like that!

passages.title: Mulgore Spice Bread
passages.text:
I am often asked, "Aska, who is making all this Mulgore spice bread?!"

It is a reasonable question. Our fine and noble bread is traded in countless settlements in the most far-away lands, even by our staunchest foes. IT'S JUST THAT GOOD.

And the answer...?

It is "YOU." Please take this packet of Mulgore spices and use it to turn bland, boring spice bread into MULGORE spice bread!

passages.title: Mulgore Spice Bread
passages.text: Have you baked that Mulgore spice bread, yet?

passages.title: Mulgore Spice Bread
passages.text:
Ooo, that bread smells delicious. You are quite the baker, <name>.

Who knows how far these exquisite loaves will go... I hear it's even popular among the draenei of the Azuremyst Isles!

passages.title: Corn Mash
passages.text:
One of Thunder Bluff's most important staples is cornmeal; bowls of corn may be found in nearly every home.

With so many of the local mills under constant attack by harpies, gnolls, reckless mining companies and Earth Mother knows what else, I often ask my students to help with the task of grinding corn into cornmeal.

Would you care to help?

passages.title: Corn Mash
passages.text: Much work is required to grind enough cornmeal for everyone's needs. Thank you for your help, <name>.

passages.title: Perfectly Picked Portions
passages.text:
Even the novice cook knows that a great dish begins with great ingredients.

I have standing orders with merchants throughout Thunder Bluff, but I'd like to see how well you do at selecting the very best of what they have to offer.

Please make the rounds and gather perfect portions of meat, fish, vegetables and herbs from local merchant stalls.

passages.title: Perfectly Picked Portions
passages.text: Have you gathered all the necessary ingredients?

passages.title: Perfectly Picked Portions
passages.text:
<Aska examines the ingredients you have chosen.>

Mmmhmmm. Yes. Well done!

I could not have chosen better myself.

passages.title: Stink Bombs Away!
passages.text:
The foolish Alliance have employed hags to fuel an attack on our city. Well, as my sister once told me, "Turnabout is fair play."

We will gladly return the favor. Speak with my sister, and she will provide you with a broomstick flight over Stormwind. While over Stormwind, drop stink bombs on the city and on the people. Make them suffer!

We will show those hags in Stormwind who is the most powerful.

passages.title: Stink Bombs Away!
passages.text: The magic those hags in Stormwind use is no match for our magic, <class>.

passages.title: Stink Bombs Away!
passages.text:
That will show the fools in the Alliance who is the strongest.

Take these treats and treat yourself to something nice, <class>.

passages.title: A Time to Build Up
passages.text:
We burn the effigy of the Wickerman as a symbol of our struggle against those who would oppose us. We wear the ashes of the burnt Wickerman as a symbol of our neverending fight against those who would enslave us.

Use the bonfire nearby and ignite the Wickerman. Then take the ashes that lay nearby and spread them across your face.

These gestures will serve as a reminder to our enemies that we shall never yield.

passages.title: A Time to Build Up
passages.text: This is the night that our enemies fear us the most, <class>.

passages.title: A Time to Build Up
passages.text: NOW is the time of the Forsaken! Power to the Forsaken - NOW AND FOREVER!!!

passages.title: Thanks, But No Thanks
passages.text:
A holiday sweater may not be for everyone.

The receipt says that you can exchange it for gold at any Smokywood Pastures merchant.

All exchanges are final.

passages.title: Thanks, But No Thanks
passages.text:
A holiday sweater may not be for everyone.

The receipt says that you can exchange it for gold at any Smokywood Pastures merchant.

All exchanges are final.

passages.title: Hero's Call: Mount Hyjal!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Varian Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Emissary Windsong at Nighthaven in Moonglade.

Our brothers in the Cenarion Circle report that Deathwing's minions have launched a destructive offensive against the world tree and threaten to burn it to the ground!

Speak with Cenarion Emissary Jademoon in Stormwind Keep to gain entry into Moonglade.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance! Fight on, <brother/sister>!

passages.title: Missing Heirlooms
passages.text:
The last of my belongings were supposed to be arriving from Theramore today. The ship has arrived, but I haven't heard from the courier. The crate he was transporting had items that've been in my family for generations.

Will you go down to Stormwind Harbor and see what's keeping him?

passages.title: Missing Heirlooms
passages.text: The crate that Anson described doesn't appear to be here...

passages.title: Missing Heirlooms
passages.text: This courier won't be meeting with his employer anytime soon and the crate he was hired to transport seems to have disappeared.

passages.title: A New Supplier of Souvenirs
passages.text:
<sigh>

Don't talk to me about last year's stein...

I think our shady stein suppliers were somehow involved with that Twilight Hammer cult non-sense that errupted just before the elementals invaded.

And that's why we have a new supplier and a better stein!

Here's a voucher for one.

Talk to Blix near the back of the Brewfest camp. He's pretty strange, even more so now that he's always wearing those goggles. He'll handle the voucher for you, and any other Brewfest transaction.

passages.title: A New Supplier of Souvenirs
passages.text: What's happening hot stuff?  Got something for me?

passages.title: A New Supplier of Souvenirs
passages.text:
What's this?  A stein voucher?  So you like drinking?  Great!  After I give you this stein, go have a few drinks!  Then a few more.  Maybe have a few more after that...  Then, now this is important, come see me.

Look, I know you'll be back eventually.  If you want your Brewfest tokens redeemed you have to see me.

Anyways, here's the stein, and remember to talk to me later.

passages.title: A New Supplier of Souvenirs
passages.text:
The less said about last year's stein, the better, <name>. I'll tell you this, our previous supplier, they were shady. Turns out they were involved in some cultist activities...

We can't work with people who are trying to destroy the world!!

So we have a new supplier and a new stein.

Take this voucher to Belbi Quikswitch near the back of the Brewfest camp. She'll give you your free Brewfest stein. She'll also handle any and all other Brewfest transactions that come up during the holiday.

passages.title: A New Supplier of Souvenirs
passages.text: What's happening hot stuff?  Got something for me?

passages.title: A New Supplier of Souvenirs
passages.text:
Aww, it's just a stein voucher... Maybe you're just playing hard to get.  So here's this year's stein for you.

But I suspect I'll be seeing a lot more of you.  After all, if you want any Brewfest tokens redeemed, I'm your girl...

Or maybe I'm his girl...  

Oooohhh... or his...

passages.title: Shopping Around
passages.text:
I told the 'gentleman' that there might be a shop more suited to his needs in the Dwarven District. It's called the Shady Lady and you can find the entrance near the Canals on the western side of the district.

Quincy Cutler is your man. He trades in merchandise an honest broker would never touch!

passages.title: Shopping Around
passages.text: You look like you know something about these missing goods.

passages.title: Shopping Around
passages.text: Finally, Cutler's given me something I can work with. Before I give up that information, I'm going to want to know who you're working for.

passages.title: The Collector's Agent
passages.text:
According to Quincy, the "collector" who wants the crate is none other than the insane Archmage Xylem of Azshara.

The archmage's faithful servant is to meet with the man who has the crate in the catacombs beneath the Cathedral of Light.

You must get there in time to intercept the exchange and retrieve the crate before it is lost to Xylem forever. When you have the crate, meet me at the Golden Keg.

passages.title: The Collector's Agent
passages.text: Tendrils of dark power dance around the crate, but there's no trace of Sanath Lim-yo. You can now claim the crate and return it to your employer.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Staff
passages.text: To train, first you must be properly equipped. Retrieve a weapon from one of the weapon racks below, bring it to me, and show me that you know how to hold it properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Burning Scroll
passages.text:
Every wisdom has a time and place, and times are changing for those of us living here on Shen-zin Su. For this lesson, I would ask two things of you.

For the first, I hold a flame in my hand. Gather your wits, and when you think you are ready, attempt to snatch the flame.

Should you succeed, I want you to then climb to the top of this temple and burn the Edict of Temperance that you find there.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Burning Scroll
passages.text: There will come time when you must trust your instincts and simply act.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Burning Scroll
passages.text:
The fact that you were able to snatch the flame so easily is no small feat.

The Edict of Temperance is a scroll of wisdom passed down from my elders' elders. Wisdom from a more peaceful time.

Every lesson has its time and place, and with darkness on the horizon, the time for this particular wisdom has passed.

The burning of the scroll is an acceptance of tidings to come and a promise to action. Your hand carried the flame, and I suspect that it will continue to do so in the future.

passages.title: What Now?
passages.text:
You've finally found the crate that Anson sent you to retrieve. However, it appears the archaeology student's warnings about the nature of the crate's contents were correct.

There's no doubt that your employer lied to you about the dangers involved in the job. Do you really want to hand the crate over to him, or would you rather give it to Hudson Barnes, who believes it better to keep the crate's contents locked away?

passages.title: What Now?
passages.text: Have you brought the crate as we discussed?

passages.title: What Now?
passages.text: Ah, you did manage to get the crate before Archmage Xylem's man could get it out of the city. Excellent!

passages.title: The Creepy Crate
passages.text:
It's been sought after, stolen, and sold. Anyone who tried to tap the magic held within has seen that power turn against him.

Yet, the crate itself appears unscathed and suffused with magical energy. From time to time, it shakes or bobs as if its contents were alive.

It seems bonded to you and now it's yours.

passages.title: Missing Heirlooms
passages.text:
I told that courier to take the zeppelin, but no, he had to use the goblin ship! Well, now he's late and my precious family heirlooms are with him.

If you're willing to help, would you go down to the docks east of Orgrimmar, board the goblin ship and see what's keeping him?

passages.title: Missing Heirlooms
passages.text: This courier won't be meeting with his employer anytime soon and the crate he was hired to transport seems to have disappeared.

passages.title: Shopping Around
passages.text:
Look, I told that shady character that there might be a shop more open to his, uh, wares in the Drag. Droffer's and Son Salvage is the name of the place.

Look for Dran Droffers. He oversees the 'salvage' of rare and valuable objects from all over Azeroth.

passages.title: Shopping Around
passages.text: You look like you know something about these missing goods.

passages.title: Shopping Around
passages.text: Leave it to Droffers to have a buyer lined up already. We should combine our efforts to track down this thief and keep the crate's contents from falling into the wrong hands.

passages.title: What Now?
passages.text:
You've finally found the crate that Edgar Goodwin sent you to retrieve. However, it appears the Reliquary representative's warnings about the nature of the crate's contents were correct.

There's no doubt that your employer lied to you about the dangers involved in the job. Do you really want to hand the crate over to him, or would you rather give it to Delian Sunshade, who believes it better to keep the crate's contents locked away?

passages.title: What Now?
passages.text: Have you brought the crate as we discussed?

passages.title: What Now?
passages.text: I never thought you'd be able to recover it. Well, let's see it.

passages.title: The Creepy Crate
passages.text:
It's been sought after, stolen, and sold. Anyone who tried to tap the magic held within has seen that power turn against him.

Yet, the crate itself appears unscathed and suffused with magical energy. From time to time, it shakes or bobs as if its contents were alive.

It seems bonded to you and now it's yours.

passages.title: Test Your Strength
passages.text:
For some people, it's all fun and games until someone gets hurt. I call those people, weak.

To be the strongest, you have to hurt someone or something. You hurt yourself as you push your body to its limits. You hurt those that threaten the well-being of others.

If you want to be the strongest, you have to fight. How bad do you want it?

I want you to crush those that would offer a challenge to you, then bring me back proof of your triumphs.

passages.title: Test Your Strength
passages.text: No pain, no gain.

passages.title: Test Your Strength
passages.text:
Did you seek out worthy challenges, or did you simply find some field of boars and slaughter them?

There is a reason I am the strongest.

Perhaps, one day you will see just how strong I really am, <class>.  Until then, keep pushing yourself.  But don't forget to take a break from time to time.

Like now.  Here, enjoy the Darkmoon Faire.

passages.title: Tonk Commander
passages.text:
Welcome to our humble little steam tank battle simulator!

For one token, you can demonstrate your tactical mastery by navigating the course and destroying the targets.

passages.title: Tonk Commander
passages.text: Have tonk, will travel!

passages.title: Tonk Commander
passages.text:
An impressive display!

Here's your reward.

passages.title: The Fallen Guardian
passages.text:
Fandral Staghelm was kept prisoner here in Hyjal. It was the green dragon Alysra - one of my very own! - who was in charge of keeping Fandral secure.

We can only conclude that the Twilight's Hammer has gotten to her. You must confront her, <name>. Destroy her if you must - I cannot bear to see it.

She was last seen in the Ruins of Lar'donir, west of the World Tree.

passages.title: A Curious Crystal
passages.text:
Power swirls inside this strange crystal. Perhaps it was once a magical focus, an energy source, or simply a good luck charm. There's no way to know for certain.

The Darkmoon Adventurer's Guide indicates that the crystal would be of interest to Professor Thaddeus Paleo at the Darkmoon Faire.

passages.title: A Curious Crystal
passages.text: What is it you have there?

passages.title: A Curious Crystal
passages.text:
Where did you get this crystal?

These are very rare and much sought-after by collectors. I would like to study this one and display it at the Faire. Would you accept a generous number of Darkmoon Faire tickets in trade?

passages.title: An Exotic Egg
passages.text:
You're not certain what kind of creature this egg harbors, but it sure doesn't look like the egg of any ordinary animal.

The Darkmoon Adventurer's Guide says that an intrepid adventurer might come across any number of strange eggs in his travels. It further notes that the Darkmoon Faire's Zoo Bizarre is always interested in acquiring such specimens.

Take the egg to Yebb Neblegear at the Darkmoon Faire.

passages.title: An Exotic Egg
passages.text: What is it you have there?

passages.title: An Exotic Egg
passages.text: Where did you find this egg? There's sure to be something monstrous and wonderful inside! It will make a great addition to our zoo. Are you willing to part with it for a generous number of Darkmoon tickets?

passages.title: An Intriguing Grimoire
passages.text:
This massive spellbook reveals very little of its origins. Its pages are filled with a variety of spells and enchantments, only a few of which are familiar.

The Darkmoon Adventurer's Guide says the tome may be of some interest to Sayge, the famous gnoll fortuneteller at the Darkmoon Faire.

passages.title: An Intriguing Grimoire
passages.text: What is it you have there?

passages.title: An Intriguing Grimoire
passages.text: A strange grimoire, how interesting! I don't think I've seen its like before. I'd love to have it for my collection. Would you be willing to accept Darkmoon tickets in exchange?

passages.title: A Wondrous Weapon
passages.text:
An inspection of the weapon reveals expert craftsmanship and intricate inlay work, but this is no ceremonial blade. Faint marks and nicks along the blade attest to its use in combat.

The Darkmoon Adventurer's Guide lists several types of rare and valuable weapons, leaving no doubt that Professor Thaddeus Paleo at the Darkmoon Faire would be interested in taking a look at this piece.

passages.title: A Wondrous Weapon
passages.text: What is it you have there?

passages.title: A Wondrous Weapon
passages.text:
Where did you find such a wonderful blade?

This is a work of astounding craftsmanship and worthy weapon for any champion. I would love to have it for display.

Would you accept a generous number of Darkmoon Faire tickets in trade?

passages.title: A Curious Crystal
passages.text:
Power swirls inside this strange crystal. Perhaps it was once a magical focus, an energy source, or simply a good luck charm. There's no way to know for certain.

The Darkmoon Adventurer's Guide indicates that the crystal would be of interest to Professor Thaddeus Paleo at the Darkmoon Faire.

passages.title: An Intriguing Grimoire
passages.text:
This massive spellbook reveals very little of its origins. Its pages are filled with a variety of spells and enchantments, only a few of which are familiar.

The Darkmoon Adventurer's guide says the tome may be of some interest to Sayge, the Faire's famous fortuneteller. Look for him near his tent on Darkmoon Island.

passages.title: A Woundrous Weapon
passages.text:
An inspection of the weapon reveals expert craftsmanship and intricate inlay work, but this is no ceremonial blade. Faint marks and nicks along the blade attest to its use in combat.

The Darkmoon Adventurer's Guide lists several types of rare and valuable weapons, leaving no doubt that Professor Thaddeus Paleo at the Darkmoon Faire would be interested in taking a look at this piece.

passages.title: The Master Strategist
passages.text:
This tome of strategy is the masterwork of the famous human general, Anduin Lothar. In his own words, the commander describes the proper deployment of forces and strategies needed to win almost any battle.

Professor Thaddeus Paleo of the Darkmoon Faire would probably love to have a look at such a rare book.

passages.title: The Master Strategist
passages.text: That doesn't look like a common book at all...

passages.title: The Master Strategist
passages.text: I don't know how you got your hands on this, and I know better than to ask. Could I convince you to part with it in exchange for Darkmoon tickets?

passages.title: The Master Strategist
passages.text:
This tome of strategy is the masterwork of the famous human general, Anduin Lothar. In his own words, the commander describes the proper deployment of forces and strategies needed to win almost any battle.

Professor Thaddeus Paleo of the Darkmoon Faire would probably love to have a look at such a rare book. Look for him at the faire's home on Darkmoon Island.

passages.title: A Captured Banner
passages.text:
This tattered banner bears a faded guild crest. This old banner must've seen more than its share of battles.

Professor Thaddeus Paleo of the Darkmoon Faire collects banners and other relics of combat and he might be interested in acquiring this one. Show the banner to him next time you visit the Darkmoon Faire.

passages.title: A Captured Banner
passages.text: What is it you have there?

passages.title: A Captured Banner
passages.text:
What a splendid banner! I'd love to have it for my collection.

Would you be willing to trade it for some Darkmoon tickets?

passages.title: The Enemy's Insignia
passages.text:
This battered badge carries the insignia of an enemy officer. While worth little more to you than the metal it's made from, this piece would have significant value to a collector of military memorabilia.

Professor Thaddeus Paleo of the Darkmoon Faire is famous all over Azeroth for his large collection of military artifacts. Show the badge to him the next time you visit the Darkmoon Faire.

passages.title: The Enemy's Insignia
passages.text: What is it you have there?

passages.title: The Enemy's Insignia
passages.text: This is a remarkable example of an officer's insignia. While many of them visit the Faire, none are willing to part with their badges. Would you be willing to accept some Darkmoon tickets in trade?

passages.title: The Captured Journal
passages.text:
This book is covered in battered leather stained with blood and mud. Leafing through the pages, you discover that it is a personal journal of an adventurer with a high opinion of himself and his adventures.

Professor Thaddeus Paleo of the Darkmoon Faire might want to see something like this.

passages.title: The Captured Journal
passages.text: What is it you have there?

passages.title: The Captured Journal
passages.text:
A remarkable find!

<The professor browses the book's contents.>

Some of these are hard to read, but if even a third of the contents of this journal are true, this is a real treasure. Would you trade it for a generous number of Darkmoon tickets?

passages.title: A Captured Banner
passages.text:
This tattered banner bears a faded guild crest. This old banner must've seen more than its share of battles.

Professor Thaddeus Paleo of the Darkmoon Faire collects banners and other relics of combat and he might be interested in acquiring this one.

passages.title: The Enemy's Insignia
passages.text:
This battered badge carries the insignia of an enemy officer. While worth little more to you than the metal it's made from, this piece would have significant value to a collector of military memorabilia.

Professor Thaddeus Paleo of the Darkmoon Faire is famous all over Azeroth for his large collection of military artifacts.

passages.title: The Captured Journal
passages.text:
This book is covered in battered leather stained with blood and mud. Leafing through the pages, you discover that it is a personal journal of a Horde adventurer with a high opinion of herself and her adventures.

Professor Thaddeus Paleo of the Darkmoon Faire might want to see something like this.

passages.title: Tools of Divination
passages.text:
This collection of well-worn runestones has seen much use. The pieces seem old; you can't recognize any of the markings on their surfaces.

Perhaps a scholar or a collector would know more about them. Bring them to Professor Thaddeus Paleo next time you're at the Darkmoon Faire.

passages.title: Tools of Divination
passages.text: What do you have there?

passages.title: Tools of Divination
passages.text:
Where did you find this collection of runes? I haven't seen anything like this in years. It'll be a splendid mystery to unravel!

Would you trade these for Darkmoon tickets?

passages.title: Tools of Divination
passages.text:
This collection of well-worn runestones has seen much use. The pieces seem old; you can't recognize any of the markings on their surfaces.

Perhaps a scholar or a collector would know more about them. Bring them to Professor Thaddeus Paleo at the Darkmoon Faire.

passages.title: Talkin' Tonks
passages.text:
The steam tonks are one of the Darkmoon Faire's most popular amusements. Our visitors love to test their skills for hours and hours, but the tonks take a real beating from all that fun.

You look like you know your way around a wrench. Mind helping me fix some of the damaged tonks and return them to working order? I'll compensate you for your time.

passages.title: Baby Needs Two Pair of Shoes
passages.text:
You may have seen my horse, Baby, over near the wagons. She pulls the cart that hauls all the animals in our Zoo Bizarre.

She's a hard worker and she tears through shoes like you wouldn't believe. It's about time for a new set. I've already bought the raw materials.

All you need to do is shape them over an anvil and apply them to Baby's feet. It's a quick job and worth some tickets, wouldn't you say?

passages.title: Rearm, Reuse, Recycle
passages.text:
Faire-goers just love the steam tonks! And when the Darkmoon Faire closes, these grounds will be littered with tonk scrap.

It'd be a shame to let all that good metal just sit in the dirt.

If you help me collect some of the larger scraps, I can use them to reforge broken tonk parts. It's a lot less expensive than buying new metal every time. What do you say?

passages.title: Writing the Future
passages.text:
As the popularity of the Darkmoon Faire grows, more and more people seek me out to peer into their futures.

Most times, they ask for knowledge best left hidden in the mists of time, but it is not my place to give such advice.

My stock of written fortunes is running low and you look to have a steady hand. Take these herbs, make ink from them, and pen a few fortunes for me. I'll see to it that you're rewarded.

passages.title: Eyes on the Prizes
passages.text:
The games are more popular than ever, and that means we're giving out prizes faster than we ever have before!

We're going to need more prizes, and fast. If you've some skill in leatherworking, I can give you a kit. You'll need to buy some of the pieces from a trade goods merchant like Shadi Mistrunner up on the central rise of Thunder Bluff, but they're inexpensive.

Are you willing to help?

passages.title: Putting Trash to Good Use
passages.text:
People don't just come to the fair for fun and fortunes, <name>. Most want something to take home with them, so I help to create the magical trinkets visitors purchase with their prize tickets.

For that, I need a steady supply of soothsayer's dust. Take a look around the grounds and you'll see a lot of discarded weapons. Those are just the kinds of items that can be broken down into dust with enchanting skills like yours. Would you like to help?

passages.title: A Fizzy Fusion
passages.text:
I'm sure you've made a lot of potions in your time as an alchemist. How would you like to help with something a bit more light-hearted?

I've always wanted to try creating a fruit-flavored version of our popular fizzy drinks. If you're willing to give it a try, you can buy some of the base drink from me and mix it with some moonberry juice.

Galissa Sundew should be able to sell you all the moonberry juice you need.

passages.title: Banners, Banners Everywhere!
passages.text:
Isn't it wonderful to see Darkmoon banners everywhere? It's my favorite part of setting up, but we have so many old and tattered ones that need to be replaced.

If you've some skill with a needle and thread, would you mind making a banner from this kit and putting it up in some loose stone on the central rise in Thunder Bluff?

You can get the rest of the supplies you'll need from Shadi Mistrunner on the central rise of Thunder Bluff.

passages.title: Keeping the Faire Sparkling
passages.text:
The Darkmoon Faire's performers and animals go through more jewelry than I'd ever imagined. Thankfully, the gems are just cut glass, but someone has to craft all of it.

If you've some skill as a jewelcrafter, perhaps you'd be willing to help craft some of the sparkling glass gems for our performers.

Sometimes you can find odd and amazing bits of glass around the grounds. Those make stunning gems when cut by someone with an eye for this craft.

passages.title: Putting the Crunch in the Frog
passages.text:
The Darkmoon Faire's crunchy frog is famous all over Azeroth!

We've just had a fresh batch of frogs delivered. How'd you like to help whip up a few and practice your cooking skills in the process?

Shadi Mistrunner sells flour, up on the central rise in Thunder Bluff. Get some flour from her and use it to coat these frogs, then cook them in the pot behind me.

passages.title: Fun for the Little Ones
passages.text:
Children are always full of questions about what an archaeologist does and how it works, so I prepared a demonstration for them.

I take artifacts and fossils and bury them in the sand behind the tent. The children get to dig and make their own discoveries, learn how bones fit together, and see how archaeology can teach them about history.

If you have any spare fossils, would you consider donating them to my side project?

passages.title: A Fizzy Fusion
passages.text:
I'm sure you've made a lot of potions in your time as an alchemist. How would you like to help with something a bit more light-hearted?

I've always wanted to try creating a fruit-flavored version of our popular fizzy drinks. If you're willing to give it a try, you can buy some of the base drink from me and mix it with some moonberry juice.

Any innkeeper in Elwynn Forest or Mulgore should be able to sell you enough juice to make your creation.

passages.title: A Fizzy Fusion
passages.text: How's that moonberry fizz coming?

passages.title: A Fizzy Fusion
passages.text:
Your creation looks promising. With any luck, we'll soon have a new favorite!

Thanks for your help!

passages.title: Fun for the Little Ones
passages.text:
Children are always full of questions about what an archaeologist does and how it works, so I prepared a demonstration for them.

I take artifacts and fossils and bury them in the sandbox beside the tent. The children get to dig and make their own discoveries, learn how bones fit together, and see how archaeology can teach them about history.

If you have any spare fossils, would you consider donating them to my side project?

passages.title: Fun for the Little Ones
passages.text: How about it? Want to donate some fossil fragments?

passages.title: Fun for the Little Ones
passages.text: These are great! They're just the kinds of pieces the kids will be excited to 'discover'.

passages.title: Baby Needs Two Pair of Shoes
passages.text:
You may have seen my horse, Baby, over near the wagons. She pulls the cart that hauls some of the animals in our Zoo Bizarre.

She's a hard worker and she tears through shoes like you wouldn't believe. It's about time for a new set. I've already bought the raw materials.

All you need to do is shape them over an anvil and apply them to Baby's feet. It's a quick job and worth some tickets, wouldn't you say?

passages.title: Baby Needs Two Pair of Shoes
passages.text: How's old Baby doing?

passages.title: Baby Needs Two Pair of Shoes
passages.text: Thank you for your help, <name>! Here's the payment I promised.

passages.title: Putting the Crunch in the Frog
passages.text:
The Darkmoon Faire's crunchy frog is famous all over Azeroth!

We've just had a fresh batch of frogs delivered. How'd you like to help whip up a few and practice your cooking skills in the process?

You can get the flour you'll need to bread the frogs from any trade goods vendor in Elwynn Forest or Mulgore.

passages.title: Putting the Crunch in the Frog
passages.text: Do I smell fresh crunchy frog?

passages.title: Putting the Crunch in the Frog
passages.text: These are perfectly cooked, <name>. You've done an excellent job.

passages.title: Putting Trash to Good Use
passages.text:
People don't just come to the faire for fun and fortunes, <name>. Most want something to take home with them, so I help to create the magical trinkets visitors purchase with their prize tickets.

For that, I need a steady supply of soothsayer's dust. Take a look around the grounds and you'll see a lot of discarded weapons. Those are just the kinds of items that can be broken down into dust with enchanting skills like yours. Would you like to help?

passages.title: Putting Trash to Good Use
passages.text: Did you manage to get any of that soothsayer's dust?

passages.title: Putting Trash to Good Use
passages.text: This will help maintain my supply. Anytime you want to help, just look up old Sayge while the Darkmoon Faire's in town.

passages.title: Talkin' Tonks
passages.text:
The steam tonks are one of the Darkmoon Faire's most popular amusements. Our visitors love to test their skills for hours and hours, but the tonks take a real beating from all that fun.

You look like you know your way around a wrench. Mind helping me fix some of the damaged tonks and return them to working order? I'll compensate you for your time.

passages.title: Talkin' Tonks
passages.text: You get those repairs done? Visitors are hard on those tonks and I'll need all of them up and running.

passages.title: Talkin' Tonks
passages.text: Good job getting those tonks back online. Here are those tickets I promised.

passages.title: Writing the Future
passages.text:
As the popularity of the Darkmoon Faire grows, more and more people seek me out to peer into their futures.

Most times, they ask for knowledge best left hidden in the mists of time, but it is not my place to give such advice.

My stock of written fortunes is running low and you look to have a steady hand. Take these herbs, make ink from them, and pen a few fortunes for me. You can get the parchment you'll need from any trade goods vendor in Elwynn Forest or Mulgore.

passages.title: Writing the Future
passages.text: Have you penned any of those fortunes?

passages.title: Writing the Future
passages.text: These look just like mine. You've quite an eye for detail. Thank you for all your help, <name>.

passages.title: Keeping the Faire Sparkling
passages.text:
The Darkmoon Faire's performers and animals go through more jewelry than I'd ever imagined. Thankfully, the gems are just cut glass, but someone has to craft all of it.

If you've some skill as a jewelcrafter, perhaps you'd be willing to help craft some of the sparkling glass gems for our performers.

Sometimes you can find odd and amazing bits of glass around the grounds. Those make stunning gems when cut by someone with an eye for this craft.

passages.title: Keeping the Faire Sparkling
passages.text: Were you able to craft any replacement gems for the performers' jewelry?

passages.title: Keeping the Faire Sparkling
passages.text: Very nice work, <name>. You've quite a talent for this.

passages.title: Eyes on the Prizes
passages.text:
The games are more popular than ever, and that means we're giving out prizes faster than we ever have before!

We're going to need more prizes, and fast. If you've some skill in leatherworking, I can give you a kit. You'll need to buy some of the pieces from any trade goods merchant in Elwynn Forest or Mulgore, but they're inexpensive.

Are you willing to help?

passages.title: Eyes on the Prizes
passages.text: Have you had a chance to make those prizes?

passages.title: Eyes on the Prizes
passages.text:
Excellent work! These look just like the others. Thank you for your help.

If you ever want to help again, look for me next time the Darkmoon Faire is in town.

passages.title: Rearm, Reuse, Recycle
passages.text:
Faire-goers just love the steam tonks! And when the Darkmoon Faire closes, these grounds will be littered with tonk scrap.

It'd be a shame to let all that good metal just sit in the dirt.

If you help me collect some of the larger scraps, I can use them to reforge broken tonk parts. It's a lot less expensive than buying new metal every time. What do you say?

passages.title: Rearm, Reuse, Recycle
passages.text: Did you manage to find any scrap? The grounds are full of it.

passages.title: Rearm, Reuse, Recycle
passages.text:
There's a good bit of scrap here. Thanks for your help. It'll be a big help when I refit the steam tonks.

Please take this as a reward for your help.

passages.title: Banners, Banners Everywhere!
passages.text:
Isn't it wonderful to see Darkmoon banners everywhere? It's my favorite part of setting up, but we have so many old and tattered ones that need to be replaced.

If you've some skill with a needle and thread, would you mind making a banner from this kit and putting it up in some loose stones scattered around the grounds of the faire?

It's missing a few pieces, but you should be able to get what you need from any trade goods vendor in Elwynn Forest or Mulgore.

passages.title: Banners, Banners Everywhere!
passages.text: Were you able to find a place for that new banner of yours?

passages.title: Banners, Banners Everywhere!
passages.text: Thanks for helping with those banners. You have quite a talent for needlework. Next time the Darkmoon Faire's in town, why not come by and help again?

passages.title: War on the Ramparts
passages.text:
Watchkeeper Gargolmar and Vazruden the Herald are in charge of defending these ramparts.

If you take them out, their forces will be in complete disarray.

Slay them both and bring me proof so the invasion can begin!

passages.title: War on the Ramparts
passages.text: This operation depends on your success, <name>.

passages.title: War on the Ramparts
passages.text:
With their leadership dead their forces should be in disarray.

But there's far more to this than killing a few guards, <class>.

passages.title: War on the Ramparts
passages.text:
Hellfire Citadel's entire defensive network relies on the ramparts as a sort of early warning system.

You need to take out Watchkeeper Gargolmar and Vazruden the Herald. Without them, taking the ramparts will be simple.

passages.title: War on the Ramparts
passages.text: Were you successful? We have a lot riding on this operation, <name>.

passages.title: War on the Ramparts
passages.text:
I knew I could count on you!

With their forces in disarray, we can really get this invasion going.

passages.title: Demons in the Citadel
passages.text:
One of our scouts spotted what he thought was an agent of the Burning Legion somewhere in the ramparts. If that is true, then Honor Hold may be in grave danger of a combined assault!

If you find this fiend in there, kill it on sight.

passages.title: Demons in the Citadel
passages.text: Did you find any demons in there?

passages.title: Demons in the Citadel
passages.text: So it's true. The fel orcs and the Burning Legion are working together in some capacity.

passages.title: Demons in the Citadel
passages.text:
One of our scouts brought back unpleasant news. We've spotted a powerful agent of the Burning Legion in the ramparts!

I need you to kill this demon before he has a chance to relay news of our efforts to his superiors.

passages.title: Demons in the Citadel
passages.text: Were you able to dispose of the foul creature?

passages.title: Demons in the Citadel
passages.text: Well done. We need the time you've bought us to investigate this link between the fel orcs and the Burning Legion. You very well may have saved hundreds of lives through your actions.

passages.title: Make Them Bleed
passages.text:
The Maker serves the purpose of creating more fel orcs by infusing them with demon blood.

My superiors believe that we may be able to reverse the process, but we need samples of their blood and The Maker's infusion rod before we can know for sure.

passages.title: Make Them Bleed
passages.text: You're back! Even better, you're not dead! Well done. Better than anyone else so far.

passages.title: Make Them Bleed
passages.text: These vials could mean the end of the fel orcs. I hope you understand just how important that is to our campaign here.

passages.title: Heart of Rage
passages.text:
We know that the fel orcs are growing their forces by infusing orcs with demon blood.

I need you to venture deep inside these unholy halls and find out how that's happening. We can't risk sending an army into this place until we know exactly what we're dealing with.

passages.title: Heart of Rage
passages.text:
<You tell Caza'rez everything you saw in the Blood Furnace.>

I see.

If they can do this to the Mag'har brown orcs, they can do it to us! We must be careful lest they turn all of Thrallmar into those mindless beasts.

passages.title: Make Them Bleed
passages.text:
The Maker uses demon blood and a special rod to turn brown and green orcs into red ones. We'd like to see if we can take that blood, mess around with it a bit, and make it turn orcs of all colors into harmless docile lumps. 

You're going to bring me some samples of their blood so we can see. Don't forget to grab that rod!

passages.title: Make Them Bleed
passages.text: You have that blood, darlin'?  Might be kind of important if we asked you to get it, you know?

passages.title: Make Them Bleed
passages.text: Out-frikkin-standing! As of right now, you are my eighth favorite person on the smoldering remains of this sorry planet!

passages.title: Heart of Rage
passages.text:
As it turns out, the eggheads back at Honor Hold can't see much into this place. Bunch of lying lazy mages, is what they are.

Either way, we don't really know exactly what's going on in here. So, you're going in to find out!

passages.title: Heart of Rage
passages.text:
<You tell Gunny everything you saw in the Blood Furnace.>

You brought back some loot for ol' Gunny, right?

No, no, you're right, clearly I owe you a reward for all your hard work. Not like Gunny didn't arrange all this and send you in there in the first place.

passages.title: Critical Condition
passages.text:
We may have won the first battle, but a critical task still remains.

Dozens of Skyfire pilots were shot down during the initial aerial battle.

Without medical aid, their condition will deteriorate over time, until they finally perish. We are their only hope for survival.

Go into the orchard and revive as many pilots as you can find.

We will leave no one behind.

passages.title: Critical Condition
passages.text: We will remember all the brave Alliance soldiers who fell today. Though they can no longer continue, we carry the fight onward.

passages.title: Critical Condition
passages.text: Good work, <name>. Those soldiers will live and fight another day because of your efforts.

passages.title: The White Pawn
passages.text:
Alright, soldier. I've got a critical mission for you.

Get down to the coastline south of here - in the cove there you'll find a wrecked Alliance vessel. I need you to search it and find out if it was the ship that was carrying Anduin. 

Then, recover the Captain's Log and see if it has any information on where we can find him.

Since the log is from a military ship, it'll be written using a cipher - take it to Nodd Codejack afterwards. He's keeping watch on the wreck from the other end of the cove.

passages.title: The White Pawn
passages.text: Well?

passages.title: The White Pawn
passages.text:
Alright... let me see... using the cipher from when the ship went missing...

<Nodd is clearly doing some calculations in his head.>

Aha!

passages.title: Lost in Action
passages.text:
You have to help me! We were sent here to investigate the various parts of the reservoir, but my friends haven't come back yet, and it's been a long time.

That's why I need you to discover what became of them. Naturalist Bite and Weeder Greenthumb went this way.

passages.title: Lost in Action
passages.text: Have you discovered anything?

passages.title: Lost in Action
passages.text:
The loss of life...it pains me.

<Watcher Jhang sighs.>

Thank you, <name>. When we are all reunited, the naga won't stand a chance.

passages.title: The Heart of the Matter
passages.text:
From what Nahuud has told me, two mighty creatures, Rokmar the Crackler and Quagmirran, were among the first enslaved by the naga when they arrived. They helped to subjugate many of the native races of Zangarmarsh.

Though it pains me greatly to ask you to do so, you must put them down.

passages.title: The Heart of the Matter
passages.text: Did you slay them?

passages.title: The Heart of the Matter
passages.text:
I'm glad that their spirits are now free. I wish we could say the same for the rest of their kind.

There is still much work to be done, especially elsewhere in Coilfang.

passages.title: Rescuing the Expedition
passages.text:
The last members of my expedition are somewhere in here. We're going to need the knowledge they've gathered and their skills if we're to have any chance at defeating the naga.

See if you can find Earthbinder Rayge and Windcaller Claw, and make sure they're ok.

passages.title: Rescuing the Expedition
passages.text: Were you able to find either of them? Are they ok?

passages.title: Rescuing the Expedition
passages.text:
Soon we'll all be together again, and I owe it all to you!

We'll bring the naga down before you know it, they don't stand a chance!

passages.title: Safety Is Job One
passages.text:
Shaffar's ethereals have completely blocked us out of the Mana-Tombs. Thankfully, I've got a plan. While we can't go in through the front door, there are sure to be several transporters inside.

I want you to clear the way for my crew first and then I want you to activate one of their transporters to teleport us inside.

Activate the teleporter in the chamber right before Shaffar's chambers when the way has been cleared. Don't worry, I'll make it worth your while...

passages.title: Safety is Job One
passages.text:
It's nearly safe for our men to come in here and take what's rightfully ours. The real danger now is Shaffar's personal army that he has crawling all over this place.

I need you to take care of his forces for me while I regain my strength.

passages.title: Safety is Job One
passages.text: Done already? You humans continue to fascinate me.

passages.title: Safety is Job One
passages.text: Splendid! Haramad will be delighted to hear the good news! All of this ripe for his taking!

passages.title: Intriguing Specimens
passages.text:
There is a creature not far inside these halls called Pandemonius who is able to twist void energies to sustain and empower itself.

A bit further in lies Tavarok, a being that takes those same void energies and converts them into a crystalline structure stronger than any I've ever seen!

I absolutely must obtain samples for further study.

passages.title: Intriguing Specimens
passages.text: If you don't have what I'm looking for, stop wasting my time.

passages.title: Intriguing Specimens
passages.text: These samples are absolutely fascinating. They'll work very nicely.

passages.title: Ashyo's Vision
passages.text:
Have a look at that!

<Ashyo motions at the massive waterfall to the north.>

This must be the water supply for the whole valley!

Think about it, <name>: the pandaren use this water to grow vegetables the size of a house. Where could it come from? What is so special about it?

The elders among my people know a technique for speaking with the water and divining the future. Perhaps this same technique can provide insight into the water's source...

It's worth a shot at least!

passages.title: Ashyo's Vision
passages.text: What is that jinyu up to over there?

passages.title: Ashyo's Vision
passages.text: I can't believe he was able to see that with a stick... perhaps there is more to "crazy jinyu rituals" than we thought.

passages.title: Defiance
passages.text:
The damn mogu hit us out of nowhere! Anyone they don't kill on sight is being dragged away into the woods.

This is the only safehouse, and its all I can do to hold the door.

What do you say, friend? Are you willing to stand up and fight for the weak?

passages.title: Defiance
passages.text: Don't worry - they won't get through me.

passages.title: Defiance
passages.text: Nice work, but there's more to be done if we are to save this village.

passages.title: Rally the Survivors
passages.text:
The people of this village are simple farmers - not fighters like you and I. Still, they are stubbornly defending their homes as best they can.

Search the village for anyone still on their feet and tell them to rally here at Hanae's place.

passages.title: Rally the Survivors
passages.text: Please tell me some still live...

passages.title: Rally the Survivors
passages.text: They're inside. Shaken, but alive thanks to you.

passages.title: Spitfire
passages.text:
We've tended these orchards and made cider from their nectar for generations. In that time, we've learned a special trick for putting out fires in a pinch.

<Hanae pushes a jug of cider into your hand.>

The cider itself - when mixed with crushed gingerleaf and saliva - quickly becomes sticky and viscous. Perfect for smothering flames.

Please, while you're out there, try to get the flames under control. I've already mixed in the gingerleaf, just swig and spit.

passages.title: Spitfire
passages.text: Best not to judge our prized cider by its flavor in this state.

passages.title: Spitfire
passages.text:
A survivor came in moments ago and said the flames are beginning to die down.

We owe our very way of life to you, stranger. I cannot possibly reward you adequately, but please take this.

passages.title: The Splintered Path
passages.text:
First... before the war-cries... we heard the trees.

Groaning, creaking, and finally crashing down as the mogu cut their way through the woods. They were making the return trip easier...

They're dragging our friends back down that path, to the ruins west of the village! Those ruins have been empty for years - our children play there.

Why would the mogu come back to them now?

passages.title: The Splintered Path
passages.text: This doesn't look like a quick snatch and run. They're setting up for something big.

passages.title: Raging Spirits
passages.text:
The Auchenai have turned their backs on everything we used to stand for. They've taken to raising the dead as unholy minions!

This cannot stand. Put the spirits back to rest, and massacre those responsible for raising them into undeath.

passages.title: Raging Spirits
passages.text: Don't speak to me again until the deed is done.

passages.title: Raging Spirits
passages.text: The dead belong in the spirit realm. Just as you belong in this one.

passages.title: Hitting Them Where It Hurts
passages.text:
The fel orcs have stockpiled many of their supplies here.

Stealing them would be a severe blow to their war effort and a great boon to ours. Are you up to the task, <class>?

passages.title: Hitting Them Where It Hurts
passages.text: How many piles were you able to take?

passages.title: Hitting Them Where It Hurts
passages.text: Well done! The long term effects of this attack will be far worse than slaying a few orcs could ever be.

passages.title: Hitting Them Where It Hurts
passages.text:
The fel orcs have stockpiled many of their supplies here.

Stealing them would be a severe blow to their war effort and a great boon to ours. Are you up to the task, <class>?

passages.title: Hitting Them Where It Hurts
passages.text: How many piles were you able to take?

passages.title: Hitting Them Where It Hurts
passages.text: Well done! The long term effects of this attack will be far worse than slaying a few orcs could ever be.

passages.title: Everything Will Be Alright
passages.text:
You've had quite an adventure, <name>. And before you've even set foot inside of the Auchenai Crypts.

I am one of the fortunate spirits. I was neither bound to Levixus nor a part of Exarch Maladaar's vile experiments in necromancy. While you have destroyed Levixus, Maladaar lives on, continuing to torment the spirits inside the crypts.

What I ask is simple. Enter the Auchenai Crypts and speak with the Draenei Spirit there. You must destroy Exarch Maladaar.

passages.title: Everything Will Be Alright
passages.text: Welcome to the Auchenai Crypts, <name>, where our two worlds meet.

passages.title: The End of the Exarch
passages.text:
Exarch Maladaar performs his unholy work in the deepest part of the crypts. He poses a threat to both of our worlds if he is not stopped.

You must slay him for the benefit of us all, dead and alive.

passages.title: The End of the Exarch
passages.text: You have done our realm a great service. You will not be forgotten.

passages.title: The End of the Exarch
passages.text:
Exarch Maladaar performs his unholy work in the deepest part of the crypts. He poses a threat to both of our worlds if he is not stopped.

You must slay him for the benefit of us all, dead and alive.

passages.title: Taretha's Diversion
passages.text:
It was Taretha who created the original diversion at Durnholde, allowing Thrall to escape.

Now the Infinite have captured Taretha. The diversion will not happen without our involvement. You must use the incendiary devices that I give you and burn down the internment lodges.

passages.title: Taretha's Diversion
passages.text: Who are you?

passages.title: Taretha's Diversion
passages.text: You are friends of Taretha? So this is her new plan? Very well then...

passages.title: Escape from Durnholde
passages.text:
I have plans for my people, stranger.

One day, they shall overthrow their oppressors and rise as one. They will break free from the bonds that hold them and from that uprising shall be born the orcish Horde.

We will leave when you are ready.

passages.title: Escape from Durnholde
passages.text: <Erozion nods.>

passages.title: Escape from Durnholde
passages.text: You have done a great thing, <name>. Alas, the young warchief's memory of these events must be as they originally were...

passages.title: Snap Judgment
passages.text:
These pools are very special: they nurture life like nothing else in Pandaria.

Unfortunately this means they draw all kinds of attention from local fauna. Recently, dragon turtles have discovered that toadspawn pools are common on the tier just above us. They're running wild up there, trampling the lotuses and snapping at my workers.

They aren't much of a threat on their own, but in groups they can be pretty nasty. Please, if you can spare your strength, help clear them out.

passages.title: Snap Judgment
passages.text:
<Yue sighs.>

If only we'd kept up with our maintenance, the situation would not have come to this.

passages.title: Snap Judgment
passages.text:
You have my gratitude, <name>.

Please take this as a token of my appreciation.

passages.title: Brother Against Brother
passages.text:
The Sethekk departed Skettis when Auchindoun exploded.

My brother, Syth, was one of their leaders and told us we had to go into the ruins and face our god.

In time, Syth had me cast out of the Halls for doubting them, but he refused to let me take our sister Lakka. Will you help me rescue her?

passages.title: Brother Against Brother
passages.text: Did you find her, <name>? Was she still being held within the halls?

passages.title: Brother Against Brother
passages.text:
Knowing that Lakka is free means I can cut the rest of my ties to the Sethekk.

Part of me will never forgive myself for Syth's death, but it had to be done. When I reach Skettis, I will perform the death rites for him.

passages.title: Terokk's Legacy
passages.text:
Terokk, hero of the Arakkoa, mysteriously vanished one day, leaving only his mask and spear behind.

Darkweaver Syth still holds his mask and Talon King Ikiss guards his spear.

It would mean a great deal to my people if these items were returned to us.

passages.title: Terokk's Legacy
passages.text: The relics of Terokk have been absent from Skettis for too long. Were you able to recover them from the Sethekk?

passages.title: Terokk's Legacy
passages.text: I may never truly be forgiven for my role in the crimes of the Sethekk, but perhaps by restoring the relics of Terokk to my people, I can begin to redeem myself.

passages.title: Allies in Dalaran
passages.text:
Welcome to Northrend, <name>. I have been asked to arrange travel for you to Dalaran so that you can meet with our allies there.

Ride the gryphon to Dalaran and once you land, make your way to our inn there, A Hero's Welcome. Find Isirami Fairwind and speak with her immediately.

She can help you bind your hearthstone to the city so you can use the Silver Enclave's portal to travel back to Stormwind quickly.

passages.title: Allies in Dalaran
passages.text:
