Welcome to Dalaran! This inn is part of the Silver Enclave, the headquarters of the official Alliance presence in our city.

Don't forget to bind your hearthstone here for easy travel to the city and access to the portal to Stormwind next door.

passages.title: Friends in Dalaran
passages.text:
Welcome to Northrend. I have been asked to arrange travel for you to Dalaran so that you can meet our friends in the city.

Speak with me and accept a ride to Dalaran. Once you land, make your way to The Filthy Animal.

Make contact with Uda the Beast immediately.

She can help you bind your hearthstone to the city so you can use the portal in Sunreaver's Sanctuary to travel back to Orgrimmar quickly.

passages.title: Friends in Dalaran
passages.text:
I've been expecting you! This inn is part of Sunreaver's Sanctuary, the Horde's enclave in Dalaran.

Don't forget to bind your hearthstone here for easy travel to the city and access to the portal to Orgrimmar, out by the fountain.

passages.title: A Proper Fate
passages.text:
Warlord Kalithresh is in charge of the entire Steamvault operation.

I need you to kill him, <name>. The naga have left us with no option but violence.

Show him no mercy.

passages.title: A Proper Fate
passages.text: I wish it had not come to this, but the naga refused all attempts to negotiate.

passages.title: Containment is Key
passages.text:
The naga are working with leper gnomes to spread a horrific disease across Zangarmarsh. It's already spread throughout the Steamvault.

Clear out anything that's been contaminated and bring me the central gear from Mekgineer Steamrigger, quickly!

passages.title: Containment is Key
passages.text: Be as thorough as possible. The fate of Zangarmarsh depends on it.

passages.title: Containment is Key
passages.text: I'm glad we were able to contain this before it spread across all of Zangarmarsh or further. Thank you.

passages.title: Windcaller Claw and the Water Thief
passages.text:
The Steamvault is the heart of the naga's efforts to pump the water out of Zangarmarsh, and Hydromancer Thespia personally oversees those efforts.

Taking her out would seriously hinder their operation.

passages.title: Windcaller Claw and the Water Thief
passages.text: Did you dispatch of the water thief?

passages.title: Windcaller Claw and the Water Thief
passages.text: Perhaps now we can restore all of the desperately needed water to the land.

passages.title: A Courteous Guest
passages.text:
I heard, I heard! The High Elder wants you to train with us!

There's going to be a banquet for us, the trainees... and you should probably bring a gift, as a sign of courtesy.

The oranges in the grove south of the temple are extra-sweet right now. Bring some back, for the banquet.

passages.title: A Courteous Guest
passages.text: Are you ready for the banquet? I can't wait.

passages.title: A Courteous Guest
passages.text:
These will do perfectly. What a thoughtful gift, <name>!

Me? I'm bringing beer, of course.

passages.title: The Great Banquet
passages.text: The banquet should be starting any time now. Go find the High Elder and pay your respects. I'll be right behind you.

passages.title: The Great Banquet
passages.text:
We will move on to the training soon enough, young <class>. First, we must talk, and drink, and eat.

Though I must say, I admire your discipline.

passages.title: The Great Banquet
passages.text:
That concludes our introductions. You should be ready to begin your training.

That is... you should be ready to begin your training... AFTER we have one more mug of ale. Perhaps two. Shall we, <name>?

passages.title: Perfection
passages.text:
Perfection can be achieved through repetition. Every single student in the training arena below will eventually perfect his or her form... assuming they don't give up first. This is a fact.

I encourage you to join them, <name>. As an honorary guest of the monastery, you are not required to perform the requisite 10,000 daily strikes. Simply follow the leader's example for a few minutes.

passages.title: Perfection
passages.text: I, too, once trained in this very arena. Times were simpler then.

passages.title: Perfection
passages.text: This isn't your first time fighting, is it? Your form isn't perfect, but it is certainly practiced.

passages.title: Attention
passages.text:
Your next test also involves concentration and attention. I want you to practice your abilities on the training bags in the pit below.

The bags are hung in groups of two. When I call out "Left", attack the bag on the left. When I call out "Right", attack the bag on the right.

If you fail to follow my simple directions, this task will become much harder.

Now beat on those practice bags until they burst, <name>.

passages.title: Attention
passages.text: What are you waiting for?

passages.title: Attention
passages.text:
You may not be a full-time trainee here, but do not let that keep you from learning anything.

I can assure you, the ability to quickly switch targets will prove valuable in future fights.

passages.title: A Proper Weapon
passages.text:
First things first, though.

A proper trainee needs a proper weapon. And a scrupulous trainee builds his own... or at least gathers the materials.

The switches which grow nearby should suffice for any respectable weapon. You'll also need to shop for black walnut extract to treat the wood. While you're there, get some ale, for...

<Wu pauses.>

...well, you know what ale is for.

passages.title: A Proper Weapon
passages.text: <Wu looks at you expectantly.>

passages.title: A Proper Weapon
passages.text:
<Groundskeeper Wu gratefully scoops up the gathered materials.>

I will have a weapon prepared for you by the end of your training. Now, onto the real work.

passages.title: A Strong Back
passages.text:
Some of our trainees have... larger-than normal appetites. We have occasionally had difficulty supplying enough food for all of them. In times like these, we have to ask for help.

A kindly older woman, who lives in a small house to the northwest, has agreed to make some stew for our trainees. All you need to do is go and get it.

passages.title: A Strong Back
passages.text:
She really is a nice woman. And an excellent cook.

The best cook in the world, actually.

passages.title: A Strong Back
passages.text:
I will see to it that this stew is distributed evenly and appropriately among the trainees.

After I set some aside for myself, of course.

passages.title: A Steady Hand
passages.text:
The black walnut extract you purchased from Miss Whiteblossom is but one of many extracts we keep in stock for various applications.

Blushleaf extract can be gathered from the flowers in the Waxwood Forest to the west. Several units can be extracted from one flower, but only those with calm nerves and steady hands can remove all of the extract from one flower.

passages.title: A Steady Hand
passages.text: It is said that the ancient herbalism masters were able to remove 20 vials of extract from each blossom.

passages.title: A Steady Hand
passages.text: Do not forget to wash your hands. Blushleaf stains forever.

passages.title: And a Heavy Fist
passages.text:
The greenwood sprites in the Waxwood Forest to the west pose no direct threat to us, this is true. However, their numbers have increased as of late, as have their wily antics.

Part of our duty as wardens of this forest is to maintain the balance. Your duty is to do so by returning these sprites to the earth.

passages.title: And a Heavy Fist
passages.text:
Very recently, I was walking in the Waxwood, when one of these sprites got on all fours behind my knees, evading my notice. Soon afterward, a second sprite approached me from the front, shoving me forcefully in the chest. Unaware of the first sprite, I stepped backwards, only to stumble on his prostrate form and fall, embarrassingly, onto my backside.

So yes, I have a vested interest in this assignment.

passages.title: And a Heavy Fist
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. The sprites' numbers will return in several days' time, but for now, the balance is maintained.

passages.title: Becoming Battle-Ready
passages.text:
Alright, <race>. I'd like to see what you're really made of.

You'll find my pupils all over the monastery. Challenge them to fights. Push them to their limits. They have been instructed to do the same to you.

Win or lose, you both will come out of the fight stronger.

passages.title: Becoming Battle-Ready
passages.text: You may be a hero in your own lands, but here, you must prove your worth.

passages.title: Becoming Battle-Ready
passages.text:
<Master Stone Fist eyes you warily.>

Alright, I've seen enough. No more beating up on the younger pupils. We will proceed to the next phase.

passages.title: Xiao, the Eater
passages.text:
You may have already met my best student, Xiao, at the banquet tables. I personally would have graduated him several times over, but Instructor Xann insists that he needs more discipline.

If you ask me, discipline means very little if you win every fight you enter. I'm curious to see if Xiao can keep his streak alive against you.

passages.title: Xiao, the Eater
passages.text: Young Xiao has a great future in martial arts. I wish you luck in your upcoming match.

passages.title: Xiao, the Eater
passages.text: I must admit, I was never surprised, <race>. You are a born fighter, and an excellent <class>.

passages.title: The Rumpus
passages.text:
Master Stone Fist has trained you in the art of one-on-one combat. Now you learn the art of one-on-many.

How does fifty sound?

Lower yourself into the Ring of Inner Focus below, then, when you're ready, set off this firework. My assistants will come at you, several at a time.

All you need to do is survive.

passages.title: The Rumpus
passages.text: Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: The Rumpus
passages.text: Your <class> fighting style is strong, <name>. Our trainees could learn much from watching you.

passages.title: Flying Colors
passages.text:
You have passed every test we prepared for you, <name>. It is now time for you to move on to bigger and better things.

...but not before another banquet. The High Elder will be waiting for you at the banquet grounds to celebrate your graduation from our monastery.

passages.title: Flying Colors
passages.text:
Congratulations, <name>. While your traineeship was strictly honorary, your results were undeniably impressive. The young ones look up to you.

Groundskeeper Wu had this prepared for you. Please, use it as you see fit.

passages.title: Find Spy To'gun
passages.text:
The Shadow Council has already killed most of our spies, but To'gun was foolish enough to escape only to go back in!

You must find him. He may be reckless, but we need to find out what he knows.

passages.title: Find Spy To'gun
passages.text: Do you think you could help me get out of this cage?  It's a bit cramped.

passages.title: The Soul Devices
passages.text:
They've been torturing me, trying to get me to tell them everything that I know.

They fed the others to Hellmaw, and I was to be next. But I told them nothing!

They're using special devices to make their summoning more powerful. You must steal these devices!

passages.title: The Soul Devices
passages.text: Were you able to find To'gun?

passages.title: The Soul Devices
passages.text: So, these are the soul devices that the Shadow Council were using to enhance their summoning power?  Intriguing.

passages.title: Trouble at Auchindoun
passages.text:
I have spies within Auchindoun and they have been sending me disturbing reports. That place has been nothing but trouble ever since it exploded a couple of years ago.

Something in there has gone horribly wrong - again - and the Shadow Council is now on a war footing. Though the reports were lacking on details, their preparations appear to be directed inward.

You must make your way to the Shadow Labyrinth. My field commander, Mahfuun, will fill you in on what needs to be done.

passages.title: Trouble at Auchindoun
passages.text:
It's about time that you arrived.

Mehlisah said that she would be sending help days ago.  And we've been fighting in here longer than that!

passages.title: The Codex of Blood
passages.text:
Two years ago the Shadow Council summoned forth a being that shattered Auchindoun in its wake.

Read the Codex of Blood to find out what happened. Be warned, Grandmaster Vorpil guards it with his life.

passages.title: The Codex of Blood
passages.text:
Opening the magically-suspended tome, a sense of dread overwhelms you.

Something is most definitely wrong here!

passages.title: Into the Heart of the Labyrinth
passages.text:
The Shadow Council has lost control of the cosmic being that they summoned here almost two years ago.

Known only as Murmur, it threatens to overrun the Shadow Council and break free into the outside world!

passages.title: Into the Heart of the Labyrinth
passages.text: Has the chaotic being been banished from our world?

passages.title: Into the Heart of the Labyrinth
passages.text:
I cringe to think what would have happened had Murmur escaped to the outside world.

Thank you, brave hero.

passages.title: Ambassador Hellmaw
passages.text:
When the Cabal found our spies, they fed them to Ambassador Hellmaw one by one.

Our men deserve justice. Slay the ritualists binding him, then dispose of Hellmaw.

It is a most deserving fate.

passages.title: Ambassador Hellmaw
passages.text: It won't bring anyone back, but at least justice has been done.

passages.title: Flying Colors
passages.text:
Well, I've done all that I can with you. Sounds like the others have, too.

High Elder Cloudfall will be waiting at the banquet grounds, ready to celebrate your departure. Not that we're happy you're leaving... he just enjoys celebrations.

passages.title: Flying Colors
passages.text:
Congratulations, <name>. While your traineeship was strictly honorary, your results were undeniably impressive. The young ones look up to you.

Groundskeeper Wu had this prepared for you. Please, use it as you see fit.

passages.title: Flying Colors
passages.text:
The Rumpus was your final test. You have mastered the disciplines taught at this monastery.

Just as your training began with a banquet, so shall it end. High Elder Cloudfall should be waiting at the banquet grounds. I'll be right behind you.

passages.title: Flying Colors
passages.text:
Congratulations, <name>. While your traineeship was strictly honorary, your results were undeniably impressive. The young ones look up to you.

Groundskeeper Wu had this prepared for you. Please, use it as you see fit.

passages.title: How to Save a Life
passages.text:
Gunny is dying from a powerful curse, <name>.

Grand Warlock Nethekurse augments his power with a pair of mystical braziers. If you bring me an ember from that brazier, perhaps it can counteract the dark magic?

passages.title: How to Save a Life
passages.text: Did you bring the ember? We don't have much time!

passages.title: How to Save a Life
passages.text: He was a good soldier.

passages.title: Fel Ember
passages.text:
Caza'rez is dying a coward's death.

Grand Warlock Netherkurse placed a terrible curse upon him. Perhaps if you were to bring me one of the embers from his braziers, we could use it to counteract the magic before it's too late?

passages.title: Fel Ember
passages.text: Did you bring the ember? Caza'rez deserves a warrior's death.

passages.title: Fel Ember
passages.text: I will sing many songs of his glories.

passages.title: Honor the Dying
passages.text:
Their elite warriors are ruthless... so... powerful.

<Caza'rez spits up blood.>

You have to kill them... or we will never defeat Kargath...

passages.title: Honor the Dying
passages.text: Are they dead, <class>?

passages.title: Honor the Dying
passages.text: Caza'rez...is no more.

passages.title: One Last Favor
passages.text:
Ol' Gunny doesn't have much longer...

Do me one last favor, and kill the biggest, meanest fel orcs ye can find.

For old times' sake, aye?

passages.title: One Last Favor
passages.text: Did ye kill 'em?

passages.title: One Last Favor
passages.text: If only we could have saved him.

passages.title: The Will of the Warchief
passages.text:
Kargath was once one of the Horde's greatest heroes.

He now wears the false mantle of Warchief. Bring me his namesake weapon so that we can remember the champion he once was, rather than the monster he's become.

passages.title: The Will of the Warchief
passages.text: Have you proof of Kargath Bladefist's defeat?

passages.title: The Will of the Warchief
passages.text: We should not forget the orc Kargath once was, nor the lessons to be learned from his downfall.

passages.title: Turning the Tide
passages.text:
There is only one true way to end the fel orc threat to Honor Hold and the Alliance.

Their Warchief must be slain.

Bring me his namesake weapon, so that we can always remember his death.

passages.title: Turning the Tide
passages.text: Have you returned with proof of 'Warchief' Kargath Bladefist's demise?

passages.title: Turning the Tide
passages.text:
We have struck a major blow against the enemy with your help.

Honor Hold is far safer than it's been in years.

passages.title: A Very Special Cloth
passages.text:
Warbringer O'mrogg has killed more brave soldiers than any enemy I've ever encountered. He is ruthless, cunning, and extremely powerful.

Take him down and bring me his warcloth so that we may fashion it into a banner and show them the fury of the Horde!

passages.title: A Very Special Cloth
passages.text: Did you bring me the cloth?

passages.title: A Very Special Cloth
passages.text: Well done. This will show those blood crazed monsters what they're up against.

passages.title: O'mrogg's Warcloth
passages.text:
Stormwind wants to see proof of our successes in the war effort.

Rather than showing him body bags, I thought we'd present him the warcloth of O'mrogg, Kargath's fiercest warrior. Think you can handle him?

passages.title: O'mrogg's Warcloth
passages.text: Did you bring me the cloth?

passages.title: O'mrogg's Warcloth
passages.text: My superiors will be very pleased to see this. Thank you.

passages.title: With Great Power, Comes Great Responsibility
passages.text:
<A voice like the sound of light bells rings in your head.>

The Mechanar employs my race's technology to create manacells, objects which provide great amounts of power.

I need you to eliminate Mechano-Lord Capacitus so that Kael'thas' forces cannot harvest that power.

passages.title: With Great Power, Comes Great Responsibility
passages.text: You have done well, <name>. But more work remains to be done.

passages.title: The Calculator
passages.text:
<A gentle wind caresses your face.>

One more task yet remains.

Pathaleon the Calculator oversees many of his master's operations. He is personally responsible for much of the recent torment that has plagued this world.

I ask that you eliminate him.

passages.title: The Calculator
passages.text: You have my gratitude, <name>.

passages.title: Lost Treasure
passages.text:
I sense that one of my kind's artifacts has been taken and stashed away in the Cache of the Legion.

We cannot give them time to discover its power. If you would kill the Gatewatchers and retrieve it for me, I would be most grateful.

passages.title: Lost Treasure
passages.text: You've obtained it, I assume?

passages.title: Lost Treasure
passages.text: You have done well. Any advantage we can take away from Kael'thas' forces is to our benefit.

passages.title: Saving the Botanica
passages.text:
Kael'thas' forces in the Botanica were unsuccessful in handling the numerous creatures contained within. We must take action to right their wrongs.

The first step is to eliminate their forces so that they cannot cause further problems.

passages.title: Saving the Botanica
passages.text: They were going to die to the creatures contained here soon even without our interference. It is for the greater good.

passages.title: The Challenger's Fires
passages.text:
You're strong of mind and strong of will, but you lack the skills to face me in combat. You must fight with your body, but in truth, it is your character that is being tested.

Let us even the playing field.

Take this torch, light it in the brazier next to me, and then use it to light the three unlit braziers around the pool.

passages.title: The Challenger's Fires
passages.text: These fires will give you the strength that you've not yet obtained. They will illuminate your potential.

passages.title: Culling the Herd
passages.text:
It seems that Kael'thas' forces have twisted the Botanica's specimens beyond saving. I do not want to see them unleashed upon Outland as so many others have.

There is one, Laj, who I would like to examine. He is different somehow. Perhaps we can learn from him.

passages.title: Culling the Herd
passages.text: I see you have obtained the frond. Very good.

passages.title: Culling the Herd
passages.text: You have done well thus far, <name>. However, there is still one more task I must ask that you complete.

passages.title: Maul Gormal
passages.text:
Thanks to you, there's a small militia of farmers hiding nearby. Hanae said something about giving them "liquid courage" which, I'm pretty sure, means they're sauced and ANGRY.

The mogu think they can walk all over us - we'll give them a fight that will open their eyes.

Follow the trail through the ruins and down to the beach. Find their leader. When you engage him, we'll be there to back you up.

passages.title: Maul Gormal
passages.text: We are ready to fight the mogu leader whenever you are.

passages.title: Maul Gormal
passages.text: This is extremely unsettling. If mogu are banding together like this all over the continent, it could become a major threat to Pandaria.

passages.title: The Black Morass
passages.text:
The Infinite Dragonflight have abandoned all pretense of subtlety. They plot to destroy the Guardian, Medivh, and prevent the Dark Portal from ever opening. While outwardly, this may appear a boon to the forces of the Alliance, it is in actuality catastrophic and will result in your world ending.

You must venture through the timeway leading to the Black Morass. Go west and then south, past my future self, until you reach the tunnel that houses the swamp specimens. Cross over and speak with Sa'at.

passages.title: The Opening of the Dark Portal
passages.text:
Here the Guardian Medivh feverishly works to open the Dark Portal.

Scattered across the morass, rifts will materialize. Infinite will pour out of the rifts and attempt to destroy Medivh's shields and, ultimately, Medivh.

Kill their rift lords and leaders until Medivh succeeds!

passages.title: The Black Morass
passages.text:
The Infinite Dragonflight have abandoned all pretense of subtlety. They plot to destroy the Guardian, Medivh, and prevent the Dark Portal from ever opening. While outwardly, this may appear a boon to the forces of the Alliance, it is in actuality catastrophic and will result in your world ending.

You must venture through the timeway leading to the Black Morass. Go west and then south, past my future self, until you reach the tunnel that houses the swamp specimens. Cross over and speak with Sa'at.

passages.title: Unbound Darkness
passages.text:
<The sound of chimes enters your head, but it is distressed.>

We imprisoned the most dangerous beings we came across in our travels.

Zereketh is a powerful void lord. If he escapes into Netherstorm, he will feed off of the abundant void energy.

passages.title: Unbound Darkness
passages.text: Creatures of the void are naturally chaotic. They are a necessary part of the universe, but they must be kept in check by the Light.

passages.title: Hey There Dalliah
passages.text:
Two powerful agents of the Burning Legion, Wrath-Scryer Soccothrates and Dalliah the Doomsayer, have begun rallying the demons on board together into a small army.

You cannot let their forces grow any larger, or the Arcatraz may soon become yet another Legion stronghold.

passages.title: Hey There Dalliah
passages.text: The Legion seeks only to consume. They hold no regard for the balance.

passages.title: Finding an Old Friend
passages.text:
It seems Shu, the spirit of water, had a play companion when he came to the pools throughout the years. An old pandaren we know as Old Man Liang.

Liang moved away from the main town and stopped practicing in the pools some time ago. I am told he lives in a small house northeast of here, up the hill.

Liang may know what has driven Shu away, and where the spirit might be found.

Go to Liang. Ask of Shu.

passages.title: Finding an Old Friend
passages.text: Visitors are rare up here, but you are welcome. It is nice to meet you, young <class>.

passages.title: The Source of Our Livelihood
passages.text:
We have done as Master Shang asked of us. I will return to the temple to inform the master of our progress. You should continue south on the road to the farmlands to seek out Wugou, the spirit of earth.

Ji awaits you at the Dai-Lo Farmstead, and he'll surely need your help. I must warn you, Ji can be reckless in his directness. Remember well the things I have taught you: discipline and patience.

passages.title: The Source of Our Livelihood
passages.text:
<name>! I wondered when I would see you again!

Well, the plus side is that finding Wugou, the spirit of earth, was easy enough. Waking him... not so much. I think he's going to wake quite sore from all the pushing and hitting I've done trying to rouse him.

passages.title: Maximum Security Breakout
passages.text:
Harbinger Skyriss is the heart of the problem in the Arcatraz.

He corrupted Warden Mellichar and made him release many of the prisoners. It is only a matter of time before the Harbinger himself is let loose.

<name>, you cannot let a servant of the Old Gods live!

passages.title: Maximum Security Breakout
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. Your actions this day have prevented countless tragedies.

passages.title: Magisters' Terrace
passages.text:
We recently sent in an expeditionary force to the Magisters' Terrace to stop the Legion forces there.

However, we haven't heard from them since, and I fear the worst.

Will you go there and try to find Exarch Larethor? He's in charge of the expedition.

passages.title: Magisters' Terrace
passages.text:
Dawnhearth thought we were dead? Hah!

I haven't sent a report because we haven't made any progress past this point.

Perhaps you can help us change that?

passages.title: The Scryer's Scryer
passages.text:
<Tyrith winces in pain as he speaks.>

Go to the terrace... use the orb.

...They're...feeding the sunwell....

 <Tyrith gasps for breath.>

Hurry... They must be stopped... before they can....

<Tyrith dies.>

passages.title: Severed Communications
passages.text:
We've had a contact embedded in Magisters' Terrace gathering intelligence for us for some time now, but we've lost contact with him.

The information he was collecting is vital to our mission.

passages.title: Severed Communications
passages.text: ...Come closer, <race>... Listen carefully to my words....

passages.title: Hard to Kill
passages.text:
As you've now witnessed, the Legion forces work tirelessly, manipulating the Sunwell's power to achieve their malevolent ends.

Kael'thas has risen from the ashes of defeat and once more leads them in their efforts. He must be stopped.

passages.title: Hard to Kill
passages.text: Well, <class>, I must admit, I wasn't sure I'd see you again.

passages.title: Hard to Kill
passages.text:
<Larethor listens intently as you explain your deeds in Magisters' Terrace.>

Tyrith will be missed - good man, that one. Thanks to you though, his death wasn't in vain.

passages.title: A Radical Notion
passages.text:
We cannot afford to lose this war. I'd like to empower our sentries so that brave men and women don't have to die.

The Legion has gotten a hold of a powerful elemental being. Its essence could be just what we need.

passages.title: A Radical Notion
passages.text: Were you able to get your hands on its essence?

passages.title: A Radical Notion
passages.text: Excellent! I can't wait to present this project to my superiors!

passages.title: Twisted Associations
passages.text:
The Legion and Kael'thas' forces are becoming increasingly intertwined. This concerns me very deeply.

From what we can gather Selin Fireheart and Priestess Delrissa work closely together to unite the two armies. You need to stop them.

passages.title: Twisted Associations
passages.text: Well done, soldier. One step at a time.

passages.title: Advancing the Campaign
passages.text:
I mostly listen, <class>. I listen so that the Warchief doesn't have to.

I've heard of the status of our campaign against the Hellfire Citadel. It is time to take the Shattered Halls, seat of power for the fel orcs.

Go speak with Stone Guard Stok'ton, he's in charge there.

passages.title: Advancing the Campaign
passages.text: Keep your head down, or it's likely to end up on the wrong end of an arrow.

passages.title: Advancing the Campaign
passages.text:
The time has come to lay the final blow against the fel orcs.

Advance Scout Chadwick awaits your presence inside the Shattered Halls of Hellfire Citadel. Make haste, their forces could strike against Honor Hold at any moment!

passages.title: Advancing the Campaign
passages.text: Be quiet! We'll surely be overwhelmed if they notice us now.

passages.title: Bring Me A Shrubbery!
passages.text:
My people use sanguine hibiscus for a number of purposes.

It grows naturally only in the Underbog, and many of the bog's denizens have taken a liking to it.

If you could bring me some, I would be very grateful.

passages.title: Bring Me A Shrubbery!
passages.text: Were you able to gather any hibiscus?

passages.title: Bring Me A Shrubbery!
passages.text: These will do nicely, but we can always use more.  Perhaps you will find yourself in the Underbog again soon?

passages.title: Regroup!
passages.text:
They have an airbase! I have underestimated this Alliance Captain for the last time. So many good warriors lost...

There must have been a few survivors who were able to bail during the crash. We need every able-bodied fighter we can get.

Find as many survivors as you can in the forest below, and I will investigate the wreckage itself. Rally everyone together at the nearby village for a counter-attack.

passages.title: Regroup!
passages.text: Did you find any survivors?

passages.title: Regroup!
passages.text:
These are the only survivors, <name>?

So be it. We will play the hand fate has dealt us.

Numbers be damned. This is where heroes are made.

passages.title: Invasion of the Bottle Snatchers
passages.text:
As if the hozu weren't enough now we have a bunch of renegade dwarven brewmaster wannabes floating around.

 Can you please recover the brewskies they stole? It would cripple the Ironforge economy if this many "entrepreneurs" started popping up.

passages.title: Down Kitty!
passages.text:
I tried to fight one of the jade tigers in the woods but they were too scary. They stare at you and you turn to a jade statue!

Honest truth! Chen's sister's friend Ni heard it from Kai's mom.

I want to be brave like you though. Can you show me how to beat up those jade tigers?

passages.title: Down Kitty!
passages.text: Wow! You are tough!

passages.title: Down Kitty!
passages.text: Wow! You were awesome! You were like *bam* and they were like *aaaaa* and then they were smashed!

passages.title: Sixteen Fluid Ounces of Prevention
passages.text:
Better safe than sorry.

The pillars of smoke surrounding the crash site will be a beacon to any Alliance who might have seen your Zeppelin in distress.

Until you and your depleted crew get your bearings, you could do without that kind of trouble.

Extinguishing the wreckage fires is just plain common sense.

passages.title: An Offering
passages.text:
Well young one, if you would do me a kindness before I help. 

Behind my hut is a small pond. I keep a stock of very rare fish that I need for ritual. It was a favorite of my late husband.

Could you please bring me one?

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Take No Prisoners
passages.text: The final leg of our journey took us west, to a large hozen village. We set up a small camp in the mountains, outside of their line of sight...

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Take No Prisoners
passages.text: Please, allow me to finish.

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Take No Prisoners
passages.text:
So there you have it. We didn't find the White Pawn, but we came back with intel that could be of even greater importance to the Alliance.

The Horde have allied with the hozen, and are arming them as we speak. They and their monkey army now outnumber us thirty to one.

passages.title: Explosive Evidence
passages.text:
I must ask you to do one more thing for me, <name>.

The personal effects on this ship cannot be left for others to find. We'll have to destroy it.

I cobbled together some Makeshift Dynamite from the scraps you brought me.

Place the dynamite anywhere on the ship, but take care not to put them too close together.

They might be...uh...a little unwieldy, so you should spread them out in case of premature detonation.

passages.title: What Goes Down, Must Come Up!
passages.text:
Rivett left behind what looks to be an important piece of equipment. Along its shaft you are able to make out the words: Goblin Drone Dispenser.

With a simple calibration, the device is set to deliver drones to Nazgrim's basecamp.

Easy enough....

There's just one problem. The only supply crates worth transporting have fallen to the cliff ledge below the crash impact.

As you ponder the issue, you see the long, coiled tail of a Cliff Glider fly by the corner of your eye...

passages.title: An Urgent Plea
passages.text:
<Your mind is racked with a howl. Beneath it, a wispy voice is barely audible, as if from far away.>

Please... help... heart of the ruins... a ritual... conjuring...

...should not be here...

My staff... on the altar... take it. Please hurry.

passages.title: An Urgent Plea
passages.text:
Spirit-binding! How can the mogu have been allowed to resume such a disgusting practice?! And now here I am, the product of a half-failed conjuring...

<The spirit fumes for a moment, then turns to you.>

What century is this?

passages.title: An Urgent Plea
passages.text:
Allow me to introduce myself: I am Pei-Zhi, Master Spiritsage under the last pandaren emperor Shaohao.

At least... I was.

passages.title: Vessels of the Spirit
passages.text:
The Spiritclaws are a sect of mogu assassin-priests who, at the height of the mogu empire, were the most elite and most feared of the emperor's troops.

All have mastered a deathblow which ensnares the spirit of the enemy, trapping it in a jade bottle for delivery to a Spiritbinder.

If you encounter any Spiritclaws further ahead in the ruins, take note: their belts hang with a cursed weight.

Relieve them of their burden and bring the bottles back to me.

passages.title: Vessels of the Spirit
passages.text:
To think the mogu have continued training the Spiritclaws for all these years...

Did you get the bottles?

passages.title: Vessels of the Spirit
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>.

I can already sense the spirits within these bottles - they cry out with fear, confusion... rage.

passages.title: Ritual Artifacts
passages.text:
So many spirits held in captivity here... I can feel them everywhere. Even the walls are a cage for the long-dead.

<name>, we cannot simply break the sorcery over this place - doing so would release countless agonized souls to wander the earth. They will need a beacon, something to guide them.

With your help, I can create a tan-chao: a bridge from this world to the heavens. For this ritual, I'll need a bowl, a candle, and a jade cong. You should be able to find them all within the ruins.

passages.title: Ritual Artifacts
passages.text: Have you found the items we need for the ritual? We cannot guide these spirits back without them.

passages.title: Ritual Artifacts
passages.text: Good work. With these, I can complete the ritual to send all of the spirits here--including myself--back where they belong.

passages.title: The Wayward Dead
passages.text:
The process of mass conjuring, as the mogu are doing here, is not without byproduct. Some spirits arrive too distraught or unruly to be harnessed, so they are confined and left to wander until their desperation leaves them more malleable.

I suspect the mogu have such a holding area somewhere nearby, likely guarded by spiritclaws.

Please, take my staff again and use it to collect these wayward spirits. You needn't fight them - present the staff and they should be drawn in.

passages.title: The Wayward Dead
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. I will take them with me into the nether.

passages.title: Back to Nature
passages.text:
I'm afraid I have another favor to ask, <name>.

The bottles you recovered contain neither the spirits of mogu ancestors nor recently slain foes; they contain spirits of beasts. It seems the spiritclaws have resorted to poaching in an effort to fuel their simulacra.

This complicates our task, for I cannot take the beasts with me through the bridge.

Take the bottles west to Tideview Thicket and smash them to return the spirits to nature. Some may be blind with rage and will need to be subdued.

passages.title: Back to Nature
passages.text: Do not fear for the spirits of the beasts - they will find peace here.

passages.title: Back to Nature
passages.text: Their bodies had long since returned to the land - their spirits can now follow.

passages.title: Pei-Back
passages.text:
<Ancestral spirits stream into the tan-chao, Pei-Zhi's bridge to freedom.

One final chamber lingers in the ruins, just north of the tan-chao. The air above crackles with foul energy. Shan Jitong is already at work.>

passages.title: Pei-Back
passages.text:
This age must be one of great strife to breed heroes such as you. I can only imagine what adventures must lie ahead.

It has been my great honor to have met you, <name>.

I will remain here to usher out the last of the spirits before crossing the tan-chao myself.

Still, I am disturbed by the spirit waker's dying curse...

"You will not stop the thunder."

What could he have meant?

passages.title: Bottletoads
passages.text:
Have you heard about the crisis we're having at the pools?

Toads have moved in and are spawning like crazy! It's become a real problem for the lotus farmers.

Coincidentally, I make a jam out of gelatinous toadspawn. I call it "Bottletoads" and it's a big hit with the kids around here. Can't keep any in stock.

If you're heading to the pools, you'd be doing everyone a favor by uh... liberating some of those toad eggs.

Into this bottle. For me.

Just look for bubbles and scoop right in!

passages.title: Bottletoads
passages.text:
"It just ain't a party without Bottletoads!"

Hmm... no, that doesn't work.

"Bottletoads: not as gross as they sound!"

passages.title: Bottletoads
passages.text: Now when the kids ask: "Do you have Bottletoads?" I can say YES!

passages.title: Family Heirlooms
passages.text:
We recently lost a fierce battle against the hozen at Moonwater Retreat.

We evacuated as many of our people as we could, but still, there were many we could not save.

We have no tokens of our lost over which to send our prayers.

If someone could go and retrieve heirlooms from the dead bodies, we could properly lay them to rest, and move on.

It would mean so much to us if you could do this, <name>.

passages.title: Family Heirlooms
passages.text: We still grieve for our fallen brothers.

passages.title: Family Heirlooms
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. You do not know how much this means to the families of the lost.

passages.title: Stealing Their Thunder
passages.text:
The vrykul are fearless in a fight. Seems they actually yearn fer a death in battle. With their numbers and that ferocity, we're doomed - plain and simple.

There's one they esteem though, goes by the name of Ingvar. Bring him down and you'll deal a mighty blow to their spirit.

passages.title: Stealing Their Thunder
passages.text:
Good to see you're well, <name>.

We've had about as many casualties as we can handle.

passages.title: Stealing Their Thunder
passages.text:
Outstanding!

This could be the turn of luck we've all been hoping for.

passages.title: Disarmament
passages.text:
Take it from me, <lad/lass>, them vrykul weapons be downright nasty! Deceptively well-balanced, wickedly sharp - just plain deadly.

I need you to pilfer some o' them weapons before they're used on us!

passages.title: Disarmament
passages.text: You pinch a load a' them vrykul axes?

passages.title: Disarmament
passages.text:
<Mordun whistles.>

Will ya just look at 'em? Incredible.

I half expected these neanderthals to be swingin' around clubs and throwin' rock.

No such luck...

passages.title: Cryin' My Eyes Out
passages.text:
I coulda taken out da whole lot of 'em, mon.

Shot 'em one by one, den played dead when dey be gettin' close. Fell for it every time, dey did - well almost every time...

One of 'em finally got wise. Called my bluff. Before I knew it, dey was usin' my eyes as marbles.

Ran off with my goods an' left me here ta die, da savages...

Help me, mon. Lemme die wit my dignity intact.

passages.title: Cryin' My Eyes Out
passages.text: You got me goods, mon?

passages.title: Cryin' My Eyes Out
passages.text:
<Zin'Jun sobs...you think.>

Dey done killed Snuff...

What'd 'ol Snuff ever do ta dem?

passages.title: Missing Mallet
passages.text:
<name>, I've got it! It's simple really. Let's make a ruckus so loud that there's no way he can sleep through it.

Why look at that, a conveniently placed gong! Makes me think this may just be how they've awoken him in the past. We just need the matching mallet to get it ringing as loud as possible.

The village leader tells me the mallet is over at the Ki-Han Brewery on the river, to the southwest. It's not far. Mind picking it up for me while I give the village some fair warning?

passages.title: Missing Mallet
passages.text: Well, they're as warned as they're going to get. Do you have the mallet?

passages.title: Missing Mallet
passages.text: Hah, <name>! Now that's a mallet if I've ever seen one! Let's make some noise.

passages.title: Still Good!
passages.text:
The virmen to the south have been running off with all of our crops, but they're taking more than they can eat. They must be stockpiling them somewhere - the ones they like anyway.

Will you go out and recover any of the uprooted crops you can find? I've got an island's worth of people to feed, and every single vegetable makes a difference.

passages.title: Still Good!
passages.text: Ever since Wugou. the spirit of earth, fell asleep, the dirt is drying out and it's getting harder and harder to get new seeds to sprout. We need to hold on to any food we can, or the island will have hard times ahead.

passages.title: Still Good!
passages.text:
Some of these have mouth-sized chunks bitten out of them! Ah well, we can still make use.

Thank you for your help, friend.

passages.title: Not In the Face!
passages.text:
Alright <name>, I was thinking about what we'd try next if the whole gong thing didn't work, and it came to me just like that! Water in the face always worked on me. It's got to be twice as effective for someone so dry and earthy!

Mind going over and asking Shu, the spirit of water, if he'll help us out? He should be playing in the pool next to the waterfall, just on the other side of that tree.

passages.title: Not In the Face!
passages.text: YEAH!!! <name>, we make quite a team. Persistence over planning, I always say!

passages.title: The Spirit and Body of Shen-zin Su
passages.text:
Well, that wraps it up here, doesn't it <name>? Now that we've got these two roused and all friendly towards you, we just need to get them back to the Temple of Five Dawns.

You go ahead. I'm going to say my goodbyes, then I'll follow you up shortly.

passages.title: The Spirit and Body of Shen-zin Su
passages.text: You have done well, young student. Three of the four spirits have been returned to the temple. We are closer to the answers we seek.

passages.title: Stronger Than Bone
passages.text:
This giant jade tiger pillar doesn't seem to fit in amidst the hozen buildings.

What it does seem is very hard. Very solid.

You know just the person to bring this to.

passages.title: Stronger Than Bone
passages.text: GOOD! A true challenge. Let us put this pillar to the test!

passages.title: Balanced Perspective
passages.text:
Aysa has been meditating on the lake since we've arrived, all her thoughts focused on Dafeng. I don't know what she hopes to discover out there, but she's no fool, and Master Shang Xi has entrusted this task with her.

You will need to cross the ropes leading from the end of the dock to reach her. It shall test your balance, but I think you're up to the task, <name>.

passages.title: Balanced Perspective
passages.text: I'm impressed. Most students that are even capable of reaching this spot do so soaking wet.

passages.title: Dafeng, the Spirit of Air
passages.text:
If you listen long enough, the wind will carry the answer to you.

Dafeng, the spirit of air, has been scared from the skies by Zhao-Ren, the Onyx Serpent. He hides within the Chamber of Whispers, at the south side of the plateau.

Go to him. Ji and I will join you there.

passages.title: Dafeng, the Spirit of Air
passages.text: Dafeng looks frightened as you approach, but settles a bit at the sound of your voice.

passages.title: Battle for the Skies
passages.text:
Dafeng, the spirit of air, is terrified by Zhao-Ren, the Onyx Serpent. We must help him face that fear, or face it for him ourselves.

When I told Ji of the serpent, he said he had an idea and would begin preparations outside of the chamber. Despite his rash nature, I must admit, I envy his passion and conviction.

Let us go outside and confront the Onyx Serpent.

passages.title: Battle for the Skies
passages.text: You have helped Dafeng, the spirit of air, find his courage! The final spirit has been restored.

passages.title: Urgent News
passages.text: I'm sure Aysa won't love this plan, but it's the only plan we've got. Would you mind being the bearer of bad news for me, <name>? She needs to know what we're doing so she can get everyone to safety.

passages.title: Urgent News
passages.text: Your friend is out fighting to save my crew. Fiercely I might add. I'm afraid your message may have to wait.

passages.title: The Healing of Shen-zin Su
passages.text:
This is more horrific than I imagined, but we can handle this. We need to gather the healers and close the wound. We need to save Shen-zin Su.

Find any healers you can! Rescue them, relieve them - whatever you need to do to get them over here healing the wound.

Keep the healers safe at all costs!

passages.title: The Healing of Shen-zin Su
passages.text: We need to get the healers to the wound and keep them safe!

passages.title: The Healing of Shen-zin Su
passages.text:
You are a sight to see when under pressure, <name>! We wouldn't have stood a chance without you.

I think it's working. The flow of blood is slowing. I knew it would work!

passages.title: New Allies
passages.text:
<name>, I did what had to be done. And the plan worked. Things could have been much worse had we not acted. I only wish Aysa could understand that.

There will be plenty of time for reflection, but for now, we need to return to the Temple of Five Dawns. We need to let them know that Shen-zin Su has been saved, and we need to sort out the fates of these new allies.

passages.title: New Allies
passages.text:
It is good to see you again, <name>. You've done all that I've asked of you and more... you have saved Shen-zin Su.

You make an old master proud.

passages.title: Proving Your Worth
passages.text:
Hello, <name>! You've earned a reputation among the flight as having - shall we say - 'nimble fingers.'

We need someone of your skills for a matter of utmost delicacy. Before I reveal more, we need to know you're the right <man/woman> for the job.

When the course of battle takes you to the Eye of Eternity, I need you to pickpocket Hagara the Stormbinder to retrieve a cryptomancer's decoder ring. Are you up to the task?

passages.title: Proving Your Worth
passages.text:
Have you completed our task?

These artifacts are crafted such that they dissolve if their bearer is killed, so only a skilled thief can acquire them.

passages.title: Proving Your Worth
passages.text:
You've found one! You're a credit to your race, <name>.

Rings like these are capable of decoding even the most complicated of ciphers. Unfortunately, the ring is inert until it is charged...

passages.title: A Hidden Message
passages.text:
Corastrasza, currently stationed at the Vermillion Redoubt in the Twilight Highlands, has intercepted a coded message of grave importance. I'll let her explain the full situation, but we need your expertise to unravel the cipher!

Take your decoder ring to an ethereal thaumaturge in your capital city - he should know how to charge it. Acquire the encoded cipher from Corastrasza and use the ring to decode it for her. Hurry! Time is ticking...

passages.title: A Hidden Message
passages.text:
I was hoping Lord Afrasastrasz would find us a competent <class>.

What have you got for us, <name>? Do you have a means of decrypting the message?

passages.title: A Hidden Message
passages.text:
What's this about? "Ravenholdt Manor?" I thought that was just a motley band of thieves up in the Hillsbrad Foothills.

What would they want with a dragon egg? More importantly, how did they find out about it?

We're going to need some answers, <name>!

passages.title: Ears of the Lich King
passages.text:
Prince Keleseth acts as Arthas' eyes and ears in the Fjord.

I don't like that one bit!

Go and give him a round o' pain. You'll be doing the world a favor by doing so.

passages.title: Ears of the Lich King
passages.text:
I bet the pale whelp felt that!

That's one more step towards yer judgment day, Arthas!

passages.title: Seein' Red
passages.text:
I was just about ta curl up an' die, mon.

Now, dis!

Snuff an' me go way back. Oh, da memories...

No way I can face Snuff in da afterlife without avengin' his death first, mon!

Dese hooligans be led by one named Konk. We gotta sniff him out an' den snuff him out - for Snuff!

passages.title: Seein' Red
passages.text:
Zin'jun is lost?

This is a dark day indeed, brother. These vermin will pay!

passages.title: Death to the Traitor King
passages.text:
Anub'arak, the traitor king, makes his home in the once proud Kingdom of Azjol-Nerub.

He has twisted and perverted our homeland into the wretched squalor it is today. He rules over an army of undead nerubians who have pledged themselves to serving the Lich King.

Bring an end to his reign.

passages.title: Death to the Traitor King
passages.text: Is it done, <class>? Has the traitor king finally met his end?

passages.title: Death to the Traitor King
passages.text:
<A fierce glow emanantes from all of Azak's eyes as he stares at the husk.>

It is DONE!

Your name shall be recorded in the extensive history of our people, <race>!

passages.title: Don't Forget the Eggs!
passages.text:
Throughout Azjol-Nerub, the scourged nerubians carefully nurture eggs that will soon hatch, providing them nerubian young to slaughter and raise.

The eggs have been tainted with foul magics. Our only recourse is to dispose of them.

passages.title: Don't Forget the Eggs!
passages.text:
Do not worry, <race>.

The eggs they found were but a fraction of our hidden stores within Azjol-Nerub.

Our mighty kingdom shall be reborn.

passages.title: The Faceless Ones
passages.text:
In my peoples' struggle against the forces of the undead, they dug deeper as they lost ground. In desperation, they dug too deep.

We inadvertently exposed a tendril of the old god's will, which was made manifest in the creatures known only as the Faceless.

In the end, we could not fight on two fronts against such powerful enemies. Our misfortune cost us the war against the undead, and ultimately, our home.

Enter Ahn'kahet, <class>, and cleanse our former home of these Faceless atrocities.

passages.title: The Gatewatcher's Talisman
passages.text:
Krik'thir, guardian of the gates to Azjol-Nerub, was not a traitor.

He fell in the War of the Spider defending our home from the Scourge.

As per his station, he was in possession of the key to the hidden empire. I'd like you to retrieve it so it may be returned to its people.

passages.title: The Gatewatcher's Talisman
passages.text: Has Krik'thir's spirit been released from the curse of undeath? What of the talisman?

passages.title: The Gatewatcher's Talisman
passages.text:
Just as I suspected.

Most of the empire has remained closed off since Krik'thir's final stand. Perhaps my people have already secured the depths and merely await release? Perhaps the faceless ones fester behind closed doors.

Only time will tell. The exposed upper reaches of Azjol-Nerub must first be cleansed of Arthas' taint.

passages.title: Get a Sample
passages.text:
It is time the Mad Brewer got a taste of his own poison.

To the east are a number of pandaren who attended a near fatal "tasting" session of Shadowpour's.

Can you head into the valley and see if they have any samples left of what they taste tested last night. If you get enough samples I can try to recreate his concoction.

Give the samples to my friend Jian. He should be able to modify them a bit.

Oh, and be careful. It would appear his beverage had some hateful side effects.

passages.title: Fix the Flavor
passages.text:
These orchids you gathered might help us fix the larger issue.

In the valley east of here is the lake Brewmaster Shadowpour contaminated. Travel there and toss these herbs in the water to draw out the contamination so you can defeat it. 

Speak to my friend Jian when you are done. He's a friendly water sprite that has helped the brewmaster and myself make a number of recipes.

passages.title: Lay of the Land
passages.text:
Curse these furry pests! Kill one, and two more rise in its place...

Nothing has changed, <name>. Orders are orders, no matter how few of us stand and regardless of the odds.

I have plans to make and problems to solve.

I want you to get out there and learn the lay of the land. Don't return until you have something useful to report.

And silence that yammering fool while you're out there!

Dismissed!

passages.title: Lay of the Land
passages.text:
Welcome, traveler.

Please, make yourself comfortable.

passages.title: Scouting Report: Like Jinyu in a Barrel
passages.text:
With our leader turned to jade, our hozen guide disappeared, and a prisoner of war in tow, there was only one thing that Kiryn and I could do:

March into our enemy's territory and deliver some vengeance.

Want to know how it went?

passages.title: Scouting Report: Like Jinyu in a Barrel
passages.text: I'm not quite done yet, <name>.

passages.title: Scouting Report: Like Jinyu in a Barrel
passages.text:
The most important thing we learned was that... not only have the Alliance befriended the jinyu, but they're giving them weapons, and teaching them how to use them.

The Alliance now control a force that outnumbers us thirty-to-one. And we - the HORDE - have befriended monkeys.

passages.title: Pupil No More
passages.text:
I once called Elder Nadox my teacher.

That changed forever when I was forced to watch him mercilessly slaughter my friends and family as a servant of the damned.

Find him within the depths and make him pay for his crimes, <race>.

passages.title: Pupil No More
passages.text: Is the mighty Nadox dead for good?

passages.title: Pupil No More
passages.text:
With Nadox gone, I hope to take his place as a leader of my people.

The Empire of Azjol-Nerub is destined for greatness, <race>...

passages.title: Reclaiming Ahn'Kahet
passages.text:
Prince Taldaram and his army of Scourge use the same wards we once used to hide our empire to keep themselves safe from the native denizens of the icy depths.

Deactivate the wards and slaughter the Scourge guarding them. My forces will help the natives slaughter the rest.

passages.title: Reclaiming Ahn'Kahet
passages.text: Much work remains to be done in Ahn'Kahet, even long after the Scourge are defeated.

passages.title: Reclaiming Ahn'Kahet
passages.text:
Excellent.

<You heard a series of clicking sounds.>

Now to vanquish our other foe.

passages.title: Acid Rain
passages.text:
Since you've been gone, more and more of these creatures are approaching our camp. They appear to be amassing for a major assault!

We're going to have to take some drastic measures if we hope to see tomorrow.

Here, take my poisoned throwing stars and figure out a way to thin out their numbers.

passages.title: Acid Rain
passages.text: Well, <name>? Do we live to see another day?

passages.title: Acid Rain
passages.text:
Excellent! What a creative solution!

That should hold them off for a while.

passages.title: What the Scourge Dred
passages.text:
One of the fleeing Drakkari trolls told me of a great raptor king, Dred, that was immune to the plague.

If you could find King Dred and bring me one of his teeth, perhaps I could fashion it into a weapon.

passages.title: What the Scourge Dred
passages.text: Does the great beast exist?

passages.title: What the Scourge Dred
passages.text:
<Kurzel's eyes open wide.>

Wow! That's enormous!

passages.title: Discretion is Key
passages.text:
Listen to me, <race>.

It's just been brought to my attention that there's been an incident at the Violet Hold. It would appear that the blues are launching a full scale invasion of Dalaran!

I need you to get to the prison and speak with Lieutenant Sinclari at once. She'll give you the details.

That is not all. I need this handled with utmost discretion. We mustn't alarm the citizens of Dalaran if it can possibly be avoided. Do I make myself clear?

Very well. Now, go!

passages.title: Discretion is Key
passages.text:
Not a moment too soon.

Are you prepared to defend Dalaran, <class>?

passages.title: Containment
passages.text:
My forces are in absolute shambles, and Malygos' assailants just keep coming.

I fear that the worst has yet to come.

You must engage them until their leader, Cyanigosa, comes. Only her death will stop the invasion and save Dalaran.

Speak to me again when you are ready.

passages.title: Containment
passages.text: Is it over? Were you able to withstand the assault?

passages.title: Containment
passages.text:
Thank you, hero!

Dalaran is safe for another day because of your bravery.

passages.title: DEPRECATED: Terror on the High Seas
passages.text:
Word has reached Stormwind of terrible crimes committed against ships carrying Alliance citizens. The Horde stands accused of stopping Alliance ships, boarding them, mistreating passengers, and stealing cargo.

Heroes of the Alliance, your help is needed to determine the truth of these allegations! Seek out Grand Admiral Jes-Tereth at Stormwind Keep if you would answer the call.

passages.title: DEPRECATED: Gathering Evidence
passages.text:
A ship called the Bravery routinely ferries passengers and cargo from Stormwind port to Rut'theran Village, right outside Darnassus.

Well, the ship has just returned with distressing news. Both passengers and crew say that Horde vessels stopped and boarded the Bravery in the waters off Teldrassil, mistreated those on board, and stole some of the cargo before turning the ship around.

We have to find out what happened, <name>. Would you go to Stormwind Harbor and listen to the stories of the passengers?

passages.title: Gal'darah Must Pay
passages.text:
It musta been da most awful thing I ever seen. Da great Akali - slain right before my eyes. Horrible...

My job be to observe only. But dis cannot stand! Gal'darah and his followers must pay!

Avenge Akali's death, mon. It be da right thing ta do.

passages.title: Gal'darah Must Pay
passages.text: Has Akali's death been avenged, <race>?

passages.title: Gal'darah Must Pay
passages.text:
Ya done it?! Dey be no more?

Here ya go, mon. Take dis gift for bringin' justice to da frozen wastes.

passages.title: Gal'darah Must Pay
passages.text:
Da mighty Akali has been slain, <race>.

My role in life be to record, not fight. But dis cannot stand! Gal'darah and his followers must pay!

Avenge Akali's death, mon. It be da right thing ta do.

passages.title: Gal'darah Must Pay
passages.text:
Ya really did it?

You surpassed my expectations, mon. Take dis gift for bringin' justice to da frozen wastes.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text:
At first glance, it be lookin' like da same old story here - trolls tappin' into forbidden powah by destroyin' da very beings dey should be worshippin'.

If what I learned be true, den dey have a special golem - one like nuthin' created before!

Bring me back a piece from dat golem ta study.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text: You get me a piece of dat golem, mon?

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text:
Ahh, yeah mon! Dat be what I'm lookin' for.

Here ya go - take somethin' nice for your troubles.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text:
Dis whole mess coulda been avoided if da Drakkari had worshipped da gods instead of destroyin' dem.

I heard dat dey have a special golem - one imbued with forbidden powah.

Bring me back a piece from dat golem so we can learn from our bruddas and sistahs.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text: You find da golem? I'm sure it's in there somewhere.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text:
Amazin'! Dis be like nothing I've ever seer before.

Good work, mon.

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text:
Gundrak looks doomed. You know dis to be true.

If you be havin' the courage, search for history tablets to see what brought the Drakkari Empire to such an end.

Perhaps one day we be bringin' dem back to der former glory.

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text: You find da Drakkari history tablets, mon?

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text:
You be havin' my thanks, mon.

These will be very useful to us, I'm sure of it.

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text:
Da land of da ice trolls is a shadow of its former glory.

If you be havin' the courage, search for history tablets to see what brought the Drakkari Empire to such an end.

Perhaps one day we be givin' dis land back to a new line of frost trolls.

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text: You find da Drakkari history tablets, mon?

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text:
We trolls been subject to da splittin' of empires for longer than some races been existin'.

We always regrow from da ruins.

passages.title: DEPRECATED: The Merchants' Plight
passages.text:
If King Wrynn thinks that the attack on the Bravery is an isolated incident, he's mistaken.

Look around the harbor and you'll see all the angry merchants who can't get their goods or money to Kalimdor. Perhaps the king will listen to their voices if he won't heed mine alone.

Go talk to them, <name>. Hear their grievances and gather their petitions before you return to Stormwind Keep.

passages.title: DEPRECATED: Captain Rufus Hardwick
passages.text:
The Gilnean captain, Rufus Hardwick, would serve our cause well.

The usual promises of plunder and booty might sway his crew, but to secure the good captain's help, we'll need to offer our assistance with a more delicate matter.

Find an alchemist's shop and purchase a supply of diluted lime sulfur, extract of dogwood, and a soothing shampoo. Bring these items to the captain, but do nothing that will embarrass him.

The fleet is depending on you.

passages.title: To Catch a Thief
passages.text:
Just beyond this cave lies Ravenholdt Manor. You need to get inside without being seen!

<Mostrasz places an enchantment on you.>

There - now I'll be able to keep an eye on you and communicate as you venture into the compound. Now sneak into that manor, locate the egg, and don't get caught...

passages.title: To Catch a Thief
passages.text:
So, you will join with me?

Good. Very good.

passages.title: The Forlorn Watcher
passages.text:
I would gladly give my life for the Makers or their creations.

However, since Loken's betrayal it seems all of Ulduar has turned on the world. One in particular, the Maiden of Grief, seems to reel in agony at her new orders.

Please lay her to rest and bring me one of her tears.

passages.title: The Forlorn Watcher
passages.text: I wish there were another way, but it seems death is the maiden's only salvation now.

passages.title: The Forlorn Watcher
passages.text:
<Kaldir stares into the crystal in silence for a moment.>

No being has ever felt such sincere sorrow as the Maiden of Grief has.

Let us remember her spirit as we continue our efforts against Loken.

passages.title: DEPRECATED: Gunner Blastbarrel
passages.text:
The second ship we'll want is captained by one of the best dwarves ever to to man a cannon, Ardan Blastbarrel. If there's anyone who can blow Horde ships out of the water, it'll be him and his crew.

You'll find Blastbarrel in the Military Ward of Ironforge. Speak with him and see if you can convince him to commit his crew to our cause.

passages.title: Corrupt Constructs
passages.text:
The iron dwarves are busy at work carving out massive stone constructs that I fear will soon be used as powerful weapons.

You must defeat their overseer, Krystallus, and the dark rune giants already walking the halls before it is too late!

passages.title: Corrupt Constructs
passages.text:
Well done, <race>.

Every weapon we can take away from Loken is a great boon to our own war effort.

passages.title: Champion of the Tournament
passages.text:
With this tournament we grow ever closer to our final confrontation with the Lich King.

<name>, fight with valor and honor. Every fighter here has gathered for the common good.

Together, we will stop Arthas!

passages.title: DEPRECATED: They Call Him Swifthands
passages.text:
The third privateer we should hire for the fleet will be "Swifthands" Sutton, a notoriously fierce fighter in close combat. Where Blastbarrel loves his cannons, Captain Sutton prefers to close in for the kill.

You'll find Sutton hanging around in Stormwind Harbor, looking for work. Be warned, he'll probably set some sort of task for you before he agrees to join us.

passages.title: Champion of the King
passages.text:
With this tournament we grow ever closer to our final confrontation with the Lich King.

<name>, you are to represent the Alliance in this grand arena.

Prove yourself against Azeroth's finest. Go forward with honor.

passages.title: DEPRECATED: Where Are Those Ships?
passages.text:
With most of our fleet leading the attack on Theramore and engaging the enemy elsewhere, we're going to need more ships to complete our blockade of Kalimdor.

The warchief ordered the shipwrights at Zoram'gar Outpost in Ashenvale to work overtime to meet the demand, but none of the new craft have arrived yet.

Travel there and put the question to their overseer. Tell them the warchief wants his ships!

passages.title: Diametrically Opposed
passages.text:
I shall speak plainly to you, little <race>. My people have not been the same since our ties with Thorim were severed.

Volkhan will not rest until either he, or we, are no more. We only want peace, but it seems we have no choice but war.

passages.title: Diametrically Opposed
passages.text:
Volkhan shall haunt the dreams of my people no more.

Continue your efforts, little <race>. In time, I am certain my people will grow to forgive Thorim.

passages.title: Whatever it Takes!
passages.text:
One way or another, Loken shall fall.

The honor and glory of his defeat shall be yours.

Return to me with his lying tongue, and earn my unending gratitude.

passages.title: Whatever it Takes!
passages.text: Has justice been brought to Loken?

passages.title: Whatever it Takes!
passages.text:
That vile worm is dead?

You have turned out to be a great boon to my people, little <race>.

Please accept this gift in return for your loyal friendship.

passages.title: Clearing the Way
passages.text:
Loken's forces prepare for war. What they are not ready for is to be attacked themselves.

Now is the moment to strike. Take out General Bjarngrim and his army, lest they mount an offensive on all life on Azeroth!

passages.title: Clearing the Way
passages.text: Have you vanquished their forces?

passages.title: Clearing the Way
passages.text: Though few outside of us shall ever know it, you have certainly saved the world on this day.

passages.title: Stormherald Eljrrin
passages.text:
I have sent an emissary to the Halls of Lightning to take the battle to Loken.

He undoubtedly needs assistance, given the strength of Loken's armies. Lend him any aid you can so that we may finally stop the traitor.

passages.title: Stormherald Eljrrin
passages.text: Our time to act is short. Loken prepares for war.

passages.title: The Silkwood Road
passages.text:
West of here is the Silkwood Road. It has fallen into shadow as the spiders there have turned to a more evil and gluttonous path.

I would face these villains myself but someone has to defend the noodle shop from... um... dangers and such.

Go, hero, and conquer these beasts! Should you succeed perhaps I shall regale you with some of my epic tales of heroism.

I'll also pay you.

passages.title: The Silkwood Road
passages.text: The silkwood stalkers are not in balance with nature. Predators are one thing but these creatures kill for pleasure. Harmony must be restored.

passages.title: The Silkwood Road
passages.text: Such a noble hero. You remind me of a younger, less good looking version of myself.

passages.title: DEPRECATED: Shadow Hunter Urko'jin
passages.text:
We need to fill the remaining slots in the new blockade fleet before the night elves can reestablish their spy network in the city.

The Darkspears have yet to contribute much to the war effort, but if we can convince Shadow Hunter Urko'jin to add his forces to the fleet, that will change.

Problem is, Urko'jin won't go to war without the blessing of the spirits. Pay a visit to Darkspear Hold in the Echo Isles, retrieve the totem of seafaring, and deliver it to Urko'jin in the Valley of Spirits.

passages.title: DEPRECATED: Captain Cartheron
passages.text:
We'll need more ships to round out the blockade fleet, and I know just the blood elf we need.

Captain Cartheron is his name and his men are some of the most experienced sailors in the Horde. Problem is, Cartheron and his men will want payment up front for their services.

Bring your gold with you to Ratchet in the Northern Barrens and find out how much it'll cost to hire Captain Cartheron's crew and how much bonus pay he's going to demand.

passages.title: A Poor Grasp of the Basics
passages.text:
Virmen - they no just eat our food. They trying to start farms of their own. The problem is... well, they ookin' dumb.

You no believe Muno? Last night, they break into tool sheds... steal equipment. When we wake up, we find rakes and wheelbarrows planted in ground.

They was WATERING them. They was trying to GROW WHEELBARROWS.

Please, while you out there, unbury our stuff.

passages.title: A Poor Grasp of the Basics
passages.text: Man, those virmen is dumb.

passages.title: A Poor Grasp of the Basics
passages.text: Thanks, friend. Now maybe a hozen can get some ookin' work done around here.

passages.title: Swallowed Whole
passages.text:
Now, back to your dilemma.

I believe you can help your people build relations with our hozen, as my people have.

The trail behind me will lead you to a body of water the hozen use to gather the fish that feeds them.

Around this time every year, fearsome beasts call those waters home and many hungry hozen are lost to them.

If you were to rescue some of the victims and gather some fish, perhaps you will be regarded more favorably.

passages.title: Swallowed Whole
passages.text: Wikket got slickies... for me!?

passages.title: Swallowed Whole
passages.text:
Wikket save hozen? And bring slickies?

Hmm, maybe wikket not so bad.

Tooki Tooki never liked Dook Ookem anyway...

passages.title: Catch and Release!
passages.text:
As you place one fish in each jar, your optimism grows.

This just might work! Ideally, rescuing the Hozen from your makeshift trap will soften their stance towards you.

Time to set some bait.

passages.title: Quill of Stingers
passages.text:
To achieve perfect paint strokes, one must have the right tools. My own have fallen into disrepair, their bristles becoming as unmanageable as hozu hair.

Have you seen the wasps throughout the Arboretum? Their stingers can be fashioned into quills that provide just the right level of sharpness in each line.

Could you gather some for me please?

passages.title: Quill of Stingers
passages.text: Have you been able to acquire some stingers? I would normally ask a monk for help with this but they all seem to be elsewhere at the moment.

passages.title: Quill of Stingers
passages.text: My thanks traveler. These will make a fine set of quills. Here is something for your trouble.

passages.title: The Pearlfin Situation
passages.text:
I've been thinking.

We are cut off from support and a long way from home.

Although these Pearlfin jinyu mistrust our presence, they do not appear to be hostile.

If we could convince them that we are their friends, an alliance between our races could prove extremely valuable.

<name>, you must go speak to the jinyu around the village.

Convince their leaders that we are not to be feared, and that we only wish for peace.

passages.title: The Pearlfin Situation
passages.text: If we can win over the jinyu, they may allow us to stay.

passages.title: The Pearlfin Situation
passages.text:
It sounds like you made quite the good impression.

Well done, <name>!

passages.title: The Elder's Instruments
passages.text:
Oh dear, oh dear... The Elder mustn't find out!

I must have left the Elder's ceremonial instruments behind during the escape.

But... Moonwater Retreat is crawling with hozen by now!

What sort of Pearlkeeper am I, to have lost them so carelessly?

<The old jinyu buries his face into his hands.>

Stranger, could you find it in your heart to help me?

passages.title: The Elder's Instruments
passages.text: The Elder is a Waterspeaker. He speaks to the waters, and they answer.

passages.title: The Elder's Instruments
passages.text:
You found them? Oh thank the spirits of water!

You have saved my tailfin, <name>.

passages.title: Seek Out the Lorewalker
passages.text:
I see that you and your people are desperate to find your Prince Anduin.

I know someone who may be able to help you, a pandaren Lorewalker who knows this land better than anyone. I cannot guarantee what kind of reception you will receive, but he will almost certainly be as curious about you as you are of him!

The Lorewalker lives in the forest to the southwest. Tell him that the Pearlfin have sent you.

passages.title: Seek Out the Lorewalker
passages.text:
You look around the empty house.

It appears you are in the right place, but there is no sign of its inhabitant.

passages.title: Finding Your Center
passages.text:
The dream brew is complete! This time, when you drink it, you must embrace the visions you see from a state of inner focus.

Follow me to my pagoda, and I will teach you how to achieve the inner calm that we pandaren value so much.

Your troubled mind will present you with many distractions, but just remember to stay centered!

passages.title: Finding Your Center
passages.text:
How did you find me?

<Anduin listens to you describe the vision from the Dream Brew.>

Remarkable! That's exactly what happened several days ago. We've been laying low since then.

passages.title: Potency
passages.text:
To make the Dream Brew, we will need several ingredients.

First, to improve its strength, I will need an ingredient from a fearsome creature, the legendary Mist Horror.

It is said that this creature only appears where the fog is deepest.

North and east of here, you will find smaller Mist Creepers roaming the swamps. Kill these creatures until the Mist Horror appears, and then bring me its heart.

passages.title: Potency
passages.text: The mists seem to have a mind of their own, do they not?

passages.title: Potency
passages.text: This is an amazing specimen! I am quite shocked that you have succeeded, actually.

passages.title: Spirits of the Water
passages.text:
Our war against the hozen rages without end, and the future of our tribe is uncertain.

This is why our waterspeaker has decided to seek wisdom from the waters.

Elder Lusshan is waiting. Please deliver the instruments so that they may begin.

passages.title: Spirits of the Water
passages.text: <The Elder's eyes are glazed over. His vision is cast inward, toward the wisdom he has gained.>

passages.title: Spirits of the Water
passages.text:
I saw the vision, <name>. What do you think it means?

I think it is clear that you play some part in it.

passages.title: Sacred Waters
passages.text:
I appreciate you coming all this way to save me, but Ren is gravely injured.

The old pandaren had no reason to help me, yet still he risked his life to save my own.

Before the fever set in, he mentioned that there are healing waters in the cave just down the hill.

It is dangerous, but I will do anything to help my friend. Will you help me retrieve the waters?

passages.title: Sacred Waters
passages.text: Perhaps I could bring some of these healing waters back to Stormwind with me.

passages.title: Sacred Waters
passages.text:
The healing waters should abate Ren's fever for a short while, but alas, I fear it is no permanent cure.

Thank you, <class>. We have granted him a little more time, at least.

passages.title: An Ancient Legend
passages.text:
My father has dedicated his life to studying the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.

The Vale is a mythical place, sealed after the Pandaren revolution twelve thousand years ago. We know so little about it!

My father followed a trail of clues to the cave down the hill, seeking a very old poem known as the Song of the Vale, but he is in no condition to retrieve it. It is guarded by some sort of ancestor spirit.

If you are heading that way anyway, would you mind bringing it back to him?

passages.title: An Ancient Legend
passages.text: Did you... find the scroll?

passages.title: An Ancient Legend
passages.text: Oh... it is the poem! Did you... read it? What did you learn about the Vale?

passages.title: A Perfect Match
passages.text:
Elder Lusshan and I agree that the best path forward will be to work together.

We will share with the Pearlfin our superior military knowledge and weaponry.

In return, they will be a powerful ally should we again encounter the Horde.

Take this crate of equipment and weapons. I need you to go around the village and equip the jinyu with weapons befitting their skills.

passages.title: A Perfect Match
passages.text: The jinyu are skilled in different ways. It is up to us to find their strengths.

passages.title: A Perfect Match
passages.text: Good. Let those Horde mongrels show their faces now!

passages.title: Bigger Fish to Fry
passages.text:
I've prepared a team of bright young Pearlfin trainees who need field experience.

Take them northeast, into the Bamboo Wilds, and kill any wildlife that you find.

Don't bring them back until they're fit for battle.

passages.title: Bigger Fish to Fry
passages.text: How are those trainees looking?

passages.title: Bigger Fish to Fry
passages.text:
