Your trainees returned recently. I could hardly believe my eyes! They did not look like the same jinyu that you left with.

Excellent work, <class>. Couldn't have done better myself.

passages.title: A Seemingly Endless Nuisance
passages.text:
I apologize for the state of things around here. The virmen - those rabbity creatures, down the hill - have been pushing further and further into my family's farm, and our crops - which are normally bigger, and more delicious, by the way - have been suffering because of it.

I'm no soldier... but you might be! Would you mind pushing some of these virmen off of our land?

passages.title: A Seemingly Endless Nuisance
passages.text: Have you pushed the virmen out yet, <class>? We need to bring in our crops soon, or they'll be lost for sure.

passages.title: A Seemingly Endless Nuisance
passages.text:
<Pang surveys the area around his farm.>

Well, they're not ALL gone yet, but there's less of them. And they aren't holding their ears quite as high anymore.

I'd guess that they're scared of you, <name>.

passages.title: Rampaging Rodents
passages.text:
I went off this morning to watch my papa fight the virmen. When I came back, the farm was full of marmots!

I don't want to kill them, but we need to get rid of them. Hey, I know! We can close the holes!

Fill in their holes with dirt, so they can't come out in our farm anymore.

passages.title: Rampaging Rodents
passages.text: The marmots won't be happy when you try to fill in their holes.

passages.title: Rampaging Rodents
passages.text: Thank you, sir! Now I can get back to my chores.

passages.title: Practically Perfect Produce
passages.text:
Here, <name>. My father will be wanting this.

Thank you, again, for helping with the virmen.

passages.title: Practically Perfect Produce
passages.text: Do I smell turnips?

passages.title: Practically Perfect Produce
passages.text: Ho ho! Now that's what I like to see!

passages.title: The Fabulous Miss Fanny
passages.text:
Most of these vegetables will be sold, but I'd like to keep some for my family. Specifically, my nephew Liang needs some to feed to his pigs.

Unfortunately, the pathway to Liang's farm is currently swarming with Snagtooth virmen. We're going to have to ask Miss Fanny to help us out.

Bring some of the food we've gathered to Miss Fanny, who stands next to my house. Then ask her - NICELY! - to send them down to Liang's ranch.

passages.title: The Fabulous Miss Fanny
passages.text: Not now, neighbor. I need to scrounge up some food for these pigs.

passages.title: The Fabulous Miss Fanny
passages.text:
I understand you're the one who sent the food down from uncle's farm. Thank you.

My pigs are picky eaters, but those turnips and watermelons are some of their favorites.

passages.title: The Meat They'll Eat
passages.text:
I told you earlier, my pigs are picky eaters. They need to eat meat to grow strong, but they don't like mutton, they don't like yak, and I'm not about to feed them any pig meat.

They do, however, eat meat off of the mushan beasts, and they're also quite partial to turtle. Both creatures can be found in abundance to the west.

My skills as a hunter are admittedly quite weak. Can you help out a young rancher and his pigs?

passages.title: The Meat They'll Eat
passages.text:
It hurts my ears to hear their hungry squeals.

Once you've been a pig rancher for a while, you can distinguish hungry squeals from regular squeals.

passages.title: The Meat They'll Eat
passages.text:
<Liang sorts through the meat.>

You're not just a <class>, but you're a butcher, too? You've got an eye for quality pig food, neighbor.

passages.title: A Neighbor's Duty
passages.text:
I'm not the only one having trouble with his stock, it seems. One of Francis' sheep has wandered over to my ranch, for the third time this week. I'm beginning to think he needs help tending to his flock.

You should check up on him, neighbor. And bring this poor little thing with you.

passages.title: A Neighbor's Duty
passages.text: Oh... you have one of my... my lambs?

passages.title: A Neighbor's Duty
passages.text: You really shouldn't have brought the lamb back to me. He... he was safer in that pigsty than he is over here.

passages.title: A Lesson in Bravery
passages.text:
<Master Shang speaks to his shepherd boy.>

Francis, you need to show bravery! You have everything it takes to make a great shepherd, except the courage to face your fears!

<He looks over to you.>

You, stranger. You helped the rest of my family. Francis is like a second son to me.

Show my apprentice what it means to lack fear. Use this rope to lasso and defeat one of the great white hawks above us.

<Shang points to the sky, looks at Francis, and leaves.>

passages.title: A Lesson in Bravery
passages.text: You lack fear. I can sense it in your heart.

passages.title: A Lesson in Bravery
passages.text:
Francis has taken longer than I expected to become an effective shepherd. We all go through these phases... my son Liang was weak once, too. As was I.

But he will learn. It is the Thunderfoot way.

passages.title: Great Minds Drink Alike
passages.text:
Hello again, <name>. What is this, the fourth time we've run into one another already?

Say... my keg is quickly becoming quite empty. I've heard mention of a brewery to the southwest, and that's where we're headed. Care to join us?

passages.title: Great Minds Drink Alike
passages.text:
If yer lookin' fer beer, you came to the right place, neighbor.

Just, ah... excuse the mess. Had me a bit of a problem with virmen the last few days.

passages.title: Getting Permission
passages.text:
My love, Lo, tried to get permission to marry me from the pandriarchs. Though they have passed beyond, their favor would carry a lot of weight.

Thing is, they are spirits, and none of the gifts or tributes we brought impress them. To win their favor they claimed that either Lo or a champion must defeat them in single combat.

Lo is a good man, but not a fighter.

Would you be our champion?

passages.title: Getting Permission
passages.text: Each of the pandriarchs earned their reputation in life and retained them afterward.  I can't even imagine how you will defeat them.

passages.title: Getting Permission
passages.text:
They... they agreed?! Fantastic! Thank you so much! With their blessing we can be the happiest pandaren in all the land!

Please, take this. We meant it to be a tribute for the pandriarchs but they didn't seem interested.

passages.title: In Search of Wisdom
passages.text:
Lorewalker Cho came by and asked for you while you were gone.

He needs your assistance urgently in the town of Dawn's Blossom to the north. For what reason, he did not say.

Speak to Kitemaster Ut-Nam. He would be happy to send you there.

passages.title: In Search of Wisdom
passages.text: Ah! You made it. Fantastic!

passages.title: In Search of Wisdom
passages.text:
Your deeds have sparked a long forgotten memory I have of an ancient prophecy. This deserves investigation.

In order to investigate, I need jade though. I have instructed Toya to gather as much as he can find and give it to you when he is done. Bring it to me and we will see about deciphering the ancient "Emperor's Omen."

While he gathers the jade, feel free to explore. You may find the people of this town are in need of a person of your caliber.

passages.title: All We Can Spare
passages.text:
Alright, I called in every favor I could. Here's what we got.

Cho must be on to something big!

Lemme know when you're ready to go see him - I got a ride all prepared for ya.

passages.title: All We Can Spare
passages.text: Ah, hello again, <name>! You received my message, then?

passages.title: All We Can Spare
passages.text:
I knew Toya would come through for me!

He can get anything, you know.

passages.title: Calamity Jade
passages.text:
You ever seen a shale spider, <class>? Usually harmless, just creepin' around eatin' rocks, but they got a taste for jade like cubs on candy. The boys call 'em "nibblers."

A few days back, we tunneled into a huge nest of these critters. They spilled out into the mines and went crazy, chewed up damn near everything in sight - including some of the boys.

You get in there and clear 'em out, and we got plenty of jade to spare. The quarry is directly west of here.

passages.title: Calamity Jade
passages.text:
Well I'll be... you actually did it!

You lookin' for a more permanent job, buddy? I could use a bruiser like you around full-time!

passages.title: I Have No Jade And I Must Scream
passages.text:
Our whole jade supply line has fallen apart. The mines are a death trap, morale is historically low, and - as if that weren't bad enough - the mason's quarter has been overrun by wood sprites!

Now even the plants are out to ruin me!

You need jade so badly, you can follow the road southwest to the mason's quarter and get it from those glorified chopsticks yourself.

passages.title: I Have No Jade And I Must Scream
passages.text: <Mann looks at you expectantly, eyes wide and nostrils flared.>

passages.title: I Have No Jade And I Must Scream
passages.text:
Catch? They were playin' CATCH with my product?!

I hope you showed those walkin' toothpicks a thing or two.

You know, maybe you ain't a cub after all. I've been lookin' for some muscle to help out with my problem at the quarry.

And judgin' by the size of the Lorewalker's restoration project here, I think you'll need a lot more jade.

passages.title: What's Mined Is Yours
passages.text:
Aw'right, so you need jade, do ya? I'd say we owe you at least that - we got plenty in the quarry, and thanks to yer help we should be back on schedule in no time.

I should probably get back to the wife, so let's you and me take this cart o' the good stuff straight to her.

Now, I ain't never met no <race> t'were too big for me to pull in a wagon. You climb on the back there and let ol' Hao do the legwork.

passages.title: What's Mined Is Yours
passages.text:
Well? Where's Hao?

Don't tell me you couldn't find him...

passages.title: What's Mined Is Yours
passages.text:
You did it! You brought my honey-bear back!

Oh thank you, <name>! Thank you!

passages.title: The Serpent's Heart
passages.text:
You've done great here, kid. Thanks to you, we have quite a bit of extra jade, and I know just the someone who could use it.

My friend Foreman Raike is running the great statue project at the Serpent's Heart.

Bring a shipment of extra jade to him, and tell him his old friend Mann says hello. He'll be eagerly waiting your arrival.

passages.title: The Serpent's Heart
passages.text:
Am I seeing this right? A whole shipment of pure, high quality uncut jade?

Thank goodness. I knew Foreman Mann would come through for us.

Oh and you too. Thanks for bringing it by.

passages.title: The Temple of the Jade Serpent
passages.text:
You've done us a huge favor here, traveler.

Now that we have enough jade to complete the statue, we should send word of our progress to Yu'Lon, the Jade Serpent.

When you arrive, speak to Elder Sage Wind-Yi outside the entrance to the Temple of the Jade Serpent.

If you wish to speed your journey, speak to Kitemaster Shoku. I'm sure he can spare an extra kite for you.

passages.title: The Temple of the Jade Serpent
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: The Temple of the Jade Serpent
passages.text:
You bring news from the Serpent's Spine?

<The Elder Sage patiently listens to your tale of what occurred at the Jade Mines and at the large jade statue.>

Thank you for coming all this way, stranger. However, I cannot allow you to speak to the Jade Serpent right now.

The ancient one is very busy, and as you can see, is not here at the moment.

passages.title: Instant Messaging
passages.text:
Welcome, wikket! Me Kah Kah - chief of Grookin Hill hozen.

Dook Ookem wanted to be chief, but good wikket grook him good - big gift to Kah Kah.

Hozen has gift for good wikket too. Gift come from great crash. Hozen keep it safe for wikket.

passages.title: Instant Messaging
passages.text:
Impressive work, <name>.

It had not occurred to me that we might somehow befriend these creatures.

With their acceptance, we can now turn our attention to more important matters.

passages.title: Furious Fowl
passages.text:
So these guys like fish, huh? Well how about we finish what you started and make them LOVE us?

I've still got some explosive powder from the wreck, just need something to attract the fish.

Guts is sure to do the trick - never fails. I saw some birds flyin' around south of town.

Well? Whatcha waitin' for?

passages.title: Furious Fowl
passages.text: You didn't touch that stuff with your hands did ya?

passages.title: Furious Fowl
passages.text:
Yeah!

Now that's the stuff. Just you wait and see...

passages.title: Boom Bait
passages.text:
There. I've plastered your bird guts over my explosives.

I call 'em Gut Bombs, patent pending.

Since you made friends with these fellas, how about you do the honors?

Just light the fuse and throw 'em down by the shoreline!

passages.title: Boom Bait
passages.text: I have yet to face a crisis that couldn't be fixed with dynamite.

passages.title: Boom Bait
passages.text:
We've just revolutionized how these cretins.. err, hozen, feed themselves.

They'll never be the same!

passages.title: Taking a Crop
passages.text:
Alright, fine. I DON'T have everything under control here. I spent all morning fighting off virmen. I managed to clear them off of my property, but they got away with some of my crops.

They took them down to the river, to the south. I have no idea what they're doing with them, but it's probably not eating them.

If my father wants his delivery now, I'm going to need some help getting those crops back. Could you help me out?

passages.title: Taking a Crop
passages.text: If my father wants his vegetables, I'm going to need your help.

passages.title: Taking a Crop
passages.text:
Perfect.

<Ang surveys the bruised turnips and the soggy watermelons.>

What were they DOING down there!?

passages.title: Beyond the Horizon
passages.text:
I recognize all you've managed to do here, <class>. My report to the Warchief will include an account of your deeds.

But there's no time to rest!

This land must be charted and prepared for Horde settlement. I've already selected an away team to do just that.

Find them before they grow comfortable here. Inform them of their mission, and try to convince your new friends to send along one of their own to serve as a guide.

You'll be staying here with me. We have preparations to make.

passages.title: Beyond the Horizon
passages.text: Has the away team been dispatched, <name>?

passages.title: Beyond the Horizon
passages.text:
Good work <name>.

The away team you assembled has departed.

I hope Gorrok had the sense to change out of that ragged red shirt. I admire his patriotism, but he's had it on since we left Orgrimmar.

They won't be surprising anyone if he's wearing it...

passages.title: Guerrillas in our Midst
passages.text:
Prince Anduin Wrynn. The very son of our enemy's king! Fortune has smiled on the Horde once again, <name>.

But there's another side of this coin. We'd be naive to think the child was left alone.

Any Alliance scum within sight of this land must be searching desperately for their precious princeling.

You and I are going to scour the area and root out his would-be rescuers.

passages.title: Guerrillas in our Midst
passages.text:
Yes!

By Thrall's bloodied fist, I've missed hunting Alliance!

passages.title: Leaders Among Breeders
passages.text:
Before any kegs are tapped, we have work to do. These virmen are no different than the virmen on the Wandering Isle... a nuisance that breeds as fast as the rabbits they resemble.

Sure, we could kill every last virmen we find, but what's the point in needless bloodshed? Let's just take out their alphas, and they'll slow down with their... reproduction.

passages.title: Leaders Among Breeders
passages.text: The virmen here have strange habits. Stranger names.

passages.title: Leaders Among Breeders
passages.text:
<Chen nods.>

Good work, <name>. You're not bad in combat.

What do you say we team up for the next part?

passages.title: Yellow and Red Make Orange
passages.text:
Uncle Chen says we're going to help this guy out with his virmen problem. Fine by me! I LOVE messing with virmen.

Here's the plan: we're going to paint some turnips orange, and then we'll try to convince the virmen that they're carrots.

This can only end in comedy.

I'll gather turnips. You find something that we can use to make edible orange paint.

passages.title: Yellow and Red Make Orange
passages.text: You have the stuff ready for the paint? I went ahead and gathered some turnips.

passages.title: Yellow and Red Make Orange
passages.text:
Whoah, whoah, WHOAH! You brought back BLOOD? I guess I should have looked around for a half second before I asked you to bring me something red.

Yeesh!

<Li Li turns back to the ingredients, spends a moment crushing the flower petals, and then mixes in some of the blood.>

<She begins to giggle.>

passages.title: Crouching Carrot, Hidden Turnip
passages.text:
Uncle Chen's still got his eye on me, which means I won't be wandering off any time soon. I guess it's up to you to take these turnips... I mean, "carrots"... into the Twisted Warren and deliver them for me.

It should be pretty simple. Just toss the vegetables in front of virmen, then watch their reaction when they find out it's really a turnip!

passages.title: Crouching Carrot, Hidden Turnip
passages.text: Go, torment those virmen, <name>!

passages.title: Crouching Carrot, Hidden Turnip
passages.text: Bah ha hah haaaa! I love messing with virmen.

passages.title: Thieves to the Core
passages.text:
You and that Chen fellow are good people, helpin' out with the virmen like you are. I don't like to ask for favors, but I ain't gonna turn 'em away, either.

While you're out there puttin' the hurt to those rabbit-men, you wouldn't mind keepin' an eye out for some bags o' hops, would ya? I'm pretty sure they lifted 'em last night.

Probably usin' em for pillows, knowin' how they are.

passages.title: Thieves to the Core
passages.text: I done told those virmen to stay off my land.

passages.title: Thieves to the Core
passages.text: Aww, thank ya kindly, sir. You're a real gentleman.

passages.title: Li Li's Day Off
passages.text:
Uncle Chen asked me not to get into any fights while he was away... but that doesn't mean I can't go exploring. Finally, a chance to look around Pandaria without stopping every forty-seven steps for another rest!

You want to come with me? I'll bet there's all kinds of cool places we can visit, not too far away from here.

passages.title: Li Li's Day Off
passages.text: You ready to go out yet?

passages.title: Li Li's Day Off
passages.text:
That was great! You and I should go exploring again sometime.

And it looks like we finished before Uncle Chen got back, too. Perfect.

passages.title: Muddy Water
passages.text:
While you're just hangin' around, I might as well get you involved in my whole beer-makin' "process". Ain't much of a process, really... I just mix all the stuff together and wait.

You probably heard - I like to use the muddy water from the riverbanks, to the south. Would you mind fillin' up this flask with that water and bringin' it back? I'll start gettin' the hops and barley all ready.

passages.title: Muddy Water
passages.text: I knowed you for a friend as soon as I seen you.

passages.title: Muddy Water
passages.text: You done good, <name>. You done good.

passages.title: Broken Dreams
passages.text:
Yes, I found the Stormstout Brewery... although I didn't exactly get the warm reception I expected.

<Chen pours himself a mug of ale.>

Do you want to hear the story?

passages.title: Broken Dreams
passages.text: Maybe I wasn't meant to settle down anyhow.

passages.title: Burning Down the House
passages.text:
Look, <name>!

These Alliance dogs built a camp up on the ridge.

Here, take my grog. Let's make a fire they can see from Stormwind!

For the Horde!

passages.title: Burning Down the House
passages.text:
The Alliance must be purged from this land, <name>!

No half-measures will do!

passages.title: Boom Goes the Doonamite!
passages.text:
It's an emergency!

Looks like you stirred up a hornet's nest killin' all them fish-folk.

They're conductin' a full-on counterattack on Grookin Hill!

I was hopin' to get some R&D time, but we're gunna hafta put my methane-grenade theory to work right away!

Meet me on the east side of the fort, and bring yer throwin' arm!

passages.title: Boom Goes the Doonamite!
passages.text: I think these methane-grenades are gunna impact the environment, if ya know what I mean...

passages.title: Boom Goes the Doonamite!
passages.text: I'd say repelling the attack is an understatement!

passages.title: Evacuation Orders
passages.text:
A few farmers remain in the fields... some perilously close to the crumbling wall. I don't want any farmers pretending to be heroes. We will take care of this mantid swarm, and then they can return to their homes.

My Shado-Pan are too busy defending this town to organize evacuations. You want to prove yourself useful? Get those farmers out of harm's way.

passages.title: Evacuation Orders
passages.text: Once these mantid are slain, we can get to work repairing the wall and restoring the town to its normal state.

passages.title: Evacuation Orders
passages.text:
A few stubborn ranchers want to make my job harder?

<The Watch Commander sighs.>

Fine. I will rob no pandaren of his right to defend his land.

passages.title: The Hidden Master
passages.text:
We should be able to handle the defense of Stoneplow from here on out.

<The Watch Commander motions towards Lin Tenderpaw.>

Lin here is searching for someone she calls "The Hidden Master". I believe I know who she's talking about, and I have a clue for you.

Go north.

passages.title: The Hidden Master
passages.text:
You seek training?

<The pandaren studies your physique for several seconds, without speaking.>

Alright.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Bamboo
passages.text:
We will start with a test: The Trial of Bamboo.

Your friend Lin failed this test.

Follow me, and listen carefully to my instructions.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Bamboo
passages.text: If you cannot pass this test, then there is probably no reason to continue our training.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Bamboo
passages.text:
You show promise, <name>. We will continue.

It is now time for your first round of training.

passages.title: Fog Wards
passages.text:
Trainee.

Several wards surround us, hidden in the woods near my home. They are quite effective at dispersing the mist, but they require constant upkeep.

You will find one to the north, one to the west, and one to the south. Find these wards and light them.

passages.title: Fog Wards
passages.text: See if you can light one of the wards while one of the mist incarnations is nearby.

passages.title: Fog Wards
passages.text: You honor your people, <name>.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Wood
passages.text: You have progressed in your training, I think. Come with me, and we will attempt the Trial of Wood.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Wood
passages.text: I'm prepared, <name>. Are you?

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Wood
passages.text: You have the gift of focus, <name>. Not many of my students make it this far.

passages.title: A Taste For Eggs
passages.text:
I can sense your anxiety, but you are not ready yet. Your training must continue before you perform the final test. As for your task... I need you to fetch me some eggs.

Yes, eggs. The marshland atop the hills to the east is home to a number of birds, all of which are generally peaceful in nature. You should have no trouble gathering enough eggs to last me several weeks.

passages.title: A Taste For Eggs
passages.text: How is your egg hunt going?

passages.title: A Taste For Eggs
passages.text:
Now you know why I don't gather the eggs myself.

Shall we continue your training?

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Stone
passages.text:
You have accomplished much in the short time you have been here, <name>. I would not normally offer this test so soon... but I feel that you're ready.

It is time you attempted the Trial of Stone.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Stone
passages.text:
This test will be trying. You will test the strength of your fists against the strength of stone. Steel yourself, <name>.

Not literally, of course.

Unless you normally wear steel gloves... in which case, you may literally steel yourself.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Stone
passages.text:
<Master Bruised Paw bows before you.>

Stone quivers and breaks beneath your fists. You have the power to move mountains, if you so desire.

There is nothing more I can teach you.

passages.title: Training and Discipline
passages.text:
I told myself that, if I ever made it here to the Hidden Master, I would learn everything I could from him. This is my chance, <name>. I'm not going to let it slip away.

Still, I fear that Stoneplow needs us. I left early, before we were able to push the mantid scouts back. I'd feel better if you would check in with the Watch Commander for me.

Oh, and if you run into the others, maybe you should tell them where the Hidden Master is...

passages.title: Training and Discipline
passages.text:
I'm glad to hear that Lin is well.

Our defenses are holding, for now. The mantid continue to send their scouts over the wall, but they haven't gotten much farther than that.

passages.title: Pages of History
passages.text:
The worst possible thing has happened, <race>.

We. Have. Bookworms.

This is a critical situation. All Bookworms in the library must be eradicated at once to prevent their spread.

We must squash this problem, literally! Please examine the infested books in the library and squash any Bookworms that you find.

passages.title: Pages of History
passages.text: My stomach is too fragile to handle the squashing of bugs. Is it done?

passages.title: Pages of History
passages.text:
Oh, wonderful! I am so relieved that we managed to avert disaster.

No no, don't get too close, please. You still have some squashed bug bits on your shoes.

passages.title: Everything In Its Place
passages.text:
You have helped us more than you can ever imagine, <name>.

I do not know what I would do if our precious scrolls were ever to be lost.

Please return to the Elder Sage Rain-Zhu and tell him that the library is in order.

passages.title: Everything In Its Place
passages.text:
Lorewalker Stonestep is back to work?

Remarkable. You were able to do what the last four priests I sent could not.

I...I think my headache is disappearing.

passages.title: A New Vision
passages.text: Please tell the Elder Sage Rain-Zhu that I will begin my work at once.

passages.title: A New Vision
passages.text: Wonderful! Knowing that the scryer has returned to his meditations has lifted a great burden from my shoulders.

passages.title: Dawn's Blossom
passages.text:
Blood and Thunder! My axe hungers!

We won't return to Orgrimmar until every last Alliance is purged from this land.

I will train these natives myself, if I have to. One way or another, this land will be made ready for Horde settlement.

In the meantime, their chief gave me this to pass on to you - a map and a message in some fancy script.

Do what you must, but be quick about it.

War is brewing...

passages.title: Dawn's Blossom
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>!

Welcome to Dawn's Blossom, a home of my people.

Sadly I must depart. Alas, a Lorewalker's work is never done.

Make yourself at home. Our people could surely make use of one with your talents.

passages.title: Wee Little Shenanigans
passages.text:
So... we bought some cheap grains in bulk. It turned out the grain was infested with sprites.

I HATE sprites. With their wee beady eyes and constant smiling.

I would like to resolve this quietly. Can I buy your services to discreetly eliminate some of these grain thieves?

passages.title: Wee Little Shenanigans
passages.text: Oh good, they didn't turn you into a frog yet. I saw them do that once you know.

passages.title: Wee Little Shenanigans
passages.text: Thank you for your help stranger! Hopefully we can deal with the rest on our own from here.

passages.title: Taste Test
passages.text:
As long as you're here, you might as well help me out. I'm feeling pretty darn unqualified for the task, seeing as I've never drank a drop of beer in my life.

You should try a little sample of each of their grains. Let's see if any of this stuff is sweet enough for Uncle Chen.

passages.title: Taste Test
passages.text: None of this seems to taste sweet enough! What's the deal?

passages.title: Taste Test
passages.text:
Huh. I guess none of that grain is going to work. Uncle Chen is pretty picky.

Maybe the Grainlord knows where we can find something more... special.

passages.title: The Quest for Better Barley
passages.text:
Looking for sweet grain? My father once mentioned a malted cave barley that sounds about right.

If you are willing to brave the peril, there is an ancient cave at the base of the Winds' Edge south of here.

There is even an old lift my father made when he would travel into the jungle.

In the cave is a bush as old as my family. From that bush you can pluck a grain so sweet it will humble your senses.

Just watch out for its guardians.

passages.title: The Quest for Better Barley
passages.text: That jungle sounds spooky.

passages.title: The Quest for Better Barley
passages.text: Now THIS smells like the right stuff!

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need weapons suited to your talents. Retrieve a spellblade and a hand fan from one of the weapon racks below, bring it to me, and show me that you know how to hold it properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need weapons suited to your talents. Retrieve a mace and a book of prayers from one of the weapon racks below, bring them to me, and show me that you know how to hold them properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need weapons suited to your talents. Retrieve a pair of daggers from one of the weapon racks below, bring them to me, and show me that you know how to hold them properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need weapons suited to your talents. Retrieve an axe and a shield from one of the weapon racks below, bring them to me, and show me that you know how to hold them properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need weapons suited to your talents. Retrieve an axe and a shield from one of the weapon racks below, bring them to me, and show me that you know how to hold them properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: Picking up your first weapon is also a symbolic gesture. Every <class> that leaves these training grounds must be ready to take up arms in defense of their fellow <race>.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: Li Li and the Grain
passages.text:
I'll let you in on my brewing plan, <name>: I'm planning on making an Emperor Stout. Done right, it should be dark, roasty, and high in alcohol.

<A frown appears on Chen's face.>

I just realized... I never told my plans to Li Li. She'll have no idea what type of grain to bring back!

Could you speak with her? I need her to bring back the sweetest malted grains she can find.

passages.title: Li Li and the Grain
passages.text:
<name>? What are you doing here?

So, Uncle Chen wants sweet malts? No problem! Let's get to the taste testing.

passages.title: Doesn't Hold Water
passages.text:
Would you mind checking in on Mudmug? He may need some assistance bringing that water back.

I'm sure he'll appreciate the help of a big, strong <class> like yourself to help him shoulder the load.

passages.title: Doesn't Hold Water
passages.text: <name>! You here to help out? That's mighty swell of you.

passages.title: Gardener Fran and the Watering Can
passages.text:
You want me to just GIVE you some hops? Pfshh! This is the third time today some little <race> like you has come up to me asking for food!

You want food? Then you'd better work!

<She shoves a watering can into your hand.>

Now go water my plants!

passages.title: Gardener Fran and the Watering Can
passages.text: Water my plants you lazy <class>!

passages.title: Gardener Fran and the Watering Can
passages.text:
Hmmph!

Nice farming.

passages.title: The Great Water Hunt
passages.text:
Look at it, <name>: the Gilded Fan. I heared lots of good things about the water they got here. Lots of bad things, too.

No sayin' what kind of water Chen's gonna be needin', so what say we make him a little sampler platter?

Come on, let's get movin'. We'll go scoop up some water together.

passages.title: The Great Water Hunt
passages.text: That Stormstout feller says that he's the best brewer that ever was. Might be true, couldn't tell ya one way or the 'nother as of yet.

passages.title: The Great Water Hunt
passages.text:
Lookee that, neighbor! That is quite the collection of water we got here. With magical water like this, I'm sure that Chen'll make a brew that really shines.

Or possibly a brew that lands someone in the outhouse for a month. I guess we'll just have to wait and see.

passages.title: Weed War
passages.text:
You want some hops? I've got plenty in the shed out back. I'll gladly share some with you... if you'll help me weed my field.

Now "hop" to it! Get it?

passages.title: Weed War
passages.text: You weed like a champion.

passages.title: Seeing Orange
passages.text:
Those virmen... they make me do horrible, horrible, silly things. All involving carrots. I couldn't tell you how many carrots they threw at me.

Let's not waste any more time. Get me out of here!

passages.title: Seeing Orange
passages.text: What's all this fuss about carrots? I don't get it.

passages.title: Mothallus!
passages.text:
The esteemed Journeyman Chu would appear to have created a monster. It is silken death with wings.

Mothallus.

You have already faced its brood. Now we ask that you help us face the creature itself.

Please, <class>, venture into the pit and rifle the bait. This will bring the beast to you.

Our mothfighters will assist you as you need, though silk tends to stick to them more than most so you may need to help them, should they become overwhelmed.

passages.title: Mothallus!
passages.text: Have you vanquished the beast?

passages.title: Mothallus!
passages.text:
We are pursuing perfection in our art and in ourselves. Along the way many mistakes will be made.

I'm sure by tomorrow this field will be swimming with more mistakes. Still, we thank you for your help.

passages.title: The Moth Rebellion
passages.text:
Oh... oh good! A <class>! Could you help me?

I created a strain of vile monsters during my experiments to improve silk output.

The result was a full-scale moth rebellion. Can you use your <class>iness and destroy some of these mutants?

passages.title: The Moth Rebellion
passages.text:
Master Goh keeps telling me I need to relax and that failure is part of learning. But this is a dangerous failure.

The kind that might get people killed.

passages.title: The Moth Rebellion
passages.text: It seems like there's not QUITE as many corrupted moths out there. At the very least, you've bought me some more time before I get in big, big trouble.

passages.title: Hidden Power
passages.text:
Our temple defenders have battled relentlessly for hours. No doubt they grow tired.

I will give you mantras to deliver to our fighters.

Do not be fooled by these pieces of paper. These ancient scriptures hold words of untold power.

passages.title: Hidden Power
passages.text: Words hold great power. Use them wisely.

passages.title: Hidden Power
passages.text:
The sha's numbers are unending, and our numbers few. But we are not daunted by difficult odds.

Thank you for doing your part to protect our home, <race>.

passages.title: Flames of the Void
passages.text:
Do you see the violent black and white flames erupting all around the temple?

The greater our doubt, the stronger they rage. Unchecked, they will devour the entire temple.

We have but one hope.

Take flight on one of our war serpents. Fly it near the pure springs of water, and then douse the fires with water from the pools.

passages.title: Flames of the Void
passages.text: These fires burn unlike anything in our world.

passages.title: Flames of the Void
passages.text: You have done much to help curb the fires. Thank you for your efforts.

passages.title: The Fall of Ga'trul
passages.text:
Alright <lad/lass>. We've taken enough jabs at this warlock army... now it's time to cut off the head.

Ga'trul's back there, in that big ol' temple ruin. Give him a good what-for, and the Horde will have lost its last stake here in Pandaria.

passages.title: The Fall of Ga'trul
passages.text: What's the matter, <name>? Didn't you find Sully? Did Ga'trul elude you?

passages.title: The Fall of Ga'trul
passages.text:
Sha...

Fighting the Horde on a foreign shore is hard enough.

passages.title: Where Silk Comes From
passages.text:
Would you like to be a Silkmaster for a day?

The first thing you'll need are fresh mulberry leaves. You can find them in our grove of mulberry bushes to the northwest.

Next you will need to feed them to a hungry silkworm in our feeding pit to the west.

And finally you should get some raw silk from our processing hut on the south side of our farm.

Have fun!

passages.title: Where Silk Comes From
passages.text: Have you found all of the items? Did you pay close attention to our process?

passages.title: Where Silk Comes From
passages.text: Superb specimens. I will see to it they find their way to the right place. Please enjoy this free sample.

passages.title: Knocking on the Door
passages.text:
Now, onward to the Stormstout Brewery! It's high time that I was reunited with the rest of the Stormstouts... and what better way to reunite than over a few mugs of ale?

You know where the brewery is, right? Just follow this road to the west. You can't miss it. Of course, you're free to share the road with us - we'll be leaving any moment now.

passages.title: Knocking on the Door
passages.text: The door... it's boarded up?

passages.title: Clear the Way
passages.text:
Are you seeing this? Virmen, hozen, and water sprites... all pouring out of the brewery doors and windows! What the heck is going on in there!?

There is another entrance, on the eastern side of the brewery. I'm going to run over there and try to figure out what's going on. In the meantime, see if you can't get rid of these creatures. There's nothing worse than a drunken hozen.

passages.title: Clear the Way
passages.text: This brewery - it's a disgrace to the Stormstout name! Something needs to be done!

passages.title: Clear the Way
passages.text: I've had just about enough of this brewery. I'm starting to think that you and I should just bust down the wall and clean house.

passages.title: Cleaning House
passages.text:
That's it, <name>. I've had enough of this.

If somebody doesn't do SOMETHING to take care of this brewery, we'll lose it forever. And there's far too much family history - and beer - in there to risk wasting.

So... we're going to break in through the back door. You, Li Li, Mudmug, and me.

It's gonna be a brawl in there.

Let me know when you're ready.

passages.title: Cleaning House
passages.text: Let's do this.

passages.title: Cleaning House
passages.text:
Take a look around - it's a lot calmer outside. All the brewery needed was somebody strong to take care of it.

It's going to take some time to clean this place up, but I don't really mind that so much.

This is, after all... my home.

passages.title: What's Eating Zhu's Watch?
passages.text:
Pandaren always welcome travelers with open arms - and open kegs! But this town full of jerks!

Everyone so busy sulking, they won't talk to Ken-Ken at all!

Can you find someone in town who will talk to us? Maybe normal pandaren just hiding in the houses?

passages.title: What's Eating Zhu's Watch?
passages.text: Something definitely not right! Pandaren supposed to be HAPPY!

passages.title: What's Eating Zhu's Watch?
passages.text: Only one lady-panda who's not crazy? This worse than Ken-Ken thought...

passages.title: Materia Medica
passages.text:
Alright, Ken-Ken pretty sure he knows what wrong with pandaren! Got old, old hozen remedy that do the trick.

Need to mix honey, fish oil, and salt. Ken-Ken saw lots of beehives in the trees around town, and there must be fish left in the dry ponds.

That just leave salt... Mei might know where we can find some.

passages.title: Materia Medica
passages.text: Can't believe Ken-Ken did not think of this sooner. It's the ONE thing that can ruin his day...

passages.title: Materia Medica
passages.text:
Pandaren got a case of the spooky-dooks!

Dooks get scared sometimes, don't wanna come out. Poor, fluffy mopey-dopes must be ready to explode by now!

This just the thing to bring 'em out. That make pandaren happy for sure!

Just like ol' gramma used to say: can't THROW if can't GO!

passages.title: Cheer Up, Yi-Mo
passages.text:
Ever since this storm began, I've just been... tired.

Not physically... no. It's like my very soul is exhausted. Worthless. Hopeless. I imagine it's what one feels when a mate leaves them for someone with a rounder belly, but I've never had a mate so how would I know?

How can I claim to know anything? I'm worthless to everyone but these thunderbirds. At least they'll have a good meal out of me.

<Yi-Mo sighs deeply and continues staring off into the sky. It doesn't look like he's going anywhere.>

passages.title: Cheer Up, Yi-Mo
passages.text:
I can't believe he was actually going to do that... This despair is worse than I had even imagined.

I cannot thank you enough for bringing him back.

passages.title: Securing the Province
passages.text:
With our grip on the province loosening, saurok from the wilds have already moved in to the cave just north of town.

Most of our hunters are face-down in their own tears, so the saurok just walk in here like they own the place and grab whatever they want!

I want to send a message that Zhu's Watch is not to be crossed.

Will you be my messenger?

passages.title: Securing the Province
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. That should teach those savages to know their boundaries.

passages.title: Borderlands
passages.text:
Bonfires are surprisingly effective at discouraging beasts from wandering out of the wilds. We have three along the border to the southwest which we normally keep lit at all times.

Nobody's been there for days, though, and the fires must be out by now. It's only a matter of time before the wilds creep back in and overtake the land we have kept safe for centuries.

Please, re-ignite the bonfires. They are critical in keeping the province safe, and they are memorials to the founders of our way of life.

passages.title: Borderlands
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

Zhu Province serves as a corridor from the upper tier of the valley down to the sea.

Keeping the province safe requires daily efforts to maintain a border against the savage Krasarang Wilds.

passages.title: Into the Brewery
passages.text:
We need to find out what's going on inside that brewery, <name>!

We may have cleared out some of the bigger pests, but I'm certain there's plenty more where they came from. Gather up a few of your friends, and meet me inside!

passages.title: Into the Brewery
passages.text:
You came! Great!

I'm looking forward to fighting by your side again, <name>.

passages.title: Why So Serious?
passages.text:
Okay, so that not work. Well... it cheer Ken-Ken up! But pandaren still sad...

We try another old hozen remedy - this time, we go back even further than gramma, way WAY back to ancient times. Hozen still do this sometimes... mostly at parties.

Ken-Ken got woodworking to do - you bring him teeth! Not yours; big ones, like a panther would have!

Oh, and some paint! Mei might know where to find.

passages.title: Why So Serious?
passages.text:
<Ken-Ken is hard at work carving something out of tree bark.>

This gonna be great, you'll see.

passages.title: Why So Serious?
passages.text:
Just in time! All done... look!

<Ken-Ken holds up a carved wooden mask with a ridiculous face.>

Now we put on finishing touches and we gots a guaranteed FUN MACHINE!

passages.title: Apply Directly to the Forehead
passages.text:
Well... THAT was unexpected!

Come to think of it, now Ken-Ken remember why hozen use mask in the first place...

A legend about the Monkey King says he used a mask to cure old pandaren emperor, Shaohao, when he was too sad to lead his people. Then they buried mask--with all his sadness--in the ground.

We should use the mask on more pandaren, but instead of putting sad away in ground, we gonna PUNCH ITS BUTT.

Let's do this, <name>!

passages.title: Apply Directly to the Forehead
passages.text:
This must be the emperor's sad coming back! That is some oooold sad.

Ken-Ken bet pandaren sad get stronger with age, too, like pandaren booze.

passages.title: Apply Directly to the Forehead
passages.text:
We saving pandaren, but the land still sad... Look, rain's not stopping at all!

<Ken-Ken shakes his tiny fists at the sky.>

How many more butts we gotta punch before we fix this town?!

<The sky darkens in response.>

passages.title: Zhu's Despair
passages.text:
Hmm... Is that Yi-Mo kid over there?

<Ken-Ken squints against the increasing torrents of rain.>

It is! He's at the well, and he's not lookin' so good.

Ken-Ken got a bad feeling about this...

passages.title: Zhu's Despair
passages.text:
We did some good work here today, <name>.

Monastery always tell us to leave a place better than we find it.

passages.title: Assassinate Creed
passages.text:
The city has been in chaos for days now. Hiram Creed, disguised as a Gilnean, has infected the lot of those dogs with his own draconic blood. Even the Forsaken are having trouble routing him out.

Only a surgical assassination can end this!

The bridge behind me is relatively unguarded. Slip in through merchant's square and head south - you'll find Creed in the middle of the military district.

I'll keep an eye on you and pull you out if there's any trouble.

...There WILL be trouble!

passages.title: Assassinate Creed
passages.text: Hiram Creed. Among the black dragons, he is known as "Creetharus."

passages.title: Assassinate Creed
passages.text:
Creed is finished. The Gilneans who followed his lead are on their own now - assuming his corrupted draconic blood works its way out of their system without killing them.

Either way they're no longer a concern of ours.

passages.title: Murozond
passages.text:
If we are to destroy Deathwing, we will need the power of the Dragon Soul. To obtain the Dragon Soul, I would have to take you back to the Sundering, ten thousand years in the past... but that time passage is blocked to me.

The creature that blocks us from accessing this time passage is named Murozond. He must be slain, here, in this twisted future, before we can continue our plot to unmake Deathwing.

This is why you were brought here, <name>.

passages.title: Murozond
passages.text:
This is a future of Azeroth, yes... but not an inevitable one.

This future is what my fellow aspects are trying to avoid.

passages.title: Murozond
passages.text: Murozond is no more. The timeways are open to me once again.

passages.title: Archival Purposes
passages.text:
From what I understand, you intend to avoid this future. If this is true, then we must archive data from this timestrand before it is lost to us.

We believe that the most interesting and valuable elements of this future are the powerful "echoes" that roam the dragonshrines.

Take this vessel with you as you silence these echoes. A portion of their energies will be archived within the bronze dragonflight's depository.

passages.title: Archival Purposes
passages.text:
Nozdormu is acting with haste. This is something that Nozdormu does not usually do.

Normally I would be more thorough with my archival. However, given the circumstances, we are forced to pick and choose what we record... and to employ the help of mercenaries like you.

passages.title: Archival Purposes
passages.text:
<Alurmi collects the vessel from you.>

I will handle these from here. Of course, they must be properly labeled, documented, and stored.

passages.title: The Path to the Dragon Soul
passages.text:
I cannot simply fly up and grab the Dragon Soul. The old gods protect it.

To make matters worse, their shield is strengthened by the swirling, arcane energies that emanate from the Well of Eternity, and those energies are being focused by the great demon Mannoroth.

Distract Mannoroth, and the link between the Dragon Soul and the Well will be broken. Without the Well's power, the old gods' ward will be weakened, and the Dragon Soul will be vulnerable.

And then I will take it.

passages.title: The Path to the Dragon Soul
passages.text: What?

passages.title: The Path to the Dragon Soul
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, stranger.

You fight well. I hope to fight with you again in the future.

passages.title: To Wyrmrest!
passages.text:
The Dragon Soul... a weapon with enough power to defeat Deathwing. Thanks to you, it is now safely in our hands.

Come! The aspects await us. We must bring the Dragon Soul to Wyrmrest Temple, in the center of Dragonblight.

passages.title: To Wyrmrest!
passages.text: Come, <name>. We do not have much further to travel.

passages.title: To Wyrmrest!
passages.text:
I owe my life to you, heroes.

Now that we hold the Dragon Soul safely within Wyrmrest, it may be that all of Azeroth owes their lives to you.

passages.title: Documenting the Timeways
passages.text:
You... <name>, was it? You assisted with our archival in the past. Well, technically it was the future, but I believe you understand. Time is highly relative.

I require more information for our archive. While you and Nozdormu don't intend to overwrite this timestrand, as you did in the End Time, we can still benefit from more data.

I require information on Captain Varo'then, one of Azshara's pretty little handmaidens, and... hmm... oh, how about that big felguard, just down those stairs?

passages.title: Documenting the Timeways
passages.text: We rarely enjoy the opportunity to employ a brave <class> like you. Our archive grows more thorough, thanks to your efforts.

passages.title: The Twilight Prophet
passages.text:
The missive reads as follows:

"The Hour of Twilight is upon us. The world-shaman Thrall approaches Wyrmrest with the Dragon Soul in hand, feebly whimpering one final threat to destroy our glorious master."

"Stop Thrall, and we win our war. I will be watching you from nearby."

 ~ The Twilight Prophet

passages.title: The Twilight Prophet
passages.text: I have my suspicions about this Twilight Prophet.

passages.title: The Twilight Prophet
passages.text:
It is truly as we foresaw: Benedictus was the Twilight Prophet. And now he is no more.

We dealt a mighty bow to the Twilight's Hammer today. Let us hope that it was a deathblow.

passages.title: The Deed is Done
passages.text:
Prince Wrathion will be pleased to hear that you've succeeded. You should report back to him at Ravenholdt Manor.

The Prince has been known to be extremely generous to those who help him.

passages.title: The Deed is Done
passages.text:
That's wonderful news, <name>. Creed was not the most powerful of the remaining black dragons, but his manipulation of the Gilneans was truly diabolical.

I've prepared a reward for you. These blades may not look like much at present, but in the right hands they may yet awaken.

Perhaps in YOUR hands...

passages.title: Cluster Clutch
passages.text:
The daggers I have given you are lifeless shells. They can do great things, once they are given a means to contain the power I have in mind.

I need for you to acquire Shadowy Gems for me. The facets of these unusual stones are like windows into the infinite. They are often used by minions of the Twilight's Hammer to control the most powerful of elementals.

A great battle is raging around Wyrmrest Temple. Collect Elementium Gem Clusters from Deathwing's minions and bring the gems to me.

passages.title: Cluster Clutch
passages.text:
How many gems have you collected?

Are my father's minions as twisted as he?

passages.title: Cluster Clutch
passages.text:
Ah, do you see how they shimmer? Many fine gems sparkle in the light, but only these seem to sparkle with darkness.

I'll perform an enchantment on these while you are on your next mission.

Are you ready?

passages.title: Our Man in Karazhan
passages.text:
Your next target is the Black Dragon Nalice, who is engaged in some sort of arcane debauchery beneath the ruined tower of Karazhan.

Your primary mission is to destroy her, but if you can bring me back a vial of her blood, I'll be able to use it to augment the power of the daggers I've given you.

Your accomplice Zazzo has already been dispatched to the scene and awaits you there. He'll have more details.

passages.title: Our Man in Karazhan
passages.text:
Madness. Insanity!

I don't know what Nalice is up to down there, but the entire basement radiates with diabolical arcane energy. She's got an entire cult worshipping her as a goddess.

If we're going to take her out, we have to do it soon. I hope you're ready for this!

passages.title: Blood of the Betrayer
passages.text:
I've pinpointed Nalice to the Master's Cellar, an extended basement you'll find in the ruins up ahead.

Dragon cultists are everywhere, and Nalice has set up some strange arcane storage devices throughout the area. Perhaps you can use those to your advantage?

Sneak past the cultists, obliterate Nalice, and grab a vial of her blood for Wrathion.

I'll keep my eyes on you and pull you out if you get into any trouble. But I'm NOT coming in there with you!

passages.title: Blood of the Betrayer
passages.text: Nalice. Dead?

passages.title: Blood of the Betrayer
passages.text:
You did it? She's dead? Unbelievable! You're some kind of miracle-worker!

Here, let me see that blood. I can preserve its energies in an arcane matrix for your trip back...

passages.title: A Score to Settle
passages.text:
Utgarde's forces are organizing under the advisory of Prince Keleseth, a san'layn ambassador of the Scourge.

We cannot allow the vrykul to benefit from his counsel any further. Silence him.

passages.title: A Score to Settle
passages.text: Is it done, <name>?

passages.title: A Score to Settle
passages.text:
Revenge feels good.  To think that this is but a taste of what's to come.

Arthas will get what he deserves soon enough.

passages.title: Victory in the Depths
passages.text:
<Zazzo performs an enchantment on the vial of blood, then quickly hands it back to you, as though it's toxic.>

Done! You'll want to get this back to Wrathion as soon as possible, along with those two daggers of yours.

I don't know what he plans to do with this stuff. Between you and me, sometimes that little dragon kid creeps me out. Good luck!

passages.title: Victory in the Depths
passages.text: Ah, you've returned! I no longer sense Nalice's presence. Is she dead? Or has she somehow eluded us both?

passages.title: Victory in the Depths
passages.text:
You are, indeed, a master of your craft. Nalice is dead, and it is time you are rewarded for your efforts.

<Wrathion takes the vial from you, his face a mask of equal parts reverence and revulsion. He drops the gems you collected one-by-one into the blood, muttering an incantation.>

<Without warning he pours the blood over the blades of the daggers, and the steel seems to writhe and twist as though alive. When the smoke clears, the daggers have altered their shape.>

passages.title: Sharpening Your Fangs
passages.text:
Do you understand why I have you assassinate the dragons, yet spare the mortals? It isn't their fault. They must seek out their own destiny, free from the meddling of my kind.

We are nearing the end of our mission, and it is time for you to seek out your own destiny as well. I can continue to augment your weapons, but collecting shadowy gems won't be enough. My work will require entire clusters. Gather them from my father's minions...

passages.title: Sharpening Your Fangs
passages.text:
How many clusters have you acquired?

The tenacity of your race continues to inspire me!

passages.title: Sharpening Your Fangs
passages.text:
You have done it! No doubt you placed yourself and your allies in great peril to acquire these. Your sacrifices will be rewarded in time. I will use these as the foundation of a powerful enchantment for you.

But we will need one additional catalyst. Are you ready for your final and most dangerous mission, <class>?

passages.title: Stoneplow Thirsts
passages.text:
Excuse me... <name>? Did I hear your name correctly?

I've come from Stoneplow, in the west. They sent me to pick up some emergency beer rations, but the Stormstout Brewery is all boarded up!

It looks like your handsome friend there - no, not Mudmug, the other one - has a few casks with him. Could you spare a keg for a town in need?

passages.title: Stoneplow Thirsts
passages.text: Greetings, <class>.

passages.title: Stoneplow Thirsts
passages.text:
Finally! Emmi's come through.

I hope all is well at the Stormstout Brewery. My men don't do well without beer.

passages.title: Cleansing Drak'Tharon
passages.text:
'Ey, mon, you be here! Dis is good, mon!

Drak'Tharon soon be cleansed of them foul undead and restored to her noble purpose. In return for your help, the keep's most valuable treasures be yours, mon!

Once ya be reachin' its top, ya must summon me, and I'll perform the ritual.

Alas, my summonin' will be comin' at a cost. Ya must collect mojo from the survivors.

passages.title: Cleansing Drak'Tharon
passages.text:
We done a great thing, mon! And dis just be da beginning....

Seek me out in Zul'Drak when da time be right.

Dere be a war to be won, mon!

passages.title: Profit Mastery
passages.text:
Two words: Tiger Blood!

This is gonna sell better than saronite back on the black market. Especially once I finish spreading a rumor about how it makes you all buff and stuff.

Thing is, I ran out of ammo. Can you round up a few vials of tiger blood for me? I'll cut you in on the scam.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text:
Mogu? They seem like the elves, ancient and an over developed sense of entitlement. Everyone of Azeroth must learn, sooner or later, that the Horde is not "visiting" this world. We are here. We are staying.

Teach them this lesson. Quell their numbers in the ruins south and west of here. Break their amassing forces before they decide to attack.

Learn what you can of how these creatures fight, and how they die.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text: You found how many? Sounds like a veritable nest of the vile creatures. If they were more civilized I might consider extending them an invitation to join the Horde.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text: These are more than just a bandit threat. They are an ancient people beginning to rally under a single banner. Mark my words, soon these lands will know war.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text:
The mogu found the Pools of Youth!

Mama Bramblestaff used to tell me old stories about those. During the mogu empire they would use the waters to extend life.

Thing is those stories never ended well for some reason. As if the waters were cursed.

Either way, we should investigate. There is a good chance those waters might help Leza.

It looks like the Pools of Youth are on the northwestern side of the ruins.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text: Leza's pain is immense. Only powers beyond my own can save her and the baby now.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text: At this point I am willing to try anything. This land is claiming my wife and unborn child. I need all the help I can get.

passages.title: Herbal Remedies
passages.text:
Kang's remedy isn't working.

There is something else at work here. A power deep beneath the soil. It is sapping us of hope, hitting us with depression and despair.

Kang tells me this land has lotus plants. I might be able to make a tea that would hopefully lend Leza some strength.

Please, adventurer, search the ruins south and west of here for lotus leaves. I will pay you for your efforts.

passages.title: Herbal Remedies
passages.text:
I've been punched, stabbed, thrown off of a cliff, hit in the face by someone's mace, hit in the face by my own mace, and fell off the elevator at Thunder Bluff on more than one occasion.

None of that pain sounds even half as bad as what Leza is going through. I hope this tea helps...

passages.title: Herbal Remedies
passages.text: Thank you hero. Kor is a brave warrior but he lacks compassion at times. Life must come before death, or there will be none of us left when the fighting is done.

passages.title: Going West
passages.text:
Leza now walks with the ancestors of this strange land. I must look now to the living.

Kor has led a group of our scouts west deeper into the jungle.

I sent a scout of my own to investigate the crane temple. Please, adventurer, seek out my scout, get their report, then meet up with Kor and lend what aid you can to him.

We will join you as quickly as we are able.

passages.title: Going West
passages.text: War. It always comes down to war.

passages.title: Going West
passages.text:
<name>! Well timed!

We were laying an ambush for the Alliance in the ruins west of here when the mogu ambushed us. They are using mage portals to call in reinforcements.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
Deep in the wilds, on the southern coast where the Krasarang River meets the sea, rests the Temple of the Red Crane, home of the great Chi-Ji and his most devout followers.

They should be told of what happened here.

If you're headed that way, I have a favor to ask; We often send supplies to the temple, but our last courier has not returned. Please look for signs of him as you travel - where the road forks at the Dojani River, he'd have gone north. When you reach the temple, find Koro Mistwalker.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
I see... And the sha have seeped out as far as the province already, have they?

Well, I hate to break it to you, but the temple is also overrun with sha. Those of us who haven't been killed or... possessed, or whatever, are fleeing for our very lives.

If you defeated the sha at Zhu's Watch, I have to implore you to help us deal with them here.

passages.title: Wild Things
passages.text:
Welcome to the Order of the Cloud Serpent, <race>. I can see from the spark in your eye that you wish to join the Order.

Let me get a good look at you.

<Elder Anli gently holds your head and gazes at your face.>

Hmm. I see honesty and earnestness in your heart. You have journeyed far to come here, but I am afraid you must go yet further.

Your path into the Order begins now.

Speak to Instructor Tong at Windward Isle to the northeast to take the first step.

passages.title: Wild Things
passages.text:
Thank goodness, they finally sent someone!

Things have gotten out of control!

passages.title: Beating the Odds
passages.text:
At first, the Slitherscale were too frightened to approach the wild serpents.

Then, I caught them snatching the eggs under the cover of night.

Now, they are slaughtering adults and hatchlings alike!

If we do not do something, these gentle creatures will be completely wiped out. Then there won't even be an Order of the Cloud Serpent to join!

Go and slay these vile Slitherscales, and then we will talk.

passages.title: Beating the Odds
passages.text: The Order rarely meddles with the natural balance on this island, but it is too important to save the serpents.

passages.title: Beating the Odds
passages.text:
Thank you, <race>.

I tried to stop the Slitherscale where I could, but I was no match for their numbers.

Your work today will help preserve an entire generation of cloud serpents.

passages.title: Empty Nests
passages.text:
When the attacks began, the young hatchlings scattered in terror.

They are roaming around the island, lost and scared.

If you want to help, take this rope and leash the lost little ones. Take them back to their nests. Return them home.

passages.title: Empty Nests
passages.text: Did you return the hatchlings to their nests?

passages.title: Empty Nests
passages.text:
Don't worry. The hatchlings will be safe inside their nests.

I can't thank you enough for arriving when you did.

passages.title: Choosing the One
passages.text:
I have examined each egg, <name>. Out of the lot that you brought me, I have chosen the three eggs with the most promise.

You may choose only one egg to take with you. Are you ready to make your final selection?

passages.title: Choosing the One
passages.text:
You may choose only one egg to take with you.

Choose carefully. There is no going back.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Excellent, just excellent! I will return the other eggs to their nests, undisturbed.

In the meantime, deliver your egg to Instructor Skythorn at The Arboretum.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text: The wild cloud serpents live in a delicate balance with nature. Their rare eggs are quite vulnerable to enemies.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Ah yes, Elder Anli mentioned that a new student had joined our ranks. I see you have already chosen your cloud serpent egg.

I will instruct you on its care. Let me see it for a moment.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Excellent, just excellent! I will return the other eggs to their nests, undisturbed.

In the meantime, deliver your egg to Instructor Skythorn at The Arboretum.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text: The wild cloud serpents live in a delicate balance with nature. Their rare eggs are quite vulnerable to enemies.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Ah yes, Elder Anli mentioned that a new student had joined our ranks. I see you have already chosen your cloud serpent egg.

I will instruct you on its care. Let me see it for a moment.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Excellent, just excellent! I will return the other eggs to their nests, undisturbed.

In the meantime, deliver your egg to Instructor Skythorn at The Arboretum.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text: The wild cloud serpents live in a delicate balance with nature. Their rare eggs are quite vulnerable to enemies.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Ah yes, Elder Anli mentioned that a new student had joined our ranks. I see you have already chosen your cloud serpent egg.

I will instruct you on its care. Let me see it for a moment.

passages.title: Flight Training: Ring Round-Up
passages.text:
Now that your serpent is fully grown, you are ready to begin flight training.

As with all novices, you must start at the beginning.

Your first task is simple. Fly through 6 of the cloud rings between the spires to the east.

passages.title: Flight Training: Ring Round-Up
passages.text: How did your first flight go?

passages.title: Flight Training: Ring Round-Up
passages.text:
What have you learned from this lesson?

Speed. It's all about speed.

passages.title: Snack Time
passages.text:
Cloud serpents love to eat, and one of their favorite treats is the sugar minnow.

These fish can be found in salt or fresh water anywhere in Pandaria. I trust you have some skill in fishing, and your own fishing pole to catch them?

Bring me a fresh catch and I'm sure the hungry beasts around here will be very grateful.

passages.title: Snack Time
passages.text: Did you find a good place to fish?

passages.title: Snack Time
passages.text: Oh wonderful! These fish will do nicely.

passages.title: Fragments of the Past
passages.text:
The Order of the Cloud Serpent's history stretches back thousands of years, and although we have tried to preserve the old ways, there are ancient techniques that have been lost over time.

You can help us recover some of this knowledge by searching Pandaria's dig sites for clues to our past.

Use your archaeology skill to survey around Pandaria and bring me whatever you find.

passages.title: Fragments of the Past
passages.text: How did the excavation go?

passages.title: Fragments of the Past
passages.text: Amazing, <name>. These relics are invaluable to our studies. We will learn much from these fragments.

passages.title: Just a Flesh Wound
passages.text:
Many of the baby hatchlings at Windward Isle have been injured as a result of all the fighting.

I have been told that you may be able to help them, with your access to powerful bandages.

Please go northeast and use some of the best bandages you can acquire to save the injured hatchlings.

passages.title: Just a Flesh Wound
passages.text: Wonderful! It is a good thing you are trained in the arts of first aid.

passages.title: Sweet as Honey
passages.text:
<The hatchling scampers about, then whines and whimpers.>

From the cloud serpent's behavior, you have a hunch that it wants a sweet treat.

The fragrant trees in The Arboretum are home to many honey hives.

It will be a simple matter to collect combs from the nearby honeykeepers.

passages.title: Sweet as Honey
passages.text: <The hatchling spins around in glee as you return.>

passages.title: Sweet as Honey
passages.text:
The hatchling leaps for your hand. It winds its long, serpentine tail around you and begins to lick the honey from your fingers.

That tickles!

passages.title: Catch!
passages.text:
<The hatchling looks up at you with a bored, listless expression.>

You have a feeling the serpent is tired of being cooped up all day.

 How about playing a little game of catch?

passages.title: Catch!
passages.text: <The serpent watches you curiously.>

passages.title: Catch!
passages.text: Oh my, I see you and your serpent are having a great time! Well done, <name>. Playtime will greatly increase your serpent's mental and physical acuities.

passages.title: The Sky Race
passages.text:
The time for the great race is upon us!

Traverse the course among the spires and pass through the checkered flags on each of the 10 balloon checkpoints.

Make sure to pass underneath the finish line when you are done.

The competition will be fierce, but I wish you luck. Speak to me when you are ready to begin.

passages.title: The Sky Race
passages.text:
Wonderful! How does it feel to finish the Sky Race?

You must be eager to collect your prize!

passages.title: Restoring the Balance
passages.text:
The situation at the islands remains dire, <name>.

The Slitherscale saurok have not responded to our attempts at peace, so only one option remains.

In order to protect the wild cloud serpents, we must rid the island of their presence. Only then can the cloud serpents be left to live in peace.

passages.title: Restoring the Balance
passages.text: The poachers will wipe out the cloud serpents completely if they are not stopped.

passages.title: Restoring the Balance
passages.text: If the poachers will not listen to diplomacy, then they will surely listen to our blades. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Feeding Time
passages.text:
<The serpent darts forward and bites your fingers.>

Ouch! It seems, without a doubt, that the little beast is hungry. You recall that some meaty-looking turtles can be found on the wild cloud serpent island to the northeast.

Perhaps some turtle meat will fill the hatchling's voracious appetite.

passages.title: Feeding Time
passages.text: <The serpent looks at you with hungry eyes.>

passages.title: Feeding Time
passages.text: You are learning well, young trainer. Saltback meat is tough, but loaded with the nutrients that a young hatchling needs to grow.

passages.title: Emptier Nests
passages.text:
Oh, thank goodness, another cloud serpent trainer!

I just received word that the wild hatchlings at Windward Isle to the northeast are in serious trouble!

While the adults fight those terrible saurok, who is watching the cute little babies? No one, that's who!

WE HAVE TO SAVE THEM!

I'm sending every trainer I can find to go and help. If you aren't too busy, can you make sure the hatchlings are safely delivered back to their mothers' nests?

passages.title: Emptier Nests
passages.text: I see you have been taking good care of the young hatchlings out there. Well done.

passages.title: Thieving Raiders
passages.text:
Saurok!

These vile creatures are obsessed with killing and stealing. They attacked our settlement without provocation or warning.

Please, <class>, can you aid us?

Help us recover our lost possessions from these Riverblade raiders that march along the river and we will gladly reward you.

passages.title: Thieving Raiders
passages.text: I think they even stole my holy spittoon.

passages.title: Thieving Raiders
passages.text:
Not many would stop to help a village in need... especially so deep in the wilds.

You are a champion to our people, <name>.

passages.title: Barreling Along
passages.text:
No, no, no, don't you worry about pickin' 'em up. I can hold these here barrels.

I may not be the handsomest pandaren, or the smartest, or any fun to be around in the slightest, but I'm stronger than a mushan beast.

I'mma just need you to lead the way.

passages.title: Barreling Along
passages.text: Where's Mudmug?

passages.title: Barreling Along
passages.text: Good! The water's here!

passages.title: For Family
passages.text:
Kor should have caught up by now. He said he was going to secure the Ruins of Korja east of here and meet us to help with the mantid threat.

He may need help against Groundbreaker Brojai. Could you assist him? Kang and I will follow shortly.

passages.title: For Family
passages.text: This land claims so much.

passages.title: For Family
passages.text:
I thank you for avenging my friend, <name>. We did not always see eye to eye, but I will mourn him.

I know he would have wanted you to carry one of his items with you as a token of his memory and gratitude.

passages.title: The Mantid
passages.text:
The mantid! They came out of nowhere and smashed our convoy to ruin, scattering our people this way and that.

Now they are preparing to hit Stoneplow.

Please, <class>, destroy some of these beasts before they get sufficient numbers to flank our home.

If my cousin, Ambassador Len, is still alive and at our convoy he should be able to reward you for your help.

passages.title: The Mantid
passages.text: It has been many thousands of years since mantid were seen on this side of the Great Wall.

passages.title: The Mantid
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, <class>! I've never seen anybody stand up to the mantid like that before.

Well, other than the Shado-Pan, of course...

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
Deep in the wilds, on the southern coast where the Krasarang River meets the sea, rests the Temple of the Red Crane, home of the great Chi-Ji and his most devout followers.

They should be told of what happened here.

If you're headed that way, I have a favor to ask; We often send supplies to the temple, but our last courier has not returned. Please look for signs of him as you travel - where the road forks at the Dojani River, he'd have gone south. When you reach the temple, find Koro Mistwalker.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
I see... And the sha have seeped out as far as the province already, have they?

Well, I hate to break it to you, but the temple is also overrun with sha. Those of us who haven't been killed or... possessed, or whatever, are fleeing for our very lives.

If you defeated the sha at Zhu's Watch, I have to implore you to help us deal with them here.

passages.title: Poisoned!
passages.text: The... mogu. Do not trust. Poison. Get sample... sample blades. Bring to Dezco... in Thunder Cleft, west of here.

passages.title: Poisoned!
passages.text: You have news of Chezin?

passages.title: Poisoned!
passages.text:
Chezin is dead? This is very bad news indeed. Kor, Chezin and I have fought dragons, undead, and Alliance on nearly every shore that has a name.

To lose him like this...

Thank you for recovering these weapons. It should teach us much about our new enemy.

passages.title: Stalker Mastery
passages.text:
Tigers! No matter what land I go to I hear about these big fanged beasts. And yet I haven't had a chance to hunt any of them.

Let's go hunt some tigers. I'll go east, you go west. I think I saw some near Dustback Gorge. I'm sure there are tons near those mushan.

passages.title: Stalker Mastery
passages.text: What's your count up to?

passages.title: Stalker Mastery
passages.text: Wow! You really racked up a count. I'll chat with Mr. Pleeb about getting the best one converted to a trophy for you.

passages.title: Mushan Mastery: Darkhide
passages.text:
My boy here is a talented hunter... in training. Let's show him an old 'Nessy style hunt shall we?

I saw a mighty big mushan east of here with a hide dark as night. It looked like it had taken down a number of hunters in its day.

If you want a big game hunt, go try an' take it on.

passages.title: Mushan Mastery: Darkhide
passages.text: Puttin' the "big" into "Big Game Hunter."

passages.title: Mushan Mastery: Darkhide
passages.text: Now that's a proper trophy right there.

passages.title: Parental Mastery
passages.text:
If them tablets were correct, all ay got ta do is a small dance ritual and the big thing o' the deep will be summoned.

When it comes out, we'll get 'em and show me pop we are both true big game hunters like him.

passages.title: Parental Mastery
passages.text: Now that is how ya big game hunt.

passages.title: Parental Mastery
passages.text: You saved me son! I canno' ever thank ye enough. Please! Take this fer your efforts.

passages.title: Flight Training: In Due Course
passages.text:
Now that you have learned the basics of the race, you should go learn the course.

Explore the spires and collect a race flag from each of the checkpoints.

Fly through each checkered flag to collect it.

passages.title: Flight Training: In Due Course
passages.text: Do you have what it takes to compete... and win?

passages.title: Flight Training: In Due Course
passages.text: Well done. If you hadn't been capable of finding the checkpoints, I fear you would never have done well in the Sky Race.

passages.title: That's Not a Rock!
passages.text:
