Okay, these spiders are seriously creeping me out. Especially those egg sacs they leave lying around that I keep accidentally stepping on only to be covered in very little but very creepy spiderlings. Ug, makes me shudder just thinking about it.

I say you burn them. Burn them all.

passages.title: That's Not a Rock!
passages.text: Thank you. I'd say I have about a week of Anji making fun of me for the screaming, and then I should be in the clear.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text:
Mogu are thugs. They have always been thugs.

Only when they ruled their empires in the old stories did they ever know any kind of magic.

But these mogu are using arcane portals and spells. We need to stop them!

adventurer, look for any artifacts the mogu are using to cast their magics with. I saw a number of their collectors and reclaimers to the west and north that were gathering these items.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text: Every artifact in our possession is one less weapon in mogu hands.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text: Well done <name>. You have removed the sword from the child's hands.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Flame
passages.text:
This is one of the challenges I put upon my warriors to keep them strong and fast. Let's see how you fare.

Survive the ring for 60 seconds without getting pushed out or killed. Stay on your toes.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Flame
passages.text: The constant danger in the ring prepares us for life or death fighting we have to endure outside the wall.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Flame
passages.text: Not bad, <class>. Not bad at all.

passages.title: Warn Stoneplow
passages.text:
So much death. And more to come, if Ambassador Han's stories of the mantid are to be believed.

We must help. We must do our part to save lives.

Travel to Stoneplow. Warn them of the coming mantid attack.

I will join you with what forces I can muster once I have laid Kor's body to rest.

passages.title: Warn Stoneplow
passages.text: Mantid from the south? This is not a good day.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Blades
passages.text:
This is one of the challenges I put upon my warriors to keep them strong and fast. Let's see how you fare.

Survive the ring for 60 seconds without getting pushed out or killed. Stay on your toes.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Blades
passages.text: The constant danger in the ring prepares us for life or death fighting we have to endure outside the wall.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Blades
passages.text: Not bad, <class>. Not bad at all.

passages.title: Mantid Under Fire
passages.text:
The mantid are attacking again, and we're a bit short-handed up on the wall. In hopes that you'd help, I saved one of the more fun posts for you: the hot oil!

It's a bit more violent and a bit less scandalous than it sounds.

It's simple really. Get up on the wall, find one of the oil stations, and dump it on any of the mantid pouring up against the wall. It's very effective.

passages.title: Mantid Under Fire
passages.text: The hard part is the cleanup. Fortunately, you're not responsible for that.

passages.title: Mantid Under Fire
passages.text: You've done devastating damage to the mantid forces. The wall defenders should be able to get things under control.

passages.title: Along the Serpent's Spine
passages.text: There are mantid on top of the wall. The defenders on the ramparts are calling for help!

passages.title: Along the Serpent's Spine
passages.text: The mantid forces on the wall have been thinned.

passages.title: Upon the Ramparts
passages.text:
Some of the mantid have made it on top of the wall. There's some risk they'll route the soldiers we have posted there if their numbers are large enough.

I need you to get on top of the wall and help clear out any that have broken through.

passages.title: Upon the Ramparts
passages.text: The mantid forces on the wall have been thinned.

passages.title: Roll Club: Vale of Eternal Blossoms
passages.text:
Follow the flags. Make the checkpoints. Round the loop. Get back to me before your time is up.

Speak to me when you're ready to roll.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Thunder
passages.text:
This is one of the challenges I put upon my warriors during peaceful times to keep them strong and fast. Let's see how you fare.

Survive the ring for 90 seconds without getting pushed out or killed. Stay on your toes.

passages.title: Learn and Grow II: Tilling and Planting
passages.text:
Okay, now we've got our seeds, it's time to plant them.

First, we have to prepare the soil! You gotta till the soil and break it up to make a nice bed for our little sprouts.

Till those two plots of soil over there, then plant the seeds in them.

passages.title: Learn and Grow II: Tilling and Planting
passages.text:
Well, go ahead - bust that soil up and plant the seeds!

You aren't giving up already are you? I need your help!

passages.title: Learn and Grow II: Tilling and Planting
passages.text:
Nicely done.

Notice how those seeds sprouted immediately? That's part of what makes this valley so ideal for farming - something about the soil here just makes veggies grow like crazy!

The work's not done yet, though.

passages.title: Learn and Grow III: Tending Crops
passages.text:
My grandfather used to say "Yoonie, a cabbage is like a woman: ignore her and she'll turn rotten. Pamper her and she'll grow big and plump and you can put a ribbon on her and take her to market to show her off to your frie-" look, he was from a different time, okay?

The point is, now that our cabbages have sprouted, they need attention! Today they look a little dry, so you should water them.

Here's the old watering can grandpa left. It will always be near the field if you need it.

passages.title: Learn and Grow III: Tending Crops
passages.text:
Come to think of it, grandpa said a lot of really offensive things.

Maybe I should avoid quoting him from now on...

passages.title: Learn and Grow III: Tending Crops
passages.text:
Great, the cabbages are tended and looking good!

Today they were thirsty, but you never know what they might need. Pay close attention to your crops and tend them accordingly.

I got all kinds of advice from my grandpa, so if you're ever unsure of how to take care of something, feel free to ask!

Just make sure it's strictly related to farming...

passages.title: Learn and Grow IV: Harvesting
passages.text:
It's time for our hard work to pay off! Normally we'd have to wait a day before the crops are ready to harvest.

Fortunately, those seeds Greenfield gave us were specially designed to grow FAST. The yield won't be worth much, but they're good for stepping new farmers through the process.

Our cabbages should be ready to harvest. I'll let you do the honors, of course!

passages.title: Learn and Grow IV: Harvesting
passages.text:
Look at those... err, what do they say around here? Oh yeah, b'yoots!

Look at those b'yoots!

I think I'm getting the hang of this farmer thing.

passages.title: Learn and Grow IV: Harvesting
passages.text:
Well, those are the basics!

Till the soil, plant the seeds, tend to any threats, then wait for the results!

Today was easy, but stay on your toes: my grandfather told me all kinds of crazy stories about farming at Sunsong Ranch.

Farming ain't all giant turnips and roses, you know.

passages.title: Learn and Grow V: Halfhill Market
passages.text:
All right friend, all of that farming was just for practice!

Are you ready to try the real thing?

There's a lady by the name of Gina Mudclaw who runs the Halfhill Market, which is across the street to the south.

I heard she's looking to buy some vegetables. Since it's your first time meeting her, you shouldn't go empty-handed.

Why don't you look around the ranch and see if there are any items hiding around?

Might be that we'll find a good gift to take to our new neighbor!

passages.title: Learn and Grow V: Halfhill Market
passages.text: Hey, haven't seen your face around here before! What's your name?

passages.title: Learn and Grow V: Halfhill Market
passages.text:
Oh my, a marsh lily!

How did you know that these are my favorite? I just might take a liking to you, stranger.

Thank you!

passages.title: Mung-Mung's Vote I: A Hozen's Problem
passages.text:
I've been thinkin' about how to get into the Tiller's good graces, <name>.

Now, the Tiller's Union accepts new farmers each year, and there are five members on the voting council.

We already got Gina's vote, but we'll have to prove ourselves to the other four members of their board.

Why don't you go over and say hello to Mung-Mung? He works with Mr. Mudclaw out on the Mudclaw's farm to the northwest.

passages.title: Mung-Mung's Vote I: A Hozen's Problem
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Growing the Farm I: The Weeds
passages.text:
Hey <name>, I've been thinkin' recently about expanding my farm.

See that plot there that's just covered in weeds? If we can get rid of those weeds, we could use that land for planting.

I heard there's a farmer by the name of Gai Lan who knows a thing or two about weed whackin'.

His farm is just out west. Go talk to him and see if he'd be willing to help us.

passages.title: Growing the Farm I: The Weeds
passages.text:
Oh yeah, Farmer Yoon. I've seen him around town.

Seems like a nice enough fella.

passages.title: Enemy at the Gates
passages.text:
The mantid forces are pouring against the wall. I've arranged for some flying serpents to cut away at their forces from the air.

Would you be willing to take the reigns on one of them?

passages.title: Enemy at the Gates
passages.text:
Kun tells me you were amazing out there. You impress my man, you impress me.

Good work.

passages.title: Bloodied Skies
passages.text:
We have cannons set up on the top of the towers flanking the main gate. They are our best method to clear the skies when the flying mantid try to pass over the wall, like they are now.

Looks like you're on, <name>.

passages.title: Bloodied Skies
passages.text: You've got good aim, <class>. I'll remember that the next time the fliers come.

passages.title: Watery Woes
passages.text:
I love fishing. I'd be enjoying myself much more, however, if I had my bait and my lures. They were thrown away in a... a misunderstanding with my wife, Rin.

<Gladecaster Lang sighs.>

Should I let a whole day of fishing be ruined, just because of a little domestic squabble? No! All I need is bugs and feathers, after all, and this glade is filled with those two things.

Care to help a fisherman out?

passages.title: Watery Woes
passages.text: I refuse to not fish. Fishing's who I am!

passages.title: Watery Woes
passages.text:
Finally, someone who understands me. Fishing is what it's all about, right?

Maybe I should leave New Cifera... just pack up my things and join the Anglers, down in the south. Of course, I couldn't leave my family behind...

But still... a pandaren can dream, right?

passages.title: The Murksweats
passages.text:
Take a good look. The river nearby is swarming with these snakes. Their venom causes a condition the locals call "the murksweats."

Several refugees were bitten as they fled the temple and have already begun to show symptoms: nausea, vomiting, and intense sweating as the body rejects all fluids, causing dehydration and potentially death.

We are administering anti-venom as quickly as possible, but we'll need more venom glands. Don't bother removing the glands yourself - just bring back the whole head.

passages.title: The Murksweats
passages.text:
<Anduin is focused intently on his hands, swiftly carving venom glands from the snakes.>

Inside the jaw... two inches behind the second set of fangs...

passages.title: The Murksweats
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>. I knew you'd be hardy enough to handle it.

Judging by the sounds coming out of these refugees, I would not wish the murksweats on my worst enemy.

passages.title: Unsafe Passage
passages.text:
As we say at the temple: "Never fight a tiger with a hozen on your back."

We will deal with the sha, but first we must see to the more immediate... nuisance.

<Koro slams the writhing saurok HARD against the stone.>

Groups of refugees from the temple are heading for a camp to the north, but they're being ambushed by saurok. Help me see the next group to the camp and we'll figure out our next move from there.

passages.title: Unsafe Passage
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. We would not have made it without your help.

passages.title: Blinding the Riverblades
passages.text:
"A hooded falcon catches no quarry."

This is one of the first mantras we teach young monks at the temple. It means that even a foe as swift and lethal as a falcon can be neutralized by depriving its senses.

The saurok have scouts all over the region acting as eyes for their raiding parties.

It's time we put their eyes out, don't you think?

passages.title: Blinding the Riverblades
passages.text:
Well done. I only wish I could have accompanied you...

The blood on these hand-wraps is not my own, you know.

passages.title: Sha Can Awe
passages.text:
The sha have the mysterious ability to evoke powerful, often overwhelming, emotional responses in their victims.

As we fled the temple, senior members of the Crane Wing order stayed behind to cover our escape. They are no doubt being subjected to intense emotional trauma, and I fear they are not all strong enough to resist falling into despair.

adventurer, we have to show them there is still hope! Show them that despair CAN be defeated!

passages.title: Sha Can Awe
passages.text: Look for Crane Wing pandaren who are falling to despair and slay sha near them while I support you!

passages.title: Sha Can Awe
passages.text:
Honestly, I'm a little surprised that worked.

Pandaria is proving to be a land where the lines between metaphor and reality are blurred.

passages.title: In the House of the Red Crane
passages.text:
"Broken are the bodies wherein hopeless hearts reside - the blight of despair strikes forth from inside."

This was the last piece of wisdom the Red Crane imparted to me, just hours before the Sha outbreak. It makes sense now...

adventurer, when the Sha attacked, they broke forth from the temple's basement...

All of his teachings - the very Way of the Crane itself... it's all been preparation for facing the Sha of Despair.

The Red Crane has been expecting this conflict for centuries!

passages.title: In the House of the Red Crane
passages.text:
You have vanquished the Sha of Despair. My order can handle the remaining cleanup from here.

It seems the time has finally come to face the consequences of Shaohao's actions.

This conflict has been a long time coming - the arrival of your people was merely a catalyst. Now, your help will be necessary if Pandaria is to survive.

passages.title: A Crocolisk Tale
passages.text:
How could this crocolisk have grown so large?

Certainly, rumors exist of very old crocolisks that have grown to enormous sizes... but this female can't be more than a dozen years old.

Perhaps someone in New Cifera can shed some light on the subject.

passages.title: A Crocolisk Tale
passages.text: What's that you've got there?

passages.title: A Crocolisk Tale
passages.text:
This tail came from a crocolisk? Funny, we don't get many crocs this far upstream.

Have you seen some of the enormous fruits and vegetables that our farmers can grow? Your crocolisk grew so large for the same reason - there's something in the water.

What it is, we're not quite sure... but we count it among our blessings. Humongous vegetables are great. The odd giant crocolisk every now and again is really just a side effect.

passages.title: Mogu Make Poor House Guests
passages.text:
Leven sent Rook here to stop mogu, but there are more than Rook can kill alone.

You help? Rook will tell Leven you helped. Promise.

passages.title: Mogu Make Poor House Guests
passages.text: Rook can handle rest of mogu.  Thanks for help.  Good man.

passages.title: Freeing Mind and Body
passages.text:
Mogu stealing peoples minds! Making them do evil things.

Don't kill them, just kill the mogu, then they forget about all the mogu mind stealing and stop being evil. You should fix people like Rook is.

passages.title: Freeing Mind and Body
passages.text: Lots of villagers inside and safe now. You do good work.

passages.title: In Enemy Hands
passages.text:
The Shao-Tien Mindbenders have taken over the minds of our defenders down at Whitepetal Lake to the west. Get down there and kill the mogu that are controlling them, but don't kill the defenders! Killing their captors should free them from their mind control.

Sooner would be better. Anji might try to go down there to help soon, and her ability to restrain herself when in the heat of things is not one of the qualities I married her for.

passages.title: In Enemy Hands
passages.text: More than one pandaren is thankful for your help today, that's for sure.

passages.title: Small Comforts
passages.text:
The mindbenders at Whitepetal Lake are pulling the spirits from the corpses of the dead to inflict who-knows-what kind of torments upon them.

I've written on this scroll a rite that will release their spirits from their bodies and send them on their way. Where they go and what happens to them from there I don't know, but it will at least free them from the cruel hands of the mogu.

Read this rite over any of the fallen you find. We'll recover their bodies later.

passages.title: The Key to Success
passages.text:
The mogu have taken prisoners. They'll be tortured or worse.

Find any way you can to free them from their cages.

passages.title: The Key to Success
passages.text: I'd rather die than live as a mogu prisoner. They are not kind captors.

passages.title: The Key to Success
passages.text: Many of those you saved are back here in camp recovering. You surely have their gratitude, and mine.

passages.title: The Battle Ring
passages.text:
We have some fresh trainees that are far from being a danger to you, but in numbers, they may prove enough of a challenge. And if not, they could use the lesson in humility.

Step into the battle ring when you're ready. Don't go easy on them.

passages.title: The Battle Ring
passages.text: Step into the ring. Show them how a real <class> fights.

passages.title: The Battle Ring
passages.text: Very impressive. It seems they have much learning to do. I'll see to that.

passages.title: Water, Water Everywhere
passages.text:
How'd you like to make yourself useful?

The season's been awful dry lately. I need someone to water the crops out in the Heartland. Here's the thing: I need you to water ALL of the crops.

I keep a few kites with Wing Nga, the flightmaster across the way. Grab one of those kites, then throw water on any areas that look dry and dusty.

passages.title: Water, Water Everywhere
passages.text: Just come back when you're done. And don't break any of my kites.

passages.title: Water, Water Everywhere
passages.text: Hmph! I knew you were a good waterer when I first saw you. You've got good watering arms.

passages.title: Chasing the Chicken
passages.text:
Say, you there! <name>, was it? I've got a problem, and I need someone with better legs than mine to help me solve it.

My prize-winning chicken has flown the coop! Now she's out in the open, mingling with the other hens, wild birds, and... <gulp> ill-intentioned roosters.

My farm is west of here, south of the Skyrange. Could you find her, and bring her back to me?

passages.title: Chasing the Chicken
passages.text: I swear, she's never done this before.

passages.title: Chasing the Chicken
passages.text:
You found her! You've got an eye for fowl, kid.

I'll hold onto her for now. Don't worry, I'll make sure she's punished later.

passages.title: Pest Problems
passages.text:
One of my farmhands, Wika-Wika, has been tilling the soil in my westernmost field. I understand he's had some problems with pests.

He's got plenty of pesticide to spray the bugs that eat my crops, but I'm afraid he has no way to deal with the marmots.

Would you lend him a hand? With rampant hozen and virmen attacks, I can't afford to lose crops to simple pests.

passages.title: Pest Problems
passages.text: Well, good. That that's taken care of. Neatly done, <race>.

passages.title: Free Spirits
passages.text:
I came upon one of the Shao-Tien Soul-Render's daggers. It radiates a strong magic. I've been told it should allow you to enter their spirit vortexes.

The mogu use these to harvest spirits and bind them to their will, but I'm hoping you can use it to free the spirits.

Enter any of the spirit vortexes you can find up on the Golden Stair, and free all the captive spirits you find.

passages.title: Free Spirits
passages.text:
Very good! I'll hold onto this dagger. Perhaps we will get the chance to make more use of it later.

Thank you so much, my friend. You have a good heart.

passages.title: Weed War II
passages.text:
Ssshhay... d'you know that guy over on the farm, with the... the *hic*... the weed problem? Gai Lan, I think his name was. I love that guy, man.

Anywayshh, he said that if I *hic* sent an adventurer over to go pick his weeds, he'd get me some ale.

It's jusht a few weeds, not too many, probably.

*hic*

passages.title: Weed War II
passages.text: Thanks, mishter *hic* <name>.

passages.title: Money Matters
passages.text:
I love working in the market, although there's one aspect of this job I really dislike: collecting debts.

While most pandaren debts are simply due to laziness, there are a few unsavory characters around town who simply don't want to pay, and there's some who are just too poor.

A few people here in town owe me money. Could you go talk to them, and remind them about what they owe?

passages.title: Money Matters
passages.text: You know, it's kind of nice having a thug... er, I mean, <class>... like you around.

passages.title: Money Matters
passages.text: I'm glad that nasty business is over with. Nobody gave you any trouble, did they?

passages.title: They Don't Even Wear Them
passages.text:
A few weeks ago, a group of those jumpy little Springtail virmen broke into my lockbox and stole several handfuls of my jewelry. I've since found a few pieces, but they still have most of my collection.

If you're headed up to the Springtail Crag, in the cliffs to the north, you should keep an eye out for them. I'd love to get my jewelry back.

passages.title: They Don't Even Wear Them
passages.text: Can you believe how irresponsible and juvenile those virmen are? Don't they know how much that jewelry COST?

passages.title: They Don't Even Wear Them
passages.text:
Oh, <name>! I'd kiss you right here and now if you weren't... well, if you weren't covered in virmen dust.

Thanks, though!

passages.title: Not in Chee-Chee's Backyard
passages.text:
Not all hozen are the same. Chee-Chee's tribe was forest hozen... came from Jade Forest. Pretty easy to get along with.

The Kunzen invaders... they come from mountains, far to the north. Not nearly as nice as Chee-Chee.

They come into our green land, take our things, leave big mess behind.

Chee-Chee wants to kill them. You like to help?

passages.title: Not in Chee-Chee's Backyard
passages.text: Great! Chee-Chee knew you could do it!

passages.title: Where It Counts
passages.text:
I've been watching those Kunzen hozen, and I've noticed a consistent pattern. Whenever they're getting ready to attack, they participate in strange, barbaric rituals around their totem.

If we can disrupt this ritual, not only will we put off any impending attacks, we can deal a huge blow to their morale! So get in there, rough them up, and make as much of a mess as possible!

passages.title: Where It Counts
passages.text: What are you waiting for? Get up there and have some fun!

passages.title: Where It Counts
passages.text: Hah! They'll be cleaning that mess up for days.

passages.title: The Kunzen Legend-Chief
passages.text:
I've heard people talk about the hozen like they're just some tribe of barely-functional idiots... but that's not true! They have brains, too - they just don't all like to use them that much.

I've heard that the Kunzen tribe has two chiefs - one in charge of fighting, and one in charge of stories, lore, and history.

What I wouldn't give to see what kind of stories they tell...

passages.title: The Kunzen Legend-Chief
passages.text: I'll bet hozen legends aren't that much different than our own.

passages.title: The Kunzen Legend-Chief
passages.text:
Wow! Look at this! It's...

<Fish flips through the pages, and her face sours.>

Oh, I think that's a dirty picture. But the rest of this is very interesting! I just love learning how other creatures think. Thanks, <name>!

passages.title: You Have to Burn the Ropes
passages.text:
I, umm... well...

Oh, never mind. It was a stupid idea.

It's just that, I was thinking that maybe we can stop the Kunzen hozen from attacking us without having to, you know... KILL anything. I noticed a few ropes on the side of the mountain. I think they're using them to climb down to our farms and...

No, forget it. It was a silly idea anyways.

passages.title: You Have to Burn the Ropes
passages.text:
<Ella's face lights up.>

You did it? For me? Oh, thank you, thank you, thank you, thank you!

passages.title: The Truffle Shuffle
passages.text:
I like to bake with truffles... when I can find them. They only grow up on the Skyrange, and in very, very scarce amounts.

They're a fantastic ingredient, but we can't risk over-farming them. That's why we need to replace what we've taken. Bring me a handful of adult truffles, and plant some of these spores in their place.

passages.title: The Truffle Shuffle
passages.text: We won't need many truffles. They're for flavor only, really.

passages.title: The Truffle Shuffle
passages.text:
These will do nicely.

Now, <name>... stand closer. Let me show you a thing or two about baking...

passages.title: The Mile-High Grub
passages.text:
Have you ever tried Mushan Tail Stew? Chances are, if you have, that it was stringy and tasteless. You see, there's a trick to making the perfect Mushan Tail Stew: you need to cook it at high elevation.

I've already gathered the ingredients. Take this pot up to the Kunzen Village, up in the mountains to the west, and prepare the stew over their bonfire.

passages.title: The Mile-High Grub
passages.text:
I used to make daily trips into the mountains, just to practice making this stew.

I was younger, then.

passages.title: The Mile-High Grub
passages.text: This is fantastic! You are quite the aspiring cook, <race>.

passages.title: Simian Sabotage
passages.text:
The hozen steal from us, and we keep stealing our stuff back. It has to stop sometime.

<Farmer Yoon hands you a barrel of fireworks.>

Find some of our stolen supplies in their mountain camp to the west, and place these fireworks beside them. Hopefully, if they see the explosions, they'll think our supplies are defective and stop stealing altogether.

It's worth a shot, right?

passages.title: Simian Sabotage
passages.text: Good luck up there, <name>.

passages.title: Simian Sabotage
passages.text: Hopefully they're put off from stealing any more of our supplies. I know I personally wouldn't want to drink any explosive beer, or use an explosive rake.

passages.title: The Lost Dynasty
passages.text:
I wonder if I could bother you for another task. My daughter, the good Sentinel Commander Lyalia here, refuses to let me go into the field.

I have spent everyday in that oubliette staring at the ruins to our north, itching to investigate.

If we are where I suspect we are those ruins could contain the key we need to finding the fabled Pools of Youth!

Please, <class>! Go to those ruins and salvage any tablets that still have writing on them.

passages.title: The Lost Dynasty
passages.text:
It is one thing to research the lost dynasties. It is quite another to visit their ancient ruins.

I am giddy as I have not felt in centuries!

passages.title: The Lost Dynasty
passages.text:
Oh! Fabulous! Fabulous!

Your one trip has advanced my research more than ten years of reading dusty tomes and decaying scrolls...

And those "mogu" you saw. I have been doing some research as well as speaking to Kang on the subject.

I suspect now that they were the race of the lost dynasties that my research is derived from.

Of course, that also means that they are the ones who used to control the Pools of Youth.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text:
North! Go north to the Pools of Youth. Get some of the water but be on your guard.

The mogu list this as a "high value" target. Kang Bramblestaff will meet you there if he has not already arrived by your side.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text: Nothing like being mortal to give one a sense of urgency.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text:
You... you found the pools! The waters do exist!

Something is wrong though. I feel equal parts shadow and light swirling in this vial.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text:
While you were at the ruins dusting off tablets for my father I lost five scouts to wandering mogu patrols.

These creatures apparently have little interest in peace and are about as trustworthy as the Horde.

They are too numerous and we are too weak, however.

Go to the ruins west of here and cull the mogu numbers. They won't be expecting a <class>.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text:
Kang has been sharing stories with me about these mogu.

Apparently ages ago they ruled as emperors subjugating all free races of Pandaria and the surrounding regions. Now they are little more than hoodlums.

To see these mogu fight though, I suspect they are trying to rekindle some of their older ideals and ambitions.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Another few missions like that and we might have to make you an honorary sentinel.

passages.title: Profit Mastery
passages.text:
Two words: Tiger Blood!

This is gonna sell better than saronite back on the black market. Especially once I finish spreading a rumor about how it makes you all buff and stuff.

And this jungle is just full of tigers. Can you round up a few vials of tiger blood for me? I'll cut you in on the scam.

passages.title: Profit Mastery
passages.text: I like hunting with Nesingwary and all but he's in it for the hunting. I'm in it for the profit, and he doesn't pay us.

passages.title: Profit Mastery
passages.text: Great! This stuff is gonna make me a mint back in Kalimdor. Here's your cut.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text:
Mogu do NOT use arcane magics.

They are thugs. They have always been thugs. Only when they ruled their empires in the old stories did they ever know any kind of magic.

But these mogu are using arcane portals and old artifacts. We need to stop them!

adventurer, look for any artifacts the mogu are using to cast their magics with. I saw piles of these items being collected near the Ruins of Korja south of here.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text: Every artifact in our possession is one less weapon in mogu hands.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text: Well done <name>. You have removed the sword from the child's hands.

passages.title: The Stoneplow Convoy
passages.text:
Help me, adventurer. These poor pandaren are in need of healing, and my powers are weakened.

I did find an old tome in my collection that allowed me to convert the herbs you collected earlier into a healing poultice.

Use this on the injured pandaren and it should get them back on their feet.

passages.title: The Stoneplow Convoy
passages.text: These mantid are a much bigger threat than I think even the pandaren give them credit for.

passages.title: The Stoneplow Convoy
passages.text:
It has been a long time since I rolled up my sleeves and helped the needy. In my lust for immortality I forgot why I became a priest.

Thank you for reminding me there is good in this world worth fighting for, <name>.

passages.title: Warn Stoneplow
passages.text:
My father gave me his life. Tyrande gave me her trust. My sentinels gave me their allegiance.

It is time I repaid them all.

With Brojai dead we can mop up the remaining mogu. The next threat is the mantid.

Go north to Stoneplow and lend them your help. Tell them I will be bringing what sentinels I can muster to aid in the defense of their city against the mantid.

passages.title: Warn Stoneplow
passages.text: Mantid from the south? This is not a good day.

passages.title: The Mantid
passages.text:
The mantid! They came out of nowhere and smashed our convoy to ruin, scattering our people this way and that.

Now they are preparing to hit Stoneplow.

Please, <class>, destroy some of these beasts before they get sufficient numbers to flank our home.

If my cousin, Ambassador Len, is still alive and at our convoy he should be able to reward you for your help.

passages.title: The Mantid
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, <class>! I've never seen anybody stand up to the mantid like that before.

Well, other than the Shado-Pan, of course...

passages.title: The Blastmaster
A Dish for Gina
passages.text: Bringing food to me on the busiest market day? What a sweetheart you are!

passages.title: A Dish for Old Hillpaw
passages.text:
I haven't had this dish since my wife died. Somehow, she must have sent you to me.

Thank you, <race>.

passages.title: A Dish for Haohan
passages.text: Charbroiled Tiger Steak for me? How did you know this was my favorite dish?

passages.title: A Dish for Jogu
passages.text: Nothing like a delicious cold brew, and some Sauteed Carrots to wash it down.

passages.title: The Waters of Youth
passages.text:
She is headstrong, my little Lyalia. I should have known she would try to challenge the Lord Reclaimer.

Since her mother died, I forsook much of the time I should have spent with her in search of immortality, insisting that we could live forever, together.

And now my obsession has cost my little Lyalia her life.

Please, adventurer, when she wakes, tell her I love her.

passages.title: The Waters of Youth
passages.text: He... he shouldn't have done that! He shouldn't have paid for my mistake!

passages.title: Call Out Their Leader
passages.text:
Clearly, you are a hero come to aid us.

Slay the Bataari Tribe in the Kun-Lai Pass to the northwest until the Bataari Fire-Warrior is angered enough to appear. Dispatch him.

passages.title: Call Out Their Leader
passages.text: If the war leader of the yaungol is slain, surely our village will be saved and the refugees will be able to return to their farms.

passages.title: Call Out Their Leader
passages.text: We are delivered! I was right about you, <class>.

passages.title: Hit Medicine
passages.text:
Our warriors are fighting to keep the yaungol at bay in the Kun-Lai Pass to the northwest.

Take this liniment. It is a powerful medicine that has been passed down in my family over the generations.

Use the dit da jow to heal the injured warriors if you do not have healing powers of your own to use on them.

passages.title: Hit Medicine
passages.text:
You have my thanks, <name>. You have shown great honor through your actions.

I hope that my family's dit da jow was of some use to you.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
Deep in the wilds rests the Temple of the Red Crane, home of the great Chi-Ji and his most devout followers. I suspect they'll know something about what happened here.

The temple is located on the southern coast of the wilds, where the Krasarang River meets the sea.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
I see... So the sha have seeped out as far as the province already, have they?

Well, I hate to break it to you, but the temple is also overrun with sha. Those of us who haven't been killed or... possessed, or whatever, are fleeing for our very lives.

If you defeated the sha at Zhu's Bastion, I have to implore you to help us deal with them here.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
Deep in the wilds rests the Temple of the Red Crane, home of the great Chi-Ji and his most devout followers. I suspect they'll know something about what happened here.

The temple is located on the southern coast of the wilds, where the Krasarang River meets the sea.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
I see... So the sha have seeped out as far as the province already, have they?

Well, I hate to break it to you, but the temple is also overrun with sha. Those of us who haven't been killed or... possessed, or whatever, are fleeing for our very lives.

If you defeated the sha at Zhu's Bastion, I have to implore you to help us deal with them here.

passages.title: Enraged Vengeance
passages.text:
<The Swordmistress does not look well. There's a darkness to her eyes uncharacteristic of the pandaren.>

I don't think I've ever been as... as furious as now. What betrayal!

I fought them off when they attacked, killed a few here, but Merchant Shi is too much of a coward to let me go and finish the job!

You, do it for me. Kill them. Kill them all.

passages.title: Enraged Vengeance
passages.text: It is satisfying to hear that our enemies are dead. Perhaps you can use one of my bodyguard's weapons.

passages.title: A Gift For Tina
passages.text:
That Tina Mudclaw is in the Halfhill Market today, visiting her sister. She's really nice, but she's really hard to get gifts for!

There's a little jewel that can be found in the cliffs to the north. It's called a chrysoberyl, and it changes color when you hold it. I'll bet she doesn't have one of THOSE!

Look inside the virmen caves. I bet you'll find one really fast.

passages.title: A Gift For Tina
passages.text: Hey there, <name>! Nice to see you again.

passages.title: A Gift For Tina
passages.text:
<Tina holds the gem in her hands, and watches it change from a pale blue to a bright red.>

A chrysoberyl? That's so sweet! Was this Andi's idea?

Of course I already have several... but this one is beautiful, too. I'll add it to the collection.

passages.title: A Gift For Chee Chee
passages.text:
That crazy Chee Chee is actually pretty neat. Mah always said that hozen were nothing but trouble, but... I guess he's just a better hozen then the rest of them.

We should do something nice for him! Those mountain hozen in the west make some really fancy stir fry, and keep bowls of it inside their little hozen houses.

I bet Chee Chee would love some!

passages.title: A Gift For Chee Chee
passages.text: Mmm?

passages.title: A Gift For Chee Chee
passages.text:
For me? Me, Chee Chee?

This brings Chee Chee back to when Chee Chee was little wikkin' baby. Chee Chee's mama used to make it just like this.

passages.title: A Gift For Sho
passages.text:
Sho - that girl who lives up in the mountains - is in town today. I saw her walking toward the Halfhill Market.

Such a long walk... she must be hungry! And I think I know just the thing that she'll like.

The hozen up on the Skyrange cook a soup out of fish and apples. It sounds gross, I know... but it's awesome. You'll find it near their big, scary totem.

passages.title: A Gift For Sho
passages.text: Oh! Hello, <name>.

passages.title: A Gift For Sho
passages.text:
I was famished! How'd you know? Who told you?

Andi, huh? That kid's gonna grow up to be a real heartbreaker someday...

passages.title: A Gift For Fish
passages.text:
That Fish Fellreed is kind of weird. First of all, her name's Fish. That's weird.

Once you talk to her, though, she's really a nice lady. Did you know that she's an animal lover?

I've got an idea! The Kunzen hozen, in the mountains to the west, make little animal statues and put them in their huts to scare off bad guys. I bet Fish would LOVE something weird like that!

passages.title: A Gift For Fish
passages.text: Hey, <name>! What's up?

passages.title: A Gift For Fish
passages.text:
Aww, look at him! He's ADORABLE! With his fuzzy little tail, and his...

<She composes herself.>

I mean, ah... thanks, dude. It's pretty cool.

passages.title: A Gift For Ella
passages.text:
That poor Ella. She's so shy! I saw her standing in the Halfhill Market, looking really hungry, but afraid to talk to any of the chefs.

We should bring her some food! And not any boring food - something special.

The Kunzen hozen make spicy shrimp dumplings from ingredients they've stolen from our farms. I don't like spicy food, but Ella might!

passages.title: A Gift For Ella
passages.text: Oh, umm... hi.

passages.title: A Gift For Ella
passages.text:
You didn't have to do this! I didn't need any... any...

<Ella eyes the dumplings, and her mouth begins to water.>

Well, maybe I was a little hungry. Thanks, <name>. And give my thanks to Andi, as well.

passages.title: A Gift For Fung
passages.text:
Farmer Fung is pretty mean, and just a little scary. Mah always said that he was one of the best farmers in the valley, though.

I think I know the perfect gift for a mean, kind of scary guy like him.

There's some big plainshawks that circle the hills to the west of here. You should get one, find a big piece of meat, and then ask Kol Ironpaw to grill it up!

passages.title: A Gift For Fung
passages.text: Harrumph!

passages.title: A Gift For Fung
passages.text:
Hey! Where'd you get that? I thought they were out of plainshawk!

Andi asked you to get this for me? Huh. Maybe I underestimated that kid.

passages.title: A Gift For Old Hillpaw
passages.text:
Old Hillpaw has about a million chickens on his farm... but that's not what he REALLY loves.

I saw. He collects blue feathers.

I don't realy know where to get a blue feather around here, but I do know where to find some blue pearls!

Check the oysters in Cattail Lake to the northwest. I'm sure a blue pearl will look nice with his feather collection!

passages.title: A Gift For Old Hillpaw
passages.text: <name>! You startled me.

passages.title: A Gift For Old Hillpaw
passages.text:
Well would you look at that! I'll have to keep this somewhere that the chickens can't get to.

Did Andi tell you to get this for me? Funny kid, that one.

passages.title: A Gift For Haohan
passages.text:
Haohan Mudclaw is the big boss of the Tillers union and the richest guy in the Valley! He's been nice to let me stay here, so I want to do something nice for him.

He likes expensive stuff, like ruby shards, but I don't have a lot of money, so I need to get him something else.

I know! I've seen a great big fish in Cattail Lake! We should get one of its teeth as a gift!

passages.title: A Gift For Haohan
passages.text: Need something, <class>?

passages.title: A Gift For Haohan
passages.text:
Well, would you look at that! You don't see a tooth like THAT everyday.

You been hunting sharks, <class>?

Thank you, <name>. And send my thanks to Andi, as well.

passages.title: A Gift For Jogu
passages.text:
Sometimes I feel sad for Jogu. He's the only jinyu around, and I don't think he has any friends. Other than his smelly bottle, of course.

You know what? I've got an idea. Farmer Yoon has a basket of craneberries inside his house, and a few apples as well. I'm sure you could bring them to the stillmaster in the Halfhill Market and get him to brew something special for Jogu.

passages.title: A Gift For Jogu
passages.text: Hmm?

passages.title: A Gift For Jogu
passages.text:
<Jogu takes a long swig from the hooch.>

That'sh it! I've got a new favorite drink. An' it'sh this one!

You know what, <name>? You're alright. I mean it, man!

passages.title: A Gift For Gina
passages.text:
Have you seen Gina Mudclaw, the market girl? She has it all - looks, brains, and nice big tummy. Could you deliver a gift for me?

I wanted to pick some orchids that grow on top of the big hills to the west, but I can't climb that high. Could you pick a few and bring them to Gina?

Oh, and when you see her... tell her I said "hi".

passages.title: A Gift For Gina
passages.text: Hey there!

passages.title: A Gift For Gina
passages.text:
These are beautiful! Did you get these for me?

Ahh... so they're from Andi, are they? I think I know somebody who's getting a kiss on the forehead later this afternoon...

passages.title: The Soul-Gatherer
passages.text: A single large mogu performing a ritual on the lake caught your attention while you were killing the other mogu in the area. It seems unwise to let his ritual complete.

passages.title: The Soul-Gatherer
passages.text: <He looks at you expectantly.>

passages.title: The Soul-Gatherer
passages.text: <As you hand the beads to He, his smile suggests that he understands perfectly what they symbolize. He nods approvingly.>

passages.title: Gauging Our Progress
passages.text:
The time for war is at hand, <name>!

We've been training these natives non-stop since you left, and I believe they're as good as they're going to get.

See for yourself. Check in with the others and return with your findings.

We must rely on our enemy being somehow... even less prepared.

passages.title: Gauging Our Progress
passages.text: How is our combat training coming along?

passages.title: Gauging Our Progress
passages.text:
At least they're confident.

That might count for something.

passages.title: Last Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text:
These hozen are behaving most unnaturally, <name>. Marching in formation? In armor?

This troubles me. We must discuss it at another time, however. I have come to ask for your assistance.

The ancient fresco, where last we spoke, is nearly unveiled. I am certain that it holds ancient wisdom - knowledge that the emperor wanted us to remember.

My meditations alone may not be enough to discern its meaning. Please, take this heirloom to the shrine of my ancestors. I shall require their assistance.

passages.title: Last Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text:
<Lorewalker Cho shudders, in spite of himself.>

The legends... they're true!

passages.title: At the Yak Wash
passages.text:
Look, my father is crazy. I love him, but he's crazy.

These yaungol managed to completely obliterate our ranch and scattered our yaks every which way.

If I know my father though, he's going to try to go head to head with the yaungol to get the yaks back.

Can you help us round up some of the yaks so my father doesn't do anything stupid?

Just ride them over to the Yak Wash so we can clean them up and sell them to the grummles.

passages.title: At the Yak Wash
passages.text:
The grummles always insist they have better luck with cleaned yaks.

As long as they pay more I'm not going to argue. We need the gold. Now more than ever.

passages.title: At the Yak Wash
passages.text: Well done, stranger! Hopefully we'll be able to cash these in and recoup some of the damages the yaungol inflicted.

passages.title: Back in Yak
passages.text:
I wasn't lying about your reward. Here, take these washed yaks to the grummle caravan master Eightcoins.

You can find him at the Grummle Bazaar west of here. He'll credit us and give you a delivery fee.

He may be short, but he is our biggest customer.

Return to me if you lose the yaks. More often than not they just come right back here anyway. Once they've been cleaned that is.

passages.title: Back in Yak
passages.text: And what have we here?

passages.title: Back in Yak
passages.text: Ah! I can smell the luck from here. The Muskpaws always have good yaks for sale.

passages.title: Love's Labor
passages.text:
Can I trouble you for another favor?

We're way behind schedule, and this jade shipment is the last we need to finish the great statue.

I've got my hands full, so could you run this ore over to the other foremen?

Historian Dinh, Surveyor Sawa, and Kitemaster Shoku can all be found around the base of the statue. Taskmaster Emi is directing production at the top of the statue.

We're on a deadline, so make sure you do it fast! Time's a wasting!

passages.title: Love's Labor
passages.text: Did you deliver the jade in time?

passages.title: Love's Labor
passages.text: What, done already? You're quite the runner, <class>. You ever thought about making a living out of this?

passages.title: The Waterspeaker's Staff
passages.text:
There is great dissent in Inkgill, <race>. Elder Shai Hu drank the sha-corrupted waters of the mere, and forced the others to do the same. When I protested, Orachi of the town guard confiscated my ritual staff and banished me.

Now, I am not only an exile, I am unable to speak with the waters that once gave me guidance!

I am not a fighter. But if you are, perhaps you can recover my staff from Orachi? He is in town to our north.

passages.title: The Waterspeaker's Staff
passages.text: Have you found the staff?

passages.title: The Waterspeaker's Staff
passages.text: Good. Now we have some hope of redeeming this situation.

passages.title: Emergency Response
passages.text:
Your companions have made themselves at home in our land, and brought with them a dangerous conflict.

The full extent of their destruction here we cannot yet know. Already it is... unspeakable.

Nevertheless, to forsake your friends out of spite would be against our way. Any that yet live are doubtlessly wounded and in desperate need of care.

These fireworks were to celebrate the statue's completion. Use them near your companions to signal Mishi, and she will bear them off to safety.

passages.title: Emergency Response
passages.text:
My thoughts will be with your fallen companions, traveler.

May their wounds mend well.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your Admiral Taylor has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs in the apothecary's house back in Binan Village.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
<name>, is that you? I can't believe we survived the destruction of the Jade Serpent.

Some of us anyway.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your General Nazgrim has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs in the apothecary's house back in Binan Village.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
Where have you been, <name>? Nevermind. As you can see, we survived the battle at the Jade Serpent.

Unfortunately, so did... they.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your General Nazgrim has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs in the apothecary's house across the way.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
Where have you been, <name>? Nevermind. As you can see, we survived the battle at the Jade Serpent.

Unfortunately, so did... they.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your General Nazgrim has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
Where have you been, <name>? Nevermind. As you can see, we survived the battle at the Jade Serpent.

Unfortunately, so did... they.

passages.title: Westwind Rest
passages.text:
<Admiral Taylor winces in pain.>

Jade Forest was a disaster. 

Anduin's gone. We lost some good people. We didn't stop the Horde from advancing into the continent. 

But I think I've found a way to get the locals on our side. You just helped fight off some of these "yaungol", no?

I hear yaungol sacked Westwind Rest, a local village. We've been told that two groups of survivors have camped out along the road west out of town.

We help them out, maybe they'll consider siding with the Allliance.

passages.title: Westwind Rest
passages.text: I will not rest until our people are returned and this village rebuilt.

passages.title: Westwind Rest
passages.text:
Well... we are alive, and that is better than we could have hoped for without your help.

But, if this is truly to become a base of operations for you, and if we are to join your Alliance, there is one more thing you must do to guarantee our security.

passages.title: Challenge Accepted
passages.text:
The yaungol have always been a difficult, proud people, but never this violent or aggressive. 

I do not know what has prompted this change in their behavior, but we don't have time to find out, now. We fear for our lives and livelihoods as long as Ur-Bataar, leader of the Bataari yaungol, lives.

Go, set the banner in his camp ablaze to challenge him, and then defeat him in battle. Only then will we be secure.

passages.title: Challenge Accepted
passages.text:
You did it! At the very least, we have justice, and safety, though in the process we have lost so much.

Regardless, it has been decided. We will join the Alliance, and with your help, rebuild this village.

passages.title: Challenge Accepted
passages.text:
The yaungol have always been a difficult, proud people, but never this violent or aggressive. 

I do not know what has prompted this change in their behavior, but we don't have time to find out, now. We fear for our lives and livelihoods as long as Ur-Bataar, leader of the Bataari yaungol, lives.

Go, set the banner in his camp ablaze to challenge him, and then defeat him in battle. Only then will we be secure.

passages.title: Challenge Accepted
passages.text: As long as Ur-Bataar lives, we cannot have peace.

passages.title: Challenge Accepted
passages.text:
You did it! At the very least, we have justice, and safety, though in the process we have lost so much.

Regardless, it has been decided. We will join the Horde, and with your help, rebuild this village.

passages.title: Farmer Fung's Vote I: Yak Attack
passages.text:
The next voting member on the Tiller's council is Farmer Fung, and it's easy to see why.

That man's vegetables are the biggest in the valley! I only hope that someday I can grow pumpkins as big as his.

If we hope to join the Tillers, he would be the next person to convince.

passages.title: Farmer Fung's Vote I: Yak Attack
passages.text: Oh? You're with that new farmer in town, aren't you?

passages.title: Farmer Fung's Vote II: On the Loose
passages.text:
You want my vote for Farmer Yoon? Ha! You're joking, right?

Listen, I'm not going to vote for some citypaw with no lick a' knowledge about farming the earth.

It would be an embarrassment to farm alongside you or that Yoon shmuck.

Now let me deal with my own problems. Some devil let my prize yaks loose, and now they're running wild northwest of Halfhill.

If I could just get my yaks back, then maybe I'd be able to sleep at night.

passages.title: Farmer Fung's Vote II: On the Loose
passages.text:
<Farmer Fung stares at you with his jaw on the floor.>

I... I can't believe... YOU recovered all of my prized shagskins!

Do you... do you know what this means to me?

My family's only been good at two things - raising enormous vegetables and raising yaks.

The shagskins you see are the result of generations of work.

You have saved my family's legacy, <name>.

passages.title: Nana's Vote I: Nana's Secret Recipe
passages.text:
The next vote we'll need is from Nana Mudclaw. She's Haohan's grandmother, and she's been a Tiller longer than you and I have been alive!

She's still working at the Tillers building in Halfhill. Why don't you pay her a visit?

passages.title: Nana's Vote I: Nana's Secret Recipe
passages.text: Yes, Nana Mudclaw... that is me. I may be old, dear, but I haven't lost my memory. Old Man Whitewhiskers, on the other hand, is another story.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote I: Bungalow Break-In
passages.text:
This is going to be tough, <name>.

The last vote we need comes from Haohan Mudclaw, the head of the Tillers Union.

I know he wasn't too keen on us to start, but we've learned so much about farming, I'm sure he'll have a change of heart!

Go speak to him. You can be very convincing, right?

passages.title: Haohan's Vote I: Bungalow Break-In
passages.text: What do you want?

passages.title: Growing the Farm II: The Broken Wagon
passages.text:
Hey <name>. I've been looking at that wagon every day, day in and day out, since the day I moved in. Quite an eyesore, don't you think?

I heard in town that Fish Fellreed is quite handy with tools. She might be able to fix it up, and then we could turn that patch of land into a plot for farming.

Why don't you talk to her and see if she'd be willing to do the job?

passages.title: Growing the Farm II: The Broken Wagon
passages.text: You need my help fer somethin'? You came to the right gal!

passages.title: Haohan's Vote III: Pure Poison
passages.text:
All right, <name>. This is our big chance!

Mr. Mudclaw's farm is in big trouble. Those mountain hozen are coming down at night, wrecking his crops and eating his hard-earned harvest.

We've got to get rid of them for good, and I know just how to do it.

Back in the day, my grandpa showed me how to mix a wounding poison to deal with the pests on the farm.

The virmen warrens to the north hold the key ingredients for my mixture.

Don't look so worried, <name>! I'm pretty sure this is going to work.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote III: Pure Poison
passages.text: The hozen are going to get a big surprise!

passages.title: Haohan's Vote III: Pure Poison
passages.text:
You got the ingredients? Good work!

Now I just need to make the concoction.

passages.title: Lost and Lonely
passages.text:
The starving, mangy dog whines piteously and attempts a brief wag of its tail.

It looks like it could use a good meal right about now.

passages.title: Lost and Lonely
passages.text: A light comes into the dog's eyes. It seems to recognize you.

passages.title: Lost and Lonely
passages.text:
The dog perks its ears up at the sight of the juicy steak.

As soon as you throw it down, the dog starts eating ravenously.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote IV: Melons For Felons
passages.text:
All right, now I happen to know that those mountain hozen love a delicious, sweet melon.

Mr. Haohan's last harvest of melons got stolen, so we're going to have to grow some of our own.

Once we have our harvest, we'll use them to lure the nasty hozen's leader out of its cave!

passages.title: Haohan's Vote IV: Melons For Felons
passages.text: Let's make sure we grow some good melons, <name>. Those crafty hozen only like the sweetest melons.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote IV: Melons For Felons
passages.text:
Wow, <name>! Those are some big melons. Those are hard to grow, and I should know because I've tried! 

I don't know how I would run this place without you, <name>.

passages.title: Growing the Farm III: The Mossy Boulder
passages.text:
Now that we're officially members of the Tillers Union, Mr. Mudclaw said he'd be happy to help us upturn this big ole' rock in the middle of our field.

Once we clear away that stone, I've got something special planned.

Run down and give him a holler to let him know that we're ready.

passages.title: Growing the Farm III: The Mossy Boulder
passages.text: Yoon needs a neighbor to lend a hand, eh? Well I'll be plenty happy to oblige.

passages.title: Learn and Grow I: Seeds
passages.text:
Well, first things first! I'm going to need lots of help 'round here.

If we're going to be partners, you've got to learn how to harvest crops, and if you wanna harvest crops you gotta plant seeds!

Now it's my understanding that a mister, uh... Grainfell? No, that wasn't it... Greedfill? That doesn't sound right...

Greenfield! That's his name! He's the man to see for seeds.

Greenfield's got a stall over at Halfhill Market, directly southeast of here - go see him and pick up some vegetable seeds.

passages.title: Learn and Grow I: Seeds
passages.text:
How'd it go, partner? Did you get those seeds from Groanfur?

Err... Greenfield?

passages.title: Learn and Grow I: Seeds
passages.text:
He waved at me! And he gave you the first pack of seeds for free?

Well, what a nice guy!

You're doing a great job so far. Here's a little... seed money. Hah!

passages.title: An Unexpected Advantage
passages.text:
Things seem to be goin' our way more and more lately, <name>. I was out doin some explorin' when I came upon this little beauty.

<Sully gestures to the ballista to his right.>

Problem is she's one of a set and the other one is still in pieces. I'd have gotten it together by now if those pesky Grimleers hadn't ambushed me and taken some of the gears and bolts.

Hey, ye seem to be pretty good at handlin' the natives. Ye wouldn't mind goin' and helpin' ol'Sully out would ye?

passages.title: An Unexpected Advantage
passages.text: Did ye find my missing gears and bolts?

passages.title: An Unexpected Advantage
passages.text:
Well these aren't as good as she deserves, but it will have to work.

<Sully pats the dismantled ballista.>

I'll get 'er up and runnin' in no time, just ye watch!

passages.title: Trouble on the Farmstead
passages.text:
I... I escaped from Farmer Chow's, to the southeast of here. It's been taken over by yaungol, but the old man and his wife just won't give it up!

Please, go there and help him out. Maybe if you do, he'll be willing to send some folks back here and help you guys farm up some food for the new town?

passages.title: Trouble on the Farmstead
passages.text:
You're a sight for sore eyes, <class>.

I'll be glad to help you Alliance fellas out. First though, you need to help me get my farm back.

passages.title: Trouble on the Farmstead
passages.text:
I... I escaped from Farmer Chow's, to the southeast of here. It's been taken over by yaungol, but the old man and his wife just won't give it up!

Please, go there and help him... Maybe if you do, he'll be willing to send some folks back here and help you guys farm up some food for the new town?

passages.title: Trouble on the Farmstead
passages.text:
You're a sight for sore eyes, <class>.

I'll be glad to help you Horde fellas out. First though, you need to help me get my farm back.

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text:
Mobility is going to be key to maintaining our foothold in this new land. Problem is, there's no way to maintain mobility without mounts, and... well, we don't have many of those here, now do we?

The local yaks seem to make good mounts. At least, the local pandaren say they do. Why don't you go round some up for us?

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text: It's going to take more yaks than that to get this place back into fightin' condition, <name>, yes it is.

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text: These yaks will do the trick nicely. Good work, <name>. I'm feeling better about this whole situation already.

passages.title: ... and the Pot, Too!
passages.text:
Sure, I'm willing to help you guys out. But we need to eat, too! I don't even have a pot to cook in! Let alone ingredients to put in it!

Here's a list of the things that I need. Now get!

passages.title: ... and the Pot, Too!
passages.text: Do you have everything from the list?!

passages.title: ... and the Pot, Too!
passages.text: Well there you go. We should be plenty good, now.

passages.title: What Lurks Below
passages.text:
Legend tells of a great beast in the forest to the north. My son is missing and I fear he may have wandered too near its lair....

Head northwest to Krasari Falls and look for a mysterious whirlpool - this is the key to revealing what is hidden there. Kill the wretched beast and recover any clues to my son's whereabouts.

passages.title: What Lurks Below
passages.text: What news of my son?

passages.title: What Lurks Below
passages.text:
My son's ring?  What does this mean?

<Rassan appears thoughtful.>

The situation is grim, but not without hope.  My son is careless with his belongings, so perhaps he simply threw it into the pool?  Thank you for your help <name>, I will not soon forget this great favor you have done for me.

passages.title: Jagged Abalone
passages.text:
Pandaren have been harvesting jagged abalone in this area for generations. Now it's time for you to learn the ritual.

The abalone can be found just northeast of here in narsong trench. Be careful, we have noticed increased shark activity in that area recently.

passages.title: Jagged Abalone
passages.text: Did you see any sharks down there?

passages.title: Jagged Abalone
passages.text: Oh!  Looks like you found plenty of abalone out there.  Great job <name>!

passages.title: Fishing for a Bruising
passages.text:
The riverblade saurok clan is attacking one of our local fishing expeditions! They need help right away!

Thin those saurok out and help that expedition return safely!

passages.title: Fishing for a Bruising
passages.text: The expedition is safe.  Thank you <name>.

passages.title: The Burlap Trail: To Burlap Waystation
passages.text:
Bad fortune for grummles today. Hozen have begun to ravage! They attack our supply line to the Serpent's Spine.

Can you help? We are not fighters. We are grummles. Good fortune to those who help grummles.

Go with a group of grummles to the Burlap Waystation. Keep them safe. Make sure at least one grummle survives.

Grummles shall reward. Grummles always reward.

passages.title: The Burlap Trail: To Burlap Waystation
passages.text: Good fortune to friends of grummles.

passages.title: The Burlap Trail: To Burlap Waystation
passages.text: Many thanks and fortune to you, friend of grummles. But the journey to the Serpent's Spine is not safe yet.

passages.title: Who Knew Fish Liked Eggs?
passages.text:
Great cranes have been nesting in this area for generations. The Narsong Spires provide a sheltered area to rear their young.

Their pristine eggs are revered as bait for catching the silver goby. Retrieve a crane egg and see if you can catch a goby!

passages.title: Who Knew Fish Liked Eggs?
passages.text: Did you catch a silver goby?

passages.title: Who Knew Fish Liked Eggs?
passages.text: The elusive silver goby!  You truly are becoming an angler <name>!

passages.title: A Monkey Idol
passages.text:
Before, grummles keep hozen from ravaging by bribing with food.

But now the Broketooth hozen south of here have their big magic idols. The Ook of Dook has trained them to use their idols to get power from sacrifices.

They are using them to kill grummles!

You must destroy these idols!

For every idol, there is a chief. Kill the chief and throw corpse on their altar.

passages.title: A Monkey Idol
passages.text: Hozen are learning that it is most bad fortune to get sacrificed on one's own altar.

passages.title: A Monkey Idol
passages.text:
A confident hozen is a dangerous hozen.

Thank you for your help, friend of grummles.

passages.title: Thumping Knucklethump
passages.text:
The Knucklethump hozen have new chief, the Ook of Dook.

He sees fear in the west, anger in the south, hatred in the north, and yaungols in the east.

And so he sets his hozen to ravage, gathering food and supplies for coming famine.

They are many Knucklethumps and dangerous.

Please, Luckydo, can you defeat their fighters?

passages.title: Thumping Knucklethump
passages.text: It is sad so many hozen must die.

passages.title: Thumping Knucklethump
passages.text: You are a true luckydo.

passages.title: Hozen Love Their Keys
passages.text:
The hozen have a yeti! They call it Old Poot Poot and keep it at the back of their cave.

Hozen are normally scared of yeti, but now they feed it grummles.

They have a Hunter Chief, Cho Cho the Wicked. Can you see if he has a key on him to the yeti shackles?

Bad fortune for hozen if a yeti is loose in their fort.

passages.title: Hozen Love Their Keys
passages.text: A luckydo would be wise to never travel near a yeti on a dirty yak.

passages.title: Hozen Love Their Keys
passages.text: Oh wow that looked like one wild ride!

passages.title: The Snackrifice
passages.text:
They took my grummles! Hozen don't eat grummles, but yeti do. And the Knucklethumps have a yeti.

Please rescue my grummles. Cut them down or let them out of cages. Rescue them any way you can.

Many fortunes and rewards if you do this.

passages.title: The Snackrifice
passages.text:
Today is a day of many good and bad fortunes. Bad fortune that hozen stole my grummles. Good fortune that my <race> saves my grummles. Bad fortune that so many hozen must die to learn lesson. Good fortune that humans are luckydos and know how to fight.

Grummles are not fighters. We carry, we explore, and we are content.

passages.title: Grummle! Grummle! Grummle!
passages.text:
Now that grummles are rescued, we need to rescue our supplies.

The Ook of Dook is only chief because he has supplies.

Go to the Dooker Dome area north west of here. Take some grummles with you. Keep them safe and get them near supply crates.

Grummles know what to do from there.

Rabbitsfoot and I will meet you there.

passages.title: Grummle! Grummle! Grummle!
passages.text: Grummles are good at carrying things.

passages.title: Grummle! Grummle! Grummle!
passages.text: Now that hozen king is going to learn why it is bad fortune to cheat grummles.

passages.title: The Leader Hozen
passages.text:
The time has come to face the Ook of Dook. We beat him, and the hozen won't have someone telling them to ravage.

Here is the plan: Yakshoe will lead Tassle in to arena and scare away Chomp Chomp.

Then, you sneak in and fight the Ook of Dook while his hozen are distracted by the yeti rampaging through their home.

We'll meet you back at Kota Basecamp with a big reward. Good fortune to you, friend of grummles.

passages.title: The Leader Hozen
passages.text: The Ook of Dook is dead! Hurray!

passages.title: Armored Carp
passages.text:
Armored Carp are a delicacy around these parts.

Unfortunately we can't fish them up since they snap our hooks with their powerful jaws. Take this fishing spear and see if you can catch a few for us.

passages.title: Armored Carp
passages.text: Any luck with that fishing spear?

passages.title: Armored Carp
passages.text: Careful with that carp, <name>.  They have been known to bite fingers off!

passages.title: Traffic Issues
passages.text:
Yaungols are attacking our Burlap Trail. This is most bad fortune for grummles.

We use that trail to carry supplies to the Serpent's Spine. Without supplies, the defenders of the wall are in danger.

Grummles are packers and explorers, not fighters. Could you be a luckydo for us and stop the yaungol blockade?

passages.title: Traffic Issues
passages.text: It is good fortune that a <race> comes to help grummles. Good fortune to friend of grummles.

passages.title: Roadside Assistance
passages.text:
A luckydo remembers to bring incense on a journey in to the mountains. The smellier the luck the better.

Can you journey up the road to One Keg and light the incense you find along the way?

This will give good fortune to grummles that must travel the road.

Brother Lintpocket can give you many rewards. Speak to him when you arrive.

passages.title: Roadside Assistance
passages.text: The pungent smell of lucky burning burlap in the morning is a big Luckydo.

passages.title: Roadside Assistance
passages.text: Welcome to One Keg! Gateway to Burlap Trail and Mount Neverest.

passages.title: Resupplying One Keg
passages.text:
If you're looking for the best supplies in Kun-Lai you've come to the right place! Oh sure, it looks a bit empty. Don't let appearances deceive you..

Oh, who am I kidding?! Between the hozen attacks, and the sprites pillaging what few supplies we do get, my stock has dwindled to a dangerous level.

If you could help me recover some of my supplies I should have enough to contribute to your journey.

passages.title: Resupplying One Keg
passages.text: Did you manage to get some of my supplies back?

passages.title: Resupplying One Keg
passages.text:
Oh thank you, <name>! If I just cut off the nibbled pieces and repair the minor damage, I may still be able to sell these.

Once your cart is ready to go I'll have the supplies I promised loaded up!

passages.title: Mogu?! Oh No-gu!
passages.text:
I know your friends are worried about the animating statues over at Mogujia, but I'll tell you what you should really be worried about.

Where there are animated statues, there are mogu. I don't know if you've seen one before, but if you haven't...

Well, let's just say mogu are bad, bad, news.

While you're dealing with whatever else you're doing, you need to get the mogu behind the trouble!

passages.title: Mogu?! Oh No-gu!
passages.text: Did you find him? Is he dead? No? Oh, man. Don't make me worried!

passages.title: Mogu?! Oh No-gu!
passages.text:
Oh, thank goodness! You've saved all of our skins, believe me.

You have no idea how much trouble those guys can stir up.

Err, or, I guess you do, now. Kind of. Almost.

Imagine that, but a lot worse, and for a couple thousand years.

passages.title: Mogu?! Oh No-gu!
passages.text:
I know your friends are worried about the animating statues over at Mogujia, but I'll tell you what you should really be worried about.

Where there are animated statues, there are Mogu. I don't know if you've seen one before, but if you haven't...

Well, let's just say Mogu are bad, bad, news.

While you're dealing with whatever else you're doing, you need to get the Mogu behind the trouble!

passages.title: Mogu?! Oh No-gu!
passages.text:
Oh, thank goodness! You've saved all of our skins, believe me.

You have no idea how much trouble those guys can stir up.

Err, or, I guess you do, now. Kind of. Almost.

Imagine that, but a lot worse, and for a couple thousand years.

passages.title: They Stole My Luck!
passages.text:
My journeys through Kun-Lai have taught me two things. First, never sneak up on a sleeping yak. Second, having luck on your side is both necessary and hard to come by.

The grummles believe in carrying a lucky trinket at all times. In my mind, if one trinket can sometimes bring luck, then many trinkets would guarantee it!

After arriving in One Keg my lucky trinkets were stolen by those little menace sprites. I'd be truly grateful if you could retrieve them for me.

passages.title: They Stole My Luck!
passages.text: Were you able to find my lucky trinkets? One can never have too much good luck.

passages.title: They Stole My Luck!
passages.text:
Thank you! It appears my trinkets were lucky for you too, <class>. While you were gone I did not gamble and lose my cart.

I would be happy to lend it to you for your journey. Besides, I have some goods to win back from this shady grummle!

passages.title: The Mantidote
passages.text:
<Mei motions towards the battlefield.>

You see those huge mantid commanders out there? They have a strange aura about them. It reminds me of the sadness we saw at Zhu's Watch.

Perhaps... they're under the influence of the sha, too?

I kept Ken-Ken's mask - the one he used to remove the sha from Yi-Mo. I believe that, if we use it on the mantid, we can convince them to turn back.

passages.title: It Does You No Good In The Keg
passages.text:
I been thinkin'.

We got all this beer that Chen brewed, and we got all these people that you've gathered. We should bring the two together.

There's a bunch o' folks out there in the fields, riskin' their lives for Pandaria. You an' I should at least bring 'em a keg or two.

They might raise their mugs in victory. They might enjoy one last drink before gettin' skivvered by a mantid. Either way, I wouldn't want 'em to fight without a good brew in their belly.

passages.title: Students No More
passages.text:
Those five students - the ones who were looking for the Hidden Master - they went up to the front lines, alone. I'd send Shado-Pan to aid them, but I haven't got any left.

There's dangerous creatures up there near the wall. If you find those students, make sure that they haven't fallen to any of them.

passages.title: Students No More
passages.text:
They can't keep fighting like this forever. Those kids are downright heroic, but I don't want them to die as heroes.

It's time to throw in the towel.

passages.title: Retreat!
passages.text:
I'm going to withdraw what few forces I have. We may have to fall back to the Stormstout Brewery, or even Halfhill. That call is Commander Loon Mai's to make.

You go ahead. Deliver word to the Commander. My Shado-Pan will be shortly behind.

passages.title: Retreat!
passages.text:
I see.

Well, we gave it our all. It's time to evacuate, save lives, and reassess our strategy, before these mantid take over the entire valley.

passages.title: The Savior of Stoneplow
passages.text:
That commander speaks hastily. He has the weapon he needs to win this battle. He has YOU.

"But it's too hard," you might say.

You would be wrong. It is not too hard. NOTHING IS TOO HARD.

Go now, <name>. Go, and save Stoneplow!

passages.title: The Savior of Stoneplow
passages.text: All is lost, <name>. Pack up your things. We're headed to Halfhill.

passages.title: The Savior of Stoneplow
passages.text:
I can't believe it! You - a foreign-born <race> - have succeeded where the Shado-Pan have failed. You've succeeded where the WALL has failed.

We may hold this farming village after all.

passages.title: The Gratitude of Stoneplow
passages.text:
One last thing, <name>. Don't worry, it's not another favor. You've killed enough mantid today.

We recently received a shipment of high-quality armor from Kun-Lai Summit. I was planning to keep them for my men... but I can't think of anybody more deserving than you. You'll find them on the second floor of the inn, here in town.

passages.title: The Gratitude of Stoneplow
passages.text: Peering inside, you find...

passages.title: Into the Vale
passages.text:
Ah, I have been waiting for your arrival, traveler.

I wish we could meet in better times, but alas, I fear the situation in the Vale is quite dire.

But let us not speak of that now. Go visit Matron Vi Vinh at the Shrine of Seven Stars.

She should be able to settle you in.

passages.title: The Shrine of Seven Stars
passages.text:
Look at this creature, traveler. Only moments after we arrived, this mogu assassin attacked with no warning.

His blade was intended for the leader of the Golden Lotus. It is very lucky indeed that we were here to stop the attack.

Seeing this attempt on Zhi's life, I fear for the safety of those who have already entered the valley.

The caretakers are settling your people into the city to the southeast. Go and speak to the leaders. Make sure they are safe.

passages.title: The Shrine of Seven Stars
passages.text:
Good work, <name>. It sounds as though they are getting on quite well at the city.

However, in order to ensure their safety, we must be even more vigilant than before.

passages.title: The Ruins of Guo-Lai
passages.text:
According to Zhi the Harmonious, the mogu are moving into the Vale from the Ruins of Guo-Lai to the west.

I sent Anji and Kun to investigate the situation, but they have not yet returned.

I need a capable <class> like you to go check on them.

passages.title: The Ruins of Guo-Lai
passages.text: Leven sent you? I hope you're ready for a fight.

passages.title: Barring Entry
passages.text:
Lao Softfoot and I scouted up the ruins to the north.

It looks like the mogu are infiltrating the valley through a cave just up the hill, and already they are sending formidable reinforcements through.

There are too many enemies to take them head on, so you'll have to meet Lao Softfoot at the entrance to the ruins.

He'll help you sneak in under the cover of stealth. Then, plant this keg of explosives at the mouth of the cave.

The rest should take care of itself.

passages.title: Barring Entry
passages.text:
Wonderful, <name>!

You and He have single-handedly crippled the mogu advance.

That is called working smarter, not harder.

passages.title: Leaving an Opening
passages.text:
This is serious.

Kun and I will keep an eye on things here, but you should go to the Golden Pagoda.

Go, swiftly!

passages.title: Leaving an Opening
passages.text:
