To arms, <name>! I thought we would have more time to set up our defenses, but the mogu are proving to be a deadly and intelligent enemy.

We've moved the refugees and our supplies into the city behind us.

It's up to us to protect the front. We must not let the mogu gain a single foothold here in the Vale.

passages.title: The Secrets of Guo-Lai
passages.text:
I just received information from a guard stationed near the Ruins of Guo-Lai that the Shado-Tien leader entered the halls, killing two of my men in the process. They're intent on something inside. We need to stop them.

He Softfoot has already followed them in. He should be waiting for you at the entrance to the western chambers.

Move quickly, <name>. I don't like the thought that the mogu may be a step ahead of us.

passages.title: The Secrets of Guo-Lai
passages.text:
The Shao-Tien were spotted marching out of the halls with a hundred jade statues. The mogu now have an immense jade army to turn against us, and we've yet to uncover their other goals in the Vale. We are all in danger.

I had thought you and He dead. It's good that I was mistaken on the last part at least. Rest. Recover. There will be much fighting ahead.

passages.title: The Mogu's Message
passages.text:
The battle against the mogu rages fiercely with neither side giving quarter.

We cannot hold our position forever. Something must be done to strike a blow at the mogu, a blow from which they cannot recover.

Go check in with Zhi the Harmonious at The Silent Sanctuary. I wish to hear his thoughts on this matter.

passages.title: The Mogu's Message
passages.text:
Zhi the Harmonious and the defenders were slaughtered mercilessly.

Your senses tingle. You realize that the Thunder King's treasures are gone!

passages.title: What Comes to Pass
passages.text: You had better report back to the Golden Pagoda immediately.

passages.title: What Comes to Pass
passages.text:
What? Zhi the Harmonious... is dead? Oh...

You did very well, given the circumstances. I'm sure a lesser <class> would have succumbed to those assassins.

Things are happening... so quickly. We must all keep ourselves together.

passages.title: The Might of Three
passages.text:
This is it, <name>. This is the end.

If we don't drive the mogu from the valley, they will seize the remnants of their ancient power and use it to break Pandaria to their will.

But our forces are few, and tired, and small. We bleed, while their warriors are made of stone.

<name>, although all odds are against us, still I must ask you to go and help our forces slay the mogu invaders.

I have prayed to the Celestials, begging their aid. I can only hope that they answer our call.

passages.title: The Might of Three
passages.text:
What? You have slain how many mogu?

Remarkable! If we survive this, you must tell me everything that happened.

passages.title: The Shrine of Two Moons
passages.text:
Look at this creature, traveler. Only moments after we arrived, this mogu assassin attacked with no warning.

His blade was intended for the leader of the Golden Lotus. It is very lucky indeed that we were here to stop the attack.

Seeing this attempt on Zhi's life, I fear for the safety of those who have already entered the valley.

The caretakers are settling your people into the city to the northeast. Go and speak to the leaders. Make sure they are safe.

passages.title: The Shrine of Two Moons
passages.text: Good work, <name>. The city should be safe for now.

passages.title: Barrels of Fun
passages.text:
Oh, well now, let's have us some fun, <boyo/girly>!

Those Ordo yaungol to the northwest have saved us the trouble o' havin' to make some bombs. They already have them there.

Let's put their explosive barrels to good use and destroy their oil-pumpin' machines, shall we?

passages.title: Barrels of Fun
passages.text: Ho ho, that were a fine sight to see. I knew I should have gone up there with ya, <name>!

passages.title: It Does You No Good In The Keg
passages.text:
I been thinkin'.

We got all this beer that Chen brewed, and we got all these people that you've gathered. We should bring the two together.

There's a bunch o' folks out there in the fields, riskin' their lives for Pandaria. You an' I should at least bring 'em a keg or two.

They might raise their mugs in victory. They might enjoy one last drink before gettin' skivvered by a mantid. Either way, I wouldn't want 'em to fight without a good brew in their belly.

passages.title: Barrels of Fun
passages.text:
I love blowing stuff up. It's in my blood!

The yaungol to the west at Fire Camp Ordo have a ton of explosive barrels just lying around.

I say we put them to good use and destroy their oil-pumpin' machines while having some fun!

passages.title: Barrels of Fun
passages.text: Um, I don't think the job's done yet.

passages.title: Barrels of Fun
passages.text: You can't tell me that wasn't fun, <name>! I knew I should have gone over there with you!

passages.title: Huff & Puff
passages.text:
Have you heard of the prickly puffer fish <name>? Of course you haven't, you're new around these parts!

They can be found in the sarjun depths, due west of here. Take this fishing spear and see if you can bring me back of few of their poison tipped spines.

passages.title: Huff & Puff
passages.text: Careful with that spear, <name>.

passages.title: Huff & Puff
passages.text: Ahh, I see you recovered some spines <name>.  These will certainly work well on my spear tips!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text: <The shield is down. Time to head into the cave and slay the Warbringer of the Ordo yaungol!>

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
You've done it, <name>! I'm in your debt!

Again!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text: <The shield is down. Time to head into the cave and slay the Warbringer of the Ordo!>

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
Once again you've accomplished what no one else could.

Was there any doubt?

passages.title: Particular Plumage
passages.text:
When the crocs started attacking, they scared a bunch of the lories out of their nests, up in that island to our northwest.

I can use those lories' feathers to make some specialized lures, which will come in handy if and when I get to stop defending my brethren from these reptiles.

You up for some feather hunting?

passages.title: Particular Plumage
passages.text: <A bead of sweat twinkles in the fur above Tony's brow.>

passages.title: Particular Plumage
passages.text: Thanks, <name>. You've made my day. I always hate to see such a prime feather-gathering opportunity go to waste.

passages.title: The Lorewalker on the Lake
passages.text:
Your raft is down in the water below. Take it out to the middle of the lake, where you should find a woman. Her name is Ana Wu.

Whenever I have a question that I can't figure out on my own, I'll ask her. She should be able to tell us why these crocolisks won't stop attacking.

passages.title: The Lorewalker on the Lake
passages.text:
You appear troubled, child.

How can this Lorewalker serve you? What is it that you seek?

passages.title: Wisdom Has A Price
passages.text:
<Ana listens to your story, and nods.>

Crocolisks attacking? I know a story about that. And I will share it with you, but first... I grow hungry.

Shark meat should do the trick. You should find enough sharks in the water beneath us.

passages.title: Wisdom Has A Price
passages.text: My hunger is great, <race>. I have been on this lagoon for several days, without food.

passages.title: Wisdom Has A Price
passages.text:
You've brought me more meat than I could ever hope to eat.

Now, I suppose I owe you a story...

passages.title: Balance
passages.text:
The story did not end happily. The Narsong crocolisk is no more.

This time, however, you may have a chance to change the ending.

The hozen to the south are overfishing these waters. With the fish gone, the crocolisks are hungry and desperate - and so they attack Marista.

Go now, <race>! Stop those hozen from their reckless fishing!

passages.title: Balance
passages.text:
<Jay listens to your account of the day's events.>

I see. We'll keep an eye on the Ungas from here. And we'll do our best not to fish these waters too heavily, either. No doubt we're part of the problem, too.

Until next time, <name>.

passages.title: Like Bombing Fish In A Barrel
passages.text:
Turns out these rays are not as easy to catch as I thought! You seem like a pretty smart <guy/gal>, think you can help me out?

I made the bombs but have been having trouble using the raft with my hurt leg. The rays are common in the shallows just west of here. Take the bombs and use my raft to bring me back their stingers!

Oh yeah, watch out for the hammerheads!

passages.title: Like Bombing Fish In A Barrel
passages.text: Find any sting rays in the shallows?

passages.title: Like Bombing Fish In A Barrel
passages.text: Looks like you're pretty handy with those bombs!

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text:
I can't believe you made it here!

I don't know how much longer I could have stayed hidden in here.

I'm sure that there are others. <class>, we have to rescue them! Then we can go to Shado-Pan Fallback. The master there will know what to do!

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text: There are survivors out there? Surely there are more, <name>?

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text:
We didn't know that there were any survivors out there.

Thank you for bringing them to safety, <name>.

passages.title: One Traveler's Misfortune
passages.text:
Did you have to throw our supplies at them?! Why not use your weapon? Maybe fancy spells or kicks? Why the supplies?!

Now we don't have enough to last us, especially with Nephew Bentnail here. His appetite is like a yeti's!

You threw it, you get us more. There is wreckage down the path. Maybe you will find supplies there.

passages.title: One Traveler's Misfortune
passages.text: Nephew Bentnail has already eaten two days worth of food. I hope you found us more!

passages.title: One Traveler's Misfortune
passages.text:
You were attacked by a mogu? That sounds terrible!

I hate to ask, but did you manage to pick up any supplies while you were fighting for your life?

No?! This is very bad luck.

passages.title: Seeker's Folly
passages.text:
I'm sure your pandaren friend has some ideas about what the mogu are after.

He headed up the mountain a few days ago without a guide, and asked that only you be sent up after him. He was very specific:

"The <class> must endure the trek alone, with only <his/her> thoughts. <He/She> will honor each shrine before meeting me at the top."

The path is just northwest of the camp, marked by flags. Please be careful! Seeker's Folly is a dangerous trek even on a lucky day.

passages.title: Seeker's Folly
passages.text: There are two shrines on the path below us, and one more just behind us.

passages.title: Seeker's Folly
passages.text:
Ah, you made it, and you honored the shrines.

I knew you could handle it.

passages.title: Unmasking the Yaungol
passages.text:
Simply killing Kobai will accomplish nothing, as he is possessed by a particularly powerful and destructive Sha - Malevolent Fury.

You will use the trap I have fashioned from the Blinding Rage Essences you brought. Lure him into the trap, and then steal his mask. Once you put it on, Malevolent Fury will appear and attempt to take control of you.

Defeat him, and we will have made a victory of this tragic situation. You can find him to the north of the retreat, where he taunts us in insane rage.

passages.title: Unmasking the Yaungol
passages.text: Is Malevolent Fury gone?

passages.title: Unmasking the Yaungol
passages.text:
I should feel shame at the loss of the village. I should feel great pride in your success. 

I should feel many things, but must not allow myself to. Until our struggle with the sha is complete, we must maintain total control of our emotions.

passages.title: The Burlap Trail: To Kota Basecamp
passages.text:
This here's hozen lands. Very dangerous. But grummles must trek through. Supplies must reach the Serpent's Spine.

Go, protect the next wave of grummles on their trek to Kota Basecamp.

If at least one survives, good fortune will find its way to you.

passages.title: The Burlap Trail: To Kota Basecamp
passages.text: Welcome to Kota Basecamp, friend of grummles.

passages.title: The Burlap Trail: To Kota Basecamp
passages.text: Ha ha! Hero of grummles! Welcome to Kota Basecamp. Enjoy good fortune for most happy grummle delivery.

passages.title: Tread Lightly
passages.text:
My students tell me the surrounding area is littered with deadly traps, no doubt set by the saurok. Stumbling into one gets you a face full of spikes.

As the saying goes: "The Way is rife with danger - tread lightly, and with scrutiny."

<Koro hands you a long tree branch.>

Here, this is scrutiny.

It should be long enough to set the traps off at a safe distance.

passages.title: Tread Lightly
passages.text: Well, I don't see any spikes in your face. That's a good sign.

passages.title: Tread Lightly
passages.text: Every trap you sprang is a life saved, be it pandaren, beast, or otherwise. Nobody deserves an honorless death like that.

passages.title: Ahead on the Way
passages.text:
Huge maws of despair are spewing out sha from the pagodas on either side of the temple. Meanwhile, your impromptu training in the Way continues.

"She who mends torn umbrella will be more dry than she who strikes at rain."

While I take issue with that particular lesson--sometimes punching the rain can be quite effective--the meaning holds true in this case.

Take out those maws of despair and give my order a chance at reclaiming the temple grounds.

passages.title: Ahead on the Way
passages.text: Koro said there's a pagoda on either side of the temple. Let's find them and wipe out the sha presence in both.

passages.title: Ahead on the Way
passages.text: Koro's metaphors can get a little tiring, but there's always true wisdom behind them.

passages.title: Scavenger Hunt
passages.text:
YOU! You're just who I have been looking for!

I need more parts for my goblin fishing bombs but I hurt my leg and can't collect them myself.

You see those shipwrecks nearby? I bet they have just what I need if you can get to it and fish it out. Take my fishing raft and see what you can find! My buddy has been trying to help me out too so you might find some extra rafts near the wreckage, feel free to use em' too.

passages.title: Scavenger Hunt
passages.text: Did you find the shipwrecks?

passages.title: Scavenger Hunt
passages.text: Looks like you found plenty of parts, another set of fishing bombs coming right up!  Thanks <name>!

passages.title: Snapclaw
passages.text: A giant, poisonous crab is wrecking havoc on our local abalone stores. I need you to go down into narsong trench and take it out!

passages.title: Snapclaw
passages.text: Did you take out that nasty crawler?

passages.title: Snapclaw
passages.text: That is quite the claw, Snapclaw must be bigger than I thought!  No matter, job well done <name>!

passages.title: Viseclaw Soup
passages.text:
Nothing tastes quite like viseclaw soup. It's a krasarang specialty!

I was just about to start up on a new batch when I realized I am missing a key ingredient, the eyes!

I need you to kill the viseclaw fishers on the beach and return with their eyes for the soup!

passages.title: Viseclaw Soup
passages.text: How many of their beady little eyes did you get?

passages.title: Viseclaw Soup
passages.text: Thanks <class>, this might be my best batch of soup yet!

passages.title: A Line Unbroken
passages.text:
When we regrouped after their initial attack, we numbered three less. You can fight, and we must plan our defense should these cursed yaungol attack again. 

If you would help us, grant our fallen comrades their last rites, and recover their armor. You will find their bodies to the west, near the gate.

And try to keep the birds off them.

passages.title: A Line Unbroken
passages.text: Our comrades, are they at rest?

passages.title: A Line Unbroken
passages.text: Good. I will see to it that the armor is returned to their pupils.

passages.title: To the Wall!
passages.text:
They are attacking again!

<Lin looks to the Ox Gate.>

Archers... on the wall!

I need you to get up there. My wife Suna went to scout the wall with that fool Lao-Chen. Perhaps if he had spent more time preparing defenses and less building that ridiculous ale lift contraption...

It matters not. Get a kite from Len, to the west, and then get up there and find my wife. She'll know what to do next.

passages.title: To the Wall!
passages.text:
Wow, that was quite a bit of kite-flying there. Good job getting up here and not dying.

It's good you're here, too. Lao-chen's got an idea he's working on, but in the meantime we've got yaungol to deal with.

passages.title: Ellia Ravenmane
passages.text:
We regularly organize one-on-one duels with trainees that we think are well-suited for one another. We have found one such trainee for you, <name>.

Her name is Ellia Ravenmane. This will be her first duel, too. She will be waiting for you at the pavilion just to the south of here.

passages.title: Ellia Ravenmane
passages.text:
Very good!

The next time you return, you will face a new challenger. Continue winning, and your favor in the eyes of Chi-Ji will increase.

passages.title: Ellia Ravenmane: Rematch
passages.text:
Ellia Ravenmane requested a rematch with you. She seems to identify you as her "rival".

We discourage rivalries here within the Cradle of Chi-Ji, but we rarely decline a rematch request. You will find Ellia near the Pedestal of Hope, on the island's eastern side.

passages.title: Ellia Ravenmane: Rematch
passages.text: Twice fought, twice defeated. It stands to reason that Ellia will not be requesting more rematches anytime soon.

passages.title: Fat Long-Fat
passages.text:
You have been matched with a... special trainee. His name is Fat Long-Fat.

<Thelonius chooses his words carefully.>

Fat Long-Fat... operates outside of the normal rules of combat. He does not fight every day, and when he does, he chooses his competitor. Today, for some reason... he has selected you.

You will find him atop Angkhal Pavilion.

passages.title: Fat Long-Fat
passages.text:
Of course you won. Fat Long-Fat does not fight to win. He fights for... other reasons.

I fear I've spoken too much about this subject already. From now on... no more questions about Fat Long-Fat.

passages.title: Ellia Ravenmane: Redemption
passages.text:
Ellia Ravenmane, your rival, has returned. She demands that you meet her atop the Pedestal of Hope.

You need to understand, <name>... something horrible has happened to her. She has changed. You will see for yourself when you arrive at the pedestal.

Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Ellia Ravenmane: Redemption
passages.text:
The Cradle of Chi-Ji has long been a bastion of hope; a place free of despair. Ellia Ravenmane tried to plant the seeds of despair on our island... and you stopped her.

We owe you a debt of gratitude, <name>. You are welcome to return whenever you like.

passages.title: Kota Blend
passages.text:
Kota Peak is famous for its kafa bushes - no other can survive at this elevation.

Grummles make very good living selling Kafa'kota Blend, but it's dangerous now thanks to my cousin here. He's got the wildlife up there hooked on kafa with his scheming.

Kafa'kota is more scarce than ever with goots gobblin' it up and yetis hoarding it in their caves.

I pay you good for any berries you bring down from Kota.

Here, take a sample. Eat it. See for yourself the power of kafa.

passages.title: Trouble Brewing
passages.text:
Lots of yetis in Kota, yup. Usually not too dangerous. Usually just eat goots.

Then they ate the goots full of kafa...

<Keenbean shoots Gootfur a mean glance.>

Now they're moody, cranky, sleep a lot but never seem rested. Typical kafa addicts.

Gonna come outta those caves soon, I'm sure. Come lookin' for more kafa.

Then we all in trouble.

passages.title: Trouble Brewing
passages.text: Don't wanna fight yetis? Can't say I blame you.

passages.title: Trouble Brewing
passages.text:
You made it!

Yeti's are tough enough on their own - can't imagine what a cranky kafa-addict yeti must be like. You brave. Or lucky. Or dumb.

Maybe all three.

passages.title: A Fair Trade
passages.text:
<The roar bellows out again, louder and more fierce than any of the yetis you've encountered so far. Again, a grummle voice replies...>

Eep! Please, great Kota Kon, forgive grummle. Let me go, I'll bring lots of kafa right away! Promise!

<The beast called Kota Kon answers with another meaty roar.>

passages.title: A Fair Trade
passages.text:
Kota Kon wants more kafa, but I already fed her all I have! Then I tried giving her a nice bow, but she's not satisfied!

<The terrified grummle gulps and leans in close to whisper.>

I think she can smell the kafa I drank for breakfast...

passages.title: A Fair Trade
passages.text:
You brought kafa?!

You...

Magnificent...

Luckydo...

Hurry, let's give it to her! Maybe she won't have us both for snack...

passages.title: The Burlap Grind
passages.text:
Okayyy... well, she's not eating anybody. That's a good start.

She must want more kafa, but we gotta give her somethin' to do with all the extra energy...

I got it! The Burlap Trail! She can smash hozen out there all day!

<Burrberry turns to the massive beast.>

What do you think, pretty girl? Wanna smash hozens?!

I think so. Here, feed her my emergency flask of kafa. She likes you.

passages.title: The Burlap Grind
passages.text: Don't push our luck... we promised her hozens-smashies.

passages.title: The Burlap Grind
passages.text:
Wow! That was VIOLENT.

Not sure what I was expecting...

Thanks to you, I think we may have just formed a mutually beneficial relationship with the Terror of Kota Peak.

passages.title: Unbelievable!
passages.text:
I simply refuse to believe the guards will not grant us entry to the monastery should we impress upon them the seriousness of the situation.

Friend, go east, to the sentinel in front of the Monastery, and demand admittance. I will come with you.

passages.title: Unbelievable!
passages.text: Unbelievable!

passages.title: Unbelievable!
passages.text: No... this is worse than I could have possibly imagined. The monastery itself has been compromised...

passages.title: Lord of the Shado-Pan
passages.text:
Our lord, Taran Zhu, has been overcome by a sha of pure hatred. The whole monastery has been lost!

<class>, you must find a way to free him of this possession. Last I knew, he was meditating in the Grove of Falling Blossoms.

passages.title: Lord of the Shado-Pan
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>. I am cleansed of all hatred.

Know that you are a hero of the Shado-Pan.

passages.title: My Husband...
passages.text:
Lin...

I don't care what Ban, Lao-Chin, or even Taran Zhu says. I'm moving ahead into Townlong. I may not be able to save Lin myself, but I'm not going to sit around waiting for everyone else to catch up.

Once Taran Zhu opens the doors to his precious monastery, we'll save Lin. Until then, I'll scout ahead and make sure he's alright.

passages.title: My Husband...
passages.text: Good. Looks like the rest of the Shado-Pan decided it was a good time to catch up.

passages.title: Ranger Rescue
passages.text:
I must ask a most important task of you, <name>.

Somewhere among the cages in the Osul camp is my husband, Lin. He is the light of my world.

Please find him and return him to me, and save as many of our fellow Shado-Pan as you can as well.

You should find keys to those cages on the Osul Marauders.

passages.title: Ranger Rescue
passages.text: How did it go?

passages.title: Ranger Rescue
passages.text:
I am truly sorry to hear that Lin did not make it.

Suna is taking the news quite hard. She will forgive me in time.

As for the rest of the Shado-Pan that you saved, well, I am very grateful to see them returned safe and sound.

passages.title: Jung Duk
passages.text:
THIS. IS. WAR.

I will have the heads of everyone who took Lin from me. EVERYONE!

We will begin with the Osul leader, Jung Duk.

Take this Shado-Pan war banner and place it at the center of their camp.

Jung Duk will have no choice but to face you.

Show him no mercy, <name>.

passages.title: Jung Duk
passages.text: Jung Duk's legacy is written in the blood of innocents.

passages.title: Jung Duk
passages.text:
Jung Duk is dead at last.

Hundreds, perhaps thousands, lost their lives due to his violent aggression.

Though they are not here to witness his demise, they owe deep gratitude to your bravery today.

passages.title: Hatred Becomes Us
passages.text:
I should have suspected a sha presence earlier!

We are safe as long as we stand inside the Totem of Harmony's protective wards, but many of our people were not so lucky.

They were trapped outside the camp when the sha's powers manifested, and now they turn upon each other!

Take one of my totems with you. Place the totem near a crazed ally to purify them, but beware.

You may have to face the darkness that gripped them.

passages.title: Hatred Becomes Us
passages.text: Our people are possessed by hatred. We must help them come to their senses!

passages.title: Hatred Becomes Us
passages.text:
Thank you.

The sha preys upon the weak and the vulnerable.

If we are not vigilant, even the strongest of us can succumb to the sha's dark influence.

passages.title: Gao-Ran Battlefront
passages.text:
With your help, we have quelled the spirits of this place.

At last, they may rest in peace.

Our journey into this cursed land, I am afraid, has only begun.

I have some important matters to finish up here, but we will be moving out soon.

I need someone to go ahead and tell Lord Taran Zhu that we are joining him.

Find him at the Gao-Ran Battlefront. Tell him what has transpired here.

passages.title: Gao-Ran Battlefront
passages.text: Did the northern expedition go well, then? What news do you have to report?

passages.title: The Torches
passages.text:
Until recently, the yaungol shaman would come here to work alongside us. Now, they bend my people to their will.

If we refuse, they kill us. Even if we oblige... they kill us.

The yaungol mist-shaman's magic flows through his torch. Take his torch away, and he has nothing.

passages.title: The Torches
passages.text:
I can use these torches in my revenge.

I have not succumbed to this wound yet. I can still have my revenge before I die.

There is time yet.

passages.title: The Torches
passages.text:
This torch... the yaungol once used these to communicate with me, with my people.

Now, they use them to undo us.

passages.title: Golgoss
passages.text:
The leader of the yaungol mist-shaman is named Jahesh. He is known for his strength.

One of my kind is also known for his strength. His name is Golgoss.

Golgoss sleeps within the mists of the Upper Sumprushes. Help me to summon him, and he will join me in avenging our people.

passages.title: Golgoss
passages.text: Golgoss is no coward. He will relish the opportunity for revenge.

passages.title: Golgoss
passages.text:
Golgoss does not speak your language, other than a few words. I suppose I am unique in this regard.

He thanks you for summoning him.

passages.title: Arconiss
passages.text:
If I am to fight Jahesh, leader of the yaungol mist-shaman, I must have Arconiss by my side. Arconiss' ferocity is second to none.

He rests beneath the mists of the Upper Sumprushes. Find his resting place, and then use these torches to awaken him.

passages.title: Arconiss
passages.text: It will be difficult to lose with Arconiss by my side.

passages.title: Orbiss Fades
passages.text:
I knew death would come. I did not know that it would come this fast.

I must buy time. The mist of the Upper Sumprushes is warm and fragrant. Such mist is nutritive to my kind.

Gather this mist however you can... in jars, in vials, within the interior of your bags. Bring it back to me, and I can use it to remain corporeal for a bit longer.

passages.title: Orbiss Fades
passages.text: I require more mist. I am fading...

passages.title: Orbiss Fades
passages.text: I told you earlier, this wound would be my death. While you have bought me a bit more time, it is not long now.

passages.title: Mists' Opportunity
passages.text:
Now is the time to strike.

Golgoss, Arconiss, and I will go east, into Jahesh's domain. Meet us there, and prepare for battle.

Today, we restore the pride of our people.

passages.title: Mists' Opportunity
passages.text:
My name will be forgotten, but my actions will not.

Nor will yours, <name>.

passages.title: The Tomb of Shadows
passages.text:
Given the artifacts you found on the altar, I would guess they were attempting to perform a Spiritbinding ritual.

Most of the texts involving Spiritbinding were locked away in the Tomb of Shadows. Perhaps we will find the answers we seek there.

Look for anything that might help us. You'll find the tomb on the first rise closest to the ritual altar.

passages.title: The Tomb of Shadows
passages.text: Did you find anything in the Tomb of Shadows?

passages.title: The Tomb of Shadows
passages.text:
These tablets recount the history of the Mogu and Zandalari alliance dating back to the time of the first Mogu emperor.

By the looks of things they have rekindled their alliance. But why now?

passages.title: Stealing Their Thunder King
passages.text:
Our only hope is to find the Thunder King's remains before they do. He must be buried within the Tomb of Conquerors.

Getting to his remains will not be easy, <name>. The tomb will no doubt be defended by guardians and other unfriendly surprises intended to ward off thieves.

Once inside we will need to figure out where his remains have actually been placed.

passages.title: Stealing Their Thunder King
passages.text: Have you figured out where the Thunder King's remains are hidden?

passages.title: Stealing Their Thunder King
passages.text:
We are fortunate they haven't gotten to Lei Shen's remains... yet.

The Zandalari will not give up until they have what they want.

passages.title: Chasing the Storm
passages.text:
We need to figure out where they are taking the Thunder King's remains. It won't be possible for them to resurrect him in the Valley of the Emperors. They would need to be somewhere remote and secure.

It appears that getting out of here may also prove to be a challenge....

Fight your way out and look for information concerning the location of the remains.

passages.title: Chasing the Storm
passages.text: Were you able to find any information on their location?

passages.title: Chasing the Storm
passages.text:
This is dark Zandalari blood magic. Once we're done with the map it should be burned.

The map indicates they have headed for the coast just outside of a tiny fishing village called Zouchin. The villagers there may be able to help us find the Zandalari. We just have to hope the village is still standing...

passages.title: The Fearmaster
passages.text:
I am not gonna take this anymore. My wife, bless her, poured her heart and soul in to that ranch making it what it is today.

Them yaungol got a leader over there being all smug and what not. I'll pay you handsomely if you knock that smug smile off his filthy, stinking, good for nothing face.

passages.title: The Fearmaster
passages.text: So many strangers in these lands these days. Luckily you <class> seem to be all right.

passages.title: The Fearmaster
passages.text: Yee haw! I knew you humans might be good for somethin'. He must of made a very satisfying "thump" when he hit the ground.

passages.title: The Scent of Life
passages.text:
Many have perished here. We will need to honor them properly, which means gathering the makings of incense of life. 

It doesn't just smell nice - it has restorative properties, and can even help plants grow. Maybe I can get a whiff of the ingredients to get me back on my feet.

The materials can be found on creatures around here - except for the spices, which were stolen by the mercenaries who pillaged the village.

passages.title: The Scent of Life
passages.text: Are those the ingredients for Incense of Life I smell on you? Or... perhaps you haven't bathed recently.

passages.title: The Scent of Life
passages.text: Beautiful, beautiful. Better to not need to bury our friends, but if we must, it is good they will have a fitting ceremony.

passages.title: The Death of Me
passages.text:
I have resolved to remove this spear from my side.

For this, I require your assistance. Your grasping hands are stronger than mine.

passages.title: The Death of Me
passages.text:
By removing this spear, I have truly guaranteed my own death.

This does not frighten me.

I would sooner die than live carrying the weapon of my enemy.

passages.title: The Healing of Shen-zin Su
passages.text:
This is what comes of such recklessness. How could he think this was even a possibility?

Nevermind, there's no time for that now. We need to act to save Shen-zin Su.

Find any healers you can! Rescue them, relieve them - whatever you need to do to get them over here healing the wound.

Keep the healers safe at all costs!

passages.title: A New Fate
passages.text:
<name>, I'm thankful the plan worked, but just barely. We would be sinking to the bottom of the ocean with all of Shen-zin Su if you hadn't been here. I don't think I can ever forgive Ji for this kind of recklessness.

There will be plenty of time for reflection, but for now, we need to return to the Temple of Five Dawns. We need to let them know that Shen-zin Su has been saved, and we need to sort out the fates of these new allies.

passages.title: A Funeral
passages.text:
As I said, I will gather the town - we will be at the funeral. 

As the one who has done so much to honor our friends, we feel it is only right that you will be the one to light the Incense of Life and usher their spirits to the life beyond.

passages.title: A Funeral
passages.text: You must light the incense to honor the dead.

passages.title: A Funeral
passages.text: Good. Let us begin the funeral.

passages.title: The Burlap Grind
passages.text:
Alright, it's time to take Kota Kon out for her "walk."

We brewed two fresh pots of kafa just for her and she's all fueled up!

passages.title: The Burlap Grind
passages.text: Kota Kon's waiting for you! She won't let anyone else ride her.

passages.title: The Burlap Grind
passages.text:
Hah hah! We could hear those monkeys screamin' from over here!

<Burrberry turns to Kota Kon.>

Who's a pretty girl? You are!!

passages.title: Kota Blend
passages.text:
Kota Peak is famous for its kafa bushes - no other can survive at this elevation.

Grummles make very good living selling Kafa'kota Blend, but it's dangerous now thanks to our cousin. He's got the wildlife up there hooked on kafa with his scheming.

Kafa'kota is more scarce than ever with goots gobblin' it up and yetis hoarding it in their caves.

Uncle Keenbean will pay you good for any berries you bring down from Kota.

Here, take a sample. Eat it. See for yourself the power of kafa.

passages.title: What Lies Beneath
passages.text:
If my suspicions are correct, this place still reels from some lingering darkness.

Whatever happened here... it could not have been the natural course of events.

Even the yaungol are not so brutal as to slaughter their own kind to the point of... this.

I will use the totems that you brought me to perform a cleansing ritual.

I need someone to assist me in the ceremony. Let me know when you are ready.

passages.title: What Lies Beneath
passages.text: I believe that we must drive the taint from this place.

passages.title: What Lies Beneath
passages.text:
We look upon the true face of hatred!

Now it all makes sense. This is the work of the sha.

passages.title: Cleansing the Mere
passages.text:
Pools of the same murky substance that came out of Mei emerged in the lake recently.

I will travel into the Mere with you. Point out the pools of corruption that you are ready for me to cleanse.

You will need to deal with whatever comes out and protect me as I complete the ritual.

passages.title: Cleansing the Mere
passages.text: Is the lake cleansed?

passages.title: Cleansing the Mere
passages.text:
The Mere... I can feel the corruption clearing. At least now, this corruption will not spread.

But, there is one more thing we must do.

passages.title: Father and Child Reunion
passages.text:
They survived? My father is alive!

I thought we would all die here in this horrible mere, at the hands of these insane Jinyu.

I will find my way back - meet me back at camp.

passages.title: Father and Child Reunion
passages.text: My boy! He is alive!

passages.title: Father and Child Reunion
passages.text: You found him! This is all I have to give, but in finding my son, you have more than earned it.

passages.title: The Fall of Shai Hu
passages.text:
I can hear the voice of the Mere - it has been purified.

But, this chapter in my people's history will never be closed - not until we defeat Shai Hu.

He has retreated to the central island in the Mere, corrupting our holiest of sites.

Beware - he is strong. But, after all we have done, I am confident we will be stronger.

passages.title: The Fall of Shai Hu
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. You have assured that this corruption will not spread, and that my people - those who have not been corrupted - will be able to live on and found a new village. 

Our history will live on. You have done more for us than we could have ever hoped.

Thank you, friend.

passages.title: Breach in the Defenses
passages.text:
Normally, it only takes a few scouts to hold this pass. Most of this territory is in sight of the wall, so archers would devastate any mantid force attempting to push through here. The problem is, most of the archers are occupied with the onslaught at the gate.

Take this flare - it will help you locate the mantid that are sneaking through the eastern pass under our diminished watch. Kill any you find. We can't let them lay a trail that might lead the mantid swarms farther into the steppes.

passages.title: Breach in the Defenses
passages.text:
The defenders on the wall are stretched thin. The Yaungol are pushing through the gates to Kun-Lai in the north. The mantid are pouring against the gates to the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. I hear that there's been a breach into the Valley of Four Winds in the south too.

We do not have the men to combat all of these threats.

passages.title: Breach in the Defenses
passages.text:
There are more getting through than I thought. I may need to stay here and clean up a while.

You've done more than your part though, <class>. Thank you.

passages.title: The Restless Watch
passages.text:
I'm being told that our scouts have been on duty in Shallowstep Pass for more than 2 days straight, no rest. No wonder mantid are slipping through. Even the most dedicated scouts would slip with those kinds of shifts.

I want you to go out there and deliver orders to the scouts that they are to return to the battlefront immediately for rest and rations. I'll arrange for a new shift to be posted.

passages.title: The Restless Watch
passages.text: This whole battlefront is being worked to the bone. We need more men out here.

passages.title: The Restless Watch
passages.text: Thank you. I'll have the new scouts at their posts shortly.

passages.title: The Motives of the Mantid
passages.text:
<class>. You may be of assistance.

The Shado-Pan wishes to know why the mantid are attacking so violently. We have our suspicions, but we cannot be sure. Furthermore, we do not want the mantid to know that we are investigating them.

That's where you come in.

I need you to kill the mantid of Kri'vess, in the north. I will lurk behind you in the shadows, and search for clues on their bodies.

passages.title: The Motives of the Mantid
passages.text: The abundance of yak hair on that mantid's body suggests one thing... it came from Niuzao Temple. Our journey continues westward, <class>.

passages.title: Set the Mantid Back
passages.text:
Every day, the mantid build up munitions for use on their enemies. We cannot stop them, just you and I... but we can set them back.

<Tai Ho hands you some explosives.>

I need to keep a low profile. Would you do the honors?

passages.title: Set the Mantid Back
passages.text: The Shado-Pan are counting on you, <name>.

passages.title: Set the Mantid Back
passages.text: We are in your debt, <race>.

passages.title: The Wisdom of Niuzao
passages.text:
Niuzao, the Black Ox, rests in the temple to the west. He may know why the mantid are attacking.

He may, in fact, know much more than that.

I will rendezvous with you at Niuzao Temple, <class>.

passages.title: The Wisdom of Niuzao
passages.text:
Your Shado-Pan associate has spoken with me. Yes, Niuzao knows why the mantid are attacking. But he is not ready to tell you.

Not yet.

passages.title: Niuzao's Price
passages.text:
Niuzao owns a statuette which he values greatly: a small icon, in his image, sculpted by one of his long-since fallen sentinels. This statuette was recently stolen by the Sra'thik mantid, and taken to their encampment to our north.

Bring back this statuette. Then we will give you - and your Shado-Pan associate - the answers you seek.

passages.title: Niuzao's Price
passages.text: Niuzao does not move quickly, nor does he make rash decisions. Perform his task, and give him time to decide.

passages.title: Niuzao's Price
passages.text:
Niuzao will be pleased.

Despite his size, our patron is a beast of grace and compassion. He treasured this icon... just as he treasures each of his followers.

passages.title: The Terrible Truth
passages.text:
It is with a heavy heart that I confirm your suspicions. The mantid are indeed under the sway of the Sha of Fear.

It was OUR sworn duty to confine that creature beneath our temple. Unfortunately, our vigil faltered, our defenses buckled, and the sha escaped. It is with the mantid now.

See for yourself. The mantid burrowed into the western side of our island.

passages.title: The Terrible Truth
passages.text:
Let me make this clear... that creature was NOT the Sha of Fear. Simply a shadow... a fraction of the sha's true power.

No, the Sha of Fear is with the mantid now. The elders of my order need to be informed of this immediately.

I will handle the rest from here. Thank you for your assistance, <race>. Once again, your kind proves to be an asset to Pandaria.

passages.title: Give Them Peace
passages.text:
I overheard. Our secret is out, then.

When I learned that the mantid had burrowed beneath our temple, I reacted hastily. I sent dozens of guardians to defend what they could, but they were not prepared. They succumbed to fear, and never returned.

A pandaren deserves to die embracing the ground, as he does in sleep... not flat on his back with his eyes transfixed in terror. Please, <name>. Give them the peace they deserve.

passages.title: Give Them Peace
passages.text: I should have gone with them.

passages.title: Give Them Peace
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>.

I should have been among them.

passages.title: Pick a Yak
passages.text:
I can't find a single good yak here. ALL the yaks are bad!

Some are too stinky, some too fight-y, others just scared.

You look like a lucky <race>. Here, take a lasso. See if you can find a good yak for me.

passages.title: Pick a Yak
passages.text: See? I told you! No good yaks.

passages.title: Pick a Yak
passages.text:
Well, well! A good yak!

Tell you what, <name>. I take this GOOD yak, and you can do whatever you want with this bad, bad one.

passages.title: Father's Footsteps
passages.text:
Yes, the boy's father - Sentinel Ku-Yao - has gone missing. He could be any number of places... we have no shortage of enemies these days.

You're free to look around, if you wish. You might start by looking for his yak, or by asking Sentinel Yalo what he knows.

passages.title: Father's Footsteps
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: Father's Footsteps
passages.text: No shield, no crossbow, no yak... something bad has happened to dad.

passages.title: Criteria Effects Test Quest
passages.text:
Hello friend! Let's test some things, shall we?

Click on the gear!
Chat with the bubble!
Heal the Green Sparkle!
Kill the kill target!
Click on the gearbody's corpse!

The loudspeaker should announce your progress.

After each objective, you will explode.

(Sorry about that last bit.)

passages.title: Fisherman's Tale
passages.text:
The villagers of Zouchin know the coast better than anyone in Kun-Lai. If the Zandalari are hiding on one of the islands, they will know.

Mishi will take you as far as Emperor's Path. I will go ahead to speak with the village elders.

Follow the path to Whispercloud Rise. Shin Whispercloud will help you reach the village.

passages.title: Fisherman's Tale
passages.text: The Zandalari are nearby, <name>. We must hurry!

passages.title: Fisherman's Tale
passages.text:
The elders have agreed to help us figure out where the Zandalari have hidden the Thunder King's remains.

They have a few conditions though...

passages.title: Make A Fighter Out of Me
passages.text:
Shhh! Don't speak so loudly! My father might hear you.

<Shomi gestures to Steelbender Doshu.>

My father is delusional! He thinks I should be studying my tea pouring while our village is under attack. It's ridiculous! I have just as much courage as any man. I just don't know how to fight... yet.

That's where you come in. Let me travel with you! I'm a fast learner and I won't get in the way I promise!

Pleaseeeeee!

If we get separated I'll meet you back in the village.

passages.title: Make A Fighter Out of Me
passages.text: I'll show my father he's wrong about me!

passages.title: Make A Fighter Out of Me
passages.text: I told you I was a fast learner! I will head back to the village to start training others. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Unending Siege
passages.text:
The mantid continue to attack us. Their numbers ebb and flow, but they do not stop.

It is no matter. The yak is stamina embodied. We will not bend to them. We will defend his home forever.

Will you help us?

passages.title: The Unending Siege
passages.text: You fight like you are one of us.

passages.title: Fallen Sentinels
passages.text:
Our sentinels can fight for days on end, but even they have their limits. Since the mantid swarm began, too many of them have pushed themselves beyond their abilities.

Please, aid them in whatever way you can. If you are unable to heal them yourself, you may give them some of this. A mouthful of nutritious yak's milk will give them the strength they need.

passages.title: Fallen Sentinels
passages.text: Things look grim out there.

passages.title: Fallen Sentinels
passages.text:
In times like these, we must trust in the power and protection of Niuzao. Should things get any worse, he will protect us.

He always does.

passages.title: Paying Tribute
passages.text:
Our patron Niuzao is a mountain on wheels... very difficult to move, even more difficult to stop. My point: once we get him moving, the mantid will have their arms full trying to slow him down.

The easiest way to get him moving is to put food in front of him. Luckily for us, food in our temple is plentiful... even in wartime.

I will send one of my strongarms with you, to shoulder the load.

passages.title: Paying Tribute
passages.text: Niuzao, please... it is time to join the battle...

passages.title: Paying Tribute
passages.text:
He will get up. Soon. Maybe not today, but soon.

And when he does...

<A smile grows on Paosha's face.>

passages.title: The Siege Swells
passages.text:
Today's mantid swarm is among the worst I've seen. We are lucky to have Niuzao join us in battle.

Help him, <class>. Return to the courtyard, and join in the defense of our temple.

passages.title: The Siege Swells
passages.text:
Look at him, <class>.

Nothing can stop Niuzao. Only Niuzao can stop Niuzao.

passages.title: In Battle's Shadow
passages.text:
Niuzao's appearance on the battlefield is a blessing... in more ways than one.

With the distraction that he's caused, our stonemasons have seized the opportunity to build up our crumbling walls. They could use your help.

Toss any loose bricks you find up their way. And hurry! Niuzao will not rampage forever.

passages.title: In Battle's Shadow
passages.text: It looks like the walls are beginning to take shape again. In time, the Temple will be whole again.

passages.title: A New Enemy
passages.text:
The power of these Dark Shaman has attracted many allies, <name>. Former members of the Horde that now work towards some dark purpose.

We need to make an example of them before we have another twilight's hammer on our hands.

Kill any cultist you come across and bring me their insignia.

passages.title: A New Enemy
passages.text: Have you collected the insignia?

passages.title: A New Enemy
passages.text: Good work, <name>. This will make it very clear how Garrosh is going to deal with failures...

passages.title: Joining the Fight
passages.text: Lao-Chin's archers will need these arrows down at the bridge. Can you bring them?

passages.title: Joining the Fight
passages.text: Welcome to the mess.

passages.title: Joining the Fight
passages.text:
Taran Zhu told me what became of my camp. I would have stopped it if I could, but the attacks from the bridge have not let up.

Thank you for bringing these arrows - my archers will make good use of them.

passages.title: Raising Spirits
passages.text:
The kegs are full of my worst stock. Good for burning, crap for drinking.

I've broken out some tankards of my best spirits and had them carried out amongst the kegs though - those are for my well-deserving men! Spirits to raise their spirits after endless, grueling fighting.

Would you be up for spreading the good cheer?

passages.title: The Taking of Dusklight Bridge
passages.text:
Let's press these insects back across the bridge and break their spirits!

Follow my lead.

passages.title: The Taking of Dusklight Bridge
passages.text: The mantid aren't likely to return soon after a beating like that... and now Lao-Chin is free to join us in the hunt.

passages.title: Heroes of the Shado-Pan
passages.text: You said that Taran Zhu is in Townlong and was asking for me? Must be something important...

passages.title: Heroes of the Shado-Pan
passages.text: I like that I can always depend on you. You have the spirit of a true Shado-Pan.

passages.title: Do a Barrel Roll!
passages.text:
When I trained as a Brewmaster, I didn't expect to use my knowledge like this...

Did you know beer catches fire when lit? Well, with yaungol oil mixed in, it's downright explosive.

I've mixed the oil in with these kegs. Roll them at the yaungol over by the gate, and ignite them when you get close. 

It'll take a few seconds for the keg to blow, but when it does...

Well, let's just say I wouldn't want to be over there.

Which is why I'll be over here. Mourning the loss of this brew.

passages.title: Do a Barrel Roll!
passages.text: Wha? I was just thinking about my poor, poor beer...

passages.title: Do a Barrel Roll!
passages.text:
Whoo, that was an explosion! Several, in fact.

Sad my beer had to go, but at least we're safe, for now.

passages.title: Where are My Reinforcements?
passages.text:
This has simply gone too far. I cannot ignore our abandonment any longer.

After all that's happened here, and all you've been through in Firebough, we must travel to the monastery.

Whatever they are doing in there can wait! We can take my balloon up the mountain to the Monastery. It's anchored back by the camp, to the northeast.

passages.title: Where are My Reinforcements?
passages.text: Here we are, then.

passages.title: Where are My Reinforcements?
passages.text: Here we are, and now you know why we cannot let our brothers sit idly by.

passages.title: Lao-Chin's Gambit
passages.text:
Alright. Thanks to you, we have the wall under control. Good job. 

I'll stay up here for a little while and make sure no more yaungol get up onto the wall.

You, though, should go back down and see what Lao-Chin has cooked up. I hate to say it, but maybe he had a good idea after all...

passages.title: Lao-Chin's Gambit
passages.text: Ah, hello again. As sad as I am to have to do this, I'm glad I came up with something.

passages.title: Lao-Chin's Gambit
passages.text: Good to see you made it back in one piece. Thanks to your help with the barrels, I've managed to brew up a good surprise for our yaungol friends at the front.

passages.title: A New Enemy
passages.text:
The horde is using dark magic to control beasts and corrupt their brethren down here, <name>.

I intend to put a stop to it, but first I need to know what it is we're fighting against. That's where you come in.

Fight through the caverns and collect the insignia that the cultists carry. With them, I can study what type of magic is at work here.

passages.title: A New Enemy
passages.text: Have you collected the insignia?

passages.title: A New Enemy
passages.text: Good work, <name>. Now we can figure out what it is they were trying to achieve down here.

passages.title: Falling Down
passages.text:
It's bad enough trying to hold off the mantid, but now we've got spiders swarming up from the ruins below.

One of my best marksmen caught a blast of webbing around his leg and got pulled straight down!

We think he's alive, but I don't have the manpower to send anyone in after him. We're stretched thin up here, <class>.

If you want to help, use the rope behind me to drop down into the ruins. You're not afraid of heights are you?

How about spiders?

passages.title: Falling Down
passages.text:
The fall wasn't that bad, actually. I've always had a knack for soft landings.

That I landed on a pile of spider corpses probably helped, too.

passages.title: Nope
passages.text:
We're holding, but just barely. Anything you can do to stem the tide of dreadspinners coming up the wall would be a big help.

Feel like tearing open spider eggs one at a time by hand?

I didn't think so. Take one of our dragon guns and light it up down there. I wanna hear those puppies pop.

passages.title: Nope
passages.text: Hey, help me out here!

passages.title: Nope
passages.text: Nice work with that dragon gun. I did what I could down here, but arrows are only so useful against these things.

passages.title: Preserved in Amber
passages.text:
Take... this...

<The dying mantid struggles to outstretch his arm. In his mangled grasp rests a metal fork with two long, thin prongs and an ornately jeweled handle.>

Awaken... the Wind-Reaver...

It is the only way... to end the swarm.

passages.title: Preserved in Amber
passages.text: The Klaxxi... call to me.

passages.title: Wakening Sickness
passages.text:
You will forgive my current state. I have slept for many years.

A Klaxxi'va should have been here to attend my Wakening with kypari sap... but you will have to do.

I sense the buzzing of sapflies to the south. They gorge on the nourishing sap I need. Bring them to me.

passages.title: Wakening Sickness
passages.text: Without nourishment, I will die where I stand.

passages.title: Wakening Sickness
passages.text: This will do.

passages.title: The Klaxxi Council
passages.text:
I must report to the Klaxxi. They would not have woken me unless the situation were dire.

You have not been entirely useless. For that, I will spare your life.

The council may even find a use for you.

passages.title: The Klaxxi Council
passages.text:
This is a sacred meeting place for the Klaxxi.

It would be wise of you to let me do the talking.

passages.title: The Dread Clutches
passages.text:
The imperial clutches have become an abomination! Clutch-Keepers rush the development of new swarmborn, saturating them in this vile "sha" energy before sending them away to the wall.

The Klaxxi wish to stem the tide of swarmborn production in these dread clutches. Put the keepers to death!

passages.title: The Dread Clutches
passages.text: A few less traitors for us to feed to the kunchong when the dust settles.

passages.title: Amber Arms
passages.text:
You! Filth!

You work for me now!

The amber blades of the Shek'zeer Bladesworn are the finest weapons in the empire.

If you are not impaled upon them immediately after leaving here, bring me as many of the blades as you can carry! I want to make sure we have weapons in reserve, should we need them.

passages.title: Amber Arms
passages.text: The bladesworn carry their swords with pride. I want them on my weapon racks!

passages.title: Amber Arms
passages.text: If all goes as planned, the Klaxxi will stop the Empress without your help. Still, it is my role to be prepared.

passages.title: Dead Zone
passages.text:
A Klaxxi'va whispers to the tower. It carries their whisper far; to other towers, to mantid, to paragons. The whisper bounces back, and the Klaxxi hear it.

This way, they see all.

A tower near the palace is quiet. This will not do. It must sing for the Klaxxi.

It is my job to fix the tower, but if you serve the Klaxxi, you should serve me as well. You fix the tower, and I will wait here!

passages.title: In Her Clutch
passages.text:
The crystal sings to the Klaxxi. They sense a paragon in the clutch, east of the tower.

Clutch-keepers are trying to pollute this one. the Klaxxi will not permit this.

Go and find the paragon. Place your hands on his chamber, and the Klaxxi will channel their whispers through you to break him free. Protect him if you can.

passages.title: In Her Clutch
passages.text:
My slumber was interrupted by sudden dreams. Unspeakable nightmares.

Then I awoke.

The Klaxxi have spoken to me. I have my orders. There is much to be done.

passages.title: Enemies At Our Door
passages.text:
The Zandalari have begun their attack! You must help defend the village!

If we can't push them back, we will never find the Thunder King's remains!

passages.title: Enemies At Our Door
passages.text: The village must be saved!

passages.title: Enemies At Our Door
passages.text:
The Zandalari have started to retreat, <name>. This victory will mean a great deal to the villagers.

In the chaos I was able to capture one of the fighters. Perhaps we can get information from him.

passages.title: The Lorewalkers
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

We have uncovered something tremendous in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. A great repository of books, scrolls, and lore that has remained untouched since the days of the mogu empire.

Please, join us at your earliest convenience. You can find this Seat of Knowledge by traveling to the infamous Mogu'shan Vaults, and then flying to the landing just above the entrance.

I look forward to your arrival!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: The Humble Grummle
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

We have received your research on the grummles and believe we have a solid idea of their etimology and history.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: Beneath the Heart of Fear
passages.text:
The Klaxxi have detected the existence of another paragon, Wakener.

This one was kept well-hidden from us, and for good reason.

The Empress already has possession of this one, and her adjuncts work to destroy it even now.

They are performing their sorcery in a chamber deep beneath the palace, and they must be stopped.

We hold Klaxxi'vess. You must go in our stead. Find the entrance to their chamber from the ledge to the west.

passages.title: Beneath the Heart of Fear
passages.text: You have done your duty well, Wakener.

passages.title: Amber Is Life
passages.text:
In order for our efforts against the mantid empire to continue, we require more amber.

There is a great deposit of amber underneath the lake to the south, but the area is inhabited by a savage saurok tribe.

I cannot spare anyone else. You must go to the lake and test the tribe's strength. Thin their numbers and eliminate their leader, who is probably hiding in his underground cavern.

Surely this is not too great a task for you?

passages.title: Amber Is Life
passages.text: The amber looks familiar for some reason...

passages.title: Amber Is Life
passages.text:
The whispers seem to be emanating from within this amber.

Could there be another paragon sleeping within?

passages.title: Living Amber
passages.text:
Liquid amber is most efficient for restoring a newly awakened paragon's strength, and is usually provided at a wakening ceremony.

Unfortunately, it seems you did not receive these instructions, so we shall have to improvise.

I can sense a vast quantity of fossilized amber in the lake below us. It will serve, but I am too weak to dig it up myself.

Do this for me, and I will see to it that you are rewarded.

passages.title: Living Amber
passages.text: Do you understand, Wakener? The amber gives life.

passages.title: Living Amber
passages.text: Thank you, Wakener. That is enough for now.

passages.title: Kypari Zar
passages.text:
What is that tree on the hill to the west? Can it be... Kypari Zar?

<Korven the Prime lapses into silence.>

When I returned from my final ravage, before being elevated to a paragon, I was given the honor of planting that very tree.

I see it has grown into a great kypari, but... it seems something is amiss.

There is an old sonar tower at the base of the tree. Take me there, Wakener. I can use the tower to take a closer look.

passages.title: Kypari Zar
passages.text: What has happened to our home? Things feel amiss.

passages.title: Kypari Zar
passages.text: Once, great rivers of amber coursed through this tree's veins. Now, it is but a dried husk.

passages.title: The Root of the Problem
passages.text:
Kypari Zar is dying.

A creature of terrible darkness corrupts it from deep beneath its roots.

The tree cannot be saved, but at least we can lessen its pain.

Look. The vile creature has carved a path to its own lair. We need only follow it down the hill, just behind this tower.

passages.title: The Root of the Problem
passages.text: The swarm knows not of their terrible folly! These precious trees must be protected at all costs!

passages.title: The Root of the Problem
passages.text:
Thank you, Wakener. Kypari Zar can now dream in peace.

However, the beast was merely a vessel for the corruption.

No... the true corruption lies much deeper.

passages.title: Grave Consequences
passages.text:
We've found ancient mogu burial urns among the ruins on Shan'ze Dao.

This is normally no problem, except these urns are home to angry mogu spirits.

Not only do these urns pose a danger to anyone unlucky enough to find one, but they could be used for destruction if they were to fall into the wrong hands.

We must rid Shan'ze Dao of their presence.

passages.title: Grave Consequences
passages.text: Did the spirits cause you any problems?

passages.title: Grave Consequences
passages.text: Good riddance, I say! Those mogu ghosts were long past their expiration.

passages.title: Between a Saurok and a Hard Place
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

We have received your research on the saurok and believe we have pieced together clues about their past.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: Between a Saurok and a Hard Place
passages.text: Before your research, I don't think pandarens ever really knew why the saurok were so vicious. We will add this knowledge to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: Riding the Storm
passages.text:
Shan Bu, the leader of the Shan'ze, is performing some kind of dark ritual at the summit of the island to the northwest.

We believe that the subjugated Shan'ze Cloudrunners are powering the spell. How, we still do not know.

We believe that the Shan'ze Cloudrunners can still be saved from the corruption that taints them.

Take these bronze claws. Use them to mount the back of a Shan'ze Cloudrunner.

Attack them. Beat some sense back into their heads!

passages.title: Riding the Storm
passages.text: How did it go?

passages.title: Riding the Storm
passages.text:
We do not fully understand what the Shan'ze are doing, or the nature of their domination over the wild serpents.

Ban's theory is that the only thing that can cut through the mind control is physical pain.

Once the Shan'ze Cloudrunners feel enough pain, it looses the corruption's hold, and they finally remember who they are.

passages.title: A Cry From Darkness
passages.text:
So, you survived the imperial clutches. You are... resilient.

The Klaxxi hear another paragon to the north, among the sha-scorched roots of Kypari Vor.

This one cries out in terror and agony. It cannot be saved.

The Klaxxi want him put down. Go and defeat him or do not return here.

passages.title: A Cry From Darkness
passages.text: The order stands. Slay the fallen paragon.

passages.title: A Cry From Darkness
passages.text:
What?! How did you...

The Deathcaller was a legendary hero. He must not have been fully wakened.

You are fortunate.

passages.title: Sacred Recipe
passages.text:
"When the horror comes a-rising
And the heavens hum with war
Our great vessel of salvation
Must be broken from its core."

The scroll continues on for several stanzas. Perhaps somebody at The Sunset Brewgarden will be able to decipher its cryptic message.

passages.title: Sacred Recipe
passages.text:
Is that some sort of scroll?

Would you mind if I took a look?

passages.title: Sacred Recipe
passages.text:
<Lya reads the entirety of the message.>

This scroll, this... this prophecy...

It's terrifying!

passages.title: Bound With Shade
passages.text:
About that scroll you found...

I keep looking at that line in the second stanza - "bound with wood and shade". The "shade", in particular, intrigues me.

I must admit, I've often considered taking some of the area's residual sha essence and incorporating it into a brew. I suspect that this is the shade which our recipe calls for.

You will find large amalgamations of sha to the southeast of our tree... though you may also be able to harvest some from the local wildlife.

passages.title: Bound With Shade
passages.text:
Beautiful. This will make a fine addition to our brew.

The most dangerous ingredients are quite often the most delicious.

passages.title: I Bring Us Great Shame
passages.text:
I have failed my fellow brewers.

I took some supplies out to the clearing, east of our tree... and I left them there. Now, with the sha corrupting the land, and the mantid on the prowl, it is too dangerous for me to bring them back.

If you would help me look for them, perhaps I could regain some of my lost honor.

passages.title: I Bring Us Great Shame
passages.text: Did you find them? Can it be?

passages.title: I Bring Us Great Shame
passages.text: You have brought me joy, traveler.

passages.title: Rending Daggers
passages.text:
Forget about them, and forget their BREW. We've got real work to do.

The scroll mentions "rending daggers of the great ones". I've got a feeling I know where to find them.

A pair of mantid lieutenants patrol the Horrid March, to the south. Each one carries a ceremonial dagger.

Bring those daggers back here, <name>. We may be on the brink of something big.

passages.title: Rending Daggers
passages.text:
I think I'm starting to understand the next few lines of this prophecy, <name>.

Do you have the daggers yet?

passages.title: Rending Daggers
passages.text:
These daggers, look!

<Lya holds the blades hilt-to-hilt.>

They were built to fit together! But how to join them...?

passages.title: Evie Stormstout
passages.text:
I was too late. She was so small... and I was too late.

She should be given a proper burial. A little warrior like her deserves better than this.

passages.title: Evie Stormstout
passages.text: <Chen is in mourning.>

passages.title: Evie Stormstout
passages.text: <Chen is, for the moment, silent.>

passages.title: The Horror Comes A-Rising
passages.text:
We are protected from the mantid. Such was the agreement made so many millennia ago.

There are forces from which we are not safe, however. The kyparites beneath the ground to the west will haunt us, chase us... even eat us. The mistlurkers eat our kind by the handful.

Help our people, outsider. Defeat our enemies.

passages.title: The Horror Comes A-Rising
passages.text: We hate being eaten.

passages.title: The Horror Comes A-Rising
passages.text:
It is good to have someone of your colossal size in our village.

You have many uses.

passages.title: Fiery Wings
passages.text:
I think that old paper said something about "fiery wings." Those little dragons around here have wings. They're kind of fiery, in a way.

You're quicker than me. Try catching some of those dragons... or at least slapping the powder off of them.

No point in killing a harmless little dragon, if all you want is the sparkle from their wings.

passages.title: Fiery Wings
passages.text: I haven't been able to catch any of those things!

passages.title: Fiery Wings
passages.text:
YEAH!!! FLITTERLING DUST!!!

<Olon throws the powder into the pot.>

This brew is turning out... strange, and pretty smelly. I'm starting to think maybe Lya was right.

passages.title: Great Vessel of Salvation
passages.text:
I know what you and the girl-panda seek. We can perform the rite for you... in time.

First, I require aid. The seeds fall from our great mother-tree. It is our responsibility to collect them, even in dangerous times like these.

Escort my chanters to the motherseeds, that they may bring them back to the collection pit.

passages.title: Great Vessel of Salvation
passages.text: The collection pit is down the hill, just to the west of here.

passages.title: Great Vessel of Salvation
passages.text:
Yes, good. The motherseeds are taken care of.

Now, we may speak of your enchantment.

passages.title: Promises of Gold
passages.text:
As soon as the creature died, a strange group of sprites appeared and took its pearl away.

The sprites have a village nearby, called Rikkitun Village. Perhaps you should investigate.

passages.title: Promises of Gold
passages.text:
This shinyseed... it was your doing? I already had one shinyseed... but two is better.

We need only the seed, not the casing. If you like, you can keep.

passages.title: Fires and Fears of Old
passages.text:
We've found the blades, bound them together with wood and shade, and blessed them with an ancient incantation. If I'm not mistaken, it's time to use this thing.

The sprites spoke of an ancient piece of sap within the Amber Hibernal, a mantid cave near their empress' palace. That must be the "Blood of Ancients" that the prophecy spoke of.

Whatever's inside that sap must be important. Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Fires and Fears of Old
passages.text: Make sure to bring that forked blade with you.

passages.title: Fires and Fears of Old
passages.text:
There was a... a mantid inside that amber? I never would have thought that the solution to our war on the mantid would be... another mantid.

There are still many things that I have left to learn, but I do know this: that CERTAINLY wasn't a beer recipe.

passages.title: Extending Our Coverage
passages.text:
The Klaxxi'va hear another paragon. His cries are weak and lost in darkness. The signal must be strengthened.

There is a tower in Amberglow Hollow that has been silent for many years. It must sing; The Klaxxi demand it!

This time I will go with you. You will help me repair it.

Take the resonating crystal and meet me in Amberglow.

passages.title: Extending Our Coverage
passages.text: Why are you just standing here?

passages.title: Extending Our Coverage
passages.text:
It is good you showed up when you did.

Perhaps you are not as useless as I thought...

The Klaxxi'va sing to the paragon now. Soon they will know where to send you. For now there are other tasks.

passages.title: Crime and Punishment
passages.text:
The Stinging Trail nurtures young Kypari trees. The empress drains the saplings too early, outsider. They must grow before the amber can be taken.

The Klaxxi'va demand punishment for this crime! It will please them if you rain death on the Ik'thik harvesters.

passages.title: Crime and Punishment
passages.text: The Klaxxi are pleased with our work, outsider. You have proven to be more resourceful than we thought.

passages.title: By the Sea, Nevermore
passages.text:
The Klaxxi'va have spoken to me, outsider. The paragon is hidden in the Briny Muck only, he is not so hidden anymore.

The lizard men surround him. He cannot fall into their scaly hands.

You will find him; you will awaken him. Do not return without him!

If you do this The Klaxxi will be pleased with us.

passages.title: By the Sea, Nevermore
passages.text:
What... what sort of creature are you?

How have you awoken me?

passages.title: Better With Age
passages.text:
It is a crime to harvest the young trees, but a much bigger crime to waste the amber.

Young amber is not as strong, but the Klaxxi need it to continue the fight. We will bring them more and they will sing my praises!

Gather the young amber. We will store it until it is aged and can be consumed.

passages.title: Better With Age
passages.text: I would go with you to gather amber, but my talents are more useful here.

passages.title: Better With Age
passages.text:
Even this raw amber will be of use. We can't afford to be picky in times like these.

The Klaxxi'va will be glad I thought of this. I will tell them you helped!

passages.title: Reunited
passages.text:
You look at me and see I am no great warrior. Why was I chosen to be a Paragon? Not all weapons can be seen, Wakener. One should not judge by appearance alone.

Before I explain further, I need to know that you are trustworthy.

Something precious to me was hidden at the time of my preservation. I am nothing without it.

Defend me as I unearth my greatest weapon, and you will have my trust.

passages.title: Reunited
passages.text: Kovok is just as impressive as the last time I saw him. He will ensure great victories for the Klaxxi.

passages.title: Feed or Be Eaten
passages.text:
After years of working with the Kunchong I developed a theory; raising one from infancy would strengthen the bond and therefore strengthen the sonic connection.

I had just begun training Kovok when I was chosen for encasement. He is still very young and will need diligent training to reach his full potential.

I'm entrusting Kovok to you, but be warned; if any harm comes to him your life is forfeit.

First, you must feed him to gain his trust. The turtles in the area should be suitable for this.

passages.title: Feed or Be Eaten
passages.text: Once the bond is formed a Kunchong will gladly give its life for you.

passages.title: Feed or Be Eaten
passages.text:
Very good! I had half expected Kovok to just eat you. What a pleasant surprise to see you both in one piece,

Perhaps Kunchong raising is in your blood.

passages.title: Hozen in the Mist
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

Your research into the hozen has proven quite enlightening.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: Hozen in the Mist
passages.text:
Hozen are, by their very nature, a rambunctious lot.

We will add this knowledge to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: Fish Tales
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

I have thoroughly enjoyed reading your research in to the jinyu. A fascinating people and quite clever too.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: Fish Tales
passages.text:
This is a real treat. I always did enjoy the jinyu. Such a peaceful people with a real appreciation for wisdom.

We will add this knowledge to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: The Dark Heart of the Mogu
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

We have always known the mogu to be dark and sinister. Your research however would imply that they are far worse.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: The Dark Heart of the Mogu
passages.text: Mogu. Even the word makes my fur stand on end. We will add this knowledge to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: What is Worth Fighting For
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

You have recovered the story of our people's freedom from the mogu empire.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: What is Worth Fighting For
passages.text:
Who would have thought the freedom of the pandaren people would begin with a single punch.

 Wonderful. We will add this knowledge to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: Heart of the Mantid Swarm
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

While we appreciate your efforts to investigate the lore of Pandaria, the documents you sent us on the mantid managed to rob me of several nights sleep. Terrifying stuff.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: Heart of the Mantid Swarm
passages.text:
When we began this research project I never thought I would learn so much about such a terrifying people.

We will add this knowledge to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: Founding of the Order of the Cloud Serpent
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

We have a wonderful story assembled from the lore you recovered on the Order of the Cloud Serpent.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: Klaxx Attack
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

We have all been quite disturbed by your findings regarding the Klaxxi.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: The Song of the Yaungol
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

Your research in to the yaungol has proven most insightful.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: The Song of the Yaungol
