passages.text: The yaungol are a warring people strengthened by their exile beyond the wall. We will add this knowledge to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: Legends of the Brewfathers
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

Your research in to the Brewfathers has proven most... thirstifying.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: The Seven Burdens of Shaohao
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

It would seem you have discovered the full tale of Shaohao, the last emperor of Pandaria.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: The Seven Burdens of Shaohao
passages.text:
This is a story I have long sought to uncover. Ever since the Sha was released I have felt in my belly that this tale was at the heart of it all.

We will add this knowledge to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: The Ballad of Liu Lang
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

At long last thanks to your research we have the full Ballad of Liu Lang.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: The Ballad of Liu Lang
passages.text: The long lost story of Lou Lang and his Wandering Isle. This is a superb addition to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Yalia Sagewhisper
passages.text:
The Shado-Pan brothers and sisters continue to whisper of your deeds, <name>.

In fact, Yalia herself has taken quite an interest in your studies.

She wishes to challenge you in the training ring.

You would do well to impress her. If you do, she just may be willing to help you in the future.

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Yalia Sagewhisper
passages.text: Did you speak to Yalia?

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Yalia Sagewhisper
passages.text:
You did it! You bested Yalia!

You have most definitely earned her favor, <race>.

passages.title: Concentrated Fear
passages.text:
Amber is power. It brings life.

This... dread amber you brought me has been twisted. It is concentrated fear.

The Vor'thik know this well. Their kypari has been completely engulfed by sha, and they use the dread amber to quicken their own swarmborn.

Bring me the crystals used by the Vor'thik fear-shapers in their rituals. The Klaxxi will study them and decide on a protocol for disposal.

passages.title: Concentrated Fear
passages.text: Do you have the crystals?

passages.title: Concentrated Fear
passages.text: What would happen, I wonder, if you ate one? What would it do to your soft, pink insides?

passages.title: Culling the Swarm
passages.text:
The Empress continues to amass her forces. Without intervention, they WILL overrun that wall - even if it means smothering it in the corpses of a million swarmborn.

Let us find a better place for those corpses.

Let me know when you are ready to depart for the clutches - I will gladly drop you in from above.

passages.title: Culling the Swarm
passages.text: We must kill faster than they can multiply. It is that simple.

passages.title: Culling the Swarm
passages.text: This will do, for now.

passages.title: Eradicating the Zan'thik
passages.text:
The warriors of Zan'vess are some of the most feared and respected in the empire, for good reason.

Impalers are unmatched in their mastery of the polearm - no doubt Malik trained among the Zan'thik in his time. Their manipulators command terrifying sonic power with the ease and subtlety of a breath.

Both will need to be dealt with.

passages.title: Eradicating the Zan'thik
passages.text: I will admit, Wakener, I am impressed.

passages.title: Assault Deadtalker's Plateau
passages.text:
We have always left the Deadtalkers alone. For so long, they were just responsible for maintaining the sacred burial grounds of the yaungol tribes.

Now, though, they are practicing dark magic, defiling the corpses of their former clanmates... 

I know not where they learned those dark magics, or why they no longer treat their dead with respect, but we do not have time to find out. 

We need to stop them.

passages.title: Assault Deadtalker's Plateau
passages.text: Have you defeated the Deadtalkers?

passages.title: Assault Deadtalker's Plateau
passages.text: By conspiring to use these dark magics, the Deadtalkers have given up their rights to protection. Your actions should deter them from their current course, I hope.

passages.title: Spirit Dust
passages.text:
The spirits that the Yaungol are entrapping from the remains of their ancestors still have a bit of the essence of life within them. 

If you defeat the spirits in battle, you can collect essence from the spirits as dust, and then return it to the corpses in the area, which will send the spirits, finally, to the next life.

This is the only way to set right what the Deadtalkers have done. It will also help keep us safe.

passages.title: Spirit Dust
passages.text: Have the spirits been returned to rest?

passages.title: Spirit Dust
passages.text: Good, you have helped right this terrible wrong.

passages.title: The Deadtalker Cipher
passages.text:
We need to understand what went wrong with the Deadtalkers. 

For so many years, the Deadtalkers were simply responsible for maintaining the burial grounds and holding funerals for fallen warriors.

From a recent raid, we've recovered a tablet from the grounds that is clearly written using a cipher, but it isn't one we've encountered before. If you can gather a ciphered scroll from one of the Deadtalkers, we can begin to put together the cypher and understand what's happened.

passages.title: The Deadtalker Cipher
passages.text: Did you find something?

passages.title: The Deadtalker Cipher
passages.text:
Aha! Show me that.

Hmm... we will send this to the monastery for analysis. As we find which of these symbols are most common in their writing, we can begin to understand the meaning of these writings.

passages.title: The Enemy of My Enemy... Is Still My Enemy!
passages.text:
The mantid are our enemies. As are the yaungol at Fire Camp Gai-Cho.

It is fortunate, then, that they are also each other's enemies. Mantid from Kri'vess constantly attack the Gai-Cho yaungol, who hold them off at their front gates.

I want you to wreak havoc. "Borrow" some highly explosive oil barrels from camp Gai-Cho, and toss them down onto the battlefield from the air.

I don't care which ones you kill, just kill a lot of them.

passages.title: The Enemy of My Enemy... Is Still My Enemy!
passages.text: How goes the battle?

passages.title: The Enemy of My Enemy... Is Still My Enemy!
passages.text: Ha! Good work. Teaches both of them to make enemies of the Shado-Pan.

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Chao the Voice
passages.text:
It looks like you're quite the fighter, adventurer.

Chao heard about it, and she's been talking about how she'd kick your...

Well, let's just say I think you should challenge her and try to get her respect.

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Chao the Voice
passages.text: Well? How did it go?

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Chao the Voice
passages.text:
I'm sure there's no hard feelings. She just loves a good fight.

You should talk to her next time I have some missions for you. She's quite an able fighter, as I'm sure you saw.

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Lao-Chin the Iron Belly
passages.text:
Lao-Chin seems to have his head in the clouds... or, rather, in his beer.

After all of his recent battles, he seems completely obsessed with with trying to develop the perfect brew for fighting. 

That's well and good, but we need him to actually do some fighting!

You should go challenge him, see if you can snap him out of his rut. 

If you beat him, he'll probably want to go out and help fight just to try to one-up you!

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Lao-Chin the Iron Belly
passages.text: Well?

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Lao-Chin the Iron Belly
passages.text: Wow, you must have impressed Lao-Chin. He can't stop talking about how excited he is to go out and fight with you. Good work.

passages.title: Fate of the Stormstouts
passages.text:
adventurer! It is so great to see you healthy, and traveling so far. It would seem that our paths are quite tightly intertwined.

I'm here looking for my family. I am told that several Stormstouts came across the wall to help face the mantid threat. I mean to find them, and join them.

Have you seen anyone named Stormstout come through here? Would you mind helping me ask around?

passages.title: Fate of the Stormstouts
passages.text: You are brave to have come across the wall, tauren.

passages.title: Fate of the Stormstouts
passages.text:
<Chen listens intently.>

Big Dan, Han, Evie, and Mama. I understand.

It seems like Dan will be safe here. I will go look for Evie, Han, and Mama Stormstout.

Take care, <name>.

passages.title: A Visit with Lorewalker Cho
passages.text:
Stranger, I may be able to help you find your prince. But first, I would like to know a little more about you and your people.

Come, help me with my chores, and we will chat.

You have the look of a grizzled war veteran, but certainly you have a few minutes to help a bookish Pandaren like myself putter around the house, yes?

passages.title: A Visit with Lorewalker Cho
passages.text: There is nothing like a little manual labor to bring strangers together, don't you think?

passages.title: A Visit with Lorewalker Cho
passages.text:
Despite your many years of combat, you've still got an eye for beauty, <name>. I like that about you!

Now, let's find this missing prince of yours.

passages.title: Kor'thik Aggression
passages.text:
I'm no brewer - just looking at all those heaps of ingredients makes my head spin. Just put the brew in front of me when it's finished, thank you.

No, I'm here to make sure that the brewers don't get cut in half while they're trying to make that perfect brew. It's not an easy job.

The Kor'thik mantid across this basin have been attacking us nightly. If you're already heading over there, why don't you return the favor and attack a few of them?

passages.title: Kor'thik Aggression
passages.text: You've got the makings of a fine brewgarden guard, <race>. Let me know if you ever get tired of the whole "<class>" thing.

passages.title: The Arts of a Monk
passages.text: When you fight, you grow in skill. As you grow in skill, you will begin to figure out new moves. Go, explore, learn, and show me what you figure out.

passages.title: The Arts of a Monk
passages.text: You picked that one up quickly. I can't wait to show you some of my other favorite tricks.

passages.title: Palm of the Tiger
passages.text:
Now that you've had the chance to test your abilities in battle, it's time to explain one more reason why training is so important.

As you get more experience, you'll be able to do new techniques you never thought of.

Go, get some experience, learn a new skill, and demonstrate it on one of the training dummies.

passages.title: Palm of the Tiger
passages.text: You're a quick learner, <name>.

passages.title: The Rear is Clear
passages.text:
Excellent work, <name>! The rear is now officially clear. We'll take care of the stragglers. I want you to go back to Marshal McBride, standing in front of Northshire Abbey, south of here, and let him know that the goblin situation is under control.

Farewell, <class>.

passages.title: The Rear is Clear
passages.text: With your help we have managed to secure the northern and western sectors of Northshire. We still have a rather large contingency of Blackrock orcs to the east and they've begun burning down the forest!

passages.title: Kick, Punch, It's All in the Mind
passages.text:
The truth is, you already have the talent and ability to learn what you need to. What I can help you do is show you where to unlock it.

First, you must practice until you begin to understand a new technique. The first technique you learn will be the Tiger Palm. Go, learn more until you have unlocked the potential within yourself, and then practice your new move!

Remember - it's all in the mind!

passages.title: Kick, Punch, It's All in the Mind
passages.text: Ahh, good work. You may return any time you need another lesson from teacher.

passages.title: Tiger Palm
passages.text:
As you walk the road of your training, you will begin to discover within yourself the power to unlock new techniques. You need not even learn them from me, or another more experienced monk - you will find that they come to you on their own.

For now, you should go and practice the basics. Gather more experience, and develop a new technique - once you have, you can practice it on the dummies nearby to master it.

passages.title: Tiger Palm
passages.text: Good, good. Your first challenge surpassed. We will learn much from each other, I can see.

passages.title: Proving Pit
passages.text:
Ya done quite well for ya'self, <class>. I'm sure I could teach ya a trick or two here and dere, but I not be wastin' ya time on tiki targets no longer.

l put one last trial before ya den, mon. Head over to da provin' pit in the middle of dis area and fight a real baddy - one dat wants ta kill ya back. Just let the jailor by the pit know when ya ready.

passages.title: Proving Pit
passages.text: All trolls gotta prove demselves before we let them move past da training grounds.

passages.title: Proving Pit
passages.text: Ya handle yerself quite well. Ya gonna be quite powerful some day.

passages.title: The Arts of a Monk
passages.text:
As ya get bettah' at fightin', you'll start to find new tings that ya nevah knew you could do.

Wanna see? Go, train up some, and learn someting new.

'Den come back and ya can show me.

passages.title: The Arts of a Monk
passages.text: Good work, mon! Dis stuff come easy to ya.

passages.title: Tiger Palm
passages.text:
You have done well. As you continue along your path, you will grow, learning new techniques that you couldn't have imagined before.

Your first lesson is the power of experience. Go, learn a new ability, and demonstrate it for me.

passages.title: Tiger Palm
passages.text: You have done well, <name>.

passages.title: The Art of the Monk
passages.text:
The true secret to the art of the monk is unlocking the knowledge and power hidden inside yourself.

Go, get more experience, and learn a new skill. Then demonstrate it on one of the training dummies.

passages.title: The Art of the Monk
passages.text: You've proven a capable student. When it is time to resume your training, return to me and I will show you other techniques.

passages.title: Monk Training
passages.text:
As you advance within your class, you will want to take advantage of the training that your class trainer can provide you. For young monks here on Sunstrider Isle, your trainer is Pao, our Pandaren visitor. Speak with her and see what training she has available for you.

Pao - as with all the trainers on Sunstrider Isle - is inside the Sunspire on the lower level.

passages.title: Monk Training
passages.text: Ah, welcome. I have been teaching your people the ways of the <class>, and they seem to be well suited for it. Perhaps you too will take to it as quickly as they.

passages.title: Tiger Palm
passages.text:
Good. You are off to a bright start. This road will be long, and as you become more accomplished, you will begin to discover that you can do things you could never have imagined before.

Go, get more experience, and learn a new technique. Once you have, demonstrate it on one of the training dummies.

passages.title: Tiger Palm
passages.text: I think you've mastered the basics of the Tiger Palm technique, <name>. Perhaps you will impress me, after all.

passages.title: The Tiger Palm
passages.text:
I hope your people are all alright... the crash was unbelievably loud and destructive!

<Mojo looks you over, evaluating your potential.>

Yes, you'll do fine. They've said that they need more people to fight, and they don't want me to hurt myself. I'm not afraid, but I don't want to intrude. So, I'll teach you.

As you may have discovered, your experiences in combat will unlock new potential within you. Go, see if you can master a new ability. Show it to me. You'll get the hang of things.

passages.title: The Tiger Palm
passages.text: Keep that technique handy, <name>. You can use it to finish off strong opponents, or just to feel awesome, like a tiger.

passages.title: The Dread Vos
passages.text:
Another paragon calls to us..

This time, the emanations grow from The Dread Vos, an ancient lake to the south.

Finding him will not be easy, for the way is guarded by our enemies.

I give you this task. If you succeed, you will live.

If you fail, I will send another.

passages.title: Skeer the Bloodseeker
passages.text:
Our efforts to secure the shallows before Zan'vess have paid off.

We have spotted another paragon buried in amber, hidden in the waters to the southwest.

Adding another paragon to our numbers is vital. Another champion from ages past could turn the tide in our favor.

I would go immediately, but unfortunately, I am needed here.

Since you are already a Wakener, you can carry out this task in my stead.

passages.title: Skeer the Bloodseeker
passages.text:
The hunger... they said it would be fierce, but I did not expect anything like this.

It is strange to feel so... weak.

passages.title: A Bloody Delight
passages.text:
A warrior is not ready for battle until he tastes the blood of his enemies.

I am still too weak to hunt, so you must go in my stead.

Only the blood from the fiercest predators will do. I can smell their presence in the waters outside this cave!

Bring this to me, and then perhaps you shall see why they call me the Bloodseeker.

passages.title: A Bloody Delight
passages.text: By drinking the blood of your enemies, you acquire their strength.

passages.title: A Bloody Delight
passages.text: Yes, this will do.

passages.title: The Scent of Blood
passages.text:
I'm afraid that I wet my hands with saurok blood while you were away.

I'm sorry, but I could not help myself. Now, watch them attack me.

Pitiful!

Do they think to take vengeance for their fallen? Do they come challenge ME?

I, who have won a hundred wars? I, who stood alone against thousands and still shouted for my enemies to come?

No, these... saurok... will crumple before me like paper before the flame!

I shall show you my might, Wakener. Fight alongside me and see.

Here they come!

passages.title: The Scent of Blood
passages.text: You have succeeded once again. Well done, Wakener.

passages.title: Fresh Pots
passages.text:
We got a load of empty crab pots out there that need fresh bait.

Now, we COULD pull them one at a time and bait them up here in comfort. A nice chair to sit on, maybe a hot cup of tea to keep you warm. Sounds nice, doesn't it?

Never gonna happen.

Head to Lonesome Cove, immediately southeast, and bait those pots with two chunks of fresh sea monarch. By "fresh" I mean killed right there in the water.

Oh, and by "pots" I mean traps. If you wanna be part of the crew, you'd better learn the lingo.

passages.title: Fresh Pots
passages.text: What's wrong, green? You aren't afraid of the dark, icy sea are you?

passages.title: Fresh Pots
passages.text: Not bad, green, not bad.

passages.title: You Otter Know
passages.text:
You know what happened to the bait in those pots?

Otters. That's what happened.

They prefer fresh clams, but they'll pick our crab traps clean if they're hungry enough.

The otters in Lonesome Cove are protected by law and we run a legitimate operation here. As much as I'd love to chum those little rats and call it a day, we just make sure they aren't hungry enough to raid the crab pots.

Toss 'em a few clams to keep them busy while you're out there.

passages.title: You Otter Know
passages.text: In the words of my old deck boss: "Do what I say, 'cause I said it!"

passages.title: You Otter Know
passages.text: That should keep their little whiskers out of our traps for awhile.

passages.title: Walking Dog
passages.text:
Dog ain't my "pet." He's a member of this crew, and my best friend. Saved my life more than once, you know.

But I'm gettin' too old to walk him anymore, and he still needs his exercise. Take Dog for a trip around the shelf for me, would ya?

He loves to swim through the hot geysers just southeast of the shallows.

He absolutely has to... er... "leave his mark" on the dead whale at the far western edge of the shelf.

Oh, and he'll want to visit our old shipwreck, too. He likes to reminisce.

passages.title: Walking Dog
passages.text: How did it go? I hope he didn't cause too much trouble!

passages.title: On the Crab
passages.text:
I just got word that a string of pots we dropped this morning hit it BIG. We're on the crab!

Problem is, the rips are getting stronger and we lost track of some of the pots. They're just sitting out there, filled with spiky blue GOLD!

I need you back out there. Hook one of these buoys up to any of the full traps you find and send it to the surface for us.

passages.title: On the Crab
passages.text: Nice work out there!

passages.title: Shark Week
passages.text:
Crabbing is our big money-maker, but we send all kinds of goods back around the wall. Oils, plants, even rare minerals - the sea's bounty is rich out here!

Right now the big craze in the markets back home is thresher teeth. Apparently they make great necklaces?

Threshers are all over the Shelf of Mazu to the west. Bring me lots of teeth!

passages.title: Shark Week
passages.text: Having actually seen someone eaten by a thresher, I'm not sure why you'd willingly string their teeth around your neck, but whatever.

passages.title: Shark Week
passages.text: Those are perfect, just put them down over there. I'd rather not touch them myself. Creeps me out.

passages.title: The Mariner's Revenge
passages.text:
I'm not gonna sit in a damn rocking chair while my crew gets devoured by a leviathan!

Come on, let's get to the dock and launch a dinghy. I got a special one set up just for this kind of situation. My own little Mist-Hopper Jr.

We'll give that thing a case of harpoon fever.

passages.title: The Mariner's Revenge
passages.text: Let's go!

passages.title: The Mariner's Revenge
passages.text:
Nice shooting out there!

I knew we could do it. Never met anything that can't be killed with enough harpoons.

passages.title: A Morale Victory
passages.text:
The mantid have statues built on Sra'vess. We don't know exactly what they use them for. They may have some sort of religious significance, or maybe they assist with their sonic communication.

When you fight your opponent, you don't just engage them physically, you also engage them mentally. Whatever they use them for, the fact is that those statues are important to them.

Which is why I want you to blow them up. Losing something important will be a substantial hit to morale.

passages.title: A Morale Victory
passages.text: The statues?

passages.title: A Morale Victory
passages.text: I'm sure they'll be upset without those statues. Right?

passages.title: Destroy the Siege Weapons!
passages.text:
The mantid don't just attack in swarms. 

They're smart. They use alchemy, bombs... and what's worst, they've got siege weapons. Those have the potential to be incredibly destructive if they attack with them.

We've got reports that they're building up a force of siege weapons to the west at Sra'vess. Go and destroy them.

passages.title: Destroy the Siege Weapons!
passages.text: Those siege weapons won't be a problem. They may rebuild, but we've bought ourselves some time.

passages.title: Fumigation
passages.text:
Our alchemists have cooked up a set of gas bombs that will discourage mantid from staying anywhere that we set them off. 

If we plant these in the critical structures of Sra'vess, they'll need to evacuate. That should sow some chaos and delay any action from the mantid there for days.

Get to it, <name>.

passages.title: Fumigation
passages.text: Have you planted the gas bombs?

passages.title: Fumigation
passages.text: Nice, I can see the smoke from here. That should definitely cause some confusion!

passages.title: Friends, Not Food!
passages.text:
Our scouts have sent a very troubling report. 

Three of our trainees have gone missing, and our scouts found them... 

They've been captured by the mantid and sent to their Kunchong pits. 

Their Kunchong FEEDING pits. We're lucky that the Kunchong don't eat that often.

I need you to get in there, give them these escape kites, and get them out!

passages.title: Friends, Not Food!
passages.text: The trainees, <name>! You have to save them!

passages.title: Friends, Not Food!
passages.text: Oh, thank goodness. I was worried about them!

passages.title: Target of Opportunity: Sra'thik Swarmlord
passages.text:
While we're here, we should do one more thing.

The Sra'thik Swarmlord is responsible for directing the mantid forces from the air. If we leave it alive, it's going to cause trouble for the garrison.

So we're not going to leave it alive. Let's take it out, adventurer.

passages.title: Target of Opportunity: Sra'thik Swarmlord
passages.text: We need to take down the Swarmlord!

passages.title: Target of Opportunity: Sra'thik Swarmlord
passages.text:
I heard you did a little... extra credit while you were out there. Good work, friend.

Come back another day - I'm sure we'll have some more work for you.

passages.title: The Arena of Annihilation
passages.text:
Ah, I can still remember running fights out of a muddy hole in the ground back in Nagrand. We've come a long way, eh, Wodin?

I tell you, there's nothing more these Tiger monks like than a good scrap. So much so that they've paid good coin for me to set up shop here and help draw the strongest fighters from all around!

So how about it? You and a couple friends up for a few rounds in the Arena of Annihilation...? Big money, big prizes!

passages.title: The Arena of Annihilation
passages.text: What are you waiting for? The monks are spoiling for a good show.

passages.title: The Arena of Annihilation
passages.text: Gurgthock said you he'd make it worth your while, kid. Take your pick!

passages.title: The Poisoned Mind
passages.text:
Before we return to Klaxxi'vess, I wish to look upon the empire.

The Klaxxi Council told me that the enemy gathers outside the Empress's palace.

My poisons are ready. What better way to announce my return than with death and destruction?

Just be careful not to mix the two serums... at least not while you're holding the vessels.

Speak to me when you are ready to fly.

passages.title: The Poisoned Mind
passages.text: Fight from above.

passages.title: The Poisoned Mind
passages.text: Thank you for returning me home, Wakener, but I fear the war has just truly begun.

passages.title: Dark Skies
passages.text:
The swarm begins, Wakener! The mantid amass at the Heart of Fear.

Already they fill the skies with their wings and rend the earth with their claws. They shall not stop the dark march until their bodies are laid open and bleeding upon the ground.

This we shall gladly do. We will attack them from above. While I fly, use my poisons to destroy their advance.

Do not mix the two serums until you are ready to attack. The reaction can be quite... violent.

Speak to me when you are ready to go.

passages.title: Dark Skies
passages.text: Such wonderful destruction!

passages.title: Dark Skies
passages.text: Well done, Wakener. You have a destroyer's aim.

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Hawkmaster Nurong
passages.text:
You've really been building up respect with the Shado-Pan, <name>.

Nurong's interested in trying out his skills against you.

The good news is, if you win, I'll allow him to go with you on your missions.

The bad news is, I really don't think you'll win.

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Hawkmaster Nurong
passages.text: Not up to the challenge? I understand.

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Hawkmaster Nurong
passages.text:
Well, well, well. Looks like I was wrong.

Good work. Nurong's looking forward to accompanying you on your missions.

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Tenwu of the Red Smoke
passages.text:
So... you've been challenged by the infamous Tenwu of the Red Smoke.

That's what he calls himself, at least. He's a good fighter, and a good rogue, but it's a wonder he manages to sneak up on anyone with how loudly he brags about himself.

Anyways, I think you should answer the challenge. Maybe it'll give him a touch of humility. Maybe not. Either way, if you win, he'll probably be willing to go with you on your missions. 

And I get some entertainment.

passages.title: The Challenger's Ring: Tenwu of the Red Smoke
passages.text:
Wow! Well done. Glad to see you fought so well.

Maybe if he's trying to keep up with your fighting it'll help keep his mouth shut.

passages.title: Prophet Khar'zul
passages.text:
Prophet Khar'zul is a powerful caster, but he is also underestimating your abilities.

Khar'zul and his forces must be destroyed to protect this village. His death will send a strong message to the Thunder King that we will not be defeated!

You'll find him on the Isle of Reckoning.

passages.title: Prophet Khar'zul
passages.text: Is Khar'zul dead?

passages.title: Prophet Khar'zul
passages.text:
These events should be learned from, <name>.

It is important that we learn from our history. Had we paid attention to the histories, we may have been able to head this off before it got this far.

Everything that has happened was already foretold, we just didn't know how to read it.

passages.title: Welcome to Dawn's Blossom
passages.text:
Cho's off on another one of his adventures, and this one requires a big order of jade. I'm going to have to call in some favors.

How 'bout in the meantime you introduce yourself to some of the locals.

Kai Wanderbrew is a good guy to know, as is Master Windfur. Oh, and say hi to Peiji Goldendraft up at the inn.

Between the three of them, you should get the feel for life in Dawn's Blossom.

passages.title: Welcome to Dawn's Blossom
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: Welcome to Dawn's Blossom
passages.text: Good, good, good. You're going to fit right in.

passages.title: Dreadspinner Extermination
passages.text:
Back in Gurthani Terrace where you found me, dreadspinners continue to occupy the attention of Shado-Pan marksmen who could otherwise be thinning out this wretched swarm.

Eradicate those spiders and offer some relief to the archers on that wall.

passages.title: Dreadspinner Extermination
passages.text: I never liked spiders. Filthy, mindless insects.

passages.title: Nope Nope Nope
passages.text:
I recovered this weapon on a recent scouting run near the wall. It would seem ideal for helping your Shado-Pan with their infestation problem in Gurthani Terrace.

The more they are focused on keeping spiders off the wall, the less time they are killing fear-gripped swarmborn.

passages.title: Nope Nope Nope
passages.text: A crude weapon, but it has its uses.

passages.title: Debugging the Terrace
passages.text:
If this Empress is truly possessed by fear and paranoia, she will have sent scouts to every corner of the land in order to cement her control.

These scout grubs are likely everywhere, but difficult to spot with the naked eye. Better to track them by the pheromone trails they leave behind.

I've already... gifted you... a reactive toxin that will reveal these trails to you for a brief time after experiencing the thrill of victory.

Go now to the Terrace of Gurthan and root out these spies.

passages.title: Debugging the Terrace
passages.text: Best not to ask how I afflicted you with the toxin - you have become quite useful to us, and it would be a shame if we drove you mad with horror just yet.

passages.title: Debugging the Terrace
passages.text: Information is power, <name>. We cannot allow the Empess to monitor our movements.

passages.title: Brain Food
passages.text:
Kovok is growing at an accelerated rate, but his brain may not be able to keep up. He'll require a special diet to ensure that he does not outgrow the capacity to control his own body.

Mushan tongue is rich in the nutrients that promote brain growth in kunchong, but they normally eat the beasts whole and fill up quickly. If we feed Kovok only mushan tongues every couple of days or so, it should balance out his growth.

Greatback mushan graze the hills east of here, near the Gurthani Terrace.

passages.title: Brain Food
passages.text: Have you found a suitable meal for Kovok?

passages.title: Brain Food
passages.text: Kovok was whining the whole time you were away. It was really quite pathetic.

passages.title: Wicked Wikkets
passages.text:
<name> good wikket, they say...

<name> help hozen, they say...

No more grookin' <name>, they say.

That ok. Look out there. Wicked wikkets fallin' like rain, ripe for the grookin'!

Go, join the fun. But remember, Chief Kah Kah gets all the shinies! That's hozen rule number two.

<Jeek Jeek scratches his head.>

Hmm, all hozen rules are number two...

passages.title: Wicked Wikkets
passages.text: Whatcha got, wikket?

passages.title: Wicked Wikkets
passages.text:
Wikket grookin' makin' hozen rich with shinies!

<name> makin' a good second impression. And for hozen, number two is most important!

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text:
Lok'tar, <class>.

We've made progress, but we're going to need mobility if we want to maintain our foothold here in Kun-Lai.

I don't see many worgs, kodo, or the like around here. What I do see are yaks. Our pandaren allies have said they make good mounts, so they'll have to do.

Go round some up and return them here, so we can get our people riding them!

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text: The yaks?

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text: Well done! Well, they're plenty stubborn, I'll say that much. But they should do nicely.

passages.title: Crane Mastery: Needlebeak
passages.text:
So, now that you've got a vibe for how cranes fight, I've got a doozy for you.

Needlebeak!

Or at least, that's what I'm calling him. Biggest crane I ever saw. And its beak is so sharp it's like a sword.

Northwest of here you'll find the big water fall that kicks off the Dojani River. Needlebeak likes to hang out by the waterfall.

You bring me its beak as a trophy and I will talk you up a good game to Nesingwary.

passages.title: Crane Mastery: Needlebeak
passages.text: I watched that bird stab a tiger through the face. What kind of place is this where birds are the predators for tigers?

passages.title: Crane Mastery: Needlebeak
passages.text: Now THAT is a trophy. Looks intimidating. Wait... is this your blood on it?

passages.title: A Little Brain Work
passages.text:
Far to the south, the swarm breeds weapons of destruction - enormous, nearly unbreakable amber scorpions.

Like all other creatures, they are subject to manipulation, but unlike other creatures, they have not yet submitted to my mind control.

It appears that further research is necessary before I can dominate them for our own purposes.

I must study their brains, and you must retrieve some specimens for me.

Take this sonic emitter. I have found it to be quite effective against the beasts.

passages.title: A Little Brain Work
passages.text: They continue to resist my sonic manipulation. I must understand why.

passages.title: A Little Brain Work
passages.text:
My my, this is interesting indeed. They are unlike any other brains I have seen.

I will study these carefully.

passages.title: Infection
passages.text:
The Empress's genemancers play with dangerous toys.

To the south, they are injecting local wildlife with pheromone-laden parasites, in an attempt to create monstrous mutations for war.

Carelessly, they have allowed their parasitic worms to escape into the local ecosystem.

Left unchecked, the infection will spread from one animal to another, until we have an outbreak.

I will inject you with a mild toxin. With it, you will be able to identify infected creatures.

Kill the carriers at once.

passages.title: Infection
passages.text:
So the infection was spreading. You halted the spread just in time, it seems.

I doubt that the genemancers will stop their outrageous experimentation, but we must continue to thwart their efforts.

passages.title: Surprise Attack!
passages.text:
Those damnable Mogu...

Those scouts were a distraction! While we were hunting their spies, the main force moved on Niuzao Temple. Corrupted serpents, Mogu everywhere... this is a disaster!

Thankfully, Ban was able to make it past their lines with the most elite members of our order. If you can slip past, too, meet up with him. We need to put a stop to this!

passages.title: Surprise Attack!
passages.text:
Niuzao has been saved. The Mogu pushed back. And you, friend, have been found worthy of a great honor. 

We shall induct you into the Shado-Pan.

passages.title: Ways of Cooking
passages.text: There are many ways of cooking, and each creates dishes with unique properties. The Pandaren Ways of Cooking are the Ways of the Grill, the Wok, the Pot, the Steamer, the Oven and the Brew. You seem to already have the basics of each way, from your experience in faraway lands. If you wish to progress further, speak with my siblings and learn the first advanced recipe each of them teaches. Find out which Way suits you the best.

passages.title: Research Project: The Pandaren Empire
passages.text:
Ah, adventurer. You come at a most opportune time. My daughter and I are researching the history of our people and have hit a roadblock in our research.

Should you come across fragments of the pandaren past, please, bring them to us here. We would benefit greatly from the additional information.

passages.title: Research Project: The Pandaren Empire
passages.text: It is dangerous to forget our past.

passages.title: Research Project: The Pandaren Empire
passages.text: Ah! Some fine pieces here. Very fine pieces indeed. My thanks, adventurer.

passages.title: Mogu Make Poor House Guests
passages.text:
Leven sent Rook here to stop mogu, but there are more than Rook can kill alone.

You help? Rook will tell Leven you helped. Promise.

passages.title: Mogu Make Poor House Guests
passages.text: Rook can handle rest of mogu.  Thanks for help.  Good man.

passages.title: Seeker's Folly
passages.text:
I'm sure your pandaren friend has some ideas about what the mogu are after.

He headed up the mountain a few days ago without a guide, and asked that only you be sent up after him. He was very specific:

"The <class> must endure the trek alone, with only <his/her> thoughts. <He/She> will honor each shrine before meeting me at the top."

The path is just northwest of the camp, marked by flags. Please be careful! Seeker's Folly is a dangerous trek even on a lucky day.

passages.title: Seeker's Folly
passages.text:
Ah, you made it, and you honored the shrines.

I knew you could handle it.

passages.title: Way of the Grill
passages.text: The Pandaren Way of the Grill produces foods that increase your physical strength. Bring some raw tiger steaks to the Master of the Grill, and he will teach you what you can do with them. There are many tigers in the Jade Forest and the Krasarang Wilds, but you can also find them in other places.

passages.title: Way of the Grill
passages.text: If you wish to learn the Way of the Grill, bring me some raw tiger steaks.

passages.title: Way of the Grill
passages.text: Good cuts.

passages.title: The Old Map
passages.text:
The old, faded leather is falling apart, but still legible.

Scrawled on it is some kind of map, and the following lines:

Deep in the valley where four winds blow,
The maiden laughs behind her golden fan.
At the feet of her ancestors' stair,
She whispers secrets into the echoing dark.

passages.title: The Old Map
passages.text: Whoa! I think you found it, <name>! You found the map to Old Man Thistle treasure!

passages.title: Just A Folk Story
passages.text:
What!?! This don't make any sense! <Fish's face falls.>

What's this mumber jumber about a maiden and an ancestor and a buncha stairs?

I can't make any reason outta this, can you?

Well, there are lotsa folks 'round here who're much older than you and me, <name>.

Can you go talk to the folks in Halfhill? I betcha they might know somethin'!

passages.title: Just A Folk Story
passages.text: Of course! It makes perfect sense. So the location of the treasure must be where the lake meets the mountains!

passages.title: Old Man Thistle's Treasure
passages.text:
Well high golly! This is turning into a real life treasure hunt!

There's gotta be some kind of entrance or opening to the north, where the mountains meet Cattail Lake.

I'll meet ya at the entrance! Let's go get that treasure!

passages.title: Old Man Thistle's Treasure
passages.text: If I weren't seeing it fer myself, I could hardly believe it!

passages.title: Old Man Thistle's Treasure
passages.text: The chest's lid slides off with the lightest touch. You peer inside...

passages.title: The Heartland Legacy
passages.text:
At the very bottom of the treasure chest, you find a stack of scrolls and a soft leather sack with seeds.

Unrolling the scrolls, you see they contain detailed farming notes, drawings of plants, numbers and calculations, locations of nearby water springs, and countless other snippets.

There might be someone at the Tillers Union who would like to see this.

passages.title: The Heartland Legacy
passages.text: What do you have there?

passages.title: The Heartland Legacy
passages.text:
Ah yes, I know the story of Old Man Thistle quite well, <race>.

There are all sorts of crazy tales about his quest for treasure.

But the truth of the matter is that he was a bit of a recluse, a bit eccentric, and an excellent farmer.

As he grew near the end of his life, he retreated up into the mountains and was never seen again.

He was just a man, and it seems that you have found his legacy.

But don't tell Fish the truth. Some stories are best left tall in the telling.

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Drink?
passages.text: Heeeey buddy, how'sh it goin'? You wanna buy a jinyu a drink?

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Drink?
passages.text: Thirsty...

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Drink?
passages.text: Thanksh, buddy.

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Round?
passages.text:
Heeeey it's my friend, the <race>!

I guesh you've seen me hanging 'round, but I should 'splain that I'm not drunk.

I mean, look at me now! Shober as a freshwater fish!

Sure I like to drown my sorrowsh in some good brew now and then, but you can't inebriate a jinyu! Might as well try to drown a fish!

No, the brewsh make me shleepy, and when I shleep, I have vishions of the future.

The shtronger the brew, the more potent my dreamsh! If you bring me a drink, I'll owe you one.

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Round?
passages.text: What do you mean I talk like I'm drunk? Thish ish how I shpeak!

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Round?
passages.text: Oooh, this is the shtuff.

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Keg?
passages.text:
My dreams grow dim recently, <race>.

I need something powerful to kick myshelf back into gear!

I heard there'sh a delishush drink that folksh are making nowadays.

It'sh called Jade Witch Brew.

I'd sure like to taste some.

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Keg?
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Keg?
passages.text: Oooh, that'sh got quite the kick! I'm growing shleepy...

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Brewery?
passages.text:
All right, <name>, in order to continue my vishions, I must now have my own brewery.

...

Just kidding! You should have sheen your own face! Hilarioush... hic!

Anyway, I heard of a new drink that is unlike any other, and I would like a tashte.

Have you heard of the Mad Brewer'sh Breakfasht? If you can bring me some of thish shtuff, you will be my friend for life.

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Brewery?
passages.text: Have you tried it?

passages.title: Buy A Fish A Brewery?
passages.text: Thank you, <name>! I will be shaving these for a rainy day... hic!

passages.title: Family Secrets
passages.text:
Our secret recipes! I was gathering them up. But then... hozen?

<Auntie looks very confused.>

How is Gao to brew anything? He needs those recipes or disaster is sure to strike!

passages.title: Family Secrets
passages.text: Well, hello!

passages.title: Family Secrets
passages.text:
Ho ho, what's this?

<Uncle Gao jiggles his fat brew belly at the sight of the family's recipes.>

Ooh, I knew I was adding too much corn!

passages.title: A Very Nice Necklace
passages.text:
The beautiful necklace is only partly smudged by dirty hozen hands.

There's only one person in the Valley who would own such a beautiful piece of jewelry.

passages.title: A Very Nice Necklace
passages.text: Oh my, this is my favorite necklace! I didn't even know it was missing! Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Tina's Tasteful Tiara
passages.text:
It's a dazzling diamond tiara. Who in the valley would be wealthy enough to own such a piece of jewelry?

Whoever it is, they might be willing to give a nice reward.

passages.title: Tina's Tasteful Tiara
passages.text: Oh, my tiara! It was missing, but wherever did you find it?

passages.title: Trouble Brewing
passages.text:
With the brewery infested by hozen and... and who knows what else, I'm sure that the brewers are in trouble.

Would you mind helping me find out what's going on, my friend?

passages.title: Trouble Brewing
passages.text:
A giant creature made of brew?! Who could have imagined such a thing?

You have my thanks for saving Gao from his own misguided brewing experiments.

passages.title: An Exquisite Earring
passages.text:
You unhook the earring off the furry creature's ear. It looks like he was having some fun wearing the dangly hoop. TOO much fun.

Perhaps the owner of this dainty bauble would like to see it returned. You don't have to tell her where you found it... or who was wearing it.

passages.title: An Exquisite Earring
passages.text:
Oh my earring! Why, it matches the one I'm wearing today!

<Tina hooks the earring onto her ear.>

Thank you, <name>!

passages.title: A Beautiful Brooch
passages.text:
It is a very old, antique brooch with very detailed molding and filigree worked into the edges. It looks very valuable.

There's only one person who keeps losing jewelry to furry hooligans, and she would probably want to see this heirloom returned.

passages.title: A Beautiful Brooch
passages.text: My grandmother's brooch! Oh, thank you for finding this! It's a family treasure.

passages.title: A Wolf In Sheep's Clothing
passages.text:
AAAIIIIEEUUGGHHHH!!!! This is the last straw!

Those stupid hozen on the mountain killed my SHEEPIE!

I know exactly who did this, and it is time for REVENGE.

If you are willing to help me, take this old sheepskin.

Use it to disguise yourself anywhere on the mountain to the north, wait for that little dooker Krungko to come out of hiding, and then break his bones!

passages.title: A Wolf In Sheep's Clothing
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. It will not bring my Sheepie back, but at least this way, no more sheep will be lost.

passages.title: Restoring Jade's Purity
passages.text:
<class>, will you aid us?

The temple's purity has been jeopardized. Even now the three masters struggle against their doubts.

Please, I beg you, head in and help Wise Mari, Liu Flameheart, and Lorewalker Stonestep in their fight against the sha.

passages.title: Restoring Jade's Purity
passages.text: Please, you must assist those within before they succumb to their doubts.

passages.title: Restoring Jade's Purity
passages.text: While I am sad to hear the fates of Wise Mari and Priestess Flameheart, you have my heartfelt thanks.

passages.title: Deep Doubts, Deep Wisdom
passages.text:
There is an ancient pandaren saying that states, "With deep doubts comes deep wisdom."

The Sha of Doubt has infested the Heart of Jade within the temple. It must be destroyed.

I dare say that you are about to become all the wiser, <class>.

passages.title: Deep Doubts, Deep Wisdom
passages.text: The Sha of Doubt must be destroyed, <name>, or we are all lost.

passages.title: Deep Doubts, Deep Wisdom
passages.text:
I never doubted you. Funny though, you don't look any wiser.

<The master winks.>

passages.title: Relics of the Four Kings
passages.text:
The mogu have reawakened and are a threat to all of Pandaria. They are on the cusp of becoming even more dangerous.

There are four great mogu kings of legend: Zian of the Endless Shadow, Meng the Demented, Qiang the Merciless, and Subetai the Swift. Four artifacts of these kings are secreted away in the Vault of Kings Past, below.

You must retrieve these relics before the mogu discover them and become unstoppable.

passages.title: Relics of the Four Kings
passages.text: We must retrieve the lantern, balance, scroll, and bow before Xin and his clans uncover them.

passages.title: Relics of the Four Kings
passages.text:
I will find a better hiding place for the four relics.

Pandaria is indebted to you, <name>.

passages.title: The Kunchong Whisperer
passages.text:
To really connect with Kovok you need to challenge him mentally and physically. You must respect his strength and intelligence; only then will he allow you to really train him.

The muckscale tribe may provide an adequate test of his abilities and with you there he shouldn't be in danger.

Additionally, this will allow us to decrease their numbers in the Briny Muck.

passages.title: The Kunchong Whisperer
passages.text:
I am most impressed with your progress, Wakener. Kovok's training is coming along nicely and he seems to be fond of you.

I have no doubt that you are the best choice to assist me in training him.

passages.title: A New Lesson for the Master
passages.text:
A new king of the mogu has arisen: Xin the Weaponmaster.

He single-handedly subjugated the mogu clans, and now they and their new leaders vie for his favor.

I've never seen or read of any who are his equal in battle. Do not underestimate Xin, <name>.

Our fate rests in your hands.

passages.title: A New Lesson for the Master
passages.text:
The king of the mogu must die.

Though another will eventually rise, none are as deadly as Xin the Weaponmaster.

passages.title: A New Lesson for the Master
passages.text:
Truly a fight for the ages.

I'm glad that you're on our side, <name>.

passages.title: Last Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text:
I must say, <name>, despite their skirmishes with the hozen, I've never seen the jinyu so militant.

This troubles me. We must discuss it another time, however. I have come to ask for your assistance.

The fresco, where last we spoke, is nearly unveiled. I am certain that it holds ancient wisdom - knowledge that the emperor would have us remember.

My meditations alone may not be enough to discern its meaning. Please, take this heirloom to the shrine of my ancestors. I shall require their assistance.

passages.title: Last Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text: Yes, <class>?

passages.title: Last Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text:
<Lorewalker Cho shudders, in spite of himself.>

The legends... they're true!

passages.title: That's a Big Bug!
passages.text:
The mantid have something they call Raigonn. It's a giant bug they're using to bust down the wall's gates!

Let's keep that thing from getting into the vale!

passages.title: That's a Big Bug!
passages.text: You need to bring that thing down before it busts through the final gate!

passages.title: That's a Big Bug!
passages.text:
If I didn't see it with my own eyes, I wouldn't have believed it.

Great job, <name>!

passages.title: Take Down the Wing Leader
passages.text:
The mantid have lain siege to Niuzao Temple.

Even now, Wing Leader Ner'onok and his forces work to cross the final chasm.

You must stop him before they reconstruct that bridge.

passages.title: Take Down the Wing Leader
passages.text: Hurry, <class>, the construction of the mantid bridge nears completion.

passages.title: Take Down the Wing Leader
passages.text:
The wing leader lies dead and the siege is broken.

You've saved the temple, <name>.

passages.title: The Lorewalkers
passages.text:
So you are interested in learning more of the lore of this land?

Very well! You should speak to Lorewalker Cho at the Seat of Knowledge.

He can be found in the room above the entrance to the Mogu'shan Palace. Speak with Mishi for a ride.

passages.title: The Lorewalkers
passages.text: Welcome, traveler.

passages.title: The Lorewalkers
passages.text: Ah yes, I can see by your face that you are an eager seeker of stories. You have come to the right place.

passages.title: The Lorewalkers
passages.text:
So you are interested in learning more of the lore of this land?

Very well! You should speak to Lorewalker Cho at the Seat of Knowledge.

He can be found in the room above the entrance to the Mogu'shan Palace. Speak with Mishi for a ride.

passages.title: The Lorewalkers
passages.text: Welcome, traveler.

passages.title: The Lorewalkers
passages.text: Ah yes, I can see by your face that you are an eager seeker of stories. You have come to the right place.

passages.title: The Golden Lotus
passages.text:
The Golden Lotus have guarded the Vale for centuries, keeping it safe and hidden from harm.

Recent events have unleashed terrible horrors upon our sacred vale, but allies of the Golden Lotus still stand against them, attempting to bring peace.

If you wish to help, you had best join them at the Setting Sun Garrison.

passages.title: The Golden Lotus
passages.text: Well met, <race>. You look capable. Glad to know we have a decent <class> on our side.

passages.title: The Golden Lotus
passages.text:
The Golden Lotus have guarded the Vale for centuries, keeping it safe and hidden from harm.

Recent events have unleashed terrible horrors upon our sacred vale, but allies of the Golden Lotus still stand against them, attempting to bring peace.

If you wish to help, you had best join them at the Setting Sun Garrison.

passages.title: The Golden Lotus
passages.text: Well met, <race>. You look capable. Glad to know we have a decent <class> on our side.

passages.title: The Klaxxi
passages.text:
The Klaxxi are only rumored to exist, far beyond the wall in the Dread Wastes.

Few have ventured into that territory, and none have returned to tell the tale.

If you are set on finding these... Klaxxi... there is a small group of Shado-Pan manning the wall to the far southwest who may know more.

passages.title: The Klaxxi
passages.text: The Dread Wastes is a very dangerous place.

passages.title: The Klaxxi
passages.text:
The Klaxxi are only rumored to exist, far beyond the wall in the Dread Wastes.

Few have ventured into that territory, and none have returned to tell the tale.

If you are set on finding these... Klaxxi... there is a small group of Shado-Pan manning the wall to the far southwest who may know more.

passages.title: The Klaxxi
passages.text: The Dread Wastes is a very dangerous place.

passages.title: Temple of the White Tiger
passages.text:
Have you heard the news, traveller? There's been an attack at one of our most sacred places, the Vale of Eternal Blossoms!

Even now, there's a human prince within the White Tiger Temple arguing that you and the other races from beyond the mists should be allowed within.

The temple is in the northeast of Kun-Lai. Maybe you can convince the White Tiger to allow you inside?

I only hope the Vale has not been utterly destroyed...

passages.title: Temple of the White Tiger
passages.text:
<class>, I'm glad you're here! The Pandaren tell of a legendary place, the "Vale of Eternal Blossoms." It's a place of great healing, if the locals are to be believed.

Between the destruction of the Cataclysm and the horrors of this light-forsaken war, the Vale may be our best hope for healing the wounds of the world.

We need to get in there!

passages.title: Temple of the White Tiger
passages.text:
Have you heard the news, traveller? There's been an attack at one of our most sacred places, the Vale of Eternal Blossoms!

Even now, there's a human prince within the White Tiger Temple arguing that you and the other races from beyond the mists should be allowed within.

The temple is in the northeast of Kun-Lai. Maybe you can convince the White Tiger to allow you inside?

I only hope the Vale has not been utterly destroyed...

passages.title: Temple of the White Tiger
passages.text:
Hello, <class>! The human prince from Stormwind has been granted an audience with the White Tiger. He seeks to gain admittance into the Vale of Eternal Blossoms... for both the Alliance and the Horde.

The Vale is a sacred place. I believe my wife Leza saw it in a vision - it's what brought my people to Pandaria. Perhaps we will find shelter there.

Do you think we will be allowed inside?

passages.title: Falling to Pieces
passages.text:
Why would the saurok have amber? More importantly, why would Oracle Hiss'ir be so protective of it?

It is unlikely this came from the heavily guarded Zan'vess, so where did it come from?

Perhaps the Klaxxi will know what to make of it.

passages.title: Falling to Pieces
passages.text: Where did you find this?

passages.title: Falling to Pieces
passages.text:
You were wise to bring this to us. This is a piece of another paragon's encasing amber.

The damage suggests the paragon may be in trouble.

I will speak with the council to decide what should be done next.

passages.title: The Four Tomes
passages.text:
There are four tomes of great necromantic evil studied in Scholomance: "In the Shadow of the Light", "Kel'Thuzad's Deep Knowledge", "Forbidden Rites and other Rituals Necromantic" and "The Dark Grimoire".

As we make our way through this cursed place, find and destroy each book so that no other fool can come along later and learn their vile secrets.

passages.title: The Four Tomes
passages.text:
The four tomes contain secrets that have damned this place and all associated with it to an eternity of suffering.

They must be destroyed!

passages.title: The Four Tomes
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

With the destruction of the tomes I'll go to my final rest knowing that those books will never again haunt a living soul.

passages.title: The Four Tomes
passages.text:
There are four tomes of great necromantic evil studied in Scholomance: "In the Shadow of the Light", "Kel'Thuzad's Deep Knowledge", "Forbidden Rites and other Rituals Necromantic" and "The Dark Grimoire".

As we make our way through this cursed place, find and destroy each book so that no other fool can come along later and learn their vile secrets.

passages.title: The Four Tomes
passages.text:
The four tomes contain secrets that have damned this place and all associated with it to an eternity of suffering.

They must be destroyed!

passages.title: The Four Tomes
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

With the destruction of the tomes I'll go to my final rest knowing that those books will never again haunt a living soul.

passages.title: Flying Tiger Gourami
passages.text: You've caught a unique fish... with wings. Perhaps it deserves the expert opinion of Nat Pagle in Anglers Wharf.

passages.title: Flying Tiger Gourami
passages.text: Flying fish?

passages.title: Flying Tiger Gourami
passages.text:
Is that a flying tiger gourami?

This little fish is a rare mutation of the tiger gourami that can fly, and are consequently caught in any freshwater here in Pandaria.

Local legend states that good luck comes to the person who eats it, and local tradition states that only royalty can eat them.  To be caught breaking this "tradition" is a death sentence.

With that in mind, I'll make sure it gets to the right person.

passages.title: Spinefish Alpha
passages.text:
You have fished up something special. It looks pretty aggressive.

Maybe Nat Pagle at the Anglers Wharf might know more about it?

passages.title: Spinefish Alpha
passages.text: Strange fish?

passages.title: Spinefish Alpha
passages.text:
That's not what I think it is, is it?  Oh wow, a spinefish alpha, one of Pandaria's deadliest predators.

Spinefish are malformed abominations created by the sha presence, and these big ones are simply terrifying.  An alpha will often eat other spinefish, even though there isn't a single part of them that's edible.

Luckily for both of us, they are very interesting to alchemists.

passages.title: Mimic Octopus
passages.text: You aren't sure how, but you've caught an extraordinary cephalopod. Nat Pagle at Anglers Wharf would be very interested to see it.

passages.title: Mimic Octopus
passages.text: Camouflage octopus?

passages.title: Mimic Octopus
passages.text:
Is that a mimic octopus?  A buddy of mine caught one of these off the coast of Zandalar a few years back.  He barely made it back alive, actually.  Pesky trolls, but great fishing!

Anyhow, they aren't as rare as you might think because they use camouflage to hide amongst rocks and plants; only a very skilled fisherman has any hope of catching this elusive, and delicious, morsel.

passages.title: An End to the Suffering
passages.text:
The key to lifting the curse of this place rests in the final death of Darkmaster Gandling.

Do it, adventurer, and make him suffer!

passages.title: An End to the Suffering
passages.text:
Behold my true form.

I owe you a debt, one which I can never repay. But, I thank you for lifting the curse off of my family.

Kel'Thuzad, the Lich King, and now Darkmaster Gandling -- all are dead.

Perhaps now I too can find some semblance of peace.

passages.title: A New Fate
passages.text:
These new allies have shed light on a great and important truth: it is not just Shen-zin Su that is ailing, but all of the land beyond the clouds. The world needs healing, and I think that you should be the ones to heal it.

I would like you, Ji, and Aysa to leave and bring your strength and wisdom to the world. These Alliance and Horde have different ideals, but at the core of both lies noble intent.

I will leave the choice of who you wish to accompany to you.

passages.title: A New Fate
passages.text: And so it is done... here we are, in our new home.

passages.title: The Shado-Pan
passages.text:
Our new recruits have spoken in hushed tones about a group of Pandaren they call the "Shado-Pan". They are apparently very strong, and secretive.

That's where you come in. Rumor is they have a base of operations to the southeast, near Firebough Nook. You should travel there as an envoy of the Alliance. Give them any help they require.

passages.title: The Shado-Pan
passages.text: Who are you? Can you fight? If so, we can use your help.

passages.title: Muskpaw Ranch
passages.text:
There's another Pandaren settlement out here, Muskpaw Ranch. I don't know if they're alright, what with everything that's been going on with the Yaungol invasion.

You've been so helpful - you should go check up on them, friend!

passages.title: Muskpaw Ranch
passages.text:
Wha? Who the heck are you? What are you doin' here?

Oh, you wanna help?

passages.title: Muskpaw Ranch
passages.text:
There's another Pandaren settlement out here, Muskpaw Ranch. I don't know if they're alright, what with everything that's been going on with the Yaungol invasion.

You've been so helpful - you should go check up on them, friend!

passages.title: Muskpaw Ranch
passages.text:
Wha? Who the heck are you? What are you doin' here?

Oh, you wanna help?

passages.title: Damage Control
passages.text:
Kor'ik has been sending signals to the empress for weeks. Everything the Klaxxi have done, the empress knows about.

That stops now!

Kypari Ik will be the first to receive news of Kor'ik's demise. It would benefit us to make sure that message does not make it to the empress.

Destroying the whisperers and beacon there will buy us enough time to come up with a plan before the empress can act.

passages.title: Damage Control
passages.text: Information is power, Wakener. Those with the most information always have the most power.

passages.title: Damage Control
passages.text:
Excellent work! This should allow us the time to repair the damage Kor'ik caused.

You may have just shifted the tide of war in our favor.

passages.title: Extracting Answers
passages.text:
Kypari Ik is just one of many locations that houses some of Empress Shek'zeer's offspring. In their juvenile state the young are reckless and difficult to control. They are also deadly.

Swarmborn are hatched with a highly toxic venom that diminishes in potency with age. The venom can incapacitate even the strongest and most skilled fighter if it hits flesh.

I would like you to bring me some of this venom.

passages.title: Extracting Answers
passages.text: Swarmborn venom will not only give us an additional weapon, it will also help us figure out what stage the swarm is in.

passages.title: Extracting Answers
passages.text:
This venom is in its advanced stages, but doesn't seem to be losing it's potency...

This is very curious. The Klaxxi will want to know immediately. Thank you, Wakener.

passages.title: Strong as a Tiger
passages.text: With the grill, you can transform those raw tiger steaks into food that makes you stronger. Learn the recipe for charbroiled tiger steaks from me. Show me what you can do.

passages.title: Strong as a Tiger
passages.text: Learn the recipe from me and demonstrate what you have learned.

passages.title: Strong as a Tiger
passages.text: Strength and good health! This is the Way of the Grill.

passages.title: Trial of the Black Prince
passages.text:
I have on good authority that you are a champion among champions, but if you'll permit me this indulgence, I would like to test your mettle for myself.

The mogu who assault the Vale of Eternal Blossoms, the mogu minions who inhabit Shan'ze Dao, and the sha-corrupted mantid swarming the Dread Wastes... these may provide an adequate challenge for one of your stature.

Prove yourself to me. No rush - I expect this to take you some time.

passages.title: Trial of the Black Prince
passages.text:
Marvelous. That did not take long at all.

Word of your many achievements has been the talk of the Vale!

Very well, I will take you under my wing.

passages.title: UNUSED
passages.text: The Pandaren Way of the Grill produces foods that increase your physical strength. Learn the recipe for Charbroiled Tiger Steak from the Master of the Grill and show him the results of your learning.

passages.title: Way of the Wok
passages.text: If you wish to make dishes that enhance agility, you should bring some carrots and rice to the Master of the Wok. The virmen around here tend to carry a lot of carrots around. You can also grow your own, if you have a farm.

passages.title: Way of the Wok
passages.text: Hello, young chef. Do you wish to learn the Way of the Wok?

passages.title: Way of the Wok
passages.text: Well done.

passages.title: Agile as a Tiger
passages.text: To cook with the wok, you need to be nimble. Your first lesson is sauteed carrots.

passages.title: Agile as a Tiger
passages.text: Let me teach you how to make sauteed carrots.

passages.title: Agile as a Tiger
passages.text: Nice work.

passages.title: The Strength of One's Foes
passages.text:
Great leadership requires the power to shape the destiny of your people, and the wisdom to make the right decisions. Pandaria boasts great power and ancient wisdom, but rarely in the same place.

Let's see if you and I can change that!

Acquire sigils of power and wisdom from fallen foes in the Mogu'shan Vaults, the Heart of Fear, or the Terrace of Endless Spring. We will put them to a much better use than their current owners.

passages.title: The Strength of One's Foes
passages.text:
Sigils of wisdom will often be found on practitioners of the arcane arts, while sigils of power are usually found on those who favor brute strength.

This is not always true, but it may help you find what you need.

passages.title: The Strength of One's Foes
passages.text:
My friend - you do not disappoint!

We will put these to good use.

passages.title: The Soup of Contemplation
passages.text: Watching over the pot, you get a lot of time to think. Let me show you how to make swirling mist soup and you'll know what I mean.

passages.title: The Soup of Contemplation
passages.text: If you want to learn the Way of the Pot, you have to start with swirling mist soup.

passages.title: The Soup of Contemplation
passages.text: Intellect is a gift you must hone with time.

passages.title: Way of the Steamer
passages.text: A great meal can lift your spirits, and none more so than food from the Way of the Steamer. Bring the Master some giant mantis shrimp and he will show you. You can fish for giant mantis shrimp in the ocean.

passages.title: Way of the Steamer
passages.text: If you want to learn the Way of the Steamer, you'll need some shrimp.

passages.title: Way of the Steamer
passages.text: Fine ingredients.

passages.title: The Spirit of Cooking
passages.text: When I cook with steam, I infuse the food with my love. Let me teach you the recipe for shrimp dumplings.

passages.title: The Spirit of Cooking
passages.text: Let me teach you how to make shrimp dumplings.

passages.title: The Spirit of Cooking
passages.text: Spirits are lifted by good food.

passages.title: Endurance
passages.text: They say that the crane appointed sentry by its flock stands guard with a stone in its beak, so that, should it fall asleep, the stone drops and it awakens. To be skilled with the oven, you need to have endurance and patience. Learn the recipe for wildfowl roast and show me that you understand.

passages.title: Endurance
passages.text: Learn the recipe for wildfowl roast from me and let's see what you can do.

passages.title: Endurance
passages.text: Stamina and endurance are needed for mastering anything. To slave over a hot oven takes patience, but the results are very much worth the effort.

passages.title: Way of the Oven
passages.text: If you are looking for a hearty meal that will sustain you and increase your stamina, you should seek out the Way of the Oven. Bring some wildfowl breasts to the Master of the Oven and she will teach you. There are plenty of cranes in the Valley of the Four Winds and in the Jade Forest, but you can obtain wildfowl breasts from other birds as well.

passages.title: Way of the Oven
passages.text: If you want to make wildfowl roast, you need to obtain wildfowl breasts.

passages.title: Way of the Oven
passages.text: We can work with these.

passages.title: Way of the Brew
passages.text: The Pandaren Way of the Brew produces... Well, I'll let the Master of the Brew explain it. Bring him some ginseng and he will show you the way.

passages.title: Way of the Brew
passages.text: You'd like to learn the Way of the Brew?

passages.title: Way of the Brew
passages.text: This is a fine example of good ginseng. Would you like to learn how to make tea with it?

passages.title: Have a Drink
passages.text: My siblings are so serious. I think life's too short to be so serious all the time. Let's have some tea together. Let me teach you how to make ginseng tea.

passages.title: Have a Drink
passages.text: Let me teach you how to make ginseng tea.

passages.title: Have a Drink
passages.text: Well done. This is delicious.

passages.title: Fear Itself
passages.text:
I've picked up a few motes of pandaren wisdom during my time here. I particularly enjoy this one:

"The timid feel fear before trouble starts; the cowards feel fear as trouble happens. The bravest among us feel fear only after the troubles have been taken care of."

Is that true? Let's find out.

The Sha of Fear has fled into the Terrace of Endless Spring. Pursue it there, defeat it, and rip out its spirit - presuming it has one.

Your bravery will be handsomely rewarded.

passages.title: Fear Itself
passages.text:
Another bit of pandaren wisdom: "Fear is not a criminal we must lock away. It is a teacher we must seek to understand."  In facing our fears, we gain great strength.

Have you faced your fears, <name>?

passages.title: Fear Itself
passages.text:
You have done it!

Some put their faith in magic or steel. But in my experience, fear is the most powerful weapon one can wield. Use it properly, and your enemies cannot bring themselves to fight you.

passages.title: Breath of the Black Prince
passages.text:
<Wrathion's piercing red eyes fixate on you.>

You are among a rare breed, <name>.

You are just what I am looking for - an individual with the potential to shape events on a global scale.

Come now, I promised you a reward, and you shall have it! East of this tavern is a series of stone steps leading up to a vista that the locals have named "Mason's Folly." Meet me there.

passages.title: Breath of the Black Prince
passages.text:
You have earned this, <name>! Use it well.

Please understand, I mean to pay off my father's debts. I will stop at NOTHING to defend this world. In the future, if you are ever uncertain, you are welcome to question my means. But never question my motives. The safety of this world is my primary concern.

Now then, let's talk about current events.

passages.title: Sonic Disruption
passages.text:
Relying on sonic whispers to manipulate the kunchong was only the most primitive stage of my research, and yet the Empire seems to have adopted the practice wholly. The manipulators of the Shek'zeer are too impatient to form a proper bond with their kunchong.

Their laziness will cost them dearly.

Strike this tuning fork near the dread kunchong in the clutches - watch as they reel in confusion and lash out at their masters. Use this to your advantage and put them down.

passages.title: Sonic Disruption
passages.text: Let this be a reminder - the kunchong should be feared and respected.

passages.title: Rank and File
passages.text:
First things first; let's kill us some crusaders.

And when I say kill the Scarlet Crusade, I mean wipe them out, root and branch, rank and file.

passages.title: Rank and File
passages.text:
You know, I've been killing the ones that you can't see behind closed doors.

But I need to maintain this disguise. So if you could just take care of all of the ones <name> there in the open, that'd be great.

passages.title: Rank and File
passages.text:
Great start, <name>!

It won't be long now before the Scarlet Crusade is nothing more than an ugly footnote in the annals of history.

passages.title: The Ten Foot Pole
passages.text:
Xuen once issued this challenge to the last Emperor of Pandaria: stand in the center of the room and hold off waves of monks using only a ten foot pole.

My record is ten. Can you beat that?

passages.title: The Torch of Strength
passages.text:
Xuen has this challenge he says helps "refine strength." I am starting to think the word "strength" means something different to him than the rest of us.

Here, take this torch to the top of the gates of the temple. If you can get it there without the torch being extinguished, you pass the challenge.

Whatever you do, do not try carrying the torch on a mount. It will blow out if you do. Trust me on that one.

passages.title: The Torch of Strength
passages.text: Need another torch?

passages.title: The Torch of Strength
passages.text: Wow! You made it. Usually I get stopped by one of those gusts of wind.

passages.title: Free From Her Clutches
passages.text:
The Shek'zeer manipulators are corralling young kunchong into that clutch and exposing them to raw fear energies, twisting them and accelerating their growth.

Disgusting! I will not allow it!

Break open the cages and set those hatchlings free.

passages.title: Free From Her Clutches
passages.text: Yes, I could see them rising up from the clutches. Beautiful!

passages.title: Rank and File
passages.text:
First things first; let's kill us some crusaders.

And when I say kill the Scarlet Crusade, I mean wipe them out, root and branch, rank and file.

passages.title: Rank and File
passages.text:
You know, I've been killing the ones that you can't see behind closed doors.

But I need to maintain this disguise. So if you could just take care of all of the ones out there in the open, that'd be great.

passages.title: Rank and File
passages.text:
Great start, <name>!

It won't be long now before the Scarlet Crusade is nothing more than an ugly footnote in the annals of history.

passages.title: Sampling the Empire's Finest
passages.text:
The wonders of the kypari sap never cease to amaze me. Among its numerous properties and applications, the sap can be refined into a nutritious and extremely delectable elixir.

Nowhere in the Empire will you find a finer execution of this brew than the palace itself. Surely, the homes of the loyalists have feeders brimming with this sweet nectar.

Fill this jar at their feeders and return it to me. I long to sample the imperial ambrosia once more.

passages.title: Sampling the Empire's Finest
passages.text: Ah, yes, hand it over! Quickly now! My forelegs are trembling with anticipation.

passages.title: Just for Safekeeping, Of Course
passages.text:
There is a book of great value to me here in the halls.

Unfortunately, it's in the possession of Flameweaver Koegler. I've tried to get close to him before, but it's never quite worked out.

You might have better luck. Just watch out -- I hear that he's gone well and truly insane. The Flameweaver plans to burn every tome they have in the library.

He'll probably burn the Scarlet Halls down in the process.

passages.title: Just for Safekeeping, Of Course
passages.text: It's imperative that I get my hands on the codex.

passages.title: Just for Safekeeping, Of Course
passages.text:
Ah yes!

<The Hooded Crusader rubs her hands together gleefully at the sight of the codex.>

And now, I have a checklist with the name of every Scarlet Crusader on it!

You know... just in case any of them are unaccounted for. I don't like loose ends.

passages.title: Wing Clip
passages.text:
The young fliers of this era are fascinating. Their exceptional agility and endurance were, in my time, the feats of incredibly skilled or mature fliers.

This would seem to indicate some kind of evolution in wing structure... Or perhaps a result of advancements in training? Induced genetic mutation? Selective breeding?

Gah! There's no way to know for certain without tissue samples.

Bring me their wings! And try not to ruin them in the process, will you? I need them intact!

passages.title: Wing Clip
passages.text: Do you have the specimens?

passages.title: Wing Clip
passages.text: Excellent, these are in fine shape.

passages.title: Ordnance Disposal
passages.text:
If the Grand Empress's agents are still operating under security standards from my time, they would have hidden powerful pheromone mines all around the clutches.

With mere whisper she could detonate them all simultaneously, engulfing the palace and rendering entire siege armies powerless.

If we hope to have any success in a large scale standoff, we need to disable those mines. My... "gift" to you when we met will allow you to see the mines. Disturb them and get to a safe distance.

passages.title: Ordnance Disposal
