passages.text:
Very nice, <name>! I knew it! I knew there were Alliance sneaking around down there!

No one messes with a Bilgewater rig and gets away with it!

passages.title: Soul Surrender
passages.text:
We assault the mogu at the Court of Bones, but I fear we merely send them fodder for their abominable rituals.

The mogu do not merely kill their prisoners - they steal their souls and imbue them in machinations of stone, or reforge the fallen into ghostly tools of war.

Horde or Alliance, it matters not. We cannot allow the mogu to bolster their numbers.

Go into the crypts. Free any prisoners that are still living.

passages.title: Soul Surrender
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. You have lightened my heart of a heavy burden through your heroic actions.

I will remember your efforts on this day.

passages.title: Storming the Beach
passages.text:
Our lumber supply is being jeopardized by constant attacks from Lion's Landing.

We've been able to keep the attackers at bay, but it's time to really show 'em some muscle!

Head down to the coast and start splitting some skulls!

passages.title: Storming the Beach
passages.text: Excellent work down there, <name>! That should keep 'em outta our hair for awhile!

passages.title: WANTED: Chief Engineer Cogwrench
passages.text:
Wanted for crimes against the Bilgewater Operation!

Chief Engineer Cogwrench was last seen building what appeared to be a giant spider tank on the edge of Bilgewater Beach.

Extreme caution should be used when approaching.

A large reward has been posted for Cogwrench's destruction.

passages.title: WANTED: Chief Engineer Cogwrench
passages.text: Excellent work, <class>! This brings us one step closer to pushing them out of Pandaria!

passages.title: WANTED: Lieutenant Ethan Jacobson
passages.text:
Wanted for crimes against the Domination Point forces!

Lieutenant Ethan Jacobson is responsible for leading several ground assaults against the Bilgewater lumber operation.

Last spotted occupying an island south of Quickchop's Lumber Farm.

passages.title: WANTED: Lieutenant Ethan Jacobson
passages.text: Do not return without his blood on your hands!

passages.title: WANTED: Lieutenant Ethan Jacobson
passages.text: It's a good day when another Lion's Landing leader falls, <class>! Good work!

passages.title: Into the Crypts
passages.text:
The Reliquary is having a field day out here, literally!

Every day, the researchers find more relics to study and catalog.

Recently, one of our adventurers found this scroll at the Court of Bones.

I believe that this incantation can be used to call beyond the grave. And if my Mogu is up to date, I'd say you should use it in the last room in the Hall of the Exalted.

Would you be willing to test out my theory?

passages.title: Into the Crypts
passages.text: Ah yes, you've just confirmed my theory! Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Preventing a Future Threat
passages.text:
The creatures the Zandalari ride don't start out so big, nor do they start out the vicious and loyal creatures they become.

If you can frighten some of the hatchling skyscreamers away from the beach, perhaps they will have a chance at a real life.

passages.title: Preventing a Future Threat
passages.text: You have returned, <race>. It is my hope that these young skyscreamers have the lives they deserve without dealing with the harsh treatment of the trolls.

passages.title: Very Disarming
passages.text:
Look around you, <class>. What do you see? I see an opportunity.

The casters here work to imbue the Zandalari weapons with powerful magic. As if a sharp blade isn't enough to cut even the strongest foe down to size.

In my scouting I've noticed the weapons are not very well guarded. This is where you come in...

If we can steal a few of these weapons we may be able to use them. At the very least they are out of enemy hands.

passages.title: Very Disarming
passages.text: So? What did you find?

passages.title: Very Disarming
passages.text:
Excellent work, <class>!

These weapons are terrifying on their own, nevermind the magic they are infused with.

passages.title: Knowledge Is Power
passages.text:
The Zandalari here practice a different kind of magic. We must understand it before we can defeat it, <class>.

Their control over the arcane and shadow is impressive. I wish to learn how they have achieved what so many others have not.

I believe their ritual artifacts may hold the answers I seek. Bring me a sampling of the artifacts you find, and I will ensure you are rewarded properly.

passages.title: Knowledge Is Power
passages.text: Did you find the artifacts?

passages.title: Knowledge Is Power
passages.text: These will do nicely, <class>. Excellent work.

passages.title: Flash! Aaaaaahhhh!
passages.text:
The gnomes have brought their flying contraptions. I want my skies CLEAR!

Get up there on whatever mount you have with you and destroy those paltry devices.

You may use this grog I "acquired" from our goblin allies. It would be better served blasting down gyrocopters than in the gullet of those little green fiends.

passages.title: Flash! Aaaaaahhhh!
passages.text: Hellscream's eyes are upon you.

passages.title: Flash! Aaaaaahhhh!
passages.text: Ha! Simple mechanical toys are no match for a well aimed bottle of grog.

passages.title: Bug Off!
passages.text:
This cave is crawlin' with nasty shale spiders! How's a girl supposed to get any work done with them gobbling up the miners AND the ore?!

This seemed like a good opportunity to use my newest invention, Bug Off. See, all you have to do is spray this stuff all over the shale spiders. They hate it and it doesn't seem to have many long term side-effects for the miners!

What could possibly go wrong?

Take this handy sprayer and get to work!

passages.title: Bug Off!
passages.text: Shale spiders. Why did it have to be shale spiders?!

passages.title: Bug Off!
passages.text: Now that's what I like to hear! I bet those spiders will think twice before messing with a Bilgewater operation again!

passages.title: Universal Remote-Explode
passages.text:
The Mecha-Pounders are really making things difficult down here, but I think I may have the solution!

I made this universal remote for myself, but it looks like I hit a specific frequency that has an useful result!

Apparently this frequency weakens their armor!

Use the remote to take them down a few notches then punch 'em in the face!

passages.title: Universal Remote-Explode
passages.text: How'd the remote work for ya?

passages.title: Universal Remote-Explode
passages.text:
Good work, <name>! I saw the fireworks from here!

Who knew being a genius was this easy? I don't even have to try anymore.

passages.title: Buried Secrets
passages.text:
I am told that the mogu once possessed hundreds of hidden armories full of earth-shattering weapons.

When a mogu army prepared for war, they struck fear and terror into the hearts of their enemies.

THIS is the knowledge I seek here on Pandaria!

I have sent an expedition to study some ruins to the west, but they work as slowly as dim-witted peons!

Go speak to Fanlyr Silverthorn, their leader. Tell him that I want to see results immediately.

passages.title: Buried Secrets
passages.text: The Warchief sent you? What does he say?

passages.title: The Source of Korune Power
passages.text:
Why hullo there! Have ya ever seen tha like o' these statues? Fascinatin'!

I was scouting up along the ruins earlier, and I spotted somethin' innerestin' up on the highest rise.

I couldn't get close enough, but I think it might be one o' these mogu statues, 'cept it was movin'!

I can't get through all those nasty blood elves, but you look like you could.

Would you mind going up there and bringing me back anything of interest?

passages.title: The Source of Korune Power
passages.text: Did ya find anything up there?

passages.title: The Source of Korune Power
passages.text: Oh my, look at this thing!

passages.title: The Korune
passages.text:
These terracotta wardens are fearsome, but not nearly as horrifying as the creature that we found at the top of the ruins.

Some of our surviving scouts reported seeing some kind of mogu spellweaver on the highest rise to the north.

He practices a type of magic unlike any other we have seen.

We must learn whatever we can from this creature. Slay him, and bring me anything you find.

passages.title: The Korune
passages.text: What did you discover?

passages.title: The Korune
passages.text: Yes, this is remarkable! This is just the kind of artifact that we came here to find!

passages.title: Meet the Scout
passages.text:
It has been two months since the parting of the mists. Alliance scouts, seeking a suitable landing site for the fleet, have engaged Horde forces on a beach in Krasarang Wilds.

Meet with Scout Lynna and help secure the landing site.

passages.title: Meet the Scout
passages.text: You have impeccable timing, <class>. King Wrynn is just about to land, and the full might of our fleet will follow soon after.

passages.title: A King Among Men
passages.text:
There's no time to waste, we need to find Troteman and secure the beach.

We should check on the dwarves, too - the Explorers' League is tough, but they're no army. They should be along the cliff just north of here.

Let us ride, <class>. For our friends. For the Alliance.

passages.title: A King Among Men
passages.text: The Alliance will be a shield, protecting Pandaria from the Horde.

passages.title: A King Among Men
passages.text: I'm satisfied with this site, it's time to bring in our fleet.

passages.title: A Little Patience
passages.text:
King Varian needs decisive adventurers to help him resolve a showdown between Tyrande Whisperwind and a detachment of Horde warriors holed up in the Temple of the Red Crane.

Report to him immediately!

passages.title: A Little Patience
passages.text:
Good to see you again, <name>.

We have a delicate situation on our hands here. We need to plan our next moves carefully.

passages.title: Meet the Scout
passages.text:
It has been two months since the parting of the mists. Horde scouts, seeking a suitable landing site for the fleet, have engaged Alliance forces on a small island off the coast of Krasarang Wilds.

Meet with Scout Rokla and help secure the landing site.

passages.title: Meet the Scout
passages.text: You are just in time. The Warchief is about to land. Once this site passes his inspection, the fleet will follow.

passages.title: The Might of the Warchief
passages.text:
Come, <class>! I want to inspect this island and ensure that my landing team has done their job.

Blood Guard Gro'tash should be somewhere on the northern side of the island looking for a suitable place to build our keep. The goblin survey team will have gone up the eastern coast in search of oil.

Let us crush this pitiful display and claim this land for the Horde!

passages.title: The Might of the Warchief
passages.text: Gorehowl thirsts for Alliance blood.

passages.title: The Might of the Warchief
passages.text: Well done. Our presence here will not be denied!

passages.title: Manipulating the Saurok
passages.text:
I have three magisters entrenched in Ihgaluk Crag, monitoring the saurok and - where they can - turning them against the mogu. I need you to find them and see if they need any supplies or assistance.

They will be concealed from view. Look for shimmering columns of light within the saurok village.

passages.title: Manipulating the Saurok
passages.text:
<The archmage listens carefully to your report.>

I understand. Thank you for your aid, <class>.

passages.title: Rise Of An Empire
passages.text:
Warchief Garrosh Hellscream travels north with a squad of his most elite soldiers.

Report to him with news of our continued victory against the Alliance.

Speak to Tak-Tak for transportation.

passages.title: Rise Of An Empire
passages.text: What do you have to report?

passages.title: Voice of the Gods
passages.text:
Too slowly!? We are working as quickly as possible for the Warchief!

We must excavate carefully, catalogue each find, and of course follow safety procedures. He must understand!

Well, we may have something to show him soon. Do you see that stone statue to the west?

We suspect it is an ancient stone storage vessel. Now we just have to find a way to open it.

If you would care to help us with our excavation, please go about it carefully.

passages.title: Voice of the Gods
passages.text: We are quite capable of handling this excavation. I understand the Warchief sent you, but he will get faster results if he leaves us to our work.

passages.title: Voice of the Gods
passages.text: Hmm... very interesting. This tablet will yield many secrets, indeed.

passages.title: Captive Audience
passages.text:
The Kirin Tor have gone too far! Now they hold our fellow Sunreavers as war prisoners!

There will be no discussion of prisoner exchange. We will handle this ourselves.

Go to Violet Rise and free as many prisoners as you can. Do not get captured yourself. We cannot afford to lose you too.

passages.title: Captive Audience
passages.text:
Those you have rescued today would no doubt thank you, if they had the strength.

Our task here will be ongoing. I refuse to leave anyone behind!

passages.title: Spellbound
passages.text:
Jaina possesses several very powerful magic artifacts. These items travel with her at all times, and are never far from her grasp. I have an interest in one of these items.

A tome, filled with knowledge, passed from one archmage to another. I have only ever seen glimpses of it.

Now that we fight on opposite sides I see no issue in removing the tome from her possession.

passages.title: Spellbound
passages.text: Do you have it? Do you have the book?!

passages.title: Spellbound
passages.text: I have desired this book for many years, <race>. It's power is too immense to describe. You have done me a great service.

passages.title: Charged Moganite
passages.text:
We have been dispatching spies into the Kirin Tor base of operations on a daily basis. Some had orders to recover charged moganite from the enemy and bring it here.

They have not returned, and I can confirm they have left the Kirin Tor base.

Search the jungle between here and there and find any of the charged moganite that might have been lost in transit. Bring it to me and we will put it to good use.

passages.title: Charged Moganite
passages.text: Well done, champion. This artifact will be put to better use in our hands than in the hands of the Kirin Tor.

passages.title: Tactical Mana Bombs
passages.text:
Ah, adventurer, just the <race> I was looking for. I have received another batch of tactical mana bombs that I need planted in key positions across Violet Rise to the southeast.

Here, take these. I do not trust our standard soldiers with such firepower. Oh... and don't shake them, whatever you do.

Plant one of the Kirin Tor ships, another one near their supplies, and the last on the construct they are building.

passages.title: Tactical Mana Bombs
passages.text:
I am sure the use of even these smaller mana bombs has Jaina squirming with rage. Serves her right.

Dalaran was my home before her grandparents were born. What right did she have to expel me from my home?

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
The Skumblade threaten our people, but responding with all-out slaughter would be an overreaction.

A more reasonable response to their threat would be to slay some of their tribal leaders. There will be less bloodshed, and they will still respect our perimeter.

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
The saurok value strength above all else. They only respond to strength.

Peace with the saurok will require some amount of bloodshed. The question is, how much?

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
I know the true price of bloodshed. I know the cost of war.

It would be simpler to blindly massacre our attackers until they yield. But is it right?

passages.title: Surgical Death
passages.text:
The Zandalari train skyscreamers to become ferocious beasts in the skies. The spiritbinders require endless sacrifices - of our people - to be brought to them. And, the jaguar warriors venture ever closer toward the heart of our camp.

Find them in Za'Tual and remove the threat.

passages.title: Surgical Death
passages.text: I shall continue my unrest until the threat is subdued, but your aid brings us closer to that goal. I thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Tear Down This Wall!
passages.text:
The time has come. Our forces are well-enough entrenched here that we can risk pressing forward, into the Thunder King's lair. Unfortunately, it doesn't look like he'll be opening that gate anytime soon.

I suppose we'll have to make a gate of our own then. Let me know when you're ready, <name>.

passages.title: Tear Down This Wall!
passages.text: Let's tear down this wall.

passages.title: Tear Down This Wall!
passages.text: With your help, we're one giant step closer to our goal.

passages.title: Decisive Action
passages.text:
Zandalari warships plunder the seas around this island. They ferry in soldiers and war beasts from Zandalar to bolster Lei Shen's army.

If we can capture the palace shipyard, the Thunder King's supply line will be cut off, and your foothold here will be secure.

I have a plan to do just that, and it won't take an entire army.

passages.title: Decisive Action
passages.text:
Excellent work! With that blasted warship out of commission, the bombardments on our forces along the coast will cease.

Taran Zhu has informed me that the Shado-Pan will keep vigil over Stormsea Landing, freeing up Sunreaver resources to press the siege elsewhere. Taoshi will be there. I am sure she will be glad to work with you again.

We are all grateful for your contributions, <name>. Thank you.

passages.title: Metalocalypse
passages.text:
You've made a good start, but now it's time to really make a dent in their operations.

Take out Metal Lord Mono-Han, of the mines.

passages.title: Fleshcrafter's End
passages.text:
The mogu responsible for the torture of the agents, Fleshcrafter Goju, stands outside the mine.

Killing him would be the only justice for what he's done to your agents.

passages.title: Compy Stomp
passages.text:
The raptors and compies of the Zandalari represent a substantial threat to our forces here. They are superb hunting beasts that can track prey over great distances and are often lethal to encounter when caught unawares.

I need you to head into the Beast Pens and cull their numbers. We need to make sure to slay them before they are fully trained.

passages.title: Compy Stomp
passages.text: Say what you will about the Zandalari but none can contest their ability to turn even the most repellant of creatures into a trained weapon.

passages.title: Compy Stomp
passages.text: We lost three good soldiers when we first arrived on this island. Killed in their sleep by compies that had snuck into their tent. Some nights I still hear the screams.

passages.title: Someone You Should See
passages.text:
adventurer? It is good fortune I find you.

Chen Stormstout says to give this to you and ask you to meet him at Binan Village of the Kun-Lai Summit.

He found a friend of yours who needs much luck to get healthy.

Chen say speak to Tak-Tak for fast travels.

passages.title: Someone You Should See
passages.text: It is not my place to choose a side in this war. But I am not going to let a troll who has accomplished so much in his day fall by the wayside.

passages.title: Someone You Should See
passages.text: Ah! You received my note. Very good. Vol'jin is near death, and I will need your help healing his wounds.

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text:
The forge lies ahead of you, and with it the heart of the mogu's weaponsmithing ability.

And beyond that, the mogu gatekeeper, who holds the key to unlocking the gate to the next part of the city.

It's time to move out!

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text: Well?

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text: Good work. What you did today brings us one step closer to our ultimate goal.

passages.title: Treasures of the Thunder King
passages.text:
My scouts have returned with word that more of the treasures from Lei Shen's tomb are being brought up into the citadel. We have access to a secret sewer entrance, but a door bars us from intercepting the shipment. If we're going to succeed in this raid, we will need a key that only the most trusted of Lei Shen's forces carry.

If you get your hands on such a key, bring it to me.

You can keep whatever spoils you steal from our raid. I simply want to see that this shipment never makes it to Lei Shen.

passages.title: Treasures of the Thunder King
passages.text:
We must disrupt Lei Shen in any way we can. Anything to hinder the rise of his power. Anything to hinder his armies from being bolstered.

If that means highway robbery, I can live with that.

passages.title: Treasures of the Thunder King
passages.text:
Not entirely unsuccessful. Still, we'll do better next time.

Thanks for providing us with that key. The raid would not have gone off without you.

passages.title: Direhorn or Devilsaur
passages.text:
We have an opportunity to disrupt the Zandalari war machine as well as have a little fun in the process.

Within these beast pens, a devilsaur and a direhorn are being outfitted with armor, their minds being enslaved to the Zandalari charms.

Go into the camp and disrupt one of these binding rituals. It doesn't matter which one. Just kill those who are trying to bind the creature. This should let the fully armored beast run mad through the Zandalari camp. Then sit back and watch the hilarity ensue.

passages.title: Direhorn or Devilsaur
passages.text: So... did you decide the devilsaur or the direhorn?

passages.title: Direhorn or Devilsaur
passages.text:
Few things in this world and beyond are more entertaining than watching a rampaging ancient beast tearing through an enemy's settlement.

If times were not so dire I would consider selling tickets to such an event.

passages.title: Dino Might
passages.text:
The Zandalari use a series of fetishes and charms to maintain their control over their menagerie of beasts.

Two can play at that game.

I want you to find some of these fetishes and try them out on the various beasts in the Beast Pens.

Take careful note of how each beast responds to each fetish. Then report your results to me.

Maybe this will give us the edge we need against the Zandalari.

passages.title: Dino Might
passages.text: I heard screaming? Was that your efforts perhaps?

passages.title: Dino Might
passages.text: Very interesting results. I am sure there is a mage somewhere that cares about the specifics. I, on the other hand, am just glad to hear the sound of trolls being assaulted by their own beasts.

passages.title: Just Some Light Clean-Up Work
passages.text:
This is not a glamorous job. Let me put it to you bluntly.

The Skumblade saurok pile all of their filth into a pool in the middle of their village. This filth is so concentrated and so rancid that it has congealed into moving, animate matter.

The saurok can keep their filth-pool, but once it starts spreading outside of the village, I'd say it's time to intervene.

passages.title: Just Some Light Clean-Up Work
passages.text: Jobs like this make me glad that I left most of my nose in the tomb.

passages.title: Disarming Irony
passages.text:
Well, it would seem the Lady Proudmoore has decided to use our own weaponry against us. Our perimeter wards reported several spies slipping through our defenses carrying tactical mana bombs.

I would enjoy the irony if these bombs were less dangerous.

Search for these bombs and disarm them. Our wards reported one near the horde ships to the north, one on a bridge to the main isle, and one near our scrying crystals on the eastern side of the Promontory.

passages.title: Disarming Irony
passages.text: Good work. The real irony is had these been normal bombs we would have had a much harder time detecting them. Some gnomish devilry could have spelled the end of our operation here.

passages.title: Old Enemies
passages.text:
To think, we were once on the same side! The Sunreavers' treachery caught us all off guard. Never again!

They have shown their true natures to us. Siding with Garrosh and his madness has marked them all for death.

Kill any agent of the Sunreavers that you find. We will show them no mercy here.

passages.title: Old Enemies
passages.text: How many have been slain?

passages.title: Old Enemies
passages.text: You have put a good dent in the Sunreaver forces here. Like vermin, there will always be more. We must be at the ready at all times.

passages.title: Desconstruction
passages.text:
The Kirin Tor constructs are primitive at best. Nevertheless, they pose a threat.

Go to Violet Rise and dismantle Jaina's pitiful war machines. Show the Kirin Tor how easily they can be defeated!

This will be a message the Kirin Tor cannot easily ignore.

passages.title: Desconstruction
passages.text:
So the constructs have fallen? Good!

We will remind Jaina and the Kirin Tor at every turn that the Sunreavers are not to be taken lightly.

passages.title: Slaughter Selenora
passages.text:
<name>... You've heard correctly. King Varian tasked me with tracking down this Council of the Black Harvest.

Unfortunately, the Horde is seeking them out as well. One of my spies recently sent word that Shadowmancer Selenora has the second piece of their journal.

Head to Domination Point, slaughter Selenora and bring back whatever you find on her rotting cadaver.

passages.title: Anduin's Plea
passages.text:
Ah, just the <class> I was looking for. I have received an urgent letter from the young Prince Anduin.

He is playing host to his father, King Wrynn, and several other Alliance dignitaries at the Shrine of Seven Stars in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.

According to his most recent correspondence, something bad is happening at the city.

Please go at once and speak with him. I must settle some affairs here at Lion's Landing, but I will join you soon.

Speak to Fennie if you'd like a ride to the Vale.

passages.title: Anduin's Plea
passages.text: Well met, <class>. We have much work to do here.

passages.title: Heart Of The Alliance
passages.text:
I can't believe this has happened, <name>. After all we have been through here on Pandaria, will our people never learn from their past mistakes?

Brann's expedition returned recently from Mogujia, bearing a sample of sha for study.

I had my reservations about this endeavor in the first place, and my worst fears have been realized.

The sha has escaped containment. I do not need to explain the horror of bringing the sha into the heart of the Vale.

We must dispel any sha we can find, and quickly!

passages.title: Heart Of The Alliance
passages.text: We must protect this land, and our people, from the sha's influence.

passages.title: Heart Of The Alliance
passages.text: I see that you and my son have been hard at work. Thank you for taking the initiative to aid our cause here in the Vale.

passages.title: Find Thrall!
passages.text:
<Vol'jin half opens an eye and begins to move his lips as if to speak. Though no sound comes, you decipher two words.>

Find Thrall.

<With an effort, Vol'jin thrusts a hearthstone into your hands and then passes out.>

passages.title: Find Thrall!
passages.text: You have come a long way to see me, <race>. Speak.

passages.title: Find Thrall!
passages.text:
<Thrall stares at the stone you have handed him.>

Vol'jin's hearthstone? My friend, has it come to this?

passages.title: Infiltrating the Black Temple
passages.text:
It's clear that Jubeka's soulstone has lead you here to the Black Temple. 

The question remains... why?

The only remaining option is to head inside and figure out why they were here.

passages.title: Infiltrating the Black Temple
passages.text: You have done more for this world than you can know, <class>. It is... something of a shame Kanrethad met this end. A shame, but inevitable.

passages.title: Insertion
passages.text:
<name>! You'll do perfectly.

We know where the Alliance have hidden the Divine Bell. We've already inserted an agent into enemy territory, we just need you to help him execute his mission.

Pack up, <name>. You're headed to Darnassus.

passages.title: Insertion
passages.text:
<name>! So glad Nazgrim selected you.

It's taken a great deal of the Horde's effort to get you here through Jaina's traps. Maintaining our illusion this close to Darnassus is considerably expensive.

Furthermore, the Sunreavers of Dalaran are risking their neutrality by assisting the Horde with this operation.

In other words, we expect only the best from you.

passages.title: The Darnassus Mission
passages.text:
The Divine Bell is in the city. We don't want to cause a scene, we just want the artifact. I need you to find a way in, WITHOUT getting caught. That means no mounts, no flying, no fighting.

I can provide aid. I will magically cloak you, so you may move with stealth. I will also give you a small charm that you may use to return to safety, should you get in trouble.

Now go, <name>. Go, locate the bell, and tag it to be teleported back with you.

passages.title: The Darnassus Mission
passages.text: The bell, <name>!

passages.title: The Darnassus Mission
passages.text:
Well executed, <race>! I knew we could count on you.

Now to get off this wretched tree.

passages.title: Get My Results!
passages.text:
Ah, adventurer. The Warchief has instructed me to dispatch you to Silvermoon.

He grows impatient with the progress of Lor'themar's research and feels they might benefit from your... unique... experiences with the mogu.

Go to Silvermoon and demand that Lor'themar increase the speed of his research.

passages.title: Get My Results!
passages.text:
The Warchief "demands" progress? His impatience is growing more destructive with each command.

As it stands, we could use your expertise.

passages.title: The Kirin Tor
passages.text:
adventurer, King Varian has asked that I send you after his son to Dalaran. He believes you can help negotiate the withdrawal of blood elves there.

These "Sunreavers" claim fealty to the Horde and represent a major threat to the war effort.

Now that our very own Jaina Proudmoore is in charge of the Kirin Tor it should be easy to convince her to remove this Horde threat to her city.

Use the portal here in Lion's Landing to go to the Purple Parlor and lend what aid you can to Prince Anduin.

passages.title: The Kirin Tor
passages.text:
I am glad to see you friend. While I have learned much about diplomacy I think Jaina is too familiar with my tactics.

I could use a friendly hand in resolving this conflict.

passages.title: The First Riddle: Mercy
passages.text:
So, you wake up the Monkey King for a mallet hmmm? Answer first, these riddles three, and then the mallet you shall see.

First riddle!

 "Softly singing a song of pain

 There is a creature tortured and lame.

 Way down south and beyond the wall,

 It hides from its wikket masters' call.

 Seek out the creature sad and somber,

 And free it from its untamed amber."

Bring me the untamed amber.

passages.title: The First Riddle: Mercy
passages.text: Ah, the wise-ish thing returns. Have you my amber?

passages.title: The First Riddle: Mercy
passages.text:
Ah! Amber! Fresh and untamed. Did you kill to get it? But of course.

Though free, the untamed amber is a dangerous thing, and many might die because of it.

Mercy comes in many forms, like spikes and mantid and really ookin' spooky storms.

passages.title: Demonstrate Your Power
passages.text:
Akama and his men are under siege by the forces you unleashed in the Reliquary of Souls. 

Demonstrate your power to Akama by saving his men from the demonic forces!

passages.title: Ogudei's Lieutenants
passages.text:
There are two extremely powerful mogu spirits that the Alliance unearthed in their ineptitude.

These are choice targets for us, <class>. If you kill them and collect each of their essences, we could make great progress on decoding the history of this strange ruin.

passages.title: Ogudei's Lieutenants
passages.text: The essence isn't going to make itself, <race>.

passages.title: Ogudei's Lieutenants
passages.text: What treasures! With any luck, the spirits will return and we will be able to sample their essence further.

passages.title: It Is A Mystery
passages.text:
We have detected several... anomalies in these mines, of an arcane or spiritual nature. They are disrupting our attempts to discern the nature of the magic used in the spirit binding rituals here.

They are quite elusive, but we've managed to isolate the arcane signature of one of these anomalies, and one of our mages has enchanted this bauble with its signature.

Take the bauble. It will begin to glow more brightly as you approach the anomaly. Once you reach it, you can use the bauble to draw it out.

passages.title: It Is A Mystery
passages.text: We are still dealing with that anomaly! Hurry!

passages.title: It Is A Mystery
passages.text: Ahh, yes. I received word from one of our researchers that they are no longer troubled by that anomaly. Well done.

passages.title: Echoes of Thunder
passages.text:
Ah, <name>, we meet again. I have heard some wondrous news.

High Chieftain Baine Bloodhoof of the tauren has arrived here on Pandaria.

He meets with Warchief Garrosh Hellscream and Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron now, at the Shrine of Two Moons in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.

He sent me a strange request - to send him a loyal champion of the Horde, capable of combat... and discretion.

I can think of none better to send than you. Speak to Tak-Tak if you seek transport.

passages.title: Echoes of Thunder
passages.text: Well met, <class>. You were sent from Domination Point? Very well. We have much to discuss.

passages.title: The Harmonic Mallet
passages.text:
adventurer! Prince Anduin has somehow slipped his guards again. His control over the light is greatly increasing.

He was last seen heading to Kun-Lai Summit. He gave our mages the slip around the Valley of Emperors.

Can you find him? He insists on searching for what he claims is a counter to the Divine Bell. Perhaps you can talk some sense into him before he seizes control of your mind and has you dance your way back here.

Talk to Fennie for a ride into the mountains.

passages.title: The Harmonic Mallet
passages.text:
I am glad you made it, my friend. I could really use your help with what is to come. My father would prefer I remain in the safe custody of his legion.

But if there is one thing Pandaria has taught me, it is a few people in the right place at the right time can make a bigger difference than the greatest of armies.

passages.title: The Fate of Dalaran
passages.text:
Jaina is refusing to hear me out. Father was hoping I would have some pull with her, but I think she still sees me as a child.

You, on the other hand, are a hero of the Alliance and I know she respects your deeds.

Is there something you can say to her to convince her we need her help?

passages.title: The Fate of Dalaran
passages.text: We are not asking for military forces. But we do need the magical support of Dalaran if we are to stop Garrosh's reckless advances.

passages.title: The Fate of Dalaran
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, hero. I hear the wisdom in Jaina's words.

Let's hope her faith in the Sunreavers is justified.

passages.title: The Kun-Lai Expedition
passages.text:
I have another message for you from High Chieftain Bloodhoof.

It seems you've made quite the impression on him.

He travels with the Warchief's vanguard into Kun-Lai Summit, to the north. They have set up an outpost, Garrosh'ar Advance, just east of One Keg.

You had best not keep him waiting. Speak to Tak-Tak for swift travel.

passages.title: The Kun-Lai Expedition
passages.text: Thank you for coming so quickly.

passages.title: The Kun-Lai Expedition
passages.text: Thank you for coming, <name>.

passages.title: Memory Wine
passages.text: The tincture is ready. Now, drink.

passages.title: Memory Wine
passages.text: What did you see?

passages.title: Memory Wine
passages.text: What did you see, <class>?

passages.title: The Kun-Lai Expedition
passages.text:
Glory to the Alliance, <class>. We are making gains against the Horde in the Krasarang Wilds, albeit slowly.

While we hold the front here, we need your help to fight a different battle - one that strikes at our enemy's heart.

Our SI:7 informant, Agent Connelly, has sent word that a Horde vanguard is moving up into the northern reaches of Kun-Lai Summit.

Go without delay. Make contact with Agent Connelly in the field, and find out what is going on.

Speak to Fennie over there for a flight in.

passages.title: The Kun-Lai Expedition
passages.text:
<You do a doubletake when the Pandaren suddenly speaks with Connelly's voice.>

'Bout time, laddie! I've been waitin' fer ya to show up.

These Pandaren are good people but can't mix a martini fer nothin'.

passages.title: Memory Wine
passages.text:
<The radio static crackles, and Agent Connelly continues speaking.>

Now comes the real challenge, <laddie/lassie>. 

Head on over to the center of camp and see what you can overhear.

passages.title: Memory Wine
passages.text: Back so fast, rookie? So what did ye learn?

passages.title: De-Subjugation
passages.text:
The Kor'kron have been trained to be the finest, most loyal soldiers of the Warchief. Their presence here means that Garrosh fears an uprising.

Vol'jin and his people are as much a part of the Horde as any orc.

We must break this occupation and free the trolls. It pains me to say this, but you must eliminate enough of the Kor'kron so that the trolls can retake their city. Then meet me at Darkspear Hold so we might challenge their officer directly.

passages.title: De-Subjugation
passages.text: How did it come to this? It is as if the word "honor" is lost on these orcs.

passages.title: De-Subjugation
passages.text:
The orcs have changed. My Horde has changed. Do I kill my fellow orcs until it is once again "my" Horde? Do I have any right to try force the Horde to be what it once was?

These are troubling times. But for now, I must see to Vol'jin's people.

passages.title: The Prince's Pursuit
passages.text:
My goal is an expedient end to this costly war. Prove to me that the Alliance deserves to win. Show me your prowess on the battlefield.

You are not fighting some abstract force like the sha: You are facing your enemy head-on, eye-to-eye.

Will you triumph?

passages.title: The Prince's Pursuit
passages.text:
Marvelous! Even in the midst of the chaos of battle you've proven that an individual can have an impact. The Horde has learned that their actions in Pandaria will not be unopposed.

I believe it is time for a more substantial challenge...

passages.title: To the Valley!
passages.text:
This sealed communication was sent for you, along with urgent orders to travel to the Valley of Emperors in Kun-Lai Summit.

This looks serious. I'd not delay if I were you.

Speak to Tak-Tak for transportation.

passages.title: To the Valley!
passages.text:
Ah, good. You have come. 

Again, I apologize for the cryptic note - but Garrosh is increasingly distrustful of us. I do not want this operation disturbed by hasty action on his part.

passages.title: A Kor'kron In Our Midst
passages.text:
Garrosh is hell-bent on finding that Divine Bell. I wouldn't be surprised if he tore Kun-Lai Summit apart to find that artifact.

The Warchief's called a gathering at Garrosh'ar Advance, just to our north.

I need to stay here to monitor troop movements, so you'll have to infiltrate their camp and overhear their discussion.

Go to Garrosh'ar Advance and steal some Kor'kron Armor from Reavers, Honor Guards, and Scouts.

Take this radio earpiece. Don't contact me... I'll contact you.

passages.title: A Kor'kron In Our Midst
passages.text: Just as you look at the assembled Kor'kron disguise, your radio earpiece crackles.

passages.title: A Kor'kron In Our Midst
passages.text:
<Agent Connelly's voice comes over the radio.>

Ey, you're good! I knew those Kor'kron wouldn't be a problem fer ya. Couldn't've done much better meself.

passages.title: Legacy of the Korune
passages.text:
I'm not prepared to throw away more of our people fighting against an enemy we don't know or understand. 

See if you can find any clues in the area as to who exactly these "Korune" mogu are. A contingency in case this operation doesn't go as planned.

passages.title: Legacy of the Korune
passages.text: Have you found anything on the mogu?

passages.title: Legacy of the Korune
passages.text:
Good. There's quite a bit to pore through here... 

I will have the Reliquary investigate these. Surely we can use them to discern more of the secrets of these Korune mogu.

passages.title: The Best Around
passages.text:
We're going to need help if we hope to figure out Garrosh's plans for Pandaria.

I have someone specific in mind, but he will not be easy to convince.

Agent Connelly considers himself retired, but one does not simply leave the SI: 7. We've had an undercover agent following his every move for months.

Currently, he is disguising himself as a high roller at Bizmo's Brawlpub. Something about settling an old debt.

Meet with our undercover agent in the Brawler's Guild.

passages.title: The Best Around
passages.text: So you think you are going to talk Connelly out of retirement? Good luck!

passages.title: The Best Around
passages.text:
Following Connelly has been interesting to say the least. The man is a master of disguise!

Talking him into joining you won't be the hard part, <class>. Figuring out which of these lively individuals is him will be next to impossble.

passages.title: To Catch A Spy
passages.text:
Now, I could tell you who Connelly is, but that would be too easy! To catch a spy you have to think like a spy.

You have to pass the test first!

The small things can say a lot about a person. It's all in the details.

I'm going to give you a drink to deliver. I will give you a small detail about something the recipient is wearing. From there it will be up to you.

Be careful who you pick to give drinks to. People here tend to get pretty hostile if you give them the wrong order!

passages.title: To Catch A Spy
passages.text: You learn to look at the details when you barkeep.

passages.title: To Catch A Spy
passages.text: You have a keen eye, <class>! I think you are ready to meet Connelly.

passages.title: He's In Deep
passages.text:
Agent Connelly has managed to infiltrate Garrosh's camp in Kun-Lai! He's been following their every move.

Connelly requested you specifically to assist him in gathering some vital intelligence.

He sent along a disguise for you. Make sure you put it on before approaching the camp! It will no doubt be heavily guarded.

He insists you will know him when you see him. Something about your keen eye for details...

Go talk to Fennie over there for a drop-off.

passages.title: He's In Deep
passages.text:
You've arrived just in time. From the intel I've gathered, Garrosh is hot on the trail of some sort of ancient mogu artifact of power.

If we can figure out what he's after, we can stop him from getting it!

We have to act fast to gather as much information as possible.

passages.title: Bugging Out
passages.text:
I've managed to plant a few bugs around the camp, but there could always be more.

I disguised the bugs to look like statues. They blend in perfectly with the other artifacts lying around.

Your disguise should allow you to move freely around the camp. Just don't go near the dog and don't linger around Garrosh! Nero and Garrosh will see through your disguise.

If you get caught I can't help you. I can't compromise the mission!

passages.title: Bugging Out
passages.text: How'd it go?

passages.title: Bugging Out
passages.text: Well done! Everyone always underestimates the little guys and it is always a grave mistake!

passages.title: Trapping the Leader
passages.text:
It is time to make our move. Go to the Tomb of Shadows, weaken him, and take him captive.

I will stay here in case Garrosh arrives. He must be delayed so that we can take our prize before he destroys it in his anger.

Hurry!

passages.title: Trapping the Leader
passages.text: Move, <name>!

passages.title: Trapping the Leader
passages.text:
We managed to capture our quarry. 

In truth, though, I am not sure what our next move should be. I will contact the leaders of our allies and see if they have ideas - I don't know that our arcane talents are going to pry the secrets of our mogu captive.

passages.title: A Change of Command
passages.text:
There's an orc general I've been keeping a close eye on. Warlord Bloodhilt curried a lot of favor with Garrosh Hellscream by beating back an Alliance advance in Southern Barrens. He's now entrenched within the fortress at Domination Point.

I doubt the Alliance can take him out. But... you've proven me wrong before.

If you wish to finish him off, bring friends. Lots of friends.

passages.title: A Change of Command
passages.text:
<Wrathion grins.>

You were being tested, <class>. I knew you were capable of great things by yourself.

But you have proven to me that you have the makings of a leader, cobbling together support among a group of strangers in the midst of a battlefield.

The Alliance is fortunate to have you.

passages.title: The Lion Roars
passages.text:
This is a global war, <name>. It has spilled onto Pandaria, and it has set hot spots across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms ablaze. How will you fare on an organized battlefront? I would like to see for myself.

I look forward to hearing your report from the front lines.

passages.title: The Lion Roars
passages.text:
<Wrathion hungrily listens to tales of your exploits on the battlefield, his eyes gleaming bright red.>

Ohh... oh! Incredible! In the very eye of battle, one's true heart is revealed.

You do not disappoint, <name>.

Neither does your Alliance.

passages.title: The Ruins of Korune
passages.text:
Garrosh sent a hundred riders to search the northern coast of Kun-Lai Summit, to seek a mogu crypt matching the one you saw in Shan Kien's memory.

Out of those, one found the resting place of the Divine Bell.

Blademaster Ishi is leading an advance party to secure the bell now.

Go and assist him. Defend that artifact from anyone who might stand in your way!

Speak to Tak-Tak without delay. He can take you there.

passages.title: The Ruins of Korune
passages.text: The Alliance beat us here. How could this happen?

passages.title: The Ruins of Korune
passages.text:
It's time for our boldest move yet, <name>.

Since you acquired intel on the location of the Divine Bell, we've amassed a top team to excavate the artifact without delay.

Commander Sarannha Skyglaive leads the expedition into the northern-most reaches of Kun-Lai Summit.

Join them at once, and use whatever skills you need to make the endeavor a success.

Good luck, <class>. I don't need to tell you how important this mission is to the Alliance.

Speak to Fennie. She'll get you there quickly.

passages.title: The Ruins of Korune
passages.text: Looks like we're well ahead of the Horde. Not surprising, but we must act swiftly.

passages.title: The Ruins of Korune
passages.text: We blasted the doors open moments ago, <class>. You arrived just in time to join us for the excavation.

passages.title: The Divine Bell
passages.text:
There's no telling what lies below, so I will lead the initial scouting party myself.

If your report was correct, then the Korune mogu hid the Divine Bell in the rooms below our very feet.

I have a feeling they would not have left such a precious artifact unguarded.

I could use a capable <class> such as yourself to watch my back. Let me know when you're ready.

passages.title: The Divine Bell
passages.text:
Fantastic work, <name>. I could not even imagine the atrocity that Garrosh would commit if this bell were to fall into his hands.

Today, we have secured a safe future for the Alliance. I will see to it that the bell makes it safely to Darnassus.

I will extoll your deeds to the King.

passages.title: He Won't Even Miss It
passages.text:
I've noticed Garrosh and that Reliquary blood elf carrying around some sort of journal.

The journal is never more than a stone's throw away. It must be important!

If you can cause enough of a distraction, you may be able to swipe the journal off the table.

These yaks might just do the trick. Give one of 'em a tap and they'll do the rest.

Just be ready to move fast!

passages.title: He Won't Even Miss It
passages.text: What did you find?

passages.title: He Won't Even Miss It
passages.text:
Phew! That was a close one! I never doubted you for a minute though.

Now let me take a look at that journal...

passages.title: The Bell Speaks
passages.text:
Your efforts have culminated in this moment, <class>.

Warchief Garrosh gathers the most elite champions of the Horde in Kun-Lai Summit to witness the ringing of the Divine Bell.

You have more than earned the right to participate.

Go now. The dawn of the new Horde begins today.

Speak to Tak-Tak. He should be able to secure your travel arrangements.

passages.title: The Bell Speaks
passages.text: I was wondering when you would arrive, <name>.

passages.title: Breath of Darkest Shadow
passages.text:
It is time, <name>. We have traveled a long path to reach this moment.

Today, our Warchief, Garrosh Hellscream, will change the course of our people's history forever.

Today, we witness the birth of Garrosh's Horde!

Do not let anything interfere with the ceremony!

passages.title: Breath of Darkest Shadow
passages.text: We cannot rely on fate or destiny. We must carve out our own future... the future that WE deserve!

passages.title: Breath of Darkest Shadow
passages.text:
They may have destroyed the Divine Bell, but I have taken the life of the Alliance's prodigal son!

It is nothing less than my own father would have expected of me.

This victory may have come at a high cost, but it is of little consequence.

I will find other ways to destroy my enemies, and bring glory to the Horde!

passages.title: The Bell Speaks
passages.text:
Horde forces are amassing in huge numbers at the Emperor's Reach, high up in the mountains of Kun-Lai Summit.

The area is an ancient mogu palace, and certainly a source of untold power.

This can only mean one thing. Garrosh is going to use the Divine Bell, and Anduin... and the Harmonic Mallet... are both missing.

I have no doubt that the fool boy went north by himself.

I don't have time to gather an elite force to detain him. You must go and stop Anduin.

Fennie can take you.

passages.title: The Bell Speaks
passages.text: <name>! Just the <class> I was hoping to see. You couldn't have arrived at a better time.

passages.title: Violence in the Arena
passages.text:
As I suspected, it gets worse up ahead. The Silver Covenant is outright attacking innocent Sunreavers!

This cannot stand. While our prime directive is to rescue Aethas Sunreaver, we must also protect as many blood elves as we can.

I will continue to scout ahead. Fight well, <class>!

passages.title: Violence in the Arena
passages.text:
So much bloodshed! In a place of peace!

Jaina has gone too far this time.

passages.title: A Tactical Assault
passages.text:
If we're to survive up above ground, we're going to need a base of operations.

I'm going to try to take the center of the city. It's risky, but hopefully Jaina and the Silver Covenant won't expect it.

Stay by my side now, <name>.

passages.title: A Tactical Assault
passages.text: Now, let's move quickly.

passages.title: The Kirin Tor's True Colors
passages.text:
Any pretense that the Kirin Tor might have had at being a "neutral" group can officially be discarded. I'm now hearing that Jaina's got Alliance troops stowed away near Antonidas Memorial.

The area's free of Sunreavers, but it still makes my blood boil to see such blatant favoritism from the Kirin Tor.

Go visit the memorial, <name>... and give those Alliance dogs a good kick on your way through.

passages.title: The Kirin Tor's True Colors
passages.text: <Rommath looks displeased.>

passages.title: The Kirin Tor's True Colors
passages.text:
Thank you for that, <name>.

It unsettles me to have to fight directly with the high elves of the Silver Covenant... but I never tire of slaying Alliance.

passages.title: The Remaining Sunreavers
passages.text:
There's still a number of significant Sunreavers who haven't been accounted for. Odds are that they're in the Sunreaver's Sanctuary, caught by surprise.

<Rommath hands you an artifact, clearly made by blood elf hands.>

The place is crawling with Silver Covenant. You'll need to get in, use the Tear to evacuate the VIPs, and then get out.

Stay alive, <name>.

passages.title: The Remaining Sunreavers
passages.text: Be on the lookout for Aethas while you're in there.

passages.title: The Remaining Sunreavers
passages.text: Excellent. They should be waiting for us in Silvermoon when we return.

passages.title: One Last Grasp
passages.text:
We've looked everywhere he's likely to be, except for one place: the Violet Citadel.

Find out if Archmage Aethas is being held within the citadel, <name>. We may get lucky. If not... at least we saved a number of lives today.

passages.title: One Last Grasp
passages.text: Is this... <name>? What's going on here?

passages.title: Darnassus Attacked?
passages.text:
As you know, our night elven allies moved the Divine Bell you retrieved to Darnassus for safekeeping and study. Moments ago, they portaled some Highbourne mages over here to ask for backup. Details are hazy - some sort of stealth attack on the city?

I don't know what to make of it, but Jaina Proudmoore is already on the scene and I suspect they need all the help they can get.

Speak to Seamus Goldenkicks over there for a quick portal to Darnassus. Find Jaina!

passages.title: Darnassus Attacked?
passages.text:
The Bell is gone...

At the scene of the crime, we found traces of arcane magic... I may be able to use my skills to track the thieves.

passages.title: Jaina's Resolution
passages.text:
For too long, I have toiled to mend fences between Alliance and Horde. Time and time again, I've given the Horde the benefit of the doubt - and time and time again, they stab me in the back.

I refuse to be betrayed again! If the Horde intends to use the Kirin Tor as a weapon against the Alliance, then they have no place in Dalaran.

Come with me, <name>.

passages.title: Jaina's Resolution
passages.text: <Jaina looks angry.>

passages.title: Jaina's Resolution
passages.text:
I will instruct you from here on out.

Jaina will be going down into the city to enforce our new rules.

passages.title: Unfair Trade
passages.text:
Most shopkeepers in the Magus Commerce Exchange have sided with the Silver Covenant, but there remain a few holdouts that must be taken care of.

<Vereesa shows you a list of names.>

They will not go easily.

passages.title: Unfair Trade
passages.text:
While I can't say I agree completely with Jaina's methods, I do understand her motives.

Sometimes, you have to fight back.

passages.title: Nowhere to Hide
passages.text:
The Sunreaver's Sanctuary is still crawling with those Horde-loving Sunreavers.

Jaina will have sent the reasonable ones to the Violet Hold. The rest refuse to leave, raising their weapons against us.

Show them the cost of their defiance. They now face the judgment of the Alliance, the Silver Covenant, and the Kirin Tor!

passages.title: Nowhere to Hide
passages.text:
This is a bloody day, <name>, and this is bloody work.

But do not forget what the Sunreavers did to bring this on: They used neutral Kirin Tor resources to aid the Horde in their fight against the Alliance.

Do not hesitate to believe that they would do the same to us, given the chance.

passages.title: Nowhere to Run
passages.text:
Compliant Sunreavers will be sent to the Violet Hold. Defiant ones are put to the sword.

NONE are to escape.

The Sunreavers keep their dragonhawk mounts on Krasus' Landing. Take this dust, and use it to render them incapable of flying.

Or kill them. I don't care.

passages.title: Nowhere to Run
passages.text: We can't have the Sunreavers escaping and plotting counterattacks against Dalaran. We need to be quick, precise, and thorough.

passages.title: Nowhere to Run
passages.text: Now, the Sunreavers have to answer to us. Jail or death - their fate is in their own hands.

passages.title: What Had To Be Done
passages.text:
Thank you for your aid today, <name>. I will be handling the purge from here on out.

Jaina will soon be off to Lion's Landing, to speak with King Varian. She asked for your attendance.

passages.title: What Had To Be Done
passages.text:
I can't fault you for following orders. In fact, I can't really fault Jaina for acting on her own behalf, for once.

But still... we aren't playing a game here. We are dealing with war, with people's lives, with the future of the Alliance itself.

At the very least, we now have the Kirin Tor on our side. Today will be remembered by all as a victory for the Alliance.

passages.title: Stirred, Not Shaken
passages.text:
Alright, I'll tell you how to find Connelly.

Agent Connelly is currently posing as the high roller, Professor Kilt. He spends most of his time in the Boom Room. Rumor has it he's after one of the fighters for some long forgotten betrayal.

Unfortunately, the lounge is by invitation only. Lucky for you I just happen to have an invitation.

Try not to look too obvious when you walk past the bouncers. If you get caught you didn't get this pass from me.

In fact you and I have never met!

passages.title: Stirred, Not Shaken
passages.text:
So the SI: 7 needs a reminder in what the word retirement means?

I suppose they wouldn't be comin' to me if the situation weren't dire.

I'll help, but I'll need a few days to gather some intel.

passages.title: Pandaren Spirit Tamer
passages.text: Legend tells of legendary pandaren spirits that roam the lands of Pandaria. Find them and defeat them in a pet battle.

passages.title: Pandaren Spirit Tamer
passages.text: I can't belive you took out those spirits!

passages.title: The Prince's Pursuit
passages.text:
My goal is an expedient end to this costly war. Prove to me that the Horde deserves to win. Show me your prowess on the battlefield.

You are not fighting some abstract force like the sha: You are facing your enemy head-on, eye-to-eye.

Will you triumph?

passages.title: The Prince's Pursuit
passages.text:
Marvelous! Even in the midst of the chaos of battle you've proven that an individual can have an impact. The Alliance buckles under Horde might, although their King refuses to break.

I believe it is time for a more substantial challenge...

passages.title: A Change of Command
passages.text:
There's an Alliance dwarf I've been keeping a close eye on. High Marshal Twinbraid proved to be a nuisance in Southern Barrens when he struck back at the Horde after the loss of Bael Modan. He's now entrenched within the Alliance stronghold in Lion's Landing, helping to orchestrate the Krasarang counter-offensive.

Only a legendary group of Horde heroes could possibly defeat him.

If you wish to finish him off, bring friends. Lots of friends.

passages.title: A Change of Command
passages.text:
<Wrathion grins.>

You were being tested, <class>. I knew you were capable of great things by yourself.

But you have proven to me that you have the makings of a leader, cobbling together support among a group of strangers in the midst of a battlefield.

The Horde is fortunate to have you.

passages.title: Glory to the Horde
passages.text:
This is a global war, <name>. It has spilled onto Pandaria, and it has set hot spots across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms ablaze. How will you fare on an organized battlefront? I would like to see for myself.

I look forward to hearing your report from the front lines.

passages.title: Glory to the Horde
passages.text:
<Wrathion hungrily listens to tales of your exploits on the battlefield, his eyes gleaming bright red.>

Ohh... oh! Incredible! In the very eye of battle, one's true heart is revealed.

You do not disappoint, <name>.

Neither does this Horde of yours.

passages.title: Dis-Assembly Required
passages.text:
Those shredders are becoming a problem down there, <class>.

We've sent in the Mecha-Pounders, but it just isn't enough. They're getting damaged faster than we can repair 'em!

I happened upon this strange remote while scouting. With a little bit of re-configurin' I think we can use it.

Try usin' it on the Jungle Shredders. Hopefully it will destroy them and then you can bring me the scrap metal.

passages.title: Dis-Assembly Required
passages.text: So what did that remote do?

passages.title: Dis-Assembly Required
passages.text: Goblin construction leaves somethin' to be desired, but it'll have to do. Good work, <name>!

passages.title: The Silence
passages.text:
D..did we... do it?

<Anduin mumbles the words, even though the effort clearly costs him.>

L..look... in.. my... bag...

Use... flare...

passages.title: The Silence
passages.text:
I hesitate to guess what would have happened if you had not been there with the young Prince, <name>.

Today, you put an end to Garrosh's plans.

You have undoubtedly saved thousands of lives, and most importantly, you brought Anduin back to us.

We are doing everything we can for the boy, but we can only wait and see.

I believe he has the fight in him. I must believe it...

passages.title: The Thunder King
passages.text:
Are you aware of recent events in Kun-Lai Summit? The Zandalari have landed on the northern shores in great numbers and have set about renewing old alliances. To that end, they have resurrected The Thunder King.

Even among the mogu, the name of the first emperor commands awe and fear. The Thunder King founded a vast empire of slavery and suffering... but also of power, riches, and splendor.

We will take the fight to him soon. Find me when your faction makes its move.

passages.title: The Thunder King
passages.text:
The Sunreavers and the Kirin-Tor are mounting an assault on the Thunder King's base of operations! My new friend here and I were just discussing the ramifications of their attack.

You and I can stand to benefit from the situation, <name>. I have a few ideas...

passages.title: Tracking the Thieves
passages.text:
We WILL get to the bottom of this.

<name>, you're coming with me. We'll search every inch of this city if we have to, but we'll find out how they took the bell... and where.

I'm picking up traces of arcane magic here... we need to follow the trail!

passages.title: Tracking the Thieves
passages.text:
I've decided.

Certain members of the Kirin Tor have put their allegiance to the Horde above the order, and I will NOT tolerate it. This is nothing short of a betrayal.

<Jaina's eyes flare with rage.>

Come with me, <name>. We're going to clean up Dalaran.

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text:
You know, there is a way we can improve your S.E.L.F.I.E. cam, if you're interested. With the right focusing lens, I could add all kinds of features to that thing.

I've heard that way out on old Yojamba Isle in Stranglethorn Vale, the mother of all basilisks has been seen. Her hide is dotted with gems that'd make the perfect lens, if I could get my hands on them.

She's not going to go down easy, though. You might want to bring some friends along.

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text: That crystal spine matriarch has the gems we need to upgrade your lens, any luck with that?

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text: Count me surprised to hear from you again, you must be tougher than I thought. You've earned my respect, kid, here's your lens upgrade kit. Now get out there and take some S.E.L.F.I.E.S!

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text:
Hi again! Oh, I forgot to tell you! I've devised a foolproof way to improve your S.E.L.F.I.E. cam! 

In fact, with just the right gemstones, I can make a lens that would allow us to do all sorts of things!

Some fellow explorers have told me about a large basilisk out on Yojamba Isle in Stranglethorn Vale. Her hide is dotted with tons of high-quality crystals! What a perfect coincidence!

She sounds pretty tough, though! You should bring some friends!

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text: Hey, stay out of my shot! Oh, it's you! Did you take down that basilisk yet?

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text: I knew from the moment we met that you were an adventurer, just like me! Here's your lens upgrade kit, now get out there and take some S.E.L.F.I.E.S!

passages.title: Light Camera Action
passages.text:
You look like you've got a discerning eye for the visual arts, want to try your hand at photography?

I can make you one of these S.E.L.F.I.E. cameras, I just need a few parts.

For the strap, grab me a Russet Belt from one of the armor merchants around here.

I've got a shipment of extra housings waiting by the back entrance to the city, grab me one when you're over there.

Oh, and a Standard Scope, most any engineer can make you one of those.

Now get out there, kid. Fame awaits!

passages.title: Light Camera Action
passages.text: You got those parts for me, or what? I'm busy here!

passages.title: Light Camera Action
passages.text: You're all set, kid. You've got a face the camera will love, now get out there and get shooting!

passages.title: A Test of Valor
passages.text:
<Without warning Wrathion slices his thumb and presses it against your forehead. His blood burns to the touch, but rapidly disappears into your skin.>

There! My eye is upon you, <class>. I am watching.

The Pandaren, like the Alliance, value the concept of "Valor." There are many ways to prove yourself valorous on this continent, from daily tasks to the defeat of heroic enemies within their lair. I will let you choose your own course.

Prove your bravery to me, <name>!

passages.title: A Test of Valor
passages.text:
<Wrathion nods slowly.>

Yes, <name>. I saw your deeds, and I was most impressed.

You are truly an instrument of change.

passages.title: A Spark of Life
passages.text: The Thunder-Laced Egg burns your hand as you hold it. You recall that Yalia Sagewhisper of the Shado-Pan discussing the history of the Thundering Cloud Serpents, perhaps she will know what to do with it.

passages.title: A Test of Valor
passages.text:
<Without warning Wrathion slices his thumb and presses it against your forehead. His blood burns to the touch, but rapidly disappears into your skin.>

There! My eye is upon you, <class>. I am watching.

The Pandaren, like the Horde, value the concept of "Valor." There are many ways to prove yourself valorous on this continent, from daily tasks to the defeat of heroic enemies within their lair. I will let you choose your own course.

Prove your bravery to me, <name>!

passages.title: A Test of Valor
passages.text:
<Wrathion nods slowly.>

Yes, <name>. I saw your deeds, and I was most impressed.

You are truly an instrument of change.

passages.title: Bolstering the Defenses
passages.text:
This island is a dangerous place, <name>. We have to worry about attacks from the Zandalari, mogu, saurok, and worst of all the Sunreavers.

I had perimeter wards placed on the outskirts of our camp for additional protection. In their current state they will only injure an attacker, but I'm done with warnings!

With your help we can super-charge the wards into a more deadly defense system.

passages.title: Bolstering the Defenses
passages.text:
Excellent work, <name>. Those perimeter wards should keep out all manner of filth.

With Violet Rise protected we can focus on more pressing matters.

passages.title: They All Fall Down
passages.text:
The Zandalari do not tolerate weakness in their ranks, <class>.

Those that are deemed weak are often sacrificed in barbaric ceremonies. The victims' spirits are captured and entombed within the sentries you see guarding the grounds.

I wish to study their essence. For this I will need your help.

Take this resonance crystal and siphon the spirits from the sentry corpses.

 Do not allow them to escape!

passages.title: They All Fall Down
passages.text: Have you completed your task, <class>?

passages.title: They All Fall Down
passages.text: Excellent work, <class>! This will aid my studies greatly, as well as advance our cause here.

passages.title: Power Play
passages.text:
The Zandalari have found a way to infuse items of great power with the essence of their loa. These items are often passed from one generation to another, each recipient adding to the item's power.

Two such items exist here. To be specific, two masks, worn by two brothers.

Spiritbinder Tu'chek and Arcanital Ra'kul must be stopped and their masks destroyed.

Kill them and return their masks to me. I will make sure the masks are disposed of.

passages.title: Power Play
passages.text: Do you have the masks?

passages.title: Power Play
passages.text: Getting these masks was no easy task, <class>. I am grateful for your service.

passages.title: The Crumbled Chamberlain
passages.text:
You there! Assist me.

In life I was the Royal Chamberlain for his majesty, the Thunder King. For my dedication, I was condemned to this stone form, forever forced to watch over a portion of his wealth.

Someone has desecrated my glorious body and sent pieces of it across the island. The thought of spending an eternity as nothing more than a head depresses me.

Search the island, recover these pieces and I shall grant you one of his majesty's treasures.

passages.title: The Crumbled Chamberlain
passages.text: I require ALL of my pieces. If so much as a pebble is missing, I shall consider forfeiting our agreement.

passages.title: The Crumbled Chamberlain
passages.text: Ah! To feel whole again! You have my gratitude, servant. Take this stone and use it wisely. Should you encounter his majesty the Thunder King in your travels, do not tell him where you received it, or you will be standing in a statue next to me for the remainder of eternity.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text:
In the Court of Bones, the Thunder King's sorcerers perform dark rituals.

To bolster their numbers, the Shan'ze soulrippers are imbuing ancient stone statues with stolen spirits from the living.

After these stone conquerors are brought to life, they will be formidable opponents on the battlefield.

We must stop their ritual before these statues can be revived.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text: It is a mystery how the mogu can imbue life into inanimate stone, but with enough study, we, too, may one day be able to understand that power.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text:
A good defense is just as effective as a strong offense. One less enemy to worry about.

Well done.

passages.title: Soul Surrender
passages.text:
We assault the mogu at the Court of Bones, but I fear we merely send them fodder for their abominable rituals.

The mogu do not merely kill their prisoners - they steal their souls and imbue them in machinations of stone, or reforge the fallen into ghostly tools of war.

Alliance or Horde, it matters not. We cannot allow the mogu to bolster their numbers.

Go into the crypts. Free any prisoners that are still living.

passages.title: Soul Surrender
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. You have lightened my heart of a heavy burden through your heroic actions.

I will remember your efforts on this day.

passages.title: Grave Circumstances
passages.text:
The Court of Bones crawls with mogu forces. Endlessly do they perform their rituals of lightning and thunder.

If our mission to take this island is to succeed, then we cannot allow them to hold such a strategic position.

They must be eliminated.

passages.title: Grave Circumstances
passages.text: Excellent. You have dealt the mogu a blow that they shall not easily forget.

passages.title: Into the Crypts
passages.text:
Every day, we uncover additional relics from the Court of Bones.

Recently, we discovered this scroll amongst the gravestones in one of the deepest crypts.

I believe that this incantation can be used to call beyond the grave. And if my Mogu is up to date, I'd say you should use it in the last room in the Hall of the Exalted.

Would you be willing to test out my theory?

passages.title: Into the Crypts
passages.text: How did it go?

passages.title: Into the Crypts
passages.text: Ah yes, you've just confirmed my theory! Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text:
In the Court of Bones, the Thunder King's sorcerers perform dark rituals.

To bolster their numbers, the Shan'ze soulrippers are imbuing ancient stone statues with stolen spirits from the living.

After these stone conquerors are brought to life, they will be formidable opponents on the battlefield.

We must stop their ritual before these statues can be revived.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text: It is a mystery how the mogu can imbue life into inanimate stone, but with enough study, we, too, may one day be able to understand that power.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text:
A good defense is just as effective as a strong offense. One less enemy to worry about.

Well done.

passages.title: Manipulating the Saurok
passages.text:
I have three magisters entrenched in Ihgaluk Crag, monitoring the saurok and - where they can - turning them against the mogu. I need you to find them and see if they need any supplies or assistance.

They will be concealed from view. Look for shimmering columns of light within the saurok village.

passages.title: Manipulating the Saurok
passages.text: Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Manipulating the Saurok
passages.text:
<The archmage listens carefully to your report.>

I understand. Thank you for your aid, <class>.

passages.title: De-Constructed
passages.text:
Saurok consistently test our borders, and our constructs usually fend them off. Some constructs, however, have been defeated and dragged back to Ihgaluk Crag.

I want those constructs back. No slithering lizard will steal Silver Covenant property under my watch.

passages.title: De-Constructed
passages.text:
Hmph... saurok.

<Modera spits.>

passages.title: De-Constructed
passages.text:
That's more like it.

Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Preventing a Future Threat
passages.text:
It pains me to think of the torture the poor skyscreamers must endure as the trolls train them to become implements of war.

The hatchlings are quite fearful, and will fly away if you even get close them. Please, frighten some away before the Zandalari corrupt them.

passages.title: Preventing a Future Threat
passages.text: Welcome back, <race>. The hatchlings you frightened will live a better life without their captors.

passages.title: Surgical Strike
passages.text:
Zandalari spiritbinders perform sacrifices to their gods, the beastcallers bend innocent skyscreamers to their will, and the jaguar warriors venture closer to us by the day.

Dispose of these threats in Za'Tual, <race>, and watch the might of the trolls weaken.

passages.title: Surgical Strike
passages.text: With a few of their more threatening kin slain, perhaps the Zandalari will show reluctance next time they decide to trifle with us.

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
The Skumblade threaten our people, but responding with all-out slaughter would be an overreaction.

A more reasonable response to their threat would be to slay some of their tribal leaders. There will be less bloodshed, and they will still respect our perimeter.

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
The saurok value strength above all else. They only respond to strength.

Peace with the saurok will require some amount of bloodshed. The question is, how much?

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
I know the true price of bloodshed. I know the cost of war.

It would be simpler to blindly massacre our attackers until they yield. But is it right?

passages.title: Just Some Light Clean-Up Work
passages.text:
This is not a glamorous job. Let me put it to you bluntly.

The Skumblade saurok pile all of their filth into a pool in the middle of their village. This filth is so concentrated and so rancid that it has congealed into moving, animate matter.

The saurok can keep their filth-pool, but once it starts spreading outside of the village, I'd say it's time to intervene.

passages.title: Just Some Light Clean-Up Work
passages.text: Sorry in advance about the smell.

passages.title: Just Some Light Clean-Up Work
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Looking at you, I'm suddenly quite proud of Dalaran's state-of-the-art plumbing system.

passages.title: Compy Stomp
passages.text:
The raptors and saurid of the Zandalari represent a substantial threat to our forces here. They are superb hunting beasts that can track prey over great distances and are often lethal to encounter when caught unawares.

I need you to head into the Beast Pens and cull their numbers. We need to make sure to slay them before they are fully trained.

passages.title: Compy Stomp
passages.text: We lost three good soldiers when we first arrived on this island. Killed in their sleep by compies that had snuck into their tent. Some nights I still hear the screams.

passages.title: Direhorn vs Devilsaur
passages.text:
We have an opportunity to disrupt the Zandalari war machine as well as have a little fun in the process.

Within these beast pens, a devilsaur and a direhorn are being outfitted with armor, their minds being enslaved to the Zandalari charms.

Go into the camp and disrupt one of these binding rituals. It doesn't matter which one. Just kill those who are trying to bind the creature. This should let the fully armored beast run mad through the Zandalari camp. Then sit back and watch the hilarity ensue.

passages.title: Direhorn vs Devilsaur
passages.text: So... did you decide the devilsaur or the direhorn?

passages.title: Direhorn vs Devilsaur
passages.text:
Few things in this world and beyond are more entertaining than watching a rampaging ancient beast tearing through an enemy's settlement.

If times were not so dire I would consider selling tickets to such an event.

passages.title: Dino Might
passages.text:
The Zandalari use a series of fetishes and charms to maintain their control over their menagerie of beasts.

Two can play at that game.

I want you to find some of these fetishes and try them out on the various beasts in the Beast Pens.

Take careful note of how each beast responds to each fetish. Then report your results to me.

Maybe this will give us the edge we need against the Zandalari.

passages.title: Dino Might
passages.text: Very interesting results. I am sure there is a mage somewhere that cares about the specifics. I, on the other hand, am just glad to hear the sound of trolls being assaulted by their own beasts.

passages.title: Centuries in Sentries
passages.text:
Sacrifices are common place in Zandalari society. There is however one oddity among these barbaric rituals; volunteers. They treat it as a great honor!

The weak still seek to contribute, even if that means giving their lives to be bound to the sentries you see walking around. Locked away in service to their people.

Take this resonating crystal. Once destroyed, drain the sentry of its Zandalari inhabitant. Return the crystal to me when your task is complete.

passages.title: Centuries in Sentries
