It's really quite convenient, I've a particular affinity for specific moments, rather than lengthy chains of events.

The timeways tell me that we will have need of its power many times in the near future.

passages.title: Timeless Nutriment
passages.text:
As you have surmised, the flora and fauna of this island are quite unusual. Not all explanations are mysterious, however. Sometimes, we must listen to the land, to hear the tales of the world around us. Have you considered that the creatures of this island grew to such proportions simply from the nutriment of the land you walk upon?

You will find nutriment in abundance throughout the island: ripe fruits, eggs, meat, flowers, nuts, and even the stones themselves. Eat, and discover the power of the land.

passages.title: Timeless Nutriment
passages.text: Have you enjoyed the abundance of the island?

passages.title: Timeless Nutriment
passages.text: The island gives in abundance, in nutriment and in answers. You only need look around to find what you seek.

passages.title: Wayshrines Of The Celestials
passages.text:
Many years ago, these grounds were a place where my people would come in pilgrimage. Here, they would listen to the words of the celestials, and meditate for many days. In their meditations, they found the fear, anger, despair, doubt, and violence that plagued their spirits.

Before them would be a pathway to enlightenment. For each, the pathway would be different. For all of them, the pathway began with wisdom.

Travel the island, as they did, and discover one of the lost wayshrines of the celestials.

passages.title: Wayshrines Of The Celestials
passages.text: The shrines will not always avail themselves to you. Do not give up, such is the test of patience.

passages.title: Wayshrines Of The Celestials
passages.text: You have experienced the power and wisdom of the Celestials. Let it flow through you now, and remain in your heart for all time.

passages.title: Drive Back The Flame
passages.text:
The pandaren once existed in harmony with the Ordon yaungol. When the island suddenly disappeared, the Ordon faced certain death. In their desperation, the chief shaman called out for aid to the Fire Lords, and was answered.

Ordos was his name. Now, he is a creature of anger and violence. Though his people were saved, he burns endlessly in molten agony.

There is harmony no longer. The Ordon seek to take the Celestial Court, and sacrifice us all to Ordos. Drive them back, and restore balance.

passages.title: Drive Back The Flame
passages.text: The Ordon are not to be trifled with. They have survived on this island under the protections of their ever-burning demigod, Ordos.

passages.title: Drive Back The Flame
passages.text: Your accomplishments are many, and your bravery cannot be questioned. The Ordon have been driven back for the moment, but do not underestimate them. To restore harmony to the isle, we must continue to be vigilant.

passages.title: Den Mother's Demise
passages.text:
This is the pelt of Darkmoon Island's monstrous den mother.

Yebb Neblegear, beastmaster of the Darkmoon Faire, will be happy to know the ghostly wolf and her spawn will no longer be terrorizing his menagerie... at least for a little while. Bring it to him.

passages.title: Den Mother's Demise
passages.text: Is that what I think it is?

passages.title: Den Mother's Demise
passages.text: At last, that vicious beast has been slain! Thank you.

passages.title: Noodle Time: Bonus
passages.text:
Hello, <name>. Think you're a truly extraordinary noodle chef?

Let's see what you've got!

passages.title: Noodle Time: Bonus
passages.text: Excellent work <name>! Everyone always loves it when they hear that you'll be making noodle soup. People come from all over Pandaria just to try a taste.

passages.title: Path of the Mistwalker
passages.text:
You have heard the words of the celestials, but what did you learn on your path to the shrines?

The wisdom of the pilgrimage is in its silence and simplicity. As you listen to the wind rustling in the trees, and note even the smallest butterfly, your mind is open to learning the deepest lessons the trials have to teach us. Perhaps you noticed the many great beasts that roam the island?

Therein lies your trial. You have learned much from Pandaria, now let us put your knowledge to the test.

passages.title: Path of the Mistwalker
passages.text: Have the lessons of Pandaria aided you in your journey?

passages.title: Path of the Mistwalker
passages.text: Let this be your daily lesson, and let it hone your strength, wisdom, and fortitude.

passages.title: Courting Destiny
passages.text:
The Vision of Time is nearly perfected, we now have much more control over the visions we seek. Your efforts have been instrumental in completing the artifact and restoring the strength of not only my flight, but also our allies in the Timewalkers. All of us are in your debt.

Quite fortunately, I have located a sort of crux in time - an intersection of timeways - right here in Pandaria. Take the Vision of Time to the Temple of the White Tiger. There, in the cellars, turn the hourglass.

passages.title: Courting Destiny
passages.text: Did you use the Vision of Time? What was the result?

passages.title: Courting Destiny
passages.text:
Ah, it seems that our little prince has a role to play yet. We should not speak further of this, lest we alter the future ourselves.

The woods have ears, hero. Keep silent, we will find our answers in time.

passages.title: South Sprint 12
passages.text: For this challenge, run through the arch, then get to the red marker, the purple marker, then return here before the bell tolls 12 times. Good luck!

passages.title: Elwynn Long Distance Trial: 25
passages.text: For this challenge: run through the arch, then get to the blue marker, the green marker, and finally return here before the bell tolls 25 times.

passages.title: Elwynn South Distance Trial: 30
passages.text: For this challenge: run through the arch, then get to the red marker, the purple marker, and finally return here before the bell tolls 30 times.

passages.title: The Warlord's Guard
passages.text:
I don't know what you are accustomed to, traveler, but these lands devour the weak. Perhaps Durotan wishes to rid himself of you. We shall see.

You must kill the Warlord of the Circle of Blood. Do this and the ogres here will be defeated. But first, you must find him.

I have located his bodyguards nearby. Slay them and bring me their heads. With them, we shall lure the Warlord into the open.

passages.title: The Warlord's Guard
passages.text:
You still draw breath, hmm?

Have you dealt with the warlord's underlings?

passages.title: The Warlord's Guard
passages.text: You have done well in this, but do not become proud. This land has dangers far greater than what you have seen here.

passages.title: Pool of Visions
passages.text:
A terrible storm gathers on the horizon, <class>.

I have prepared a ritual. You must consult the pool to see what destiny holds for us all.

passages.title: Pool of Visions
passages.text:
This Iron Tide threatens to sweep over all of Draenor.

The pool has shown you a possible future. This vision of the Frostwolf clan's destruction must not be allowed to come to pass.

You must stop it, <name>.

passages.title: Mulverick's Plight
passages.text:
You were sent here to free me? It seems that makes us allies.

Slavemaster Turgall within the Soostained Mines will certainly have the key to this cage.

While you're in there, do you think you could see which of those spineless taskmasters took my axes?

passages.title: Mulverick's Plight
passages.text: These ogres will be seeing the other side of my axes soon.

passages.title: Mulverick's Plight
passages.text: You have my sincere gratitude, <name>.

passages.title: Northshire Sprint Practice
passages.text:
Welcome to the Irongnome games! For this challenge: run through the arch...
Get to the blue marker...
Get to the green marker...
then return here.

You have all the time you need for this.

passages.title: The Ritual
passages.text:
You are good to have come so quickly. I must ask you to put your lives in danger once more in order to save Kalimdor.

Amnennar's apprentice, Death Speaker Blackthorn, hopes to return his master to the realm of the living! We must quickly make our way atop the Spiral of Thorns and defeat him before the ritual can be completed. We must strike together, only with our combined force can we hope to stop him!

passages.title: The Ritual
passages.text: Quickly <name>, you must stop the ritual!  Amnennar cannot be allowed to return.

passages.title: The Ritual
passages.text: A job well done, <name>. With Amnennar's phylactery now protected by the Red dragonflight we can now rest at ease.

passages.title: Felblood
passages.text:
Fascinating. The doomguard in the courtyard southwest of here have disguised themselves as orcs and do not die when defeated in battle.

You see, they are powerful magical beings, and their essence manifests nearby as a blood creature that revives its body upon reaching it.

I would like to study these essences without dealing with the demons myself. Bring me a few samples, would you?

passages.title: The Secrets of Gorgrond
passages.text:
Our victory today was costly. Too costly. There is no guarantee that we can turn another attack.

We need to know what the Iron Horde is up to, and there is only one place we can go to find out.

Gorgrond.

It is a savage land that few ever return from.

I mean to go there, I mean to find their stronghold at Blackrock, and I mean to learn how we can defeat these vile orcs.

Will you join me, Commander?

passages.title: The Secrets of Gorgrond
passages.text: Welcome to Gorgrond, Commander. We only just arrived ourselves.

passages.title: Deeds Left Undone
passages.text:
In his haste, Ga'nar advanced before this area was secured. He is a matchless warrior, mind you, but his tactics are sometimes costly.

Gol'kosh and his troops were ordered to destroy enemy supplies, but ogres have stolen the oil he needs.

Retrieve the oil and see that their mission is carried out, traveler. Then, if they still live, direct them to rejoin me at the citadel's entrance.

I must see my wounded brothers to safety.

passages.title: Deeds Left Undone
passages.text: Lok'tar, traveler.

passages.title: Deeds Left Undone
passages.text: Gol'kosh has completed his mission, then.

passages.title: We Die Laughing!
passages.text:
Are you here to help or hinder?

This village is being eaten, and we must move quickly to salvage what we can.

Gather the masks of our fallen Laughing Skull brothers and sisters and meet me on the western side of the village.

I will need them if our clan is to rebuild.

passages.title: We Die Laughing!
passages.text: We are the Laughing Skull! We do not flinch in the face of death. We laugh at it.

passages.title: We Die Laughing!
passages.text: These are more than fancy facewear. With a mask and some proper incentive, we can make anyone a Laughing Skull.

passages.title: Eye Candy
passages.text:
You! Get in the fight or get out of our way.

This is no ordinary goren attack. Look over there, a gronnling is sacking our grubhall. That hunchbacked gorebucket bit a chunk out of my lovely Marrow!

Rip the eye out of its forehead and bring it to me.

That should buy me enough time to get her clear of this goren hole.

passages.title: Eye Candy
passages.text: Did you make that thing scream? Did it beg for mercy? Did you kill it before taking its eye? Tell me everything.

passages.title: Eye Candy
passages.text:
These puppets of the magnaron will pay for the skulls they claimed today.

For now, I shall wear this eye across my waist so this fool you have slain may watch as I slowly slaughter his brethren until my dying breath.

passages.title: Steamscar "Reagents"
passages.text:
Now we get to the heart of the matter, heh. Saberon have strong hearts, our shaman find many uses for them.

I will search for the ancient's magic if you get me those hearts. Do we have a deal?

passages.title: Steamscar "Reagents"
passages.text: I will need those hearts <class>.

passages.title: Steamscar "Reagents"
passages.text: These are good strong hearts! You have done well <class> and I will hold my end of the bargain.

passages.title: Plant Pruning
passages.text:
I have a hunting den not far from here where I gather my trophies as well as reagents for the Laughing Skull. Not long ago this giant plant monster charged in from the overgrowth and was killed by several of the giant rock monsters. Since it died smaller plant beasts have sprung up and made a mess of the place.

They have also cut me off from my best source of reagents. Kill them, I will attempt to reach my den and salvage what I can...

passages.title: Plant Pruning
passages.text: Have you cleared a path yet?

passages.title: Plant Pruning
passages.text: They just keep coming back! I would hate to lose this hunting ground. We shall find a way to clear this growth, I swear it.

passages.title: Laying Dionor to Rest
passages.text: You have given me a tremendous gift with this bloom. I can finally send Dionor back to the Overgrowth for good and end this nightmare. All that remains is the ritual... stay and behold something you will never see again in your lifetime...

passages.title: Laying Dionor to Rest
passages.text:
At last it is done.  Dionor has left and his spawn shall follow him in due time.

I grow weary of this conflict and the desire to return to the Overgrowth has left me.

Perhaps I will travel beyond these lands and see what other surprises you little beasts have to share...

passages.title: Decommissioned Mission
passages.text:
Ketya Shrediron,

Your new Iron Shredders are a menace to our own soldiers.

Decommission the prototype and store it in the cave on Talador beach until you've worked out the kinks.

I will send Engineer Draxen to work on it in the meantime.

- Orgrim Doomhammer

passages.title: Decommissioned Mission
passages.text: A prototype Iron Shredder, huh?! I bet we can get this thing working... they didn't have ME to fix it!

passages.title: Gazlowe's Solution
passages.text:
I've identified some high value targets down in the forest below.

When you get near one, you can deploy my solution.

Deploy it and the objectives will be neutralized with great ceremony.

passages.title: Gazlowe's Solution
passages.text: I always love a good explosion.

passages.title: Pieces of Us
passages.text:
When the fires broke out, I took only my daughter's hand before we fled. It was the right decision, of course, but I do long for some of the things we left behind.

I am an artificer, a shaper of crystals and gems. Without my tools I am just another refugee.

Our town records are kept in a memory crystal in the main hall. With it, I can carry forward the knowledge and legacy of Aruuna.

Also, my daughter is terrified - it would be a great comfort for her to hold her favorite doll again.

passages.title: Pieces of Us
passages.text:
These are more than mere objects. They are our livelihood, our past and future, our comfort.

They are pieces of us.

passages.title: Pieces of Us
passages.text: Thank you.

passages.title: Burning Sky
passages.text:
It happened so fast. A white-hot flash of light ignited the nearby woods, followed by terrible winds that swept the flames across Aruuna.

Moments later, arakkoa began descending through the smoke.

I need to get Melani to the Pilgrim's Road. From there we can head for Anchorite's Sojourn and the protection of the vindicators. With the arakkoa roaming the area freely, I fear we'll be run down or worse: taken by the spreading wildfires.

passages.title: Burning Sky
passages.text: Their deaths will not bring back Aruuna, but it does give me comfort to know that some among us can stand against them.

passages.title: Barum's Notes
passages.text:
<This hefty tome contains notes on the refining and shaping of Draenor's natural gems and crystals, including several full-page technical diagrams depicting complex cut patterns.

The most recent pages detail a series of cuts intended to aid the draenei vindicators in battle.>

"...honed to a fine edge, the material can expose weaknesses..."

"when rounded and polished to such a degree, it wards off harmful..."

"...this incredible discovery that a crystal can be attuned to the bearer's vitality!"

passages.title: Barum's Notes
passages.text: Hm, what is that book you have there?

passages.title: Barum's Notes
passages.text:
My notes! In the chaos, I completely forgot about them!

This is my life's work, <name>. I cannot thank you enough.

passages.title: Harbingers of the Void
passages.text:
Our scouts have made a horrifying discovery, <name>.

The souls of the prisoners are being used to summon creatures from the void.

Inside, three beings of darkness already await - the Essence of Shadow, the Essence of Darkness, and the Essence of Anguish.

They must be destroyed immediately, before their power can be unleashed.

passages.title: Harbingers of the Void
passages.text: The souls of innocents were used to birth the foul creatures. All that is depraved, and sick, and twisted in this world, are embodied within them.

passages.title: Harbingers of the Void
passages.text: I knew I could trust this task to you, <name>.

passages.title: Swamplighter Queen
passages.text:
It looks like those plant creatures used some kind of poison when they attacked Gidwin.

It's a powerful concoction to say the least.

If we are going to cure Gidwin we need one more special ingredient. This one might be a bit harder to obtain than the others.

You up to the challenge, <name>?

passages.title: Swamplighter Queen
passages.text: I just wanted to pick some herbs and relax with my boys... I should have stayed in Azeroth.

passages.title: Swamplighter Queen
passages.text: Wow, that was fast! Ok, let's get to it!

passages.title: WANTED: Kuu'rat's Tusks
passages.text:
Posted by: Eremor

A ferocious elekk of unprecedented size has been seen near Gloomshade Grove.

Known to some as the ivory death, she is abnormally aggressive and has already taken the lives of several unwary travelers.

The rangari have as yet been unable to corner this creature. Anyone capable of taking down this beast should exchange proof of her demise to Eremor for a hefty bounty.

passages.title: WANTED: Kuu'rat's Tusks
passages.text: Are you here for the bounty on Kuu'rat?

passages.title: WANTED: Kuu'rat's Tusks
passages.text:
The ivory death is slain? Impressive, traveler.

Thanks to you, we are all safer with Kuu'rat gone. I will share news of this deed with the other villagers.

passages.title: WANTED: Kliaa's Stinger
passages.text:
Posted by: Dyuna

A vicious queen swamplighter has made the northern forests of Shadowmoon its home.

Unfortunately, this poisonous pest terrorizes the forest between Embaari Village and Shattrath. As local traders put their lives at risk, prices of goods will continue to rise.

Anyone who can put an end to the beast should detach its stinger as proof and bring it to Dyuna in Embaari Village. The merchant traders will reward generously.

passages.title: WANTED: Kliaa's Stinger
passages.text: Word around town is you've been hunting Kliaa. Any luck?

passages.title: WANTED: Kliaa's Stinger
passages.text:
By the elders of Karabor... that thing is huge!

Our trade routes will be safe once again. Well... as safe as you can be running through the northern forests.

Well done, <class>!

passages.title: The Plight of the Worgen
passages.text:
King Greymane, my father, has fallen ill! Every day he's worse, losing control over his mind, becoming... feral. He's bedridden in Stormwind as we speak, and he isn't the only one.

Krennan Aranas found what he thought might be the cure in Outland, but it was corrupted beyond recognition. I need to find the cure before he loses every bit of his humanity!

Hemma, one of my guards, is sick as well. I need you to collect some soothpetal flowers and frog eyes. We have to try something.

passages.title: Aruumel's Rest
passages.text:
It is my job to see what others cannot. I keep the memories and read them for others, but I can no longer do so because of my son.

My son turned his back on the light. When he perished I could not stand the thought that his spirit might not be welcomed into Auchindoun.

I interfered and trapped him here. Now he twists and tortures the memories until they cannot be read.

You must do what I cannot bear to do myself. Use this elixir to enter the spirit realm...

...and destroy my son's spirit.

passages.title: Aruumel's Rest
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: Aruumel's Rest
passages.text:
Some memories are better left forgotten. Thank you, <name>.

I will return you to our world.

passages.title: Balance of Power
passages.text:
The Prophet needs to locate the arkonite crystals, but in order to do that, I'll need to fix the projection discs on that platform.

Speak to my assistants around the observatory and bring me an Optical Disc, a Conducting Crystal, and my wrench.

passages.title: Closing the Door
passages.text:
The Shadowmoon orcs are using portals to bring in reinforcements and smuggle away draenei captives.

If we are to have any hope of retaking the village, we must destroy the portals at once.

The only way to do this is to kill the portalmasters who keep the rifts open.

passages.title: Closing the Door
passages.text: Breaking the fabric of space is extremely costly magic. It must rend their very souls.

passages.title: Closing the Door
passages.text:
Wonderful. That should slow down the attack.

Our forces should be able to retake the forest quickly.

passages.title: WANTED: Grondo's Bounty
passages.text:
Grondo, a mad gronn, has been seen roaming the Crackling Plains.

This beast has been killing entire herds of clefthoof and devouring innocent frost wolves. We must destroy this threat before it reaches the Garrison.

passages.title: WANTED: Grondo's Bounty
passages.text: Very good. We don't be needin' a gronn bearin' down on us before we get our defenses all established.

passages.title: The Heart of Auchindoun
passages.text:
A band of Shadow Council orcs stole the Heart of Auchindoun!

The Heart powers all of Auchindoun's defenses. Thankfully we were able to save its core and one of its four pieces.

The warlock O'mogg Blackheart is using Karab'uun, one of the stolen pieces, to power the largest portal in the Burning Front. Return Karab'uun to me.

passages.title: The Heart of Auchindoun
passages.text: I trust you have Karab'uun. I am not known for my patience when the countless souls inside Auchindoun are in danger.

passages.title: The Heart of Auchindoun
passages.text:
<Soulbinder Nyami's lips curl into a smile.>

Well done. Only two pieces remain. I've already dispatched my soulbinders to track them down.

passages.title: Into the Hollow
passages.text:
I've learned that the Shadow Council is using the nearby deathweb spiders' venom to spread fel corruption and augment their forces after their defeat at the Burning Front.

One of my soulbinders saw a dreadlord headed into the eastern mines with Sha'tari, one of the remaining pieces of the Heart of Auchindoun.

I need you to wrest Sha'tari from the dreadlord's quivering corpse and bring it to me, champion.

passages.title: Into the Hollow
passages.text: Did the demon have Sha'tari as we thought?

passages.title: Into the Hollow
passages.text: Just as I suspected. Thank you, <name>. With Sha'tari back in our possession there is only one piece of the Heart left to retrieve.

passages.title: Into the Hollow
passages.text:
I've learned that the Shadow Council is using the nearby deathweb spiders' venom to spread fel corruption and augment their forces after their defeat at the Burning Front.

One of my soulbinders saw a dreadlord headed into the eastern mines with Sha'tari, one of the remaining pieces of the Heart of Auchindoun.

I need you to wrest Sha'tari from the dreadlord's quivering corpse and bring it to me, champion.

passages.title: Into the Hollow
passages.text: Did the foul demon have Sha'tari as we thought?

passages.title: Into the Hollow
passages.text: Just as I suspected. Thank you, <name>. With Sha'tari back in our possession there is only one piece of the Heart left to retrieve.

passages.title: Never Forget
passages.text:
We had to escape Telmor with what few we could save.

Someone disabled Leafshadow's cloaking field; I know not who, but I suspect it had to have been one of our own.

We will retrieve our livelihoods in time, but we cannot risk losing our sacred artifacts.

If you are able, bring Leafshadow, our town registry, and our prayerbook to safety.

passages.title: Never Forget
passages.text: Some things are worth fighting for, <race>. These are such things.

passages.title: Never Forget
passages.text: With these, we can account for our fallen and rebuild. We will persevere.

passages.title: Origin Unknown
passages.text:
For my first field assignment, I would say I'm doing quite well!

I've discovered a strange portal in this cave that has unleashed a number of equally strange void creatures, and there's no clear reason why! Fascinating, isn't it?

Scientific inquiry aside, these things may be benign right now, but at the rate they're pulling energy in that won't last long.

I need you to take them out, send their essences back to... wherever it is they came from, and shut down that portal!

passages.title: [DEPRECATED] Keeping Calm
passages.text:
My husband, one of our shaman, went to the ritual cave just below the village to seek the advice of our ancestors.

Just before you arrived I heard sounds of fighting coming up from there. I fear that one of Ner'zhul's agents has attacked him!

Please, will you go find him and return him home safely?

passages.title: Savage Vengeance
passages.text:
The Thunderlord are a blight <name>.

<Ruk'gan spits in disgust.>

My daughter, Grishna, was killed by those monsters. Only their blood will bring me peace now.

If you would help me then I need you to cause a distraction so I can sneak to a position closer to their camp.

Killing a few of their so called "Iron Thunderguard" would be perfect.

passages.title: Savage Vengeance
passages.text:
You have done well, <class>.

Now before we can continue our assault we need to look for any supplies in the area that could help our fight.

passages.title: Vul'gath's End
passages.text:
Vul'gath's time has come to an end, <name>. My daughter's blood is upon his hands, now his blood will be on ours!

Show no mercy and strike him down!

passages.title: Vul'gath's End
passages.text:
Thank you,<name>.

I wish we could bring him back just to kill him again but I guess this will suffice.

I hope the spirit of my little one will now know peace.

passages.title: Thaelin's Quick Fix
passages.text:
Those orcs sure like to pile things up in one place. That gave me an idea...

I've built this ingenious device for ya! When you get near a target, it'll let you know, and you can deploy it for a big, satisfying, kerBOOM!

passages.title: Thaelin's Quick Fix
passages.text: BOOM! Ahahahahaaa!

passages.title: Thaelin's Quick Fix
passages.text: Nothing like a good explosion to warm the heart.

passages.title: Decommissioned Mission
passages.text:
Ketya Shrediron,

Your new Iron Shredders are a menace to our own soldiers.

Decommission the prototype and store it out of the way until you've worked out the kinks.

I will send Engineer Trak to work on it in the meantime.

- Orgrim Doomhammer

passages.title: Decommissioned Mission
passages.text: A prototype Iron Shredder, huh?! I bet we can get this thing working... they didn't have Thaelin Darkanvil to fix it!

passages.title: Desperate Measures
passages.text:
We've identified the location of Teron'gor's compound, but his forces are already far stronger than anything we've ever faced. We need to gain an edge, and quickly.

The cursed spirits of the Ango'rosh ogres, our ancient enemies, linger in nearby ruins. Go there and gather the Ango'rosh Spellbook and the Grimoire of Binding.

Perform the ritual described within at their altar to lift their curse and seek their aid.

It's a long shot, but we don't have any other options.

passages.title: Desperate Measures
passages.text: Were you able to acquire the aid of the Ango'rosh?

passages.title: Desperate Measures
passages.text:
You radiate the power of the Ango'rosh!

<Restalaan smiles.>

It is time to take this battle to Teron'gor's doorstep.

passages.title: The Mark of Defiance
passages.text:
As you look upon the Frostwolf banner you remember struggles that have led you and the Frostwolves to this point.

Ruk'gan has suffered in his battles with the Thunderlord and would appreciate an extra show of defiance. 

As the banner rustles in the wind you're inspired to mark the foes of the Frostwolf with its standard.

passages.title: The Mark of Defiance
passages.text: Anything to report, <name>?

passages.title: The Mark of Defiance
passages.text:
Good work,<name>!

Seeing Frostwolf banners standing proudly over our crushed foes fills me with pride!

Let them forever fear the wrath of the Frostwolves!

passages.title: WANTED: Kil'uun
passages.text:
I have a bounty set on a bird, commander. Yes, a bird.

The issue is this thing is massive, and it was last sighted a stone's throw away from the Horde base to the south in the forest. The locals call it Kil'uun.

If you'd like to track the creature down and bring back its beak I wager it would fetch a sack or two of gold for your coffers!

passages.title: WANTED: Kil'uun
passages.text: Any luck tracking down that bird, commander?

passages.title: WANTED: Kil'uun
passages.text: I have no idea how you managed to track down the creature so close to the Horde base, but well done sir.

passages.title: WANTED: Hilaani
passages.text:
O'riley wants to thank our peasants for their hard work with a riverbeast dinner.
$I don't want to waste your time asking you to slaughter the things all day, commander. We've gotten reports of a huge riverbeast called Hilaani that would feed the whole fort twice over living in the lake to the south.

If you have a chance to bring cuts of her meat back, the men would be grateful.

passages.title: WANTED: Hilaani
passages.text: Have you had time to kill Hilaani?

passages.title: WANTED: Hilaani
passages.text: Thank you, commander! The peasants will be singing songs about your generosity tomorrow.

passages.title: WANTED: Ra'tok the Hammer
passages.text:
I've got an issue that could use your assistance, commander.

A few of our men spotted an Iron Horde lieutenant wandering in the cliffs near here. We suspect she's directing their forces to strategic ground as they land on the Orunai Coast.

I would feel much better about the safety of this fort if you could take her out.

passages.title: WANTED: Ra'tok the Hammer
passages.text: All hail your glory, commander.

passages.title: WANTED: Ra'tok the Hammer
passages.text:
The Iron Horde have no honor. They disgust me.

We spotted one of their lieutenants wandering the cliffs not far from our base. I believe that she is tracking our movements to prepare for some sort of assault from the Orunai Coast.

I understand you have much to do, commander. If you have the time, I believe it would be beneficial to our position's integrity.

passages.title: WANTED: Ra'tok the Hammer
passages.text: I knew you'd kill her. No Iron Horde is safe from your wrath.

passages.title: WANTED: Hilaani
passages.text:
We need more meat, commander.

I know what you're thinking. What about all of that meat right behind me?

That's the problem. It'll be gone in a day if we're lucky.

There's a riverbeast that lives in the lake to the south. Locals call her Hilaani. Massive, lots of meat.

If you would take down the beast and bring me her meat, your wolves will be better off for it.

passages.title: WANTED: Hilaani
passages.text: Good to see you, commander.

passages.title: WANTED: Hilaani
passages.text: Is that what I think it is? You are too kind, commander!

passages.title: WANTED: Kil'uun
passages.text:
It's that damned bird!

Every few hours, this blasted thing flies right past here, and none of these idiots will stop it.

"It's got the crazy in its eyes," they tell me. Pah!

Commander, this bird will be the end of me. If you see it, could you cut off its stupid head and give it to me?

It'd make me feel better.

passages.title: WANTED: Kil'uun
passages.text: If you decide to kill that creature, I will name my first-born in your honor.

passages.title: WANTED: Kil'uun
passages.text: Praise to <name>! For the Horde!

passages.title: Book Burning
passages.text:
Please, <name>... I don't have much time.

The Shadow Council have allowed themselves to be turned into demons by Teron'gor and his warlocks!

I have reason to believe that the shadowborne dementors are using spells given to them by Gul'dan to empower the demonic orcs. Take their spellbooks and cast them into the fire by me... it will be a pleasant sight to die to.

passages.title: Book Burning
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Book Burning
passages.text: Thank you... kill a couple more for me on your way out, if you can...

passages.title: Mutation Station
passages.text:
Grulk very weak...barely stand.

Grulk not always look this way. Grulk once was orc...Iron Horde make Grulk mutant. Grulk angry at Iron Horde...so Iron Horde lock Grulk in cage...hurt Grulk.

Grulk HATE Iron Horde...Grulk want SMASH them...make them PAY!

Take serum...use on Grulk to make Grulk strong! Help Grulk SMASH Iron Horde!

passages.title: What Must Be Done
passages.text:
I believe we have seen this demonic corruption your friends speak of.

The Mother of Wolves has not been herself lately. Now, her pack has her surrounded.

The wolves are protecting our hunters and will not let them near. They're not likely to stop you, though.

If the alpha mother is infected with this fel-energy, then she must be put down.

You would greatly honor the Frostwolves by returning with her corpse and giving it a proper burial.

passages.title: What Must Be Done
passages.text: Is it done? Does the Mother of Wolves finally rest in peace, <name>?

passages.title: What Must Be Done
passages.text:
Unfortunate that there are those that would pervert such noble creatures.

You have honored their family once more, <name>. They will not forget.

Now it is time to take the fight directly to the Shadow Council.

passages.title: Desecration of the Dead
passages.text:
These filthy warlocks are desecrating the dead in the boneyard!

<The farseer trembles as he fails to keep his composure.>

I WANT THEM DEAD!

Destroy the necrophytes. Destroy their demonic abominations.

passages.title: Desecration of the Dead
passages.text:
For what they've done, it is not enough.

<name>, when you find their base, you salt the earth.

passages.title: Mutation Station
passages.text:
Grulk very weak...barely stand.

Grulk not always look this way. Grulk once was orc...Iron Horde make Grulk mutant. Grulk angry at Iron Horde...so Iron Horde lock Grulk in cage...hurt Grulk.

Grulk HATE Iron Horde...Grulk want SMASH them...make them PAY!

Take serum...use on Grulk to make Grulk strong! Help Grulk SMASH Iron Horde!

passages.title: Ashes Of The Past
passages.text:
The ogres are a plague upon my kind. They summon my kin and force them into servitude, working them without rest till their heat fades away and they crumble into dust.

Their ashes must return to the lava flows so that they can be reborn!

The Ogres keep the dust in pouches on their person thinking it would enhance their strength. Go slay them and recover the ashes of my people!

passages.title: Ashes Of The Past
passages.text: Do you bring me the remains of our fallen?

passages.title: Ashes Of The Past
passages.text: Thank you flesh creature. In the lava the ashes will mix and the cycle shall continue as it has ever since the beginning.

passages.title: Flames Of The Earth
passages.text:
I've searched the depths of the earth and found the means to break the spells that hold my people captive, but it only functions to free one who is completely bound. I would be unable to prevent myself from becoming bound by the same magic.

You, flesh creature, are not of the flames below so their binding spells should not affect you.

Please take my jewel, use its power to free my people!

passages.title: Flames Of The Earth
passages.text: Do my people have their freedom?

passages.title: Flames Of The Earth
passages.text:
The lava already burns bright with the return of my people's freedom!

We will have our revenge upon the ogres for everything they have done to us, this I assure you. But for now, we shall rest.

passages.title: We Must Construct Additional Pylons
passages.text:
We came here to retrieve a reserve pylon to power Auchindoun's defenses, but we've been pinned to this position by the Shadow Council for hours!

I need to get these injured back to Exarch's Refuge, but we still need the backup system!

Please, gather Arkonite crystals and an Arkonite pylon from the tomb and meet me at the refuge as quickly as you can!

passages.title: We Must Construct Additional Pylons
passages.text: Do you have the arkonite pylon and the crystals?

passages.title: We Must Construct Additional Pylons
passages.text: Light bless you, hero! We need to hold out as long as we can so Nyami can track down the remaining power shards. This pylon will help take the load off of our soulpriests.

passages.title: For the Horde!
passages.text:
Without you, none of us would have made it to the shores of my homeland. You will be the one to lead our forces here on Draenor. This is your garrison to found.

I leave it to you to plant the banner and claim this territory. When you are ready, I will have Khadgar open a portal to bring through a few necessary reinforcements.

passages.title: For the Horde!
passages.text: I'm under orders to obey your orders, commander.

passages.title: Establish Your Garrison
passages.text:
It's time for the main event! We've got the materials, we've got the manpower, we've got another thing that starts with "m."

Let's build this thing!

I got a gaggle of assistants up on that ridge to the west.

They should have your personal surveying stand set up by now.

Head on over there and you should be able to watch our progress from it.

passages.title: Establish Your Garrison
passages.text: I'm almost as excited about building this as you are. I want to see if it falls apart!

passages.title: Establish Your Garrison
passages.text: Right! I think we've got this well in hand now. And hardly an explosion to be found!

passages.title: The Portal's Power
passages.text:
This portal is fueled by powers neither mechanical nor arcane.

Look to either side of us, <name>. The screaming souls of slain prisoners are being channeled into the heart of the portal itself.

And they are channeling these souls through the body of Gul'dan.

Find a way into the chamber beneath us, and do whatever it takes to get Gul'dan to stop his channeling. Our last hope rests on you, <name>.

passages.title: The Portal's Power
passages.text: Go now, hero! Lives hang in the balance!

passages.title: The Portal's Power
passages.text:
Gul'dan... free. This was not the victory I'd planned for.

Gul'dan may be loose due to our actions, but I gladly bargain his freedom against the lives of the innocents on the other side of this portal. You made a wise decision, <name>.

passages.title: Blaze of Glory
passages.text:
We can't stay here forever. We NEED to keep moving. But first - we need a distraction.

<Khadgar conjures a small gem.>

This bead should burn anything flammable that you get close to. With your skill, and a bit of luck, you might be able to take the attention of the Bleeding Hollow orcs off our group.

passages.title: Blaze of Glory
passages.text: We cannot hold out here forever, <name>.

passages.title: Blaze of Glory
passages.text:
Out of the frying pan, into the woods.

Take a breath, then get ready, <name>. There's not much time to rest.

passages.title: Altar Altercation
passages.text:
You see that altar down there? There's a magical eye settled at its peak, and I fear our group will not survive if it sees us.

Distract the eye, <name>. Cause a commotion, kill some ritualists, whatever you have to do - just occupy that thing long enough for me to guide the rest of our group past its gaze.

<Khadgar looks over his shoulder.>

Bring that strapping orc with you. The one that's not Thrall.

passages.title: Altar Altercation
passages.text:
<Khadgar looks concerned.>

No - we cannot wait for Ariok. He knew what he was getting into.

His sacrifice cannot go to waste. We must keep moving.

passages.title: A Potential Ally
passages.text:
One of the captured orcs is receiving some... preferential treatment, if you can call it that. While others are tied down and tortured, this one is tied to a stake and burned for the amusement of his captors.

Use this runestone. It should handily deal with the ring of fire that surrounds him.

passages.title: A Potential Ally
passages.text: I owe my life to you, stranger. I offer you and your company my support. Together, we may make it out of this jungle alive.

passages.title: The Shadowmoon Clan
passages.text: We will protect the wounded prisoners and make sure Kargath doesn't get through the rubble. You go ahead and clear the cave, <name>.

passages.title: The Shadowmoon Clan
passages.text:
You fight exceptionally well, <name>... better than I could ever hope to.

With those orcs out of the way, Khadgar and Maraad should now be able to safely guide the rest of our group through the cave.

passages.title: Kaelynara Sunchaser
passages.text:
The focusing crystal is complete, <name>. When you are ready I will use the crystal to shatter Kaelynara's shield.

However, it is unsafe to confront her within the mine. The moment her shield is down I will teleport us to a safe location outside of the Jorune Mine. She will be much easier to deal with when she is far away from the crystal.

Speak with me when you are ready to begin.

passages.title: Kaelynara Sunchaser
passages.text: Are you prepared to end Kaelynara's madness?

passages.title: Kaelynara Sunchaser
passages.text: A wise elder of my order once told me, "True power is the strength to act and the wisdom to know when not to act." May those words and the memory of Kaelynara stay with you on your journey, <name>.

passages.title: Kaelynara Sunchaser
passages.text:
The focusing crystal is complete, <name>. When you are ready I will use the crystal to shatter Kaelynara's shield.

However, it is unsafe to confront her within the mine. The moment her shield is down I will teleport us to a safe location outside of the Jorune Mine. She will be much easier to deal with when she is far away from the crystal.

Speak with me when you are ready to begin.

passages.title: Kaelynara Sunchaser
passages.text: A wise elder of my order once told me, "True power is the strength to act and the wisdom to know when not to act." May those words and the memory of Kaelynara stay with you on your journey, <name>.

passages.title: Build Your Barracks
passages.text:
You are going to want to build your barracks, which you're gonna need to properly bash faces.

The first step is to go find the blueprints and learn 'em. I think I left some blueprints lying around here somewhere.

Next ya gotta pick which plot you want us to build it on. Just point it out on my architect table and we'll get started constructing that thing right away.

passages.title: Build Your Barracks
passages.text: You pick the plot, we'll build the spot!

passages.title: Build Your Barracks
passages.text: This will be a mighty fine barracks, I think. I am sure Warmaster Zog will complain about how it needs to be bigger, and with more spikes. He likes spikes...

passages.title: A Potential Ally
passages.text:
One of the captured draenei is receiving some... preferential treatment, if you can call it that. While others are tied down and tortured, this one is tied to a stake and burned for the orcs' amusement.

Use this runestone. It should handily deal with the ring of fire that surrounds this draenei.

passages.title: A Potential Ally
passages.text: I owe my life to you, stranger. I offer you and your company my support. Together, we may make it out of this jungle alive.

passages.title: Destination: Unknown
passages.text:
Teron'gor and Gul'dan were just leaving through the portal as I arrived... and I... I know I won't be able to defeat them.

I'll hold open the portal as long as I can. It will be up to you to strike the killing blow.

Our fate is in your hands, <name>.

passages.title: Destination: Unknown
passages.text:
Teron'gor and Gul'dan... they slaughtered everyone...

...and then they just... disappeared... into the shadows...

How did they know where to go?

passages.title: Obliterating Ogres
passages.text:
With actual ogre mages present, the Highmaul have been increasing patrols and aggression.

Thinning their ranks will go a long way to deterring the Highmaul from making a comeback in Nagrand.

Head up to my sister Mirana afterwards, she should have more news.

passages.title: Obliterating Ogres
passages.text: Perfect, they will have to concentrate more on base defense now.  Hopefully things will get back to normal out there.

passages.title: Step Three: Prophet!
passages.text: You have arrived in Shadowmoon Valley. It is time to speak with the prophet.

passages.title: Step Three: Prophet!
passages.text:
<The prophet welcomes you with a curious look, then a warm nod.>

So it begins.

passages.title: Gas Guzzlers
passages.text:
<Sir/Ma'am>, to make the best equipment for your arsenal I need not only the best materials, but to use the best techniques.

Over the years I've developed a method to greatly strengthen my metal, but it does require an exotic resource: goren gut gas!

The nearby mine at Kuuro's Claim just came down with an infestation of the things. Could you collect a few samples for the arsenal supplies? Just kill a few goren and give their bodies a good prod with this gas extractor.

passages.title: Gas Guzzlers
passages.text:
Thank you boss, this is just what I needed.

By the way, Goren gas is rather difficult to come by. We should probably hold off on clearing those guys out till we can stockpile enough.

Just a thought.

passages.title: For the Alliance!
passages.text:
We wouldn't have survived Tanaan without your strength, <name>. Many draenei and Alliance alike owe you a great debt.

Before we departed for the Dark Portal, King Wrynn personally recommended that I place you in charge of our operations here in Draenor. After seeing you in action, I'm inclined to agree.

This is your garrison to found. Plant the banner and we'll begin construction immediately, commander.

passages.title: For the Alliance!
passages.text:
So this is Draenor? A bit darker than expected. Still, after building Stormwind, this project should be a walk in the park.

Well then, are you ready to begin, commander?

passages.title: Reglakk's Research
passages.text:
These ogres have been using ancient Titan artifacts to empower a small cadre of specialized units called the Breakers. This Magister Reglakk is here studying ways to improve the process.

Let's put a stop to whatever rituals he has going up on the bluff.

passages.title: Reglakk's Research
passages.text:
That Felbreaker sounded tough! Good thing there's only a small number of them.

Nice job stopping Reglakk, but I'm sure he's safely back in Highmaul. The ogre capital will have to be dealt with sooner rather than later.

passages.title: Creating the Ink
passages.text:
We need a way to create an artificial nexus at your tower.

I know where we can get the conduit to do that, but it's well-guarded. We need to keep our cool and do this the right way.

I have a plan - a scroll of mass teleportation.

The fungal giants and shamblers down below are covered with pustules full of an oily substance. We can use the oil to craft a makeshift ink substitute for the scroll.

passages.title: Creating the Ink
passages.text: The giants are harder to take down, but they will yield more pustules!

passages.title: Creating the Ink
passages.text: This isn't quite what they taught me in Dalaran, but it'll have to do!

passages.title: Gas Guzzlers
passages.text:
To complete my master's designs and to stock up the artillery tower we need to use an exotic resource, namely goren gut gas.

The nearby mine at Kuuro's Claim just came down with an infestation of the things. Could you collect a few samples for me? The stuff is concentrated, so only a few are needed. Just kill one and give its body a good prod with this gas extractor.

passages.title: Gas Guzzlers
passages.text:
Thank you, this is just what I needed.

Goren gas is rather difficult to come by but thankfully we can make this supply go a long way.

passages.title: Creating the Ink
passages.text:
We're going to need a way to create an artificial nexus at your tower.

I know where we can get what we need, but it's heavily protected. We don't have the firepower to just waltz in the front door.

I have a plan - a scroll of mass teleportation.

The fungal giants and spore creatures down below are covered in pustules filled with an oily substance. If we gather enough of the oil I can craft a makeshift ink substitute for the scroll.

passages.title: Creating the Ink
passages.text: The giants have many more pustules than the sporebats, but are much tougher.

passages.title: Creating the Ink
passages.text: These pustules are sizzling with energy. They'll do nicely.

passages.title: Professional Processing
The Rise of Aku'mai
passages.text: We barely escaped the Twilight's Hammer sacrificial altar, but there are others who need help deeper within these caves. If these cultists complete their blood ritual, they will unleash Aku'mai the Devourer onto the world. You cannot let this happen.

passages.title: The Rise of Aku'mai
passages.text: Hurry, <name>! Aku'mai must be stopped before he devours our world!

passages.title: The Rise of Aku'mai
passages.text: That was incredible, <name>! The Old Gods will think twice before trying to crawl out of their pit again.

passages.title: The Rise of Aku'mai
passages.text: We barely escaped de Twilight's Hammer sacrificial altar, but others be needin' help deeper in. If de blood ritual be complete, they be unleashin' Aku'mai da Devourer. Don let this be happenin', mon.

passages.title: The Rise of Aku'mai
passages.text: Move, <name>! Aku'mai be wantin' to devour de world!

passages.title: The Rise of Aku'mai
passages.text: Dat was amazin', <name>! De Old Gods be thinkin' twice before tryin' to take anudder bite outta you, mon.

passages.title: Getting Gladiators
passages.text:
When we fled Stonemaul, we had to leave others behind.

If we try to rescue them and are recognized, the ogres will know our purpose, and the first thing they will do is kill our friends.

The ogres do not know you, which might give you a fighting chance.

Enter Stonemaul, find the other gladiators, and release them from their bonds. Do this and you will have our loyalty.

passages.title: Getting Gladiators
passages.text: Thank you, strange one. Now we are free to split that chieftain Kor'gall wide open!

passages.title: The Axe of Kor'gall
passages.text:
Time for vengeance! We are going to kill Kor'gall and you are going to take his axe.

Shatter this feeble barrier, follow the bridge beyond until you reach the chieftain's throne.

You freed us, so the honor of first blood is yours. Strike the first blow and we will join you in the cutting.

passages.title: The Axe of Kor'gall
passages.text: Kor'gall has ruled uncontested for far too long.

passages.title: The Axe of Kor'gall
passages.text: This blade has caused enough pain and suffering for one lifetime. We shall see to it that it is properly disposed of.

passages.title: Mo'mor Might Know
passages.text:
We know the Warsong packleader that attacked the caravan is in Telaar. She has the blueprints.

We don't know where she is down there, but there's one who might.

Vindicator Mo'mor was last seen alive, but taken prisoner. If he's still alive, he might know where the blueprints are.

passages.title: Mo'mor Might Know
passages.text: Please forgive me. I'm in no condition to stand, commander.

passages.title: The Shadowmoon Clan
passages.text: We will protect the wounded prisoners and make sure Kargath doesn't get through the rubble. You go ahead and clear the cave, <name>.

passages.title: The Shadowmoon Clan
passages.text:
You fight exceptionally well, <name>... better than I could ever hope to.

With those orcs out of the way, Khadgar and Maraad should now be able to safely guide the rest of our group through the cave.

passages.title: Shields Down!
passages.text:
Did you hear that? They got the shield up. There'll be no getting into Telaar now.

You must get that shield down. The only way to do it is to destroy the Arkonite crystal.

Don't worry about me. You're going to kill two birds with one stone; Packleader Kargora is the one who stole your blueprints.

passages.title: Shields Down!
passages.text: Good news?

passages.title: Shields Down!
passages.text:
Perfect! You retrieved the blueprints.

There's only one thing left to do.

passages.title: A Choice to Make
passages.text:
We're just about ready to go here. All that's needed now is for you to make your choice.

Take a look at the blueprints on the drafting table.

Are we going to construct a corral or a tankworks?

passages.title: A Choice to Make
passages.text:
This is a momentous occasion, commander. I'll have Thaelin and his people get to work right away.

You'll see; this decision is going to be critical in our efforts against the Warsong.

passages.title: Migrant Workers
passages.text:
<name>, more recruits arrive at your garrison every hour. We will soon run out of food.

I have made contact with Exarch Akama in hopes of securing rations from Elodor, the breadbasket of this valley. He has agreed, provided we supply labor for the harvest. Everyone wins.

If you agree with my plan, speak with Foreman Zipfizzle here in the courtyard - he has gathered together available laborers. Akama and I will escort them and meet you at Elodor, far to the east!

passages.title: Migrant Workers
passages.text: Where's the rest of the caravan?

passages.title: Migrant Workers
passages.text:
You made it!

But... one of our wagons didn't. Have you seen Maraad? He's still out there somewhere.

passages.title: Circle the Wagon
passages.text:
One of our wagons fell behind, and disappeared somewhere in the woods to the northwest. Vindicator Maraad and several of your workers are stranded out there.

Find them and bring them back!

passages.title: Circle the Wagon
passages.text: Did you find them? Check the woods to the northwest. If I know Maraad, he probably tried to take the shelter of a hill.

passages.title: Circle the Wagon
passages.text:
I am keeping the sickles. They remind me of a lesson so many of us draenei forget - that the Light lives in every farmer as much as in any priest.

You fight well, and I am pleased to call you friend. Your laborers will be safe here in Elodor. If you are not convinced, speak to Exarch Hataaru here. His devices secure all the draenei strongholds.

passages.title: Invisible Ramparts
passages.text:
Exarch Akama is too cautious, but we shouldn't ignore a threat from the Shadowmoon clan. It is good you are here!

Since we arrived on Draenor I have dedicated myself to recreating the technology we left behind. This large structure here is a defense ward. It should counter a Shadowmoon advance - provided we power it up.

I have prepared resonance crystals at my workshop to the south. Carry one crystal at a time to the three pylons that surround the ward, then activate the control panel nearby!

passages.title: Invisible Ramparts
passages.text: <The console thrums with energy. You can't interpret anything on the display, but some of the lights are still blinking needily.>

passages.title: Invisible Ramparts
passages.text:
The console thrums with energy and lights up as you draw near, as though sensing your presence. Simply touching the main panel brings the defense crystal to life outside.

If this is the kind of technology Hataaru was able to cobble together from spare parts, you can only imagine the splendor of the world he came from.

passages.title: Fun with Fungus
passages.text:
It is our mission as rangari to explore and understand this world. Around you is the Umberfen. Many draenei lost their lives when we first discovered this place. The volatile spores burst whenever anyone approaches.

But we watched... and we learned.

Around the swamp you'll notice "Shimmershrooms," distinguished by their orange glowcaps. Their dust will make you invisible to the volatile spores. Grab the spores - gently! - and bring them to me.

We will forge this savage world into a weapon.

passages.title: Fun with Fungus
passages.text: Remember, unless you are covered in shimmershroom dust, the spores will explode as soon as you get near.

passages.title: Fun with Fungus
passages.text:
Careful with those... hand them here. Wonderful!

I will have my rangari bury these around the perimeter of Elodor. If the Shadowmoon orcs dare attack us again, they are in for a nasty surprise!

Draenor is a hostile world, but if we take the time to learn and understand it, we can turn it to our advantage.

I will finish up here and meet with the Exarch Council shortly. I will be sure to back your proposal.

passages.title: Engorged Goren
passages.text:
You must be the <class> that so impressed Exarch Hataaru. Can you help?

The Elodor Dig just behind me is overrun by strange stone creatures. These so-called goren actually devour minerals, metabolize them, and grow crystalline structures from their arms and back. Like most of the wildlife on this world, they completely baffle us.

Please slay as many as you can and gather their crystal scales for me. You'll be protecting our earthworkers and aiding our research at the same time.

passages.title: Engorged Goren
passages.text: What's the status inside the dig?

passages.title: Engorged Goren
passages.text:
<The artificer withdraws a loop and peers intently at the scales you've brought him.>

Unreal. The crystalline matrix is flawless, as if produced from one of our forges on Argus.

I wish we could hook up these creatures to our machinery... but I suspect the Exarch would take issue with that.

Thank you for your help!

passages.title: Exarch Maladaar
passages.text:
The council is almost assembled: Othaar, myself, Hataaru and Naielle are ready. Only Exarch Maladaar remains. He has not been himself since he returned from his capture at the hands of the Iron Horde... but Vindicator Maraad was able to track him down.

Find Maladaar at the Fey Landing, just south of the town center.

passages.title: Exarch Maladaar
passages.text:
<name>, my Alliance friend from Tanaan! I have not forgotten my debt to you.

I will do everything in my power to convince the council to support you in every way possible. However...

I have grave concerns about our safety here.

passages.title: Friend of the Exarchs
passages.text:
Only three members remain of the Exarch Council, but we are all deeply indebted to you. The vote is unanimous: Your Alliance will have our full support on Draenor.

We are also going to place a draenei representative under your direct command. Three potential candidates are here in the courtyard. Speak to them and choose who you want - we will dispatch him or her immediately to your garrison!

passages.title: Friend of the Exarchs
passages.text: Who are you going to pick, <name>?

passages.title: Friend of the Exarchs
passages.text:
An excellent choice! We'll send your pick directly to your garrison to help with any missions you encounter.

Now, about those supplies you requested...

passages.title: Speaker for the Dead
passages.text:
This was a betrayal from within. There's no other explanation for it. None of the Exarchs trust each other now - especially me. But Othaar and Akama can damn their laws. We've got to rout out the traitor and the only way to do it is to speak to the corpse!

Join me just outside the Altar of Sha'tar atop the eastern cliffs. Soulbinder Nyami and I will perform an exorcism to save Hataaru's immortal soul... and maybe learn who did this to him.

Do you trust me, <name>?

passages.title: Speaker for the Dead
passages.text: Exarch Hataaru didn't deserve to die that way. Not like this.

passages.title: Speaker for the Dead
passages.text:
One of the five Exarchs is dead. Another is a traitor. Dark times.

We will end this here and now. Can I count on you for one final task?

passages.title: The Sting
passages.text:
The exarchs seem to trust you, <class>. Are you venturing into the Umbrafen?

The Sporebats in this area are usually docile, but something's got them all riled up. When they attack, their stingers wrap around exposed limbs. I've seen them tear through reinforced leather like it was paper. How do they work, I wonder?

Could you bring me a pristine sporebat stinger? I'd love to study it.

passages.title: The Sting
passages.text: Most draenei avoid the Umbrafen, but we rangari seem drawn to the most dangerous places - that's where you really learn how the world works.

passages.title: The Sting
passages.text:
Would you look at that - the entire tentacle is barbed. Uggh. No wonder the wounds they inflict tend to get infected. We could learn something from this. I wonder if rangari explorers should start equipping themselves with whips?

Thank you, <name>. This Alliance that you come from must be quite the collection of heroes!

passages.title: Warning the Exarchs
passages.text:
You set the book ablaze, but not before noting its contents. The demonic tome was dedicated to enchanting weapons with fel energy. It looked as though the goal was to ensnare the victim's soul.

The Exarchs must be warned that traitors are among them! The Council should be meeting now just up the hill to the east.

passages.title: Warning the Exarchs
passages.text:
Dead! Exarch Hataaru is dead! His body was discovered moments ago, stabbed in the back. The weapon that killed him was fel in origin. Tell me everything you know.

<Maladaar nods as you describe what you found.>

Yes. The traitors wanted to capture Hataaru's soul. Someone wants something he knows, dead or alive... We must act at once.

passages.title: The Traitor's True Name
passages.text:
We must give the traitor no place to hide. I have a focusing lens that will illuminate cloaked fel energy. If it were placed on a high point, it could act like a beacon, lighting up anyone in town who reeks of the fel taint.

There is a prayer circle atop the Exarch's Rise to the north that will serve our purpose. Plant the focusing lens, <name>. If you reveal anything, deal with it. Then meet me below.

passages.title: The Traitor's True Name
passages.text: What happened up there?

passages.title: The Traitor's True Name
passages.text:
<The Exarch listens to your tale, his face contorting into concern, grief, and finally anger.>

So Othaar has lost his way. "Socrethar" he calls himself now. At last we have our answer. I fear my capture at the hands of the Iron Horde was his doing. There may be other traitors amongst us - I must hurry back to Auchindoun and make sure we are safe.

In the meantime, I believe the Exarchs owe you a decision...

passages.title: Send Them Running
passages.text:
Your scouts have located the saberon's alpha male just outside our gates!

Commander, I believe that dispatching this target will send any of these remaining vermin running back to their caves.

I do not wish to ask more of you, but you are the only one capable of this task, <sir/ma'am>.

passages.title: Send Them Running
passages.text: Is the alpha male dispatched?

passages.title: Send Them Running
passages.text: For <name>! For the Horde!

passages.title: Not In Your House
passages.text:
<Sir/Madame>, we have located the saberon's alpha male just outside our gates!

We believe that slaying him will send any remaining saberon running with their tails between their legs, but the beast is positively massive!

I do not wish to call upon you once more, but you are the only one capable of this task.

passages.title: Not In Your House
passages.text: Victory! For the Alliance!

passages.title: What We Got
passages.text:
Every fortress needs three things.

One: peons! Find Skaggit and have him get our peons back to work.

Two: building materials. I had the peons set up a cache for you where they will store resources they create while you are away. You should check it out.

And three: raw experienced muscle! Constructing buildings in a garrison can take some time but I think we can speed up your first building by hiring Skaggit's recently promoted Senior Peon II. Find him and tell him I sent ya.

passages.title: What We Got
passages.text: If buildin' a stronghold were easy, everybody'd be doin' it.

passages.title: What We Got
passages.text: Yeah, that's the stuff. Lumber, stone, peons, more peons. It's like we are building you a stronghold or something.

passages.title: Last of the Talonpriests
passages.text:
Talonpriests live among us in secret, guarding the rites of the Talon King's return.

The Adherent proclamation you acquired in Skettis revealed two of them living in the Shadowglade to the north. Orcs have moved into the region, and the Adherent's beam weapon left Veil Akraz a smoking crater.

As you can see, my people are beset by enemies on all sides.

Talonpriest Ishaal survived and is in hiding. Drink this elixir near his hut to peer into the shadows and make contact with him.

passages.title: Last of the Talonpriests
passages.text:
Hm, not what I was expecting when I heard that Iskar was sending help.

No matter. You'll have to do.

passages.title: Behind the Veil
passages.text:
Soon after the orcs swept in, Veil Akraz was laid to waste by a beam of light from Skyreach.

<Ishaal's eyes glass over as he peers into his orb.>

It seems they missed their true target. Zellek is still there, hiding in the realm of shadow.

And... someone else as well. The orc assassin who used my orb.

Take this. Drink it in Veil Akraz and find Zellek.

Oh, and be careful. It's a little more potent than the last one. You'll see...

passages.title: Behind the Veil
passages.text:
Well, you are not stabbing me yet.

That is a good sign.

passages.title: Forbidden Love
passages.text:
My son, Kral'za, is beyond stubborn. 

After we split from the Shadowmoon Clan he refused to let go of his relationship with a young Shadowmoon orc.

I forbid him to see her anymore. He ran off earlier today and has not returned. 

I don't trust Dol'mak. Like the other Shadowmoon orcs she continues to dabble in the void.

passages.title: Forbidden Love
passages.text: Aka'Magosh, <class>. I knew that void witch was no good.

passages.title: To Even the Odds
passages.text: [TEMP] The Shattered Hand orcs are using their prisoners as living training dummies. Let's even the odds and give them some weapons.

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text:
The blade is not the only important item a blademaster carries.

Once he has passed his final tests in the Masters' Caverns, the blademaster is given the honor of wearing the Burning Blade's banner.

When my petition to reclaim my rightful place with the clan fell upon deaf and craven ears, I was stripped of that honor.

No doubt, my banner has been stored away somewhere in Hallvalor. They'll give it to some other aspiring blademaster if they don't burn it first.

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text: Do you have my banner?

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text:
I don't expect you to understand the importance of what you've done.

Perhaps one day you will.

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text:
The Gordunni were given copies of my blades as a gift from the Iron Horde. But what do they use them for? Toothpicks!

Sure the blades are low grade copies but it's still MY design and I can't stand to think of them in those ogre hands for a moment longer!

<Sir/Ma'am>, While we are in here can you do me a favor and get those blades out of their hands!

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text: Were you able to get all of my blades back?

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text: Thank you, commander. With this another stain on my honor has been removed.

passages.title: Challenge of the Masters
passages.text:
The time has come to challenge the Burning Blade masters.

Go to the back of the cavern. There you will find the challenge ring and the masters watching over it from above.

Pull the blade from the middle of the ring to issue your challenge. My clan values honor above all else and will respect your claim to trial by combat.

As reward, you will be allowed to walk away with your blueprints and your life. Or, you will be dead.

passages.title: Challenge of the Masters
passages.text: Do you have the garrison blueprints, commander?

passages.title: Challenge of the Masters
passages.text:
The garrison blueprints. Outstanding.

There's only one thing left to do.

passages.title: The Lord of the Gordunni
passages.text:
Witch Lord Morkurk is the leader of the Gordunni. He's the one that set up the Iron Horde trade and, even worse, my former boss gave him one of my best maces!

We got to get my mace back! I mean... we need to kill him to secure the jovite for your arsenal!

Morkurk is an accomplished mage so you better be prepared. Here, take the rocket pack and use it if you need to dodge an attack quickly or something.

Also, if you happen to find my mace I'd like to get it back.

passages.title: The Lord of the Gordunni
passages.text: Do you have my mace?

passages.title: The Lord of the Gordunni
passages.text:
Fine work commander! Your combat skills are clearly second to none. I am honored to be your armorer!

Let's get back to the outpost so we can take stock of our new inventory. I saved a few flares to call us in a ride back.

passages.title: Loola's Lost Love
passages.text:
Oh it was horrible.

My husband and I were fishing in the marsh, I fell asleep and when I woke up he had been turned into a toad!

I'm sure it was one of those Shadowmoon orcs I hear so much about.

He jumped into the muddy waters before I could catch him.

Will you help me find my lost love, <class>?

passages.title: Loola's Lost Love
passages.text: Hmm... I'm sure one of these toads is my husband.

passages.title: Earth, Wind and Fire...and Water
passages.text:
The Elemental Plateau has become unstable, and so the cycle of rebirth must begin.

It is a natural part of our life cycle that impurities are accumulated in the elemental body over time.

When enough contamination has taken place, an elemental will become unstable and in some cases volatile.

A necessary part of rebirth is pure, living essence which can be found atop the Elemental Plateau, as well as in the body of an elemental spirit.

Return to me with the essence and we shall begin the rebirth.

passages.title: Earth, Wind and Fire...and Water
passages.text: Bring to me the living essences of the elements, that I may plant the seeds of rebirth.

passages.title: Earth, Wind and Fire...and Water
passages.text:
You have done well.

Although the Elemental Plateau is no longer stable, the cycle of rebirth will soon take place and the elements will be born anew.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text:
It's time to fight fire with fire.

We have Morkurk cornered. His protections gone. Use the scroll once you engage Morkurk...

...and enjoy the fireworks.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text: Ogres. It's always ogres.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text:
That's what we were after.

Let's get out of here!

passages.title: A Choice to Make
passages.text:
We're ready to start building. All that we need is for you to make a choice.

The blueprints are on the drafting table. Take a look.

Then, let me know if we're going to construct a corral or a tankworks.

passages.title: A Choice to Make
passages.text:
This is a momentous occasion, commander. Thazz'ril and his peons will get to work right away.

You'll see; this decision is going to be critical in our efforts against the Warsong.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text:
We have Morkurk cornered. He's all ours now. Use the scroll once you engage Morkurk...

...and enjoy the blizzard of your forces raining down on his head.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text: It's all come down to this moment.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text: Looks like Morkurk was no match for the two of us, huh?

passages.title: The Blessing of Samedi
passages.text:
Three of mah shadow huntas come here wit' me. De Warsong kill dem.

We need ta help dey souls move on. Jus' in case ya find dem first, use dis on dere bodies.

It send dere souls ta Samedi, Loa of de Grave.

passages.title: The Blessing of Samedi
passages.text:
Dey movin' onta a betta place. Samedi be sendin' dem on all dey missions now.

Dank ya, <name>.

passages.title: Shields Down!
passages.text:
De time has come, commanda. Packleader Kargora an' de Arkonite Shield no longa protected.

We need ta kill her an' destroy de shield crystal.

passages.title: Shields Down!
passages.text:
I'm sorry to hear about Kajassa's shadow hunters, but we couldn't afford to let the Warsong have Telaar.

With the death of Kargora and her pack, we're one step closer to the invasion of the Warsong's home, Grommashar.

One step close to justice.

passages.title: Cult of the Ravenspeakers
passages.text:
These outcasts are not the only cursed arakkoa holding their ground in Arak.

A curious cult has formed in worship of Ka'alu, my consort and the keeper of my brood. They are considered to be quite... odd.

Regardless, the outcasts will need their help. Without the wings of the ravens, Iskar can never take his fight to the spires.

Take this feather and place it in the offering basket south of here. The so-called "Ravenspeakers" will surely take notice.

passages.title: Cult of the Ravenspeakers
passages.text:
Ah, you come to learn the truth of things.

We will need to test your dedication first, yes!

passages.title: Polishing the Iron Throne
passages.text:
These stinking Blackrock cowards think they're humiliating me.

They're just making me angrier.

Overseer Gotrigg, in the hut over there, carries my shackle key. If I'm going to get out of there, I'm going to need that key. Then... vengeance can begin.

passages.title: Polishing the Iron Throne
passages.text: You'll have to pry that key out of his cold, ugly hand.

passages.title: Polishing the Iron Throne
passages.text:
<Ga'nar works his neck out of the shackle.>

Much better.

passages.title: The Debt We Share
passages.text:
These mortal shells that we call bodies are not ours to keep. The body is a gift of earth that must one day be returned from whence it came.

The time has come for this body to return to the elements.

Know that you have lifted the weight from an old heart, <name>. As I pass on from this realm, I do so without regret. I have fought on behalf of my people and my land, I have served the elements, and I have loved.

It would honor me if you would stay during these final moments, <class>.

passages.title: The Debt We Share
passages.text: When I face my ancestors in the realm of spirits I will do so without shame or fear, for I have lived an honorable life.

passages.title: The Debt We Share
passages.text:
Gar'rok was a loyal keeper and a true friend. He will be missed, but so is the cycle of life on this world.

In time we will call a new keeper of the elements, and he will serve us as Gar'rok did before him.

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text:
The blade is not the only important item a blademaster carries.

Once he has passed his final tests in the Masters' Caverns, the blademaster is given the honor of wearing the Burning Blade's banner.

When my petition to reclaim my rightful place with the clan fell upon deaf and craven ears, I was stripped of that honor.

No doubt, my banner has been stored away somewhere in Hallvalor. They'll give it to some other aspiring blademaster if they don't burn it first.

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text: Do you have my banner?

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text:
I don't expect you to understand the importance of what you've done.

Perhaps one day you will.

passages.title: Challenge of the Masters
passages.text:
The time has come to challenge the Burning Blade masters.

Go to the back of the cavern. There you will find the challenge ring and the masters watching over it from above.

Pull the blade from the middle of the ring to issue your challenge. My clan values honor above all else and will respect your claim to trial by combat.

As reward, you will be allowed to walk away with your life. Or, you will be dead.

passages.title: Challenge of the Masters
passages.text:
A great victory over the Burning Blade!

This new Warlord Azuka Bladefury sounds formidable. We'll have to keep an eye on her and her blademasters.

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text:
The Gordunni have plagued the people of Shattrath ever since the city was founded. Over time they amassed quite a hoard of weapons they captured from our defenders in raids.

Getting these weapons in the hands of our soldiers would be practical and I personally would like to get them out of the hands of the ogres.

While we are in here can you do me a favor and gather up any of those weapons you come across.

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text: Were you able to find any weapons?

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text: Thank you, commander. With this a great dishonor on the legacy of Shattrath has been removed.

passages.title: The Lord of the Gordunni
passages.text:
Witch Lord Morkurk is the leader of the Gordunni. We need to kill him to secure the jovite for use in our artillery tower.

Morkurk is an accomplished mage so you better be prepared. Here, take the rocket pack and use it if you need to avoid any of his deadly magic.

Archenon poros!

passages.title: The Lord of the Gordunni
passages.text:
Fine work commander! Your combat skills are clearly second to none. I am honored to be your armorer!

Let's get back to the outpost so we can take stock of our new inventory. I saved a few flares to call us in a ride back.

passages.title: To the... Rescue?
passages.text:
The Parchment of Dust reads: "Put the featherless against one another so that our claws remain unsullied!" How wise the high Ravenspeaker is to foresee this day.

There is a great beast on the hillside to the west by the name of Stonescale. It has abducted one of the flock and despite our many attempts we have been unable to defeat it. 

Go, prove yourself by slaying the beast and rescuing Tillik! Fulfill your destiny in the name of the Raven Mother!

passages.title: To the... Rescue?
passages.text: Tillik's disappearance caused great sadness to the Flock.

passages.title: To the... Rescue?
passages.text:
Tillik! Dear friend I'm so glad you have returned! All of the acolytes missed your witty banter after the evening chants.

<Iktis looks back towards you.>

Yes, now your great test is done. You have fulfilled the requirements of The Parchment of Dust!

passages.title: Talon Watch
passages.text:
By now you must be wondering about all of this curse business. What could distort a majestic arakkoa into... well, into this?
