passages.title: Survey Ashran
passages.text: You have the spirit of a true explorer, <name>.

passages.title: The Road of Glory
passages.text:
THE ALLIANCE! <Stomps feet> THEY NEED TO BE REMOVED FROM ASHRAN IMMEDIATELY! MARCH INTO THE ROAD OF GLORY AND SLAY AS MANY AS YOU CAN! 

NOW!

passages.title: The Road of Glory
passages.text: ONLY FIVE? UGH. TAKE THIS REWARD AND GET BACK OUT THERE.

passages.title: Into The Wilderness
passages.text:
YOU KNOW WHAT'S BETTER THAN KILLING ALLIANCE SCUM IN THE ROAD OF GLORY?

KILLING THEM EVERYWHERE ELSE. <Laughs>

GO INTO THE OUTSKIRTS OF ASHRAN AND SLAY ANY ALLIANCE MEMBER. BRING ME BACK SCRAPS OF THEIR DISGUSTING ARMOR AS PROOF. THE BLOODIER THE BETTER.

passages.title: Into The Wilderness
passages.text: SHOW ME THE ARMOR SCRAPS!

passages.title: Into The Wilderness
passages.text: YES... YES! <Takes a deep whiff of the armor scrap> MMMM,  ITS FRESH!

passages.title: The Restless Spirit
passages.text:
This hammer was once used to craft magnificent weapons for my Frostwolf brothers and sisters.

When I was taken prisoner by the Thunderlords, however, I refused to wield it. How could I craft weapons to be used against my own people?

It saddens me to see that it has been damaged and abused.

I wished to one day pass it down to Kugra, but now, her anger prevents her from even visiting my grave.

Please adventurer, can you help me repair my hammer and seek revenge on those that caused this?

For Kugra....

passages.title: The Restless Spirit
passages.text: So, it is done?

passages.title: The Restless Spirit
passages.text: <name>, thank you for avenging my death.

passages.title: Breaking into the Trap Game
passages.text:
When we came through the portal, we weren't able to bring any of our animals with us. For us to produce leather and furs, we'll need to trap some of the native beasts and bring them back here.

We can get a load of leather from the elekk, or furs from the talbuk, right here in Shadowmoon.

Take this iron trap and use it on a wounded adult talbuk or elekk, then bring the trap on back here and we'll start a work order.

passages.title: Breaking into the Trap Game
passages.text: Have you tried your hand at trapping yet?

passages.title: Breaking into the Trap Game
passages.text:
Great job, commander! We'll have your leather or fur ready in no time.

Now that you know how to use the trap, it will be available for your use at any time. We can only handle so many beasts in the barn at one time, though, so make sure you've got room before you start trapping!

passages.title: Feeding An Army
passages.text:
We've had a chance to work with these beasts for a while now, and that's allowed us to develop a brand-new trap for you to try out. It should be much sturdier than the last one!

Mind giving 'er a run, commander? The Improved Iron Trap will let you capture some of the meatiest wildlife, like the big boars and riverbeasts out in Gorgrond. We'll be able to turn them into some tasty steaks.

passages.title: Feeding An Army
passages.text: Did ya try the trap out yet?

passages.title: Feeding An Army
passages.text: Great work, commander! We'll get to grillin' up those steaks right away. I can already smell them!

passages.title: Bigger Trap, Better Rewards
passages.text:
Good news, commander! With the materials we've gathered here in Draenor, we've been able to construct a trap strong enough to immobilize even the mightiest beast!

Why don't you head on out to Nagrand and give it a try? Word has it that the western plains are home to some of the most magnificent beasts this side of Crystal Lake.

I'm going to warn you, though, these beasts are tough. You may want to bring some friends along.

passages.title: Bigger Trap, Better Rewards
passages.text: Well? How'd it go?

passages.title: Bigger Trap, Better Rewards
passages.text:
That must have been quite a fight, commander!

The materials we obtain from beasts of this magnitude will last us for quite a while.

passages.title: The Search For Research
passages.text:
My research notes are missing!

They must have gone missing during the podling attack on the research station. All of my work will be lost if they are not found!

Come to think of it, I'm also missing my expedition supply bag, as well as my anti-fungal boots....

How can I do biological research without my equipment?!

No... this will not do at all.

Please, go and search the Zangar Shore for my missing belongings so that I may continue my fungal research!

passages.title: The Search For Research
passages.text: Have you retrieved my missing belongings?

passages.title: The Search For Research
passages.text:
Ah! I see you have my research with you... and what's this? You also have my supply bag and the anti-fungal boots!

Spectacular! I now have the tools I need to continue my research into the Zangar fungal strain....

passages.title: Victory is Within Reach
passages.text:
We have dealt a crippling blow to the Adherents, but our fight is not yet finished.

Gather your allies and prepare for the final siege on Skyreach!

"Shadows gather when the raven swallows the day.

Burning sky is extinguished as black wings fold gently about the heavens.

Rest, my children, rest. For even the sun must sleep."

This was Rukhmar's lullaby, sung by her to the first arakkoa. My, how we've lost our way.

passages.title: Victory is Within Reach
passages.text: Let us finish what we have started.

passages.title: Victory is Within Reach
passages.text: Perhaps there is now hope for a brighter future. I can only hope some of those in Skyreach have been awakened.

passages.title: Primal Fury
passages.text:
It looks like this is it, commander.

We must stop the Iron Horde at all costs. I have sent stormcrows to your garrison, and called for Bodrick Grey to deploy your troops to the Gates of Tanaan at once.

By the time you get to northern Talador, he should be waiting for you... with an entire army.

There is no time to delay.

passages.title: Primal Fury
passages.text:
Your feats seem to know no limits, <name>. Today, our garrison forces have struck a terrible blow to Warchief Hellscream and the Iron Horde.

However, he is not defeated so easily. If anything, his hunger for vengeance will grow.

We must destroy the root of his operations in Tanaan Jungle, but first, there is much preparation to be done.

Until then, bask in the glow of our momentous victory.

passages.title: UNUSED
passages.text:
When we came through the portal, we weren't able to bring any of our animals with us. For us to produce meat, leather, and furs, we'll need to trap some of the native beasts and bring them back here.

I've heard word that the best grazing grounds are out in Nagrand. We can get a load of meat from the elekk, leather from the clefthooves, or furs from the talbuk.

Take this iron trap and use it on a wounded adult beast, we'll haul it on back here and get to work.

passages.title: Feeding An Army
passages.text:
We've had a chance to work with these beasts for a while now, and that's allowed us to develop a brand-new trap for you to try out. It should be much sturdier than the last one.

The Improved Iron Trap will let you capture some of the meatiest beasts on Draenor. You will find that a single riverbeast or boar from Gorgrond can feed many warriors.

Trap one and bring it back, and we will cook you a savage meal.

passages.title: Feeding An Army
passages.text: Did you try the trap out yet?

passages.title: Feeding An Army
passages.text: Ah, so the trap held! I can smell the meat already. This will make a great feast for our warriors!

passages.title: Breaking into the Trap Game
passages.text:
When we came through the portal, we weren't able to bring any of our animals with us. For us to produce leather and furs, we'll need to trap some of the native beasts and bring them back here.

Although the plains are frozen, there are many clefthooves and wolves in Frostfire. We can gather leather from the clefthooves, or furs from the wolves.

Take this iron trap and use it on a wounded adult beast. Bring the trapped creature back to us, and we will begin our work.

passages.title: Breaking into the Trap Game
passages.text: Have you tried your hand at trapping yet?

passages.title: Breaking into the Trap Game
passages.text:
Very good. We will have your leather or fur ready soon.

Now that you know how to use the trap, it will be available for your use at any time. We can only handle so many beasts in the barn at one time, though. I would not advise taking more from the land than necessary.

passages.title: Bigger Trap, Better Rewards
passages.text:
Ah, commander, it is good to see you again. With the materials we have gathered here in Draenor, we have been able to construct a trap strong enough to immobilize even the mightiest beast.

These enormous creatures can be found on the western side of Nagrand, among the most fertile plains.

A word of warning: these beasts are great and powerful. You may want to bring some friends along.

passages.title: Bigger Trap, Better Rewards
passages.text: Did you manage to break one of the great beasts?

passages.title: Bigger Trap, Better Rewards
passages.text:
Blood and thunder, that must have been quite a battle!

The materials we obtain from beasts of this magnitude will last us for quite a while.

passages.title: Field Trial
passages.text:
Look, I didn't tell Kimzee about this because I don't want to hurt her feelings, I chose not to leave Pinchwhistle Point.

See, I've been working on a serum that I think should be able to cure the infected, but when I tried to test it I got surrounded and I injured my leg during the escape.

I know I'm on the right track but I need to test it. Do me a favor and take this vial and go try it out on one of the infected outside.

passages.title: Field Trial
passages.text: Have you completed the field test, <name>?

passages.title: Field Trial
passages.text:
The serum did what!??!

I must have used too much growth hormone. Possibly... the mixture just needs to be shaken prior to dosage?

passages.title: Legacy of the Ancients
passages.text:
Opening the ancient tome you see that it's not actually a tome at all, but a container. Inside are four empty slots.

Upon closer inspection each slot has next to it a carving of what appears to be a unique Draenor ancient, some glyphs and a receptacle used to hold a piece of the pictured ancient. There also appear to be directions to where these ancients may be found: medium timber -- Shadowmoon, Gorgrond, the Spires of Arak and Nagrand.

These are assassination instructions. From trees to kill trees.

passages.title: Legacy of the Ancients
passages.text: What have you got there, commander?

passages.title: Legacy of the Ancients
passages.text:
So what you're saying is that this here book is actually a container to hold the remains of targets on a hit list? And the assassination was being perpetrated by another... tree?

This world is crazy.

Now let's see what happens when we put all the pieces into place.

passages.title: Plant Pruning
passages.text:
There may be more to this aberrant growth than it seems, but we will need to clear the way a bit before we can get to the bottom of this, yes?

I suggest clearing out some of the angrier defenders to be on the safe side.

passages.title: Plant Pruning
passages.text: How goes the pruning <class>?

passages.title: Plant Pruning
passages.text:
I have slain quite a few as well but they continue to spring up here.

We will need another solution...

passages.title: Saberon Population Reduction
passages.text:
We are closer to our goals but a host of sharp toothed saberon bar our way.

If we are to get anywhere up here, some of the more aggressive ones will need to be put down I think.

passages.title: Saberon Population Reduction
passages.text: Many are finding bolt-holes to weather your storm, friend. That should keep them out of our way.

passages.title: Laying Dionor to Rest
passages.text: You have given me a tremendous gift with this bloom. I can finally send Dionor back to the Overgrowth for good and end this nightmare. All that remains is the ritual... stay and behold something you will never see again in your lifetime...

passages.title: Laying Dionor to Rest
passages.text:
At last it is done.  Dionor has left and his spawn shall follow him in due time.

I grow weary of this conflict and the desire to return to the Overgrowth has left me.

Perhaps I will travel beyond these lands and see what other surprises you little beasts have to share...

passages.title: Stealing the Declaration
passages.text:
Commander, you and Raleigh did a great job finding me, but I'm exactly where I need to be.

We've been working tirelessly since we got here, trying to crack these Draenic texts.

I really thought I was gonna get the scrolls, but they nabbed me at the last possible second!

Please, you've gotta help me out... up the hill to the east, you'll find the Master Siegesmith's tent.

If you can grab the documents out of his chest, possibly this key too, I'll finally have enough to translate their languages.

passages.title: Stealing the Declaration
passages.text: A book of poems? I'll let you hang onto that one for now....

passages.title: Stealing the Declaration
passages.text:
<name>, this is it, THIS IS IT! Just give me a moment while I look through these.

Hmm... I think there are a few things here that you may find very useful. Here, take these plans with you.

Don't worry about me, commander. I'm just gonna take another look around before I sneak out of here.

passages.title: A Green Ogron?
passages.text:
Kaz always told me green ogron are bad.

The botani here have a green ogron and it is mean.

It was strong enough to take out my dad's entire hunting party.

Are you strong enough to kill it?

passages.title: A Green Ogron?
passages.text: Yay! Burn the bad guy! Burn him a lot!

passages.title: Fire Ammonite
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Frostfire Ridge for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Fire Ammonite
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Fire Ammonite
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: Jawless Skulker
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Gorgrond for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Jawless Skulker
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Jawless Skulker
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: Fat Sleeper
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Nagrand for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Fat Sleeper
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Fat Sleeper
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: Blind Lake Sturgeon
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Shadowmoon Valley for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Blind Lake Sturgeon
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Blind Lake Sturgeon
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: Blackwater Whiptail
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Talador for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Blackwater Whiptail
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Blackwater Whiptail
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: Abyssal Gulper Eel
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Spires of Arak for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Abyssal Gulper Eel
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Abyssal Gulper Eel
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: A Green Ogron?
passages.text:
Them botani got themselves a green ogron. A green ogron!

I mean I may not know much about plant people but that canno' be a good thing.

Think ya can take it in a fight?

passages.title: A Green Ogron?
passages.text: Is it still twitchin'? I think I saw it still twitchin'.

passages.title: Bigger is Better
passages.text:
Ya know boss, I think I know how we can take this place to the next level. Bigger walls. More buildings. Some space to stretch your arms after a long day of adventuring.

Don't get me wrong, it's going to take a lot of resources, but what else are these things for?

We can plot it out on the drafting table whenever you're ready. It's going to be GLORIOUS.

passages.title: Bigger is Better
passages.text: What ya waitin' for boss? Let's take this thing to the next level!

passages.title: Bigger is Better
passages.text:
Now THAT'S what I'm talkin' about! Look at this place!

We've even got a pool out back. Little cold, sure, but ya can't always have a tropical paradise.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text:
With the Heart of the Mangaron, we wield a powerful weapon against the Iron Horde.

They amass far to the north at the Iron Approach. This will not be easy, but we must seize the opportunity to deal a blow to the Iron Horde while we possess the artifact.

We are prepared to depart at your command. Speak with Grinslicer when you are ready.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text: The mysteries of this land sometimes bear fruit.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text: <name>, we have dealt a great blow to the forces of the Iron Horde.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text:
With the Will of the Genesaur, we wield a powerful weapon.

Our scouts have discovered an Iron Horde base, and I believe it is time to seize an opportunity.

They amass far to the north at the Iron Approach. This will not be easy, but we must deal a blow to the Iron Horde while we possess the artifact.

We are prepared to depart at your command. Speak with Grinslicer when you are ready.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text: The mysteries of this land sometimes bear fruit.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text: <name>, we have dealt a great blow to the forces of the Iron Horde.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text:
With the Will of the Genesaur, we wield a powerful weapon.

Our scouts have discovered an Iron Horde base, and I believe this is the time to seize an opportunity.

They amass far to the north at the Iron Approach. This will not be easy, but we must deal a blow to the Iron Horde while we possess the artifact.

We are prepared to depart at your command. Speak with Rangari Rajess when you are ready.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text: We must eradicate the Iron Horde.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text: We have dealt a great blow to the Iron Horde, commander. We will defeat them yet.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text:
With the Heart of the Magnaron, we wield a powerful weapon against the Iron Horde.

They amass far to the north at the Iron Approach. This will not be easy, but we must seize the opportunity to deal a blow to the Iron Horde while we possess the artifact.

We are prepared to depart at your command. Speak with Rangari Rajess when you are ready.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text: We must eradicate the Iron Horde.

passages.title: Strike While the Iron is Hot
passages.text: We have dealt a great blow to the Iron Horde, commander. We will defeat them yet.

passages.title: Bigger is Better
passages.text:
Commander, I've been working on schematics that you might be interested in.

What do you think about pushing out the walls and making room to get some additional structures in here? Our forces have been growing, and things are getting a little cramped, and I'd really like us to put some of those additional blueprints to use.

If you could, take a look at the plans on the table here. As soon as I have your go ahead, I'll get everyone to work immediately.

passages.title: Bigger is Better
passages.text: What do you think? Time for an upgrade?

passages.title: Bigger is Better
passages.text:
MUCH better!  A lot less bumping into walls to be sure.

There should be room to get in another building or two now. We can get the additional construction going whenever you're ready - just point me at anything you're interested in on the table here.

passages.title: Breakers Invasion! UNUSED
passages.text: Quakes have been shaking the garrison for the last hour, and a few of our scouts aren't reporting in.

passages.title: My Very Own Fortress
passages.text:
Boss! Guess what?! I finally got that new larger draft paper in that I ordered when we first came here. And ya know what larger draft paper means?

It means I can draw a bigger fortress!

And if I can draw it, I can certainly make it! Making's the easy part, as long as you've got a few thousand stones and logs lying around.

So whada'ya say, boss? Shall we get building?

passages.title: My Very Own Fortress
passages.text:
I think I could just fall over and die happy right now. It's a dream come true!

I already ordered some even larger draft paper, boss. Don't you worry...

passages.title: My Very Own Castle
passages.text:
Commander! Some good news. I finally got that new larger draft paper in that I ordered when we first came here. And do you know what larger draft paper means?

It means I can draw a bigger castle!

And if I can draw it, we can certainly make it! Making it is the easy part, assuming you have a few thousand stones and logs lying around.

So what do you say, sir? Shall we get building?

passages.title: My Very Own Castle
passages.text:
I... I think I like it. A little more blue paint, maybe some taller towers, but you can really call it home, you know?

I already ordered some even larger draft paper, sir. Don't you worry...

passages.title: The Secrets of Gorgrond
passages.text:
Commander, I was dispatched to intercept you.

Yrel and Maraad have landed at Wildwood Wash, the rangari base of operations for the area.

Your presence is requested immediately. 

We keep a small feywing presence just east of here. If you speak with the flight master they should be able to provide you safe passage to the Wash.

passages.title: The Secrets of Gorgrond
passages.text: Welcome to Gorgrond, Commander. We only just arrived ourselves.

passages.title: Your First Work Order
passages.text: Now that you have a profession building, we can start producing work orders for you. When you have the ingredients we need, please come to me to start the first batch.

passages.title: Your First Enchanting Work Order
passages.text: Now that the enchanter's study is complete, we can start producing draenic dust for you. When you have the ingredients, please speak with my assistant to start the first work order.

passages.title: Your First Enchanting Work Order
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Your First Enchanting Work Order
passages.text:
Let me unpack that for you.

I should let you know - while we managed to expedite this one, future work orders will take longer.

passages.title: Assault on Stonefury Cliffs
passages.text:
Bloodmaul ogres from Frostfire Ridge have been ambushing trade routes throughout the continent, and are putting captured soldiers to work in their slag mines.

Bodrick Grey has requested the rescue of friendly troops that have been taken prisoner in the main Bloodmaul compound at Stonefury Cliffs.

passages.title: Assault on Stonefury Cliffs
passages.text:
Word of the assault has already made it back, as have some spoils from the fight.

Well done sir, if you don't mind me saying.

passages.title: Assault on Shattrath Harbor
passages.text:
Shattrath City is in the hands of Sargerei forces under the leadership of the traitor Exarch, Socrethar.

Members of the Sha'tari Defense have been requesting aid against the Shadow Council forces in the eastern portions of the city.

passages.title: Assault on Shattrath Harbor
passages.text:
Word of the assault has already made it back, as have some spoils from the fight.

Well done sir, if you don't mind me saying.

passages.title: Assault on Shattrath Harbor
passages.text:
Shattrath City is in the hands of Sargerei forces under the leadership of the once Exarch, Socrethar.

The Shadow Council forces in the eastern portion of the city are gaining in power through the aid of demons from the Nether, and need to be culled before they become a threat to all of our operations.

passages.title: Assault on Shattrath Harbor
passages.text:
News about da assault beat ya back, boss-mon. And some spoils of the fightin'.

Ya be a force to be reckonin' with.

passages.title: Assault on the Iron Siegeworks
passages.text:
Iron Horde war machines are being shipped onto battlefields by the dozens, and our forces are struggling to hold their ground. Most of these machines seem to be originating from the Iron Siegeworks in eastern Frostfire Ridge.

A strategic attack to disrupt and dismantle the Iron Horde at the siegeworks could be just what we need to turn the tide of the war.

passages.title: Assault on the Iron Siegeworks
passages.text:
Word of the assault has already made it back, as have some spoils from the fight.

Well done sir, if you don't mind me saying.

passages.title: Assault on Magnarok
passages.text:
Colossal magnaron, gronn, and other stone monstrosities have been threatening our outposts in the west. Most seem to originate from Magnarok in Frostfire Ridge.

If we strike at them at their home, we should be able to force them back. It's risky, but it may be our best move. While you're there, see if you can recover any of our supplies.

passages.title: Assault on Magnarok
passages.text: How goes the assault, sir?

passages.title: Assault on Magnarok
passages.text:
Word of the assault has already made it back, as have some spoils from the fight.

Well done sir, if you don't mind me saying.

passages.title: Assault on the Everbloom Wilds
passages.text:
Botani and the plant monstrosities they conjure have been slowly encroaching on our outposts in the north. For every plant we kill, new ones seem to rise in its place.

Bodrick Grey has put together a plan for striking at the heart of their lands, in Everbloom Wilds. He thinks this will draw them back into the wilds of Gorgrond, giving us more room to maneuver around them.

passages.title: Assault on the Everbloom Wilds
passages.text:
Word of the assault has already made it back, as have some spoils from the fight.

Well done sir, if you don't mind me saying.

passages.title: Assault on the Broken Precipice
passages.text:
Massive ogron have been battering our frontlines, and no matter how many we down, there seem to be more to replace them.

Most of these ogron appear to be coming from the Broken Precipice, deep in western Nagrand. If we're to stand a chance in the coming battles, we need to find a way to remove these ogron from the battlefield.

passages.title: Assault on the Broken Precipice
passages.text:
Word of the assault has already made it back, as have some spoils from the fight.

Well done sir, if you don't mind me saying.

passages.title: Assault on Mok'gol Watchpost
passages.text:
Warsong raiders out of Mok'gol Watchpost have been terrorizing anything and everything not behind a tall wall. We've warned travelers not to stray out alone, but many don't listen.

If we were to launch an assault on Mok'gol Watchpost, we would almost certainly put the Warsong back on the defensive, restricting most of their riders to Nagrand.

passages.title: Assault on Mok'gol Watchpost
passages.text:
Word of the assault has already made it back, as have some spoils from the fight.

Well done sir, if you don't mind me saying.

passages.title: Assault on Darktide Roost
passages.text:
There's been a resurgence of rylaks on the battlefield in our skirmishes against the Iron Horde. If we don't stop them at the source, we'll quickly lose control of the roads and be pushed back into our outposts.

The most likely source of these additional rylaks is in southeastern Shadowmoon Valley, at Darktide Roost. If we move quickly, we should still have time to get ahead of the problem.

passages.title: Assault on Darktide Roost
passages.text:
Word of the assault has already made it back, as have some spoils from the fight.

Well done sir, if you don't mind me saying.

passages.title: Assault on Socrethar's Rise
passages.text:
Recent reports suggest a notable rise of activity by Sargerei forces at Socrethar's Rise in southern Shadowmoon Valley.

Socrathar's disciples pose a threat to draenei and our garrison alike. We need to quell them at our soonest convenience.

passages.title: Assault on Socrethar's Rise
passages.text:
Word of the assault has already made it back, as have some spoils from the fight.

Well done sir, if you don't mind me saying.

passages.title: Assault on Lost Veil Anzu
passages.text:
Some of our best scouts have gone missing in the vicinity of the lost ruins of Veil Anzu.

Bodrick Grey has requested any available resources be dispatched to identify the threat and see if any of our men yet remain alive within the ruins.

passages.title: Assault on Lost Veil Anzu
passages.text:
Word of the assault has already made it back, as have some spoils from the fight.

Well done sir, if you don't mind me saying.

passages.title: Assault on Pillars of Fate
passages.text:
Remnants of the Shadowmoon clan continue to operate out of the peaks on the eastern border of Spires of Arak.

Bodrick Grey is concerned at their proximity to the garrison, and has put out a request that we thin their forces as soon as possible.

passages.title: Assault on Pillars of Fate
passages.text:

Well done sir, if you don't mind me saying.

passages.title: Assault on Skettis
passages.text:
We've been receiving regular reports of birdmen from the south ambushing and burning caravans along the main roads.

Guards from our outposts are requesting that we launch a counter attack against the main presence of Adherents of Rukhmar at Skettis in Spires of Arak.

passages.text:

passages.title: Assault on the Heart of Shattrath
passages.text:
Sargerei forces from deep in Shattrath have grown stronger and bolder by the day. We can no longer risk ignoring the threat that they pose.

Bring allies if you wish to face the Sargerei so deep within the city.

passages.title: Assault on the Pit
passages.text:
The Blackrock forces based out of the Pit in Gorgrond make up the bulk of the Iron Horde army. If we crush them on their home soil, the rest of the Iron Horde will have little hope of standing against us.

If you choose the battle, bring friends. The Blackrock won't be defeated easily.

passages.title: Subversive Infestation
passages.text:
As lord of the Everbloom my charge was the weaponization of nature.

You have likely seen the fruits of my labor in your journeys across my world.

My discoveries have allowed my kind to control the invasive species of Draenor through subversive infestation. I speak of total systemic control of the invading organism - the mind and the body.

Now that you are my master I offer these gifts to you, but first you must retrieve my research and tools from the Everbloom.

Do this and great power is yours.

passages.title: Subversive Infestation
passages.text: Retrieve what I have asked for, master. I will show you the true strength of nature.

passages.title: Subversive Infestation
passages.text:
Within this pouch I have placed three Everbloom seeds. You merely have to crush the seed to release the spores within. Inhale deeply and let the subversive infestation take hold.

Once empowered you will become an unstoppable force of nature; though be warned, I have modified these seeds to cause you minimal harm, thus their potency is somewhat reduced.

You must not undergo the transformation too frequently.

Should you require more seeds I will offer them to you - for a small price.

passages.title: Your Second Alchemy Work Order
passages.text: Place another work order with my assistant. Once it is complete, we will leave it out here for you to collect.

passages.title: Your Second Alchemy Work Order
passages.text: We look forward to serving you again.

passages.title: DEPRECATED
passages.text:
You there... you look the fighting type. I want some sweet Revenge on the Scourge that killed my family. Go get me 2 Stone Hunks O' Gargoyle so that I can throw them on the ground and stomp on them violently until they are mashed into itty bitty pebbly bits. 

Yes. Go. Kill.

passages.title: Warlord of Draenor
passages.text:
Durotan...

<Raza'kul spits.>

He cowers behind the white flag of peace, relying upon diplomacy to win over our sworn enemies.

Enemies that have taken our homes and driven us from our ancestral lands.

There is only one way to deal with the draenei and their newfound alliance of cowards - blood for blood.

Join me in crushing our enemies. Together we will flood this hallowed ground with the bones of the Alliance and earn tributes fit for a warchief!

Return here when your bloodthirst is sated.

passages.title: Warlord of Draenor
passages.text: I will not rest until this bloodied ground overflows with the bones of our enemies.

passages.title: Warlord of Draenor
passages.text:
We may kill from sky break to sky fall and still our work will never be done. Yet at the end of days when we are measured for our accomplishments, only the bloody wake that we have left behind us will show our true strength. For this reason you must never stop the slaughter of those that would seek to harm us and our loved ones.

Promise me, <name>.

Never. Stop.

passages.title: Warlord of Draenor
passages.text:
The Exarchs do nothing but squabble amongst themselves over petty issues while our people are slaughtered in their homes by orc filth. If they will not raise a fist of defiance against our enemies, I will.

I wish to join your Alliance and rid this world of Horde. ALL HORDE - "Iron" or otherwise.

This Altar of Bones that I stand upon represents glory in battle against our Horde enemy. Place an offering upon it and earn a conqueror's tribute worthy of your unrelenting bloodthirst.

Kill. Them. All.

passages.title: Warlord of Draenor
passages.text: I will not rest until this bloodied ground overflows with the bones of our enemies.

passages.title: Warlord of Draenor
passages.text:
It is a start, to be certain, but there is much work to be done if Draenor is to be saved. Show no mercy, for they will show none to you.

The only warlords left upon Draenor will be you and I.

passages.title: Nemesis: Becoming Death
passages.text:
You have chosen your quarry and surely soon they will feel your merciless wrath, but first you must venture out into the wilds of Draenor and rip out the still-beating heart of a human in mortal combat. Return here with your prize.

Through the heart of your enemy the spirits will attune your senses, granting you second sight and keenness in hearing - all to stalk your prey and claim dominance.

passages.title: Nemesis: Becoming Death
passages.text: Have you recovered the heart of a worthy foe?

passages.title: Nemesis: Becoming Death
passages.text: With this heart you will see and hear things as only the great spirits can. Your enemy will be unable to hide from your unrelenting assaults.

passages.title: Taming a Talbuk
passages.text:
If we're going to start sending out patrols in this wilderness, we'll need swift mounts for our troops. We can capture young beasts and bring them back here for training, eventually turning them into formidable beasts of war.

The talbuk is one of Draenor's fastest creatures, and that makes them just that much more difficult to capture. Take this talbuk lasso and head out to Shadowmoon Valley. Mount up and rope one of the young talbuk, and follow it until it's tamed. Don't let it get too far from you!

passages.title: Taming a Talbuk
passages.text: That talbuk's already settled down for the night. It will need some rest and grooming before it's ready for the next stage in its training.

passages.title: Capturing a Clefthoof
passages.text:
Greetings, friend. I have been told that you are in need of a master of beasts. I come from the icy slopes of Northrend to finally shake this snow from my fur.

This savage land holds many creatures that we may tame so that our forces may ride on formidable war mounts. The mighty clefthoof reminds me of the mammoths from my home. Take this lasso and head out to the northern reaches of Frostfire Ridge. Mount up and use it to capture one of the young beasts.

passages.title: Capturing a Clefthoof
passages.text: I have bedded the clefthoof down for the night, it will need rest before it is ready for training.

passages.title: Entangling an Elekk
passages.text:
Well, you're pretty good at this whole taming thing. What's next?

We've done big, and we've done pointy. Let's do big AND pointy. I'm talking Elekks.

Way out on the fertile plains of Nagrand, you'll find the finest specimens of beast this world has to offer. Grab one of the younger elekks, and we'll see if we can't get it trained like the Draenei used to.

passages.title: Entangling an Elekk
passages.text: Quite a big one, but it fits! It's resting, we'll talk about training it tomorrow.

passages.title: Capturing a Clefthoof
passages.text:
Way up north in the frozen peaks of Frostfire Ridge, you'll find the wooly clefthoof.

They're sturdy, for sure, and fierce when you corner them. Don't expect them to be tamed without a fight.

Here's a lasso, see if you can't manage to tame one before it tugs the rope out of your hands.

passages.title: Capturing a Clefthoof
passages.text: Was it cold up there? This guy seems to appreciate the warmth, he's already snoozin'!

passages.title: Taming a Talbuk
passages.text:
The next beast is one of the fastest in Draenor, but will test your skills at infiltrating into enemy territory.

The young talbuk can be found on the flowery hills of Shadowmoon Valley. Take this talbuk lasso and head out.

When you encounter one, mount up and throw this rope, then follow it until it is tamed. Good hunting!

passages.title: Taming a Talbuk
passages.text: The talbuk appears to be doing well. Allow it to rest before you continue the beast's training.

passages.title: Requisition a Riverbeast
passages.text:
I wasn't sure about this next beast, but it turns out that they've got a key strategic purpose. The riverbeast is quite at home in the water!

You'll find the best ones around in Talador, around about Duskfall Island. Look for the huge, floating lumps out in the water.

Try not to get wet!

passages.title: Requisition a Riverbeast
passages.text: I've gone and dried it off already. We'll see about training this thing tomorrow.

passages.title: Nemesis: Manslayer
passages.text:
<Raza'kul hands you the bloody heart.>

The ritual is complete. Your nemesis is marked for death.

Now your work to rid this world of the enemy truly begins. Kill all humans that stand defiantly against the Horde. Let their deaths serve as a warning to the rest of the Alliance: they will leave Draenor or they will die.

Return when you have quenched your rage with the blood of man.

Conquer our enemy and be known as manslayer. Fail and be nothing.

passages.title: Nemesis: Manslayer
passages.text:
The truth of your deeds is in your eyes. Your hunger for the enemy sated with cries for mercy and rivers of blood.

Take now your place as manslayer.

passages.title: Warning Orgrimmar
passages.text:
We have slowed the Iron Horde down, but this war is far from over... I'll stay here and continue our efforts to hold back the Iron Horde.

The Warchief needs to know about what we have accomplished here today, and the threat we face in the future.

It is probably best if you report to High Overlord Saurfang yourself, <class>.

passages.title: Warning Orgrimmar
passages.text:
This is more trouble than I first tink. Da Iron Horde be strong, but we are da true Horde, and we be stronger.

I fear this is da start of much bloodshed, before we go ta war, we be needin' a plan.

passages.title: Report to the King
passages.text:
This is worse than I imagined.

The Iron Horde is proving to be a massive threat to our people... I don't want anymore bloodshed, but I fear we are out of options.

We need a plan before we strike.

passages.title: Requisition a Riverbeast
passages.text:
I have seen great beasts floating slowly along the rivers of Talador. The 'riverbeasts,' I believe they are called.

Their hides are solid, like rock, and yet they float along the waters easily. I would quite like to see one of these up close, if you should head that way. Tormak has created for you another rope, if you are interested.

passages.title: Requisition a Riverbeast
passages.text: Quite a sight, I must say. Big and powerful, yet full of so much air. It will be ready for training tomorrow.

passages.title: Entangling an Elekk
passages.text:
The plains of Nagrand are the most lush and fertile that I have ever seen. Should you ever see them, you will come upon the mightiest beasts that this place has to offer.

Among them, the great elekk. A magnificent beast with horns that can grow larger than you or I.

Here is another rope, should you wish to tangle with such a beast.

passages.title: Entangling an Elekk
passages.text: A powerful creature, it nearly took down the wooden posts of the stable. We will begin training it as soon as it wakes.

passages.title: Auctioning for Parts
passages.text: You can hear the power building inside the unit...

passages.title: Talbuk Training: The Garn
passages.text:
I've got one last challenge for ye, commander, but if it isn't a doozy.

They call them the garn. Wolves as black as night, and twice the size of a normal wolf, they can tear a man apart in seconds. Any beast in their right mind would be scared witless at the sight of such a predator.

There's a lone garn that's made it from their usual home in Frostfire, all the way over to Nagrand. Take your talbuk, mount up, and bring it down. If the two of you survive, your talbuk will truly be ready for war.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: The Garn
passages.text:
Your talbuk has grown from a wee silverpelt into a fine specimen of war beast, and it's all due to your diligence.

I'm happy to hand over the reins of this fully-trained mount to you, commander. Ride it with pride!

passages.text:

They call them the garn. Wolves as black as night, and twice the size of a normal wolf, they can tear a man apart in seconds. Any beast in their right mind would be scared witless at the sight of such a predator.

passages.title: Clefthoof Training: The Garn
passages.text: Your clefthoof is now fully-trained, and it's all thanks to you! I'm going to tear up here if I don't just hand you these reins and send you on your way. Great job, commander!

passages.text:

passages.title: Riverbeast Training: The Garn
passages.text:
You know, I didn't really believe you when you decided to start training this thing. But here it is, a trained riverwallow.

I guess if a beast needs training, you're the one to do it! Great work, commander!

passages.title: Auctioning for Parts
passages.text: You can hear the power building inside the unit.

passages.title: Elekk Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text:
This beast is surely at home in Nagrand, and I bet ye after all of the years of domestication by Draenei, it's going to be a snap to train.

Let's set it loose against the ogres of the region that yer familiar with. That Gorian Beast-Lasher, the one that smells of blood and fear, go on and see how your elekk reacts to that.

passages.title: Elekk Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text: Those poor beasts! I'm glad you two put that ogre out of commission. Check back in tomorrow and we can continue the training.

passages.title: Elekk Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text:
The Warsong Clan of Nagrand are some of the best hunters I've ever had the misfortune of meeting. If anyone can pose a real test for your future mount, it's one of their chief beast-killers.

Out in Nagrand, you'll find an orc by the name of Karak. They call him the Great Hunter, and he's taken down more fierce beasts than any other in the clan. Get astride your elekk and bring him down. In the name of the poor wee beasts!

passages.title: Elekk Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text: Hunted the hunter, eh? Your beast doesn't seem any worse for wear, either! I'll brush it down.

passages.title: Elekk Training: The Garn
passages.text:
I've got one last challenge for ye, commander, but if it isn't a doozy.

They call them the garn. Wolves as black as night, and twice the size of a normal wolf, they can tear a man apart in seconds. Any beast in their right mind would be scared witless at the sight of such a predator.

There's a lone garn that's made it from their usual home in Frostfire, all the way over to Nagrand. Take your elekk, mount up, and bring it down. If the two of you survive, your elekk will truly be ready.

passages.title: Elekk Training: The Garn
passages.text:
A fine beast, to be sure, commander. It'll stand up in even the toughest battles.

I'll admit, I'm a bit jealous of ye'! Here's the reins! I'll be sure to take good care of it when ye bring it back.

passages.title: Wolf Training: The Garn
passages.text:
I've got one last challenge for ye, commander, but if it isn't a doozy.

They call them the garn. Wolves as black as night, and twice the size of a normal wolf, they can tear a man apart in seconds. Any beast in their right mind would be scared witless at the sight of such a predator.

There's a lone garn that's made it from their usual home in Frostfire, all the way over to Nagrand. Take your wolf, mount up, and bring it down. If the two of you survive, your wolf will truly be ready.

passages.title: Wolf Training: The Garn
passages.text:
I can't believe you've managed to train your wolf already! It feels like it was just yesterday that the little ball of fur and death came into my stables.

I'll hand it to ye, that's a fierce little mount ye got there. Here's the reins, enjoy!

passages.title: Sigil of the Black Hand
passages.text:
<Goraluk sighs with... relief? ...or perhaps regret?>

Once I walked these halls with pride, holding my head high as an orc of the Blackrock clan. But this is a wrong path. Our hammers were meant to craft axes, swords... not these machines from the stranger's whispers.

The Warlord will not be swayed, but by force. If you can retrieve essences from the Foundry's most powerful guardians, I can craft for you a sigil that will permit direct access to Blackhand's Crucible.

passages.title: Sigil of the Black Hand
passages.text: I will require essences from each of the Foundry's guardians if this is to work.

passages.title: Sigil of the Black Hand
passages.text:
You have done it!

<Goraluk takes the items from your hands, and turns his back for a few moments>

Now, I will touch this Sigil to your hand, and the entrance to the Crucible will open at your touch. Good luck.

passages.title: Salvaging the Situation
passages.text:
Here at the Salvage Yard we inspect any extra material your followers bring back from the field, preserving anything that may be useful.

I have an extra pack of material our people brought in that I've yet to go through. Why don't you take it over to the incinerator and see if it contains anything useful?

passages.title: Salvaging the Situation
passages.text: Have you burned through that bag of salvage yet?

passages.title: Salvaging the Situation
passages.text:
That's all? Well. don't feel too bad. Some days we find nothing and the next we hit the jackpot!

Here, I have a fresh supply of items from our latest outing. Check them out.

Good luck!

passages.title: Clefthoof Training: The Garn
passages.text:
The last test for your mount will pit it against one of the great terrors of this land.

The garn. Wolves as black as night, and twice the size of a normal wolf, they can tear an orc apart in mere moments. The beasts here wisely fear them.

There is a lone garn that calls Nagrand its home. Take your clefthoof, mount up, and bring it down. If the two of you survive, your clefthoof will truly be ready.

passages.title: Clefthoof Training: The Garn
passages.text: The clefthoof is now fully-trained and prepared to be your mount. Take care of the beast, I hope to see the two of you again shortly.

passages.title: Elekk Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text:
This beast is surely at home in Nagrand, and after the years of domestication by Draenei it will be quite easy to train.

We shall face it against the ogres of the region that you are familiar with. The Gorian Beast-Lasher, the one that smells of blood and fear, see how this elekk reacts to him.

passages.title: Elekk Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text: Those beasts will recover, in time. Let us rest for tonight, you have done well.

passages.title: Elekk Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text:
The Warsong Clan of Nagrand are some of the finest hunters the world of Draenor has ever known. Their beast-killers will aid us in putting this mount to the test.

Out in Nagrand, you will find an orc by the name of Karak, the Great Hunter. He has slain more fierce beasts than any other in the clan. Face him astride your mount, and avenge the slain.

passages.title: Elekk Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text: Ah, you have hunted the hunter. Many beasts will be pleased tonight.

passages.title: Elekk Training: The Garn
passages.text:

The garn. Wolves as black as night, and twice the size of a normal wolf, they can tear an orc apart in mere moments. The beasts here wisely fear them.

There is a lone garn that calls Nagrand its home. Take your elekk, mount up, and bring it down. If the two of you survive, your elekk will truly be ready.

passages.title: Elekk Training: The Garn
passages.text: A fine beast, sure to be your companion in many battles to come. Here are the reins, be strong but fair in your care of this great beast.

passages.title: Riverbeast Training: The Garn
passages.text:
The last test for your mount will pit it against one of the great terrors of this land.

The garn. Wolves as black as night, and twice the size of a normal wolf, they can tear an orc apart in mere moments. The beasts here wisely fear them.

There is a lone garn that calls Nagrand its home. Take your riverbeast, mount up, and bring it down. If the two of you survive, your riverbeast will truly be ready.

passages.title: Riverbeast Training: The Garn
passages.text: I had never seen such a beast before coming here, but you have trained it. No small feat, to be certain. Take the reins, you have earned them.

passages.title: Fight, Kill, Salute!
passages.text:
The greatest gladiators on Draenor have fought for glory and honor inside the Coliseum. Will you become a legend like Kargath Bladefist or will you be nothing more than bone dust beneath the boots of a more savage gladiator? There is only one way to find out.

You must enter the competition and fight! The price of victory is 100 lives!

I will admit you without cost once per day, but if you fail and wish to fight again you must pay the price of admission in blood and bone!

passages.title: Fight, Kill, Salute!
passages.text: Remarkable! You have proven yourself a true gladiator. And to a true gladiator goes more than honor and glory!

passages.title: Salvaging the Situation
passages.text:
Here at the Salvage Yard we inspect any extra material your followers bring back from the field, preserving anything that may be useful.

I have an extra pack of material our people brought in that I've yet to go through. Why don't you take it over to the incinerator and see if it contains anything useful?

passages.title: Salvaging the Situation
passages.text: Have you burned through that bag of salvage yet?

passages.title: Salvaging the Situation
passages.text:
That's all? Well. don't feel too bad. Some days we find nothing and the next we hit the jackpot!

Here, I have a fresh supply of items from our latest outing. Check them out.

Good luck!

passages.title: Talbuk Training: The Garn
passages.text:
The last test for your mount will pit it against one of the great terrors of this land.

The garn. Wolves as black as night, and twice the size of a normal wolf, they can tear an orc apart in mere moments. The beasts here wisely fear them.

There is a lone garn that calls Nagrand its home. Take your talbuk, mount up, and bring it down. If the two of you survive, your talbuk will truly be ready for war.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: The Garn
passages.text: A powerful and swift companion, and now unafraid of the creatures you may run into. You have done well in your training of the beast, and I am pleased to present you with the reins.

passages.title: Wolf Training: The Garn
passages.text:
The last test for your mount will pit it against one of the great terrors of this land.

The garn. Wolves as black as night, and twice the size of a normal wolf, they can tear an orc apart in mere moments. The beasts here wisely fear them.

There is a lone garn that calls Nagrand its home. Take your wolf, mount up, and bring it down. If the two of you survive, your wolf will truly be ready.

passages.title: Wolf Training: The Garn
passages.text: A savage beast, yet you have tamed it. I should learn to never underestimate you. It awaits your command patiently, almost like it knows you wait for it. Here are the reins, may your companion be ever at your side.

passages.title: An Ogre Without His Sword...
passages.text:
Before I was shipped off to Gorgrond, I was stationed at the Broken Precipice in Nagrand, maintaining order over the unruly dredges. Vizier Dar'gud refused to let me take my favorite sword; he told me "I wouldn't need it where I was going."

I want it back, commander, and we are powerful enough together to take it from Dar'gud's bloody corpse.

It would mean a great deal to me. An ogre without his sword isn't an ogre at all.

passages.title: An Ogre Without His Sword...
passages.text: I want my sword more than I can tell you, commander.

passages.title: An Ogre Without His Sword...
passages.text:
Yes... this is it.

Commander, I will cleave your foes like never before now that I have my sword.

passages.title: The Light of Exodus
passages.text:
My grandfather always told me stories of a powerful crystal made of the Light that would grant power to those who intended to use it for good. He called it the Light of Exodus.

I never believed him... until now.

Your scouts have found a crystal that sounds just like it. It has been taken by a terrible demon and is being corrupted at the Beacon of Sha'tar in Shattrath.

We have to hurry!

passages.title: The Light of Exodus
passages.text: If the Light of Exodus is half as powerful as my grandfather told me, we cannot let it fall into the Legion's hands.

passages.title: The Light of Exodus
passages.text:
It's so beautiful...

Oh, commander, thank you. A million times thank you!

passages.title: Settling Grievances
passages.text:
Our scouts have found a powerful draenei crystal being corrupted by Ambassador Hellmaw at the Beacon of Sha'tar in Shattrath. The draenei call it the Light of Exodus.

Commander, I'd like to accompany you on this mission. Hellmaw slew my brother in Outland... this is personal.

passages.title: Settling Grievances
passages.text: We cannot allow the Legion to gain any advantage.

passages.title: Settling Grievances
passages.text: It is done. The Legion have suffered a mighty blow.

passages.title: The Dark Lady's Concern
passages.text:
The botani in the Everbloom Wilds kill anything foolish enough to wander too close to their blooms and are raising their corpses as mindless soldiers.

This is all too reminiscent of the Scourge... and the Dark Lady has taken notice. She has a special mission for us, commander.

There is a particularly large infested creature that was recently raised. We are to destroy it and retrieve its remains.

passages.title: The Dark Lady's Concern
passages.text: I assure you, commander, the Dark Lady has the Horde's best interests at heart. We must stop these botani immediately.

passages.title: The Dark Lady's Concern
passages.text: Thank you, commander. The Dark Lady will appreciate this greatly.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text:
There are others that harness the shadows to do their bidding. You know of them, commander... the Shadowmoon orcs.

They have begun to master their craft... they call to the shadows beyond this realm...

I desire their power. They have one who possesses a staff of particular interest... we should claim it as our own.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text: Taking out our enemies and gaining great power in one motion... my people have a saying for this: Killing two orcs with one stone.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text:
Yes... yes... this will do nicely. We can use this to do great things.

Thank you, commander.

passages.title: Ogre Ancestry
passages.text:
Lunk no like fight, want to learn. You help Lunk learn?

Find Lunk ancestors. Lunk have many question. Where Lunk come from? Why Lunk Lunk?

Lunk stay here. Small ogres mean, big ogres meaner.

passages.title: Ogre Ancestry
passages.text: How can Lunk Lunk if Lunk not know what Lunk is?

passages.title: Ogre Ancestry
passages.text:
Lunk know you kill many ogre for this, and Lunk very upset about this, but Lunk also still grateful.

Wait, dis not Lunk family club...

passages.title: Budd's Gambit
passages.text:
Listen, I don't know how I got here, but I have it on good authority that there is an entire island made of shiny things and it's just off of the coast a ways.

All we have to do is hop in the water and swim out there, then we can load up our pockets and swim back! I'm just going to rest up and do some stretching before heading out.

Don't try and stop me!

passages.title: Budd's Gambit
passages.text: What?

passages.title: Budd's Gambit
passages.text:
Oh... this is... well that's very shiny isn't it? I think... I'll just sit here for a while.

<Budd smiles contentedly.>

passages.title: Oralius' Adventure
passages.text:
Me n' Winky, off on adventures again! This is the life, I tell ye. No burning air to breathe, an' plenty of ogres to kill!

<Oralius rubs his belly.>

We did leave a bit of a mess back there in the Blackrock Spire, though. A whole mess of these iron-plated orcs and some proto-dragons marched right on up from the south and took it over.

Ol' Winky, he couldn't take the guilt. Went on back by himself he did, to stop them!

Or... to JOIN them! Winky, ye two-timing son of an orc. Ye've got to stop him!

passages.title: Oralius' Adventure
passages.text: Did ye stop him?

passages.title: Oralius' Adventure
passages.text:
Good thinkin'. Winky always loved these flameflies. If we gather enough of them, maybe we can convince hiim to come back!

Maybe, er, you should hold onto this for a while, eh?

passages.title: The Void-Gate
passages.text:
My 'master' is an idiot, but you look like you've got some smarts in that oddly-shaped head.

Listen up, the Twisting Nether is a chaotic abyss, and things work differently there. I've felt some disturbances, and they don't bode well for any of us.

Yes, there are things happening here, in Draenor, that are causing ripples in the nether. No, don't try to wrap your head around how that works, you'll only hurt yourself.

It's simple: bring me a Void-Gate Key, and maybe I can stop the bad things.

passages.title: The Void-Gate
passages.text: You do know that any time you waste talking to me brings us closer to doom, right?

passages.title: The Void-Gate
passages.text:
Perfect, here's a prize for your efforts.

I've got to head out and save everyone now. Again.

passages.title: Feeling A Bit Morose
passages.text:
So many years of waking up as a spirit, reanimated by some unseen force time and again, has left one with certain desires - the comforting, velvet blackness of death being chief amongst them.

One will, however, settle for the lesser prize of a solution capable of removing the scuff marks that the commander's wonderful compatriots left behind in the dining hall in their woefully short stay in Karazhan, whereupon they barely had enough time to irreparably damage the priceless furniture.

passages.title: Feeling A Bit Morose
passages.text: Was the commander successful?

passages.title: Feeling A Bit Morose
passages.text:
One is eternally in your debt for what is, one is certain, an entirely selfless act on the part of the commander.

Though more barrels were likely available, one will staunchly make do with the single barrel provided, comforted in the knowledge that the commander must deal with the great pressing issues of this land, and does not have time to clean up the mud that that so dutifully follows the commander's heroic allies.

passages.title: Shadowy Secrets
passages.text:
Though the Lich King has been defeated, we are no closer to unlocking the secrets of the Frozen Throne than we were when jousting pointlessly at the Argent Tournament. Bolvar remains resigned to his fate.

Perhaps there is something here, though, that can aid us. Ner'zhul was not always the Lich King, you know. Once, he was a mere orc dabbling in dark powers beyond his comprehension.

Find whatever you can of his early studies, and we may have our answers.

passages.title: Shadowy Secrets
passages.text: Did you find any of Ner'zhul's notes?

passages.title: Shadowy Secrets
passages.text:
You have my thanks. I will bring this back to the Ebon Hold immediately.

Take this, I... acquired it... from one of the Shadowmoon.

passages.title: The Huntresses
passages.text:
I do not wish to come out of the shadows, but I mean you no harm. My purpose here is my own secret to keep, I simply needed a warm place to bed down for the night.

I can see that you are not the type to be easily swayed into leaving. Very well, perhaps you can aid me in my search.

I am looking for someone, it is not important who. All you need to know is that I will reward you for any sign of high elven weaponry that you should come across.

passages.title: The Huntresses
passages.text: Did you find anything?

passages.title: The Huntresses
passages.text:
This is... it can't be.

I must be off, here is your reward. I do not part with it lightly...

passages.title: For The Children!
passages.text:
Wait, wait! Don't attack me! I've changed!

Really, I've turned over a new leaf, I promise. I haven't said "DOOOOOOM!" in months! All I care about now is saving the poor little orphans of Azeroth, whose parents have been taken by this tragic war.

That's why I'm here! Why, with just a single Miniature Iron Star, I could provide clean water and power for all of the orphans of Azeroth! And no one could stop me!

So, what do you think, sweetcheeks? Want to help ol' Milhouse save the orphans?

passages.title: For The Children!
passages.text: Did you find the Iron Star?

passages.title: For The Children!
passages.text:
You know, you're quite handy, and awfully powerful. Why don't I just follow you for a while?

Look out Draenor, DOOOOOOOOM is coming!

passages.title: An Ogre Without His Sword...
passages.text:
Before I was shipped off to Gorgrond, I was stationed at the Broken Precipice in Nagrand, maintaining order over the unruly dredges. Vizier Dar'gud refused to let me take my favorite sword; he told me "I wouldn't need it where I was going."

I want it back, commander, and we are powerful enough together to take it from Dar'gud's bloody corpse.

It would mean a great deal to me. An ogre without his sword isn't an ogre at all.

passages.title: An Ogre Without His Sword...
passages.text: I want my sword more than I can tell you, commander.

passages.title: An Ogre Without His Sword...
passages.text:
Yes... this is it.

Commander, I will cleave your foes like never before now that I have my sword.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text:
There are others that harness the shadows to do their bidding. You know of them, commander... the Shadowmoon orcs.

They have begun to master their craft... they call to the shadows beyond this realm...

I desire their power. They have one who possesses a staff of particular interest... we should claim it as our own.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text: Taking out our enemies and gaining great power in one motion... my people have a saying for this: Killing two orcs with one stone.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text:
Yes... yes... this will do nicely. We can use this to do great things.

Thank you, commander.

passages.title: Put a Bird on It
passages.text:
<name>! Have you met the peachick you saved the other day?

<Mylune holds up a peachick hatchling, then trills and twitters at it. She gestures to you, says your name, then continues chirping animatedly to the little bird. The two ignore you and engage in a lengthy bird-conversation, long enough to make you feel awkward. Finally the dryad turns her attention back to you.>

Did you hear that? More peachicks are still trapped in the Everbloom! If you don't save them... well, you heard what will happen!

passages.title: Put a Bird on It
passages.text: <Mylune stamps her hooves impatiently.>

passages.title: Put a Bird on It
passages.text:
Oh, thank you <name>! You've made a lot of wee baby birds very happy.

You're my favorite <race>!

passages.title: A Fruitful Proposition
passages.text:
The head of just ONE ogre won't be enough to stop the fruit vendor. No, the fruit vendor is wise, they would not put all of their fruit into one basket.

Bring me the head of ANOTHER ogre! Ha! Then what will the fruit vendor do? Cry onto their bananas as they rot and fall to the ground.

DESPAIR, FRUIT VENDOR. SO DELICIOUS!

passages.title: A Fruitful Proposition
passages.text: THE FRUIT VENDOR STANDS NO CHANCE!

passages.title: A Fruitful Proposition
passages.text: We are one step closer to crushing the fruit vendor's grapes into muddy wine.

passages.title: Like A Dwarf In A Mine
passages.text:
Baelog and Eric swear there's got to be treasure at the bottom of the mine. Why? Because it's a mine! An' we sure do love rocks that sparkle.

On our last trip, we were beaten back by huge ogres. Baelog held up the rear, swingin' his sword, while Eric rushed on ahead to try and find a quick exit.

Wouldn't you know, in all that excitement, I done lost my shield AGAIN?

<Olaf looks at you imploringly.>

passages.title: Like A Dwarf In A Mine
passages.text: <Olaf sobs.>

passages.title: Like A Dwarf In A Mine
passages.text: By the light, that's her! You've done it again, an' I can't thank you enough! We'll try to be more careful next time.

passages.title: Bloody Expensive
passages.text:
Welcome back, commander. The commander is obviously in a great hurry, and certainly the thought of removing their coat or boots or not dripping all over the floor are much too far beyond consideration.

The commander remembers the acidic solution, yes? Quite effective it was, though one barrel was not enough to remove ALL of the blood stains from the portraits, or the tapestries, or the ceiling.

Surely this must have been the most heroic and viscous battle in recent history.

passages.title: Bloody Expensive
passages.text: Was the commander successful?

passages.title: Bloody Expensive
passages.text: Again, though more barrels were likely available, one will staunchly make do with the single barrel provided, comforted in the knowledge that the commander must deal with the great pressing issues of this land, and does not have time to clean up the mud that that so dutifully follows the commander's heroic allies.

passages.title: Like Father, Like Son
passages.text:
He's done it again! My son took my knife and yelled something about a 'chromatic hide,' then ran off for the Spire! What would he even do with something like that, wear it around like a cape?

If it's not too much to ask, would you keep an eye out for the knife? You know, next time you're around Upper Blackrock Spire. Which, hopefully, is soon. VERY soon.

passages.title: Like Father, Like Son
passages.text: Where's my knife?

passages.title: Like Father, Like Son
passages.text: You've saved it! A little nicked, but that can be fixed. Thanks!

passages.title: Secrets of Soulbinding
passages.text:
We have reviewed Ner'zhul's notes, which you brought to us previously. Though we are closer to understanding how these warlocks have learned to bind souls and control the undead, the picture is incomplete.

We will need more pages if we are to see the whole picture. I do not want to experiment with partial information and create an abomination. There are enough of those in Northrend as it is.

passages.title: Secrets of Soulbinding
passages.text: Did you find any of Ner'zhul's notes?

passages.title: Secrets of Soulbinding
passages.text: We are greatful for your aid. I shall retire shortly.

passages.title: Fate of the Fallen
passages.text:
I feel that I can trust you, perhaps. You have, at least, not spoken of my secret to anyone, and for that I thank you.

I have need of your aid again, and in return, I will share some of my own information. I am here, you see, to find an elf by the name of Alleria. She was lost years ago, on Draenor. It is my faint hope that the twisting nether brought her here.

I do not know if such a thing is even possible, but do keep an eye out for any signs of high elves as you travel.

passages.title: Fate of the Fallen
passages.text: Did you find anything?

passages.title: Fate of the Fallen
passages.text:
Another one? How curious.

I may not be much closer to finding her, but these arrows bring some comfort to me, at least.

passages.title: The Leaf-Reader
passages.text:
Good ta see you again, mon!

De Cenarion Circle sent Zen'kiki out here ta find some more of dem plants. We not likin' what we be seein' here.

If ya find any more of dem leaves, bring one on back. Dey can see right through Zen'kiki's tree disguise, even when he plant himself in da ground!

And dat make it harder to run!

passages.title: The Leaf-Reader
passages.text: Did ya have much luck, mon?

passages.title: The Leaf-Reader
passages.text: Thanks, mon. I'm gonna bring this back to the Circle, just as soon as I can figure out how ta fly in da savage winds of dis place.

passages.title: Lessons of the Past
passages.text:
I have returned! You must have known that a world so rich in history could not keep me away for long!

<Lorewalker Cho chuckles, holding his enormous belly.>

I have perhaps been taking part in too many celebratory feasts, now that the Vale has been cleansed. There is so much to celebrate in Pandaria!

Should you find any future evidence of titanic influence on the native species, I will be here, heartily enjoying the roast clefthoof.

passages.title: Lessons of the Past
passages.text: Have you found any signs of the titans here?

passages.title: Lessons of the Past
passages.text: Another excellent find from our most illustrious hero! I will immediately begin transcribing your heroic deeds!

passages.title: Learning Is Painful
passages.text:
The academy is up and running, in a secret location of course. Maybe it doesn't exist at all?

By the by, I appear to be running quite dry on sharp, pointy instruments of education.

<Lonika winks at you several times before nudging you sharply in the ribs with her dagger.>

passages.title: Learning Is Painful
passages.text: Did you find me some weapons?

passages.title: Learning Is Painful
passages.text: Once again, you have proven yourself invaluable. Perhaps you would like a teaching job?

passages.title: Flamefly Trap
passages.text:
Ol' Winky still hasn't come back! Now I'm gettin' worried.

Do me a favor and get another one of those flameflies from Upper Blackrock Spire. If we get enough of em,' Winky's sure to see the glimmer and come heading on back.

An then we'll have him right where we want him!

passages.title: Flamefly Trap
passages.text: Did ye get another fly?

passages.title: Flamefly Trap
passages.text: Oi, that's a bright fly! Thank ye, we'll just keep on tryin' until that two-timing ol' Winky comes on home.

passages.title: Whispers in the Darkness
passages.text:
If you don't mind, I'm trying VERY hard to prevent all of our worlds from collapsing into the void, AGAIN.

Oh, right, you helped me last time, didn't you? Well, you've got great timing. I'm in need of another Gate-Key.

Well? Go on! The infinite horrors of the abyss aren't just going to wait until you've had a nap! Having that many tentacles makes them really antsy.

passages.title: Whispers in the Darkness
passages.text: You do know that any time you waste talking to me brings us closer to doom, right?

passages.title: Whispers in the Darkness
passages.text:
Perfect, here's a prize for your efforts.

I've got to head out and save everyone now. Again.

passages.title: They Came From the Sea
passages.text:
You're looking for Prince Farondis?

<The ghostly elf narrows her eyes warily.>

I can take you to Farondis... but first things first. These naga attacked suddenly. They take orders from one called Zarrin, in the low hills to the west.

Help me take Zarrin's head, and you'll have my ear.

passages.title: They Came From the Sea
passages.text: <The nightwatcher looks at you expectantly.>

passages.title: They Came From the Sea
passages.text:
<Idri stares at the ugly head.>

Yes, that's him.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Gug'rokk
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a formidable group and head into the depths of the Bloodmaul Slag Mines. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and free the miners of Gug'rokk's tyrannical rule.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Gug'rokk
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. The families of the rescued miners will never be able to thank you enough for eliminating Gug'rokk and his slavers.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Ner'zhul
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a resolute group of warriors and venture into the Shadowmoon Burial Grounds. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and put a stop to Ner'zhul's communion with the void before he takes all of Draenor with him.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Ner'zhul
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Putting an end to Ner'zhul and his deathly rituals will allow many to sleep better at night.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Ner'zhul
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a resolute group of warriors and venture into the Shadowmoon Burial Grounds. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and put a stop to Ner'zhul's communion with the void before he takes all of Draenor with him.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Ner'zhul
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Putting an end to Ner'zhul and his deathly rituals will allow many to sleep better at night.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Warlord Zaela
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a group of stalwart adventures and journey back to Azeroth and Upper Blackrock Spire. Activate the Challenger's Orb, enter the old home of the Blackrock clan and defeat the Ironmarch Vanguard and their new ally, Warlord Zaela.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Warlord Zaela
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Defeating the Ironmarch Vanguard at Upper Blackrockspire is a major blow to the Iron Horde and Azeroth can rest a bit more knowing Warlord Zaela's bid for revenge has been permanently dealt with.

passages.title: The Bloodshed Never Ends
passages.text:
You are insatiable, gladiator! Let none doubt your voracious appetite for destruction and death!

Imperator Mar'gok will be very pleased to see you battling upon the arena floor of the Coliseum once more!

As before, I will accept nothing less than 100 lives!

Kill or be killed, gladiator!

passages.title: The Bloodshed Never Ends
passages.text: To the victor go the spoils! All hail <name>!

passages.title: Bronze Victory
passages.text: With every victory, or claim here grows more strong.

passages.title: Gold Victory
passages.text: A complete victory! Draenor denizens will mewl for weeks as they lick their wounds, in whatever dark places they live.

passages.title: The Prophet's Final Message
passages.text:
This unassuming iridescent crystal contains some of the final thoughts of Great Prophet Velen, created sometime in the hours before he confronted Ner'zhul.

Deliver the crystal to Prophet Velen's Memorial beneath the Coliseum of Light near Karabor to hear his final message.

passages.title: The Prophet's Final Message
passages.text: The arcanum hums in your hand as you get close to the memorial.

passages.title: The Prophet's Final Message
passages.text: The shrine has dozens of niches where the Prophet's followers have placed their own memory crystals, mourning the great leader's sacrifice. You slide the crystal into an empty socket and the memorial comes to life...

passages.title: Fungal Bundle
passages.text: The umbraspore giant you killed seemed immune to the volatile spores in the area. Perhaps the odd growths you found all over its body contribute to its immunity. You grab a big, disgusting fungal lump in order to give it to the rangari for study.

passages.title: Fungal Bundle
passages.text: What did you find, <class>?

passages.title: Fungal Bundle
passages.text:
Oh - you were attacked by an Umbraspore Giant? They're very dangerous - you were brave to face one down!

This growth you found doesn't seem to be part of the giant. It's almost like another organism living in symbiosis. We'll have to study this more closely and see what benefit it conveys to the host.

Thank you, <name>. Outstanding work!

passages.title: Proving Grounds
passages.text:
Greetings commander.

Word of your exploits has made its way back to Trial Master Rotun, and he has humbly requested to see your prowess in person. Fighting in his proving grounds would be an excellent way to spread your reputation to the farthest reaches of the Alliance, and beyond.

If you're interested in proving yourself, talk to me to enter Trial Master Rotun's Proving Grounds.

passages.title: Proving Grounds
passages.text: Have you completed your challenge?

passages.title: Proving Grounds
passages.text:
Congratulations, commander. You have survived Rotun's trial and proven yourself powerful indeed. 

Here, take this weapon, that you may further dominate your foes in battle!

passages.title: Proving Grounds
passages.text:
Hail commander.

Word of your exploits has made its way back to Trial Master Rotun, and he has requested to see your prowess in person. Fighting in his proving grounds would be an excellent way to spread your reputation to the farthest reaches of the Horde, and beyond.
