Word of your success has already been passed on by our scouts. 

Lok'tar!

passages.title: Assault on the Temple of Sha'naar
passages.text:
Up in the hills of Tanaan Jungle, the Sargerei have converted a once-sacred temple into a den of demonic summoning.

We must attack them now, before their rituals complete. The longer we delay, the stronger our enemy grows.

passages.title: Assault on the Temple of Sha'naar
passages.text: How goes the attack, sir?

passages.title: Assault on the Temple of Sha'naar
passages.text:
Welcome back, General. Our scouts just returned with word of your success.

Well done!

passages.title: Breaching the Barrier
passages.text:
The ritual site is already prepared, and it is protected by a barrier... one that I created. I can destroy the barrier, but I will need three items currently in use at Forge Camp Vengeance.

If you can get those ritual items, I will meet you at the Corrupted Refuge and remove the barrier. Even if it kills me.

passages.title: Breaching the Barrier
passages.text: Not a moment too soon. He has summoned something, I fear the ritual is close to complete.

passages.title: The Cipher of Damnation
passages.text:
Your ally and I will remove this barrier now, though it will take a greater part of our strength. What lies beyond will not be easy.

Gul'dan will have empowered an elemental lord with the Cipher, driving it insane. He will use it to destroy the link between the elements and Draenor. If you destroy that elemental, we could recover the Cipher.

passages.title: The Cipher of Damnation
passages.text:
You have saved us all. The Cipher has become fragmented with Cyrukh's death. This means its guardians can hide the shards all over Draenor so the chances of piecing it together will be impossible.

This victory will echo through the halls of your warriors and spur them to greater deeds. Gul'dan can continue plotting... he will fail...

passages.title: Will of the Thorignir
passages.text:
In the summit of storms the dragons await. Born of the gods, they will test your will. 

They roost above Hrydshal, where their children serve the Drekirjar. But they are no allies to man or vrykul, and so you must earn their blessing as they see fit.

A friend of yours awaits in Hrydshal, no doubt searching for the answers you now possess. Go to her, and together, you will test your might against the storm!

passages.title: Will of the Thorignir
passages.text:
It's good to see you, <name>. Greymane sent me away to scout this village for more information on the Aegis. 

I haven't gleaned much so far, other than that the locals here don't seem so friendly. Of course, when are they ever?

I hope your search fares better.

passages.title: Strange New Ores
passages.text:
You smell that, smith? Ahhhh... that there's the smell of opportunity.

Dalaran's taken us to some strange new shores, filled with mysterious metals. I'm tethered to my shop here, but you... you've got the freedom to explore and mine at will.

Bring me something interesting, and we'll see what we can make with it.

passages.title: Strange New Ores
passages.text: Come up with anything interesting?

passages.title: Strange New Ores
passages.text: Fascinating...

passages.title: Leysmithing Mastery
passages.text: Well, now that we have the flux we can put it to work and see how it goes. Why don't you take a crack at it this time and make some gauntlets for me. I'll observe your work... from a distance.

passages.title: Leysmithing Mastery
passages.text: Did it work? I haven't heard an explosion yet.

passages.title: Leysmithing Mastery
passages.text: Excellent work! This new flux may do wonders for other craftable materials as well.

passages.title: Nature Provides
passages.text:
This is interesting, it says that leystone reacts violently with anything it views as a contaminant. Our foreign-mined flux was enough to cause the small explosion.

Local ingredients, however, have learned to coexist with leystone. Up in Highmountain, an herb called foxflower grows that can be turned into a suitable flux.

Go and gather some foxflower that we can turn into a usable flux.

passages.title: Nature Provides
passages.text: How goes the search for foxflower?

passages.title: Nature Provides
passages.text: Excellent work. Let's get these turned into flux right away.

passages.title: Grayheft
passages.text:
Our tribe regularly crafts legplates out of leystone. I will share our pattern with you... if you do me a favor.

My father fell to the drogbar several years ago, and they took his hammer as a trophy. That hammer was in my family for countless generations. Now, it languishes in the hands of the vile drogbar, Kubrul.

I would very much like to have it back.

passages.title: Grayheft
passages.text:
I have no patterns for helms or boots.

A tauren who cannot survive a few blows to the hoof has no place in battle. Boots are of little use to us.

A helm is a coward's armor. I am sorry if this offends you, but it is true.

Legplates, however, do play a vital role. I will gladly share this pattern with you, once you bring me my father's hammer.

passages.title: Grayheft
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

Thank you.

passages.title: Leystone Hoofplates
passages.text:
Here, bring these hoofplates to Mei Francis, down at the mounts and pets store, to get your mount properly shod.

I'll share the pattern when you return.

passages.title: Leystone Hoofplates
passages.text:
Now that Mei's fit the plates to your mount, you should be able to put them on easily yourself.

Oh, and before I forget, here's the pattern. Enjoy!

passages.title: Leystone's Potential
passages.text:
As I'm sure you've deduced, all of the leystone recipes you know can be improved.

By learning to harness leystone's true potential, you can reduce the amount of material you use and still yield an equivalent result. Here, I'll show you.

We'll start, as one does, with the humble bracer. This particular piece of armor benefits from the addition of brimstone runes. See for yourself.

passages.title: Leystone's Potential
passages.text: Keep it up, <class>.

passages.title: Leystone's Potential
passages.text:
Solid work.

Leystone is a fickle metal. Its armguards benefit from the addition of brimstone, but to improve the production of shoulderpads? Enchanting dust. Helms benefit from uncarved gemstones. And so on.

passages.title: Leystone Mastery
passages.text:
Smiths that seek access to the Firmament Stone must first prove complete mastery over leystone.

Craft an entire set of Leystone Armor, then submit it to me for inspection. Thala can provide you with an armor stand.

passages.title: Leystone Mastery
passages.text: Remember, <name>: I do not tolerate sloppy work.

passages.title: Leystone Mastery
passages.text:
<The tauren carefully looks over your handiwork, brows furrowed.>

You've learned some things, I see.

Very well. You have succeeded.

passages.title: A United Force
passages.text:
The paladins of Azeroth must stand united behind a single leader. With Tirion's passing, you are the one most worthy to wear the mantle of Highlord.

If you agree to accept this duty, inscribe your name into the Libram of Ancient Kings and I will address the masses on your behalf.

The Order of the Silver Hand is reborn, with you as its champion!

passages.title: A United Force
passages.text: Yes, Highlord?

passages.title: A United Force
passages.text:
We've done it, Highlord <name>.

The Order of the Silver Hand is reborn!

passages.title: We Need a Shipwright
passages.text:
Whatever be left of da Iron Horde be fallin' back ta Tanaan Jungle, where Gul'dan is turnin' them into sumthun' even worse. A frontal assault be suicide.

But da seas be open. If we attack by both land an' sea, Gul'dan got ta fall back somewhere. <name>, it be time ta build a shipyard!

We need local resources. Go to da Iron Docks. Gazlowe's boys are already there. Gather any equipment ya find, and see if ya can recruit us a proper Horde Shipwright!

passages.title: We Need a Shipwright
passages.text:
Commander! I was hoping some backup would arrive. This place is going crazy. The Iron Horde retreated from the Foundry and now, under Gul'dan's orders, they're using these docks to flee to Tanaan.

But my people found something that might interest you, if you act fast...

passages.title: Hook, Line, and... Sink Him!
passages.text:
I can build you a shipyard. And not some wasteful piece of over-engineering like this place.

But I'm going to need my blueprints. My work was confiscated when Gul'dan turned this harbor over to Admiral Knar.

<Roark spits.>

Gul'dan's green poison courses through Knar's veins. He's calling the shots from on high. We'll need to grapple up there to take him out.

passages.title: Hook, Line, and... Sink Him!
passages.text: I will rebuild.

passages.title: Hook, Line, and... Sink Him!
passages.text:
<Solog Roark takes in the view of his harbor one final time.>

We built it all for nothing, <class>. Gul'dan will claim whatever your troops do not destroy.

Next time, I will build something that will last.

passages.title: We Meet at Light's Hope
passages.text:
With you on our side, I know the Legion will fall! But before we march on the Broken Isles, we must put Highlord Tirion to rest.

There is but one place suitable for a paladin of his caliber... Light's Hope Sanctum, a secret bastion of the Light hidden beneath our chapel.

Paladins the world over are on their way to the ceremony. I know Tirion would want you there most of all.

passages.title: We Meet at Light's Hope
passages.text:
It is fitting that you are here.

Time and again, you have fought to save our world. Now, I fear I must ask you to undertake an even greater act of service.

passages.title: Assault on the Throne of Kil'jaeden
passages.text:
The Shadow Council are summoning their demonic masters upon a mountain they are calling the Throne of Kil'jaeden. Make no mistake; This is the most dangerous region in Tanaan.

Gather together a war party and assault the Throne of Kil'jaeden before the Legion gains a foothold here!

passages.title: Assault on the Throne of Kil'jaeden
passages.text:
Welcome back, commander. Our scouts just returned with word of your success.

Well done!

passages.title: Assault on the Throne of Kil'jaeden
passages.text:
The Shadow Council are summoning their demonic masters upon a mountain they are calling the Throne of Kil'jaeden. Make no mistake; This is the most dangerous region in Tanaan.

Gather together a war party and assault the Throne of Kil'jaeden before the Legion gains a foothold here!

passages.title: Assault on the Throne of Kil'jaeden
passages.text:
Word of your success has already been passed on by our scouts. 

Lok'tar!

passages.title: Will of the Thorignir
passages.text:
In the summit of storms the dragons await. Born of the gods, they will test your will. 

They roost above Hrydshal, where their children serve the Drekirjar. But they are no allies to man or vrykul, and so you must earn their blessing as they see fit.

A friend of yours awaits in Hrydshal, no doubt searching for the answers you now possess. Go to her, and together, you will test your might against the storm!

passages.title: Will of the Thorignir
passages.text:
These vrykul are so boring! Why does Nathanos send me on missions like this? Does he really think the Aegis is here?

I hope you've come to stir up some trouble.

passages.title: A Grapple a Day
passages.text:
So some old magic vrykul is helping us out? I guess that's good, but this trial of yours might be tricky. You see, the only way up that mountain, is through those big walls.

You know, the ones with the mean-looking drakes on them.

I scouted a bit, but couldn't get too far without those drakes trying to make lunch out of poor Duchess. The vrykul have them trained, which can't be good.

I say we sneak in. I managed to snag a few grapple launchers earlier. Grab one and meet me outside the city walls.

passages.title: A Grapple a Day
passages.text: Yes, that should do quite nicely.

passages.title: No Wings Required
passages.text:
That thing looks like it's got the range to get us over the wall. There's a good spot to hook onto right past us - you should be able to spot it from here.

Once you're inside, do me a favor and see if you can distract the guards so I can slip through. I'll see what else I can find out about these vrykul.

passages.title: No Wings Required
passages.text:
Those vrykul were so distracted seeing someone flying through their village, they never noticed me slip by. 

I hope that didn't get you too much unwanted attention.

passages.title: To Weather the Storm
passages.text:
When I was scouting this place out, I noticed the vrykul here are no strangers to the treacherous mountain path we're trying to get to. They've got some specialized equipment they're using, and if I were you I'd try to get my hands on some.

You'll want to find some climbing treads to keep your grip and an oiled cloak to keep you dry. They've also got these stones they carry to keep the lightning at bay, so you'll want to pick one of those up as well.

passages.title: To Weather the Storm
passages.text: Were you able to get all the gear you needed?

passages.title: To Weather the Storm
passages.text:
Well, the sizing might be a bit big, but I think you can make them work. 

That path doesn't look pleasant, so it'll help to be prepared.

passages.title: Impalement Insurance
passages.text:
It looks like the elements aren't the only thing you'll need to worry about going up that path. Those harpoon launchers on the wall look pretty nasty, and unless we take them out first, they're likely to make short work of anyone trying to scale that path.

They're up on top of the walls, so you'll need to use that grapple launcher to get to them. Just try not to end up drake food!

passages.title: Impalement Insurance
passages.text:
We won't have to worry about those scrap heaps anymore! 

It looks like we've got a hitch in our plan though. That bridge was the only way up.

passages.title: Another Way
passages.text:
Wait, do you still have that grapple launcher? I think you can still get to the path if you can launch from the top of that tower. The gap doesn't seem too bad there.

Of course, we'll have to take out the big guy out front first. He looks tough, but I think we have a chance if we can flank him.

passages.title: Another Way
passages.text: This should be a piece of cake!

passages.title: Another Way
passages.text:
What a fight! 

And here I thought this place would be boring.

passages.title: Above the Winter Moonlight
passages.text:
There, it looks like there's a good spot to launch to right across from here. This path should take you all the way to the top.

According to my intel, your dragons should be up there. Let's just hope that they're still in a state to help you.

passages.title: Above the Winter Moonlight
passages.text:
You are here for the trial? I'm afraid you might be too late.

This battle with these Felskorn has taken its toll. I am too weak to grant you the power you seek...

But perhaps you may be able to help...

passages.title: The Farmsteads
passages.text:
Forgive us, stranger. Mayor Heathrow has been under a lot of stress recently.

I can't blame him: his own daughter, Penelope, has been missing for two days.

In fact, we could use information on several farmsteads to the south: Mayor Heathrow's house, Granny Marl's farm, and the Radcliffes' dock. Can you go check on the situation out there?

Help us, and perhaps the mayor's heart will soften.

passages.title: The Farmsteads
passages.text: How does it look out there?

passages.title: The Farmsteads
passages.text:
I'm sorry for my suspicion earlier. We're all on edge with the recent attacks.

I couldn't be more grateful to you and your friend.

Thanks to you, our situation is under control now. We've got a lot of rebuilding to do, but we'll survive.

passages.title: Answering Aggression
passages.text:
I weep for the Nightborne this day.

<Silgryn gestures out the door.>

Elisande demonstrates the ultimate disdain for her people. So many lives... wasted!

All to relay a message: This is what happens to those who defy her.

<name>, my friend, we must answer her. We must show her that she cannot slay her people without retribution.

Fight back, <name>.

passages.title: Answering Aggression
passages.text: It had to be done.

passages.title: The Sword of Truth
passages.text:
Lord Ravencrest's army rises from the dead, but I believe they are controlled by Gul'dan's will.

Take this - Lord Ravencrest's blade, Fal'shathil. It was known for a unique, magical quality. Those who gazed upon its mirrored blade found themselves unable to deny the truth.

Take the blade and plant it in the ground. Attack the night elven ghosts near its light. Once they are weakened in its presence, perhaps they will regain their senses.

passages.title: Competitive Exorcise
passages.text:
Think you're good at sending demons back to the hell from whence they came? Show me!

I once bagged 15 in under 10 minutes. Do better than that and there'll be brew money waitin' for ya.

passages.title: An Urgent Gathering
passages.text:
A critical decision must be made, <name>.

The Legion devastated our forces at the Broken Shore. The mightiest army this world has ever known was reduced to cinders in moments.

We must gather those with the conviction to save our home. Travard of Tyr's Guard and Orik Trueheart have each made plans to do just that, but we must not let them walk alone.

I ask that you seek them out and guide them to Krasus' Landing so that we may make this decision together.

passages.title: An Urgent Gathering
passages.text: Thank you for helping us gather together, <name>. We must stand united.

passages.title: The Rook's Guard
passages.text:
Black Rook Hold is not the same place I knew. Its walls have crumbled, a ghostly echo of its former glory.

If Lord Ravencrest has returned, then surely he will have his former officers at his side.

Kester Farseeker, captain of the guard.

Trelan Shieldbreaker, peerless master of maces.

Starlys Strongbow, who could split arrows while blindfolded.

If we stand any chance of entering the tower itself, they must be eliminated.

passages.title: The Rook's Guard
passages.text: Warriors and fighters came from across kaldorei lands to pledge loyalty to Master Ravencrest. We would have followed him to the ends of the earth.

passages.title: The Rook's Guard
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. May their spirits be at peace.

passages.title: Stop the Bombardment
passages.text:
Jace's wards are not going to hold out much longer. We need someone to go out there and make sure those Legion devastators are destroyed.

<Kayn pointedly looks at you with his spectrally-enhanced vision.>

passages.title: Stop the Bombardment
passages.text:
True leadership is hard to come by. Leading from the front is an even rarer trait.

We are just about ready to assail Brood Queen Tyranna's command center.

passages.title: The Keystone
passages.text:
<name>, Brood Queen Tyranna is just ahead in the command chamber. The others already charged in. She has the Sargerite Keystone in her possession.

Finally, the object of all our sacrifice is at hand.

passages.title: The Keystone
passages.text: <name>, are you ready?

passages.title: The Keystone
passages.text: Now that we have the keystone in our possession, there is just one last thing left to do...

passages.title: Set Them Free
passages.text:
Cyana went down to the Molten Shore. She was going to help some of the demon hunters who came in through the gateway ahead of us. Instead, she got herself into trouble.

This inquisitor revealed they're being held prisoner by some new type of demon called a 'jailer'. The thing sucks the souls out of its victims. I doubt they can hold out much longer.

passages.title: Set Them Free
passages.text: Some of our demon hunters are missing. Did you see them back on the Molten Shore?

passages.title: Set Them Free
passages.text:
Their souls were being sucked dry by a jailer demon?

The Burning Legion in this place is far more powerful and brutal than we have ever seen before.

passages.title: Enter the Illidari: Shivarra
passages.text:
Our Shivarra demonesses are waiting at the Black Temple. It's a gamble bringing them here... they used to be part of the Burning Legion after all. But, they are some of the most powerful in Lord Illidan's arsenal.

<Jace looks at you for a long moment.>

I have a feeling that the ultimate sacrifice is going to have to be made in order to summon them in.

passages.title: Enter the Illidari: Shivarra
passages.text:
Grim. But demon hunters are no strangers to sacrifice. We have given everything to become what we are.

The Legion will fall. We await your orders, <name>.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Nal'ryssa's Sisters
passages.text:
I was not the only miner in my family. I was the youngest of four sisters.

I say "was" because the other three are gone.

Two of them went too far. They overloaded their bodies with felslate and succumbed to the will of Sargeras. They are more demon than elf, now.

The third, I have not heard from in quite some time. The last I heard, she was investigating the Darkheart Thicket.

I fear she may have fallen, too - one way or the other.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Nal'ryssa's Sisters
passages.text: Any sign of my sister?

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Nal'ryssa's Sisters
passages.text:
Yes, this is my sister's ring.

The fact that you found it on a demon's corpse suggests that she has either fallen in battle or, like my other sisters, thrown in her hat with the demons themselves.

Thank you for bringing this to me. We don't have many spare materials here on the front lines... but I can do without these.

passages.title: Infernal Brimstone Analysis
passages.text:
In order to mine Infernal Brimstone, we first need to understand the way in which ore comes into being. I currently have three of my apprentices doing research on different ores around the world.

Find Forinn Stoneheart in Deepholm, Rhol Landers in Twilight Highlands and Krul Rockhorn in Icecrown and collect any information they've gathered on the ore at those locations.

passages.title: Infernal Brimstone Analysis
passages.text: What's that you've got there, boy?

passages.title: Infernal Brimstone Analysis
passages.text: Fascinating...

passages.title: Orders for Your Captains
passages.text:
All that is left is to deliver your orders to our Illidari captains. The mightiest of the Legion's forces have arrayed themselves within the volcano. But, they will not remain on the defensive for long.

We must strike first and we must strike hard.

Once we destroy them, we can fly up to the command ship, defeat Brood Queen Tyranna, and take the keystone for our own. Lord Illidan will be pleased.

passages.title: Orders for Your Captains
passages.text: Are we ready to commence the assault?

passages.title: Orders for Your Captains
passages.text:
Our forces have engaged the Legion.

Soon we will stand together victorious with Lord Illidan at the Black Temple.

passages.title: Their Numbers Are Legion
passages.text:
Yes, those devastators must be silenced, but there's also a great deal more to be done.

Despite the odds, we're counting on you. The Brood Queen's primary leaders are in control of the volcano. They must be killed. We must smash the Legion and do anything else necessary to achieve absolute victory.

passages.title: Their Numbers Are Legion
passages.text:
I am in complete agreement. From where I'm standing, you utterly decimated their forces.

What do you think? Are we ready to fly up to that command center and take the Sargerite Keystone?

passages.title: The Runes that Bind
passages.text:
The stone tablet here describes a ritual where a powerful spirit can be broken into weaker pieces by binding them to special runestones. It looks like the Bonespeakers may be using this very ritual to weaken the spirit of Ashildir.

It may be impossible to summon her with her spirit so weakened. The rituals must be stopped.

passages.title: The Runes that Bind
passages.text:
These mystics have gone to great lengths to weaken Ashildir. 

We must hope that her spirit is strong enough for the wakening.

passages.title: Unused
passages.text:
<Oronok adjusts his posture and stands to his full height.>

I had to be sure, <name>. And to be sure, I had to test you. Please excuse the little masquerade. I am as much a farmer as you are <female/male>. Which is to say, not at all.

If you are to recover the Cipher of Damnation, you will need to listen to what I have to tell you. When you are ready, let me know and I will tell you the story.

passages.title: Assault on the Fel Forge
passages.text:
The Iron Horde continue to bring in reinforcements from all over Draenor to reinforce their position at Hellfire Citadel. If we don't cut off the flow of supplies then we risk losing control of our plans in Tanaan.

A strategic attack to the supply lines at Ironhold Harbor is just the thing to keep the Iron Horde on the defensive and maintain our momentum.

passages.title: Assault on the Fel Forge
passages.text:
The Iron Horde continue to bring in reinforcements from all over Draenor to reinforce their position at Hellfire Citadel. If we don't cut off the flow of supplies then we risk losing control of our plans in Tanaan.

A strategic attack to the supply lines at Ironhold Harbor is just the thing to keep the Iron Horde on the defensive and maintain our momentum.

passages.title: Tearing down the Legion
passages.text:
A piece of paper is tacked to the controls. On it is a tally of demons slain by the previous pilot.

Your ego demands satisfaciton.

passages.title: Return to the Broken Shore
passages.text:
Fear not, <name>. I'm angry, but I don't chase my own death.

We will fly in and scout the ideal point of attack. The demons are still drunk on their victory, but we will put a swift end to their revelry!

Take my spare mount and we will fly to the Broken Shore. There we will bring honor to our dead.

passages.title: Return to the Broken Shore
passages.text: Welcome to Skyhold, hero. Normally one must die to gain entrance, but times have changed.

passages.title: Secrets of Highmountain
passages.text:
Mayla's father, Ulan, was our last high chieftain. He was slain trying to stop the Underking from seizing the Hammer of Khaz'goroth.

I have watched Mayla all her life and can tell you she has both the courage and the strength to wear the mantle of High Chieftain.

She needs only our help to realize it herself.

Will you meet us at the city entrance along the southern bluff? There is a ritual that might help, but we will need your aid to survive it.

passages.title: Secrets of Highmountain
passages.text: Ah, thank you for coming. Mayla is as stubborn as her father if not more so.

passages.title: His Name Was... Stormstout
passages.text:
The land is ripe with rumors of an unusual pandaren monk whose power was matched only for his appetite for brew.

He was traveling with his young niece who's mouth seems to get them into a lot of trouble.

The locals say these two were headed to the Valley of the Four Winds. You should meet him! Just... watch out for that right hook.

passages.title: His Name Was... Stormstout
passages.text:
Ha ha! You were sent by Bolo? The "Keg Mender," right? From the Drunken Hozen?

How is his eye healing? Is his friend still hung over?

Ahh... that was an enjoyable evening.

passages.title: Sew It Begins
passages.text:
Every time Dalaran takes us to a new shore, I get anxious over what types of fabric and cloth we might find below.

Threads imbued with magic? Something demonically-tinged?

Ugh, I hope it's not FURS again.

You're an adventurer... and tailor to boot. Head on down there and see what you can scrounge up!

passages.title: Sew It Begins
passages.text: I wouldn't mind working with some cashmere...

passages.title: Sew It Begins
passages.text:
Now this... this I can work with!

Reminds me of some old night elven festival cloth I've seen.

passages.title: This Should Be Simple... Right?
passages.text:
I have plenty of silk patterns that we can put this cloth to work on.

Help me to prepare the materials, <name>. We're going to put this cloth to good use and make you a new robe.

passages.title: This Should Be Simple... Right?
passages.text: We're back in business again. How exciting!

passages.title: This Should Be Simple... Right?
passages.text:
That's a shame. Without the ability to do any stitching, we can hardly do anything with this fabric.

<Tanithria pouts.>

Still, there ARE patterns we know that don't require stitching. Shoulderpads are easy, and belts should be a cinch.

passages.title: So You Think You Can Sew
passages.text:
Very good, I think we're ready to begin.

<Lyndras steals a glance at your powerful weapon. A look of hunger washes over his face before he shakes it off and continues.>

Let's prepare our materials and make the robe and bracers that you so rightfully deserve!

passages.title: So You Think You Can Sew
passages.text: You're pretty lucky to have found me.

passages.title: So You Think You Can Sew
passages.text:
There you have it!

No, no, don't thank me. I'm just happy to have been of service.

passages.title: Advanced Needlework
passages.text:
You've already learned the patterns for bracers, belts, epaulets, and of course, robes. Unfortunately, your technique was wasteful... you need a better method.

That's where our needles come in.

Here, I'll show you how to improve the process of these patterns.

passages.title: Advanced Needlework
passages.text: Keep your eye on your needlework. Don't lose focus now.

passages.title: Advanced Needlework
passages.text: Now isn't that just lovely. Go on, try it out yourself!

passages.title: Sew Far, Sew Good
passages.text:
Your tailoring skill really is impressive and, although I don't have my patterns with me, I do have some patterns memorized. One of those patterns is for a simple bag.

Follow my lead, <name>.

passages.title: Sew Far, Sew Good
passages.text: There's nothing quite like a new bag.

passages.title: Sew Far, Sew Good
passages.text:
There you have it. Not the best bag in the world, but it's better than most.

I want to apologize again for running off, <name>. My hunger... err, curiosity... occasionally gets the better of me. I promise it will not happen again.

passages.title: Left Behind
passages.text:
I do truly want to help you work on your tailoring, but without my patterns or my supplies, there isn't much more I can do save for teaching you what little I remember.

If my memory still serves true, you're just missing a good pattern for some gloves and a hood.

The first thing I need you to do is grab a few things from where you first met me. Here's what I need...

passages.title: Left Behind
passages.text: I had no clue I'd be magically teleported here, otherwise I would have gathered my things myself.

passages.title: Left Behind
passages.text:
Excellent! It's always nice to have familiar things.

This will make instructing you much easier for me.

passages.title: Eye of Azshara: The Depraved Nightfallen
passages.text:
In order to craft the gloves, we'll require a special item. This will be no easy task to recover it, <name>.

The naga of Azsuna are said to be hard at work trying to summon a terrible creature into this world.

The creature's heart holds immense energy that we can use to channel into the gloves, making them incredibly powerful.

I need... I mean, we need that heart if we are to produce a suitable pair of gloves for someone of your presence.

passages.title: Eye of Azshara: The Depraved Nightfallen
passages.text: What were you able to find?

passages.title: Eye of Azshara: The Depraved Nightfallen
passages.text:
Lyndras ran off again before you could return, <name>. He left a note and a pattern for you.

The note reads,

"I'm sorry, <name>, but I'm afraid I may become a threat to the fellow tailors of this shop. I'm off to find somewhere to try and control my urges, or fall into depravity. It has been an honor training you.

Sincerely,

Lyndras"

How sad...

passages.title: The Path to Suramar City
passages.text:
I recall Lyndras mentioning a guild of tailors within Suramar City. Perhaps they could further our understanding of how to utilize this new cloth.

Unfortunately from what I've heard, they've sided with the demons and anyone opposed to them is to be killed on sight.

You must find a way to move safely within the confines of their city if we're to continue our research.

passages.title: The Path to Suramar City
passages.text: Now that you can move safely around the city, it's time to find some new masters.

passages.title: The Final Lesson?
passages.text:
Now that we have everything we need, let's work on the hood.

After we're finished, we'll move onto the gloves.

passages.title: The Final Lesson?
passages.text: Come now, <name>. Let us sew.

passages.title: The Final Lesson?
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Before long you may be the one teaching me a thing or two.

passages.title: Secret Silkweaving Methods
passages.text:
Okay, done mourning! Let's look through his stuff.

<Tanithria takes a moment to leaf through Lyndras' journal. Her eyes open wide.>

Our friend has been keeping secrets from us. Look at this! Every single one of the recipes he's taught us can be improved.

Let's start simple, with some bracers. I can supply most of the materials, but you'll have to talk to Alard Schmied in the blacksmithing shop to get this powdered brimstone.

passages.title: Secret Silkweaving Methods
passages.text: These patterns are fascinating. I never knew you could get this kind of result out of simple silks.

passages.title: Secret Silkweaving Methods
passages.text:
The good news is that we can now craft more efficient patterns out of silkweave.

The bad news is that we've expended the remainder of Lyndras' knowledge. Where should we turn next?

passages.title: Master of Silkweave
passages.text:
While Tytallo is busy exacting withered genocide, it falls on me to take care of the more mundane aspects of training.

We're going to need to see how talented you are.

Craft an entire set of silkweave armor for me. Leyweaver Mithrogane can provide you with a proper mannequin for displaying it.

passages.title: Master of Silkweave
passages.text: If you wish to learn what we're about to teach you, you need a solid foundation.

passages.title: Master of Silkweave
passages.text:
Your stitching is still a little rough, but you've already mastered all of the basics.

Well done.

I don't say that very often. Savor it.

passages.title: The Queen's Grace Loom
passages.text:
Great power comes only with sacrifice. Even the most masterful tailor can only do so much with silkweave. To improve your patterns any further, bargains must be made.

You are prepared, <name>, to learn about working with Imbued Silkweave.

Use the teleportation crystal behind me, and speak with Azayna, the leader of our order.

passages.title: The Queen's Grace Loom
passages.text: Return once you've spoken with Azayna.

passages.title: The Queen's Grace Loom
passages.text:
Don't look at us that way, <name>. Selling our services to the demons may have been morally dubious, but our skills have grown exponentially since Azayna made the deal.

Continue your training with us, or don't. If you want to leave now, nobody's stopping you. If you want to learn more... we are the only game in town.

passages.title: Inspire Me!
passages.text:
I am, and always will be, a student of robemaking and dressmaking. You can keep your gloves, belts, and cloaks. Nothing beats a good robe.

I'll share my pattern for an imbued silkweave robe with you if you can teach me some of the robe and dress patterns you've learned along your tailoring journey.

passages.title: Inspire Me!
passages.text: I never turn down the opportunity to learn a new robe pattern.

passages.title: Inspire Me!
passages.text:
Not quite what I'd expected, but it was an interesting history lesson, at least. You can keep the robes, I've learned all I need just by watching you work.

Now, as promised, I shall show you what I know.

passages.title: The Call of Icecrown
passages.text:
<A powerful presence again touches your thoughts.>

I have ordered your brethren to Icecrown to prepare for the coming conflict, but I have a more important fate in mind for you. You, <name>, will be the hand of our vengeance!

Use the Death Gate to return to Acherus and I shall reveal your role in this.

passages.title: The Call of Icecrown
passages.text: It is time to begin, <name>.

passages.title: The Call of Icecrown
passages.text:
The Lich King made a wise choice in giving you those blades, <name>. You've more then proven yourself worthy of them.

I have to admit though, I'm glad it wasn't me, I'm through with having magical weapons dictate my fate.

passages.title: To Farahlon!
passages.text:
<name>, have you ever heard of Farahlon? Archmage Vargoth would never stop talking about it - beautiful fields and forests dotted with natural crystalline formations that make it the magical nexus of Draenor. It's nearly impossible to get to. The magical storms in the seas around it are frequent and unpredictable.

For your ring, we'll need a magical artifact from Farahlon. You will need an absolutely top-notch crew to sail safely to the region and get back alive. Choose carefully and get me that artifact!

passages.title: Ogres of the Deep
passages.text:
It might surprise you to know that at its peak the Gorian ogre empire had a small but powerful navy. It probably wouldn't surprise you to learn that many of its largest warships sunk. They were built out of stone.

I've found an old chart indicating the last-known position of "The Emperor's Foot," lost at sea with a valuable artifact I need. An ogre decoder.

Right! To salvage it you'll need a submarine and a crack crew. This is an extremely dangerous mission which is why I'm giving it to you.

passages.title: Unused - The Fish Must Flow
passages.text:
Our village is running low on food, and undead spies from Black Rook Hold have started targeting our fishers.

It's a surgical move, hitting our people and our food supply all at once.

Help us out and send those ghosts a message. Pare down their forces and bring back the food they've stolen.

passages.title: The Time to Strike
passages.text: This configuration of the stars causes an unusual vibration in the crystals strewn across Draenor, relics of the ancient Apexis. Some swear that the crystals will multiply when left unattended beneath the night sky, but none have seen the phenomenon firsthand. Regardless of the true cause, these crystals should be far more plentiful should you seek them out.

passages.title: The Time to Strike
passages.text: Ah, the unmistakable hum of crystals when the Apexis star shines....

passages.title: The Time to Strike
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Fortunately, a skilled diviner can use Apexis crystals to reveal oil deposits beneath the earth. I cannot teach you this art, but you may nevertheless reap its benefit.

passages.title: Meeting With the Queen
passages.text:
We can use some of that essence to complete my ritual. You'll be able to spy upon the Legion leaders and see what they're planning.

Use the nether crucible and complete the ritual.

passages.title: Meeting With the Queen
passages.text: If we don't know what they're planning, we're at a disadvantage fighting them.

passages.title: Meeting With the Queen
passages.text: That's new. She looks like some kind of spider demon. As if the Legion needed spiders...

passages.title: By Any Means
passages.text:
We need to figure out what rock Varedis is hiding under - the only way we're going to do that is by getting inside this prison.

Do what you must.

passages.title: By Any Means
passages.text: A truly impressive display.

passages.title: By Any Means
passages.text: Suramar is not far from here.

passages.title: Ship Shape
passages.text: Now that we have the blueprints, let's get started on our first ship, a transport! Speak to me when you are ready to begin construction.

passages.title: Ship Shape
passages.text: Get that ship started yet?

passages.title: Ship Shape
passages.text: We have our first ship!  Great work <name>.  I will get to work preparing her for travel to Tanaan right away.

passages.title: Critters of Draenor
passages.text: I love collecting pets, and I've picked up a few unusual pets here in Draenor. What would you say to a battle? If you can defeat my humble team, I think we'll both learn a few new tricks.

passages.title: Whispers from the Dark
passages.text:
We still have little knowledge of the Horde's activities in the region, but I'm hoping you can help change that.

Lately the woods have been crawling with Sylvanas' agents. The few we have taken out carried orders from her Dark Rangers, who are no doubt in command of her forces here.

While you're on the hunt, keep an eye out for any scouting orders. They may help us pinpoint Sylvanas' objective in the area.

passages.title: Whispers from the Dark
passages.text: What have you found?

passages.title: Whispers from the Dark
passages.text:
Excellent. The puzzle is finally coming together. 

We may not know why Sylvanas' forces are here, but I think we know where they are.

passages.title: Upgrading The Fleet
passages.text: You have been doing a great job out there commander. However, we are going to need more experience and resources to upgrade this shipyard. Once we reach our goals, we can upgrade the capacity of the shipyard to hold more ships!

passages.title: Upgrading The Fleet
passages.text: Finding success on these new naval missions?

passages.title: Upgrading The Fleet
passages.text: Great work!  We will get to work right away on the upgrade.

passages.title: Naval Domination
passages.text:
Our naval domination continues!

However, we are going to need even more experience and resources to take this shipyard to the next level. Once we reach our goals, we can upgrade the capacity of the shipyard to hold even more ships!

passages.title: Naval Domination
passages.text: Gather those resources yet?  I am ready to get this upgrade started!

passages.title: Naval Domination
passages.text: Controlling the seas of Draenor is in our grasp!

passages.title: Becoming the Ascendant
passages.text:
Our course is now clear. We must enter the vault and prevent Sylvanas from obtaining the power to create more Val'kyr. 

The entrance is barred, which is likely what has kept her out so far, but you may have already uncovered the key to this barrier.

You must become the next ascendant.

Complete the rites as depicted on the shields and take down the barrier to the vault. I will send word to Greymane of our findings - he will wish to confront Sylvanas himself.

passages.title: Becoming the Ascendant
passages.text:
It is good to see you, <name>. 

The assault on Dreadwake's Landing fared poorly, and I had thought our cause lost until Crowley informed me of your success.

Now, let's finish this!

passages.title: A Sundered Tribe
passages.text:
Dargrul didn't just take the Hammer of Khaz'goroth. He slew the High Chieftain -- my father -- to get it.

There are some who claim our tribe died with my father, and they have gone their separate ways.

But you... you look like someone they might listen to. You might convince them to return or at least send reinforcements.

Can you speak with the representatives of the three tribes?

passages.title: Dreadwake's Dilemma
passages.text:
The situation has taken a dire turn, <name>. We were unprepared for Greymane's sudden assault, with only a token force left behind at Dreadwake's Landing, and we are paying the toll.

The beach is now swarming with worgen infiltrators, and if the cannons breach our defenses, they will likely swarm in on us. We're spread too thin here to take the fight to them, but you could change that.

Wipe them out.

passages.title: Dreadwake's Dilemma
passages.text:
It looks like the ravens will feast on worgen flesh today, <class>.

Well done.

passages.title: To Skold-Ashil
passages.text:
Thanks to your initiative, <class>, the situation at Dreadwake's Landing is under control. We have no time to rest on our laurels, however - Sylvanas's mission must still be carried out.

The dark rangers are heading up operations in Skold-Ashil from the tower overlooking the river junction. Seek them out there, and see if you can aid in completing this task.

passages.title: To Skold-Ashil
passages.text:
You seem surprised to find me here? I was surprised as well, to find that my forces were unable to even breach the city of these cursed vrykul! 

The time has come to employ some different tactics, and your arrival couldn't have been more fortuitous.

passages.title: Becoming the Ascendant
passages.text:
It would seem that the engravings depict a rite of ascension, which allows the shieldmaidens to enter the vault. I believe we can use this to our advantage.

You must become the next ascendant.

Go to the temple and perform the rites. Should you need to wade through the corpses of the shieldmaidens to do so, then so be it. 

Find me when you have completed this task, and we will take the vault for the Horde!

passages.title: Becoming the Ascendant
passages.text:
The hero returns, and with the barrier disabled. I will see that you are commended for this. 

But first, we must claim this vault!

passages.title: Moose on the Loose
passages.text:
There's been chatter around the hunters' lodge about a crazed moose that is terrorizing the basin. 

I've never laid eyes on the beast myself, but they say its antlers are illuminated with magic. 

Where other lesser hunters have tried and failed, you will prevail, and collect me a one-of-a-kind trophy!

passages.title: Moose on the Loose
passages.text: I'm looking forward to hanging the antlers of an ancient spirit within the walls of the hunters' lodge!

passages.title: Moose on the Loose
passages.text: These antlers are going to look quite impressive hanging from the walls of the hunters' lodge.

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Blade's Edge Mountains!
passages.text: The Warchief is calling for champions to put an end to the ogre threat in Blade's Edge Mountains. Make your way north into the mountains, to the orcish stronghold of Thunderlord Stronghold and let Gor'drek know of our plight. Any help he can spare would be most welcome.

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Blade's Edge Mountains!
passages.text: Thank you for coming, <class>. We have many enemies here and we can use all the help we can get.

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Grizzly Hills!
passages.text:
We've received a request for help from our base in the Grizzly Hills. Go to see Conqueror Krenna.

She's attempting to secure all of the natural resources. Just watch your back around her. The word is that she's aggressive even for an orc.

You can reach her by traveling east from Dragonblight.

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Grizzly Hills!
passages.text:
Who are you?

Tell me why I shouldn't split you in two where you stand!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Grizzly Hills!
passages.text:
While we focus to hold our ground at Wintergarde and deal with the unfolding events of the Wrathgate, battalions from as far away as Westfall battle their way through the dense foliage and inhospitable denizens of Grizzly Hills. All in hopes of finding an alternate route into Icecrown.

Lieutenant Dumont, stationed at Amberpine Lodge, has enlisted the aid of able bodied citizens willing to risk life and limb in the uncharted wilds. Will you rise to meet this challenge?

passages.title: Hero's Call: Grizzly Hills!
passages.text:
Savage monsters - those Horde.

Payback will come for what they've done. You can count on at least that much, <class>.

Now, it's time to put you to work.

passages.title: Sholazar Basin
passages.text:
Hemet Nesingwary was last heard from leading an expedition into the jungle depths of Sholazar Basin. His expedition has not been heard from since.

Monte Muzzleshot is a pilot who was dispatched to provide them supplies, but he hasn't returned, either.

Archmage Pentarus in Dalaran is standing by with a flying machine to take you to the last known location of Monte Muzzleshot.

passages.title: Sholazar Basin
passages.text: Aye, Hemet's here. He's at the camp, just go northwest toward the river and you'll soon see it. And for the love of the Light, lad, have him send someone to cut me down!

passages.title: Don't Hate, Excavate!
passages.text: Well <name>, the good news is that our excavation team breached a chamber below right outside some sort of vault. The bad news is that the Horde were there too. Go down there and take a look.

passages.title: Don't Hate, Excavate!
passages.text: Good work <name>! It's not a pretty situation down there.

passages.title: Court of Blood
passages.text:
A council of orc clans has assembled and must be adjourned... permanently.

Gurtogg Bloodboil of the Bleeding Hollow, Jubei'thos of the Burning Blade, and Dia Darkwhisper of the Shadowmoon clan can all be found within the accursed walls of Hellfire Citadel.

passages.title: Amphitheater of the Eternal
passages.text:
The Exarch betrayer, Socrethar, was defeated with the assistance of Lady Liadrin and Exarch Maladaar.

But, he has returned. His vile spirit is now within the Soulbound Construct in Hellfire Citadel, and must be destroyed once again.

passages.title: Don't Hate, Excavate!
passages.text: At last <name>, you've arrived and not a moment too soon. Quick, go down into the mine and take a look at what we've discovered. You may run into some Alliance down there. It is a minor inconvenience that is easily remedied.

passages.title: Don't Hate, Excavate!
passages.text: Good work <name>! You see the mess the Alliance has made I'm sure.

passages.title: Ship Shape
passages.text: You want to take the fight to Gul'dan? You need a transport! Speak to me when you are ready to begin construction.

passages.title: Ship Shape
passages.text: Get that ship started yet?

passages.title: Ship Shape
passages.text:
It is done. Quite the beauty! You provide the army, she'll get 'em where they need to go.

I will prepare her for the trip to Tanaan.

passages.title: Upgrading The Fleet
passages.text: You have been doing a great job out there commander. However, we are going to need more experience and resources to upgrade this shipyard. Once we reach our goals, we can upgrade the capacity of the shipyard to hold more ships!

passages.title: Upgrading The Fleet
passages.text: Finding success on these new naval missions?

passages.title: Upgrading The Fleet
passages.text: Great work!  We will get to work right away on the upgrade.

passages.title: Naval Domination
passages.text:
Our naval domination continues!

However, we are going to need even more experience and resources to take this shipyard to the next level. Once we reach our goals, we can upgrade the capacity of the shipyard to hold even more ships!

passages.title: Naval Domination
passages.text: Gather those resources yet?  I am ready to get this upgrade started!

passages.title: Naval Domination
passages.text: Controlling the seas of Draenor is in our grasp!

passages.title: The Hunt
passages.text:
This hunt is yours to lead, <name> - a select few Illidari will join you to make sure Varedis meets his end.

The rest of us must stay behind; a small team will have the best chance of making it to his hold undetected.

We will meet you at Krasus' Landing to see you off when you are ready.

passages.title: The Hunt
passages.text:
What of the others? Did they...?

I see. They gave their lives for a worthy cause - the Twinblades will change the tide of this war, mark my words.

passages.title: Court of Blood
passages.text:
A council o' orc clans has assembled and must be taken care of, if ye know what I mean.

Gurtogg Bloodboil o' the Bleeding Hollow, Jubei'thos o' the Burning Blade, and Dia Darkwhisper o' the Shadowmoon clan can all be found within the accursed walls of Hellfire Citadel.

passages.title: Amphitheater of the Eternal
passages.text:
The Exarch betrayer, Socrethar, was defeated with the assistance of Lady Liadrin and Exarch Maladaar.

But, he has returned. His vile spirit is now within the Soulbound Construct in Hellfire Citadel, and must be destroyed once again.

passages.title: Give Me Sight Beyond Sight
passages.text:
Jace Darkweaver swears that for a split second he sensed a demonic presence up and behind us. He took some of our forces up to the cave just to the southeast to investigate.

They found nothing in the cave, but he is certain that something is amiss.

Would you lend him your guidance, and more importantly, your spectral sight?

passages.title: Give Me Sight Beyond Sight
passages.text:
<name>, we need you to scan the cave with your spectral sight.

We must know if there are Legion forces magically hidden within.

passages.title: Give Me Sight Beyond Sight
passages.text: I KNEW that I'd sensed something foul!

passages.title: Ashran Dominance
passages.text: The Alliance refuse to back down in Ashran. Teach them that the Horde will not stand aside while they plunder the power of the ancient ogre empire to use for their own schemes.

passages.title: Ashran Dominance
passages.text: As we feared the Horde are trying to consolidate their position here on the island by looting it, just like we feared. Get out there and show them the Alliance won't put up with their aggression.

passages.title: Empty Nest
passages.text:
I've taken an inventory of the eggs you recovered. Some among the bunch may still have a chance to hatch.

They will need to be returned to an empty nest, and with any luck, an eagle will claim the eggs as her own and watch over them once again.

There is a nest just outside the entrance, on a rocky ledge above the cave.

Be careful, <name>. The eggs are very delicate.

passages.title: Empty Nest
passages.text: If there's any hope for those eggs hatching, they'll need to be returned to their nest.

passages.title: Empty Nest
passages.text:
Thanks to you, the great eagles of Highmountain will live on.

One of the eggs I thought was too damaged to salvage appears to be hatching...

passages.title: Nursing the Wounds
passages.text:
I know why Mayla sent you. But as you have seen, the drogbar are not the only threat to Highmountain.

I will not send forces to support until we deal with the minions of High Crawliac.

If you want to help, find my shaman. He was supposed to be dispersing these fires that are ravaging my village.

He was last seen heading for his spirit lodge to the south just before these Cinderwitches descended on us.

passages.title: Nursing the Wounds
passages.text: These harpies are all over the place!

passages.title: Nursing the Wounds
passages.text:
Julan is dead? He was a good shaman and full of life. Not as morbid as some of these spiritwalkers.

I will miss his laughter tonight.

passages.title: Get Your Mix On
passages.text:
Let's see... potion stains on your tabard, crushed herbs on your boots... I know a fellow alchemist when I see one!

We will do good work together, the two of us. I trust you're not averse to learning new tricks.

Be sure to use my state-of-the-art alchemy table. I built her myself!

passages.title: Get Your Mix On
passages.text: I hope you're making good use of my alchemy table. It's my pride and joy!

passages.title: Get Your Mix On
passages.text: I trust you were successful in making the potions? This will be the first step in building trust between us.

passages.title: A Dormant Burner
passages.text:
I've heard that someone over in the engineering shop is selling a burner that might be usable. You could likely negotiate a fairer price than I could!

The shop is just across the street. I'll make a note on your map for you.

passages.title: A Dormant Burner
passages.text: It's a good thing the other crafters around here make such items. I couldn't imagine wasting my time on such endeavors.

passages.title: A Dormant Burner
passages.text:
Ah, this burner is exactly what we need for the alchemy table!

Wait just a moment... No, no, this will never do!

passages.title: Furbolg Firewater
passages.text:
Oh! I recognize these corks you brought me, <name>. I recently acquired several from a furbolg tribe in Val'sharah. They need sturdy corks to keep a tight seal on that potent firewater they brew.

We need more firewater potions--the corks would make an ideal addition to our alchemy table!

passages.title: Furbolg Firewater
passages.text: Did you find more firewater potions? I bet it's tempting to take a swig!

passages.title: Furbolg Firewater
passages.text: These potions have the corks we need for the alchemy table. Another successful endeavor!

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Potent Powder
passages.text:
I've heard rumors that the ancient drogbar collected powder from the residue of dragon's breath. If it's true that Neltharion's Lair lies somewhere below us, it seems a likely source.

Go there and try to find a replacement for my powder.

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Potent Powder
passages.text: What have we here?

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Potent Powder
passages.text:
You... you found some? I'm impressed, and that doesn't happen easily I'll have you know.

Now let's see what exactly it was that you found...

passages.title: Vault of the Wardens: Demon's Bile
passages.text:
The key to a crucible like this is that it must be bathed in the foulest of fel energy. I hate to say it, but the most efficient method of accomplishing such a feat is to subject it to the bile of a demon.

Yes, I said the bile of a demon. Ready to get to work?

In the Vault of the Wardens, such a demon exists. An imp mother by the name of Grimoira. The door to her room is sealed by an invisible lock.

I'd suggest bringing some Skaggldrynk with you. Use it when you get to her door.

passages.title: Vault of the Wardens: Demon's Bile
passages.text:
You did it! I must say, I was a bit concerned for your well-being, but once again you've proven resourceful.

Now that the crucible's lining is restored and it has been bathed in demon's bile, it's ready for use on the alchemy table.

Well done!

passages.title: The Price of the Black Market
passages.text:
I may have what you're looking for, burettes you say? Not a very common item.

For that, I require a moderate favor. Nothing too big, just a few things really.

A silver hair from a high-ranking archmage... the blood of a titan, and, oh... some wine and cheese.

What?! I have appetites that need satiating.

passages.title: The Price of the Black Market
passages.text: Don't take too long now. Who knows who else may be in the market for your precious burettes.

passages.title: The Price of the Black Market
passages.text:
You got the hair?!

<Ms. Xiulan laughs audibly.>

Oh, I wish I could have been there to see the look on his face. Nevertheless, a deal's a deal.

passages.title: Halls of Valor: The Prime Ingredient
passages.text:
This first ingredient can only be obtained by visiting the next realm. Fortunately for us, there's a gate in Stormheim that can take you there.

In the Halls of Valor, there is a sand that's used for polishing their architecture. Eternity Sand, it's called. I'll need an ample amount of it as the base for the new glass.

This ingredient won't be easy to work with either. I'll need something to keep me going, you know, keep my stamina up.

passages.title: Halls of Valor: The Prime Ingredient
passages.text: What a sight the Halls of Valor must be. You'll have to tell me about them sometime after your return.

passages.title: Halls of Valor: The Prime Ingredient
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Once we have everything together, I'll get started right away.

passages.title: Black Rook Hold: Heavy, But Helpful
passages.text:
The next ingredient on the list will supposedly add strength to the mix, according to Deucus. I've heard of it before, but haven't really used it.

It's called Sabelite Sulfate, and it's said the elves of Black Rook Hold use it in their blacksmithing.

Something like that won't just be lying around. You may have to delve deep into the hold to find it.

And due to its weight, I may need a concoction of yours to compensate, something to give me a bit more strength.

passages.title: Black Rook Hold: Heavy, But Helpful
passages.text: I hope Deucus was right about these ingredients. This'll be the first time I'm making something like this.

passages.title: Black Rook Hold: Heavy, But Helpful
passages.text:
<Alard takes the bag from you and peers inside.>

So this is the stuff? It's definitely true what I've heard. It is quite heavy.

passages.title: Maw of Souls: A Hope in Helheim
passages.text:
For this last ingredient, well...

<Alard begins pondering for a moment, then nods his head.>

Yes, that's the only way. For this last one, you'll need to go to the land of the damned, Helheim.

Well, not there exactly, but aboard the boat that ferries the dead across the Maw of Souls. Upon that boat may be the final ingredient we need.

It's called Dragur Dust. Keep an eye out for it.

Also, one needs to be quick when adding this ingredient. I'll need something to heighten my reflexes.

passages.title: Maw of Souls: A Hope in Helheim
passages.text: Were you able to board the ship? Did you find the dust?

passages.title: Maw of Souls: A Hope in Helheim
passages.text:
It was there? You found some?

<Alard takes the crate and opens it. He reels back from the smell.>

Yep, that's the stuff alright. By the light, does that reek.

passages.title: Hags of a Feather
passages.text:
The drogbar you freed me from were unusually aggressive. The tribe in the nearby caves seems to be apart from the rest of them, but that didn't stop the Bloodtotem from going on the offensive just in case, capturing some of their number.

That move left the woods exposed to the harpies, however. Your help dealing with these witches would not go unnoticed by Torok. Bring back their feathers as proof of death.

passages.title: Hags of a Feather
passages.text: Your size belies your strength, <name>.

passages.title: Hags of a Feather
passages.text: I could hear them screeching from here. With this victory and the defeat of the Witch of the Wood, Torok will surely be willing to see you.

passages.title: A Gift for Greymane
passages.text:
It looks like the Gilnean infiltrators brought some heavy ordnance to the fight. It's likely they intend to use them on the walls of Dreadwake's Landing.

If these could be rigged to Greymane's ship, it could make for a decisive end to his assault on the outpost.

passages.title: A Gift for Greymane
passages.text: <insert>

passages.title: A Gift for Greymane
passages.text:
By the Dark Lady's favor, you did it! I witnessed the explosion from here - there's no way that Greymane could have survived such destruction! 

You have done a great deed today for the Forsaken. Rest assured, it will be remembered.

passages.title: Destroying the Competition
passages.text:
One battle does not win the war, Commander.

That Transport isn't gonna hold up long against this Iron Horde navy. We are going to need another ship. Lucky for us, a local smuggler has supplied us with the plans we need to build Destroyers. We should construct one of these ships immediately!

passages.title: Destroying the Competition
passages.text: What is the status of the Destroyer?

passages.title: Destroying the Competition
passages.text: They lured us right into their trap, Commander.  I want revenge!

passages.title: Destroying the Competition
passages.text:
One battle does not win the war, Commander.

That Transport isn't gonna hold up long against this Iron Horde navy. We are going to need another ship. Lucky for us, a local smuggler has supplied us with the plans we need to build Destroyers. We should construct one of these ships immediately!

passages.title: Destroying the Competition
passages.text: What is the status of the Destroyer?

passages.title: Destroying the Competition
passages.text: They lured us into a trap, commander.  I want revenge!

passages.title: The Eagle Spirit's Blessing
passages.text:
The spear is linked to a spirit called Ohn'ahra. It has been tradition for us to speak with her and receive her blessing before going after the spear. She may also impart some knowledge.

If you would accompany me to Spiritwatch Point, I will summon the Eagle Spirit and ask for its blessing in the coming fight.

passages.title: The Eagle Spirit's Blessing
passages.text: We've done it!

passages.title: The Eagle Spirit's Blessing
passages.text: We saved the Eagle Spirit and received her blessing. I feel even more confident we will get Talonclaw now!

passages.title: Assaulting the Haglands
passages.text:
Proceed on foot into the Haglands and slay any harpies you find.

Quell their numbers!

We will provide air support and force your prey to the ground where you can deal with them.

Show these witches the fury of your... well... your "you."

passages.title: Assaulting the Haglands
passages.text: It has been many years since we have had to enter the Haglands in force.

passages.title: Assaulting the Haglands
passages.text: Haha! You are covered in the feathers of your enemies.

passages.title: Unknowable Power
passages.text: The one they call Gul'dan has ruined his own people, and now seeks to ruin what remains of mine as well. The fallen outcasts at Kra'nak have already pledged themselves to Gul'dan in a false promise of a return to the skies. He has given the most powerful of his minions the power of the Apexis, but twisted in a way that I cannot explain. Bring one of these fragments to me.

passages.title: Unknowable Power
passages.text: This is simply the beginning of what you must do to save what remains of the Arakkoa.

passages.title: Unknowable Power
passages.text: As your archmage told me, the power that has warped these crystals comes from far beyond this world. I will need more help in discovering how to turn back the darkness inside my people.

passages.title: Unseen Influence
passages.text: The corruption in the Apexis has begun to affect many of my people. We are so accustomed to the power it grants us that more succumb to the whispers every day. You must bring me more samples so I can free my people from yet another curse.

passages.title: Unseen Influence
passages.text: I fear even your help may not be enough to avert the doom of the Arakkoa.

passages.title: Unseen Influence
passages.text: I will continue to need your help until this world is free of whatever terrible presence Gul'dan has invited to destroy us.

passages.title: Stonedark Relics
passages.text:
The murlocs managed to steal some of our sacred relics and carry them down into the lower cavern.

While we warm up, do you think you could go find them?

passages.title: Stonedark Relics
passages.text: We have possessed these relics for generations until the murlocs put their fishy flippers on them.

passages.title: Stonedark Relics
passages.text: You found them! Not sure how you carried them all at one time...

passages.title: You Lift, Brul?
passages.text: Do you even lift? If you can carry these weights to the statue of Liftbrul and back, maybe we can talk.

passages.title: You Lift, Brul?
passages.text: Those arms fallin' off?

passages.title: You Lift, Brul?
passages.text: Stronger than you look, little one.

passages.title: Assault on the Throne of Kil'jaeden
passages.text:
The Shadow Council are summoning their demonic masters upon a mountain they are calling the Throne of Kil'jaeden. Remember the first war, we know the destruction the legion can cause if they are unchecked.

Head to the Throne of Kil'jaeden and let's put an end to this invasion before it can begin.

passages.title: Assault on the Throne of Kil'jaeden
passages.text:
The Shadow Council are summoning their demonic masters upon a mountain they are calling the Throne of Kil'jaeden. We know the destruction the legion can cause if they are left unchecked.

Head to the Throne of Kil'jaeden and let's put an end to this invasion before it can begin.

passages.title: Cave of the Blood Trial
passages.text:
All Bloodtotem and distinguished guests must go through a trial of blood in the cavern beneath this outpost.

I hope it's a good sign that they wish you to participate in this rite of passage. You will need to show proof of your deeds, defeat a Warmonger in single combat, then perform sacrifice at an altar deep in the cavern.

passages.title: Cave of the Blood Trial
passages.text: Are you afraid of the dark?

passages.title: Cave of the Blood Trial
passages.text: They said an outsider would wield the Hammer of Khaz'goroth. I doubt you could even lift it.

passages.title: Cut Out the Heart
passages.text:
This map points out the strategic locations of the Forsaken forces around Greywatch. A marker to the east indicates an apothecary camp where Dread-Riders are being supplied from.

If you were to take out the apothecary in charge of creating this plague, it could stem the invasion and prevent the Dread-Riders from spreading the plague any further.

passages.title: Cut Out the Heart
passages.text:
To think that the Forsaken were brash enough to brew their blight in our own backyard. With the loss of their apothecary, their invasion force is left without teeth. 

You have done well, <name>.

passages.title: Infestation
passages.text:
Those bugs are destroying our crops and attack any of us who get near them.

Would you exterminate some of those vile creatures?

passages.title: Infestation
passages.text: With fewer of those insects out there, I can tend to some of the crops.

passages.title: The Flow of the River
passages.text:
We can leave Farmer Maya in charge of the farmland now that the greatest threat has been reduced.

But we aren't out of hot water just yet, <name>. The fisheries are just as important as our fields, and they are in even greater danger than the farm if what Angler Creel says is true.

passages.title: The Flow of the River
passages.text: I'm glad you arrived when you did. The drogbar are increasing their aggression as we speak.

passages.title: Well of Souls
passages.text: As you defeat Gul'dan's minions, his hold over this fel citadel weakens, allowing me to teleport you and your allies deeper into the dark halls. If I only I had some Soul Remnants - four of them, let's say - none of this would be necessary, and I could harness that power to send you directly into the upper reaches of the Citadel.

passages.title: Well of Souls
passages.text: Did you manage to find any of those Soul Remnants I mentioned?

passages.title: Well of Souls
passages.text:
A-ha! Soul Remnants!

<Khadgar cradles the Remnants briefly and focuses intently upon them.>

There, now you and your companions may access the upper level of the Citadel directly.

A-ha! Soul Remnants!

There, now you and your companions may access the upper level of the Citadel directly.

passages.title: The Fel Spire
passages.text:
This would all be so much simpler if we could just teleport directly to the top of the Citadel, where Gul'dan works his dark magic, wouldn't it? But while demonic power fills the halls, my magic cannot penetrate to such heights.

If only I had powerful Fel Essences to work with, I could attune my magic to their defenses and bypass them. But the only place you might find such concentrated fel energy would be atop the Citadel itself. What a conundrum....

passages.title: The Fel Spire
passages.text: Have you been to the top of the Citadel so that I can send you to the top of the Citadel?

passages.title: The Fel Spire
passages.text:
You did it!

Strange, these Fel Essences bear the unique signature of the pit lord Mannoroth.... How in the world did you manage to... It's almost like you've been here before!

<Khadgar peers at you curiously.>

No matter! With this power, I can send you and your companions straight to the top of the Citadel!

passages.title: Bloodied Blades of Zeth'Gol
passages.text:
Them Bleeding Hollow orcs do blood magic - like voodoo but it hurt more. They cut their own flesh. Most of 'em carry curved ritual blades for carvin' themselves up.

Bring me them blades, commander. We can turn their power against 'em.

passages.title: Bloodied Blades of Zeth'Gol
passages.text:
Watch your back in Bleeding Hollow lands. They fight dirty.

'Course, we fight dirtier.

passages.title: Bloodied Blades of Zeth'Gol
passages.text:
<Denjai runs one of the blades along his thumb. A sinister smile spreads across his elongated face.>

These will do, commander. These'll do nice.

passages.title: A Little Wetwork
passages.text:
What be left of the Iron Horde is comin' to Tanaan through Ironhold Harbor. If we knew who was comin' and when, we could use our shipyard to cause some chaos.

Go to Ironhold Harbor and fish up some intelligence!

passages.title: A Little Wetwork
passages.text: Whatcha learn for us, commander?

passages.title: A Little Wetwork
passages.text:
Yes, yes, this be the good stuff commander.

I'll send a messenger with these to your shipyard. Don't you worry none, me hunters slip through this jungle like they was invisible.

passages.title: Blood of Fallen Brothers
passages.text:
Orcs that drink Gul'dan's poison turn into fel beasts. Soulless savages.

Lady Liadrin an' the Blood Knights think maybe there be a way back. They be wantin' samples of blood from freshly turned orcs. Get their blood, <name>!

You be findin' fel orcs all over Tanaan, but the Iron Front, the Fel Forge, and the Throne of Kil'jaeden is where you find the most.

passages.title: Blood of Fallen Brothers
passages.text: You bleed 'em dry, commander?

passages.title: Blood of Fallen Brothers
passages.text:
I get these to Lady Liadrin then.

You really think there be a way back for these monsters, commander? You got a brighter outlook then me, mon.

passages.title: Secrets of the Shadow Council
passages.text:
Gul'dan be growin' his Shadow Council like a spider spin a web. But some of this new blood, they not so smart. They write down the secrets but don't burn 'em.

Catch his minions out in the open and bring their secrets back to me! You find them workin' with the arakkoa in da Ruins of Kra'nak or atop the Throne of Kil'jaeden.

passages.title: Secrets of the Shadow Council
passages.text: You find anything, commander?

passages.title: Secrets of the Shadow Council
passages.text: This be just what we need! I get my people at work on these right away, commander.

passages.title: Disarming Sha'naar
passages.text:
Draenei at the Temple of Sha'naar would mine these mountains for perfect crystals used to channel their magics. Now demons be lootin' the place. We gotta keep those crystals out of demonic hands, commander!

Attack the mines behind the temple and grab them crystals.

passages.title: Disarming Sha'naar
passages.text: What you find up there, commander?

passages.title: Disarming Sha'naar
passages.text:
They don't look like much, do they?

I put these in safekeeping, commander. The blood elves might know what to do with 'em.

passages.title: Harnessing Their Power
passages.text:
Ol' Grommash Hellscream found a way to weaponize the gronn. Vol'jin wants to know how.

Travel to the Iron Front and kill one of them big beasties, then bring back its war harness. You might be needin' help.

passages.title: Harnessing Their Power
passages.text: Did you break one?

passages.title: Harnessing Their Power
passages.text:
You lugged that thing all the way back here? You must got a bit of gronn-blood yourself, commander!

We send this to the goblins at Orgrimmar to take a look at.

passages.title: Pressing the Attack
passages.text: We got Gul'dan's minions on the run, commander! If you be feelin' it, we should put some pressure on some of his other strongholds as well.

passages.title: Pressing the Attack
passages.text: How goes the fight?

passages.title: Pressing the Attack
passages.text: You done it, commander! Day by day, we be conquerin' this whole Jungle.

passages.title: Tooth and Claw
passages.text:
Beyond the meager shelter of these fortress walls, the jungle closes in. Can you feel it? That is the untamed wilderness, <class>, calling forth our primal instincts. There is no better way to feel alive than to court death.

Join me in the hunt, <name>! Collect teeth from the wild beasts. The ravagers in Thornmire, the raptors in Zorammarsh - even the sea creatures along the strand and the little podling plants themselves all have teeth. Bring them to me!

passages.title: Tooth and Claw
passages.text: I trust the hunt goes well?

passages.title: Tooth and Claw
passages.text: Oh, this is quite the collection. How many of these sunk into your flesh? Exhilarating, isn't it?

passages.title: Bloodied Blades of Zeth'Gol
passages.text:
The Bleeding Hollow clan is infamous for their blood rituals. The brutes carve sigils into their flesh and create potions from the blood of their strongest warriors.

The curved ceremonial blades they use have a power all their own. Gather some of these for me. We will deprive them of these weapons and learn something about our enemy at the same time.

passages.title: Bloodied Blades of Zeth'Gol
passages.text: We draenei have had little contact with the Bleeding Hollow before this war. They were an insular clan living in one of the most hostile parts of Draenor.

passages.title: Bloodied Blades of Zeth'Gol
passages.text: What terrible instruments these are! We will learn what we can from these and then destroy them.

passages.title: A Little Wetwork
passages.text:
The shattered remnants of the Iron Horde pour into Tanaan through Ironhold Harbor. If we knew more about their fleet we could dispatch countermeasures from your shipyard in Shadowmoon.

Perhaps you could gather some naval intelligence for our cause?

passages.title: A Little Wetwork
passages.text: The Prophet said it was always wise to know one's enemy before engaging.

passages.title: A Little Wetwork
passages.text: Wonderful, wonderful. I'll send a messenger to your shipyard with the information we learned. Thank you, commander.

passages.title: Breaking Their Fel Bonds
passages.text:
Gul'dan's fel poison turns already ferocious orcs into hateful, vicious creatures with no soul. But were he here to guide us, Prophet Velen wouldn't give up on the whole race. If you could find samples of their blood, maybe we can reverse the process?

You'll find fel orcs all over Tanaan, but the Iron Front, the Fel Forge, and the Throne of Kil'jaeden are the most densely populated.

passages.title: Breaking Their Fel Bonds
passages.text: Were you able to secure some blood samples? I will not inquire as to your methods, commander.

passages.title: Breaking Their Fel Bonds
passages.text:
Thank you, commander. Our scholars will study these samples at once!

We mustn't give up hope. Our eredar brothers are seemingly lost forever, but orcs from the world of Azeroth managed to break free from the Burning Legion....

passages.title: Secrets of the Shadow Council
passages.text:
Gul'dan has been building a spy network for himself - the so-called "Shadow Council". As they struggle to control Tanaan, the Shadow Council has grown careless. Their members are out in the open, recruiting arakkoa at the Ruins of Kra'nak or summoning demons at the Throne of Kil'jaeden.

Find members of the Shadow Council and acquire any intelligence they were foolish enough not to destroy!

passages.title: Secrets of the Shadow Council
passages.text: What have you learned?

passages.title: Secrets of the Shadow Council
