passages.text: Yes, yes, so many papers... Ah, some of this is in code. It's all very crude, though. Our scholars will learn much from this. Well done commander!

passages.title: Disarming Sha'naar
passages.text:
Draenei at the Temple of Sha'naar would mine these mountains for perfect crystals to power our arcane devices. Sadly, the temple is lost to us - we have been betrayed by the Sargerei.

<name>, it is imperative that you venture into those mines and secure those crystals before the Sargerei use them in their demonic rituals. If you must kill our former brothers and sisters, so be it.

passages.title: Disarming Sha'naar
passages.text: That temple was once a place of peace and solitude. I fear it is forever corupted.

passages.title: Disarming Sha'naar
passages.text: Very good, <name>. Our scholars will be able to use these crystals to protect and empower our people.

passages.title: Harnessing Their Power
passages.text:
We have always believed that the primal creatures of Draenor could not be tamed. And yet, the Iron Horde found a way to weaponize the gronn. It would be to our advantage to learn how.

Venture to the Iron Front, slay a Wargronn, and retrieve its harness. You may want to find help.

passages.title: Harnessing Their Power
passages.text: Exarch Maladaar reports that the battlefield is in chaos. Were you able to persevere?

passages.title: Harnessing Their Power
passages.text:
My word, that device is enormous. Thank you for carrying it all the way back here.

There is so much my people can still learn about this world!

passages.title: Pressing the Attack
passages.text: Gul'dan's minions are on the run, commander! If you have the strength, now would be an opportune time to press forward and assault some of his other strongholds.

passages.title: Pressing the Attack
passages.text: Be wary of the jungle, commander.

passages.title: Pressing the Attack
passages.text: This is wonderful news, commander. We will soon have Gul'dan's ghoulish citadel completely surrounded!

passages.title: Tooth and Claw
passages.text:
These wimps lugging wood around the jungle keep talking about how dangerous it is. You know, between the ravager den to the south or the raptors that stalk Zorammarsh - hey, even the beach creatures or podlings have teeth!

What do you say you and I do a little hunting? Collect teeth from wild beasts. The bigger the beast, the more teeth. Meet me back here and we'll compare our haul!

passages.title: Tooth and Claw
passages.text: Ready to compare notes?

passages.title: Tooth and Claw
passages.text:
<Parvink is covered in bleeding scratches and shredded leaves.>

Hey, not bad! We'll call it a tie. This jungle don't scare me for nothin'.

Maybe we can hunt some more tomorrow?

passages.title: Ahead of the Game
passages.text:
The watcher Yotnar keeps the vault, and he is a fickle one. Challengers come from far and wide seeking the trials, but the watcher chooses not to see.

If you wish to catch his eye, show him you are worth being seen.

Some of these challengers await in camps throughout the Valley of the Sword. Bring their heads to Yotnar, so that he may see them, and you.

passages.title: Ahead of the Game
passages.text: An ironic gift you bring me, challenger.

passages.title: Ahead of the Game
passages.text:
It is a shame to see the first worthy challenger for the Aegis treating the trials with such disrespect. Such hubris cannot win the Aegis, for the gods will surely strike him down for his arrogance.

You, however, seem different. You have shown that you are a worthy challenger. 

I will allow you to begin the trials.

passages.title: A Trial of Valor
passages.text:
To seek the Aegis of Aggramar, a champion must complete three great trials before riding into glorious battle through the Gates of Valor. Here you will find the knowledge of the trials you must seek out, as well as the first challenge you must face.

Above us, adorning the central plateau, you will find the archive for the Trial of Valor. Seek it out, and learn where your path leads.

passages.title: A Trial of Valor
passages.text:
You have learned of the obstacles you must face. 

Do you still wish to continue?

passages.title: A Trial of Will
passages.text:
Upon the highest point of the plateau above, you will find the archive device for the Trial of Will. Seek it out to learn what awaits you in Thorim's Peak. 

Be on your guard, outsider. The one called Skovald has left behind many of his army, and they will no doubt be unfriendly.

passages.title: A Trial of Will
passages.text:
The knowledge you've gained is a powerful tool to use against your foes. 

Do not forget this.

passages.title: If At First You Fail, Try Again!
passages.text:
Looks like that Submarine had a bit more firepower than we thought! They used First Strike to hit us before we even saw it coming.

Losing ships is a part of naval battles, Commander. Luckily, we were prepared for this exact sort of situation. Speak with Yanas down at the dry docks, he should be able to help us quickly produce another Destroyer. Head back here when the ship is complete, we will have a new mission ready for you.

passages.title: If At First You Fail, Try Again!
passages.text: Get that replacement Destroyer built?

passages.title: If At First You Fail, Try Again!
passages.text: That was an amazing turn around commander!  Great work.

passages.title: Wolf Pack Attack
passages.text:
It's time to attack the pack! I've preloaded the hand cannon. All you have to do is point and shoot.

The critters should survive the blast and hit the ground running. The howlers will be distracted by the critters, allowing you to focus on killing the packleaders.

Happy hunting!

passages.title: Wolf Pack Attack
passages.text: The critter hand cannon is loaded and ready for use! Just aim for one of the packs nearby. The packleaders should be easy to kill once the howlers are distracted.

passages.title: Wolf Pack Attack
passages.text:
You made it back without any scratches. It looks like the backfire issue from the last prototype worked itself out.

A few more tweaks and I'd say this hand cannon is ready for mass production. Thanks for the help, <name>.

passages.title: A True Naval Commander
passages.text: Yes! Those are the blueprints I misplaced when I was fishing last week. These instructions match my prototype equipment one for one. Take this Blast Furnace and install it on one of our ships. This should let us break the naval blocade and expand our control of the Draenor seas.

passages.title: A True Naval Commander
passages.text: Get that equipment installed?

passages.title: A True Naval Commander
passages.text: Equipment can really make a difference out there!

passages.title: If At First You Fail, Try Again!
passages.text:
Looks like that Submarine had a bit more firepower than we thought! They used First Strike to hit us before we even saw it coming.

Losing ships is a part of naval battles, Commander. Luckily, we were prepared for this exact sort of situation. Speak with Solog down at the dry docks, he should be able to help us quickly produce another Destroyer. Head back here when the ship is complete, we will have a new mission ready for you.

passages.title: If At First You Fail, Try Again!
passages.text: Get that replacement Destroyer built?

passages.title: If At First You Fail, Try Again!
passages.text: That was an amazing turn around commander!  Great work.

passages.title: A True Naval Commander
passages.text: Yes! Those are the blueprints I misplaced when I was fishing last week. These instructions match my prototype equipment one for one. Take this Blast Furnace and install it on one of our ships. This should let us break the naval blockade and expand our control of the Draenor seas.

passages.title: A True Naval Commander
passages.text: Get that equipment installed?

passages.title: A True Naval Commander
passages.text: Equipment can really make a difference out there!

passages.title: Frozen in Time
passages.text:
The Wardens kept all kinds of dangerous monsters locked up within this Vault. Now that Gul'dan's forces have breached the walls, it's proving rather... inconvenient.

Many of our forces are occupied with containing a fearsome magma destroyer in the southern chamber. With us freshly awoken from stasis, we don't have the means to take it down. However, we might be able to reactivate the room's containment field.

Go join up with Kayn. Do whatever it takes to seal that chamber!

passages.title: Frozen in Time
passages.text: I knew you could do it, <name>. We could not let that creature escape.

passages.title: Master vs. Commander
passages.text:
I've been doing a little digging - or whatever you call digging in naval terms. Snorkeling?

Gul'dan has sent his most powerful flagship on a scouting mission to the four corners of Draenor. He is mapping out all the oceanic ley-line conjunctions. This is information that I could use to upgrade your ring... But in Gul'dan's hands, it could be catastrophic.

Scramble the fleet, <name>! Hunt down his infamous flagship, "The Master's Call," and steal that map before they complete their mission. Hurry!

passages.title: Master vs. Commander
passages.text: I hope the Master's Call hasn't sent too many of your ships to the bottom of the sea...?

passages.title: Master vs. Commander
passages.text:
Yes yes, this is it. This map is invaluable. By triangulating these oceanic junction points we can graph out Draenor's key ley lines. Hmmm... there's where I built my tower, of course. Energy also seems to converge near Karabor. And here, by the throne of elements.

Oh very good, we'll be able to put this to use very soon.

passages.title: Ironhorn Leysmithing
passages.text:
I sense great strength in you, yet you refuse to wield it. We Ironhorn use double the metal of any normal blacksmith to craft our wares.

There is also a technique in how you hammer such quantities of leystone that I will instruct you on.

Use our scrap metal and hammer out the pieces for a gauntlet. I will weld the pieces together when you are finished.

passages.title: Ironhorn Leysmithing
passages.text: I'm waiting, outsider.

passages.title: Ironhorn Leysmithing
passages.text: Your hammerwork is solid, outsider. You have separated yourself from the chaff.

passages.title: A Ring Unbroken
passages.text:
Our defeat at the Broken Shore was decisive. The Burning Legion has a foothold on Azeroth, and the best of our armies are retreating in tatters.

The elders of the Earthen Ring have called an emergency council near the heart of our world - the Maelstrom. <name>, your triumphs throughout Azeroth and Draenor are the stuff of legend. We need you more than ever.

Join me at the Maelstrom. Stormcaller Mylra will be flying there shortly - find her at Krasus' Landing here in Dalaran.

passages.title: A Ring Unbroken
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. You saved me. You saved us all.

I was... outmatched. My relationship with the elements has changed since the events on Draenor. I have some soul-searching to do. <name>, you must carry the Earthen Ring forward without me. You are the leader they need.

passages.title: For Whom the Fel Tolls
passages.text:
<Matthew eyes you up and down, growling slightly>

You wish me to help you understand this rock? First you do something for me.

The legion has brought many of its fel machines to conquer this world. Those machines are powered by cores filled with fel energy. And those cores are carried by the lowliest of their minions for distribution.

Bring me some cores and I'll give you the information you need.

passages.title: For Whom the Fel Tolls
passages.text: Have you acquired what I requested?

passages.title: For Whom the Fel Tolls
passages.text:
<Matthew lets out a gleeful howl>

Impressive.

passages.title: Wax On, Wax Off
passages.text:
I've been dead for centuries without having my grave so disturbed... The leader of the local kobolds has stolen my skull from my grave and wears it upon his head!

He's down in the cave below, but a gate blocks your path from retrieving it directly. Kobolds know their leadership by the skulls they wear, and they are unintelligent enough to believe you their leader if you have one yourself.

Kill one of their Skullcaptains and recover his Skull of Bossing Around, and they may let you into the cave.

passages.title: Wax On, Wax Off
passages.text: The desecration...

passages.title: Wax On, Wax Off
passages.text: This will work perfectly, I believe.

passages.title: The Gates of Wax
passages.text: Go talk to the Bluewax Gatekeeper and see if he will let you through to the Candleking. If you can get through by donning the skull, the smell will be worth it.

passages.title: The Gates of Wax
passages.text: What you want, stinky?

passages.title: The Voice of Thunder
passages.text:
The White Tiger has prepared a series of challenges for everyone who wants to possess the weapons of the storm.

Now you know of their power - these are the very artifacts that Ra-den himself wielded during the age of the Titans.

Come! I have led arena teams to victory across three continents. With me in your corner, you cannot lose!

passages.title: The Voice of Thunder
passages.text: We have trained our whole lives for this, <name>. We cannot fail.

passages.title: The Voice of Thunder
passages.text:
You really are the chosen one, <name>. I will gladly lay down my life for you.

Wherever you take the Earthen Ring, I will follow!

passages.title: Demon Detainment
passages.text:
The demons that escaped must be detained. Killing them is not an option. Uriah was entrusted to deliver the prisoners to Allari for interrogation, and I will not let him fail.

I've seen Uriah trap many demons. It seems... complicated, but I think I can pull it off. I'll just need you to subdue them first.

passages.title: Demon Detainment
passages.text: You must weaken the demons so I am able to trap them.

passages.title: Demon Detainment
passages.text: Thank you for you help, <name>. I will honor Uriah's memory by completing our journey to Azsuna and delivering the demon prisoners to Allari as planned.

passages.title: A Stone Cold Gamble
passages.text:
The second target is a basilisk called Stonefang that lives off the bank of the nearby river. 

I put a bigger wager on him, so if you can take him out I'll make sure you get a cut.

I'll need his jaw to verify the kill. Hurry, before those tauren get him first!

passages.title: A Stone Cold Gamble
passages.text: Did you take him out?

passages.title: A Stone Cold Gamble
passages.text:
Well, well. I half expected to find your statue on the riverbank. You're gonna get a nice payout once those tauren get back...

You haven't seen them around, have you?

passages.title: Rigging the Wager
passages.text:
Care to help settle a bet, chum?

Those tauren are Skyhorn, and they fancy themselves big-time hunters. I bet them a pretty penny that they wouldn't be able to take out some of the biggest beasts in Stormheim.

If you take em out before they do, I'll split the wager. Deal?

The first is a big eagle nesting in the foothills. They call him Spitefeather. You can bait him with some meat, but he's up pretty high, so you'll need a grapple gun to get there. I think there's one of them layin around here...

passages.title: Rigging the Wager
passages.text: You got my trophy yet?

passages.title: Rigging the Wager
passages.text:
So you took him out, eh? Those tauren are gonna be so jealous when they get back!  

Naturally, you'll have to wait till the tauren get back and pay their wager before I can give you your cut. But in the meantime, I've got another target for you.

passages.title: Eating Into Our Business
passages.text:
Greetings traveler! You are welcome to rest at our camp, but if you plan on sticking around a while, I have a proposition for you.

As you can see, the land here has been very good to us, providing a great natural bounty. Lately, however, the worg have become problematic, and are thinning the herds to unacceptable levels.

I can't take care of them all, so I will offer a bounty for every worg slain in the mesa. Return to me when you have culled their pack a bit.

passages.title: Eating Into Our Business
passages.text:
Oh, hey! You must be lookin for them tauren was camped here. They just stepped out for a bit, but Snaggle here and I - we can take care of ya!

You say they were gonna pay you for killin' some worgs, huh? No prob, bub!

I ain't got a lot of gold, but these goods are pretty valuable. Take your pick!

passages.title: Lay Them to Rest
passages.text:
I would ask a favor, outsider.

As you step through the graves of ancient heroes, you will no doubt come across spirits of the restless dead, agitated by the Bonespeakers misdeeds. They must be returned to the earth where they are buried, so that they may be judged as well.

Take this bough - it carries with it the essence of the Runewood. Channel its power into a weakened spirit, and it will return to rest.

passages.title: Lay Them to Rest
passages.text:
I see you carry a branch of the Runewood. Then it was you who laid the spirits to rest? 

Though I do not know your purpose, outsider, I appreciate what you have done for our people.

passages.title: A Stack of Racks
passages.text:
So while we're waiting here, maybe you could fetch us up some grub. Them tauren were runnin low on meats, so I'm sure they'd be thankful to have more.

I hear that musken ribs are the specialty here. The wild musken here are too lean for any good meat, but across the river there are some nice fat ones. Maybe you should check those out!

Don't worry, I'm pretty sure there aren't any dragons over there...

passages.title: A Stack of Racks
passages.text: Aint nothin like some good old meaty musken ribs, eh pal?

passages.title: A Stack of Racks
passages.text:
Oh hey, it's... you again! Of course you didn't have any trouble with those musken. You're a big, tough hero after all!

The tauren still aren't back, though. I'm a bit worried that they may have gone off and hunted a bit more that they can chew.

Oh, I'll take those ribs, though. What do you want for em?

passages.title: Only the Finest
passages.text:
Say, you're a pretty good hunter, eh? Maybe you could help these tauren out by stocking them with some rare furs. I'm sure they'd appreciate it when they got back!

I hear that Stormheim goat hair can be woven into all kinds of things. The rarest are from the silver-tail goats. I think I saw some in that mountain over there.

Why don't you go and fetch some? I'm sure them tauren would pay you handsomely!

passages.title: Only the Finest
passages.text: Make sure to get the good stuff!

passages.title: Only the Finest
passages.text:
You're back? 

I mean... hey, you're back!

Well, the tauren haven't come back yet, but no worries, I'll take that stuff off your hands! Let me show you some of my prime trade goods.

passages.title: Greymane's Gambit
passages.text:
The Skyfire is prepared to make way to Stormheim. Should we become engaged, I will require my best fighters on the front line.

This includes you, <class>.

passages.title: Greymane's Gambit
passages.text:
It seems you were spared the brunt of the explosion. If only Greymane were so lucky...

On your feet! We had better get a move on before the Forsaken are on top of us!

passages.title: The Splintered Fleet
passages.text:
Preparations have been made, and we are ready to set sail.

We must strike out at once. Do not dally, or you will be left behind.

passages.title: The Splintered Fleet
passages.text:
Hey, you're alive! I guess Withers isn't as crazy as I thought.

It's a miracle you escaped the Skyfire alive! The pieces of that thing must be scattered all over these mountains after that explosion!

passages.title: Hellfire Citadel: Hellfire and Brimstone
passages.text:
When Khadgar's group stormed Hellfire Citadel, they faced many foes that commanded demons, but none more powerful than Archimonde himself.

Perhaps there's somethin' on his corpse that can answer the final questions of unlocking the mystery of this brimstone.

passages.title: Hellfire Citadel: Hellfire and Brimstone
passages.text: Don't go alone, lad. That place is teemin' with demons.

passages.title: Hellfire Citadel: Hellfire and Brimstone
passages.text:
You actually found something?!

<Mama Diggs thumbs through the codex, a stern look on her face as she reads each page.>

Aye, here it is. All the answers are within these pages...

passages.title: An Unworthy Task
passages.text:
This place is Helheim, the realm of the unworthy dead. Here, the spirits of the dishonorable spend eternity in an endless futile battle, always seeking glory but never able to attain it.

We should not be here.

We must find a way out. I will scout ahead - you should try and release some of these captive spirits here. Perhaps one may have some answers for us.

passages.title: An Unworthy Task
passages.text:
Free at last! 

The kvaldir caught me while I was tryin' to put together a plan to sneak past that foul dog, Guarm, and have had me locked up ever since! 

I thought surely my fate was sealed.

passages.title: One Mage's Trash
passages.text:
I can help you build your forge. I can even supply the metal for it. I do, however, require a few more... difficult-to-acquire components.

I need an alchemical heat source, some sort of insulator, and a calefactor. I'm certain that all of these can be found here in the Underbelly... if the guards are looking the other way.

passages.title: One Mage's Trash
passages.text: Don't let those guards see you. They may be corrupt, but they're vigilant.

passages.title: One Mage's Trash
passages.text: I hope these weren't too much trouble to obtain.

passages.title: The Muck Stops Here
passages.text:
For my next project - sticking the forge's components to one another - I need a magical adherent. And I've found that the built-up sludge of Dalaran's sewers works perfectly for just that.

It cakes up on the feet, boots, and slithering bellies of Dalaran's more long-lived residents. Scrape some off and bring it here.

passages.title: The Muck Stops Here
passages.text: When you live in a sewer, you have to be ready to improvise.

passages.title: The Muck Stops Here
passages.text: Let's not make a big deal out of this. You wanted a forge... I'm making one for you. The ends will justify the means.

passages.title: Sign This
passages.text:
Ah, a fellow scribe!

You don't look too dim, so how 'bout you and I work together in an effort to discover what we can about the Broken Isles?

(That's the big mass of islands we're floating over.)

However! I never agree to a partnership without getting all the requisite legalities out of the way. Sign this for me and we're in business.

passages.title: Sign This
passages.text: Did you remember to cross your t's and dot your lower case j's?

passages.title: Sign This
passages.text:
Hey, look at that, you know how to spell your name correctly.

Good job, now we can begin!

passages.title: Sundered
passages.text:
I imagine the power of your weapon will be what allows us to defeat Geir, but right now you are too weak for the confrontation. We must reclaim the missing pieces of your spirit.

Helya must have scattered them throughout her realm to keep them from you. If you can find them, shine the lantern and they should be set free.

Be careful, though. It is unlikely that Helya left your spirit fragments unguarded.

passages.title: Sundered
passages.text: Have you recovered your power?

passages.title: Sundered
passages.text:
Yes, I can feel your power returned. 

Helya will regret the day she challenged one such as you.

passages.title: Note-Eating Goats
passages.text:
I've followed Hemet on all his expeditions from Stranglethorn to Nagrand to... Nagrand again, taking notes on his grand adventures and turning them into timeless literary tales.

But my heart is really in the hunt. I want nothing more than to put down the pen, and pick up a rifle!

Hemet promised to teach me how to hunt once I finish his latest novel, but the goats around here ate my first draft!

I have no hope of becoming a hunter if my manuscript isn't recovered.

passages.title: Note-Eating Goats
passages.text:
I've been waitin' all day for Addie to finish her first draft.

How hard can it be to write a few words about the greatest hunter who's ever lived?

passages.title: Note-Eating Goats
passages.text: I've been eager to get my hands on this manuscript! I was startin' to think the gnome had writer's block.

passages.title: Tying Up Loose Ends
passages.text:
Malfurion Stormrage managed to make landfall in Val'sharah and has already taken care of things there. It seems our fortune is finally turning around!

He's waiting for you as we speak in Lorlathil. Life is so magical when everything goes according to plan.

passages.title: Tying Up Loose Ends
passages.text: Highlord <name>! You couldn't have arrived at a better time.

passages.title: Tying Up Loose Ends
passages.text: Elune-Adore, <name>.

passages.title: Trial By Fel Fire
passages.text:
The substance you hold is something that we call "obliterum". We had theorized its existence, but until now, we had never actually been able to produce any.

You say this came from a fire? Of COURSE! Calefaction! Why hadn't I thought of that sooner?

We'll need to reproduce these results before we take any further action. I know it's asking a lot, but I'll need you to get me some more high-quality armor, in a variety of styles.

passages.title: Trial By Fel Fire
passages.text: You needn't spend money on expensive breastplates or robes. Simple bracers will do.

passages.title: Trial By Fel Fire
passages.text: You have the bracers? Very good, now stand back...

passages.title: I'm Not Lion!
passages.text:
I've hunted many exotic beasts in my day, but I've never seen a lion like the one I encountered while scouting the basin.

The beast's amber eyes locked on mine, luring me closer. I was helpless to this predator's enchanting gaze. It was only when the lion pounced did the stupor break.

I've told Hemet of this magical beast, but he laughs. I'm not lying, <name>! The lion exists.

If you find the beast, bring me a trophy of your kill, and I'll reward you handsomely.

passages.title: I'm Not Lion!
passages.text: I'll have the last laugh when Hemet sees proof that this magical lion exists!

passages.title: I'm Not Lion!
passages.text:
So I was right! The lion with the amber eyes did exist.

Here's the gold as promised. This is worth every copper. You can't put a price on proving that you're right!

I'll keep this eye, but I wouldn't want the rest of our prize to go to waste. Let's eat!

passages.title: Some Enchanted Evening
passages.text:
Welcome! It's nice to see familiar faces returning to Dalaran. You might remember Ildine, Vanessa, and me from Northrend. 

Archmage Starsinger is in charge of the shop, but he's away on Kirin Tor business at the moment. He's a fine fellow... mostly.

Your arrival is fortunate. We've run into a problem that we'd love to solve before the archmage returns. Interested in lending a hand?

passages.title: Some Enchanted Evening
passages.text: I'm relieved you've come, <name>. We could certainly use another enchanter in the shop at a time like this.

passages.title: The Last Few
passages.text:
As you can see, <name>, we're hard at work producing enchants for the battle against the Legion. Since you're here, we could really use your help wrapping up one of our orders.

If you could, acquire some vellums and start enchanting them with Versatility. Here, I'll teach you the formula.

passages.title: The Last Few
passages.text: Almost done enchanting those vellums?

passages.title: The Last Few
passages.text:
<You hand Ildine the vellums.>

And that's the last of 'em. Thanks, <name>!

passages.title: Strong Like the Earth
passages.text:
There are many types of spirits in this world, <name>. Some benevolent, some troubled.

They all resonate with different reagents which we use to enchant our armor. One such reagent are the crystals of the ambershards.

They are a violent creature born of the earth and have recently been disturbed by the drogbar. However, disturbed or not, the crystals they bear are of great use to my people for enchantments. Bring me some and I'll show you what I mean.

passages.title: Strong Like the Earth
passages.text: Crystals aren't the only thing the spirits respond to. There are others, but that is another tale for another time.

passages.title: Strong Like the Earth
passages.text:
These will do perfectly for my explanation.

<Guron begins to describe the process of speaking to the spirits and how they interact with the crystal.>

I believe you may have come across another type of crystal: the "leylight shard". That crystal works similarly, but resonates with different spirits.

passages.title: Waste Not
passages.text:
While fighting the ambershards for their crystals, you may come across enchanted armor from our fallen braves. The ambershards care not for such things, but our tribe does not believe in letting anything go to waste.

I'd like you to retrieve our braves' armor and disenchant them into the components from which they were imbued.

Bring me back the reagents so my tribe may use them to enchant new armor.

passages.title: Waste Not
passages.text: To waste what we are given, is to laugh at the spirits who gave it to us to begin with.

passages.title: Waste Not
passages.text: You honor our tribe with your deeds. I will see that this dust goes to good use.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: The Glamour Has Faded
passages.text:
I once taught the night elves how to enchant their armor to strengthen themselves against the evils of this land. One elf in particular garnered my favor.

Arch-Druid Glaidalis is his name. He now resides in the forest known as the Darkheart Thicket, plotting to undo this world with this awful blight.

Before his betrayal, I gave him my book of enchantments to study. I would very much like it back.

I trust you with this task, enchanter. Bring my book back to me.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: The Glamour Has Faded
passages.text: If you're truly a friend in this war, then be my sword and strike down Glaidalis.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: The Glamour Has Faded
passages.text:
You found it? I trust Glaidalis fell in the process?

While I feel relieved such a powerful foe has been defeated, I can't help but feel sad for what could have been...

Regardless, you've proven yourself an ally. As a reward, I will teach you one of my enchantments.

passages.title: No Longer Worthy
passages.text:
The elves of Black Rook Hold have decided to turn their backs on us. They stay inside their keep, attacking any outsider who dare try to enter.

Such behavior is intolerable... especially after all the help they've received from my folk and the others of this land.

I want you to do me a favor, <name>. Take their enchanted sigils and reduce them to dust. Bring me back the dust as proof of your deeds.

passages.title: No Longer Worthy
passages.text: Their behavior was so odd and sudden. It makes no sense why they'd turn their backs on us. Still, it's inexcusable.

passages.title: No Longer Worthy
passages.text:
<Nalamya takes the dust from you.>

Well done, <race>.

passages.title: Halls of Valor: Revenge of the Enchantress
passages.text:
For many centuries, even after death, I was capable of weaving enduring enchantments. But since the theft of my enchanting rod by a greedy king, I can barely sustain the little magic I have left.

If you can recover my enchanting rod from the god-king's ghost, I will reward you in kind.

passages.title: Halls of Valor: Revenge of the Enchantress
passages.text: The rod is an extension of me, and I of it. It would be nice to hold it once more.

passages.title: Halls of Valor: Revenge of the Enchantress
passages.text:
You have brought back to me my most prized possession. For this I will grant you a bit of my knowledge.

Should you wish to learn more, you only need bring me a few, small components.

passages.title: Prepping For Battle
passages.text:
To earn my mark, <class>, you must first prove yourself in battle to me. There is a naga I wish to kill, but I am not strong enough to slay him.

Before we go into battle together, I need your help as an enchanter to become stronger. I'm sure by now you have a bevy of enchantments in your repertoire.

Make some for me so that I may become strong enough again to make a difference in this world.

passages.title: Prepping For Battle
passages.text: Once I have the power I need, we shall test both our strengths.

passages.title: Prepping For Battle
passages.text:
<Alynblaze takes the vellums from you and applies them to his gear.>

Yes! I feel like I can take on the entire Legion now!

Well, that may be a bit of an exaggeration, but I certainly feel up for some battle.

passages.title: The Druid's Debt
passages.text:
In order to grant you my mark, <class>, I must first be made strong enough to come to your aid should you need it.

Within the ruins of Nar'thalas, my idols sit dormant. As I've said, I'm not strong enough to get them myself.

But you are strong, I can sense it. Strong enough to take on those honor-less naga who plague my home.

Find my idols and return them to me. Do this and I will grant you my mark.

passages.title: The Druid's Debt
passages.text: Have you found them? Are they still intact?

passages.title: The Druid's Debt
passages.text:
<Merrus takes the idols from you and clutches them closely to his chest.>

You've no idea how long it's been since I've held these. Thank you, <name>.

You have earned my respect and as promised, you shall have my marks.

passages.title: Sentinel's Final Duty
passages.text:
Now that I'm stronger, it's time to test your mettle, and mine. As I mentioned earlier, there is a powerful naga I wish to kill.

His name is Fathom-Commander Eksis. He was responsible for slaying many of my kin before he retreated into hiding, commanding his troops from the shadows.

I've finally discovered his whereabouts in a cave just east of here. Let us bring vengeance upon him for my lost brothers and sisters.

passages.title: Sentinel's Final Duty
passages.text: He will rue the day he ever set foot upon my homeland.

passages.title: Sentinel's Final Duty
passages.text:
You fought bravely, <name>. I see that you truly are worthy of my marks and I hereby grant them to you.

Perhaps one day we shall stand again side by side in battle.

passages.title: Turnabout Betrayal
passages.text:
Enchantress Ilanya remembers me?

<The satyr pauses to wipe a tear away.>

I made a fool's bargain ten millennia ago. I learned of the queen's alliance with the Legion and betrayed my heart to join their side. I was transformed into a monstrosity, only to die in battle against the mortals.

Now the Legion returns, but I linger as an impotent spirit. Be my vessel and slay the demons ahead of us. Take their demonic runes and render them to dust.

passages.title: Turnabout Betrayal
passages.text: The death screams of the Legion bring me some semblance of joy.

passages.title: Turnabout Betrayal
passages.text:
After watching these demons helplessly for so long, you have given me a chance to strike back at them!

Now the real work begins.

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Rod of Azure
passages.text:
Before we can begin though, there is a small favor I need to ask of you. I'm rather ashamed about this matter, to be honest, but it must be done in order for us to work together.

When I was summoned to this land, I hadn't been given a chance to collect my things. Most importantly, I left behind my enchanting rod.

Instead of retrieving it I believe it would be much simpler to reconstruct it.

Here's what we'll need...

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Rod of Azure
passages.text: How goes the hunt for the rod components?

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Rod of Azure
passages.text:
Oh yes, that seems to be everything.

<Kharmeera takes the components from you and assembles the rod.>

Now, let's see what I can share with you.

passages.title: Down to the Core
passages.text:
The ring enchantments you know now are good, but I know of better ones that exist. That is to say, I know of stronger enchantments that would be suitable for rings.

According to legend, there are four constructs whose cores were imbued with magical enchantments. These constructs now patrol the streets of Suramar City.

If you were to gather some friends and defeat these constructs, you could take their cores for us to study.

passages.title: Down to the Core
passages.text: Remember to bring some friends with you, those constructs are incredibly powerful.

passages.title: Down to the Core
passages.text:
I'm truly amazed at what you're able to accomplish for such a young creature.

Shall we get to work then on learning from these cores?

passages.title: Smashing Herbs
passages.text:
Now that the formalities are out of the way, let's have you do something actually useful.

On the islands below, there's a plethora of new and exotic herbs that we've yet to experiment with.

I'd like you to get some of those herbs and create some new pigments from them. Once you have enough, come back to me and I'll see what you've come up with.

passages.title: Smashing Herbs
passages.text: Well? Do you have the pigments, or are you just wasting my time?

passages.title: Smashing Herbs
passages.text:
Yes, these pigments look like they will do the trick. Well done, student.

In fact... I've been researching a new glyph that these pigments would work splendidly with. Why don't you give it a shot?

passages.title: Fish Ink
passages.text:
You know, herbs aren't the only ways to obtain ink. Other materials can be inkified.

Slightly related! I've been tinkering with the idea of creating my own type of Darkmoon card. Surely if those troggish carnival people can do it, then so can I.

To do so, we'll need some special reagents. Go down to Azsuna and collect some oils for me, then mill them into a suitable ink.

passages.title: Fish Ink
passages.text: My pigment?

passages.title: Fish Ink
passages.text: Holy mackerel! This stuff really puts the "ink" in "stink", doesn't it?

passages.title: Opposites Repel
passages.text:
There's a balance that must be struck, <name>, when becoming a demon hunter. In order to maintain that balance, we must infuse ourselves with opposite forces of nature.

Fel energy is counteracted by arcane energy. We mark our bodies with arcane runes to keep our fel forces in check.

You are a scribe, yes? Then you should have no trouble mixing a suitable ley pigment from the ley dust on the creatures in the ruins up ahead.

passages.title: Opposites Repel
passages.text: Even though they are opposites, one can not exist without the other.

passages.title: Opposites Repel
passages.text:
If you can believe it, that was the easy part. The next part will be a bit more challenging

...at least, for me it will.

passages.title: Demon Ink
passages.text:
These sigils would make for a fantastic new tarot card. Quite powerful, in fact. We simply require an ink sturdy enough to inscribe them.

Fortunately, I have students like you that excel at fetching hard-to-get items.

For this project, I require ink mixed from demonic blood. The blood of the demons at Felsoul Hold will serve as a suitable base. You will also need Blood of Sargeras, of course.

passages.title: Demon Ink
passages.text: If you're unsure where to get demon blood, go to Suramar and look around. You're bound to trip on a demon sooner or later.

passages.title: Demon Ink
passages.text:
This is more than enough. Excellent work!

<Professor Pallin produces a small quill, dips it in the ink and begins scribbling on a small card.>

Just as I thought, easy enough to make.

As is usually the case with tarot cards, you'll have to make a complete set in order for them to yield their full potential.

passages.title: Skin Deep
passages.text:
Welcome, <name>. It's an honor to be working with someone of your caliber.

In order for us to begin our work together, we'll first need to collect some materials.

The Broken Isles are home to many strange, exotic creatures which no doubt have interesting hides to experiment with. We'll need scales to make mail armor with as well.

Go and collect some materials for us so we may begin working.

passages.title: Skin Deep
passages.text: I trust you gave the creatures a merciful death?

passages.title: Skin Deep
passages.text:
These materials have my mind racing. I can't wait to see what we can make with them!

I'm just going to keep some to study. You can have the rest back.

passages.title: Huln's War - The Arrival
passages.text:
Huln Highmountain is the origin of our strength as a tribe. He bested the Legion when last they threatened our survival and unified many disparate tribes.

Live his story, and you will know why his name imbues courage in the cowardly and sows fear in the fearless.

passages.title: Huln's War - The Arrival
passages.text: [In broken Common] Feathered one said you come. Unng Ak not hope for you come. Tauren have thanks.

passages.title: Trail of Echoes
passages.text:
The Nightborne could prove powerful allies against the Legion. We must aid this Thalyssra if we can.

We should be able to find her by tracking her magical echoes, the same way I found her distress call.

I can teleport you near the location where she recorded that message. From there, you must search for ripples in the very fabric of the arcane itself.

My wand should do the trick. Follow the sparks it creates--they should lead you to places where Thalyssra used her magic.

passages.title: Trail of Echoes
passages.text: Who are you?

passages.title: Trail of Echoes
passages.text:
An outlander...

You received my message?

passages.title: A True Hunter
passages.text:
I don't know why Hemet hunts with Razik. His contraptions are unreliable at best! 

A true hunter doesn't need gadgets to hunt. They rely on instinct, skill, and agility.

So tell me, <name>, do you have the skills of a true hunter? Better yet, prove it.

Take down some of the Bonebeak Hawks that circle the nearby meadow.

passages.title: A True Hunter
passages.text: You can't be huntin' hawks if you're here chattin' at me.

passages.title: A True Hunter
passages.text: Now that's how a real hunter does it.

passages.title: Stem the Tide
passages.text:
Skovald has profaned the Gates of Valor with his demonic allies. Among his forces his twisted mystics have conjured portals to ferry his fel allies from their blighted worlds. 

If we wish to stem this tide, these portals must be destroyed. 

I will gather my allies. Take this horn and signal when you have found a portal, and we will strike from the skies!

passages.title: Stem the Tide
passages.text: The portals must be closed if we wish to stop Skovald's forces!

passages.title: Stem the Tide
passages.text:
I do not understand, the portals are closed and yet Skovald's demonic forces still assault the gates! 

We must find where they are coming from!

passages.title: A Slip of the Hand
passages.text:
As you harvest the aethril, your hand brushes the flower's pollinating organs against one another, creating a reaction.

You may have discovered a new herbalism technique. Your trainer in Dalaran would be a good person to discuss this with.

passages.title: A Slip of the Hand
passages.text:
<Kuhuine listens to your story about the aethril.>

What you're saying rings true, <name>. I have heard tales of herbalists that could coax flowers into quickly reproducing, but I was never able to master the technique myself.

Well done, herbalist. I feel great pride.

passages.title: The Last Straw
passages.text:
We cannot falter in our crusade against this corruption, <name>.

It is our duty as heroes. As herbalists.

As hero-balists.

Slaying simple satyrs will not do. We must attack their leaders. Bring this fallen herb to Shala'nir, in the northeast. Find Tur'xoran's summoning stone, and place this herb in front of it. Then... rip off his head.

Do it for the plants.

passages.title: The Last Straw
passages.text: <The druid seethes.>

passages.title: The Last Straw
passages.text:
I thank you for your bravery, <name>.

The next time you approach a sprig of dreamleaf, you may just find that the land thanks you, too.

passages.title: Foxflower Sample
passages.text:
Something about this herb catches your eye... and your nose.

Your herbalism trainer in Dalaran would certainly be interested in studying some samples of this piquant new flower.

passages.title: Foxflower Sample
passages.text: <The tauren sniffs the air.>

passages.title: Foxflower Sample
passages.text:
I like this herb you've brought me, <name>. In a way, it reminds me a bit of the Gorgrond Flytrap: both of them have a habit of attacking your nose.

Look. If you collect the herb this way, your yield should be a bit higher...

passages.title: Chase the Culprit
passages.text:
This is a powerful herb, <name>. Creatures will occasionally snack on some simpler herbs, but usually they avoid plants of such potency.

I'm intrigued. What kind of animal would eat foxflower? A moose?

You should investigate further. Find out what creature has been snacking on foxflower, and then see if you can wrestle some of the flowers from its mouth, before it escapes.

passages.title: Chase the Culprit
passages.text: Did you find out what was eating the foxflower? Was it a goat? A beaver? A nightsaber?

passages.title: Chase the Culprit
passages.text:
Foxes.

Huh.

That... that makes sense. I suppose I should have guessed that.

Well, now that I feel sufficiently stupid, let's look at these bits of flower, to see if there's anything we can learn...

passages.title: The Pied Picker
passages.text:
As you finish gathering the foxflower, a particular part of the bloom catches your eye.

One of the leaves has a small protuberance, right where it meets the stem. Further investigation suggests that this is where the foxflower's unusual smell comes from.

Your herbalism trainer would be interested in seeing this.

passages.title: The Pied Picker
passages.text:
<Kuhuine sniffs the small gland.>

That's certainly a scent gland, alright. It seems to be mostly inert from an alchemical point of view... but I'd guess that this is what is attracting those foxes.

Express this gland when you can, and you may find yourself attracting a friend or two.

passages.title: Fjarnskaggl
passages.text:
There! It seems that there was a vrykul herbalist, Torgus, who brought a gift of fjarnskaggl to a seaside cairn - presumably in Stormheim - and by doing so received a blessing from his ancestors.

<Kuhuine shrugs.>

It's worth a shot, though without knowing what you're getting into, you may want to bring friends with you.

passages.title: Tharillon's Fall
passages.text:
He mentions your name... his blade... aethril...

I'd say that this is absolutely from Herbalist Tharillon, and by the look of it, he may have succumbed to the plight of the nightfallen. Furthermore, if he's looking for aethril, he's probably in Azsuna somewhere.

Tharillon is currently our only hope for learning more about starlight roses. Seek him out, but you may want to bring friends... he likely won't go without a fight.

passages.title: Tharillon's Fall
passages.text: May the Earthmother walk with you, <name>.

passages.title: Tharillon's Fall
passages.text: Fantastic work, <name>! With this knowledge, we may never have to suffer a handful of starlight rosedust again!

passages.title: Felwort Analysis
passages.text:
I sent felwort samples to some of my fellow herbalists, but haven't heard back from them yet. Could you please follow up with them and collect their analyses.

Ryno Bloomfield is currently working in Un'goro Crater.

Dani Earthtouch is researching Freya's influence in Sholazar Basin.

Finally, Lohor has been working in the overgrown portion of Gorgrond.

passages.title: Felwort Analysis
passages.text: Thank you for your willingness to travel, <name>.

passages.title: Felwort Analysis
passages.text:
Much of this is very technical and mundane, but Ryno's analysis can be applied right away.

Look at this, here...

passages.title: The Emerald Nightmare: Felwort Mastery
passages.text:
I have a theory on how we can better harvest this felwort, <name>. You see, sometimes in order to understand how something comes into being, you have to work backwards.

I've recently heard of the corruption of one of our greatest gods, Cenarius. I have no doubt the same corruption that lives in these herbs also resides within him now.

If you were able to cleanse that corruption, find a way to understand how it works and remove it, I think we can apply that to how we harvest these herbs.

passages.title: The Emerald Nightmare: Felwort Mastery
passages.text: I hope you bring some friends with you on this journey, for this may be your greatest lesson.

passages.title: The Emerald Nightmare: Felwort Mastery
passages.text:
<Kuhuine carefully takes the seed from you and listens to your tale of Cenarius' cleansing.>

Fascinating! If what you're saying is true then that means we can harvest Felwort in a similar manner. Now listen...

passages.title: Strings of the Puppet Masters
passages.text:
I understand you were just here to deliver the vellums, but we could use your skills as a <class>. Our forces can only hold back the demon invasion, disallowing us to send anyone further into the enemy's camp.

The stronger of their forces stay in the back, commanding from a distance. They carry enchanted runes to keep control over the frontline demons.

I would very much like to study one of these runes. Please retrieve one for me, so we may learn from it and use it against the Legion.

passages.title: Strings of the Puppet Masters
passages.text: Have you found any runes yet?

passages.title: Strings of the Puppet Masters
passages.text:
Yes, this is it.

<Jace turns the rune over in his hands, studying the intricate markings.>

Excellent work, <name>. I'll make sure Nalthanis is made aware of your contribution.

passages.title: Fledgling Worm Guts
passages.text:
The drogbar use these caves as a place to train fledgling worms.

The rockcrawlers are young and fairly weak, for now, but in time they will grow in size and strength. Without our intervention, the worms will morph into the monstrosities that the drogbar ride into battle.

Their guts are also known to be quite useful, and I have need of them. Two worms, one stone.

passages.title: Fledgling Worm Guts
passages.text: What are their guts for? Well, you'll see. You might not like it, but you will soon find out.

passages.title: Fledgling Worm Guts
passages.text: Those worm guts will be perfect for a special sort of rope.

passages.title: Halls of Valor: Securing the Aegis
passages.text:
The Felskorn may be broken, but the head of the beast yet lives. The God-King will still vie for the Aegis if left unchecked.

You, who have completed trials upon trials, must not let this come to pass. You must claim the Aegis over Skovald's broken bones!

The Halls of Valor await!

passages.title: Halls of Valor: Securing the Aegis
passages.text: With the God-King's defeat, the Aegis of Aggramar is yours to claim.

passages.title: The Invasion Begins
passages.text:
Our advance force of demon hunters is here and has engaged the Legion.

Make our presence known. Let's send a shiver down every demon spine. Raise our colors with pride, <name>.

passages.title: The Invasion Begins
passages.text:
That ought to get their attention.

Now, onto the business of summoning in the rest of our forces.

passages.title: A Heavy Burden
passages.text:
With Ashildir's judgment, your final trial is complete. 

But even Valhallas can wait, for now we must eat! Being dead works up quite an appetite.

Come now, bring some of that fish to roast over the fire. It is far too heavy for me to carry.

passages.title: A Heavy Burden
passages.text:
It is clear that your cooking prowess is only matched by your might in combat. 

Now, on full bellies, we ride to Valhallas!

passages.title: Murlocs: The Next Generation
passages.text:
The time has come! Murky and his followers need a place to hide out and train--away from the mature murlocs--so that they can prepare to take over in the future.

There's a nice cave not too far away... only problem is that it's filled with makrura.

This would be a good base for the tadpoles. Murky must go show them what for!

Mindmeld with Murky in his egg and show him how it's done!

passages.title: Murlocs: The Next Generation
passages.text: These young murlocs show such promise. They'll do this shore good.

passages.title: Murlocs: The Next Generation
passages.text: This cave will make a great base for the young tadpoles!

passages.title: Repairing the Source
passages.text: <A glint catches your eye in the dirt. A brief excavation yields a mostly intact piece of an arcane construct's power core. The breaks appear to be clean, perhaps you could repair it if you find the other fragments.>

passages.title: Washed Clean
passages.text:
Mighty though the Legion is, theirs is not the strongest power in Azeroth.

There is a place where Enchantress Ilanya and I spent many blissful hours together. The love that infuses such a place is more potent than fel magic, <name>.

Go to the Nor'Danil Wellspring. Its waters can purify the fel dust you have collected... and perhaps purify me as well.

I will meet you there.

passages.title: Washed Clean
passages.text: It... it worked! I am myself again at last!

passages.title: Washed Clean
passages.text: The demon I was is no more. I believe I am ready to return.

passages.title: Stonehide Leather Sample
passages.text:
The quality of this leather scrap appears representative of the beast hides found in the Broken Isles.

Your skinning trainer in Dalaran would be interested in seeing this.

passages.title: Stonehide Leather Sample
passages.text: How may I help you?

passages.title: Stonehide Leather Sample
passages.text: Greetings, <name>. What have you brought for me today?

passages.title: In One Piece
passages.text:
<Your trainer looks over the hide.>

This hide is usable, but it is mournably small. You disrespect the beast by chopping it up like this, <name>. You make light of the gift that it gave to you.

Go out into the wilds again. Skin the leathery beasts below us, and this time, bring me hides in one piece.

passages.title: In One Piece
passages.text: <Kondal sternly watches you approach.>

passages.title: In One Piece
passages.text:
Mm. This is better.

Keep my advice in mind the next time you take out your skinning knife.

passages.title: Highmountain Hides
passages.text:
So, ye're a skinner too, aye?

That's great news, <name>! I don't think I ever knew we shared that in common.

Ye've GOT ta see some o'the hides we've got here in Highmountain. Why, I'd give me spare monacle just t'get me hands on some o'those fine, silky hides...

passages.title: Highmountain Hides
passages.text: <Hemet looks lustfully at the horizon.>

passages.title: Highmountain Hides
passages.text:
Y'got these fer me, laddie? I... I don't know what ta say!

Here, take this. It's the least I can do.

<Hemet buries his nose deep into the bear hide.>

passages.title: The Freedom to Roam
passages.text:
I remember bein' young, <name>. D'ye remember it? So much less responsibility... I could just run around as I pleased. Now, I'm pretty much stuck with my hunting crew, here in Highmountain.

There're so many interestin' creatures in the other regions o'the Broken Isles, though. I'll mark yer map, you get out there and do some skinnin'!

passages.title: The Freedom to Roam
passages.text: Once ye're done, I'll show ye a trick or two.

passages.title: The Freedom to Roam
passages.text:
These are marvelous, <name>. Well done.

I can show ye how t'get better results from yer skinnin'. Take a look at this wolf hide, here...

passages.title: Trial of the Crusader: Hides of Legend
passages.text:
Ya, I can train you. Ting is, I'm still workin' on my techniques 'ere in Suramar. In fact, you can probably help.

I need ta look at a few special skins, for comparison. I need a strong white yeti pelt, a really big demon skin, and da thickest direhorn skin you can find.

Do that, and I'll share my results with you and' ol' Kondal up in de city.

passages.title: Trial of the Crusader: Hides of Legend
passages.text: Any luck findin' dose hides?

passages.title: Trial of the Crusader: Hides of Legend
passages.text: Ya gone and outdid y'self. Look at dese hides, bruddah!

passages.title: Ske'rit's Leather Handbook
passages.text:
An' wit dat, my research be done.

<Ske'rit hands you a scroll casing.>

Dis is what I been workin' on here in Suramar. Bring it to Kondal, so dat he can teach it to all you other skinnahs.

Since you been helpin' so much, I put your name on it, <name>. Hope you don't mind.

passages.title: Ske'rit's Leather Handbook
passages.text:
You've returned, and with Ske'rit's book, I see.

Let's look through this together, <name>...

passages.title: Stormscale Sample
passages.text:
This scale shimmers with electrical energy.

Your skinning trainer in Dalaran would be interested in seeing this.

passages.title: Stormscale Sample
passages.text: Yes, skinner?

passages.title: The Core of the Stormscale
passages.text:
Ahh, yes. The elusive stormscale.

I have seen similar scales in Northrend, and some in Skywall, but it would appear that such a scale is common here. My colleagues that specialize in mail armor will be happy to learn this.

To more efficiently harvest this type of scale, you must first understand its power. Look for broken, unusable scales on your quarry, and remove the sparks within them. Once you have seen the sparks, you will better understand the stormscale.

passages.title: The Core of the Stormscale
passages.text: Have you seen the sparks?

passages.title: The Core of the Stormscale
passages.text: Very good, <name>. Greater understanding of the stormscale leads to more efficient skinning, which in turn leads to fewer unnecessary animal deaths.

passages.title: Return to Karazhan: Scales of Legend
passages.text:
I know a ting or two about scales, but I'm losin' my edge. I been starin' at stormscales so long, I be forgettin' what de other kinds look like.

I need ta look at a few special scales, for comparison. I need a nether dragon scale, a nice hot black dragonscale, and da thickest piece o' insect chitin you can find.

Gotta get dese stormscales outta my head, bruddah.

passages.title: Return to Karazhan: Scales of Legend
passages.text: You been gone a while. You get de scales?

passages.title: Return to Karazhan: Scales of Legend
passages.text:
Dese'll do, skinnah.

Dese'll do.

passages.title: Ske'rit's Scale-Skinning Suggestions
passages.text:
Now dat I got all dese scales, I tink I know what I need to know.

<Ske'rit hands you a few pages of handwritten notes.>

Here's my latest findin's on stormscales. Bring 'em to Kondal, an' read through em' togethah.

passages.title: Ske'rit's Scale-Skinning Suggestions
passages.text:
You've been working together with Ske'rit? I should've known. You two are cut from the same hide.

Let's see what he has written here.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Demons Be Different
passages.text:
Oh yes, I've seen me fair share of demons while in dese lands. And skinnin' dem ain't no easy task.

Their hides are tougher than normal animals, fibrous, see? But if you be wantin' to make da most of their skins, den ya need to be practicin' more.

There be a creature I've heard of in da Darkheart Thicket whose hide's as tough as a demon's. When ya go ta skin him, try cutting with da grain in one even stroke.

Bring me his skin to show me you be picking up on what I'm sayin'.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Demons Be Different
passages.text: Any luck on gettin' dat skin?

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Demons Be Different
passages.text:
<Ske'rit takes the hide from you and looks it over.>

You definitely got da hang of it, bruddah.

passages.title: The Story of Huln
passages.text:
You work to unite the tribes. That is no small task. It has only been done once before in the history of this mountain.

Huln Highmountain last united the tribes thousands of years ago to take on the Legion during the War of the Ancients.

passages.title: The Story of Huln
passages.text: The history of this place extends beyond our limited memory.

passages.title: The Story of Huln
passages.text: You have seen only a taste of what Huln Highmountain accomplished during his lifetime. Let us delve deeper into the past...

passages.title: The Swirling Vial
passages.text: As you touch the vial, your mind is flooded with memories, not all of which are your own. The most vivid is a memory of exchanging a similar vial with someone in Shattrath, with A'dal's light shining behind you. Despite your best efforts however, you can't pinpoint when that might have been - maybe it hasn't been, and is yet to be?

passages.title: The Swirling Vial
passages.text:
Oh, interesting! 

<Cupri quickly grabs the vial and studies it intensely.>  

Perhaps Zeph was right to keep investigating here. This vial certainly didn't originate from any currently known timeline. Most curious! Thank you for bringing it to me. Or did you already bring it once before?

passages.title: The Unstable Prism
passages.text: As the prism struggles to stabilize in a single time flow, it bleeds a shadowy chill, the likes of which you haven't felt since Northrend. Surely some mage in Dalaran would be interested in this relic.

passages.title: The Unstable Prism
passages.text:
Let me see that. 

<Auzin ponders the prism for a while, before turning back to you.>

Hmm... Cupri could run tests on this for an eternity. This certainly qualifies as further evidence of meddling by a third party... or is it a sixth party...

Do you mind if I keep it?

passages.title: From Head to Toe
passages.text:
You've been busy, <name>. And you have some new patterns in your repertoire, I see!

How about we add another?

passages.title: From Head to Toe
passages.text: I'm very excited to see how this turns out.

passages.title: From Head to Toe
passages.text:
I'm still amazed at how easily this leather takes shape. It's so flexible, yet keeps its strength.

I think from here you can take my pattern and make it your own.

passages.title: Over Your Head
passages.text:
Alright, <name>, I'd like you to assist me with creating a helm.

First we'll need to shave the hides, then tan them, and finally cut them into usable pieces.

Follow my lead.

passages.title: Over Your Head
passages.text: I'm starting to think we make a pretty good team.

passages.title: Over Your Head
passages.text:
Well done, <name>. Here's a copy of that pattern to add to your collection.

I personally specialize in softer leather armor. If you want to make a MAIL helm, talk to Ranid... although I'm sure he'll charge you a pretty penny for it.

passages.title: Rats!
passages.text:
I tell you, <name>, I have the worst luck sometimes.

A package recently arrived from Hrul containing leatherworking patterns, and while my back was turned, some filthy rats came in and ran off with them down into the sewers!

Probably building nests with them as we speak. Please, <name>, can you go down there and see if you can retrieve any of them?

passages.title: Rats!
passages.text: I hope they're not too badly damaged.

passages.title: Rats!
passages.text:
Nice work stitching these back together. Too bad you couldn't get all the rat saliva off of them.

Let's read them together, shall we?

passages.title: Respect for the Past
passages.text:
We record the mistakes of the past so we can learn to avoid them in the present. However, recording history is not just about preventing missteps, but also to celebrate our successes.

Scattered around Highmountain at sacred locations are racks with stamped leather, much like the ones here, with stories to tell.

Go to these locations, pay your respect, and learn their lessons.

passages.title: Respect for the Past
passages.text:
You look wiser, <name>. The ancestors clearly deemed you worthy of their lessons...

...as do I.

passages.title: Eye of Azshara: Scales of the Sea
passages.text:
When we first met, I spoke of the naga, and the armor they're able to craft. No grander armor is worn, however, than by their top warlords.

One in particular resides within the Eye of Azshara itself. His name is Warlord Parjesh, and the hauberk he wears is one of legend.

Repel his forces, and obtain his armor. Do this, and I will teach you more of the Azsunian way of leatherworking.

passages.title: Eye of Azshara: Scales of the Sea
passages.text: He will not just hand it over, <name>. You're in for a rough fight.

passages.title: Eye of Azshara: Scales of the Sea
passages.text:
You've taken down a mighty adversary, <name>. The naga no doubt will be on the hunt for you.

Before they get to you though, allow me to show you a few things...

passages.title: A Hunter at Heart
passages.text:
Addie's one heck of a writer, but I've never seen her hold a rifle. She's keen on learning how to hunt, but who's ever heard of a gnome hunter? 

You seem to have a knack dealin' with amateurs, so maybe you'd be willin' to let the gnome tag along on a hunt? She could learn a thing or two by shadowing someone with your skill.

Ya best start off with some small game. We don't want the lass to get discouraged.

passages.title: A Hunter at Heart
passages.text: Keep an eye on the gnome while you're huntin'. She's never held a rifle before.

passages.title: A Hunter at Heart
passages.text: You haven't got any holes in ya, I guess that means Addie's aim isn't as bad as I thought!

passages.title: An Offering of Ammo
passages.text:
The mountains have seen many new travelers pass through their valleys, some without an understanding of our traditions.

Our leaders have turned their focus to more pressing matters, but Losro and I cannot ignore the recent arrival of hunters in the nearby basin.

They hunt with guns and gadgets, forgoing the experience of hunting with a bow and arrow.

While I know that some will remain stuck in their ways, perhaps an offering of arrows will encourage these outsiders to hunt the way we always have.

passages.title: An Offering of Ammo
passages.text: We gave up usin' that kind of ammo long ago! Don't worry though, we won't let the gift go to waste. I'm sure we can use the arrows for kindling.

passages.title: The Imp Mother's Tome
passages.text:
See this giant cave? There's a terrifyingly powerful imp mother inside.

But that's not the good part. The good part is what she has.

Apparently, she's some kind of keeper of fel secrets. She's in there performing profane Legion rites and scribing them into a book.

We need that power! We need her tome!

passages.title: The Imp Mother's Tome
passages.text: Do you have it?

passages.title: The Imp Mother's Tome
passages.text: Can you feel the power emanating from the book? I cannot wait to learn its secrets.

passages.title: The Hammer in the Deep
passages.text:
<Thrall listens intently.>

You found it! The Doomhammer fell to the Crumbling Depths... But the Legion remains a step ahead of us. If we hurry, we can follow the demon Geth'xun and retrieve the hammer before any more of this realm is corrupted.

Therazane will open a portal directly there. Let's go!

passages.title: The Hammer in the Deep
passages.text: What of the Doomhammer?

passages.title: The Hammer in the Deep
passages.text:
The orcs had a prophecy about the Doomhammer. It was said that a stranger will raise the hammer high, and with it, justice shall reign. Maybe... maybe YOU were meant to be that stranger all along.

Come, <name>. The Earthen Ring needs you. And Azeroth needs us.

passages.title: A Ring Reforged
passages.text:
Speak with Nobundo, and take your place around the circle, <name>. The Earthen Ring will rise again, with you as its leader!

Within these stones stands the legendary Heart of Azeroth, which we can use as a base of operations. Perhaps the power of your artifact can unseal the hidden chambers...

passages.title: A Ring Reforged
passages.text: The Alliance and Horde are in chaos. If we are to save Azeroth, we <class> must bind together!

passages.title: A Ring Reforged
passages.text:
The Earthen Ring rises once more to defend Azeroth. You will be our Farseer, <name>, and we will be your instruments. Only by working together can we preserve our world.

We are yours to command, Farseer.

passages.title: Scout It Out
passages.text:
You've proven that a gnome can shoot a rifle, and that's no easy feat, but a true test of Addie's skill will be to see if she can track down an elusive beast.

Rumor has it that a ravenous roc circles the basin, cursed by harpy magic, but no one's seen the beast up close.

Take this flare, and shoot it into the sky once you've spotted the roc. When we see the signal, the huntin' party will rush in and help bring down that magnificent bird!

passages.title: Scout It Out
passages.text: Don't just stand there, head out into the basin and find that bird!

passages.title: Scout It Out
passages.text:
That was a kill I won't soon forget!

Addie will write the tale of our adventures here today, but not many will believe that a gnome hunter took down a beast ten times her size.

passages.title: Oh, the Clawdacity!
passages.text:
The leader of the Cavemoss makrura, Clawdayshus, has been ordering raids into the Cavemoss village to steal the young for snacks.

This isn't going to do at all. In order to prove their power, Murky and the tadpoles must destroy him as well!

This is a job for murlocs.

Mindmeld with Murky in his egg and show him how it's done!

passages.title: Oh, the Clawdacity!
passages.text: Clawdayshus is ruthless. Murky must stop him.

passages.title: Oh, the Clawdacity!
passages.text:
You did it! Murky will make a great leader for the next generation of the murlocs here.

I can't help but feel sad over losing my little buddy, but you've got to let them go sometime.

passages.title: The Dawning Light
passages.text:
It was a miracle that you were able to survive, <name>. It is with great sorrow that I have to say that Grand Master Hight was not so lucky. His spirit now rests with the ancestors.

Now we must look to a new leader for our order, our broken temple. I have spoken with the other masters and we are all of one mind on this.

We all agree that new leader should be you, <name>. You have shown strength, wisdom, courage, and kindness beyond measure.

Walk with us to the temple and we will announce our decision.

passages.title: The Dawning Light
passages.text: Congratulations, Grand Master <name>!

passages.title: Asking a Favor
passages.text:
Caria Felsoul was one of our best... before she answered the Legion's foul call.

She now wields the Aldrachi Warblades - the soul-rending armaments of the ancient race's greatest champion, who fell only to Sargeras himself.

We sent a party to track Caria down, but we have not heard from them in some time. Jace has nearly repaired a Legion communicator so we can make contact - we need only a power source.

Could you ask Khadgar for assistance? Our friends in this world are few.

passages.title: Asking a Favor
passages.text: It's good to see you again. If there's anything I can do to help you take the fight to the Legion, just let me know.

passages.title: An Unexpected Message
passages.text:
Ah, Felo'melorn. I am familiar with this weapon. 

For ages the Council of Tirisfal attempted to recover the blade. Its control over the primal forces of fire would be devastating in the wrong hands. 

As luck would have it, an associate of mine, Archmage Modera has recently uncovered some information on this artifact. This crystal contains a message from her.

I suggest you start your search there. The portal over there will bring you back to the city.

passages.title: An Unexpected Message
passages.text:
<name>, I'm glad you came.

I've found information on just the thing we need to turn this war in our favor.

passages.title: The Path of Atonement
passages.text:
Felo'melorn, the runeblade of the kings of Quel'Thalas. It was said to harness the very essence of flame and after being reforged by Kael'thas could even stand against the legendary Frostmourne.

We thought that the blade was lost with Kael'thas's death but an associate of mine has a lead on where it may be located.

We need every advantage we can get and with Felo'melorn in your hand the Legion surely will tremble!

Ah, our company is here.

passages.title: The Path of Atonement
passages.text:
Our next journey will be to Icecrown, <name>.

There, in the heart of the Scourge, we will find Felo'melorn.

passages.title: Tools of the Trade
passages.text:
I used to visit here before the barrier was raised. While the ruling council and the Grand Magistrix argued and politicked I watched the caretakers perform their rituals and venerate the dead.

I would honor the spirits here one last time. I am headed to the tombs. If some of the sacred oils, burial shrouds, or incense survived the ages then bring them to me.

passages.title: Tools of the Trade
passages.text: Did you find anything?

passages.title: Tools of the Trade
passages.text:
Truly a testament to our preservation techniques. I had lost hope that anything would have survived looting and the sands of time.

The ancestors will be pleased with this.

passages.title: Band of Blood Brothers
passages.text:
You are the one that Toryl was bellowing about? Perhaps you can help me.

When I set out to search for Throndyr, I was not alone. Three vrykul loyal to Throndyr also accompanied me. As you can plainly see, I now stand alone.

Find my kin, <name>.

I cannot bear to think that they also share Throndyr's fate.

passages.title: Band of Blood Brothers
passages.text: I must know what has befallen my kin.

passages.title: Band of Blood Brothers
passages.text: My kin are safe. Let us see to these serpents!

passages.title: Feathersong's Redemption
passages.text:
I must confess I was not entirely honest with you, <name>. I meant to drink the potion and join my wife.

And even she was taken from her rest... I cannot fail her again. I must live and do what I can to stop this coming storm to be worthy of joining her.

Come, young one. Let us take care of the harpy matriarch and restore Tel'anor to its former glory. We cannot let this poison go to waste, eh?

passages.title: Feathersong's Redemption
passages.text: It will take time, but Tel'anor will flourish again. I swear it on my life.

passages.title: Feathersong's Redemption
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. You have given me clarity of purpose and a reason to live again. Together we will save Suramar and atone for the sins of my people.

passages.title: Beach Bonfire
passages.text:
Do not let... my body lie in... the mud.

Set my flesh... aflame.

passages.title: Beach Bonfire
passages.text: Throndyr deserved a more honorable death.

passages.title: Beach Bonfire
passages.text: Hail Jarl Throndyr. May your soul find its place in Valhalas.

passages.title: Fisherman's Tonic
passages.text:
If you detest these serpents as much as we do, I ask that you continue the fight against them.

That will mean fighting them in their watery domain. I don't see any gills on you, so we're going to have to concoct an old tonic used by vrykul fishermen.

The ingredients are plentiful around here, taken that you do not mind picking through entrails.

passages.title: Fisherman's Tonic
passages.text: I will help you collect what we need.

passages.title: Fisherman's Tonic
passages.text:
<Brandolf mixes the concoction together.>

Well, I never said that it would taste good. Bottom's up.

passages.title: Turning the Tidemistress
passages.text:
The Tidemistress has fallen back to the elven ruins and is licking her wounds.

Her guard is undoubtedly protecting her. To best her, you will have to break her defenses.

Construct a ballista using the parts that you salvaged and end her once and for all.

passages.title: Turning the Tidemistress
passages.text:
We finally have the advantage against the Sashj'tar.

Now is the time to kill the Tidemistress.

passages.title: Turning the Tidemistress
passages.text: You have done it, <name>. You have slain the Tidemistress and saved Jandvik from the Sashj'tar.

passages.title: Candle of Command
passages.text: You no come in yet! Give orders to other kobold on Throne of Ordering Around if you want in, then maybe we talk.

passages.title: Candle of Command
passages.text: What you lookin' at, stink head?

passages.title: Candle of Command
passages.text: What you doing back so soon?

passages.title: Bubble Trouble
passages.text:
<class>! The sea giants have already eaten half of my kin.

We are helpless in these accursed bubbles. I beseech you to get us out of here.

Take heed. These bubbles are strong. You will need something that is extremely sharp to pierce them.

passages.title: Bubble Trouble
passages.text: Move quickly, <class>! These sea giants have an insatiable appetite!

passages.title: Bubble Trouble
passages.text: There is no glory or honor in being digested.

passages.title: Purge the Unclean
passages.text:
Do you feel it in the air, <race>? The stage is set for us to make things right.

While you were busy I was able to track down the elder elemental that rules these waters. Its name is the Azurefall Guardian and it resides within the channels below Tel'anor.

Take the ritual focus, it should help you during the battle.

passages.title: Purge the Unclean
passages.text: Did you find the source of the corruption?

passages.title: Purge the Unclean
passages.text:
It is done. Already I can feel the corrupting presence washing away.

Thank you, <name>. You have done this place a great service.

passages.title: A New Direction
passages.text:
<name>, as leader of the Illidari in Lord Illidan's absence, you must choose your second-in-command.

Kayn or Altruis. You can only choose one.

The chosen shall become your personal champion, and their ideology will color our decisions for the Illidari going forward. No matter who is chosen, our mission remains unchanged.

If you need a reminder of our past, gaze into the Pool of Judgment. Remember the sacrifices that forged us into demon hunters. Speak to me when you are ready to choose.

passages.title: A New Direction
passages.text: Have you made a choice?

passages.title: A New Direction
passages.text: I see. I support you no matter your choice. With this new beginning, we shall rebuild the Illidari.

passages.title: Enter the Illidari: Ashtongue
passages.text:
Lord Illidan has placed you in charge. Now, we just need the rest of our Illidari attack force.

There are three Burning Legion gateways ahead. Activate them and our Illidari will pour through from the Black Temple.

Like most Legion constructs, the gateways are powered by souls. I think we have provided enough to activate this first one, don't you? Let us bring in our Ashtongue forces.

passages.title: Enter the Illidari: Ashtongue
passages.text: <name>, I remind you that we need our Ashtongue forces to be brought through the gateway back on Despair Ridge.

passages.title: Enter the Illidari: Ashtongue
passages.text: I saw them run by. Not the most impressive of our troops, but the Ashtongue have proven effective in the past.

passages.title: Enter the Illidari: Coilskar
passages.text:
The next gateway's down on the Molten Shore. Our Coilskar forces are waiting at the Black Temple on the other side.

Personally, I wouldn't have chosen to bring our naga allies. But, their leader did swear fealty to Lord Illidan. I suppose we'll see.
