For my plan to succeed, my expedition party needs to die. Can't have them telling anyone I'm missing...

passages.title: Dead Men Tell No Tales
passages.text: So it's done then? I never really liked Hendricks, anyway.

passages.title: A Tribute for Death
passages.text:
Everything for de ritual is together. Now, it is time to begin. 

For dis to work, I must chant de words of old. It is an exhausting task, so I need you to take my mojo fetish and draw de ritual circle, then beat upon de drums.

If all goes well, Bwonsamdi may invite us into de temple.

If not, our souls are forfeit.

Let's not make any mistakes.

passages.title: A Tribute for Death
passages.text: Ya be brave ta come here, but ya need ta have more than just bravery if ya be wantin' Bwonsamdi's favor.

passages.title: Preserve the True Future
passages.text:
I know how this looks, <name>. I'm not asking for your help simply because I don't want to get killed.

I need your help because this isn't how I'm SUPPOSED to die. I will die - I've seen it! - but it happens much later than this. Besides, meddling with the timeways for personal reasons - well, it goes against pretty much everything my dragonflight stands for.

Let's stop all four of the dragonshrine attacks. That should do the trick.

passages.title: Preserve the True Future
passages.text:
We've stopped all four attacks from the dragonshrines - but the timelines are still incorrect. I'm still being assassinated, elsewhere, at the same time.

Looks like our work isn't done yet, <name>!

passages.title: The Deaths of Chromie
passages.text:
It looks like we're going to have to stop all eight attacks on me. In one fifteen-minute span.

Even to me, that doesn't seem like a lot of time.

Still, if anybody can do it, it's us. Are you ready, <name>?

passages.title: The Deaths of Chromie
passages.text: We've done it! The timelines are exactly as they're supposed to be again. With me, alive.

passages.title: Pork Chop
passages.text:
Roland Hacksaw was the best butcher I've ever worked with... but he's gone insane! He's still processing pigs into sausage!

You have to stop him!

passages.title: Pork Chop
passages.text: Poor Roland. He was... very good at his work. One of the finest butchers in Drustvar. It is a true shame his talents were put to such horrible use.

passages.title: The Final Effigy
passages.text:
<The effigy's protection has been broken.

All that remains is to break the effigy itself.>

passages.title: The Final Effigy
passages.text:
What's... going on? How long have I been standing here?

A curse!? You're saying the whole village was just... stuck? I knew there was something terribly wrong with that old crone...

It seems that Fallhaven owes you a great debt, stranger.

passages.title: Scars of the Past
passages.text:
The Army of the Light's warframes have won countless battles on Argus. Despite their power, not all who descend into the fray return.

My modifications to this frame should give us the edge we need, but several critical components are still missing.

There are remains of battles past in Nath'raxas that we can still scavenge. If you can find the pieces I need, the Legion will feel our fury yet.

passages.title: Scars of the Past
passages.text: Do you have the components?

passages.title: Scars of the Past
passages.text: Perfect! Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Preventive Measures
passages.text:
There is no end to the Legion's depravity. Every battle won, every world conquered, yields more souls to fuel their war machine.

They have not yet defiled all of the fallen warriors in the hold, but I fear it is only a matter of time. Please, take this talisman with you into the hold and use it to sanctify any corpses you encounter.

They deserve a better fate.

passages.title: Preventive Measures
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. Your actions deny the Legion power and grant the dead the peace they deserve.

passages.title: Chaos Theory
passages.text:
Despite their strength and their numbers, even the Burning Legion requires order to fight. Disrupt that order... and they fall like the rabble they are.

The plan is simple. Let chaos reign in their ranks, and the day will be ours.

passages.title: Chaos Theory
passages.text: We must do whatever it takes to see this done.

passages.title: Chaos Theory
passages.text: Now that their forces are in disarray, let us proceed.

passages.title: Dawn of Justice
passages.text:
Thanks to your efforts, our enemy is in disarray and their defenses inoperable.

We must take the ground at the spire's base and tighten the noose around their commander's neck.

You have more than earned the honor to take the warframe into battle. We will follow your lead once the way is clear.

passages.title: Dawn of Justice
passages.text: Well fought! Now for the commander.

passages.title: Overt Ops
passages.text:
My soldiers are out there, <name>.

I need you to find Baraat, Sorvos, and Telaamon. They were in the process of securing this area for Velen when the Legion came down on top of our heads.

Inform them that their orders are to regroup with the Prophet at once.

The time for subtlety has passed. There is a small army between us and them. Do what you must.

Light keep you safe.

passages.title: Overt Ops
passages.text: Fareeya's forces are the best the Army of the Light has to offer. Our mission is that much more likely to succeed with them at our side.

passages.title: Beginner Equitation
passages.text:
You may know how to ride already, but you don't know how to ride like a Kul Tiran!

We'll let you borrow a horse for the festivities. Take one of our lesson masters, Cooper. He's trained many a beginner in his day!

Mount up, get in the ring, and show us what you've got! I'm sure you'll be a quick learner!

passages.title: Beginner Equitation
passages.text: Kul Tiran riding is a true show of mastery and sport!

passages.title: Beginner Equitation
passages.text: Well done, <name>! I think you're ready to take it to the next level!

passages.title: Ascending Alchemy
passages.text:
I've seen other alchemists come through our camp carrying interesting looking trinkets. I believe they refer to them as... "alchemist stones"?

I can sense the power they radiate, but they appear fel-tainted. The herb that grows on this planet is particularly good at cleansing corruption. I use it to purify the primal sargerite that's often found amongst the herbs.

I'm certain that if we used a purified sargerite with one of those stones, we could elevate the power within it.

passages.title: Ascending Alchemy
passages.text: I know it's a lot of materials to ask for, but it's necessary.

passages.title: Ascending Alchemy
passages.text:
And there you have it! I believe this will be far more useful for you in your fight against the Legion.

Allow me to explain how it's done...

passages.title: The Glory of Argus
passages.text:
<Amazed that anything so pure could continue to grow on this planet, you pick the flower from the ground. You feel a small power radiate from it and then vanish.>

<As it falls apart in your hands, you wonder if anyone on this Light-forsaken place knows how to handle this precious herb.>

passages.title: The Glory of Argus
passages.text:
So you were trying to gather astral glory I see. Yes, there is a method to doing it correctly.

The flower has a power to it, allowing it to protect itself from anything it thinks may seek to destroy it. If it feels truly threatened, it extinguishes itself.

You mustn't try to pick it with intent to harm, but to protect. It's an unfortunate irony as we eventually destroy it in the process of making items with it.

However, this deception is necessary for it to yield itself to you.

passages.title: Empyrium Deposit Chunk
passages.text:
<As you swing your pickaxe into the ore, it hits with a resounding thud, sending a small chunk of it to the ground. At this rate, it would take you all day to get a sufficient amount of ore from this deposit.>

<Perhaps someone can give you some insight into how to mine this deposit properly.>

passages.title: Empyrium Deposit Chunk
passages.text:
Empyrium requires a precise strike to yield the best results. Aim your pick at the brightest bits of the ore, which also happen to be very small, hence the precision.

This will break the deposit apart faster and you'll be able to harvest ore quicker.

passages.title: Angling For a Better Strike
passages.text:
<Looking at the empyrium dust from taking down this deposit, you wonder if there's a way to prevent part of the deposit from shattering with each impact.>

<Perhaps Khamir will know something further that he can share with you.>

passages.title: Angling For a Better Strike
passages.text:
As I mentioned before, precision is key with mining empyrium. You've learned to strike at the correct spots, now you must learn to strike at the correct angle.

Take out your pick and I'll show you what I mean...

passages.title: Precision Perfected
passages.text:
<While you've learned to extract as much of the deposit as you can, the core of the deposit is always left unusable. Looking closely, you can see where your strikes were causing fractures in its structure.>

<One more lesson from Khamir might be needed to correct this problem.>

passages.title: Precision Perfected
passages.text:
You've learned where to strike and at what angle to strike, but should you wish to leave the core intact to mine, you must finally learn how hard to strike.

The fractures you found in this core are the result of striking the ore too hard. As I'm sure you no doubt know by now, mining empyrium is not just a task, but an art.

Come, let us practice your swing until it's just right.

passages.title: Empyrium Seam Chunk
passages.text:
<At first you thought the ore to have a mirrored surface, reflecting the starry space above you. After breaking off a chunk, you realize that the ore itself has a starry quality all of its own.>

<Perhaps someone back at the Vindicaar can give you some insight on how to better extract these seams more efficiently.>

passages.title: Empyrium Seam Chunk
passages.text:
Empyrium is quite a sight to behold once it's been mined. And while the deposits of this ore require precision, the seams require exposure.

If you spend some time picking away the surrounding rock, you'll find much more ore to harvest.

passages.title: Balancing the Break
passages.text:
<Getting down to the root of the seam, you're left with nothing but small bits and pieces. Collectively though, they would have been enough to work with.>

<Khamir might know a way to prevent this from happening.>

passages.title: Balancing the Break
passages.text:
Much like the deposit, empyrium requires a balanced extraction. Its core is its most fragile section.

If you swing too hard, it breaks, too soft and you'll be there forever. The same is true for loosening it from its surrounding rock.

Here, let me show you a method which balances both.

passages.title: Tainted Scraps
passages.text:
<As you begin to carefully remove the skin from the corpse, you notice it quickly becoming corrupted by the decay of the creature.>

<Pulling away, you were only able to extract a small amount of leather and something foul smelling. Perhaps someone on the Vindicaar might know more about this foul hide.>

passages.title: Tainted Scraps
passages.text:
If you haven't already guessed, the key to skinning these creatures properly is speed. They're born of foul energies and those spill out once you begin to cut into the corpse.

I would suggest training your hand to become faster at removing the hide.

passages.title: A Larger Cut
passages.text:
<While you've become quicker at removing pieces of the hide, there is still much that is spoiled before you're able to remove it.>

<Enstraa might have a better idea of how to remove more of the hide before it becomes tainted.>

passages.title: A Larger Cut
passages.text:
So you've become faster, but you're still thinking in your old ways.

Instead of cutting away small pieces at a time, try making one large cut and removing as much of the hide in as few cuts as possible. Move away from the corpse and begin cutting the large pieces into smaller, usable pieces.

passages.title: Order of Operations
passages.text:
<The skins have been more abundant, but you're only able to gather a couple teeth and claws before they take on the corruption.>

<Unsure as to how to extract as many teeth and claws as possible, you find yourself wanting to have one last conversation with Enstraa back at the Vindicaar.>

passages.title: Order of Operations
passages.text:
So it's just more teeth and claws you're after? This should be simple to explain then.

The teeth receive the greatest exposure to the creature's foul insides, so removing them first will still give you time to dissect the rest of the beast. Next, remove the hide. And lastly the claws, as those take the longest to take on any corruption.

passages.title: Empyrial Strength
passages.text:
I see my armor's caught your interest. It's made from the finest material on Argus: empyrium. I actually specialize in crafting breastplates.

I could show you how to craft one, but you'll need to bring your own supplies, I'm afraid. Our stores of the ore are low and we need all that we have.

But here are the plans so you'll know what you need to find...

passages.title: Empyrial Strength
passages.text: I hope those plans weren't too complicated for you to understand.

passages.title: Empyrial Strength
passages.text:
This is quality work. It appears you even solved an issue I was having with the spacing between the front and back chest plates.

You wouldn't mind if I kept this, would you? A fair trade for the recipe, yes?

passages.title: A Harsh Mistress
passages.text:
So there I was thinkin' about how to get everyone ready for movin' around Argul or whatever it's called, since I figure its gravity is different than ours, and I come up with a design for a device you slip onto your shoes, or hooves or whatever you're wearin' down there.

Next thing I hear, the gravity on that planet? Completely the same as ours!

Regardless, I figure I could get the prototype workin'. Mind givin' me a hand? Maybe when we're done you can like, sell 'em to kids or somethin'.

passages.title: A Harsh Mistress
passages.text: This is gonna be fun... to watch!

passages.title: A Harsh Mistress
passages.text:
That last jump looked about what I had in mind for how the gravity was gonna be.

<Hobart scribbles some notes on the schematic.>

And there ya have it. They'll only last ya a few minutes before they're spent, so use 'em wisely.

passages.title: Extraterrestrial Exploration
passages.text:
<name>, I hear you've been over to that large green planet in the sky already. Swarming with demons too, I hear.

I was thinking maybe we could put together another wormhole generator for it. Make it easier to zip around the planet.

Problem is we need to get readings on the landscape, and I'd go, but uh... well I need to stay here and run the shop. Can't leave it to these bozos to handle.

Here, take this and get some readings for me, will ya?

passages.title: Extraterrestrial Exploration
passages.text:
Oh, this is great stuff. That's some landscape up there! Let me just get this information written down...

<Didi begins to scribble some notes on some blueprint paper.>

That should do it. As with all generators, you'll need to use local materials for it, so whatever you can find on that planet should work.

passages.title: A Colorful Key
passages.text:
<name>, I hear you're a jewelcrafter. I too am a master cutter, but I fear my designs will be lost to the Legion.

I hurried out of my home with the intention of returning, but I fear that may not be a possibility. You see, I left my most prized possession, a book of jewelcrafting designs.

But you, you're strong, you could fight your way into my home and recover my book!

However, I locked it away in a special chest that requires the gems of this land to unlock. You'll need one of each to open it.

passages.title: A Colorful Key
passages.text: The combination isn't that difficult, just put the gems in their appropriate settings.

passages.title: A Colorful Key
passages.text:
My book! And it doesn't appear to be damaged either, thank the Light.

Look here, <name>.

Here are the designs for turning those gems into accessories of power.

passages.title: A Crowning Achievement
passages.text:
With my book nearly being lost forever, it occurs to me that I shouldn't keep all this knowledge in one place. I would like to pass it along to you, <name>.

My most recent designs are ones that I am particularly proud of. I call them Empyrial Crowns. Each one uses a different combination of gems to render different effects of power.

Let me show you how to construct one and then I'll show you how different combinations of gems create different results.

passages.title: A Crowning Achievement
passages.text: Perhaps in time you too will find a student whom you may pass all your knowledge unto.

passages.title: A Crowning Achievement
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>. Now, onto the different combinations...

passages.title: Counterbalancing
passages.text:
In the past, I was able to make glorious items from the beasts of this land. But then the Legion came and wiped out all those amazing beasts.

Now I'm forced to use their polluted hides to craft armor for my allies. I have, however, found a way to remove their taint.

The cloth we use is made from special thread infused with Light energy. I devised an oil which when combined with the cloth purifies the leather and makes it usable.

Here, take my oil and see for yourself.

passages.title: Counterbalancing
passages.text: I often dream of working with unsullied leather again. But who knows when that will ever be...

passages.title: Counterbalancing
passages.text:
An interesting balance, but necessary. You may keep the oil, I have plenty.

Oh, and now that you know how to purify the leather, let me show you how to use it. Here are some shoulder patterns my allies ask for regularly.

passages.title: Equine Retrieval
passages.text:
I like the cut of your jib, friend!

I'll tell you what. The rest of the partygoers should be arriving any time now. Would you do me the honor of retrieving my favorite horse from the estate on the hill?

Imagine, our guests' first impression of you to be on the most regal horse in all of Tiragarde! Wondrous!

passages.title: Equine Retrieval
passages.text: <name>! The troggs have invaded!

passages.title: Equine Retrieval
passages.text: I don't believe I'm saying this, <name>, but troggs are invading the estate!

passages.title: Krag'wa's Chosen
passages.text:
Dis be a real mess, <name>. Da naga be drainin' da magic of Krag'wa's frogs ta feed demselves!

Dere be three frogs, Krag'wa's champions, dat dey be torturin' as we speak.

Take dis potion, it be returnin' da power of dem noble frogs. Dey deserve better dan bein' drained by dese snake bastards.

I be stayin' here. Da naga got in some lucky hits on me. All me life, I wanted ta see Krag'wa, and I let meself get hurt by some naga!

passages.title: Krag'wa's Chosen
passages.text: Ya did it! Krag'wa gonna be pleased wit' dis, I be sure of it.

passages.title: Rescue Rangers
passages.text:
We're barely holding off those monsters here. If it hadn't been for the Thornspeakers, we'd surely be dead. I was worried Rebecca hadn't made it!

You've brought Rebecca's supplies just in time. We have many injured out in the field, Thornspeaker, ranger, and companion alike. I'll hold the line here. Go into the ruins and heal as many of the wounded as you can!

passages.title: Rescue Rangers
passages.text: Thank you for helping us, Mainlander.

passages.title: Troublesome Troglodytes
passages.text:
Troggs are base creatures. They barely have any brain process, living mostly on survival instinct alone. They are pests through and through, and need to be dealt with.

The fewer of them there are, the better.

passages.title: Troublesome Troglodytes
passages.text: Fewer troggs means fewer of our people getting attacked.

passages.title: The Burden of Proof
passages.text:
I think we have everything we need to conduct three of the villagers' tests. Let us hope this is enough to convince them.

I'm sure Constable Framer is champing at the bit to proceed with his trial, and I would prefer it if you were the one to administer the tests. I may not know you well, but I trust you farther than the constable.

Speak with him when you're ready to begin.

...and do me a favor. Make this quick.

passages.title: The Burden of Proof
passages.text:
That... didn't turn out as expected.

It appears that my absolution may truly be in your hands.

passages.title: The Burning Heart
passages.text:
The loss of Xe'ra is a blow, especially to Turalyon. But even the Light Mother could not be allowed to force destiny upon us.

I wish Illidan had found another way to refuse her... but I too have had choices imposed upon me by the naaru.

This must not distract us from our mission. Now that we have the Army of the Light survivors with us, it is time to press our attack.

We need a foothold on the Antoran Wastes from which we can assault the Burning Throne. It is time to deprive Sargeras of his prize!

passages.title: The Burning Heart
passages.text: I never imagined such destruction... such horror.

passages.title: Securing a Foothold
passages.text:
Alleria and I have scouted this area before, alongside some of our best soldiers. We stationed encampments on either side of our current position, but I fear they will have come under heavy attack. They need reinforcements.

Our first order of business is to set up a teleportation beacon directly below the Vindicaar. From there, we will have access to both fronts.

Speak to Romuul when you are ready to head down to the surface.

passages.title: Securing a Foothold
passages.text: We need that teleportation beacon set up if we are to reinforce our positions.

passages.title: Securing a Foothold
passages.text: Good. From here we can quickly access and reinforce each of the encampments.

passages.title: Reinforce Light's Purchase
passages.text:
Now that we have established a foothold, we need to rendezvous with our soldiers in the field.

We have an Army of the Light encampment to the south, near where the Legion is keeping their strongest warriors in some sort of stasis.

Alleria went to scout the area. Find her, and see what information she has gathered.

passages.title: Reinforce Light's Purchase
passages.text: The camp lies to the south. When you find the large stasis capsules, look for a passage on the left.

passages.title: Reinforce Light's Purchase
passages.text:
We have a foothold here... for now.

I am unsure how long it could hold out against a sustained assault.

passages.title: Reinforce the Veiled Den
passages.text:
The foothold you established allows us to check in with our field operatives.

On our last mission here, we set up a bastion to the northeast. It should be defensible for now, but that could change at any moment.

Illidan has gone ahead to assess the situation. I suggest you go there and see if he needs a hand.

passages.title: Reinforce the Veiled Den
passages.text:
The camp lies to the northeast.

It may appear hidden at first glance, but you can find the Light shining in the darkest places.

passages.title: Reinforce the Veiled Den
passages.text: So many demons. So much work to do.

passages.title: The Burning Throne
passages.text:
The time has come, <name>, to begin our assault upon Antorus. Everything we have fought for, everything our friends and family have sacrificed, has brought us to this moment.

We will fire Light's Judgment upon the walls of the accursed citadel and storm their seat of power. We will end the Legion.

After all you have done, it is fitting that you have the honor. Activate the Crown of the Triumvirate and let us finish our mission.

passages.title: The Burning Throne
passages.text: We have not come this far to stop now.

passages.title: The Burning Throne
passages.text: After so many years... so many sacrifices... victory is finally within our grasp.

passages.title: The Seat of the Triumvirate: Armor of the Triumvirate
passages.text:
This reforged key will grant entry into the armory inside the Seat of the Triumvirate.

Locked away inside is the Armor of the Triumvirate, crafted in the days before Sargeras brought ruin to our world. We cannot let this armor be stolen by the Void's forces.

Once the armor is in your possession, please bring it to Archivist Ionaa. He has collected our most sacred relics in the cave just up the path. No doubt he would be very glad to receive it.

passages.title: The Seat of the Triumvirate: Armor of the Triumvirate
passages.text: Have you brought me something, <class>?

passages.title: The Seat of the Triumvirate: Armor of the Triumvirate
passages.text:
The Armor of the Triumvirate! I never believed I would see it again. It is a reminder of our proud history, one which the evil of the Legion will never overshadow.

Gaal told me of your dedication, <name>. It is fitting that you don this armor. May it serve as a beacon of the Light in these dark times.

passages.title: Recovering the Pieces
passages.text:
The fragment you found is only one part of the key. I fear the other pieces have fallen into the hands of these ethereal beings you speak of... the Shadowguard. 

We must recover them all. The Shadowguard leaders and lieutenants in and around the Seat of the Triumvirate may well have the fragments in their possession.

Get those key fragments, <name>... any way you have to.

passages.title: Recovering the Pieces
passages.text: Did you find all the fragments?

passages.title: Recovering the Pieces
passages.text:
Nice work, Huntmaster. Those ethereals stood no chance against you.

Now that we have the fragments, I can prepare them for reforging.

passages.title: A Nose for Magic
passages.text:
I have it! The readings from the ruins are unmistakable. Somewhere to the south and west of the ah... "foot", as it were, is a source of great magical energy.

It can be nothing but the Eye of Xibala!

We will need to place a few more scrying vessels to pinpoint the Eye's exact location.

Meet me deeper in the ruins. I will personally oversee this effort.

passages.title: A Nose for Magic
passages.text:
I seem to have overestimated the ah... accuracy... of my scrying.

And thus, our enemies have located the Eye first.

passages.title: Work Order: Lightblood Elixirs
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, alchemist. We needed these potions badly.

passages.title: Work Order: Tears of the Naaru
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, alchemist. We needed these potions badly.

passages.title: Siphoning Souls
passages.text:
<Tacha rummages through her sack of scavenged supplies.>

So these golems are powered by Zandalari souls?

No problem... I've had to deal with that before... I've got just the tool for it.

<Tacha pulls out an eerie Zandalari totem.>

Here it is! Found this ol' soulcatcher totem in one of the southern ruins years ago. It's gotten us out of a few jams.

Disable the golems and throw down this totem next to it. It'll siphon off the souls.

Keep the totem. We'll need it later.

passages.title: Siphoning Souls
passages.text: See? I told you that the soulcatcher totem would make it easy. A tool for every problem, I say.

passages.title: Work Order: Astral Glory
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, herbalist. We needed this astral glory badly.

passages.title: Supplies Needed: Astral Glory
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, <class>. We needed this astral glory badly.

passages.title: Work Order: Empyrium
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, miner. We needed this empyrium badly.

passages.title: Pulse of the Wharf
passages.text:
I am at a loss for ideas, <name>. The tides churn, and I can feel their pain as if it is my own.

While I am out of ideas, perhaps the merchants in town may have seen something? They are always watching and gossiping, making them quite good sources of information.

passages.title: Pulse of the Wharf
passages.text: In the name of the sea! Did you see that?

passages.title: Possessive Headgear
passages.text:
It is fortunate that we have found Alby. He has filled me in on the situation in the packing district.

It's not good, <name>.

The workers walk, yes. They work as if nothing is out of the ordinary, yet they are controlled by parasites. Mindstealers that force them to do their bidding.

It is they who contaminate the shipments.

You must destroy as many of those mindstealers as you can. Free the minds of the possessed!

passages.title: Possessive Headgear
passages.text: Our priority is saving our people. We must do whatever we can.

passages.title: Possessive Headgear
passages.text: This has never been a simple illness. There is foul magic at work here.

passages.title: Supplies Needed: Empyrium
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, <class>. We needed this empyrium badly.

passages.title: Work Order: Fiendish Leather
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, skinner. We needed this fiendish leather badly.

passages.title: Supplies Needed: Fiendish Leather
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, <class>. We needed this fiendish leather badly.

passages.title: Work Order: Florid Malachite
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, jewelcrafter. We needed these florid malachites badly.

passages.title: Work Order: Hesselian
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, jewelcrafter. We needed this hesselian badly.

passages.title: The Young Lord Stormsong
passages.text:
When the town fell, I got separated from my charge.

Lord Stormsong is being held hostage in his own house. I should've been there to protect him.

When you go in there, succeed where I failed. Bring him back safely.

passages.title: The Young Lord Stormsong
passages.text:
<Alby clears his throat.>

It is good to see the young lord safe.

...Thanks.

passages.title: Deep Sea Defilement
passages.text:
The sea...

I understand its screams now. It is as if a veil has been lifted, revealing the chaos that has taken hold.

Corrupting such a vast swath of sea cannot be done with simple spells. The cultists must have erected some sort of structures to channel their dark magics through...

You must find and destroy them, <name>. Only then can we hope to restore the waters to balance.

passages.title: Deep Sea Defilement
passages.text: My mind is bursting with the tide's cries. It is almost too much to bear.

passages.title: Deep Sea Defilement
passages.text: The screams have subsided, if ever slightly.

passages.title: Work Order: Lightweave Cloth
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, tailor. We needed this lightweave cloth badly.

passages.title: Supplies Needed: Lightweave Cloth
passages.text: Thank you for assisting us, <class>. We needed this lightweave cloth badly.

passages.title: Grand Theft Telemancy
passages.text:
They must not keep the Eye, <name>.

Fortunately I am more than an archaeologist. I am a telemancer. Chief Telemancer Oculeth himself trained the woman who trained my master. I can retrieve the relic with these arts.

All you need to do is place a telemancy beacon near the Eye. I can then retrieve both it AND you safely back to camp. The Alliance will find themselves empty-handed.

While you're at it, do deliver my "thanks" to the individual responsible for snatching the Eye out from under us.

passages.title: Grand Theft Telemancy
passages.text: Did you find the source of the disruption?

passages.title: Grand Theft Telemancy
passages.text: Ahhh... it must be so disheartening to be at the mercy of such magics. Well done.

passages.title: The Scamps
passages.text:
You there! You have legs and a need for money? I wish to hire you.

Confounded, despicable, parentless children have been stealing my scrolls again. Those scrolls are dangerous in the wrong hands.

What is worse, I believe these junior vagabonds to be organized.

Find these street scamps and relieve them of their bounty, and I shall pay you for it.

passages.title: The Scamps
passages.text: The little rascals are crawling all over these accursed docks.

passages.title: The Scamps
passages.text: It pains me to pay you for something I could have done myself when I was younger, but these legs do not move as swiftly as they once did.

passages.title: Together We Are the Horde!
passages.text:
What began with a simple feast led to a battle against an ancient evil seeking to consume the world.

My kind of day!

Your deeds have helped secure an alliance between Orgrimmar and Highmountain. These tauren will make a valuable addition to the Horde.

The Warchief will be pleased.

passages.title: Together We Are the Horde!
passages.text:
It seems we have secured a new ally. You have done well.

The Highmountain tauren are famed for their prowess in battle. I look forward to the pummeling they will unleash upon the Alliance.

passages.title: Remnants of Darkfall Ridge
passages.text:
My riders have talbuk, but my people need supplies. Food. Tools. Weapons.

For millennia, we have migrated from one hovel to the next, moving each time the Legion discovered us. Never able to flee with our possessions, we left them behind.

You are powerful, your followers are capable, but you do not know Argus. The landscape will dispatch you as mercilessly as the Legion. Recover our supplies from Darkfall Ridge, and I will order my people to guide your forces through the Argus Wastes.

passages.title: Remnants of Darkfall Ridge
passages.text: You have recovered our supplies. As promised, we will aid your forces on Argus.

passages.title: Nath'raxas Hold: Rescue Mission
passages.text: Your forces are adequately equipped for the mission to save my people from Nath'raxas. Order your champions to bolster my assault, and together we will dismantle the Legion's stranglehold over the region.

passages.title: Nath'raxas Hold: Rescue Mission
passages.text: We were a great civilization, once. But, now?... Thank you, <name>. Our combined forces freed many from Nath'raxas. With fewer slaves, and the Army of the Light on their doorstep, the Legion's influence over this region will be greatly diminished.

passages.title: The Ruins of Oronaar
passages.text:
Many krokul wander the city below, shrouded in shadow. I will not accept that they are all beyond redemption.

Arkhaan was a leader, once. Some among his followers may still reside in the ruins of Oronaar, straddling the thin divide between reason and oblivion. Enlist the aid of your order. Scour the ruins for any that can be saved.

passages.title: The Ruins of Oronaar
passages.text: Your champions discovered someone living in a cave beneath Oranaar. He is hiding from the Void-Touched, and he appears lucid.

passages.title: Shadowguard Dispersion
passages.text: Lend me the aid of your order once again, that we might end the Shadowguard threat permanently. While you confront the Legion, we will face the void. The attack commences once your forces arrive.

passages.title: Shadowguard Dispersion
passages.text: With L'ura defeated, and the voidcallers eliminated, the Shadowguard's dominance over the city has been crippled. if our campaign against the Legion is successful, there could be a future for the creatures living here.

passages.title: Hindering the Legion War Machine
passages.text:
<class>t, I could use your help. The Army of the Light is coordinating an attack against the Spirit Crucible, Terminus, and Shaper's Rise to cripple the Legion's ability to wage war outside of the Antoran Wastes. We do not have enough soldiers to defend our footholds and execute this operation.

Will you approach the <class>s on our behalf? This gambit could succeed with them fighting by our side. We can paralyze the Legion war machine.

passages.title: Hindering the Legion War Machine
passages.text: Three Legion facilities decimated in a single operation. Extraordinary.

passages.title: Strike Back
passages.text: As you may have seen, the ritualists in this forest kidnap our people and perform heinous rituals on them. The souls of our fallen now roam as twisted creatures. This sin cannot go unpunished. Kill as many ritualists as you are able, but be sure to strike at the dark demon that leads them.

passages.title: Strike Back
passages.text: You've been a great asset to my wranglers here. Please take this as a token of our gratitude.

passages.title: Where They Least Expect It
passages.text:
The Legion's fanatical crusade leaves them spread thin. As they focus their defenses on Argus, we are free to tear into their forces on other worlds.

Travel through an Invasion Point on Argus and show the Legion that there is no hiding from death.

passages.title: Where They Least Expect It
passages.text: No demon is safe while I draw breath.

passages.title: Where They Least Expect It
passages.text: So many Legion worlds are ripe for the taking...

passages.title: Respecting the Rites
passages.text:
If we be deliverin' Kel'vax's soul ta Bwonsamdi, we need ta be doin' it properly. We need ta be doin' two things.

First, dere be torches remainin' around da temple nearby. Light dem with da torch I gave ya.

Da torches used ta be our way ta show dat we be deliverin' a spirit ta Bwonsamdi. Kel'vax will be knowin' it be his time.

Second, I be needin' special ritual powder dat be deep within da temple. It be da key ta stoppin' Kel'vax.

Go now, I be prayin' Bwonsamdi be favorin' us.

passages.title: Respecting the Rites
passages.text: Light dem torches and get da powder so we be gettin' Bwonsamdi's favor.

passages.title: Respecting the Rites
passages.text: Good! Did ya feel Bwonsamdi's presence, even if it just be for a second?

passages.title: Kel'vax's Home
passages.text:
Kel'vax's soul be bound ta three phylacteries, protected by his voodoo. Even if ya destroy him, he just be reformin' in dem.

Me old power be returnin' after ya lit dem torches. I be able ta enchant dis powder dat allow ya ta go through Kel'vax's voodoo.

Find dese phylacteries and bring 'em ta me. We gonna look Kel'vax in da eye when we destroy 'em.

I should warn ya... dis powder might be messin' with ya head. Ya may have some... visions after ya use it. Be careful.

passages.title: Kel'vax's Home
passages.text: We need dem phylacteries if we be havin' a chance ta destroy Kel'vax.

passages.title: Kel'vax's Home
passages.text: Good! I be savin' dis for later. I want to be lookin' Kel'vax in da eye when we be destroyin' his phylacteries.

passages.title: A Moment of Respite
passages.text:
For all we have seen, we must remember not to dwell on the past, but to look forward and prepare for what is to come.

Take this opportunity to familiarize yourself with the Vindicaar.

passages.title: A Moment of Respite
passages.text: Light guide your path.

passages.title: A Moment of Respite
passages.text: Are you ready to continue on our journey?

passages.title: Hope They Can't Swim
passages.text:
We've got a small boat docked right across the way there. If we can get these villagers safely on board, they should be able to make it to Fallhaven by river.

You're a capable fighter, no doubt. Can I count on you to fend off any attackers while we get them to safety?

passages.title: Hope They Can't Swim
passages.text: We can begin evacuating on your mark.

passages.title: Hope They Can't Swim
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>. Those villagers owe you their lives.

Now that they're safe, we can focus on taking back the town.

passages.title: Charming the Lifeless
passages.text:
<You've seen a charm like this in Fallhaven being used to control a wicker construct.

If you can figure out how to use it, you may be able to take control of one of the coven's wicker constructs.>

passages.title: Charming the Lifeless
passages.text: What's this?

passages.title: Charming the Lifeless
passages.text:
You were able to control one of their creations?! That's amazing!

This could really turn the tide for us!

passages.title: Nazmir, the Forbidden Swamp
passages.text:
Da Horde promised Princess Talanji dat we be dealin' with dese blood trolls in Nazmir before dey can attack Zuldazar.

Grab a pterrordax and get over ta Talanji's camp in Nazmir. We be waitin' for ya there.

Make sure ya ready, <name>. Dere be no civilization in Nazmir, just us and whatever be lurkin' dere.

passages.title: Nazmir, the Forbidden Swamp
passages.text:
Good, you made it. We had to move fast to avoid getting caught up in any politics.

Let us proceed.

passages.title: Aiding the Wharf
passages.text:
We have read the tides, and never before have I seen them in such turmoil. They call to the tidesages, begging for help.

A debilitating sickness is running rampant amongst the villagers, and it comes from the sea.

We are but few. There is only so much we can do!

Please, take this list and gather the listed reagents from around the pier while I attempt to calm these folks. I should be able to create a tonic that will help.

I hope.

passages.title: Aiding the Wharf
passages.text:
My day-to-day job usually just consists of blessing the ships, reading the waters, finding the best spots to fish�

I fear that this may be out of my league.

passages.title: Aiding the Wharf
passages.text: No seaweed? This will not do at all!

passages.title: Strike Back
passages.text: The scroll details a dark spell which steals the souls from the neighboring Krokul to create a new demon, the Ur'zul. The scroll is signed by Lady Shahrazad.

passages.title: Strike Back
passages.text: You've been a great asset to my wranglers here. Please take this as a token of our gratitude.

passages.title: The Source of the Problem
passages.text:
I checked my work twice when working on this fountain. I made no mistakes. 

There must be something wrong at the source. 

The fountain draws water from a modest reservoir above the terrace. 

Would you mind checking it out?

passages.title: The Source of the Problem
passages.text: There's no good reason why this fountain should be malfunctioning.

passages.title: The Source of the Problem
passages.text: Well then, snakes! That explains it. I'm glad you cleared up that clog. The gulch looks greener already!

passages.title: The Irontide Crew
passages.text:
You see those salty looking guys in red? That's the Irontide crew.

They're the worst of the worst. Cutthroats and brigands, to a man.

Irontide wouldn't be guarding the docks if they didn't stand to gain something...

Lighten their pockets. See what kinda hardware they've got.

passages.title: The Irontide Crew
passages.text: What have you found?

passages.title: The Irontide Crew
passages.text:
Just as I thought - Irontide cut some kind of deal with Ashvane.

Figures... birds of a feather and all that.

passages.title: Crocolisk Life
passages.text:
I need my shaman mojo back if we are going to kill Urok. He beat me bad de last time I tried to put him down.

You help me get my power back, and I help you make Urok dead. Deal?

First step, I need you to use dis dagger to absorb what is left of de life force of any crocolisk you kill.

When de dagger seems full, come find me.

Heh heh, dat's right Sur'jan. Dey gonna help us, den Urok will see who de strongest is!

passages.title: Crocolisk Life
passages.text: Ah, dat looks good! Dis will make de ritual go by real nice.

passages.title: Felfire Shattering
passages.text:
A thin series of stone bridges connects the Burning Breach to Felfire Armory over Fiend's Run. The Army of the Light will stem Legion reinforcements while your people deal with the armory itself.

Work swiftly.

passages.title: Felfire Shattering
passages.text: There's nothing more beautiful than a lightburst charge erupting in a Legion stronghold. Your people afforded themselves well.

passages.title: Loaded for Bear
passages.text:
<This glittering cannonball stands out from the others. You notice the familiar sheen of Azerite across the surface.

You can't help but notice the nearby cannon, conveniently pointed at the ships loaded with stores of Ashvane Company weapons.>

passages.title: Loaded for Bear
passages.text: <Better to destroy these new weapons than to let them fall into the wrong hands.>

passages.title: Bolas and Birds
passages.text:
Up in the mountains we know the value of a good hunting companion. We use bolas to shoot down our flying prey, then our retrievers go and bring us our kill!

You want to take a shot? Nickel can accompany you. Shoot down some of the falcons in the woods. My dog will finish the job.

passages.title: Bolas and Birds
passages.text: There's nothing like man and beast working together for a clean hunt!

passages.title: Army of the Light
passages.text: Assist the Army of the Light by completing 4 world quests.

passages.title: Army of the Light
passages.text: The Army of the Light thanks you.

passages.title: Armies of Legionfall
passages.text: Assist the Armies of Legionfall by completing 4 world quests.

passages.title: Armies of Legionfall
passages.text: Return to me when you have finished aiding the Armies of Legionfall, <name>.

passages.title: Armies of Legionfall
passages.text: The Armies of Legionfall thank you, mate.

passages.title: Argussian Reach
passages.text: Assist the Argussian Reach by completing 4 world quests.

passages.title: Argussian Reach
passages.text: The Argussian Reach thank you.

passages.title: Changing Seasons
passages.text:
I appreciate you saving me again, but we should do something to prevent this from happening to anyone else.

So long as that Wicker Man stands, it will attract more like Autumnvale to it.

We should destroy it! Are you with me?

passages.title: Changing Seasons
passages.text: The Wicker Man must be destroyed!

passages.title: Changing Seasons
passages.text:
Well I've certainly learned my lesson.

Thank you, friend. I will return to Boralus with my parents now.  

Here, take this for your troubles.

passages.title: Pollen Punching
passages.text:
What I think happened is that some creature lapped up all the pollen with it's tongue.

While I'm curious as to what creature could have done this, I doubt it matters. I believe we can safely reproduce this without needing any sort of rare or dangerous reagents.

Next time you find a siren's sting, simply try wetting your glove so the pollen will stick to it. Water, wine, spit... It shouldn't matter.

passages.title: Akunda's Bite - Rank 2 Unlock
passages.text:
Amazed that anything so pure could continue to grow on this planet, you pick flower from the ground. You feel a small power radiate from it and then vanish.

As it falls apart in your hands, you wonder if anyone on this Light-forsaken place knows how to handle this precious herb.

passages.title: Akunda's Bite - Rank 3 Unlock
passages.text:
Amazed that anything so pure could continue to grow on this planet, you pick flower from the ground. You feel a small power radiate from it and then vanish.

As it falls apart in your hands, you wonder if anyone on this Light-forsaken place knows how to handle this precious herb.

passages.title: Aromatic Pollen - Rank 2 Unlock
passages.text:
Amazed that anything so pure could continue to grow on this planet, you pick flower from the ground. You feel a small power radiate from it and then vanish.

As it falls apart in your hands, you wonder if anyone on this Light-forsaken place knows how to handle this precious herb.

passages.title: Aromatic Pollen - Rank 3 Unlock
passages.text:
Amazed that anything so pure could continue to grow on this planet, you pick flower from the ground. You feel a small power radiate from it and then vanish.

As it falls apart in your hands, you wonder if anyone on this Light-forsaken place knows how to handle this precious herb.

passages.title: Gathering Mementos
passages.text:
I have a task that I can't really trust to anyone else, and I feel you could handle it with the reverence it deserves.

An old friend of mine came to me today, bringing a wilted sea stalk flower with her. Her husband was on a ship south east of Freehold. I'm not sure if it was pirates, the Horde, or a squall, but she said she didn't want revenge, just closure.

If you could get her something to remember him by, I'll tell you everything I know about sea stalks, and you'd have my gratitude.

passages.title: Gathering Mementos
passages.text: Have you found any of his personal effects?

passages.title: Gathering Mementos
passages.text:
I can't thank you enough for this.

Death seems to always haunt this land, but it's sting is somewhat lessened if we can still hold on to the memories of those departed. I'll need to get some fresh star moss for the funeral, but I'd prefer to do that myself.

Sadly, there isn't much left I can teach you about sea stalk. Let's see... something to help... ah, yes!

To help you get the most of each plant, instead of cutting it off, carefully pull it out of the sand and tear off the roots.

passages.title: Three Sheets to the Wind
passages.text:
Hey, <name>. Now isn't a great time for me.

If you're interested in learning, you could talk to Franklin, my old apprentice. He used to be a damn fine miner, but now he's just a washed up drunk. You can find him asleep on the docks.

I don't remember what he drinks, but if you bring him something he's sure to at least try it. He'll talk if he likes it.

Talk to Harold Atkey, the bartender, he's sells a variety of drinks, I'm sure one of them is his choice.

passages.title: Three Sheets to the Wind
passages.text:
<Myra's former apprentice, Franklin drunkenly stares at you.>

I ain't talkin'.... 'less you got a drink.

passages.title: Three Sheets to the Wind
passages.text:
<Franklin rambles almost incoherently, explaining the mechanics of mining storm silver from a seam>

... and that is how you... get the most of mining... Zzz...

<As Franklin drifts to sleep amidst a pungent cloud of alcohol vapors, you think of the advice he provided.

Eager to experiment with your new mining technique, you leave the sleeping man laying where he is.>

passages.title: Herb 07 - Rare - Rank 2 Unlock
passages.text:
Amazed that anything so pure could continue to grow on this planet, you pick flower from the ground. You feel a small power radiate from it and then vanish.

As it falls apart in your hands, you wonder if anyone on this Light-forsaken place knows how to handle this precious herb.

passages.title: Herb 07 - Rare - Rank 3 Unlock
passages.text:
Amazed that anything so pure could continue to grow on this planet, you pick flower from the ground. You feel a small power radiate from it and then vanish.

As it falls apart in your hands, you wonder if anyone on this Light-forsaken place knows how to handle this precious herb.

passages.title: Stone Soup
passages.text:
On the surface of the rock you find carvings of what you make out to be ingredients.

If you find the ingredients, perhaps you can make the troggs' soup for yourself.

passages.title: Stone Soup
passages.text: The flavor of the soup doesn't seem quite right. It must be missing ingredients.

passages.title: Stone Soup
passages.text:
The soup has somehow taken on a somewhat floral quality. It feels well-balanced on the tongue and goes down very smoothly.

This may be, in fact, the most delicious cuisine you have ever tasted.

passages.title: Fuel of a Doomed World
passages.text:
There is a rare and precious resource to be found in these wastes, <name>.

Argunite was once abundant on Argus. Its magical properties helped eredar civilization thrive. Far better for us to make use of its power than the Legion.

Seek out all the pristine argunite you can, champion. Every bit you recover will aid our cause.

passages.title: Fuel of a Doomed World
passages.text: Victory requires every resource we can muster.

passages.title: Fuel of a Doomed World
passages.text: A good start, hero. There is plenty more where that came from.

passages.title: Mark of the Bat
passages.text:
Dere are three witches in de camp who have talismans empowered by Hir'eek.

I need you to get those talismans for me to use after you prove my poison works perfectly.

I will use de essence of Hir'eek within de talismans to make my own poison strong enough to use against de loa.

If my poison doesn't work... well, I do not want to think about dat. It will work, because we need it to. 

Just go get de talismans. I will be here, hiding from de blood trolls.

passages.title: Mark of the Bat
passages.text: Did you get de talismans? We don't have much time until Hir'eek comes back out to try and eat us!

passages.title: Mark of the Bat
passages.text: You did it! Just need to grind dem up like dis... and done. Either dis poison will work... or we will both be dead.

passages.title: Isolating Zalamar
passages.text:
Hir'eek, de loa of bats, has been corrupted by G'huun! We will get no help from him.

We only have one option if dey have a loa on their side... we must kill Hir'eek.

It's crazy, and we will both probably die, but I have a plan. We need to isolate dis place first.

De blood trolls have wardrummers who sound an alarm if anything happens here. We need dem gone... but you have to be sneaky about it.

You have a good disguise, so you can order de drummers to go leave their posts.

passages.title: Isolating Zalamar
passages.text: Did you take care of de wardrummers?

passages.title: Isolating Zalamar
passages.text: Hah! Now we have plenty of room to mess with dis camp. Dere will be no reinforcements from de other blood trolls.

passages.title: Humbling the Terrors
passages.text:
When we first got here, I be findin' a whole buncha problems on da other side a Zardrax's barrow. 

Dere be dese monstrous zombies walkin' around da area. We gotta take 'em down ta make sure dey don't get ta Zuldazar.

I used me voodoo ta be modifyin' dat fetish ya just found. Use dis new fetish ta weaken and kill dem zombies.

passages.title: Humbling the Terrors
passages.text: Good work. We be savin' lots a people in Zuldazar from bein' crushed by dem zombies.

passages.title: Big Gulls Won't Die
passages.text:
Still one more... takes my bait... my fish...

My finger...

Kill him... you will be... rewarded...

passages.title: Big Gulls Won't Die
passages.text: Must... catch...

passages.title: Big Gulls Won't Die
passages.text:
Is he dead?

Yes... now I can catch... and gut... and catch...

More entrails... only the best for the sisters...

passages.title: Monstrous Energy
passages.text:
Have you ever heard about eel juice? I don't know if it's safe for <race>s like you, but tortollans love it! It gives us a burst of energy, and puts a spring in the step of even the oldest tortollan.

I saw some eels to the north of the estate when we were traveling. Can you go collect some of their venom for my dad?

passages.title: Monstrous Energy
passages.text: My dad will be so excited when he sees his favorite drink!

passages.title: Monstrous Energy
passages.text: Oh boy oh boy! He's gonna be pumped!

passages.title: Show Me What You've Got
passages.text:
It looks like you understand the basics. Now it's time to put everything together.

Head for the ring. Once you hear the starting pistol, you will have one minute to score as high as possible.

Gnolls are worth one point. Run 'em through with the harpoon!

If you see a paper zeppelin, bag it with your bolas for fifty points!

Leaping fences gives you style. Style gives you more points when you skewer gnolls or down zeppelins. It's super important, so don't forget to keep jumping fences!

passages.title: Show Me What You've Got
passages.text: Kul Tiran riding is a true show of mastery and sport!

passages.title: Show Me What You've Got
passages.text: What a showing!

passages.title: Salvage Rights
passages.text:
This poor trader was set upon by the yetis. There's nothing we can do for him now, but we would be remiss to let his supplies be laid to waste by these brutes.

See if you can find any supplies worth salvaging. You can use Bella as a pack horse.

Don't worry, she's a brave mare. She won't spook easily.

passages.title: Salvage Rights
passages.text: Have you found anything salvageable?

passages.title: Salvage Rights
passages.text:
I'm impressed. I didn't think there would be this much left from his shipment. This will be very helpful to our men at the gate.

Bella knows the way, so she should be able to get these to them.  This place is too dangerous to keep her hitched up, anyway.

passages.title: Blood of a Titan
passages.text:
<Before your eyes, a trickle of blood from the fallen titan Argus congeals into a flawless gemstone. Holding it in your palm, you sense an almost unfathomable power emanating from within... along with echoes of pain and sorrow.

It is the last remnant of a battle that should not have been winnable. An impossible achievement. Yet, as with all victories, this one came at tremendous cost.

You realize immediately to whom you must convey this prize.>

passages.title: Blood of a Titan
passages.text:
Champion, you have returned... and not a moment too soon.

The object you hold in your hands is but one of many mysteries unfolding before us.

passages.title: Forced Grounding
passages.text:
<This is one of the spears that Faithless trappers use to pull pterrordaxes to the ground. It has a long chain attached to its base.

With good aim, you could use it to pull a Faithless pterrordax rider to the ground so you could fight them.>

passages.title: Forced Grounding
passages.text: <Rakjan lifts his head proudly.>

passages.title: Forced Grounding
passages.text: <Rakjan nods in approval. That's one less Fangcaller to worry about.>

passages.title: A Jolt of Power
passages.text:
I have you to thank for removing that usurper. 

My strength is returning, unfortunately, the damage to my children has already been done. 

They are weak and dying. I need you to restore them.

My blessing will give you power over the storms. 

Use it to save my children, as you have saved me.

passages.title: The Burning Throne
passages.text:
The time has come, <name>, to begin our assault upon Antorus. Everything we have fought for, everything our friends and family have sacrificed, has brought us to this moment.

We will fire Light's Judgment upon the walls of the accursed citadel and storm their seat of power. We will end the Legion.

After all you have done, it is fitting that you have the honor. Speak to Romuul and let us finish our mission.

passages.title: The Burning Throne
passages.text: After so many years... so many sacrifices... victory is finally within our grasp.

passages.title: Antorus, the Burning Throne: The Death of a Titan
passages.text:
There is no way to express the depth of my sorrow. My rage. What Sargeras has done...

Argus, my home world, holds the soul of a titan. It has been twisted and corrupted beyond redemption, its power harnessed to fuel the Legion's infinite army.

We must do the impossible... breach the depths of Antorus and sever the Legion's connection to the world soul.

Please, <name>. End its pain, its suffering. In striking down the dark heart of Argus, we will defeat the Legion... and redeem the soul of my world.

passages.title: Antorus, the Burning Throne: The Death of a Titan
passages.text: Argus... what could have been...

passages.title: Antorus, the Burning Throne: The Death of a Titan
passages.text:
It is finished. At long last, the Burning Crusade is over.

I thank you for all you did, <name>. With the power of Argus feeding his Dark Pantheon, Sargeras would have been unstoppable.

On behalf of the draenei, the eredar, the countless worlds destroyed by the Legion...

Thank you.

passages.title: Fragments of the Abyss
passages.text:
Our scouts have delivered a disturbing report, champion.

Some of the more powerful creatures of the Void are carrying powerful crystals that augment their abilities. They now pose a greater threat than before, and we can no longer ignore them.

Find these void-tainted monstrosities and take their crystals. We will find a way to dispose of them safely.

passages.title: Antorus, the Burning Throne: Dark Passage
passages.text:
Despite the dangerous energies pulsing out from the heart of Argus, the Soulhunter travels unhindered through the Burning Throne. Our scouts report that his vessel harnesses the power of demonic runes to safely reach the Hallowed Felworks.

If we obtain those runes, it would allow the Vindicaar to follow the same route. This could save our forces valuable time.

passages.title: Antorus, the Burning Throne: Dark Passage
passages.text: Without the runes, we must face Sargeras' army head on.

passages.title: Antorus, the Burning Throne: Dark Passage
passages.text:
Magnificent work!

Once these runes are integrated into our shielding matrix, the Vindicaar will be able to bypass the Burning Throne's defenses and strike directly at the felworks.

passages.title: Best In Show
passages.text:
Now that the troggs have been taken care of, let's get on with the real show!

You've more than proven yourself as a capable rider - ready to get back in the ring and go big?

See if you can beat three hundred points!

passages.title: Best In Show
passages.text:
Some people say you cannot simply ride the horse - you must BECOME the horse.

That's poppycock. Just ride the horse.

passages.title: Best In Show
passages.text: What a showing!

passages.title: Souls for the Death Loa
passages.text:
Dere be blood trolls swarmin' all over dis place. Dey really be pickin' Torga clean, even eatin' his meat.

Dat be dark, even for me. 

Da souls of dese blood trolls be corrupted by eatin' a loa. Somethin' ya should be rememberin' for future reference.

Dese souls be worth a lot ta me, more dan just da normal souls of dese blood trolls. 

Get me da corrupted souls of dese blood trolls and I be callin' da spirit of Torga to ya.

passages.title: Souls for the Death Loa
passages.text: Ya haven't killed enough blood trolls!

passages.title: Souls for the Death Loa
passages.text: Good! I be collectin' all their souls now.

passages.title: Dreadtick Combustion
passages.text:
This whole thing is crazy, you know that? I don't think any story can top this one...

Bah! Do you hear that insufferable sound?

It's those stupid dreadticks sucking on Torga's meat. Makes my skin crawl! 

What? You can't hear it? Meh, trust me, they're around, and they need to be taken care of.

Here, take this scroll. We've had to deal with these dumb insects in the past. Read it near them and it'll cause them to explode.

passages.title: Dreadtick Combustion
passages.text: Blow those dreadticks up! Less of them overall is good for existence.

passages.title: Dreadtick Combustion
passages.text: I can rest a little easier knowing there are fewer of those... things in the world.

passages.title: Ritualistic Denial
passages.text:
I can't believe we're dealing with a death loa, a DEAD loa, and blood trolls. This isn't what I had planned today!

Look, some of the other tortollans have said there are some blood rituals going on. They were spooked and started heading for the coast when they saw it.

Take this scroll and read it near any blood rituals. It should cause it to disperse.

Be careful with my scroll! It's old and they don't make them like they used to.

passages.title: Upward and Onward
passages.text:
It is sad dat Hir'eek had to die, but at least de blood trolls are weaker now.

My potions are healing me up nicely. I did some looking around and came across dis guy.

He's skittish, but not hostile. I think you can use him to get out of here.

Hurry up and jump on, before he breaks de rope! I'll find my own way out; you don't have to worry.

passages.title: Upward and Onward
passages.text: Hurry up, dis guy is strong!

passages.title: Upward and Onward
passages.text:
Sorry. You did what you had to do... I can't believe dat dis G'huun could  corrupt a loa, of all things.

Nazmir is a cursed place... for everybody.

passages.title: Killer Crawgs
passages.text:
You heard Torga. We need to be taking de fight to de blood trolls if we want to stop dis herald of G'huun.

De blood trolls have monstrous crawgs in a camp nearby. We destroy dem, we weaken de blood trolls! 

De rest of us will move ahead to find out what else de blood trolls have planned around dis place.

passages.title: Tortollan Rescue
passages.text:
If Torga wants us to help you kill the herald of G'huun, then I guess we'll help. First, we need to rescue our people.

I found out that the blood trolls are draining the blood of our friends nearby and then feeding them to crawgs! 

This is no way for a tortollan to die, not after hundred of years gathering stories on Azeroth. 

Take this scroll. It'll purge whatever blood magic the blood trolls using on my friends.

Be careful with my scroll! I want it back in one piece.

passages.title: Negative Blood
passages.text:
Okay, you want to kill the herald of a blood god? We can figure something out.

There's corrupted blood nearby that's feeding this monster's power. Lucky for you, I've heard stories of this sort of thing before.

Take this scroll, but be careful with it! It'll destroy the corrupted blood that's feeding Jungo.

Oh, and I need you to find a scroll Holbruk was carrying, called the Scroll of Fate's Hand. It's REALLY powerful. We'll need it.

passages.title: Negative Blood
passages.text: Did you get that scroll and deal with the corrupted blood?

passages.title: Negative Blood
passages.text:
Good! Looks like that herald was weakened by what you did, and you got the scroll! Be careful, it's ancient! 

Holbruk always talked about how powerful that scroll was. We're going to see if he was right.

passages.title: Forcing Fate's Hand
passages.text:
I got some good news and bad news for you about this whole quest to destroy the herald of G'huun. Bad news first.

There's an entire army of skeletons between us and the next area. I'm guessing they used Torga's blood to animate them.

Good news is that scroll you recovered from Holbruk can summon the powerful Hand of Fate.

...and the bad news is that the scroll got damaged when Holbruk died and is only good for one more use.

Meh. Take this scroll and destroy that skeleton army!

passages.title: Forcing Fate's Hand
passages.text: I saw the destruction from here! Hrm, maybe I should try to fix that scroll up, you know, for future use.

passages.title: Loa-Free Diet
passages.text:
Princess Talanji thinks we're almost ready to kill this herald of G'huun. Maybe she's right, maybe we're all dead, who knows?

What I do know is the blood trolls here are... are carving and carrying away parts of Torga. Ugh!

From what I can tell, they're using poor Torga's meat to power their blood rituals. This has to stop!

Go out there and steal those pieces of meat from the blood trolls. I'll figure out a way to dispose of it.

passages.title: Loa-Free Diet
passages.text: You... get that loa meat yet?

passages.title: Loa-Free Diet
passages.text: This is no way for Torga's remains to be treated, <name>. I'll make sure this is properly destroyed.

passages.title: Sanctifying Ground
passages.text:
We are so close to weakening dis herald, <name>. Dis is our final push. De nearby area is brimming with blood magic.

While you were fighting, I was working on creating totems dat can cleanse de area of blood magic.

Take dese totems and place dem nearby. Dey should drain some of de blood magic out of de area.

De herald should be weak enough for us to actually kill after all dis.

passages.title: Sanctifying Ground
passages.text: Have you put de totems down yet?

passages.title: Sanctifying Ground
passages.text: De blood magic is dissipating from dis place. It is time for us to strike, before de blood trolls gain any more advantages.

passages.title: Crushing the Skullcrushers
passages.text:
Look, <name>, I'll be happy once we've killed this herald and we can have things go back to normal.

Until then, you need to deal with these monstrous blood trolls called "skullcrushers". Lovely, right?

As far as I can tell, these things have some sort of connection to this herald, might be why they're so huge.

You kill these skullcrushers and maybe we weaken this herald a bit more. Or maybe it gets even angrier and kills us all. 

We'll have to see.

passages.title: Crushing the Skullcrushers
passages.text: Those skullcrushers aren't going to kill themselves.

passages.title: Crushing the Skullcrushers
passages.text: Princess Talanji was saying something about feeling the blood magic dissipating from inside of Torga. I sure hope she's right.

passages.title: Antorus, the Burning Throne: The Heart of Argus
passages.text:
Hatuun tells me that after Argus fell, Sargeras ordered a temple of darkness to be built deep within the planet's core. Little is known of it, for only the titan's most devoted acolytes are given sigils that permit entrance.

If we lay claim to these sigils, they could be infused into the Vindicaar. This would allow our forces to stage a direct assault upon the fetid heart of Argus.

passages.title: Antorus, the Burning Throne: The Heart of Argus
passages.text: Have you located the sigils?

passages.title: Antorus, the Burning Throne: The Heart of Argus
passages.text:
With these sigils, the Vindicaar can bypass the Burning Throne's defenses.

The time has come to press our advantage and end this war.
