This must be the concoction Wrathion wrote about in his journal. Just standing near it grants you a sense of peace and clarity.

You may not have found the Black Prince himself, but perhaps what he left behind for you can help Ebonhorn.>

passages.title: Save Ebonhorn
passages.text:
My mind is finally my own again. Whatever Wrathion brewed into that potion has quieted the whispers.

But I take it you did not find the Black Prince himself.

passages.title: The Halls of Origination
passages.text:
It looks like the Halls of Origination have been claimed by a group o' tol'vir calling themselves the Amathet. I don't know much about them other than they're new in town and not the friendliest of types.

We'll need tae get in there and re-activate the forge, or else Azeroth will be done for!

passages.title: The Halls of Origination
passages.text: Azeroth's gonna be done for if we dun get this thing back online!

passages.title: The Halls of Origination
passages.text:
We got the forge back, but not before N'Zoth was able tae cripple her systems. 

I'm afraid our work is far from done.

passages.title: WANTED: Lady Naz'jess
passages.text:
Wanted for attacks against the people of Nazjatar. 

Lady Naz'jess has been driving the weapon masters to create crueler devices.

Last seen skulking about Zanj'ir Terrace. She is vicious, proceed with caution.

Upon completion of the mission, report to Seacaller Unow for commendation.

passages.title: WANTED: Lady Naz'jess
passages.text: Has her command come to an end?

passages.title: WANTED: Lady Naz'jess
passages.text: Well done, <class>. Lady Naz'jess had become a thorn in the side of the people here.

passages.title: WANTED: Commander Sarj'eth
passages.text:
Wanted for attacks against the people of Nazjatar. 

Commander Sarj'eth has attempted to enslave many Horde survivors.

He commands slavers in Zanj'ir Terrace. Extreme caution advised!

Upon completion of the mission, report to Seacaller Unow for commendation.

passages.title: WANTED: Commander Sarj'eth
passages.text: Did the brave commander reach the end of his days?

passages.title: WANTED: Commander Sarj'eth
passages.text:
Sarj'eth was a high-ranking commander among the naga. 

These people will sleep better, knowing he is gone.

passages.title: WANTED: Lord Ha'kass
passages.text:
Wanted for attacks against the people of Nazjatar. 

Lord Ha'kass has attempted to enslave many Horde survivors.

He commands slavers in Zanj'ir Wash. Extreme caution advised!

Upon completion of the mission, report to Seacaller Unow for commendation.

passages.title: WANTED: Lord Ha'kass
passages.text: Was the villain found?

passages.title: WANTED: Lord Ha'kass
passages.text:
Filth like him does not deserve to keep their head.

You just made the world a little bit better.

passages.title: WANTED: Lady Narjiss
passages.text:
Wanted for attacks against the Horde!

Lady Narjiss is responsible for leading several raids and ambushes against our soldiers.

Last seen on the outskirts of Zanj'ir Terrace. Extreme caution advised!

Upon completion of the mission, report to Seacaller Unow for commendation.

passages.title: WANTED: Lady Narjiss
passages.text: Did you silence her?

passages.title: WANTED: Lady Narjiss
passages.text: Lady Narjiss brought with her a darkness. The world feels a little lighter now.

passages.title: WANTED: Gler'thogg
passages.text:
Gler'thogg is responsible for the death and torture of many of the Unshackled. 

They have shared with us their pain. Bring back his eye.

He dwells in the Deepcoil Tunnels. Extreme caution advised!

Upon completion of the mission, report to Seacaller Unow for commendation.

passages.title: WANTED: Gler'thogg
passages.text: Is this your first enucleation?

passages.title: WANTED: Gler'thogg
passages.text: That tentacled terror will torture them no more.

passages.title: WANTED: Inquisitor Ithriza
passages.text:
Wanted for attacks against the Horde!

Inquisitor Ithriza is responsible for leading several raids and ambushes against our soldiers.

Last seen in the vicinity of Dragon's Teeth Basin. Extreme caution advised!

Upon completion of the mission, report to Seacaller Unow for commendation.

passages.title: WANTED: Inquisitor Ithriza
passages.text: Did you knock him down a peg?

passages.title: WANTED: Inquisitor Ithriza
passages.text: One tormentor down, so many to go.

passages.title: Reinforced Cache
passages.text:
The heavily reinforced chest is of naga construction and appears to be reinforced with a heavy-duty lock of some kind.

Reinforcement aside, the cache still requires a key to unlock.

The key is most likely being held by one of the nearby naga commanders.

passages.title: Reinforced Cache
passages.text: The chest is locked and requires a key.

passages.title: Reinforced Cache
passages.text: As you turn the key you can hear the heavy latches of the chest snap open with considerable force...

passages.title: Void Cache
passages.text:
The heavily reinforced chest is of naga construction and appears to be reinforced with a magical lock of some kind.

Magical reinforcement aside, the cache still requires a key to unlock.

The key is most likely being held by one of the nearby naga commanders.

passages.title: Void Cache
passages.text: The chest is locked and requires a key.

passages.title: Void Cache
passages.text: The magical barrier dissipates as you insert the key...

passages.title: Arcane Cache
passages.text:
The heavily reinforced chest is of naga construction and appears to be reinforced with a magical lock of some kind.

Magical reinforcement aside, the cache still requires a key to unlock.

The key is most likely being held by one of the nearby naga commanders.

passages.title: Arcane Cache
passages.text: The chest is locked and requires a key.

passages.title: Arcane Cache
passages.text: The magical barrier dissipates as you insert the key...

passages.title: Friends In Need
passages.text:
I doubt that will be the last we've seen of Priscilla, but at least she is no longer one of our immediate concerns.

We must think carefully before making our next move. In the meantime we should continue to build upon our relationship with our new allies, the Ankoan. Work with them to secure the area and hone their skills, we're not out of the woods yet.

I fear the biggest battle is still to come. Let's show them that together we can take on Azshara's forces and succeed!

passages.title: Friends In Need
passages.text: Good work, while you were gone Shandris and I have been talking and I think she's found a promising lead for us to focus our efforts.

passages.title: Down But Not Out
passages.text:
Ashvane won't trouble us for now, but our situation remains perilous.

I must consider our next move, <name>. In the meantime we should continue to build upon our relationship with our new allies, the Unshackled. Test them in combat, train them while you can, we will need their aid in the battles to come.

We will show them that through unity there are no obstacles that can stand in our way.

passages.title: Down But Not Out
passages.text: Good work, while you were gone I was able to make some progress in locating our next objective.

passages.title: Preserved Clues
passages.text:
We have found similar chests, as you describe. We believe they were left behind by one that came before the naga.

Some are even locked by odd arcane runes, the naga seem most interested in those.

I know little about them, save that we find them most often in the city ruins.

If you seek to decipher their history, I would begin there.

passages.title: Preserved Clues
passages.text:
<A simple tome with a small series of runes inscribed along the spine, it appears remarkably well-maintained amongst the ruins. 

Upon further inspection, it appears to be a diary of one of the citizens of the city. No doubt the magic that preserves it was intended to allot for the lengthy lifetimes of the elves.>

passages.title: Preserved Clues
passages.text:
If you find anything else in those chests that you don't need, you feel free to bring it on over my way.

Found a few of them myself. Don't look like they belong to the naga, probably someone that lived in the city.

Some are locked tight by arcane magic, seen the naga taking those back with them. Probably got the good stuff in there.

I don't know much more than that. If you want a history lesson, I'd snoop around the city ruins.

passages.title: Preserved Clues
passages.text:
<A simple tome with a small series of runes inscribed along the spine, it appears remarkably well-maintained amongst the ruins. 

Upon further inspection, it appears to be a diary of one of the citizens of the city. No doubt the magic that preserves it was intended to allot for the lengthy lifetimes of the elves.>

passages.title: The Battle of Alterac
passages.text:
The Explorers' League believes there are artifacts in Alterac Valley, but the Frostwolf orcs won't let us explore. We can't allow the Horde to stop our scholarly pursuits! Defeat the Frostwolf general, Drek'Thar. With him dead, the orcs will lose their edge.

Drek'Thar is in Frostwolf Keep, in the south of Alterac Valley. Vanquish him, and then return to me.

passages.title: The Battle of Alterac
passages.text: Well done, <name>!  With the Horde's nose bloodied after the death of their general, we'll have the breathing room we need to explore!

passages.title: The Battle for Alterac
passages.text:
The Stormpike dwarves and their allies have invaded Alterac Valley, and we must drive them out! To win the battle for Alterac, we must defeat their general, Vanndar Stormpike!

You will find Vanndar in Dun Baldar, in the north of Alterac Valley.

Destroy him, <name>, and then return to me.

passages.title: The Battle for Alterac
passages.text:
Well done, <name>!  Stormpikes have no hope in this foolish invasion.

Hah!  So far, all they've done is get their general killed!

passages.title: Ivus the Forest Lord
passages.text:
The Frostwolf Clan is protected by a taint of elemental energy. Their shaman meddle in powers that will surely destroy us all if left unchecked.

The damage has grown too great for the Circle to control! Ivus must be called to our aid.

The Frostwolf soldiers carry elemental charms called storm crystals. We can use the charms to conjure Ivus. Venture forth and claim the crystals, <name>!

passages.title: Ivus the Forest Lord
passages.text: Have you brought us some crystals, <name>?

passages.title: Ivus the Forest Lord
passages.text: Well done, <name>. I will use the power of this charm to augment the magic that has already been gathered. When enough power has been amassed, I shall focus the collected energies and call upon the Forest Lord to aid our cause.

passages.title: Lokholar the Ice Lord
passages.text:
I come from Thunder Bluff, <race>. Cairne himself has seen to it that I assist the Frostwolf Clan in these dire times.

But let us not waste any more time. You must strike down our enemies and bring to me their blood. Once enough blood has been gathered, the ritual of summoning may begin.

Victory will be assured when the elemental lord is loosed upon the Stormpike army.

passages.title: Lokholar the Ice Lord
passages.text: Have you come with an offering?

passages.title: Lokholar the Ice Lord
passages.text: The blood of our enemies has been shed. I shall mix this blood with the rest that has been gathered. Once the offering is complete, the Ice Lord shall show these Stormpike dogs the full wrath of the Frostwolf Clan!

passages.title: We've Got Crabs!
passages.text:
<name>, you're just in time. Everything's ready for the crab hunt!

Okay, okay... I know what you're thinking. A founding member of D.E.H.T.A. that condones hunting?

I'm going to level with you, <name>. I've got a bar full of hungry murlocs that only eat three things: crabs, fish, and people.

If that's not reason enough, crabs are overpopulated in this region and they're decimating the local grub worm population!

How many innocent grub worms need to die before we do something, <name>?

passages.title: We've Got Crabs!
passages.text: How many innocent grub worms need to die before we do something, <name>?

passages.title: We've Got Crabs!
passages.text: That's quite the case of crabs you've got there, <name>. Well done! Please set it down behind the bar and I'll take care of the rest.

passages.title: Drunk Angry Murlocs
passages.text:
Those no-good Bloodfins ran off with all of the beer!

I've been experimenting with brews that only use ingredients native to Nazjatar, but it's still a work in progress. For now, I must rely on whatever I can scrounge up from the shipwreck.

My supply of beer was already limited, but now it's all gone thanks to those thieving Bloodfin murlocs! We're going to have some very angry customers here if we don't get it back.

Please recover the stolen lager from Bloodfin Village before it's too late!

passages.title: Drunk Angry Murlocs
passages.text: Please tell me you found the beer.

passages.title: Drunk Angry Murlocs
passages.text: Good work, <name>! You've recovered pretty much all of the stolen beer. Those Bloodfins are more trouble than they're worth!

passages.title: Mgglurky's Mugglrgl
passages.text:
My cook, Mgglurky, lost his mugglrgl and he's refusing to work until he gets it back.

I've got a bar full of hungry murlocs and nothing to feed them until Mgglurky starts cooking. If Mgglurky doesn't find his mugglrgl soon, we're going to have a riot on our hands!

I don't know about you, but I definitely don't want to be the main course tonight.

There were some Bloodfins lurking around earlier. Search Bloodfin Village for the mugglrgl and bring it back to me once you find it.

passages.title: Mgglurky's Mugglrgl
passages.text: If Mgglurky doesn't find his mugglrgl soon, we're going to have a riot on our hands!

passages.title: Mgglurky's Mugglrgl
passages.text: You've found it! So this is a mugglrgl? For some reason I thought it would be bigger. Mgglurky will be happy you returned it!

passages.title: The High Life
passages.text:
You there, I require some help.

Everyone where I once called home lost their lives to the flood. I still don't know what became of my father, Corin. 

It pains me to return to the estates, and there are vengeful spirits who haunt the once pristine grounds. Will you help me find out what happened to my father?

passages.title: The High Life
passages.text:
<name>, Corin is being tormented by that naga shadowcaster. 

We have to do something!

passages.title: Your First Charge is Free!
passages.text:
Do you feel the energy rippling through the ground here, my dear test subject?

<Flip inhales deeply.>

Without that constant bristle of electricity, nothing of any meaning would exist.

My dear sister and I have tapped into a high-voltage power line buried here, but the real juice is over in Bondo's Yard. He selfishly hoards access to the heftiest power line in Mechagon!

If you want to recharge your empty energy cells, you're going to have to get access to the Charging Station from Flux.

passages.title: Your First Charge is Free!
passages.text:
Flux is rude, crude, and I suspect more than a little unglued.

Be careful with that wondrous energy cell. Those little packs of power are worth their weight in gold out here in Mechagon!

passages.title: Changing Tides
passages.text:
We are out of time. We must gain control the Tidestone of Golganneth and the Javelin is our best shot at piercing the barrier surrounding it.

The guardian is formidable, but must be defeated if we are to take the fight to Azshara. What forces we have will be arrayed below, just outside their encampment.

I would trust you with the Javelin of Suramar, <name>. We will need your strength in the coming battle.

passages.title: Changing Tides
passages.text: If we do not take the Tidestone, we are finished.

passages.title: Changing Tides
passages.text: Quickly, the Tidestone!

passages.title: Uncovering the Artifact Fragments
passages.text: The Artifact Fragments seem to come from any creature we've found in the outskirts of Ashran. Go out and kill any you find and bring at least fifty to Ecilam the Mage near the campfire in Stormshield Stronghold.

passages.title: Uncovering the Artifact Fragments
passages.text: Are those Artifact Fragments, I see?

passages.title: Uncovering the Artifact Fragments
passages.text: Good work. If you happen to find anymore Artifact Fragments, bring them to me or the others in need of them to contribute to the war effort.

passages.title: Uncovering the Artifact Fragments
passages.text:
The Artifact Fragments seem to come from any creature we've found in the outskirts of Ashran.

Go out and kill any you find and bring at least fifty Artifact Fragments to Fura the Mage in Warspear Outpost.

passages.title: Uncovering the Artifact Fragments
passages.text: Are those Artifact Fragments, I see?

passages.title: Uncovering the Artifact Fragments
passages.text: Good work. If you happen to find anymore Artifact Fragments, bring them to me or the others in need of them to contribute to the war effort.

passages.title: Volrath Must Die
passages.text:
The Horde are getting in our way of completing our mission here in Ashran. Their leader is High Warlord Volrath. He must be put down.

Push forth through the center road, enter Warspear and slay Volrath.

passages.title: Volrath Must Die
passages.text: Well done. That will give the Horde something to think about next time they decide to test us here in Ashran.

passages.title: Tremblade Must Die
passages.text:
This battle in Ashran has waged on long enough. It appears they're being led by Grand Marshal Tremblade. If she falls, the Alliance will crumble.

Push forward through the center road, make your way into their keep and take down Tremblade.

For the Horde!

passages.title: Tremblade Must Die
passages.text: That's what I like to see, good work <class>.

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: We Can Make It Stronger...
passages.text:
Now that it's functioning, it occurred to me while repairing it that it has the capability to output even more energy.

Of course that will require stronger materials to upgrade and the only place I can think of is in the Eternal Palace.

Azshara's army and even herself carry items of extraordinary power. If you could bring some of those back, I could at the very least test my theory and see if it's viable.

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: We Can Make It Stronger...
passages.text: How goes the search for those items?

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: We Can Make It Stronger...
passages.text:
Yes, these will do nicely. Good work, <name>.

I'll get started right away on upgrading the core.

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: Pushing the Limits
passages.text:
Now that we know how to increase the potency of this tool, I think we can push its capabilities even further.

Bring me back more of those ornaments. LOTS of them.

Let's see just how far we can make this go.

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: Pushing the Limits
passages.text: Any luck on retrieving more of those ornaments?

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: Pushing the Limits
passages.text:
Wow, that's...a lot!

Alright, let's see what this thing can do.

passages.title: Scouting the Palace
passages.text:
We cannot hide here forever, <name>. Azshara must be dealt with.

It would be an act of folly to assault her palace without knowing what defenses she has in place. I dispatched a scouting team while you were gone, but they have not reported back.

I'm getting concerned, <name>. Let me know when you're ready and I'll perform a ritual to see what has happened to our scouts.

passages.title: Scouting the Palace
passages.text: Are you ready?

passages.title: Scouting the Palace
passages.text: The Tidestone! Of course...

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: Pushing the Limits
passages.text:
Now that we know how to increase the potency of this thing, I think we can push its capabilities even further.

Bring me back more of those ornaments. LOTS of them.

Let's see just how far we can make this go.

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: Pushing the Limits
passages.text: Any luck on retrieving more of those ornaments?

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: Pushing the Limits
passages.text:
Wow, that's...a lot!

Alright, let's see what this thing can do.

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: We Can Make It Stronger...
passages.text:
Now that it's functioning, it occurred to me while repairing it that it has the capability to output even more energy.

Of course that'll require stronger materials to upgrade and the only place I can think of is in the Eternal Palace.

Azshara's army and even herself carry items of extraordinary power. If you could bring some of those back, I could at the very least test my theory and see if it's viable.

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: We Can Make It Stronger...
passages.text: How goes the search for those items?

passages.title: The Eternal Palace: We Can Make It Stronger...
passages.text:
Yes, these'll do nicely. Good work, <name>.

I'll get started right away on upgrading the core.

passages.title: Battle Tested
passages.text:
A weapon like this could really turn the tide against King Mechagons Troops. Let's go see how their gear matches up against our new toy.

Take out King Mechagon's Sentries wherever you can find them

passages.title: Battle Tested
passages.text: Go kill something!

passages.title: Battle Tested
passages.text: This is what I like to see!

passages.title: Be Kind, Rewind
passages.text:
You exist here due to a time anomaly, but you must return to your own time and help us there.

The Visual Holo Sphere from the Vaultbot nearby contains the data necessary to defeat King Mechagon before he can use the Mechoriginator.

Deliver the Visual Holo Sphere to me in your reality. With luck I will be able to rewind history and prevent this existence from ever happening.

passages.title: Be Kind, Rewind
passages.text: You will have to return to your time period.

passages.title: Be Kind, Rewind
passages.text: Let's hope that you bringing me this, is not what triggers that alternate reality.

passages.title: Break a Few Eggs
passages.text:
The naga are using these caverns as a hatchery for their deadly deepcoil serpents.

These deepcoil serpents are especially dangerous because they have been infused with dark void magic.

We must put a stop to this operation before it is too late. The naga forces are already quite powerful. I do not wish to imagine what would happen if Azshara also had an army of these deepcoil serpents as well.

Our only hope is to destroy the deepcoil eggs before they hatch.

passages.title: Break a Few Eggs
passages.text: Have you destroyed the deepcoil eggs?

passages.title: Break a Few Eggs
passages.text: You have done well, <name>. We cannot allow the naga to amass an army of these mutated deepcoil serpents. We will need to keep a close eye on this place...

passages.title: Forging Onward
passages.text:
Thanks fer helpin' me back there at the forge. It's vexin' that N'Zoth was able to infiltrate it so quickly, but at least we arrived in time tae keep it from bein' completely wrecked!

Now comes the task of gettin' her back tae a hundred percent. MOTHER has been workin' on a solution, and we think we've got a plan.

passages.title: Forging Onward
passages.text: Aye?

passages.title: Forging Onward
passages.text: It looks like we're in for quite an adventure, champion!

passages.title: A Bolt from the Blue
passages.text:
You have done much to empower the Heart of Azeroth, and I am proud that the dragonflights have lent their strength to your cause.

It is now time for the blue dragonflight to do the same.

When I first learned of the essences, I knew that some remnant of my dragonflight's power must be out there, coalescing where we were once strong.

That is exactly what I have found. The Kirin Tor have isolated its signature at the Nexus, but only the wielder of the Heart of Azeroth can claim it.

passages.title: A Bolt from the Blue
passages.text: The power of the Heart of Azeroth never ceases to amaze me.

passages.title: A Bolt from the Blue
passages.text:
We entrust you with this power, champion, because we believe that you will be the one to save Azeroth.

Wield it well.

passages.title: Wastewander Coins
passages.text:
It may be too late for some of our fallen brothers and sisters, but it is not too late to give solace to their families.

Every Wastewander carries with them a unique coin, signifying their status as a member of our group.

If you find any of these coins, please bring them to me and I will make sure they are properly returned to their next of kin.

passages.title: Wastewander Coins
passages.text: Do you have coins to return?

passages.title: Wastewander Coins
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. I will see to it that these make it into the right hands.

passages.title: On Ghostly Wings
passages.text:
We will meet you back where our journey began, <name>. 

Corin and I have been separated for many years. We have so much to catch up on. 

As a token of our gratitude we will remain in the area to help you in your travels through this cursed land.

passages.title: On Ghostly Wings
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

Because of your efforts, we have some the peace of mind that was long lost.

My father and I are at your service.

passages.title: Small Skull
passages.text:
<Inside of the gelatinous remains of the slime you find a small skeleton.

Someone in Rustbolt might be missing. 

You pick up the skull, it might still be able to be identified.>

passages.title: Small Skull
passages.text:
Another one? Don't worry, there's no tragedy behind this skull. It's not real.

When we first started finding the skeletons, we feared the worst. Our children getting lost in the wastes and devoured!

But no, the kids are safe.

It's him, he's tormenting us. King Mechagon. Heard he has some new technology, calling it "thrice die mentioned smithing." Lets him make whatever he wants.

And he chooses to make fake baby skeletons.

<Vera shakes her head.>

Just toss it in the grinder with the rest.

passages.title: Rusty Tube
passages.text:
<The malfunctioning junkbot is now a mere heap of metal, its signature tube poking out of the remains.

You remove the tube. The citizens of Rustbolt seem to trade in junk, maybe someone will want it.>

passages.title: Rusty Tube
passages.text:
A tube? A rusty tube. Aw, you shouldn't have!

<Vera laughs and then looks closer at the tube.>

Hold a moment, an 18 unit tube? You're telling me the circumference of this tube is 18 standard units. That's what I'm seeing here with my unit gauge.

Holy manufactured light, that is just perfect for my hair dryer.

You're the best! Well, best tube-finder, at least.

passages.title: Flashing Siren
passages.text:
<Despite the robot being destroyed, the siren continues flashing.

Clearly this was a key sentry of King Mechagon. The citizens of Rustbolt will want to know of its demise.>

passages.title: Flashing Siren
passages.text:
Gold trim on the base. This must be from that golden robot patrolling the city outskirts?

Nice hit, that thing has been a pain in our side for as long as I can remember.

Not because it actually catches us--it's terrible at that.

No, the thing wanders into the city in the middle of the night, and looks in our rooms! Just imagine -- you're sound asleep, then the room is lit up bright red, and there's a robot just standing there, looking at you.

It wanders away eventually, but wow, how rude!

passages.title: Mechanical Egg Sac
passages.text:
<You find a mechanical egg sac inside of the defunct spiderbot.

This doesn't make any sense, robots don't reproduce this way.

Or do they?

Someone in Rustbolt might have the answers.>

passages.title: Mechanical Egg Sac
passages.text:
Well that's creepy.

Maybe King Mechagon thought we'd be scared of mechanical creatures that could reproduce.

I could see him doing something like that. Reveals his own fears more than ours.

Or maybe the mechanical spiders are... evolving.

Can programs do that?

...

Am I a program?

<Vera sits down to think.>

passages.title: Can of Critter Spray
passages.text:
<Inside the wreckage of the robot, you find a sealed can of anti-critter spray.

Destroying all life, down to the rats, seems cruel but on par for King Mechagon.

Someone in Rustbolt might be able to provide additional insight.>

passages.title: Can of Critter Spray
passages.text:
Oh, yeah, you didn't hear? Proclamation 7: King Mechagon outlawed non-mechanicals smaller than a baby.

He thought that was so important that it was his SEVENTH proclamation ever made.

<Vera shakes her head.>

The king hated bugs, rats, anything uninvited that always finds its way into a city. So, he made them illegal. 

He arrested rabbits, squirrels, even fish. Held tiny trials, sentenced them to mechanization, or death, or exile.

He made those flying robots to deal with any that remained.

passages.title: Cluckbox
passages.text:
<In the sparking, smoldering wreckage of Unit 35, you find a small, black cube.

It looks to be made of a metallic substance and appears unharmed.

Looking closely, you see a single word imprinted in the metal -- "Cluckbox."

This particular mechanical fowl was operating quite strangely. Someone in Rustbolt will probably want to investigate.>

passages.title: Cluckbox
passages.text:
Is that the cluckbox from that rust-blooded Unit 35? I hate that thing!

<Vera grabs the box from you and throws it to the ground. She stomps on it a few times, then once more for good measure.>

Someone programmed that thing to wake up the island at dawn every morning! Who does that?

<Vera glares in the direction of the city.>

If you see that thing show up again, smash it good for me.

passages.title: Broken Unit 6
passages.text:
<Unit 6 sits here, nonfunctional following your attack.

There is something different and unsettling about this mechanical frog. It appeared to be mimicking frog behavior, but in a way that seemed wrong somehow.

None of the other mechanical frogs in the area behave similarly.

Instead of taking back only part of the unit for inspection, you pocket the entire frog. It's pretty small, after all.>

passages.title: Broken Unit 6
passages.text:
Is that one of the mechanical critters? Ah, one of the dark metal ones.

I've never seen one up close. I kept my distance because they never felt... right to me.

No one in Rustbolt knows where they came from. Perhaps King Mechagon sent them to watch the other critters as they mechanized? He would be the type to want to watch their suffering.

Most think they're here to spy on us. You shouldn't have brought the whole thing back to the town. Just grab an eye, or a liver, next time.

passages.title: Mechanical Eye
passages.text:
<As the mechanical body of Unit 17 crumples into a heap, one eye lights up.

You hear a popping noise, and the eye flies from the head, aided by a small explosion.

You pick up the eye and notice it twitch a few times, then power down.

The citizens of Rustbolt seem to like junk, maybe they'll be interested in this.>

passages.title: Mechanical Eye
passages.text:
You retrieved this from a mechanical marmot? It must have been that one with the smoke-colored metal.

Did I ever tell you my story about that sinister Unit 17?

So there I was, browsing the scrap heap for junk, like you do. Suddenly, it's right in front of me -- Unit 17. 

I froze. Did it see me? What would it do? I took one step backwards, it twitched, I yelped.

Then it blared at me in a tone I will never forget.

"Error 74."

I ran back as fast as my legs could take me.

<Vera shudders.>

passages.title: Wiggletail's Poking Fork
passages.text:
<The tenacious tine of the vanquished prince.

It does not thrum with any power whatsoever. In fact, it appears quite plain, and a bit rusted.

You pocket it anyway. Perhaps Artisan Itanu would be interested?>

passages.title: Wiggletail's Poking Fork
passages.text:
Ah hello again, have you more treasures from the deep?

Oh, an eating instrument. You will have to convince me of its value here, friend.

It came from a small naga? Hm, yes. I have seen one such as you describe. 

I have thought many long hours about where it may have come from. 

I have concluded that it is best not to think on it.

I will gladly take this fork from you to aid in removing the barnacles from my home, though.

passages.title: Wiggletail's Poking Fork
passages.text:
<The tenacious tine of the vanquished prince.

It does not thrum with any power whatsoever. In fact, it appears quite plain, and a bit rusted.

You pocket it anyway. Perhaps Finder Palta would be interested?>

passages.title: Wiggletail's Poking Fork
passages.text:
Oh hey, how's it going? Got anything to sell? Or buy?

A fork? You brought me a fork? 

It came from a tiny naga? Oh, yeah, I've seen that one. We talk about it all the time! What even is that thing?

Is it a baby naga? Or maybe just a vision from the deeps? Where did it come from?

I have no answers for you, friend. But I'll take that fork -- it's almost dinner time.

Think I'll have the fish.

passages.title: Leathery Venom Gland
passages.text:
<You pry a leathery gland from the snapdragon corpse. Drops of venom spill from an opening on one end and sizzle as they touch the ground, leaving small holes behind.

This toxin appears to be very potent. It would be best to bring it back to Mezzamere.>

passages.title: Leathery Venom Gland
passages.text:
Friend, let me take that from you, it is best not to handle the venom for too long.

The naga tame the snapdragon with ease, but we have more difficulty. They seem to have a natural affinity for them. I envy them somewhat, the creatures are both vicious and loyal.

The venom they spit is deadly. I have only known one to truly master it, a naga commander. We believe she feeds on the substance to give herself immunity. I do not know how this is possible, she must be a terror in combat.

passages.title: Half-Digested Deepcoral Pod
passages.text:
<Upon inspection of this oddly-aggressive fathom ray, you find several halfway-digested pods.

You've seen similar pods on the coral of this region, it appears to be one of the foods of the fathom rays.

This may explain their strange ability to fly.

Artisan Itanu might know more.>

passages.title: Half-Digested Deepcoral Pod
passages.text:
Hello again, have you come to trade?

Ah yes, the coral produces such pods. The fathom rays have a liking for them, we can sometimes lure one into a trap with them, to tame or consume.

The pods are filled with a gas of some sort, I have never ventured to breathe it myself, but I surmise this diet now keeps the rays aloft.

The creatures of the deeps have not seen the air before, yet I could not have foreseen such an outcome. It is fascinating.

passages.title: Molted Spineshell
passages.text:
<The molted shell of a defeated spine crab, a vicious species of crab first encountered in Nazjatar.

The spines that stick out from it are quite sharp.

Artisan Itanu may have some use for this.>

passages.title: Molted Spineshell
passages.text:
That is quite a pretty shell, we find them around when the spine crabs molt.

Spine crabs lurk in the deep trenches, waiting on large fish to spear and devour. The beasts of our waters are not as kind as yours.

The shells themselves are not useful to us -- they become flimsy and brittle over time.

Once, the children would fill them with sand and hang them on the coral as decorations.

That was long ago.

<Itanu tosses the shell into the sand with a deep sigh.>

passages.title: Pearlescent Shell
passages.text:
<A large, hardened shell of a vanquished hermit crab.

The shell itself was much larger than the crab, and shines in different colors when you look at it at different angles.

Surely someone back at Mezzamere would be interested in this beautiful shell.>

passages.title: Pearlescent Shell
passages.text:
Ah, a hermit crab shell. The crabs here are not easy to hunt, nor are they worthwhile. The size of the crab is so small, barely makes for a single meal.

The shells themselves are quite useful. We use them in making spear tips, shields, even cookware and pots. They are quite versatile and do not lose their durability with time.

I shall add this one to the supplies, with our thanks.

passages.title: Eel Jelly
passages.text:
<You examine the corpse of the abyssal eel, only to find it bathed in a strange slime.

The slime coats your hands and arms, and seems quite difficult to remove.

One of your deep sea allies may know more about it.>

passages.title: Eel Jelly
passages.text:
Eel jelly? What have you gotten yourself into? Eels, I would guess.

Here, let me remove it from you. We have many uses for it, if you can believe it. Few other things can make things slick, here beneath the waves. You may find it useful as well.

<Itanu rubs some jelly on your arms and legs.>

You will slide between coral like the tides now, friend.

passages.title: Mottled Hydra Scale
passages.text:
<The scale of a recently-defeated hydra hatchling, it appears to be a mixture of several colors.

There appears to be a battle for dominance between the hydra of the region, one of your new allies may know more.>

passages.title: Mottled Hydra Scale
passages.text:
Ah, a hydra scale, we do have a fair bit of them around here.

They have three matriarchs leading their packs. Each one has attempted to gain dominance over the area for years, yet they always fail.

The naga amuse themselves by sending slaves into the area to be devoured.

They are friends of none, we had best leave them be.

passages.title: Strange Organ
passages.text:
<You find a strange organ in the corpse of the mindbender. Upon picking it up, your head begins to throb.

The octopus-like creatures have long been one of Azeroth's mysteries, this organ may shed some light on them.

Someone in Mezzamere may know more.>

passages.title: Strange Organ
passages.text:
The organ from a mind-squid, yes, I am familiar with them.

The children of Ozumat flood the deeps, too numerous to count. 

They attack our thoughts with the aid of this organ. It makes a sound that speaks directly to the mind.

Let me show you.

<Itanu pushes on the organ, and your mind is assailed by a deafening psychic scream.>

The very creature itself seems built to harass the mind, and service the old ones.

I will dispose of this now, away from the camp.

passages.title: Overgrown Stone
passages.text:
<A stone taken from the earthy elemental you recently defeated, covered in kelp and various other underwater plants.

You have not seen many such creatures in the deeps. Perhaps there is a story to them.

One of your new undersea allies may know more.>

passages.title: Overgrown Stone
passages.text:
Oh hello, what have you there?

A fragment from a kelp-covered elemental? Most fortuitous. Such stones can be used to enhance the growth of most sorts of plants that we know of.

At times, I use them to grow healing wraps for us, when I can find them. The elementals themselves are quite rare.

I thank you for this donation.

passages.title: Crackling Mandible
passages.text:
<The mandible of a tidal guardian, still crackling with electricity.

One of your new allies might have a use for this.>

passages.title: Crackling Mandible
passages.text:
Oh, let me handle that with care, I do not want another shock.

You have met the tidal guardians, then? They have lived in the naga caves for as long as I can recall, serving their masters faithfully. I have not seen one while hunting in the wild in my lifetime.

We can make many things with their mandibles, from spearheads to electrified traps. I will put this to good use.

passages.title: Frenzy Fang
passages.text:
<You remove a fully-grown fang from the fallen frenzy.

You have heard of some seafaring groups that made weapons or decorations out of fangs found in the deeps, perhaps your new allies could find use for this?>

passages.title: Frenzy Fang
passages.text:
<Itanu holds the tooth between his fingers.>

The frenzies serve none but themselves.

You do not know of them.

<Itanu looks at the open sky.>

They cannot come here, now. Once they were a force that even the naga feared. Even their most powerful champions feared them.

What little light we would have would be doused, when the frenzies would come. Their numbers would blot out the sun. Their teeth would find all unhidden flesh.

You will never know the terror of the deeps, dry one.

passages.title: Opaline Conch
passages.text:
<The conch slumps following your assault -- the battle appears to be over.

It doesn't move. You bend over and pick it up, instinctively turning it over, wary of any attack.

It appears to be dead, but intact. You consider bringing the entire conch back to your allies in Mezzamere.>

passages.title: Opaline Conch
passages.text:
Ah, a great find.

<Itanu takes the conch from you and flips it over. Before you can see it, he has a small knife in hand. The conch is quickly speared, the slug within removed.>

Most delightful! It would ruin it to touch fire. This... is a delicacy. It must be savored.

<Itanu closes his eyes and breathes deeply, then devours the snail in a single gulp.>

Hm, mm. Slimy, oddly rough on the insides. 

Magnificent.

passages.title: Leathery Venom Gland
passages.text:
<You pry a leathery gland from the snapdragon corpse. Drops of venom spill from an opening on one end and sizzle as they touch the ground, leaving small holes behind.

This toxin appears to be very potent. It would be best to bring it back to Newhome.>

passages.title: Leathery Venom Gland
passages.text:
Is that a venom gland in your pocket or... why is that in your pocket? You know how potent those things are, right?

Yeah, the snapdragons have been a pain in our side for a long time. The naga can easily sway them with their mind-bending tricks, or even just meat, they're not very smart creatures. A few good meals and they're as good as tamed.

I've heard of a naga commander that can handle the venom in combat. Rumor has it she even eats the stuff. 

Hope I never meet her!

passages.title: Opaline Conch
passages.text:
<The conch slumps following your assault -- the battle appears to be over.

It doesn't move. You bend over and pick it up, instinctively turning it over, wary of any attack.

It appears to be dead, but intact. You consider bringing the entire conch back to your allies in Newhome.>

passages.title: Opaline Conch
passages.text:
Oh, hey, that's a giant conch, right? Let me see that.

<Palta flips the conch over and pulls the innards out by the antennae.>

That's the stuff. Look at it! Full-slime, all scales, this one is going to be great.

I'll prepare this for the meal tonight, that should lift some spirits. Nothing like a slice of spireshell to remind you of home.

Thanks for bringing this.

<Palta nods at you.>

passages.title: Half-Digested Deepcoral Pod
passages.text:
<Upon inspection of this oddly-aggressive fathom ray, you find several halfway-digested pods.

You've seen similar pods on the coral of this region, it appears to be one of the foods of the fathom rays.

This may explain their strange ability to fly.

Finder Palta might know more.>

passages.title: Half-Digested Deepcoral Pod
passages.text:
Hey, you're back! What's that? Something you ate?

Oh, yeah, the fathom rays love these pods. They grow on the coral around the area, seem to be filled with gas.

I always thought it was just air but it appears it's lighter than air, I can fill a fishskin with what's in a pod and it floats above water!

Must help them survive in the deeps, somehow. Not sure how that works, life is a mystery, you know?

passages.title: Molted Spineshell
passages.text:
<The molted shell of a defeated spine crab, a vicious species of crab first encountered in Nazjatar.

The spines that stick out from it are quite sharp.

Finder Palta may have some use for this.>

passages.title: Molted Spineshell
passages.text:
A spine crab shell? We find them around, though I try to stay away from the dark places myself.

That's where they live, you see? The spine crabs lurk in the darkness, waiting for fish to spear. Once I saw a group of them skewer a whale shark! 

When they devour prey, they make a chittering noise -- I hate it.

The shells themselves aren't very useful -- they get brittle and shatter easily.

Watch!

<Palta flings the shell against a nearby rock, shattering it to pieces.>

Woo-ha!

passages.title: Pearlescent Shell
passages.text:
<A large, hardened shell of a vanquished hermit crab.

The shell itself was much larger than the crab, and shines in different colors when you look at it at different angles.

Surely someone back at Newhome would be interested in this beautiful shell.>

passages.title: Pearlescent Shell
passages.text:
That's a big shell! Like the sheen on it, too. Really catches the light, especially now that we can see the sun directly.

You know what I haven't made in a while? With all this fighting and barely surviving? Jewelry. I miss it! We used to find all kinds of things to wear dropped by your ships.

<Palta smashes the shell into many pieces and holds two irregular shards up to her ears.>

Well, how do I look?

<Do you answer?>

passages.title: Eel Jelly
passages.text:
<You examine the corpse of the abyssal eel, only to find it bathed in a strange slime.

The slime coats your hands and arms, and seems quite difficult to remove.

One of your deep sea allies may know more about it.>

passages.title: Eel Jelly
passages.text:
You are really covered in slime, there. Mind if I take some?

Eel jelly is incredibly useful to us. Not a whole lot of things can be used to make things slippery underwater, you know. Eel jelly is just great at it.

Here, let me show you.

<Palta rubs some jelly on your arms and legs.>

Your skin is looking better already! Slimier. Much better.

passages.title: Mottled Hydra Scale
passages.text:
<The scale of a recently-defeated hydra hatchling, it appears to be a mixture of several colors.

There appears to be a battle for dominance between the hydra of the region, one of your new allies may know more.>

passages.title: Mottled Hydra Scale
passages.text:
You'd like to know a little about the hydra of the area? Not much to tell, truth be told.

There are three matriarchs, they've been battling for dominance of the area for generations.

Sometimes, the naga throw slaves to them, for their amusement.

They don't serve anyone, just themselves. The depths aren't aligned against you, newcomer. They're just... hostile to outsiders.

passages.title: Strange Organ
passages.text:
<You find a strange organ in the corpse of the mindbender. Upon picking it up, your head begins to throb.

The octopus-like creatures have long been one of Azeroth's mysteries, this organ may shed some light on them.

Someone in Newhome may know more.>

passages.title: Strange Organ
passages.text:
Mindbender brain-organ? Great, thanks, I have a use for this.

They use this organ to attack our thoughts. Or, at least, it's a part of the process.

Here, watch.

<Palta points the organ at you and pokes it. You hear a deafening psychic scream in your mind.>

It's like they were made just to service the Old Gods and drive people insane.

Anyway, thanks. I'm going to save this for when my friend comes over to talk about her gardening.

passages.title: Overgrown Stone
passages.text:
<A stone taken from the earthy elemental you recently defeated, covered in kelp and various other underwater plants.

You have not seen many such creatures in the deeps. Perhaps there is a story to them.

One of your new undersea allies may know more.>

passages.title: Overgrown Stone
passages.text:
Hey, what's that? Really fuzzy rock you've got there.

It's from one of those earthy elementals? Oh, neat, yeah I can use that. Things grow on them like crazy, I just need to plant it in the garden and the next crop will be great.

Not sure where the elementals came from. We don't see many of them around, they're quite rare.

Anyway, thanks! Think I'm going to make my own kelp garden with this one.

passages.title: Crackling Mandible
passages.text:
<The mandible of a tidal guardian, still crackling with electricity.

One of your new allies might have a use for this.>

passages.title: Crackling Mandible
passages.text:
Yowch! You've got to warn a person before you hand them something electric! You picked this up from a tidal guardian?

The tidal guardians have guarded the naga domain for as long as I can remember. It seems like they have always been intertwined, I can't recall ever having seen one in the wild.

They're really quite beautiful when they're swimming, mesmerizing even.

Anyway, I use these things to make drinks. You mix some kelpflower wine with a bit of ground mandible, really gives it a kick!

passages.title: Frenzy Fang
passages.text:
<You remove a fully-grown fang from the fallen frenzy.

You have heard of some seafaring groups that made weapons or decorations out of fangs found in the deeps, perhaps your new allies could find a use for this?>

passages.title: Frenzy Fang
passages.text:
<Palta pokes the tip of the fang.>

Frenzy fang, huh? Those things... we don't joke about them.

<Palta looks up at the open air.>

You're lucky, they can't come here anymore.

I remember, one time, we had gone out looking for supplies. I was the only one to make it back. I can still hear the screams of the devoured. They came out of nowhere, by the hundreds. It was all clouds of red.

The deep places of the world are dangerous, friend. Avoid them if you can.

passages.title: Unprofitable Ventures
passages.text:
This land is already a monumental disaster, but it could get worse!

The Venture Company is here, and will exploit this land for every ounce of profit they can make. We must make their venture here unprofitable, so they will leave.

Destroy the three expensive security units with them, and they may leave for more profitable ventures.

passages.title: Unprofitable Ventures
passages.text: This certainly hurts their profits. Now we see if they leave!

passages.title: Envenomed Spider Fang
passages.text:
Even wary bees have been known to fall prey to these enormous spiders. They lie in wait near flowerbeds and ambush them while they collect their harvest. Thanks to you, they have one less spider to worry about.

The Hivemother will be interested in this item.

passages.title: Envenomed Spider Fang
passages.text:
<The Hivemother buzzes at you.>

Bzzzzzz!

passages.title: Hivekiller Stinger
passages.text:
Wasps are a bee's natural enemy, and none are more deadly than this highly specialized killer. It will terrorize the hive no longer, thanks to you.

The Hivemother will be interested in this item.

passages.title: Hivekiller Stinger
passages.text:
<The Hivemother buzzes animatedly at the sight of the stinger.>

Bzzzz!

passages.title: Spiral Yeti Horn
passages.text:
All manner of creatures are attracted to the sweet smell of fresh honey, but relatively few are willing to withstand the painful and often deadly stings of the largest of bees. This yeti, however, has been a persistent thorn in the hive's side, until now.

The Hivemother will be interested in this item.

passages.title: Spiral Yeti Horn
passages.text:
<The Hivemother buzzes animatedly at the sight of the horn.>

Bzzz! Bzzzz!

passages.title: Storming the Battlefields
passages.text: We cannot afford to let up on any front, continue to press the war.

passages.title: Storming the Battlefields
passages.text: If we keep up the pressure there is no way the Horde will succeed.

passages.title: Storming the Battlefields
passages.text: We cannot afford to let up on any front, continue to press the war.

passages.title: Storming the Battlefields
passages.text: If we keep up the pressure there is no way the Alliance will succeed.

passages.title: My Chickens are Not for Eating!
passages.text:
If you've spent any time with that arrogant nitwit, Overspark, you know why I'm here.

To silence his boasting and finally prove that my inventions are better!

I've released countless mechanical chickens across this island to analyze the technology here, adopt it, and evolve their own circuitry. One of them will become my ultimate battle chicken!

But those idiot troggs think my chickens are edible and keep bashing them.

Protect them, so my techno-evolutionary experiment can run its course.

passages.title: My Chickens are Not for Eating!
passages.text: Imagine being so dumb that you try to eat a mechanical chicken...

passages.title: My Chickens are Not for Eating!
passages.text:
Superlative intervention, <name>!

Now, we sit back and let the robots evolve themselves through natural selection... with no negative side effects whatsoever.

passages.title: The Mysterious Sigil
passages.text:
<The slain mogu clutches a sigil in his hand -- a symbol of the mysterious clan he belongs to.

Perhaps if you could track down his clan, they may know more about the mantid's invasion of Mogu'shan Vaults and how they can be overcome.

Lorewalker Cho is well known as font of lore for Pandaria. He may be able to track down the origins of the mogu's sigil.>

passages.title: The Mysterious Sigil
passages.text:
So Mogu'shan Vaults has been taken by the mantid? A strange turn, indeed, though hardly surprising. 

Seeking the help of the mogu to reclaim it though, that is unexpected. Last I heard, they weren't precisely on speaking terms.

passages.title: Proof of Tenacity
passages.text:
If the Highkeeper is so convinced that we don't stand a chance against our enemies, perhaps a show of force would sway him.

I am not sure how you would manage, but if you could bring proof of a victory against those who threaten the Vale, it may convince him that action should be taken.

passages.title: Proof of Tenacity
passages.text: What is it this time?

passages.title: Proof of Tenacity
passages.text:
So, you managed to defeat one of the Vale's would-be conquerors? A notable feat, but Azeroth's enemies are innumerable.

The Burning Legion, the Old Gods, the Void... sooner or later the scales will tip against this world.

...but I have been mistaken before.

passages.title: The Engine of Nalak'sha
passages.text:
Your kind have proved me wrong in the past, so I will give you a chance to do so again.

The titan structure which houses the Engine of Nalak'sha spans the entirety of Pandaria. There are more ways to reach it than just the Mogu'shan Vaults.

There are many such routes, but the closest would be through Mogu'shan Palace. The chambers beneath the palace are interconnected with the vaults. 

Seek your fate there, champion.

passages.title: The Engine of Nalak'sha
passages.text: Your courage is impressive. I only hope it is not wasted.

passages.title: The Engine of Nalak'sha
passages.text:
You have done a great thing for the Rajani today, champion.

I hope the Engine of Nalak'sha provided the power you seek.

passages.title: Real Ultimate Power
passages.text:
When I say that power is life, I'm not speaking figuratively, my dear test subject.

Properly harnessed, power can create life itself--or at least a close enough facsimile for our purposes.

There is a massive reserve of discarded technology lurking deep in the mucky depths of the Outflow. As usual, Mechagon's trash is our treasure.

I've finally perfected my device that will animate the sludge to bring that technology up to the surface for you.

All you have to do is pop 'em and grab the tech!

passages.title: Real Ultimate Power
passages.text: Please thoroughly document any adverse side effects you experience while using the Spark-7143.

passages.title: Real Ultimate Power
passages.text:
Glorious recovery!

And you say that the Spark-7143 did NOT cause an extreme burning sensation in your gut?

<Flip makes a quick note and smiles.>

Wondrous indeed!

passages.title: Dark Tides
passages.text:
A tidemistress leads some nefarious ritual above a pool.

Do not look in the pool when we approach it, or you will be rewarded with a view of our drowned allies.

We must put a stop to this ritual. The tidemistress is key.

passages.title: Dark Tides
passages.text: We must not underestimate this tidemistress.

passages.title: Dark Tides
passages.text: The ritual ceased as soon as we killed the tidemistress.

passages.title: Killclaw the Terrible
passages.text:
<You see a crude sign made by the ogres. It contains a warning.>

BIG bear! Bad!

Big bear guard big ogre treasure!

Kill after ritual! Get treasure, make more power!

passages.title: Killclaw the Terrible
passages.text: <You find a cache of treasure, just like the ogres' sign mentioned!>

passages.title: Lunar Preservation
passages.text:
My staff has served me well for many years. It has stood by my side, been through many trials... and as I grow older I find myself leaning on it more and more.

Its flowers bloom every Lunar Festival, basking in the Elune's might. They bring me so much joy, I wish for them to stay all year long. I know a way... but my bones are too old to make the trip.

Perhaps you would take the journey for me? Empower my staff in the light of the moon at the moonwells around the world. Then my flowers can stay.

passages.title: Lunar Preservation
passages.text: Flowers flourish under Elune's light. She was always known to cherish them.

passages.title: Lunar Preservation
passages.text:
You've done it! I can feel Elune's power within. Now I can enjoy the company of my flowers for the rest of my days.

Perhaps I can do the same for you. If you have flowers you wish to preserve, bring them to me. I may be able to help.

passages.title: Crown of Prosperity
passages.text:
Your crown is so colorful! Such beautiful pinks and yellows and blues... if only it could last.

Although those particular flowers cannot, I know some that can!

Similar flowers to those bloom every Lunar Festival. They hold a special connection to Elune that I can empower, thanks to you. Retrieve them for me, and we can fashion a crown that you can enjoy year round!

passages.title: Crown of Prosperity
passages.text: Elune has a soft spot for flowers. Those that bloom during Lunar Festival are quite special.

passages.title: Crown of Prosperity
passages.text:
Such a multitude of colors! These flowers will bring happiness to all who see them.

This crown shall bring you great prosperity.

passages.title: Crown of Good Fortune
passages.text:
Those flowers remind me of Elune herself! I wear similar ones year round, to remind me of her watchful grace.

Perhaps you would like to as well?

Your crown is made of ordinary blossoms that will one day wilt and die. It is an unfortunate fate for such delicate beauties, but my crown is made of similar flowers that I made to last year round! If you bring me specific flowers that bloom only during Lunar Festival, I can bless them so that you too can enjoy your crown all year long.

passages.title: Crown of Good Fortune
passages.text: Between you and me, I believe these flowers are Elune's favorite. They mirror her lunar radiance so splendidly!

passages.title: Crown of Good Fortune
passages.text:
Ah, flowers that match my own. I can feel Elune's presence within them.

This crown shall bring you great fortune in life.

passages.title: Rebels on the Road
passages.text:
This is unacceptable. The stoneborn rebels have ambushed a convoy intended for the Tithelord. He is the local Harvester who rules this ward. 

We need to get through this mess. The bridge on the far side of this conflict leads to Darkhaven. The Master typically keeps some of his own Stone Legion forces there. 

Carve us a way through, Maw Walker. Destroy any who would delay us. We must not keep Sire Denathrius waiting.

passages.title: Rebels on the Road
passages.text: Your talents in combat show promise. Perhaps with a few more centuries and a little humility we might make something of you.

passages.title: A Worthy Ally
passages.text:
Some of our bravest ankoan have volunteered to join you on your expedition.

You will find each have their own special interests and they will mark your map with different opportunities every day.

Use the Deepflame Campfire when you are ready. Choose a noble ally to join you, and explore what remains of Nazjatar.

Choose wisely! You may only select one friend per day.

passages.title: A Worthy Ally
passages.text:
My brethren reported that you were quite skilled in the field, <name>.

We are honored to have you here.

passages.title: Assault: The Warring Clans
passages.text:
The opportunistic mogu clans seek to take the Vale while its defenders are recovering from N'Zoth's attack. 

They are both cowardly and foolish.

Show them the error of their ways.

passages.title: Assault: The Warring Clans
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Assault: The Warring Clans
passages.text:
These pretenders will learn that they must either join the Rajani or be ground to dust.

You have done well to show them that.

passages.title: Harnessing the Power
passages.text:
Heart Forge online.

Initiate final attunement sequence.

Awaiting input from champion unit <name>.

passages.title: Harnessing the Power
passages.text: Standing by.

passages.title: Harnessing the Power
passages.text:
Well, well! Looks like the Heart o' Azeroth has got new capabilities, just like MOTHER said!

Be on the lookout fer more o' those essences. They've got tae be all over Azeroth.

passages.title: A Once Sweet Sound
passages.text:
The bells! That sound!

Their song has been twisted! If their dire toll continues, we will all succumb.

<Eridia presses her hammer into your hands.>

Find the great vespers within the temple and strike them with my hammer. May the mallet's tonal purity restore their true voices!

I will listen for their clarion call and meet you near the bridge. Go swiftly!

passages.title: A Once Sweet Sound
passages.text: Such a bitter sound!

passages.title: A Once Sweet Sound
passages.text: I can hear their song once more. It is a boon on my mind, but the loudest voice remains. We must silence it before it destroys all that we hold dear.

passages.title: Mogu at the Gates
passages.text:
The time has come. The other mogu clans have set their sights on the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.

They will not conquer it.

Some of your kind have already gone to the gate to scout out the size of their force. If you think yourself worthy for such a mission, meet them there.

passages.title: Mogu at the Gates
passages.text:
The mogu have not massed in numbers like this since... well I cannot remember!

We must be careful. They have overtaken the entire plains.

passages.title: Return to Mistfall
passages.text:
We have done all we can here. We know how much the mogu are a clear threat.

The forge is in great danger of falling into their hands if we lose our hold on the Vale.

Let us return to Mistfall and report to the Rajani. They will want to know what we are up against.

passages.title: Return to Mistfall
passages.text:
So the other clans seek to invade the Vale with their armies?

We will show them what true might looks like.

passages.title: A Fitting Reward
passages.text:
Although the X-52 Personnel Armor's power-core was destroyed during the battle with Gallywix, the invention was a success!

I doubt anyone will be interested in purchasing the rights to the X-52 without a working power-core, so why don't you hang onto the armor instead? It is quite stylish after all!

Now that Crapopolis is saved and Gallywix is conveniently trapped inside of his own mechanical pummeler, I think I'm going to renegotiate that "contract" of his.

He is a "captive audience" after all!

passages.title: Legacy of the Mad Mage
passages.text:
<This rather large jewel has an inscription etched on its base:

Property of Mardivas. If found please return to my laboratory. 

Perhaps this laboratory can still be found somewhere?>

passages.title: Legacy of the Mad Mage
passages.text: <The chest appears to be simply constructed, but the locking mechanism hums with arcane energy.>

passages.title: Legacy of the Mad Mage
passages.text: <The ancient lock clicks open, revealing the contents within.>

passages.title: This Ain't Mine
passages.text:
Sylvanas's loyalists have collapsed part of the canyon path to Orgrimmar. Our forces are now cut off from each other.

We need to reinforce our front line or the Banshee will pick us off at her leisure. We have come too far to be slain by a thousand cuts.

Gazlowe and one of the Alliance's gnomes believe they have an answer. You'd best ensure that their plan does not backfire.

passages.title: This Ain't Mine
passages.text: Hmm. Maybe that goblin's gadgets have some use.

passages.title: This Ain't Mine
passages.text: Swift action saved our soldiers' lives, but there is still more to do.

passages.title: Fallen to Their Vices
passages.text:
Lysonia's forces ransack our sacred temple... they are long gone from the Archon's embrace.

It pains me to say, but you must defeat them so they can no longer abuse our people.

Take Compassion with you. You will find it more than helpful, now that its power has returned.

passages.title: Fallen to Their Vices
passages.text: Fighting the Forsworn, our brothers and sisters... it never gets easier.

passages.title: Her Will, Inflicted
passages.text:
I feel myself drawn across the double bridges to the west...

Lysonia must be there.

Come, <name>. We must confront her before she can escape again. Who knows what she plans.

passages.title: Her Will, Inflicted
passages.text: It seems that... I am the fool.

passages.title: The Penitent Hunt
passages.text:
You will descend upon these poor souls. Remember, you are helping them and Revendreth through the terror you bring. When a soul is filled with fear, their resistances to our methods falter.

The Master has requested that you hunt the Accuser yourself. But we must prey upon some of the others first.

I will be able to guide you through your first hunt.

passages.title: The Penitent Hunt
passages.text: The souls must be hunted.

passages.title: The Penitent Hunt
passages.text:
Well done. The fear we struck allowed us to extract ample anima for Revendreth.

Onto our final target.

passages.title: Breaking the Hopebreakers
passages.text:
The Fearstalker has surely sent her hunters across the entirety of the Banewood in search of us, <name>. 

Draven informed me that some of her top hunters are scouring Dredhollow as we speak. We can use this to our advantage. Slaying them should get her attention.

<The Accuser hands you a collection of bright red vials.>

Throw these on her hunters. It should draw the attention of the devourers infesting this place.

passages.title: Breaking the Hopebreakers
passages.text:
Sounds like it worked better than expected. 

Perfect. The Fearstalker stands no chance.

passages.title: Power Protocol Initiation
passages.text:
We've come a long way, <name>.

Once the power from the auxiliary systems are brought online MOTHER will be able tae run diagnostics.

All that's left is settin' the final pieces in place.

passages.title: Power Protocol Initiation
passages.text: Quite the journey so far.

passages.title: Power Protocol Initiation
passages.text: Best get tae it 'fore things get out of hand.

passages.title: The First Cleansing
passages.text:
This situation may feel familiar, <name>.

When you found Pelagos, he was undergoing a similar rite. As you saw, it can end in violence.

This will be the first time you are asked to draw out the burdens that held you to a mortal life. It may be a painful process. It is for many.

For you, this is the path you must walk to attain your goals. To earn the right to stand among us, to be heard. So we may carry your message to the Archon herself.

Center yourself. When you are prepared, we will begin.

passages.title: The First Cleansing
passages.text:
This is a moment worthy of celebration, <name>.

You have done it. They have come.

passages.title: The Hand of Doubt
passages.text:
Quickly! We have no time to lose. Lysonia has weakened Eridia to the point that she may fall. Our Paragon will do what she can, but we must intervene.

We will challenge Lysonia, and perhaps buy Eridia more time. 

This so-called Hand of Doubt will make no easy foe. Stand ready, <name>.

passages.title: The Hand of Doubt
passages.text:
That you should join us now, on the precipice of this treachery, is curious.

<The Paragon of Purity studies you with a piercing gaze.>

You have done well. The Archon will know of your contributions this day.

passages.title: Quartermaster's Bounty
passages.text: Victory at any cost.

passages.title: Maintaining Focus
passages.text:
At present, the focus holds but a fraction of N'Zoth's true power. If we further empower it, we could craft even more effective weapons to wield against him.

N'Zoth's influence is everywhere, <name>, and is most concentrated within powerful foes. Vanquish them and claim whatever vestiges of the Old God's power remain.

passages.title: Maintaining Focus
passages.text: We are embarking upon a dangerous gambit, <name>. Caution is of the utmost importance.

passages.title: Maintaining Focus
passages.text:
Excellent. These should provide just what we need.

I will draw out the corruption from these physical vessels and infuse it into the focus. Then you will be able to use it to create more powerful items.

passages.title: Beginning the Descent
passages.text:
Protecting one's mind against the old gods requires an object of pure corruption. Unbeknownst to many, one such object exists--dormant beneath the molten pits of Blackwing Descent.

Until recently, one of my agents stood watch over the area, keeping detailed records of suspicious activities. Unfortunately, this agent has gone silent. It is now clear we are not the only ones with this knowledge.

If we are to find answers, there is one place to look.

Our journey continues, <name>. Blackrock awaits.

passages.title: Beginning the Descent
passages.text: Have you recovered what we discussed?

passages.title: Beginning the Descent
passages.text:
The scales of corruption now serve as protection for those who stand against it.

How fitting.

Now, let's see what a <class> of your caliber is capable of when dressed for the occasion.

passages.title: Soldier of Time
passages.text:
Long ago, the land of Alterac Valley was peaceful. However, when the Frostwolves moved in it became highly contested real estate between them and the Stormpikes. Battles used to rage for days. 

Well, actually the battle is still ongoing, the bronze dragons have figured out a way for you to revisit those early days.

passages.title: Soldier of Time
passages.text: Did you have fun exploring Alterac Valley as it used to be?

passages.title: Soldier of Time
passages.text: The battles for Alterac were bloody affairs, I'm glad they're done. Oh wait, the battles are still ongoing! The cycle of strife is never ending.

passages.title: Callous Concoctions
passages.text:
I witnessed your success with the Pool of Potions and I think you could be of help. Within this larger pool, we create more dangerous mixtures!

There are three different oozing ingredients we mix together in different combinations to create violent creatures. When enough ingredients have been added to the pool, the mixture takes shape and a creature will emerge!

Bring any combination of these ingredients, Mephitic Goo, Viscous Oil, or Miscible Ooze to the Pool of Mixed Monstrosities.

passages.title: Callous Concoctions
passages.text: Have you completed the mixture?

passages.title: Callous Concoctions
passages.text: You may continue to add as many ingredients as you wish. The more we add, the more we create!

passages.title: Alterac Valley Graveyards
passages.text:
The graveyards in Alterac Valley are prized territories. Both the Horde and the Alliance fight savagely for these sacred grounds. Are you, <name>, ready to join that fight?

I want you to assault an enemy graveyard. Find a graveyard with a Horde banner in its midst, and pull it from the ground! Do that, and your task will be complete....

But if you can also hold the graveyard for a few minutes, then our troops will soon come to relieve you.

passages.title: Alterac Valley Graveyards
passages.text:
Well done!  Graveyards are vital to our control of Alterac Valley.  When you capture one, you help ensure the Alliance's sovereignty here.

Go now, <name>.  Reenter the battle, and if you see a graveyard under the Horde's control... you know what to do!

passages.title: The Quartermaster
passages.text:
<name>, our quartermaster charged me to direct new recruits to him. He needs supplies from caches stored in the mines of Alterac, and he'll probably send you to get them.

Follow the road. You'll find our quartermaster to the west.

passages.title: The Quartermaster
passages.text:
It's good to see fresh troops here, <name>, but with a little luck you'll get into some action and won't be fresh for long!

Speak with me again.  I have tasks I must discuss with you....

passages.title: Capture a Mine
passages.text:
The mines in Alterac Valley hold more than just minerals. Both the Frostwolf and Stormpike have cached excess supplies in the Irondeep and Coldtooth mines... that's not a bad idea, if we could only maintain control of them!

Capture a mine, then return to me. To capture a mine, enter one that we do not control and kill its leader. When you do that, the mine will be ours, and we'll send troops to protect it!

passages.title: Capture a Mine
passages.text:
You did it!  Well done, <name>!

When we control a mine and have troops stationed there, it's much easier to gather minerals and supplies from it.

passages.title: Armor Scraps
passages.text:
Battles rage constantly in Alterac Valley, and the supplies we get from Ironforge are not enough to outfit our experienced troops.

If you find armor scraps from the battlefield, aid the war effort and bring those scraps to me!

passages.title: Armor Scraps
passages.text: Did you bring any armor scraps, <name>?

passages.title: Armor Scraps
passages.text:
These are some good pieces, <name>.  I can use them to fashion new equipment for our troops.

If my supply level gets high enough, then maybe our seasoned fighting units will enter the field!

passages.title: Towers and Bunkers
passages.text:
Towers and bunkers are key defensive positions, and so we must hold as many as possible! I want you to attack a tower or a bunker in Alterac Valley.

To do that, enter a tower with a Horde banner atop it. You will see another enemy banner inside. Pull out that banner, and a white Alliance banner will appear in its place. Well done!

At that point your mission for me will be complete, but hold the area long enough, and if the Horde doesn't take it back, then it will be destroyed!

passages.title: Towers and Bunkers
passages.text: I received a field report stating you helped secure an enemy banner.  Well done, <name>!  With their ranged troops out of position we can move the line of battle forward!

passages.title: The Battle of Alterac
passages.text:
The Explorers' League believes there are artifacts in Alterac Valley, but the Frostwolf orcs won't let us explore. We can't allow the Horde to stop our scholarly pursuits! Defeat the Frostwolf general, Drek'Thar. With him dead, the orcs will lose their edge.

Drek'Thar is in Frostwolf Keep, in the south of Alterac Valley. Vanquish him, and then return to me.

passages.title: The Graveyards of Alterac
passages.text:
The battle lines of Alterac Valley are ever shifting. Territories swing back and forth as we meet our opponents in deadly combat. And graveyards, <name>, are where battles rage most fierce.

I want you to attack an Alliance held graveyard! Find a graveyard with an Alliance banner in its midst and pull it from the ground.

Do that and your task for me will be complete, but... if you hold the graveyard for a few minutes, then it will be ours and troops will come and relieve you.

passages.title: The Graveyards of Alterac
passages.text: Well done, <name>!  With each graveyard under our control, the spirits of our enemies will wander more lost and aimless.

passages.title: Speak with our Quartermaster
passages.text:
<name>, the Frostwolf Quartermaster is looking for recruits, for tasks that lead into the mines of Alterac Valley. Speak with him; he will tell you more.

Follow the road west into the bunker, then take the west exit and you'll find our quartermaster.

passages.title: Speak with our Quartermaster
passages.text: Hail, <name>!  It is good to see a <class> like yourself, eager to do his part for the Horde.  Speak with me again, for I have vital tasks for you...

passages.title: Capture a Mine
passages.text:
As battle rages over the landscape of Alterac Valley, so too does it rage through the Coldtooth and Irondeep mines. Both are rich sources of minerals and both are used to store supplies; it's no wonder they are so highly valued!

Help our war effort, <name>! Capture one of the mines for the Horde! To capture a mine, enter one that we do not control and kill its leader. When that is done, the mine will be ours and we'll send troops to protect it!

passages.title: Capture a Mine
passages.text: You haven't yet captured a mine, <name>!  Find one that we do not control and defeat it's leader!

passages.title: Capture a Mine
passages.text:
You captured a mine!  With our own warriors protecting it, it will be much simpler to extract minerals from its depths, or gather supplies that have been cached there.

Well done, <name>.  The deed you have done is a great boon to our battle efforts.

passages.title: Towers and Bunkers
passages.text:
Towers and bunkers are important positions, and we must capture and hold them all! So to that end, I want you to attack a bunker that is controlled by the enemy.

To do that, enter one with an Alliance banner. You will see another banner inside. Pull out that banner, and a white Horde banner will appear in its place. Well done!

At that point your task for me will be complete, but if you hold the place long enough, and if the Alliance doesn't take it back, then it will be destroyed!

passages.title: Towers and Bunkers
passages.text:
I heard of your mission's success!  That pleases me...

Our troops can now charge forward with impunity, and show the Alliance that Alterac Valley is no place for them!

passages.title: Enemy Booty
passages.text: When you fight the enemy, gather the scraps of their armor and bring them to me. I'll use those scraps to make armor for our own troops!

passages.title: Enemy Booty
passages.text: How goes the hunting, <name>.  Do you have any armor scraps for me?

passages.title: Enemy Booty
passages.text:
These will do nicely.  I'll melt them down and patch them up and you'll never know they came from those Stormpike cowards!

Thanks, <name>.  And let me polish up that armor of yours...

passages.title: The Battle for Alterac
passages.text:
The Stormpike dwarves and their allies have invaded Alterac Valley, and we must drive them out! To win the battle for Alterac, we must defeat their general, Vanndar Stormpike!

You will find Vanndar in Dun Baldar, in the north of Alterac Valley.

Destroy him, <name>, and then return to me.

passages.title: Prototypes for Profit
passages.text:
<Gazlowe pulls you in close and whispers.>

Lookit here, <name>. I gotta keep my nose clean here in front of the prince.

But I trust you know what's gotta be done outside of town, yeah?

Outside of town... where all the tech is...

Tech that Alliance grubs are tryin' to get their clumsy mitts on...
which we could use for the Horde...
to build big weapons...
and scary robots...
and other lucrative products...?

I don't gotta spell this out for you, right?

passages.title: Prototypes for Profit
