We need a great deal of anima. The masked fae must be keeping a stockpile somewhere within the grove--we just need to find it.

They likely used soulwebs to collect and move the anima. If I examine them, I should be able to pick up the trail.

passages.title: Read the Roots
passages.text: I sometimes mourn what was lost. And then I remember what work there is still left to do.

passages.title: Read the Roots
passages.text:
The Drust have stolen more anima than I expected. To think that they have deprived us of this much in the midst of a drought...

We must take back whatever we can. Not only for the sake of the wildseed, but to also thwart whatever the Drust intend to do.

passages.title: Rituals of Blood
passages.text:
Anji and I have fought in many battles, so we know how to handle a few mogu, but the blood magic used by these Dokani is just unsettling!

As if it weren't bad enough for them to kill everyone in their path, but to use their corpses to fuel their unholy rituals? I just can't stomach it!

Do me a favor. If you ever come across any of these rituals, put a stop to them! Even our enemies don't deserve to be defiled with their dark magic.

passages.title: Rituals of Blood
passages.text: I hope you were able to do something about those rituals.

passages.title: Rituals of Blood
passages.text:
It is a relief to know that you've put an end to those rituals.

Just thinking about them turns my stomach.

passages.title: Built to Fall
passages.text:
The Baruk use the forbidden arts of necromancy to trap souls of fallen mogu into the statues that fight for them. 

These tactics are a disgrace to our people, and cannot be allowed to continue.

Break their precious statues, and give them no vessels with which to contaminate with their stolen spirits.

passages.title: Built to Fall
passages.text:
As their statues crumble, so too shall their clan.

You have performed adequately.

passages.title: Plunder the Plunderers
passages.text:
Our raids on Lei Shen's treasuries did much to ensure the Thunder King's downfall. I think we should employ the same strategy here.

Seek out the hoarded plunder of the mogu clans and relieve them of it. 

We must do all we can to disrupt their advance.

passages.title: Plunder the Plunderers
passages.text:
Well done. We should continue to keep these supplies out of our enemies hands.

Even the smallest measures taken to disrupt our enemy can turn the tide of battle.

passages.title: Network Diagnostics
passages.text:
Unfortunately, we've got no clue where N'Zoth has been lurking since his escape. We do, however have an idea where he might strike.

Back when the keepers were imprisoning the Old Gods, they built defense mechanisms against their corruption into the titan forges. If N'Zoth wants tae corrupt Azeroth, he'll have tae go through them first.

Fortunately, we've got ourselves hooked up tae them now, so we can monitor them from here. Go ahead an' take a look.

passages.title: Network Diagnostics
passages.text: The consoles should tell ye how the forges are holdin' up.

passages.title: Network Diagnostics
passages.text:
I was hopin' we'd have more time tae prepare.

Looks like now's the time tae act.

passages.title: Eyes of the Master
passages.text:
I worry about entering the city. I'm sure you have noticed how well we... stand out here.

Denathrius's loyalists have eyes everywhere, and no more dedicated soldiers than the stoneborn.

Their eyes and ears watch over the Chalice District. Take out their leaders so none can report our presence here before we acquire the seal.

passages.title: Eyes of the Master
passages.text: The stoneborn forces can never be truly defeated, but they can be quelled for a time.

passages.title: Eyes of the Master
passages.text:
This city makes my skin crawl. I feel like I am constantly being watched, that people are whispering behind my back.

Taking out the stoneborn leaders should slow the flow of information back to Denathrius's loyalists.

passages.title: Gothic Fashion
passages.text:
Making my way into the city unseen was not as simple as I thought.

I trekked through some mud, where I came across these... small men.

Perhaps Kleia is right. I draw far too much attention here to be of much use. 

Perhaps I can disguise myself? Please, help me by gathering some venthyr clothing as a disguise.

passages.title: Gothic Fashion
passages.text:
<Pelagos sifts through the clothing you brought him.>

Such fine fabric... I believe this could work!

passages.title: Through Glass
passages.text:
The mirror frame rests at the bottom of Redelav Hall. Kleia and Pelagos wait there.

With these shards, I can piece it together.

We will go through, grab the sinstone, and go face the Countess. Let nothing stand in our way.

passages.title: Through Glass
passages.text:
Venthyr carry their pasts as a burden, a weight upon them.

The kyrian stand free of ours.

passages.title: Through Glass
passages.text:
So much power in one stone.

Your past can be used against you. This is why we free ourselves.

passages.title: The Seal of Contrition
passages.text:
Preparations for the Seal are complete.

Go, insert it into the Crest. Be delicate, yet firm! Move with purpose, but a steady hand.

passages.title: The Seal of Contrition
passages.text: <The orb hangs in front of you. The Seal in your hand pulses quickly.>

passages.title: The Seal of Contrition
passages.text:
<You see the Seal of Contrition flash with power as you pull your hand away from it.

One singular item, connecting the denizens of Bastion and Revendreth in more ways than the obvious.>

passages.title: Right our Wrongs
passages.text:
General Kaal was sent here on a mission for Denathrius long ago.

On that mission, they concealed anima siphons, making their presence impossible to detect, to limit the amount of anima this workshop could use. That destabilized this area. The Forsworn must have noticed this and exploited the weakness.

These previous actions are in opposition to our goal. Take Theotar and destroy those siphons.

passages.title: Right our Wrongs
passages.text:
The job is done. 

This should allow the anima to return. 

Your dedication to our cause is great. I cannot think of one more fitting to wear this cloak.

passages.title: Visions of the Dreamer: Origins
passages.text:
The spirit within the wildseed dreams of her birth and youth, in the primordial days of her world.

Go to the first Dreamshrine outside of Hibernal Hollow. Meditate at the shrine, and soothe this vision of how her life began.

passages.title: Visions of the Dreamer: Origins
passages.text: We all start somewhere. Sometimes in unexpected places. Me, I just popped out of the ground like a flower.

passages.title: End of the Dream
passages.text:
The time has come. The ritual will be complete when you have fully entered into the spirit's dreams.

It will be as if you are her, in every aspect.

She relives the moment of her death over and over again. It torments her. Something about how she ended... she had no control over her actions. She hurt the ones she loved.

Speak to me when you are ready to immerse yourself in her nightmare of the end.

passages.title: End of the Dream
passages.text: Have you entered into the spirit's final dream and witnessed her fate?

passages.title: End of the Dream
passages.text:
What a terrible end for such a majestic spirit... 

But that was why she connected with you! Because you are of the same world! Azeroth!

Now, I can finally feel her nightmares wane. At last, she knows some peace.

Thank you, my friend.

passages.title: Pillars of Oblivion
passages.text:
In ages past, the black obelisks of the Old Gods would herald the coming of their forces. The dark conjurers among the k'thir and n'raqi would utilize these monuments to establish footholds in our world and usher in more of the Old Gods' minions.

Today, we see these very same obelisks littering the battlefields. So long as they stand, N'Zoth's forces will be without end.

Make sure they do not.

passages.title: Pillars of Oblivion
passages.text: Is your task complete?

passages.title: Pillars of Oblivion
passages.text:
You've destroyed the obelisks? Good, the Old Gods must be given no ground.

Remember this in your battles.

passages.title: Read Between the Lines
passages.text:
Ah, mortal, how fortunate that I, humble Ta'eran, happen to be standing here just as you, the outsider everyone is talking about, happens to wander by!

In the spirit of cooperation and mutual interests, there is a matter I wish to discuss.

A nearby structure called the Sepulcher of Knowledge was built as a repository for military strategy. I fear the knowledge contained within may soon be lost.

If you would do me the honor of escorting me to the Sepulcher, I can share what else I know.

passages.title: Read Between the Lines
passages.text: Mortal, are you ready to help me save these valuable writings?

passages.title: Repeat After Me
passages.text:
The Primus placed guardians in the area around the Sepulcher to protect the knowledge within. Each embodied the virtues of one of the five houses.

To gain entrance, you must prove yourself worthy by besting these protectors. 

Seek out the rune stones that represent the houses of Maldraxxus. Pay attention to the words inscribed on each stone, then pay deference each house's values.

If you honor the stone, its protector will come forth. Defeat each of them.

passages.title: Repeat After Me
passages.text: The Primus was clever indeed.

passages.title: Repeat After Me
passages.text: Now that those guardians are dispatched, we can focus on unlocking the door.

passages.title: Pauldrons of Imperium
passages.text:
Now we know who is responsible for the unrest in Maldraxxus.

If Kel'Thuzad has allied with the Banished One, then he wields greater power than anyone realizes. 

We must lay siege to the House of Rituals, but we need time to prepare. Attacking without a flawless strategy will only ensure our defeat.

For now, return the pauldrons to the Seat of the Primus. I will meet you there.

passages.title: Pauldrons of Imperium
passages.text: The battle has only just begun.

passages.title: Ny'alotha, the Waking City: The Corruptor's End
passages.text:
Usin' the mogu's research, MOTHER and Ra-den found a way tae focus the forge's Origination Protocol through the Chamber of Heart. The only problem was findin' out where tae shoot it.

That is, until now.

Take these anchors and head through that portal. Ye'll need tae find some prominent landmarks tae place 'em so we can focus the weapon. Once they're set, we'll be ready tae fire.

Ye'll only get one shot. Make it count!

passages.title: Ny'alotha, the Waking City: The Corruptor's End
passages.text: It's time tae blast N'Zoth back tae the void he came from!

passages.title: Ny'alotha, the Waking City: The Corruptor's End
passages.text:
Ye did it! N'Zoth's forces are scattered and his grip on our world is fading!

Ye truly are the champion of Azeroth!

passages.title: Opening the Gateway
passages.text:
The fabric of reality is torn. But there's no need for me to tell you that, <name>. You've seen it firsthand. 

It's only a matter of time before these realities become one, veiled in eternal darkness. Instead of hiding, perhaps it's time we embraced the darkness.

With the help of our titan friend here we may be able to thread the needle of this reality through the fabric of another, creating a bridge of sorts.

After all, the key to understanding an enemy's weakness is to understand their intentions.

passages.title: Opening the Gateway
passages.text: Uncertainty comes before discovery.

passages.title: Opening the Gateway
passages.text: The time has come for us to confront the darkest of these manifestations.

passages.title: A Deeper Dive
passages.text:
Something just isn't adding up about these Amathet. Why would protectors of titan works attack and damage the Forge of Origination?

I think we need tae take a closer look. I think I saw a monument on the terrace over there. Perhaps the writings there could tell us more about these tol'vir.

passages.title: A Deeper Dive
passages.text: I'm ready when ye are, <class>.

passages.title: A Deeper Dive
passages.text:
This monument was a good start, but it still doesn't explain what we're looking for.

Fortunately, uncovering mysteries is what the Explorer's League does best!

passages.title: A Crack in the Armor
passages.text:
The artifacts you helped excavate show the Amathet as a tribe who prided themselves on protecting the works of the titans. 

This confirms our assumptions, and indicates that something drastic must have happened to them to cause them to damage the very works they swore to protect.

We should continue to track down their writings. I think I saw a more recent monument outside the Halls of Origination.

passages.title: A Crack in the Armor
passages.text: I cannae wait tae solve this mystery!

passages.title: A Crack in the Armor
passages.text:
Someone, or something, has been manipulating the Amathet from within. 

Sounds familiar, don't you think?

passages.title: Shared Goals
passages.text:
The decree you found made mention of a plan to defeat the Old Gods. 

I know that the Amathet aren't likely to work with us toward that goal, but if they have a plan tae take out N'Zoth, it's worthwhile for us tae look at it.

The decree mentions the Engine of Ascension. I think that might be what they call that solar empowering device we saw earlier. We should take a peek underneath and see if we can figure out what they're planning!

passages.title: Shared Goals
passages.text: Let's see what we can find in the Chamber of the Stars.

passages.title: Shared Goals
passages.text:
These Amathet are off their rockers! 

They've decided that Azeroth is too far gone for saving!

passages.title: The Garden of Night
passages.text:
That should take care of things out here. Now we must tend to the inner garden. Once we're done, I'll sort out my recalcitrant husband.

Hopefully, any remaining spriggans will have cleared out on their own after hearing us dispatch the others.

passages.title: The Garden of Night
passages.text: This is my fault... just like before...

passages.title: The Garden of Night
passages.text:
I should have never left! He's told me time and again that I should face my...

Never mind. I can deal with that later.

The situation would have been much more dire if the two of you were not here.

passages.title: Sinkeeper
passages.text:
This is a Bell of Remembrance. Before the recent... "events" we used them to beckon souls from the Crypt of the Forgotten to deem their fate. 

If they are less arrogant than they were before, they may continue in the process. If not, they must spend additional time in the crypt.

Let's put this one to use, shall we? It's pretty beat up, let's hope we can get at least one use out of it.

passages.title: Sinkeeper
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. You have helped that soul, even if it does not feel like it.

passages.title: Thick Skin
passages.text:
The Primus forged a fine blade, but it will do you no good in its current state.

Fortunately for you, I possess the skill to finish his work!

That being said, I will require materials. The other Chosen have been too preoccupied with their combat drills to assist me at the forge, even as they demand more weapons and armor.

That's where you come in. You want a new blade? You'll have to earn it.

passages.title: Thick Skin
passages.text: Can't be that difficult, can it?

passages.title: Thick Skin
passages.text: You work quickly, don't you? I could use more assistants like you.

passages.title: Subjugated Serpents
passages.text:
Where the Zan-Tien march, the warserpents are sure to follow.

I cannot stress to you enough how dangerous these beasts are. It is a shame to see them subjugated by the mogu, but we cannot afford to let them run rampant.

I need you to put them down before they can wreak havoc on our lines.

passages.title: Subjugated Serpents
passages.text: Have you taken care of the serpents?

passages.title: Subjugated Serpents
passages.text:
It is unfortunate to see the cloud serpents cut down, but the Zan-Tien have driven them beyond recovery.

Don't worry, we'll make them pay.

passages.title: Cutting Stone
passages.text:
One problem with waging war against other mogu is that weapons dull and break very quickly when used against foes of stone and metal. 

Being the sole blacksmith among the Rajani, it is sometimes difficult to keep up with our warriors needs.

If you come across any weapons in your battles with the mogu, I'm sure I could put them to good use.

passages.title: Cutting Stone
passages.text: What have you found?

passages.title: Cutting Stone
passages.text:
These weapons look to be in good enough shape.

They will serve our warriors well.

passages.title: Champions of the Swarm
passages.text:
It is clear that Shek'zara is fully committed to this invasion. Our scouts have spotted some of her greatest champions among the battlefield.

Any one of these mantid could prove too much for the soldiers of the Golden Lotus to overcome. We must hunt them down and eliminate them ourselves.

Are you in?

passages.title: Champions of the Swarm
passages.text:
Impressive kill count. You almost kept up with me.

Maybe next time, though.

passages.title: Stashed Supplies
passages.text:
The invading mantid have been making off with the Golden Lotus' supplies lately. They're probably hoping they can starve us out.

Well, they may be right if we can't get some of our supplies back. 

While you're taking the fight to the swarm, keep an eye out for anywhere they might have stashed our supplies. You'd be doing the Golden Lotus a big favor if you could recover some.

passages.title: Stashed Supplies
passages.text: Did you manage to find our supplies?

passages.title: Stashed Supplies
passages.text:
You've found them! What luck!

These supplies will help us hold out against the mantid, maybe even long enough to drive them back! 

The Golden Lotus owes you one!

passages.title: Dread Menders
passages.text:
The ambercasters are among the highest castes of mantid society. Through their magic, they can mend and form amber to their will, allowing hastened recovery of the mantid's forces after a battle.

They are strategic targets, and we should seek them out. 

Care to join us?

passages.title: Dread Menders
passages.text:
With no one to mend their wounded soldiers, it's only a matter of time before the swarm is driven back to the wastes.

You did well.

passages.title: Testing the Untested
passages.text:
During a swarm, the mantid send their youngest in great numbers against the enemy to test their mettle. Those who survive join the swarm as true warriors of the mantid.

We should do our best to ensure that they don't make it through this test.

passages.title: Testing the Untested
passages.text:
The mantid are foolish to send such untested creatures against a well-prepared foe.

May this be a lesson they never learn.

passages.title: Rampaging Destroyers
passages.text:
The last mantid swarm is still very fresh in the memory of the Golden Lotus. Prior to the advancement of the swarm, the mantid would send their massive kunchong to soften up the defenders' lines.

It would seem their tactics have not changed.

We must stop those kunchong if the Golden Lotus hope to mount a defensive against the swarm. I'm counting on you to strike them down.

passages.title: Rampaging Destroyers
passages.text: Have the beasts been halted?

passages.title: Rampaging Destroyers
passages.text:
The kunchong are dangerous beasts. You are a brave <class> for taking them on.

The Golden Lotus thanks you.

passages.title: The Empress' Guard
passages.text:
The Zara'thik are the empress' elite guard. Empowered with plundered Azerite, they will stop at nothing short of absolute conquest of all of Pandaria.

If we allow them to advance past the Serpent's spine, the Golden Lotus will be no match for them.

Stop them at the wall, <class>.

passages.title: The Empress' Guard
passages.text: We must break the Zara'thik advance!

passages.title: The Empress' Guard
passages.text:
You seem to have halted their advance. That will have to do for now.

I'll alert you if the situation worsens.

passages.title: Blades of Amber
passages.text:
The mantid are frail and easily broken, but the amber blades they wield are formidable.

With a bit of work, they could be reshaped into something suitable for the mogu.

Bring them to me, and I can see about repurposing them to service the Rajani.

passages.title: Blades of Amber
passages.text: Have you brought me some blades?

passages.title: Blades of Amber
passages.text:
It surprises me how such a sharp and durable blade could be made from something as fragile as a tree.

Perhaps we have something to learn from the mantid, after all.

passages.title: Crushed Underfoot
passages.text:
In the past, the mantid would safeguard their hatchlings in incubation chambers until they were ready to be tested in the swarm. 

These Vil'thik are sloppy, however, allowing their larvae to scurry out in the open. 

Wouldn't it be a shame if someone crushed them?

No, of course it wouldn't.

passages.title: Crushed Underfoot
passages.text:
Ah to see the future of your enemy crushed underfoot.

It is a good feeling, is it not?

passages.title: Taken by the Swarm
passages.text:
There's something different about this mantid swarm. Instead of just killing everything in sight like the mantid usually do, they've taken to capturing our defenders and holding them alive.

I really don't want to know what they have in store for the captives. 

Why don't you go rescue them so we don't have to find out?

passages.title: Taken by the Swarm
passages.text:
You've freed them? Oh, thank goodness!

I cannot fathom what a mantid would want to do with live prisoners, but it cannot be good!

passages.title: Halting Production
passages.text:
The mantid use amber in nearly all aspects of their lives, from the structures they live in to the weapons they wield. Of course, I'm more interested in the latter.

If we can deprive the mantid of their materials, we will deprive them of their means to create implements of war.

Find where they keep their amber and make sure they are unable to use it.

passages.title: Halting Production
passages.text:
Without their precious amber, the mantid will be unable to resupply.

Well done, <class>.

passages.title: Standards of the Swarm
passages.text:
The brazen mantid think they've already won. Even now, they fly banners along the Serpent's Spine, announcing their dominance.

They must learn that Pandaria belongs to the pandaren.

Burn their banners down.

passages.title: Standards of the Swarm
passages.text:
Their marks have been erased from the Vale. Soon, so will their forces.

I hope to fight by your side when we finally drive them back over the Serpent's Spine.

passages.title: Siege Breaker
passages.text:
The Golden Lotus can hold their own against the mantid's warriors, of that I have no doubt. Their war wagons, on the other hand, have the capability of crippling an entire squad of our fighters in a single volley.

If we wish to maintain the upper hand in this battle, we will need someone to infiltrate their positions and sabotage their siege engines.

I would like you to volunteer.

passages.title: Siege Breaker
passages.text:
Our scouts have reported several mantid war wagons seem to have been destroyed in spectacular fashion.

I assume I have you to thank for this.

passages.title: Hatching Problems
passages.text:
The aqir are multiplying faster than we can put them down. If this pace continues, we will be outnumbered before long.

The only way to slow down their assault is to attack their hives directly and destroy their eggs, but we have been unsuccessful in doing so.

That's why I wish to conscript your services.

Will you help?

passages.title: Hatching Problems
passages.text:
Destroying those eggs should buy us the time we need to regroup before they can throw another wave at us.

Your may just mean the difference between victory and defeat.

passages.title: Getting Ahead
passages.text:
Morale's been down at the camp lately. Funny how getting chewed on by some bugs can spoil the mood of a place.

I've got an idea to perk the troops back up, though. We need a trophy!

See if you can get me the head of one of those big tanky-looking ones so we can put it on display to show these bugs that we mean business! Just try to make sure it's not too mangled, okay?

passages.title: Getting Ahead
passages.text: Show me what ya got!

passages.title: Getting Ahead
passages.text:
Wow, that thing is massive!

If a giant severed bug head doesn't lift the troops' spirits, I don't know what will!

passages.title: Heralds of the Hive
passages.text:
The aqir that have assaulted our camp seem to mainly consist of their shock troops. However, our scouts who dare venture behind their lines have spotted a different kind of creature -- tall and thin, wielding dangerous void magic.

My instinct tells me that these creatures are the leaders behind this invasion. They should be seen as targets of opportunity, and cut down wherever they're met.

Are you up to the task?

passages.title: Heralds of the Hive
passages.text: What do you have to report?

passages.title: Heralds of the Hive
passages.text:
Even a hydra will die if you sever enough of its heads.

Remember that as the battle rages on.

passages.title: Terrors from the Deep
passages.text:
The Aqir threaten the livelihood of the Wastewanders with each passing day, but I have heard of greater terrors that have been unearthed with them.

Our fighters are able, but I fear what might happen if one of these ancient terrors falls upon us. 

I know that you have experience putting down great foes. I would like to ask you to do the same for us. 

After all, we can hardly help protect the forge if we've been decimated by some long-buried monster.

passages.title: Terrors from the Deep
passages.text:
Uldum is a degree safer today, because of you.

I thank you on behalf of the Wastewanders.

passages.title: Things Left Behind
passages.text:
The invading aqir forced the Wastewanders to flee many of our settlements in Uldum. In our haste to escape, much was left behind.

I understand you intend to take the fight to the beasts. While you're there, could you keep an eye out for any of the supplies we had to leave behind? 

You can keep anything of use to you, of course.

passages.title: Things Left Behind
passages.text: Were you able to find anything?

passages.title: Things Left Behind
passages.text:
You found the supplies? Thank goodness!

The desert nights can be punishing on the unprepared. These will help ensure our survival out here.

The Wastewanders owe you much, <class>.

passages.title: Misguiding Mentors
passages.text:
These aspirants... we trained together. Learned together.

The Forsworn have swayed them from the path, now leading them to their demise.

They betray the path. Take out the Ascended that lead these forces against us.

passages.title: Misguiding Mentors
passages.text:
For an Ascended to use the trust their aspirants have in them...

They do not deserve their wings.

passages.title: Misguiding Mentors
passages.text: The sting of aspirants choosing to walk against the Archon's will is a feeling that will never be soothed.

passages.title: Where a Soul Belongs
passages.text:
This soul is no longer tethered to his world of Azeroth.

Kleia must perform her duty and bear him to Oribos to be judged by the Arbiter.

Take this vesper. When you are ready, it will call Ascended to ferry you back across the Veil to Oribos.

Go in service.

passages.title: Where a Soul Belongs
passages.text: It is the duty of all kyrian to ferry souls to Oribos.

passages.title: Where a Soul Belongs
passages.text: I... need some time to process this.

passages.title: Ascended
passages.text:
With success over their trials, our aspirants shall now start the next chapter of their afterlives.

They have proven themselves through eons of training and cleansing, and will now earn ascendance.

As each aspirant is called, I ask you and Pelagos to please assist by ushering them up. It is a tradition we have practiced for eons, reinforcing the bonds that we share.

passages.title: Ascended
passages.text:
The Forsworn, now?

This is an all-out attack!

passages.title: The Spires of Ascension
passages.text:
Our task is not complete yet.

We may have pushed back the Forsworn here in Elysian Hold, but it was only a distraction to split our forces.

The Archon and the Paragons fight to retake the Spires themselves.

We cannot hesitate to aid them in this time of need!

passages.title: The Spires of Ascension
passages.text:
This attack has taught us much. The Archon shall be convening with the remaining Paragons to discuss this Forsworn threat.

We shall call upon you once more when you are needed.

passages.title: Void Incubation
passages.text:
Well one thing is for certain with this egg, it requires great amounts of void energy in order to thrive. 

It is fortunate for us that an Old God is attacking Azeroth at this very moment, yes?

No? Oh...

In any case, there should be an abundance of void energy wherever N'Zoth's minions strike. You should head out and find some.

passages.title: Void Incubation
passages.text: Have you found a reliable source of void energy?

passages.title: Void Incubation
passages.text:
Brilliant! The void energy emanating off these crystals will be perfect to incubate the egg.

Don't worry, I'm sure there won't be any side effects from carrying those around.

passages.title: Continued Incubation
passages.text:
The egg is doing well, but we're going to need more of those void crystals to keep it healthy.

Could you go out and gather some?

passages.title: Continued Incubation
passages.text: Did you bring more void crystals?

passages.title: Continued Incubation
passages.text:
Yes, this will do nicely.

I will continue to tend to the egg and keep you updated on its progress.

passages.title: Encased in Amber
passages.text:
You know who would probably know a lot about how to properly incubate this egg? The mantid!

Of course, they're too busy trying to kill us to share their expertise, but there might be another way to benefit from their knowledge!

Perhaps we could repurpose one of their incubation chambers. That could help speed up this process, I'm sure!

If you could find and mark one for me, I could airlift it out of there.

passages.title: Encased in Amber
passages.text:
This is perfect! 

What a cozy little home this will make for our egg.

passages.title: A Balanced Diet
passages.text:
Now that our larva is hatched, we'll need to figure out what we can feed it to keep it healthy. 

It would seem that the aqir are carnivores, but the only things I've seen them eat are... well... us.

Of course, we can't feed our little friend people, so we'll have to find an alternative. Perhaps we could substitute animal meat?

passages.title: A Balanced Diet
passages.text: He looks hungry, I hope you brought a snack.

passages.title: A Balanced Diet
passages.text:
It looks like animal meat is not his favorite. 

He should be okay for now, we'll try something different later.

passages.title: Meat Alternatives
passages.text:
In the wild it is actually fairly common for insects to eat others of their species. I wonder if this rings true for the aqir as well.

Could you bring back some meat from the aqir or mantid? We'll see if that's more palatable for our friend here.

passages.title: Meat Alternatives
passages.text: I do hope this works.

passages.title: Meat Alternatives
passages.text:
Poor little thing, the insect meat gave him tummy troubles.

We'll have to try something else tomorrow.

passages.title: Fetid Filets
passages.text:
You know, it occurred to me that since this creature has been imbued with void energy, it may prefer a more... corrupted food source.

I speak, of course, of the Minions of N'Zoth.

It's a long shot, but it's worth a try.

passages.title: Fetid Filets
passages.text: Who knew aqir would be such picky eaters?

passages.title: Fetid Filets
passages.text:
Well done! Our little guy cleaned his plate!

It's a good thing, too. I was not looking forward to asking Phaoris for fresh tol'vir corpses.

passages.title: Bindings of Fleshcrafting
passages.text:
These are the Bindings of Fleshcrafting! They empowered the Primus to shape the very flesh and bone of Maldraxxus.

We must return them to their rightful place, so their power can bolster us all.

passages.title: Bindings of Fleshcrafting
passages.text: I can feel their power. Perhaps they will give us the advantage we need.

passages.title: A Bloody Treat
passages.text:
I have heard that a clan of the mogu called the Dokani have mastered the harnessing of life force into a substance they call "anima."

If this stuff is indeed life condensed into a liquid form, then it could have spectacular properties when applied to our aqir larva.

Go see if you can bring back some of this anima in a form that we can use. We'll see if our little friend here likes it!

passages.title: A Bloody Treat
passages.text: Have you returned with the anima?

passages.title: A Bloody Treat
passages.text:
He sure took a liking to that! I guess it helps that it's blood-flavored.

I'll keep note of any changes the anima causes in our friend's growth.

passages.title: Aqir Instincts
passages.text:
In observing the aqir battling the Wastewanders, I have seen the newly hatched immediately join the aqiri assault. It would seem the need for combat is born into these creatures.

We should exercise this in our new hatchling, under your supervision of course. Take him out with you and show him how to fight our enemies. 

He may not be able to fight for long, so don't call him until you're ready for training.

With luck, he will come to see us as part of his hive.

passages.title: Aqir Instincts
passages.text: Take care of your hatchling. He will return here if he becomes too injured.

passages.title: Aqir Instincts
passages.text:
That must have been an exciting day for our little hatchling.

He'll need to rest up for now, but we can try again tomorrow!

passages.title: Honing Instincts
passages.text:
It looks like our little friend is anxious and ready to practice more combat.

Would you care to show him the ropes?

passages.title: Honing Instincts
passages.text: How goes the training?

passages.title: Honing Instincts
passages.text:
The little guy is tuckered out after your adventures. 

Don't worry, I can tend to him here while you're off saving Uldum.

passages.title: Kyrestia's Grace
passages.text:
I remember this particular soul...Uther. Devos brought him before us some time ago. She pleaded her case about his soul having a connection to the Maw.

She then took him under wing, ascending him before he was ready. He became her other hand alongside Lysonia, as it were.

He may proclaim a change of heart, but we shall see. Place him under guard. He may stay by the Archon's grace, but I will not take any chances with one so...broken.

passages.title: Kyrestia's Grace
passages.text: May Thenios's efforts be fruitful. I have never seen a soul so broken in all my eons.

passages.title: Who Are You Fooling?
passages.text:
We cannot conduct the ritual without a very special guest. He's a silkstrider larva named Grubby and he's my best friend.

Unfortunately, the nasty spriggans took him! What's worse is they cast illusions on what they steal, so no one can take it back!

The spriggans often carry trickster powder. If you can take some of that stuff, I can reverse their illusions and rescue Grubby.

passages.title: Who Are You Fooling?
passages.text: We need to find Grubby!

passages.title: Who Are You Fooling?
passages.text: We found him!

passages.title: Seeds Away!
passages.text:
I think we have a problem. Plucking the seed from this root must have shaken some burrowed gorm awake. This isn't good!

Grab on to me. I will fly us out of here, but we must stop the gorm before they overrun the local Vorkai defenses!

passages.title: Seeds Away!
passages.text: I can't believe this. Blue seeds, red seeds, flying faeries!

passages.title: Seeds Away!
passages.text: Okay, I think everything is finally ready, <name>.

passages.title: More Fetid Filets
passages.text:
Our little guy is getting hungry again. 

Could you pick him up a quick bite to eat?

passages.title: More Fetid Filets
passages.text: My, this thing has an appetite.

passages.title: More Fetid Filets
passages.text:
Excellent! This will make sure he grows up big and strong!

Let's hope he doesn't try to eat us then!

passages.title: Someone His Own Size
passages.text:
While fighting alongside you no doubt provides excellent training for our hatchling, sometimes it is better to have him fight on his own against enemies his own size.

I know of one such opponent nearby, observing the Amathet near the Obelisk of the Stars. You should seek it out.

passages.title: Someone His Own Size
passages.text:
I bet that was quite an exhilarating battle!

We should try to get some more training in tomorrow.

passages.title: Big Bad Beetle
passages.text:
It could do our hatchling some good to face off against another aqir, to learn what his kind are capable of.

I have found an opponent who could provide a challenging fight.

passages.title: Big Bad Beetle
passages.text:
Looks like we've got a tough little hatchling on our hands!

That should be enough training for today, though.

passages.title: The Mantids' Mettle
passages.text:
Observing the combat techniques of the mantid may prove helpful for our hatchling's training, offering a different way to use the natural weapons of an insect.

I have found a mantid opponent that our hatchling could face in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. Take him there and see how he does.

passages.title: The Mantids' Mettle
passages.text: How did our hatchling fare against the mantid?

passages.title: The Mantids' Mettle
passages.text:
It looks like our little guy learned much from his battle with the mantid.

No doubt he'll be ready to face fully grown opponents soon.

passages.title: The Littlest Defender
passages.text:
The Baruk mogu are known for animating ancient statues to serve as defenders of their territory. They are a resilient foe, and much can be learned from battling an enemy with such rigid defenses.

Fortunately, it seems like one of their Stoneshapers mistakenly animated a small idol. It has been discarded as useless to the mogu who made it, but it could prove a valuable training opportunity for our hatchling.

Find this miniature defender in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.

passages.title: The Littlest Defender
passages.text:
I knew our little hatchling could handle the mogu creation!

His prowess grows with each passing day!

passages.title: Otherworldly Armaments
passages.text:
To craft a saddle for your beast, I'll need some special materials. Mainly, it will require metals much lighter than what we have available.

I have noticed that the Black Empire cultists carry with them weapons made from otherworldly materials, which are impossibly light and strong. 

If you could retrieve some of their weapons for me, I may be able to melt down this metal and shape it into a saddle for the aqir.

passages.title: Otherworldly Armaments
passages.text: Have you found my materials?

passages.title: Otherworldly Armaments
passages.text:
These weapons... they are both disturbing and fascinating.

I will melt them down at once. Visit me tomorrow to claim your saddle.

passages.title: Lost Flight
passages.text:
<A small dragon emerges from one of the side chambers found within N'Zoth's great carapace. It appears confused.

You surmise that such chambers must have been used to corrupt the dragons, exposing them directly to N'Zoth's dark whispers. At a young age, they would be driven mad, moreso than any other members of the twilight dragonflight that you had met before.

There would be no turning back from such madness.

But maybe it's not too late for this one...>

passages.title: Lost Flight
passages.text:
I can sense great pain, confusion, and loss, within this little one. This poor creature has led a short, heartbreaking life.

As have many of my kind, at the hands of... others.

<Wrathion looks pained for a moment.>

Some day, little one, we will find ourselves again.

<Wrathion touches the dragon's head and closes his eyes.>

There, your mind is cleared. 

This one is still young, it has much to learn and much to see. I trust you will care for it?

Do not let me down, hero.

passages.title: Death's Power Grows
passages.text:
Listen closely, <name>. A time of great destruction lies on the horizon that will challenge our very existence. Now more than ever, we must rise to the defense of Azeroth.

It is for this reason I have expanded the ranks of my champions to include your people. Your sacrifice sets you apart from all others. Hold your head high. Forevermore, you will be a death knight of the Ebon Blade.

Now swear your fealty.

passages.title: Death's Power Grows
passages.text: Swear your fealty, <name>.

passages.title: Death's Power Grows
passages.text:
I accept your pledge. Serve us well.

To that end, new weapons worthy of a Knight of the Ebon Blade have been forged.

Choose, my champion.

passages.title: Alpaca It Up
passages.text: <Munches enthusiastically on the Gersahl greens, while humming gleefully.>

passages.title: Defender of Azeroth
passages.text:
An excellent choice.

Troubling times come. As one of the chosen few, it is both your burden and privilege to defend our world. It is a great honor.

But also know you will be met with the scorn of the ignorant. Oftentimes, mortals are incapable of seeing past our fearsome appearance. Ignore these fools and do what must be done.

Speak with your commander. Then, use his death gate to travel to the land of the living and choose your destiny.

passages.title: Defender of Azeroth
passages.text:
An excellent choice.

Troubling times come. As one of the chosen few, it is both your burden and privilege to defend our world. It is a great honor.

But also know you will be met with the scorn of the ignorant. Oftentimes, mortals are incapable of seeing past our fearsome appearance. Ignore these fools and do what must be done.

Speak with your commander. Then, use his death gate to travel to the land of the living and choose your destiny.

passages.title: License to Ride
passages.text:
The captain said you'd be coming here to pick up your mount. I hope you didn't have any problems finding the place!

Now, before you ride off into the sunset, you'll need to learn how to... well, how to ride! Luckily, we have a riding trainer right here!

Speak with Darlene Stokx when you're ready to learn how to ride.

passages.title: License to Ride
passages.text: Now that you've learned the basics, feel free to return any time you want to advance your riding skills or purchase additional mounts!

passages.title: Evil Grubbies
passages.text:
Oh no! This place is littered with mites!

They are cute like Grubby, but they grow into horrible gorm! If we cleared some of them out, then the Sylvari will have less to fight against later.

They can burrow away, so it's best to burn them up with Pelagos' red seeds. They'll be good for something after all.

passages.title: Evil Grubbies
passages.text: How many more are there?

passages.title: Evil Grubbies
passages.text: It will be hard for them to return.

passages.title: The Blue Seed
passages.text:
I remember seeing a blue seed with red leaves nearby, but it was in a cave behind a wall of brambles. I didn't think of it at the time, but maybe you could use the red seeds to get us in?

I wish I didn't mix up the instructions or we wouldn't be in this mess. But maybe it's all going to work out anyway. Let's go!

passages.title: The Blue Seed
passages.text: This has been quite the fun adventure. Wouldn't you say?

passages.title: The Blue Seed
passages.text: The seed!

passages.title: Alpha Bat
passages.text:
Dredbats are quite useful to us. We make them just like stoneborn, but they lack their same... intelligence. With very little direction, they strike fear into stubborn souls' hearts.

With the anima drought, our dominion over them has waned. One, Duskterror, has wreaked the most havoc.

This presents us with an opportunity. Take this soul and draw her in. When she's weak, we can capture her for our own purposes.

passages.title: Alpha Bat
passages.text: Is Duskterror captured?

passages.title: Alpha Bat
passages.text: Now that Duskterror is captured, we have a little more control over these grounds.

passages.title: The Divine's Shield
passages.text:
This island has been cursed by necrotic magic. The Light can only just reach this place.

Call upon its Divine Shield to step through the barrier before us unharmed and destroy this vile altar.

Show the darkness on this island that you are protected by the Light's embrace.

passages.title: The Divine's Shield
passages.text: Do you require aid? Use Divine Shield to safely pass through the necrotic barrier.

passages.title: The Divine's Shield
passages.text:
You have done well, <name>. Dispel this foul magic wherever you encounter it.

My task has been fulfilled. The Light calls to me. 

Good luck, and remember that the Light's warmth will always embrace you.

passages.title: I MADE You!
passages.text:
I have had it with this insolence!

I have an idea to reset this Mnemis's personality, but you will need to keep it busy.

It will try to fight you, through whatever means it posseses. I suggest you try not to perish. Kleia can hold her own, so hide behind her if so inclined.

Hop to it!

passages.title: I MADE You!
passages.text: I hope you will forgive my behavior. I was not feeling quite like myself.

passages.title: Mnemis, At Your Service
passages.text:
Greetings, I am Locus-Keeper Mnemis and I would be delighted to assist you.

I recall that you are trying to access a particular memory. Due to the contents, that memory can only be viewed within the Vault of the Archon.

In order to gain access to the Vault, you must collect offerings for the two guardians who watch over it. I have hidden these offerings from the Forsworn, as they are not authorized to enter.

The Forgelite Prime is the only one among you who can grant authorization. How convenient!

passages.title: Mnemis, At Your Service
passages.text: Did you find the offerings of which I spoke?

passages.title: Mnemis, At Your Service
passages.text: Your search was fruitful. I am delighted to see you remain intact.

passages.title: Runeforging 101
passages.text:
As knights of the Ebon Blade, we must always be prepared for a variety of martial situations. To this end, the dark art of runeforging is yours to command. With it, runes of great power can be engraved upon your weapons.

Above us in the Heart of Acherus are runeforges. Visit one and use your power to imbue a weapon with a rune of power.

passages.title: Runeforging 101
passages.text: Have you emblazoned a rune upon your weapon, <name>?

passages.title: Runeforging 101
passages.text:
Remember, runeforges exist in only a few locations, including Acherus and certain places within Icecrown. You may only emblazon your weaponry at a Runeforge.

Return whenever you desire to replace the rune. Until then, suffer well.

passages.title: A Bittersweet Prize
passages.text:
I... I don't know what to say.

All that is left is to return Willo... the vessel... to Polemarch Adrestes in Bastion. This sacrifice must not be in vain.

passages.title: A Bittersweet Prize
passages.text:
You have brought the vessel we require for the completion of the Crest of Ascension. I understand it came at a great cost.

We must endeavor to repay our friends in Ardenweald one day.

passages.title: A Shaman's Duty
passages.text:
Greetings, young one. Your companions cannot see me. Only you, for you have been trained in the ways of a shaman.

The shadow energies of this island have ensnared my pack. I need your aid to free them.

Gather veil blossoms from the surrounding area. Burn them on the campfire and breath deep of their smoke.

Then you will be able to see my packmates and release them from their bonds.

passages.title: A Shaman's Duty
passages.text: The veil blossoms shall grant you the sight you need to rescue my pack.

passages.title: A Shaman's Duty
passages.text:
My pack and I are too weak to oppose the dark forces on this island.

We will use the last of our strength to grant you our power.

Use it to rid the island of the ogres' necromancy.

Free the countless souls they have trapped here.

passages.title: Her Rightful Place
passages.text:
Mor'Bitan has met his end... and a painful one at that.

Your fortitude contributed in no small part to my success. You have earned my allegiance... for the time being. 

There is much left to do, should you truly desire ownership of this realm.

Let us regroup at the Seat.

passages.title: Her Rightful Place
passages.text: Were you successful?

passages.title: Her Rightful Place
passages.text: It is good to have allies. Even ones so stubborn.

passages.title: In Death We Are Truly Tested
passages.text:
Vyraz is the one who trapped me within the Maw. He has long been in league with the House of Rituals and the House of Constructs.

No doubt he intended to trap you within that hellish place as well.

It is time he be brought to justice for his treason. Stand with me, and we will face him as one.

passages.title: In Death We Are Truly Tested
passages.text: We are struggling to hold the line. We need to act fast.

passages.title: Call to Arms: Vale of Eternal Blossoms
passages.text:
Our objectives in Vale of Eternal Blossoms are being interrupted by the influx of Alliance scum.

Clear as many of them out of the area that you find, then report back.

passages.title: Call to Arms: Vale of Eternal Blossoms
passages.text: Good work, <class>.

passages.title: Call to Arms: Vale of Eternal Blossoms
passages.text:
Our mission in Vale of Eternal Blossoms is being compromised by the Horde incursion. 

Get into Vale and take out as many as you can.

passages.title: Call to Arms: Vale of Eternal Blossoms
passages.text: Good work, <class>.

passages.title: Herald Their Demise
passages.text:
Since the dawn of Revendreth, Temel has been charged with proclaiming the sins of souls for all to hear.

Every soul here, including venthyr, has been forced to endure his wrathful pronouncements on at least one occasion.

He will know how to wield Inquisitor Stelia's sinstone to break through her defenses.

Simply command him to do so after you locate the inquisitor, and eliminate her.

passages.title: Herald Their Demise
passages.text: Is the inquisitor dead?

passages.title: Herald Their Demise
passages.text:
The ward on the Accuser's sinstone is weakened by the inquisitor's death.

But we must kill both inquisitors before the ward will fully fall, and we can access the Accuser's sinstone.

passages.title: Ending the Inquisitor
passages.text:
Inquisitor Vilhelm hides smugly in the back of the courtyard, flanked by several gargons and loyal venthyr.

We must kill him to break the ward on the Accuser's sinstone, so that Lord Chamberlain can use it in his battle.

Temel will once again help you penetrate the inquisitor's defenses. Do not tarry.

passages.title: Ending the Inquisitor
passages.text: Once the inquisitor is dead, the warding spell will be broken.

passages.title: Ending the Inquisitor
passages.text: Lord Chamberlain confirmed the kill. We should hurry.

passages.title: Curses!
passages.text:
Oh, dear me, this is terrible! Just terrible!

I know precisely which awful curse afflicts that poor soul! But these damnable spriggans keep stealing my scrolls, scattering them all over and ripping them apart! 

Now the falls are overrun with all manner of dangerous magic!

The spriggans have the pieces of the scroll you need. Gather them along with a binding from one of the major hexes, and you can put it all back together.

passages.title: Curses!
passages.text: Hmm... Yes, this looks like it could be the one.

passages.title: Curses!
passages.text: I knew Dreyden would have the scroll we need. We don't have time to waste!

passages.title: Renny the Vulpin
passages.text:
<The small vulpin kit runs up to you with a cheerful bounce and an air of mischief.

You, it seems, are interesting. Interesting enough that this child of Lord Renard of the Court of Winter has decided to tag along with you.

What could possibly go wrong?>

passages.title: Supply Chain
passages.text:
My friend! I could sure use your expertise right now.

One of our wagon convoys was attacked nearby! It was transporting critical supplies... and new goods for me to sell! 

It's important--no--vital, that we recover as much of that equipment as possible.

So, you ready to go? Let's head out and salvage what we can!

passages.title: Supply Chain
passages.text: Did you find those items?

passages.title: Supply Chain
passages.text: Atticus will set a box aside each week with spare supplies in case you need any of them.

passages.title: Vaunted Vengeance
passages.text:
So you are from my baroness's home world? It must be a special one to breed such powerful individuals.

The necromancers here have already begun preparation for Mor'Bitan's ritual. We should capitalize on their progress. 

Three necromancers act as the ritual's architects. Should we acquire their drafts, we could modify them to suit our purposes.

Collect the plans... and feel free to savor your victims' torment.

passages.title: Vaunted Vengeance
passages.text: We are hopeful for your success.

passages.title: Vaunted Vengeance
passages.text: Yes... They will be made to know our pain.

passages.title: Rebel Reinforcements
passages.text:
<General Draven looks around.>

We require additional reinforcements.

I know of two here that are fiercely loyal to the true purpose of Revendreth. The Fearstalker left them here to be consumed by the anima drought due to their allegiance.

They are both fully capable of assisting us in our mission.

Take this anima stake and infuse them. Direct them to me, I will explain the situation.

passages.title: Rebel Reinforcements
passages.text: Are our allies infused?

passages.title: Rebel Reinforcements
passages.text: Our numbers are bolstered. Our survival chance is only slightly less grim.

passages.title: Tainted Cores
passages.text:
This lich seeks a reward for his assault on the House of Eyes. But the power he craves will be his downfall.

We will use our knowledge of his secret ritual to lure him out of the House of Rituals. 

Take these crystals, <name>. Charge them with anima reclaimed from Mor'Bitan's slain minions.

But fracture them first, so that they shatter as the ritual nears completion... but not before Mor'Bitan believes that it has begun.

That is when we will strike.

passages.title: Tainted Cores
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: Tainted Cores
passages.text: Well executed.

passages.title: A Lesson in Humility
passages.text:
Thank you for your service in deposing the Accuser and elevating Lord Chamberlain in her place.

The Accuser's unprompted betrayal has rendered her both undeserving and unfit to serve on the Court of Harvesters.

Now, please, observe what happens to traitors in Revendreth.

passages.title: A Lesson in Humility
passages.text: Please observe silently, Maw Walker.

passages.title: A Lesson in Humility
passages.text:
I am nothing if not merciful and understanding.

The Accuser will be given every opportunity to repent her errors and learn from them.

passages.title: The Prince's New Crown
passages.text:
The crown is ready. I will entrust you to deliver it to Renathal.

Make haste, <name>. This power will surely attract assailants if word gets out.

You may use the mirror to return. Know that I will be dispatching others to destroy it after your arrival. 

Safe travels, Maw Walker.

passages.title: The Prince's New Crown
passages.text:
Excellent work, <name>. 

With this crown, I can focus the magic of the Harvesters into an unstoppable force. Now we continue our mission to redeem Revendreth. As a token of my appreciation for all of your help, I open up our armory to you. Please pick your reward.

passages.title: Their New Home
passages.text:
It pains me to leave my mother behind... but the souls of my people must be brought to safety.

I heard the attendants in Oribos speaking of a place called Ardenweald. A realm of ancient forests where the spirits of nature slumber.

This is a land you know well, is it not? I would see its wonders with my own eyes.

Perhaps the spirits there will know how to save my minn'do from the Night Warrior's power.

passages.title: Their New Home
passages.text: You've returned. But what of the others?

passages.title: Their New Home
passages.text:
My heart aches for Tyrande. The might of the Night Warrior is empowering her to battle these monsters... but it will consume her if we do nothing.

Shandris and I will investigate a... promising whisper that I have heard. I shall call upon you when I know more.

passages.title: The Fearstalker
passages.text:
The trap has been set and the Fearstalker has walked right in.

Just as I expected, her pride has blinded her to the obvious. Have that vial I gave you earlier ready. It may prove useful in the fight ahead.

When you are ready, we can spring the trap.

passages.title: The Fearstalker
passages.text: The Fearstalker must be defeated.

passages.title: The Fearstalker
passages.text:
This medallion will serve us well. But we lack our leader to don it.

We must seek out more allies.

passages.title: How to Catch a Glimmerfly
passages.text:
Yes! Proper tools collected. Now to catch glimmerflies!

Anima drought more severe in northern pools. Many Starving Glimmerflies, most eager to drink from our animyllis blooms.

Place blooms, then while glimmerflies are drinking attach to filaments! Then return to me.

passages.title: How to Catch a Glimmerfly
passages.text: Glimmerflies will surely help me fly!

passages.title: How to Catch a Glimmerfly
passages.text:
<Kowalskos gets very excited> 

Wow! It worked! I hope they hold me up, too!

passages.title: Hunting the Stalker
passages.text:
Now that you have your trap, there's a problem we need to deal with.

A wild beast has been stalking our camp. It's already stolen some of our food. We have little enough as it is.

You and I will work together. Set your freezing trap and lure out whatever this creature is.

Once it is caught, I will determine if the beast can be tamed... or if it needs to be put down.

passages.title: Hunting the Stalker
passages.text: Use the Freezing Trap anywhere within the Ogre Ruins. Just don't do it right within the camp.

passages.title: Hunting the Stalker
passages.text:
Thank you for the help, <name>. I have one last lesson to impart--calling a different companion to your side.

There are plenty of wild beasts on this island. See which ones you can tame.

passages.title: Plaguefall: Knee Deep In It
passages.text:
There are many in the House of Plagues who survived its destruction only to later fall victim to the plagues released in the explosion. Margrave Stradama herself was driven mad from a mixture of twelve different airborne poxes!

These dangers still remain and spread out from the ruins, infecting new victims daily.

I need you to travel into the ruins and recover samples from the victims there.

passages.title: Plaguefall: Knee Deep In It
passages.text: Have you brought me the Poxedskin Samples?

passages.title: Plaguefall: Knee Deep In It
passages.text: Working together will benefit both of us greatly!

passages.title: No Rest For the Dead
passages.text:
Excellent work, my apprentice! You have completed your training and are now a true Necrolord.

That also means you've taken on additional responsibilities. Such is the burden of genius!

I believe Baroness Draka wanted to have a word with you.

passages.title: No Rest For the Dead
passages.text: I hope you're settled--there's no rest for the weary in Maldraxxus.

passages.title: Pulling Hairs
passages.text:
The abominations are well organized and well supplied. We've not been able to gain any ground.

A little disorganization in their supplies and reinforcements might give us an edge.

I need you to work you way behind their lines and eliminate three abominations handling their supplies.

passages.title: The Last Labor
passages.text:
The evil that threatens Bastion crumbles beneath us. But if we allow this cruel baroness to evade justice, we have not won this day.

She cowers in the necropolis above, casting her shadow on this once sacred temple.

We will pull the dagger from our backs. This wound will heal.

passages.title: The Last Labor
passages.text: This is all that remains.

passages.title: The Last Labor
passages.text: May her memory fade from this place.

passages.title: Harvester of Envy
passages.text:
Thank you for meeting us at a minimum safe distance from the Caretaker's Manor. There are enough people around here that may still find the idea of me in a cage to be worth the trouble.

It is too dangerous for you or I to speak to the Tithelord. He is too impulsive and eager to please Denathrius. I recommend we send Temel. 

The stone fiend is a common messenger for Revendreth and few aside from a handful of observers will bat an eye at his arrival. Just shove him when you are ready.

passages.title: Harvester of Envy
passages.text:
The Tithelord. I believe he is the two hundred and seventy fifth Caretaker to lord over the Village Ward. 

He is as dangerously ambitious as every Harvester of Envy before him, and will help only if he believes he stands to gain more power.

passages.title: Comfortably Numb
passages.text:
A mortal in Revendreth. It's rumored that you can traverse the Maw? Astonishing. I have so many questions.

But, I must restrain my curiosity. I have a ... shall we say ... proposition for you that I feel would be advantageous for us both. If it is true that you are able to freely travel these lands then you have access to certain information I cannot reach. 

You see how you could be useful to me? Come, let us discuss the matter further.

passages.title: Comfortably Numb
passages.text: My sinstone, please.

passages.title: Comfortably Numb
passages.text: Oh, well done! I had a moment there when you drank the poison that I feared for you. But you're a hearty sort.

passages.title: The Court
passages.text:
Well, we have quorum. You have done all you can do for us at this stage, Maw Walker.

It falls to me, now, to convince these ancient fools to forsake the greatest patron in all of their reality and throw their lot in with me, a failed rebel with a "new" plan.

Let us see if I can still sway a crowd, as it were. Wish me luck.

passages.title: The Court
passages.text:
Well, that could have gone better. I did not expect them to come around right away, but I had hoped at least one or two of them might.

Now we must do it the hard way. We should leave before they send forces to re-capture this tower.

passages.title: It's a Trap
passages.text:
At last, I will have my vengeance!

I am certain Matyas will flee again if he sees me first so you will need to confront him on my behalf, friend. Then, while he's distracted, I will engage him.

At that point, your obligation as my second is a formality. You must assure Matyas does not dishonor the duel and cheat. When he inevitably does, I expect you'll help me defeat him.

He's just through the portcullis there.

passages.title: It's a Trap
passages.text: Matyas will apologize, or he will die.

passages.title: It's a Trap
passages.text: I would have allowed an apology, but he chose treachery and has paid the price.

passages.title: One Little Whisper
passages.text:
Here be da deal, <name>. To get Mueh'zala talkin', we gotta feed him a teeny bit a da life essence of everybody in dis room.

Why ya be lookin' at me like dat? When has ol' Bwonsamdi ever let ya down?

Me gonna use da mojo ya got to pull da truth outta him while he be feedin'.

Oh, uh, just two more tings. First, I need ya to be ringin' an invitation to a special... friend.

Den I be giving ya more of me mojo powder. Use it during da ritual if any o' me followers be gettin' too weak.

passages.title: One Little Whisper
passages.text: I be eager to hear what ol' Mueh'zala be have ta say...

passages.title: One Little Whisper
passages.text:
Dere be one loa o' death, <name>. And it be ol' Bwonsamdi. 

Ya best not forget dat.

passages.title: The Afflictor's Key
passages.text:
Sylvanas thinks us broken. She believes she has already won.

We will show her how mistaken she is.

First, I will need your help. The bonds that hold me are impossibly strong. We will need the key to free me of them.

My... imprisonment here has been overseen by a creature they call the Afflictor. The key is likely in its possession.

passages.title: The Afflictor's Key
passages.text: Did you find the key?

passages.title: The Afflictor's Key
passages.text:
I had almost forgotten the feeling of freedom.

Now, let us take the fight to these fiends.

passages.title: Cultist Captors
passages.text:
Those damned cultists are relentless!

They caught us off guard and managed to drag a few of our crusaders back to their camp.

Light only knows what they're doing to them up there...

Word is you're quite capable of holding your own. Our numbers are stretched thin enough as it is... if you could rescue the captives, we'd be in your debt.

You can find the cultists lurking up in their mountain camp.

passages.title: Cultist Captors
passages.text: What news have you?

passages.title: Cultist Captors
passages.text: Why am I not surprised? You almost make it look too easy.

passages.title: Winter Be Comin'
passages.text:
Da boss be puttin' together an army of terrible loa. Hakkar and Dambala may only be da beginnin'. How da boss get so strong? I not be seein' him use power like dis before...

Da Winter Queen not be fond of ol' Bwonsamdi, but we gonna need her help to stop Mueh'zala.

Ya be friendly wit' da Queen, no? If she be willin' to rally her forces, we might be able to stop Mueh'zala before it be too late.

Head to da Heart of da Forest and speak wit' da Queen. She be our only hope now.

passages.title: Winter Be Comin'
passages.text: We gotta convince da Winter Queen to join forces against Mueh'zala...

passages.title: Winter Be Comin'
passages.text: I am not eager to do any favors for Bwonsamdi, but Mueh'zala's actions cannot be ignored.

passages.title: Bet On Yourself
passages.text:
Dear Maw Walker... my friend... you're going to lose. Everyone knows you can't compete in the arena. 

The entire Challenger's Promenade knows it, the brokers in Oribos know it, even Zo'umlo knows it.

I've brought in a special challenger just to prove the point. Face Mistress Dyrax in the Theater of Pain and prove us wrong... or prove us right.

We will be betting, so don't disappoint.

passages.title: Bet On Yourself
passages.text: What did you prove?

passages.title: Bet On Yourself
passages.text: Your performance has netted me a nice profit... Zo'umlo bet poorly.

passages.title: Bet On Yourself
passages.text:
Dear Maw Walker... my friend... you're going to lose. Everyone knows you can't compete in the arena. 

The entire Challenger's Promenade knows it, the brokers in Oribos know it, even Zo'umlo knows it.

I've brought in a special challenger just to prove the point. Face Devmorta in the Theater of Pain and prove us wrong... or prove us right.

We will be betting, so don't disappoint.

passages.title: Bet On Yourself
passages.text: What did you prove?

passages.title: Bet On Yourself
passages.text: Your performance has netted me a nice profit... Zo'umlo bet poorly.

passages.title: WARNING: This is Only a Test!
passages.text:
Where some see a problem, I see an opportunity. What this Scourge fiasco calls for is a creative solution!

Behold--my "secret weapon"!

Controlled by none other than my Carefully Constructed Control Device, or C.C.C.D. for short!

Hmm, that name might need a little work.

You're the first to see it, so that means you'll be the first to test it. But don't worry, I'm pretty sure it's safe.

Good luck!

passages.title: WARNING: This is Only a Test!
passages.text: So, how's it goin'?

passages.title: WARNING: This is Only a Test!
passages.text:
Oh boy! Did you see the look on their faces?

I mean, some of them didn't really have faces, but you know... their jaws and whatnot. Hah!

That was great. The possibilities are endless!

passages.title: Finders-Keepers, Sinners-Weepers
passages.text:
Oh hello, mortal. You have a real knack for arriving at the most opportune times. I wonder what Taskmaster Matyas wants with you. Curious.

As for me, again Matyas has used my sinstone against me. I was already enraged that he caged me and I assure you that this latest attack will not go unanswered. Yet, while he has my sinstone I am unable to act against him directly. So we must remedy that.

You question the laborers and I will read this journal while I regain my strength.

passages.title: Finders-Keepers, Sinners-Weepers
passages.text: Have you discovered anything useful?

passages.title: Finders-Keepers, Sinners-Weepers
passages.text: Ah. A pity none of these are mine. Still they may prove useful.

passages.title: Combat Nullifier 07-X
passages.text:
While everyone is busy fending off our enemies with swords and magic, how about we try something different.

Behold, my latest invention--the Combat Nullifier 07-X!

With this device, no enemy is truly your enemy any longer!

Now, I haven't quite worked out the exact energy modulator calculations, but I am certain it works. Mostly.

For now, we'll need to "borrow" some energy from our enemies in order to operate it.

Go ahead. Charge it up and give it a whirl!

passages.title: Combat Nullifier 07-X
passages.text: How's it going?

passages.title: Combat Nullifier 07-X
passages.text: Whoa! That was a blast, huh?

passages.title: Parting Ways
passages.text:
Me don't know what fate be comin' for ol' Vol'jin... but it be waitin' for me in Ardenweald.

Ashamane, Hir'eek, Shadra... dey belong dere, too.

We best be gettin' outta here. Me had enough of da Maw for an eternity.

passages.title: Parting Ways
passages.text:
It fills me with joy to know that the spirits lost to the Maw are safe once more.

None can say what fate has in store for Vol'jin. The path on which he has embarked has never before been walked by a mortal soul.

Yet whatever awaits him, know that your efforts are what made it possible.

passages.title: Field Reports
passages.text:
The Scourge can strike anytime, anywhere.

To counter their unpredictability, the Argent Crusade has secured key locations along the southern road heading east. However, I have yet to receive any reports from our scouts in the field.

With the erratic nature of these attacks, I fear the worst.

Travel the road and take stock of our outposts. I'll be expecting a full report when you return.

Light be with you, <name>.

passages.title: Field Reports
passages.text: Gregor sent you?

passages.title: Field Reports
passages.text:
This is far worse than we thought.

Commander Gregor must be told of the true extent of the Scourge's resurgence.

passages.title: A Message from Icecrown
passages.text:
We received word from our forces in Northrend. Justicar Trueheart requests our immediate assistance.

As you are an experienced <class>, I ask that you answer the call.

The urgency of this summons cannot be ignored, even if it means braving the terrors of Icecrown itself.

I know you fear for the safety of everyone here. I will continue to coordinate our efforts and call in additional reinforcements.

Light be with you, <name>.

passages.title: A Message from Icecrown
passages.text: You arrive just in time. Commander Gregor spoke highly of you.

passages.title: The Golden Dawn
passages.text:
The machinations of war commence. Gharmal's crimes are now evident to all of the Shadowlands.

Bastion demands vengeance, and we shall share it with them. Only our combined forces will defeat the Constructs once and for all.

Meet Draka at the overlook. Your presence there will help solidify an agreement.

passages.title: The Golden Dawn
passages.text: An alliance is secured. Now we plan the attack.

passages.title: Cooking Meat
passages.text:
This is Won'sa, a shaman who was with the expedition.

She is dying of starvation. A death unfit for the Horde!

Slay some of the nearby wildlife for their meat and cook it over the fire.

Won'sa can tell us what happened to the missing expedition after she eats.

passages.title: Cooking Meat
passages.text: Please... I be needin'... food...

passages.title: Cooking Meat
passages.text:
<Won'sa quickly eats the meat that you cooked.>

Looks I not gonna be knockin' on Bwonsamdi's door, after all.

Ya best hurry. Da quilboar took Shuja and da rest of da expedition!

passages.title: Forbidden Quilboar Shadow Magic
passages.text:
Quilboar are savage and violent. I did not think they knew how to use shadow magic.

Obviously, we cannot allow them to continue their rituals. And certainly not on members of the Horde.

Slay the quilboar in the den. They must learn the fatal error of their ways.

passages.title: Forbidden Quilboar Shadow Magic
passages.text: A fine job. The quilboar seem to be keeping their distance. Perhaps they learned their lesson.

passages.title: The Re-Deather
passages.text:
I got the perfect plan. You're gonna ride the Choppy Booster Mk. 5 and BLAST those walkin' cadavers from the sky!

I hereby dub the Re-Sizer the "Re-Deather." We're gonna show them where the undead belong!

Er, except for OUR undead. They're totally fine.

Anyway, hop on the Choppy Booster Mk. 5 and I'll pilot it.

Once we save Wrathion, we'll blast our way to all the other survivors!

passages.title: The Re-Deather
passages.text: Thank you, stranger. I failed the Horde... I was not strong enough to stop this threat on my own.

passages.title: Purge the Totems
passages.text:
The harpies have placed vile totems throughout the area to attain more power.

We must destroy those totems in order to debilitate our foes.

Take this torch and burn any totems you see. It is wise to weaken one's enemy before the fight even begins.

passages.title: Purge the Totems
passages.text: The harpies grow weaker with their totems destroyed. Let us hope they realize that the Horde is a force to be reckoned with.

passages.title: Message to Base
passages.text:
Let us return to camp with Herbert in tow.

We're one step closer towards thwarting the ogres and their plans.

passages.title: Message to Base
passages.text:
It is good to see you all back in one piece. You are testament to the Horde's strength of will!

Let's hope Gloomburst is as powerful as he is unhinged.

passages.title: Who Lurks in the Pit
passages.text:
There's a whole lot of shadow energy coming from this pit. I'm guessing a ritual is being performed down there. And that means a sacrifice.

Do you hear that? I've got the best hearing around, ever since I got this new ear sewn onto me.

It sounds like there are some more of our soldiers trapped down there. Probably all webbed up.

Won'sa and I will... stay up here and help anyone who gets out.

You should jump in and rescue anyone who is left down there!

passages.title: Who Lurks in the Pit
passages.text:
Crenna Earth-Daughter will be vital to our cause. Her connection to nature will help us understand what the ogres have done to this island.

Good work, recruit.

passages.title: Stocking Up on Supplies
passages.text:
Provisioner Jin'hake managed to recover some other supplies from the shipwreck.

Take a look at what he has before heading out.

passages.title: Stocking Up on Supplies
passages.text: Provisioner Jin'hake should have some supplies that you can use.

passages.title: Stocking Up on Supplies
passages.text:
I hope you have what you need. 

Throg found this bag nearby and thought you might have use of it.

passages.title: Hunting the Stalker
passages.text:
Now that you have your trap, we can move onto the true problem at hand.

A strange creature not native to this island has been stalking our camp.

I think we should capture it and see how it can help us.

Set the freezing trap within these ruins to lure it out. We'll see just what we are dealing with.

passages.title: Hunting the Stalker
passages.text:
I admit, I am rather ashamed I did not immediately recognize this beast.

It must be quite resilient if it was able to survive this long on its own!

Here, let me teach you another trick. You'll want to have multiple pets to switch between if you're to be a <class> of any worth.

passages.title: A Shaman's Duty
passages.text:
Greetings, young one. Your compatriots cannot see me. Only you, for you have been trained in the ways of a shaman.

The necrotic energies of this island have ensnared my pack. I need your aid to free them.

Gather veil blossoms from surrounding area. Burn them on the campfire and breath deep of their smoke.

Then you will be able to see my packmates and release them from their bonds.

passages.title: Like Ogres to the Slaughter
passages.text:
This is worse than I thought. The ogres were counting on us to stage a rescue attempt.

It seems that they plan to attack our camp while they near completion of the ritual.

We can't let that happen. Crush the ogres! Show them the strength of the Horde!

passages.title: Like Ogres to the Slaughter
passages.text: Show the ogres no mercy!

passages.title: Like Ogres to the Slaughter
passages.text: That should weaken the ogres long enough for us to put an end to their plotting.

passages.title: Controlling their Stones
passages.text:
Warlord Thunderwalker won't last much longer. Soon, his life essence will be completely drained. 

Gor'groth mentioned that they are keeping him captive through the use of ward stones.

I want you to recover these ward stones and bring them here so we can release Thunderwalker.

passages.title: Controlling their Stones
passages.text: These were the ward stones used to bind me? Perhaps even the ogres have heard tale of my strength!

passages.title: Controlling their Stones
passages.text:
Thank you for the aid, but saving me will not stop the ogres. 

They already have enough life essence to complete the ritual!

passages.title: Dungeon: Darkmaul Citadel
passages.text:
Gor'groth seeks to use shadow magic to gain control of Kalecgos, the aspect of the Blue Dragonflight.

He's collected enough life essence to attempt to finish the ritual. I do not know what will happen, but we cannot let him complete it!

Gor'groth will not stop until he is slain!

You must storm the citadel and slay Gor'groth before he can complete his ritual!

I would charge in beside you, were I not still recovering from his dark magic.

passages.title: Dungeon: Darkmaul Citadel
passages.text: Victory for the Horde! It is time we returned to Orgrimmar as heroes and conquerors.

passages.title: An End to Beginnings
passages.text:
You've done well here, <name>. Kalecgos and Wrathion are planning to continue on to the Dragon Isles.

I must return to Orgrimmar. This shadow magic is concerning... and requires that I look into it more.

Talk with Kalecgos. He'll get you to the Dragon Isles and inform you about what's going on there.

passages.title: An End to Beginnings
passages.text:
It's good to be back in Orgrimmar. 

I must report to the warchief, but I know what you can do in the meantime...

passages.title: The Final Countdown
passages.text:
